text: The 15 cm sIG 33 (schweres Infanterie Geschuetz 33) was the standard German heavy infantry gun used in the Second World War. It was the largest weapon ever classified as an infantry gun by any nation.<cr>Sources differ on the development history, but the gun itself was of conventional design. Early production models were horse-drawn, with wooden wheels. Later production models had pressed steel wheels, with solid rubber tires and air brakes for motor towing.<cr>The sIG 33 was rather heavy for its mission and it was redesigned in the late 1930s to incorporate light alloys in an effort to save weight. This saved about 150 kilograms (330 lb), but the outbreak of war forced the return to the original design before more than a few hundred were made, as the Luftwaffe had a higher priority for light alloys. A new carriage, made entirely of light alloys, was tested around 1939, but was not accepted for service.<cr><cr>
translation: 15厘米sIG 33（重型步兵炮33）是德国在第二次世界大战中使用的标准重型步兵炮。它是任何国家分类为步兵炮的最大武器。<cr>资料来源对开发历史存在分歧，但该火炮本身设计传统。早期生产型号由马匹牵引，配备木轮。后期生产型号则使用压铸钢轮，并配有实心橡胶轮胎和空气制动器以适应机动牵引。<cr>在20世纪30年代晚期，sIG 33因任务需求较重而被重新设计，尝试采用轻合金减轻重量。这大约节省了150公斤（330磅），但战争爆发迫使恢复到原设计，因为德国空军对轻合金有更高优先级。<cr>一种完全由轻合金制成的新炮架在约1939年进行了测试，但未被接受服役。

text: The Karabiner 98 kurz (carbine 98 short, often abbreviated as Kar98k, K98, or K98k) is a bolt action rifle chambered for the 7.92?57mm Mauser cartridge that was adopted on 21 June 1935 as the standard service rifle by the German Wehrmacht.It was one of the final developments in the long line of Mauser military rifles. Although supplemented by semi- and fully automatic rifles during World War II, it remained the primary German service rifle until the end of the war in 1945. Millions were captured by the Soviets at the conclusion of World War II and were widely distributed as military aid. The Karabiner 98k therefore continues to appear in conflicts across the world as they are taken out of storage during times of strife.<cr><cr>
translation: 毛瑟98k步枪是一种采用7.92×57毫米马усс子弹的栓动步枪，于1935年6月21日被德国国防军采纳为制式步枪。它是漫长系列毛瑟军用步枪中的最后一种发展成果之一。尽管在第二次世界大战期间有半自动和全自动步枪作为补充装备，但直到1945年战争结束，它一直是主要的德军制式步枪。在第二次世界大战结束后，数百万支毛瑟98k被苏联俘获，并广泛分发为军事援助。因此，在世界各地冲突中，这些步枪在动荡时期从仓库取出时仍会继续出现。<cr><cr>指挥官报告<cr><cr>

text: The 122 mm howitzer M1938 (M-30) was a Soviet 121.92 mm (4.8 inch) howitzer. The weapon was developed by the design bureau of Motovilikha Plants, headed by F. F. Petrov, in the late 1930s, and was in production from 1939 to 1955. The M-30 saw action in World War II, mainly as a divisional artillery piece of the Red Army (RKKA). Captured guns were also employed later in the conflict by the German Wehrmacht and the Finnish Army. Post World War II the M-30 saw combat in numerous conflicts of the mid- to late twentieth century in service of other countries' armies, notably in the Middle East.<cr><cr>
translation: M1938（M-30）型122毫米榴弹炮是苏联在1930年代后期由莫托维利赫工厂设计局开发的一种121.92毫米（4.8英寸）榴弹炮，该设计局由F.F.彼得罗夫领导。从1939年到1955年期间生产这种武器。M-30型榴弹炮在第二次世界大战中主要用于红军的师级炮兵。<cr>被俘获的火炮也在后来的冲突中被德国国防军和芬兰军队使用。<cr>二战后，M-30型榴弹炮还在20世纪中期至后期为其他国家的军队服务，在中东地区尤为突出。<cr> <cr>

text: A carbine based on the M1891/30 design that was produced from 1939 to 1945 at the Izhevsk arsenal and in 1940 and 1944 at Tula. They were intended for use by second-echelon and noncombatant troops. Very few M38 carbines were made in 1945 and are highly sought after by collectors. Essentially a M1891/30 with a shortened barrel and shortened stock (the M38 is 40 inches (1,000 mm) in overall length versus 48 inches overall length for the Model 91/30), this carbine did not accept a bayonet and was in fact designed so that the standard Model 91/30 bayonet would not fit it. However many M38 carbines were fitted into M44 stocks by the Soviets as a wartime expedient. M38s in the correct M38 stock command a premium over M38s in M44 pattern stocks. The M38 was replaced by the M44 carbine in 1944.
translation: 一种基于M1891/30设计的卡宾枪，从1939年到1945年由伊热夫斯克兵工厂生产，并在1940年和1944年由图拉兵工厂生产。这些卡宾枪是为二线部队和非战斗人员使用而制造的。很少有M38卡宾枪是在1945年生产的，因此备受收藏家追捧。本质上，M38是一种缩短了枪管和枪托（全长为40英寸或1,000毫米，相比之下M1891/30全长为48英寸）的M1891/30，并且不接受刺刀，实际上设计成标准的M1891/30刺刀无法安装。然而，在战争期间许多M38卡宾枪被苏联改装成了M44型枪托。带有正确M38枪托的M38卡宾枪比使用M44模式枪托的更值钱。M38在1944年被M44卡宾枪取代。

text: The Messerschmitt Bf 109, commonly called the Me 109 (most often by Allied aircrew and even amongst the German aces themselves,even though this was not the official German designation), is a German World War II fighter aircraft designed by Willy Messerschmitt and Robert Lusser during the early to mid-1930s.The 'Bf 109' designation was issued by the German ministry of aviation and represents the developing company Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (at which the engineer Messerschmitt led the development of the plane) and a rather arbitrary figure. It was one of the first truly modern fighters of the era, including such features as all-metal monocoque construction, a closed canopy, and retractable landing gear. It was powered by a liquid-cooled, inverted-V12 aero engine.<cr>The Bf 109 first saw operational service during the Spanish Civil War and was still in service at the dawn of the jet age at the end of World War II, during which time it was the backbone of the Luftwaffe's fighter force. From the end of 1941, the Bf 109 was steadily being supplemented by the superior Focke-Wulf Fw 190.<cr>Originally conceived as an interceptor, later models were developed to fulfill multiple tasks, serving as bomber escort, fighter-bomber, day-, night-, all-weather fighter, ground-attack aircraft, and as reconnaissance aircraft. It was supplied to and operated by several states during World War II, and served with several countries for many years after the war. The Bf 109 was the most produced fighter aircraft in history, with a total of 33,984 airframes produced from 1936 up to April 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 梅塞施密特Bf 109战斗机，通常被称为Me 109（主要是盟军飞行员和甚至德国王牌飞行员自己这样称呼，尽管这不是官方的德国防空名称），是德国在二战期间设计的一款战斗机。该型号由Willy Messerschmitt 和 Robert Lusser 在20世纪30年代早期至中期设计完成。Bf 109 的命名是由德国航空部指定的，代表了开发公司巴伐利亚飞机制造厂（工程师Messerschmitt 领导该公司进行飞机研发）以及一个相当随意的数字。它是当时首批真正现代战斗机之一，具有全金属单体结构、封闭式座舱和可收放起落架等特征。它装备了一台液冷倒V12航空发动机。<cr>梅塞施密特Bf 109首次在西班牙内战期间投入实战，并一直服役到二战结束，直至喷气机时代来临。在这段时间里，它是德国空军战斗机部队的主力机型。从1941年底开始，性能更优的福克-武尔夫Fw 190逐渐取代了Bf 109。<cr>最初被设计为拦截机，后来的型号则发展成为能够执行多种任务的飞机，包括护航轰炸机、战斗机轰炸机、昼间/夜间/全天候战斗机、对地攻击机以及侦察机。在二战期间，该机型被多个国家采购并使用，并且战后还继续服役于多个其他国家多年。梅塞施密特Bf 109是历史上产量最大的战斗机之一，从1936年到1945年4月共生产了33,984架。<cr>

text: The Panzer III Medium Tank was the main German battle tank for the first two and a half years of the Second World War, only beginning to lose that status after the appearance of the Panzer IV Ausf F2 in March 1942. Until then the Panzer III had been the only German designed tank armed with a gun designed to penetrate enemy armour.<cr>The Ausf H was similar to late production Ausf Gs, with the same wider tracks and 5cm gun. Extra 30mm armour plates were attached to the front and rear of the hull and the front of the superstructure. Less than half of the original order were produced, before it was replaced by the Ausf J.<cr><cr>
translation: 三号中型坦克是德国在第二次世界大战最初两年半里的主要战斗坦克，直到1942年3月四号坦克Ausf F2出现后才开始失去这一地位。在此之前，三号坦克是唯一一种装备有专门用于穿透敌方装甲的火炮的德国设计坦克。<cr>三号坦克H型与后期生产的G型相似，拥有相同的加宽履带和50毫米火炮。在车体正面、背面以及前部上部结构附加了额外的30毫米装甲板。在被J型取代之前，不到原订单的一半数量得以生产。<cr><cr>

text: The Kliment Voroshilov (KV) tanks were a series of Soviet heavy tanks named after the Soviet defense commissar and politician Kliment Voroshilov and used by the Red Army during World War II. The KV series were known for their extremely heavy armour protection during the early part of the war, especially during the first year of the German invasion of the Soviet Union.They were practically immune to the 3.7 cm KwK 36 and howitzer-like, short barreled 7.5 cm KwK 37 guns mounted, respectively, on the early Panzer III and Panzer IV tanks fielded by the invading German forces. Until more effective guns were developed by the Germans, the KV-1 was invulnerable to almost any German weapon except the 8.8 cm Flak gun. Even then, the sloped and reinforced front armor and turret of the KV-1 caused some hits from the 8.8 cm Flak gun to ricochet.<cr>Prior to Operation Barbarossa (the German invasion of the USSR), about 500 of the over 22,000 tanks then in Soviet service were of the KV-1 type. When the KV-1 appeared, it outclassed the French Char B1, the only other heavy tank in operational service in the world at that time. Yet, in the end, it turned out that there was little sense in producing the expensive KV tanks, as the T-34 medium tank performed better (or at least equally well) in all practical respects. Later in the war, the KV series became a base for the development of the IS (IS - Josif Stalin) series of tanks.<cr><cr><cr><cr>
translation:
克里门特·伏罗希洛夫（KV）重型坦克是苏联在二战期间用于红军的一系列以苏联国防委员兼政治家克里门特·伏罗希洛夫命名的重型坦克。KV系列坦克以其极厚的装甲而闻名，尤其是在德国入侵初期阶段，特别是第一年。它们几乎对德军早期装备的3.7厘米KwK 36和类似火炮、短管7.5厘米KwK 37（分别安装在早期三号坦克和四号坦克上）具有免疫性。直到德国开发出更有效的武器之前，KV-1重型坦克几乎不受任何德军武器的威胁，除了88毫米高射炮以外。即使如此，KV-1倾斜且加固的前装甲和炮塔仍使一些来自88毫米高射炮的射击弹跳开。

巴巴罗萨行动（德国入侵苏联）之前，在当时苏联服役的超过2.2万辆坦克中，大约有500辆是KV-1型。当KV-1出现时，它超过了当时世界上唯一其他在役重型坦克——法国夏尔B1坦克。然而最终发现生产昂贵的KV系列坦克意义不大，因为T-34中型坦克在所有实际方面表现得更好（或至少同样好）。后来在战争期间，KV系列成为IS（IS - 约瑟夫·斯大林）系列坦克发展的基础。<cr>

text: Franz Halder (30 June 1884 2 April 1972) was a German general and the chief of the OKH General Staff from 1938 until September 1942, when he was dismissed after frequent disagreements with Adolf Hitler. Until December 1941 Halder's military position corresponded to the old Chief of the General Staff position, which during World War One was the highest military office in the German Imperial Army. Halder's diary during his time as chief of OKH General Staff has been a source for authors that have written about such subjects as Adolf Hitler, the Second World War and the NSDAP (The Nazi party). In William Shirer's The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich, Halder's diary is cited hundreds of times.<cr><cr>
translation: 弗兰茨·哈尔德（1884年6月30日—1972年4月2日）是德国的一位将军，从1938年至1942年9月担任陆军总司令部总参谋长。由于与阿道夫·希特勒频繁发生分歧，他在1942年被解职。直到1941年12月，哈尔德的职位仍然相当于第一次世界大战期间德国帝国军队中的总参谋长一职，这是当时德国军队中最高的军事职务。哈尔德担任陆军总司令部总参谋长时期的日记成为许多作者撰写有关阿道夫·希特勒、第二次世界大战和纳粹党的书籍的重要资料来源。在威廉·夏伊勒的《第三帝国的兴亡》一书中，哈尔德的日记被引用了数百次。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: Shaposhnikov was born at Zlatoust, near Chelyabinsk in the Urals. He was of Orenburg Cossack origin.He joined the army of the Russian Empire in 1901 and graduated from the Nicholas General Staff Academy in 1910, reaching the rank of colonel in the Caucasus Grenadiers division during World War I. In 1917, unusual for an officer of his rank, he supported the Russian Revolution and in 1918 joined the Red Army.<cr>Shaposhnikov was one of the few Red Army commanders with formal military training, and in 1921 he joined the Army's General Staff, where he served until 1925, when he was appointed commander of the Leningrad military region. From 1928 to 1932 he commanded the Moscow military region, then the Privolzhsk military region. In 1932 he was appointed commandant of the Red Army's Frunze Military Academy, then in 1935 returned to the command of the Leningrad region. In 1937 he was appointed Chief of the General Staff, in succession to Alexander Ilyich Yegorov, a victim of the Case of Trotskyist Anti-Soviet Military Organization secret trial, Joseph Stalin's Great Purge of the Red Army. In 1940 he was appointed a Marshal of the Soviet Union.<cr>Shaposhnikov planned the invasion of Finland in 1940. The Winter War did not become the success the Soviet side had hoped, and Shaposhnikov resigned as Chief of the General Staff in August 1940, officially due to ill-health. At the time of the German invasion, he was reinstated as Chief of the General Staff (until November 1942) and also became Deputy People's Commissar for Defence, the post he held until his career was cut short by ill-health in 1943. He held the position of commandant of the Voroshilov Military Academy until his death in 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 夏泊尼科夫出生于乌拉尔地区的车里雅宾斯克附近的捷洛亚乌斯特。他是奥伦堡哥萨克的后代。他于1901年加入俄罗斯帝国军队，并在1910年毕业于尼古拉总参谋部学院，在第一次世界大战期间，他在高加索掷弹兵师中晋升为上校。<cr>1917年，对于他这样级别的军官来说非常罕见的是，夏泊尼科夫支持了俄国革命，并于1918年加入红军。<cr>夏泊尼科夫是少数拥有正规军事训练的红军指挥官之一，在1921年加入了总参谋部，并在那里工作到1925年，当时他被任命为列宁格勒军区司令。从1928年到1932年，他先后担任了莫斯科军区和普里沃尔日斯基军区的指挥官。在1932年，他被任命为红军弗鲁涅洛夫军事学院院长，在1935年又回到列宁格勒地区任司令。1937年，他接替亚历山大·伊利亚奇·叶戈罗夫担任总参谋长，后者是托洛茨基反苏军事组织案秘密审判的受害者之一，斯大林对红军的大清洗行动中的一员。在1940年，夏泊尼科夫被任命为苏联元帅。<cr>夏泊尼科夫计划了1940年的芬兰入侵。冬季战争并没有成为苏联方面所期望的成功，并且夏泊尼科夫于1940年8月因健康原因辞去了总参谋长的职务。<cr>在德国入侵时，他被重新任命为总参谋长（直到1942年11月），同时担任副国防人民委员一职，这一职位一直保持到1943年他的职业生涯因健康问题而中断。他在弗鲁涅洛夫军事学院院长的职位上直至去世于1945年。<cr><cr>

text: Jagdgeschwader 1 (JG 1) was a German World War II fighter unit or 'wing' which used the Messerschmitt Bf 109 and Focke-Wulf Fw 190 aircraft, between 19401944. The name of the unit derives from Jagd, meaning 'hunt' and Geschwader, meaning 'wing'. First formed in May 1939 in eastern Prussia, I./JG 1 was one of the original groups created by the Luftwaffe as part of its expansion plans.<cr>Between 1940 and 1942, JG 1 operated primarily over the Western Front and northern occupied Europe. During the initial days of the war, JG 1 faced little resistance, apart from occasional Royal Air Force (RAF) excursions. The unit was rarely engaged in large-scale confrontations during this time. From late 1942 onwards it was tasked with defence of the Reich. After D-Day, elements of JG 1 were moved to France and were tasked with air support to the Wehrmacht Heer, along with their air defence role. Operation Bodenplatte severely reduced the strength of JG 1.<cr>Towards the end of the war, the unit was disbanded and its remaining pilots and aircraft were re-organized. What remained of these groups surrendered to Allied forces at the end of the war.<cr>JG 1 was the first unit to attempt 'aerial bombing' techniques against the United States Army Air Forces (USAAF) heavy bomber formations. It was the only unit to be equipped with the Heinkel He 162 jet fighter.<cr>In 1944 the 'Oesau' suffix was added to the unit's title, after its late Geschwaderkommodore Oberst Walter Oesau (127 kills), who was killed in action.<cr>Some 700 enemy aircraft were claimed shot down during the war by the unit.<cr><cr>
translation: JG 1（第1战斗机联队）是德国空军在第二次世界大战期间使用Bf 109和Fw 190战斗机的战斗机单位，活跃时间为1940年至1944年。该单位名称中的“Jagd”意为“狩猎”，而“Geschwader”则指“联队”。第1战斗机联队于1939年5月在东普鲁士成立，是德国空军扩张计划中最早建立的单位之一。<cr>从1940年至1942年，JG 1主要在西线和被占领的北欧地区执行任务。战争初期，该联队遭遇的抵抗很少，除了偶尔遇到英国皇家空军（RAF）的小规模行动外，几乎没有参与大规模空战。<cr>从1942年末开始，JG 1的任务转变为保卫德国本土。诺曼底登陆后，JG 1的部分兵力被调往法国，并承担支援国防军陆军的空中任务以及防空职责。在“博登platte”行动中，JG 1的实力受到严重削弱。<cr>接近战争结束时，该联队解散，剩余飞行员和飞机重新编组。这些单位残余的部分最终向盟军投降。<cr>JG 1是第一个尝试对美国陆军航空部队重型轰炸机编队进行“空中轰炸”的单位，并且也是唯一装备Heinkel He 162喷气式战斗机的单位。<cr>1944年，为了纪念该联队已故指挥官Oberst Walter Oesau（击落70架飞机），在其名称后加上了“Oesau”字样。<cr>JG 1在战争期间宣称击落敌机约700架。

text:
On 19 January 1944, the 15th Guards Airborne Division was renamed the 100th Guards Rifle Division and its component brigades renamed the 298th, 301st and 304th Guards Rifle Regiments. In addition to this core strength, the division had two artillery regiments and various complementary contingents, including communications.<cr><cr>In June 1944, the division was sent to the Karelian Front to take place in an operation aimed at clearing Karelia of Finnish forces. The attack started on June 21, 1944, with the 100th Guards Rifle Division performing a force-crossing of the Svir River. After three days of violent attacks, Finnish defenses were overrun and the Leningrad Oblast completely liberated.

The offensive resumed shortly afterwards, and had to pass through the former Mannerheim Line, reinforced between 1941 and 1944. Taking heavy casualties, the division advanced north and arrived to the shore of Vidlitsa river on July 1, 1944. A day later, the river was crossed in force and the division resumed its offensive. However, it was stopped three days later by another river coupled with extensive defensive fortification. After yet another assault crossing and heavy fight, the offensive stopped on July 14, 1944, and the division assumed a defensive stance until mid-August. The operation lasted in total for 40 days, with the division advancing more than 200 kilometers starting from its initial positions around Leningrad. The Svir River, crossed in force by the division, would later give its name to the unit.

In August 1944, the division was relocated to Kalinin and renamed the 100th Guards Svir Airborne Division, only to be renamed back to 100th Guards Svir Rifle Division a few months later. After receiving reinforcements and a new commander, Major General Ivan Alekseevich Makarenko, the division was transported to Hungary in January 1945 and integrated into the 9th Guards Army's 39th Guards Rifle Corps.

Starting from mid-February, the division was part of the Soviet reserve force during the German Operation Frhlingserwachen, east of Lake Balaton, in which the 6th SS Panzer Army was trying to get through Soviet defenses. On March 16, 1945, the Wehrmacht's offensive was stopped, and an offensive on Vienna was launched immediately afterwards. The 100th Division had the task of 'cleaning up' encircled pockets of German resistance. On April 2, 1945, the division started its march towards Vienna. Five days later, the troops arrived within sight of Vienna, which was turned into a fortress defended by the II SS Panzer Corps and ad hoc training and anti-aircraft units.

The operation aimed at capturing Vienna started on April 7, 1945. The division occupied the southern outskirts of the city, and then executed an enveloping maneuver westwards, going around the city through the Vienna woods, engaging in heavy combat in the center of the city, seizing key targets such as the railway terminal and the parliament, and force-crossing the Danube. After five days of violent urban warfare, Vienna fell on April 13, 1945.

By early May, the division was committed to the offensive towards Prague, still in the hands of the Wehrmacht. It crossed the Czech border on May 10, meeting American forces advancing from the west.<cr><cr>
translation:
1944年1月19日，第15近卫空降师更名为第100近卫步兵师，其组成旅分别改名为第298、301和304近卫步兵团。除了这些核心部队外，该师还拥有两个炮兵团和其他辅助单位，包括通信部队。<cr>1944年6月，该师被派往卡累利阿方面军参加旨在清除芬兰军队的行动。攻击于1944年6月21日开始，第100近卫步兵师在斯维尔河上进行了强渡。经过三天激烈的进攻后，突破了芬军防御，并完全解放了列宁格勒州。

进攻不久后重新开始，必须通过之前曼纳海姆防线的位置，该防线在1941年至1944年间得到了加强。遭受重大伤亡后，师向北推进，并于1944年7月1日抵达维迪利察河岸。<cr><cr>一天之后，该师强渡河流并继续进攻。然而，在三天后被另一条河和广泛的防御工事所阻挡。<cr><cr>经过又一次强行军渡河和激烈战斗后，进攻于1944年7月14日停止，师采取了防守态势直到8月中旬。<cr><cr>整个行动持续了40天，师从列宁格勒周边的初始位置推进超过200公里。强渡斯维里河之后，该单位后来以这条河流命名。

1944年8月，该师被调往加里宁并改名为第100近卫斯维里空降师。几个月后又被重新命名为第100近卫斯维里步兵师。在得到增援和新指挥官伊万·亚历山德罗维奇·马卡连科少将之后，该师于1945年1月被运往匈牙利，并编入了第9近卫集团军的第39近卫步兵军。

从二月中旬开始，该师成为苏联预备部队的一部分，在德国“春季觉醒”行动期间位于巴拉顿湖以东地区。在此次行动中，第6装甲集团军试图突破苏军防线。1945年3月16日，国防军的进攻被阻止，并立即发起了对维也纳的攻势。第100师的任务是“肃清”包围圈内德军残部。1945年4月2日，该师开始向维也纳推进。五天后，部队抵达距维也纳不远处的位置，此时维也纳已变成由党卫军装甲军、临时训练单位和防空单位守卫的堡垒。

该行动旨在夺取维也纳，于1945年4月7日开始。师占领了城市的南部郊区，并向西执行了包围机动，绕过城市穿过维也纳森林，在市中心进行了激烈战斗，夺取了火车站和议会等关键目标，并强行渡过了多瑙河。经过五天的激烈城市战后，维也纳于1945年4月13日陷落。

到五月初，该师被投入到进攻布拉格的行动中，当时这座城市仍在德国国防军控制下。5月10日，它越过了捷克边境，遇到了从西边推进的美军部队。<cr>指挥官报告：<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The division first saw action in southern Russia with the 17th Army in 1941, where it fought at Uman and Kiev, and was involved in the sweep to Odessa. It opposed the Russian winter offensive of 1941-42, fought in the Battle of Kharkov (May 1942), in the encirclement and Battle of Staryyoskol, in the advance across the Don, in the drive to the Volga, and in the street fighting in Stalingrad(1942). It was with 6th Army when it was encircled in November 1942, and was destroyed when Stalingrad fell in January 1943.<cr>A second 100th Jger Division was created in the Belgrade area on April 17, 1943. That summer it was transferred to Albania and was rushed to the southern sector of the Eastern Front in March 1944. Here it joined the II SS Panzer Corps and helped rescue the 1st Panzer Army, which was encircled between the Bug and the Dnestr. It also took part in the Battles of Tarnopol and Brody and in the retreat to the Carpathians. Subsequently transferred to Army Group Centre, it took part in the withdrawal from Russia and the battles in southern Poland in the fall of 1944. It was fighting the Soviets in Silesia when the war ended and surrendered to the Red Army in May 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 该师于1941年首次在南部俄罗斯与第17集团军作战，参加了乌曼和基辅的战斗，并参与了向敖德萨推进的行动。它对抗了1941-1942年的俄冬季攻势，在哈尔科夫战役（1942年5月）中作战，在斯塔里奥斯科尔包围圈及战役中参战，跨越顿河进攻，驱逐至伏尔加河，并在1942年的斯大林格勒巷战中作战。它随第6集团军于1942年11月被围困，并在1943年1月斯大林格勒陷落后被消灭。<cr>第二支第100步兵师于1943年4月17日在贝尔格莱德地区成立。那年夏天，它被调往阿尔巴尼亚，并于1944年3月迅速部署到东线南部战区。在这里，它加入了II装甲军并帮助救援了在布格河和德涅斯特河之间的包围圈中的第1装甲集团军。它还参加了塔尔诺波尔战役、布鲁迪战役以及撤退至喀尔巴阡山脉的战斗。随后被调往中央集团军群，在1944年秋季从俄罗斯撤离及波兰南部的战斗中参战。该师在西里西亚与苏联军队作战，于1945年5月向红军投降。<cr>德国战斗序列 第二卷 291至999步兵师、命名步兵师和特殊部队在二战中的运用，萨缪尔·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text:
The 100th Rifle Division fought in the Winter War with Finland. When Operation Barbarossa began, it was part of 2nd Rifle Corps, with 2nd Rifle Corps immediately subordinate to Western Front. It became 1st Guards Rifle Division on 18 September 1941, one of the first Guards units, immediately after the Yelnya Offensive.

According to Poirer and Connor's Red Army Order of Battle of 1985, the division was recreated at Vologda in March 1942. Fought near Stalingrad, and in Ukraine and Belorussia. It was awarded the honorific 'Lviv' for its part in the capture of that city during July 1944. On 27 January 1945, the division liberated the Auschwitz-Birkenau Concentration Camp. During the Moravia-Ostrava Offensive, the division captured Ratibor and entered Czechoslovak territory. It then fought in the Prague Offensive. It was with 60th Army of the 4th Ukrainian Front in May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
第100步兵师参加了与芬兰的冬季战争。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师隶属于第2步兵军，而第2步兵军直接隶属于西方面军。该师于1941年9月18日改编为第1近卫步兵师，成为首批获得“近卫”称号的部队之一，这发生在叶连纳攻势之后。

根据Poirer和Connor在1985年的《红军战斗序列》中记载，该师于1942年3月在沃洛格达重建。曾在斯大林格勒附近作战，并参与了乌克兰和白俄罗斯地区的战斗。由于该师在1944年7月攻占利沃夫城中的表现，被授予“利沃夫”荣誉称号。1945年1月27日，该师解放了奥斯威辛-比克瑙集中营。在摩拉维亚-奥斯特拉发攻势中，该师占领了热舒夫，并进入了捷克斯洛伐克领土。随后参加了布拉格攻势。1945年5月隶属于第60集团军（第四乌克兰方面军）。<cr> <cr>

text: The 101st fought in the drive across the Ukraine and southern Russia in 1941 (including the battles of Uman, Kiev and Kharkov), and in the winter battles of 1941-42. In 194243, it took part in the Second Battle of Kharkov (also called Izyum), in the capture of Rostov, in the Caucasus campaign, and the retreat into the Kuban, during which it suffered heavy casualties, fighting off partisans and regular Soviet troops. Evacuated across the Kerch Straits, it was transported through the Crimea to the lower Dnieper in the latter part of 1943, where it fought at Nikolajew and Vinniza.<cr>In March 1944, it was surrounded with the 1st Panzer Army and formed the rear guard of the XXXXVI Panzer Corps in the subsequent breakout. Cited for its conduct in the retreat across the northern Ukraine, the 101st Jger fought in the Carpathians and was withdrawn to Slovakia in the fall of 1944. Sent south in early 1945, it fought in the retreats through Hungary and into Austria. It ended the war at battle group strength on the southern sector of the Eastern Front, but managed to surrender to the Americans in the Nesselbach/Rosenberg sector of the Sudetenland.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第101猎兵师参加了1941年在乌克兰和南部俄罗斯的攻势（包括乌曼、基辅和哈尔科夫战役），以及1941-42年的冬季战斗。1942年至1943年间，它参与了第二次哈尔科夫战役（又称伊久姆）、罗斯托夫的占领、高加索战役，并在库班地区撤退期间遭受重大伤亡，击退了游击队和正规苏联部队。通过刻赤海峡撤离后，该师被运送到克里米亚，在1943年下半年抵达第聂伯河下游地区，参加了尼古拉耶夫和文尼察的战斗。<cr>1944年3月，它与第一装甲集团军一起被包围，并在随后的突围中成为第四十六装甲军的后卫。因在北部乌克兰撤退中的表现而受到表彰，第101猎兵师参加了喀尔巴阡山脉的战斗，并于1944年秋季撤至斯洛伐克。<cr>1945年初被派往南部作战，在匈牙利和奥地利境内撤退期间参战。该师在东线南段以战斗群规模结束战争，但最终在美国控制的内塞尔巴赫/罗森贝格地区的苏台德地区投降。<cr>德国战斗序列 第二卷 291至999步兵师、命名步兵师及特种部队（二战中的步兵师和特殊部队），作者：萨缪尔·W·米奇姆少校

The 101st Tank Division was sent to Western Front's Operations Group Rokossovskii on 17 July, immediately after forming with '80 old tanks' and 7 KV's. By early September it had lost enough of its armor that it was redesignated 101st Mechanized Division. As a mechanized division, with only a single battalion of about 30 light tanks, it was part of Group Boldin in Western Front by late September. In early October it was surrounded and destroyed in the Vyazma pocket.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: The 102nd Infantry Division was part of Army Group Center and fought at Smolensk, Vyazma, and Rzhev. In December it suffered heavy losses in the vicinity of Moscow during the Russian winter offensive of 1941-42. The next month the 102nd was encircled south of Lake Volga with the XXIII Corps, but was later rescued by the 9th Army. In February 1942 it was withdrawn to Germany to rest and refit. While there, the 235th Infantry Regiment was dissolved, and the 84th Infantry Regiment of the 8th Infantry Division was assigned to replace it. Returning to the central sector of the Russian Front in April 1942, the division took part in the Rzhev withdrawal and later fought in the battles of Kursk and Gomel.<cr>By October it was at battle group strength. The 102nd absorbed the remnants of the 216th Infantry Division, which had been shattered at Kursk. Its TOE (Table of Organization and Equipment) now included the 84th and 232nd Grenadier Regiments (two battalions each), Division Group 216 (with the 348th and 396th Regimental Groups), the 102nd Fusilier Battalion, and the normal divisional troops. (The 233rd Grenadier Regiment and the II/104th Artillery Regiment had meanwhile been disbanded.) Back at the front in January 1944, the 102nd Infantry Division was assigned to the 2nd Army and was sent to the Pripjet (Pripyet) marshes sector. It thus escaped the disaster that overtook most of Army Group Center in June and July 1944. The 102nd, meanwhile, fought at Brest-Litovsk and Navel. By February 1945, it was in the East Prussian Pocket and surrendered at Hela as the Third Reich passed into history.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第102步兵师隶属于中央集团军群，参加了斯摩棱斯克、维亚兹马和热季夫的战斗。1941-42年冬季攻势期间，该师在莫斯科附近遭受了重大损失。次月，它与第XXIII军一起被包围在伏尔加湖以南地区，但后来由第9集团军解救出来。1942年2月，该师撤至德国休整和整补。在此期间，解散了第235步兵团，并将第8步兵师的第84步兵团调来替换它。1942年4月返回俄罗斯前线中部地区后，该师参与了热季夫的撤离行动，并在库尔斯克战役和戈梅尔战斗中作战。<cr>到10月份，该师已恢复为战斗群规模。它吸收了第216步兵师的残部（后者已在库尔斯克被击溃）。其编制表现在包括第84掷弹兵团（每团两个营）和第232掷弹兵团、第216师团（含第348团群和第396团群）、第102轻步兵营以及通常的师属部队。（在此期间，解散了第233掷弹兵团和第II/104炮兵团。）<cr>1944年1月重返前线后，该师被分配给第2集团军，并部署到普里皮亚季沼泽地区。因此它避免了中央集团军群在1944年6月至7月期间遭遇的大部分灾难。<cr>与此同时，该师参加了别列津纳和内夫尔的战斗。到了1945年2月，它陷入东波美拉尼亚包围圈，并于赫拉投降，随着第三帝国覆灭而结束其历史使命。

text:
On 22 June 1941, the 102nd Rifle Division was stationed in Kremenchug. It was ordered on June 28 to march to Chernigov. On 1 August 1941, BSSA lists the division as part of the 67th Rifle Corps, 21st Army, part of the Bryansk Front. In August, the division was surrounded and destroyed in the Gomel area.

The division was recreated at Chimkent in the Central Asia Military District in January 1942. James Goff writes that the new division was reformed from the briefly active 462nd Rifle Division, which was only active from 22 December 1941 to 1 February 1942 before being redesignated the 102nd Rifle Division (Second Formation).

The division was again reformed from Far East NKVD Division at Khabarovsk in June 1942 and joined the 70th Army. It fought at the Battle of Kursk, Operation Kutuzov, Operation Bagration, the East Prussian Offensive, and the East Pomeranian Offensives. It was with the 48th Army of the 3rd Belorussian Front in May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
1941年6月22日，第102步兵师驻扎在克雷门奇格。该师于6月28日接到命令前往切尔尼戈夫。1941年8月1日，苏军总参谋部将该师列为第67步兵军、第21集团军的一部分，隶属于布良斯克方面军。同年八月，该师在戈梅利地区被包围并被消灭。

1942年1月，该师在中亚军区的钦察重建。詹姆斯·戈夫写道，新组建的步兵师是由短暂活跃的第462步兵师重组而成，后者仅于1941年12月22日至1942年2月1日期间存在，并随后被重新指定为第102步兵师（第二次编成）。

该师再次在1942年6月从远东内务人民委员部的一个师在哈巴罗夫斯克重建，并加入第70集团军。它参加了库尔斯克会战、库图佐夫行动、巴格拉季昂行动、东普鲁士进攻和东波美拉尼亚进攻。1945年5月，该师隶属于第三白俄罗斯方面军的第48集团军。<cr><cr>指挥官报告1941年6月22日，第102步兵师驻扎在克雷门奇格。该师于6月28日接到命令前往切尔尼戈夫。同年八月，在戈梅利地区被包围并被消灭。<cr>1942年1月，该师在中亚军区的钦察重建，并再次由远东内务人民委员部的一个师在哈巴罗夫斯克重组。它参加了库尔斯克会战、库图佐夫行动、巴格拉季昂行动、东普鲁士进攻和东波美拉尼亚进攻。<cr>1945年5月，该师隶属于第三白俄罗斯方面军的第48集团军。<cr><cr>

When 102nd Tank Division was assigned to 24th Army in late July, it actually had some modern tanks - a single company with 8 KV's, in addition to its 100 BT-7 light tanks. By late August, at the battle for Yelnya, the two tank regiments had been combined into a single unit: 102nd Tank Battalion, and the 102nd Howitzer Regiment was split off to become a separate regiment. As a result, by September the division, effectively a single understrength rifle regiment, was reformed as 144th Tank Brigade.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: The 103rd Guards Rifle Division was formed from the 13th Guards Airborne Divison on 18 December 1944 in Bykhaw. The 3rd Guards Airborne Brigade became the 317th Guards Rifle Regiment, the 5th Guards Airborne Brigade became the 322nd Guards Rifle Regiment and the remaining rifle units became the 324th Guards Rifle Regiment. The division became part of the 37th Guards Rifle Corps and in February were embarked on trains and moved to positions south of Budapest. Between 16 March and 1 April, the division advanced along Lake Balaton after participating in the repulse of Operation Spring Awakening. On 23 March, the division helped capture Veszprem, on 26 March Devecser, on 28 March Sarvar and finally Szombathely on 29 March. On 2 April, the division captured Gloggnitz and then fought in Vienna. After the capture of Vienna in the Vienna Offensive, the division advanced westward, pursuing retreating German units.<cr><cr>

The 103rd Mechanized Division was formed in March 1941 at Voroshilovgrad in the North Caucasus Military District as part of 26th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>

Formed in an interior Military District, this division, like the entire 26th Mechanized Corps, had a very low priority for personnel and equipment in early 1941. There is no indication that the 103rd ever had any tanks assigned, and the entire corps was so lacking in mobility that it was left behind when 19th Army mobilized from the District in May 1941. 103rd Mechanized Division went into battle with 24th Army in mid-July. During August all the tanks in the division were organized into 103rd Tank Battalion, which by the end of the month had just 15 light tanks left. In September 1941 the division was reformed as 103rd Rifle Division by adding the 688th (Reserve) Rifle Regiment.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: On 18 December 1944, the 12th Guards Airborne Division became the 105th Guards Rifle Division in Maryina Horka. On 5 January 1945, it was assigned to the 38th Guards Rifle Corps. From 21 January to 20 February, it was transported to Szolnok, where the corps became part of the 9th Guards Army. On 30 March, the division crossed the Raba. The division advanced into Austria and captured Pressbaum on 6 April. During the Vienna Offensive, the 105th Guards blocked the Vienna-Linz road, cutting Vienna off from German reinforcements and allowing other Soviet troops to capture the city. Along with other units, the division caused severe losses among the 3rd SS Panzer Division Totenkopf, the 2nd SS Panzer Division Das Reich, and the Hungarian 2nd Armored Division and 9th Infantry Division of the 3rd Army. On 26 April, the division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner. On 5 May, the division marched into Czechoslovakia and captured Znojmo on 9 May. On 12 May, the division met American troops on the Vltava near the village of Tsisek.<cr><cr>

text: The division went to Russia with Army Group Center in 1941, fought at Vilna, Smolensk, Vyazma and Klin, and suffered heavy casualties in the final thrusts toward Moscow and in the subsequent Soviet counteroffensive that winter. In January 1942 the divisions infantry strength was down to 500 men, and it had hardly any of its original leaders left. Sent to St. Omer in northern France to rest and rebuild that spring, it did not return to the Eastern Front until the spring of 1943. The 106th fought in the Battle of Kharkov in May 1943, and in the Krementschug and Kirovograd fighting in the second half of that year. The 106th Infantry had been reduced to Kampfgruppe (battle group) strength by October. It was rebuilt in November 1943 and now included the 239th and 240th Grenadier Regiments (each with two battalions) and Division Group 39 (with Regimental Groups 113 and 114). It also added the 107th Field Replacement Battalion. Still understrength, it absorbed the infantry of Shadow Division Milowitz at the end of February 1944. Meanwhile, the division took part in the withdrawal behind the Dniepr(January-March 1944) and the successful defense of Pruth, Romania in April. Caught up in the disaster that befell 6th Army in the autumn of 1944, the 106th was encircled and destroyed at Kishinev, Romania, in August 1944.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

The 106th was supposed to be formed as a Tank Division in mid-July 1941, but lack of tanks caused it to be organized with only one tank regiment and two motorized rifle regiments. This meant that, as a mechanized division, it had the same number as a rifle division already fighting in the Crimea. Within less than a month after it entered combat, the unit was redesignated as 106th Rifle Division - which meant that there were then two 106th Rifle Divisions in the Soviet army on different parts of the front at the same time! This not only confused German intelligence but, because the 106th (Mech) Rifle Division was wiped out in October 1941 in the Vyazma pocket, means that almost nothing is known about the strength and composition of this unit.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text:
The 109th Mechanized Division was formed from 109th Rifle Division in January 1940 in Transbaikal Military District with:<cr>
381st Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
602nd Motorized RifleRegiment (from 82nd Motorized Rifle Division)
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
16th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - each 52 BT tanks
404th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
Reconnaissance Battalion
Antitank Battalion
Antiaircraft Battalion
Sapper Battalion<cr><cr>One of the first mechanized divisions formed, the 109th was at full strength with 275 light tanks by July 1940 when it became part of 5th Mechanized Corps. The division was stationed at Chita in Transbaikal until late May 1941, when it began moving west by rail. On 18 June, just days before the war with Germany started, the first division elements, were arriving at Berdichev and Proskurov in the western Ukraine. Because most of 5th mechanized Corps' other elements were diverted to the Western Front area after the war started, 109th Mechanized Division was the only division under the Corps HQ in its first battle at Ostrog on 26 June.<cr>Because of the splitting of 5th Mechanized Corps, 109th Mechanized Division actually fought as part of the improvisied 'Group Lukin' (named after the 16th Army commander) and, after 2 July, as part of 5th Army. Having fought without much support against the spearheads of 1st Panzer group for most of two weeks, by early July the division was virtually without tanks or motorization.<cr>On 12 July 1941 the 109th Mechanized Division was withdrawn into Southwestern Front reserves. In the next few days, it was converted into the 307th Rifle Division by adding the 807th (Reserve) Rifle Regiment and redesignating or disbanding the motorized elements of the division.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

作为最早组建的机械化军之一，第109机械化军在1940年7月拥有275辆轻型坦克时达到满编，并成为第5机械化军的一部分。该军驻扎在赤塔直到1941年5月下旬才开始向西移动。6月18日，在德国战争爆发前几天，第一支抵达乌克兰西部伯迪切夫和普斯科罗夫的部队已经到达。

由于第5机械化军其他部分被调往西方战区，第109机械化军成为其首次在奥斯特罗格战役（6月26日）中唯一参战的师。<cr>

由于第5机械化军被拆分，第109机械化军实际上作为临时组建的“卢金集团”（以第16集团军指挥官命名）的一部分作战，并从7月2日起成为第5集团军的一部分。在与德军第1装甲集群尖刀部队对抗两周后，该师到7月初几乎已经没有坦克或摩托化装备了。<cr>

1941年7月12日，第109机械化军被撤出西南方面军预备队，并在接下来的几天内重组为第307步兵师，通过增加第807（预备）步兵团并重新指定或解散该师中的摩托化部队实现。<cr><cr>苏联战斗序列 第一卷 作者：查尔斯·C·肖普

text: The 109th Rifle Division was a Red Army infantry division that was formed three times, briefly in 1939, during 1942, and again from 1942-45. The first formation of the division was converted to a mechanized division after about nine months. Its second formation served for six months in 1942 in the defense of the fortress of Sevastopol, in the southern sector of the siege lines. After being destroyed there in July, a third division was formed by re-designating an existing rifle division near Leningrad in August, and it successfully held its positions for nearly a year and a half, in spite of shortages of food and supplies due to the German/Finnish siege. The 109th then participated in the offensive that drove the Germans away from the city in early 1944, helped drive Finland out of the war, and then joined the offensive along the Baltic coast towards Germany. This third formation compiled an admirable record of service, but was disbanded in 1946.<cr><cr>
translation: 第109步兵师是红军的一个步兵师，曾三次组建：第一次是在1939年短暂成立，第二次在1942年，第三次则从1942年至1945年。该师的第一个编制在大约九个月后被改编为机械化师。其第二个编制于1942年在塞瓦斯托波尔要塞的南部围攻线上服役六个月，在防御中发挥作用。7月被消灭后，同年8月重新指定位于列宁格勒附近的一个步兵师作为第三个编制，并成功坚守阵地近一年半时间，尽管由于德军和芬兰军队的包围导致食物和补给短缺。109步兵师随后参加了在1944年初将德国人从城市驱逐出去的进攻行动，帮助迫使芬兰退出战争，并加入沿波罗的海海岸向德国推进的攻势。第三个编制表现优异，但在1946年被解散。<cr>指挥官报告：<cr>第109步兵师在第二次组建时参加了塞瓦斯托波尔要塞的防御，在第三次组建时成功坚守阵地，并参与了驱逐德军和芬兰军队的行动。

text:
The 109th Tank Division was formed July 1941 in Amur district of Far Eastern Front with:<cr>
217th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Tank Bns - each 32 tanks
218th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Tank Bns - each 32 tanks
109th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Bns
109th Howitzer Regiment
1st, 2nd Bns<cr>
By the time 109th Tank Division arrived at the front at the end of July, it was just too late to be caught in the battles around Smolensk. As a result it was one of the original units used to form 43rd Army in Reserve Front in August, and in September, still in 43rd Army, was redesignated as 148th Tank Brigade.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: On 22 June 1941, at the onset of Operation Barbarossa, the 10th Army was part of the Soviet Western Front. It consisted of the 1st Rifle Corps (2nd and 8th Rifle Divisions); 5th Rifle Corps (including 13th, 86th, and 113th Rifle Divisions); 6th Cavalry Corps (6th and 36th Cavalry Divisions) and 6th and 13th Mechanised Corps, under General K.D. Golubev. It was encircled by German forces in June 1941 and largely destroyed.<cr>By late June, the German Army Group Centre surrounded the 3rd, 4th and the 10th Armies in the Battle of Bia?ystok-Minsk. In the end, all the formations and units of the 10th Army were defeated. On 30 June, while trying to cross the highway Minsk-Baranovichi, the army headquarters was destroyed, coming out of the remnants of the environment were addressed by fitting of the 4th Army. The headquarters was officially disbanded on 5 July 1941. The commander of the 10th Army, Major General KD Golubev, and the army artillery commander, Major General M. Barsukov, escaping from the encirclement in a consolidated group with the August 86th Border Detachment of the NKVD, in late July Golubev was appointed commander of 13th Army, which participated in the Battle of Smolensk.<cr>It was formed three times in 1941, next in October in the Southern Front, but its formation 'was halted due to severe battle conditions'.<cr>It was then reformed in November 1941 in the Volga region, with nine divisions, seven of which were new formations. Soviet official websites give the nine divisions as the 322nd, 323rd, 324th, 325th, 326th, 328th and 330th Rifle, and 57th & 75th Cavalry, thus including two cavalry divisions. Nine of these divisions had been formed in the space of three weeks from the reserve of the Moscow Military District and been trained for 12 hours a day. General Lieutenant Filipp Golikov took command. Golikov's 1967 book describes how the army finished its concentration in the Penza area on 8 November 1941, after which 15 days were devoted to combat training and 5 days to construction of living quarters and other facilities. There were shortages of everything including warm winter clothing. The majority of the troops were between 30 and 40 years of age and, in some cases, up to 65% of the men had no military training. Initially part of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (Stavka Reserve), it was reassigned to the Western Front for the Battle of Moscow, after moving up to Ryazan attacking on the morning of 6 December 1941. In 1942, it continued its defensive operations on the central axis, and in 1943 took part in the second Battle of Smolensk.<cr>The 10th Army headquarters with associated units was withdrawn from the Western Front to the Stavka Reserve in early April (General Staff's directive of 7.04.44). From 10 April, it was moved to Roslavl, where it was to take control of the 81st and 103rd Rifle Corps (total 5 divisions). That same month, the army was disbanded and its headquarters formed the basis of Headquarters 2nd Belorussian Front while its formations were reassigned to the 49th Army.<cr><cr>
translation:
1941年6月22日，巴巴罗萨行动开始时，第10集团军是苏联西部方面军的一部分。它包括第1步兵军（第2和第8步兵师）；第5步兵军（包括第13、第86和第113步兵师）；第6骑兵军（第6和第36骑兵师）以及第6和第13机械化军，由K.D.戈卢别夫将军指挥。该集团军于1941年6月被德军包围并大部分被消灭。<cr>到六月底，德军中央集团军群在比亚韦斯托克-明斯克战役中包围了第3、第4和第10集团军。最终，第10集团军的所有部队都被击败。6月30日，在试图穿越明斯克-巴罗夫希齐公路时，该集团军司令部被摧毁，幸存者由第4集团军接替指挥。该集团军司令部于1941年7月5日正式解散。<cr>第10集团军的指挥官K.D.戈卢别夫少将和炮兵指挥官M.巴苏科夫少将在86边防部队（内务人民委员部）的协助下，从包围圈中逃脱，并于7月底被任命为参与斯摩棱斯克战役的第13集团军指挥官。<cr>该集团军在1941年共组建了三次，下次是在十月，在南部方面军，但其组建因恶劣的战斗条件而停止。它于1941年11月在伏尔加河地区重建，下辖九个师，其中七个是新组建的。苏联官方网站列出这九个师为第322、323、324、325、326、328和330步兵师以及第57和75骑兵师，其中包括两个骑兵师。这些师在莫斯科军区预备队中仅用三周时间组建，并每天训练12小时。菲利普·戈里科夫少将接任指挥官。根据戈里科夫1967年的著作描述，该集团军于1941年11月8日在彭塔集中完毕，在接下来的15天中进行战斗训练，并在随后的五天内修建生活设施和其他设施。物资短缺严重，包括冬季保暖衣物不足。大多数士兵年龄在30至40岁之间，有些情况下多达65%的人没有军事训练经验。最初作为最高统帅部预备队的一部分（Stavka 预备队），它被重新分配给西方方面军参加莫斯科战役，并于1941年12月6日早晨从梁赞发起进攻。在1942年，该集团军继续在其中央轴线进行防御作战，在1943年参加了第二次斯摩棱斯克战役。

<cr>第十集团军司令部及其相关单位于四月初（总参谋部的指令为1944年4月7日）从西方方面军撤出并重新分配给最高统帅部预备队。自4月10日起，该集团军被转移到罗斯拉夫利，并将控制第81和103步兵军（共五个师）。同月，该集团军解散，其司令部成为第二白俄罗斯方面军司令部的基础，而其部队则重新分配给第四十九集团军。<cr><cr>

text: Part of North Caucasus Military District in June 1941, the division was disbanded on 1/21/42 and reformed from cadres of 12th Cavalry Division, 13th Cavalry Division, and 1st Krasnodor Militia Cavalry Division. It was assigned to XVII Cavalry Corps. It was disbanded once again 4/17/42 but not before being awarded the honorific 'Tersk-Stavropolsk'. <cr><cr>The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II: volume V - Book B Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Trafford, 2009 <cr><cr> Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert,The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 1941年6月隶属于北高加索军区，该师于1942年1月21日解散，并由第12骑兵师、第13骑兵师和第1克拉斯诺达尔民兵骑兵师的骨干重组。它被分配给第XVII骑兵军。然而，它在1942年4月17日再次解散之前获得了“特尔斯克-斯塔夫罗波尔斯基”的荣誉称号。<cr>第二次世界大战中军事战斗序列和组织：卷五-B书 苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟 特拉法坊，2009年<cr>罗伯特·普瓦里耶与阿尔伯特·康纳，《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》 普雷斯迪奥出版社，1985年<cr>词条由斯图尔特·金贡献

text: The 10th Guards Army was formed on 16 April 1943 from the 30th Army. When formed, the army was located southwest of Vyazma.<cr>It fought under command of the Western, Kalinin Front, 2nd Baltic, and Leningrad Fronts from then until the end of the war.<cr>The 10th Guards Army fought in the Battle of Smolensk, the Leningrad-Novgorod Offensive and the Riga Offensive.<cr>From October 1944, the 10th Guards Army was one of the Soviet formations committed to besieging German Army Group Courland in the Courland Peninsula. This was a lengthy operation that continued until the Germans in Courland surrendered on May 12, 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第10近卫集团军成立于1943年4月16日，由第30集团军改编而成。成立之初，该集团军位于维亚兹马西南方向。<cr>从那时起直到战争结束，它一直隶属于西方方面军、加里宁方面军、第二波罗的海方面军和列宁格勒方面军指挥。<cr>第10近卫集团军参加了斯摩棱斯克战役、列宁格勒-诺夫哥罗德攻势以及里加攻势。<cr>从1944年10月起，第10近卫集团军成为苏联部队中负责围困库尔兰半岛上的德国中央集团军群的部队之一。这一行动持续了很长时间，直到1945年5月12日德军在库尔兰投降。<cr>

text: Formed 8/27/42 from 13th 'Kuban Cossack' Cavalry Division, it was part of IV Guards Cavalry Corps. It fought in the Kuban in 1943, defended Taganrog through the summer and fought along the coast of the Black Sea into 1944. The division participated in the liberation of Odessa in April 1944, was part of the Belorussian Offensive in June-July, was part of the Budapest that winter. It ended the war in the Czech Republic. The division was awarded the honorific titles 'Baranovici' and 'Slutsk'. Soldiers from IV Guards Cavalry Corps occupied the village of Brnenec and liberated the prisoners working there in Oskar Schindler's factory; this group of Jewish prisoners were made famous in the movie Schindler's List,/i>. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该师成立于1942年8月27日，由第13“库班哥萨克”骑兵师改编，并隶属于第四近卫骑兵军。它于1943年在库班作战，在夏季保卫塔甘罗格，并沿黑海海岸战斗至1944年初。该师参与了1944年4月敖德萨的解放，参加了6月至7月的白俄罗斯攻势，冬季则参与了布达佩斯战役。战争结束时位于捷克斯洛伐克境内。该师获得了“巴兰诺维奇”和“斯卢茨克”的荣誉称号。第四近卫骑兵军的士兵占领了布伦内茨村，并解放了奥斯卡·辛德勒工厂中的囚犯；这些犹太囚犯在电影《辛德勒名单》中广为人知。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军战斗序列：伟大卫国战争，Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: On 25 October 1943 the 30th Uralsky Volunteer Tank Corps renamed the 10th Guards Uralsky Voluntary Tank Corps. The corps then fought in battles at Bryansk, Lower Silesia, Upper Silesia, Proskurovo-Kamenetc-Podolsk, Lvov-Sandomierz and during the Vistula-Oder, Berlin and Prague Offensives. On 16 March 1944, Major General Yevtikhy Belov became the corps commander. On 22 October 1944, Belov became deputy commander of the 4th Tank Army and Colonel Nil Chuprov replaced him in command. Chuprov was wounded on 10 February 1945 and replaced by Belov. The corps was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, the Order of Suvorov and the Order of Kutuzov. The 62nd Guards Perm-Keletcky Tank Brigade, which had earlier received an honorific named for Kielce, was in addition awarded the Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky for heroism shown in battle.<cr><cr>
translation: 1943年10月25日，第30乌拉尔志愿坦克军改名为第10近卫乌拉尔志愿坦克军。该军随后参加了布良斯克、下西里西亚、上西里西亚、普罗斯库罗夫-卡缅策-波多利斯基、利沃夫-桑多梅日战役以及维斯瓦河-奥得河、柏林和布拉格攻势。1944年3月16日，叶特基希·别洛夫少将接任军长职务。1944年10月22日，别洛夫被任命为第4坦克集团军副司令，尼尔·丘普罗夫上校接替他担任军长。丘普罗夫于1945年2月10日负伤，由别洛夫接任。该军获得红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫勋章和库图佐夫勋章。此前因基尔采而获荣誉称号的第62近卫佩姆-凯列茨克坦克旅，还因其在战斗中的英勇表现获得了博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基勋章。<cr>指挥官报告：别洛夫少将、丘普罗夫上校

text: The 10th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 10th Light Division. The Hungarian Government reluctantly agreed to support the Germans 1942 summer offensive Fall Blau and allocated the division as part of the Hungarian Second Army to the task. Each light division in the Second Army was reinforced with three battalions from sister divisions in Hungary but nonetheless each division was only slightly larger than half the size of its German counterparts. Second Army's role in the offensive was to guard the German northern flank on the Don River. During the Stalingrad Campaign the Second Army suffered over 60% casualties but was generally able to retreat in good order. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 10th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 10th Infantry Division. The division was one of the defenders of the Hungarian capital when In November 1944 the Russians commenced their 102 day Siege of Budapest. The division was disbanded in February of 1945 when the city surrendered.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第10匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括约9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖2个步兵团（每个团有3个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多兵力以支持东线作战，并且大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而其编制表基本保持不变。该旅更名为第10轻型师。匈牙利政府勉强同意在1942年夏季攻势（蓝色行动）中支援德国，将该师分配给匈牙利第二集团军的任务。每个轻型师都从匈牙利的兄弟部队得到3个营的增援，但即便如此，每个师仍然只有其德军同行的一半左右规模。在进攻期间，第二集团军负责保护顿河上德国北部侧翼的安全。在斯大林格勒战役中，该集团军伤亡超过60% c%，但仍能有组织地撤退。作为战后对匈牙利军队进行重组的一部分，在1944年11月苏联开始长达102天的布达佩斯围城战时，第10轻型师与其他部队合并并更名为第10步兵师。该师是保卫匈牙利首都部队之一。在1945年2月城市投降后，该师被解散。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr><cr>词条提供：Chris Munson<cr><cr>

text: The 10th Motorized Division invaded Russia with Army Group Centre on June 22 1941. The division crossed the Bug and fought at Bobruisk, Smolensk, the Dniepr crossings, Gomel, Kiev, Bryansk, and Tula, and in the Battle of Moscow and other important battles in 1941, suffering heavy casualties in the process.<cr>After the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42 was halted, the 10th Motorized remained on the central sector during the defensive actions of 1942 (mainly at Moshaisk, Juchnow and Spass Demjansk), and took part in the unsuccessful Kursk offensive of July 1943. Meanwhile, it was officially redesignated the 10th Panzer Grenadier Division on June 13, 1943, and received the 7th Panzer Battalion in October. Sent to the southern sector, the 10th suffered heavy losses in the Battle of Kiev in the fall of 1943. It also fought at Krementschug and in the retreat to the Dnieper. By January 1944, it had only 3,700 men and was defending ten miles of frontage. It retreated through the Ukraine and suffered such heavy losses in the Bessarabia (Romania) debacle in August 1944, that it had to be withdrawn for rest and reorganization. Later that year, it returned to the Eastern Front; now, however, it was only at battle group strength and had only three panzer grenadier and one motorized artillery battalion remaining. In late 1944 and early 1945, it fought at Krakau, Radom, in the retreat from the Vistula, at Goerlitz, and in Silesia. By now, however, the tanks of the 7th Panzer Battalion had been lost and had been replaced by assault guns; the 41st Panzer Grenadier Regiment had apparently been disbanded; and the 10th Panzer Artillery Regiment had only one battalion left. The division, however, continued to resist. It was forced to retreat into Moravia in April, and the remnants of the 10th Panzer Grenadier Division surrendered to the Soviets at Deutsch-Brod on May 10, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation:
第10摩托化师于1941年6月22日随中央集团军群入侵俄罗斯。该师穿越布格河，在鲍里索夫、斯摩棱斯克、第聂伯河渡口、戈梅利、基辅、布良斯克和图拉等地作战，并参加了1941年的莫斯科战役和其他重要战役，过程中伤亡惨重。<cr>在苏联于1941-1942年冬季的攻势被阻止后，第10摩托化师继续留在1942年的防御行动中的中央战区（主要是在莫谢伊斯基、尤赫诺夫和斯帕斯德梅扬斯克），并参加了1943年7月库尔斯克进攻中失败的一方。与此同时，该师于1943年6月13日被正式重新命名为第10装甲掷弹兵师，并在同年10月接收了第7装甲营。随后被派往南部战区，在1943年秋季的基辅助攻中遭受了重大损失。它还参加了克雷门楚格的战斗以及撤退至第聂伯河的行动。到1944年1月，该师只剩下3,700人，并在长达十英里的战线上进行防御。它通过乌克兰撤退，在1944年8月罗马尼亚的比萨拉比亚灾难中遭受了如此严重的损失，以至于不得不被调离休整和重组。同年晚些时候，它重返东线战场；然而此时，该师仅剩战斗群规模，并且只剩下三个装甲掷弹兵营和一个摩托化炮兵团。

在1944年末和1945年初，第10装甲掷弹兵师参加了克拉科夫、拉多姆的战斗，在撤退至维斯瓦河时作战，并参与了戈尔利茨和西里西亚的战斗。此时，第7装甲营的坦克已经损失并被突击炮所取代；第41装甲掷弹兵团似乎已被解散；而第10装甲炮兵师仅剩下一个团。

尽管如此，该师继续抵抗。它被迫在1945年4月撤退至摩拉维亚，并于同年5月10日在德意志布罗德向苏联投降。<cr> 德国战斗序列 第三卷 - 二战中的装甲、装甲掷弹兵和武装党卫军师 <cr> Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text: The 10th Panzer was sent to Russia in June 1941, and fought in the battles of the Minsk Pocket, Smolensk, Vyazma (Vjasma), and the Battle of Moscow. It was heavily engaged against the Russian winter offensive of 1941-42 and held Juchnow (near Rzhev) against repeated attacks. The division suffered such heavy losses that it was sent to the Amiens area of France in May 1942, to rest and rebuild. It never fought again in the east.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第10装甲师于1941年6月被派往俄罗斯，参加了明斯克包围圈、斯摩棱斯克、维亚兹马（Vjasma）以及莫斯科战役。该师在1941-42年的苏联冬季攻势中遭受重创，并且多次击退了对朱琴诺（里热夫附近）的进攻。由于损失惨重，第10装甲师于1942年5月被调往法国亚眠地区休整和重建。它再也没有在东线作战过。<cr>德国战斗序列 第三卷 - 二战中的德军装甲、装甲掷弹兵及武装党卫军师<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text: At the outbreak of hostilities, the corps was stationed in Lithuania as part of the Baltic Military District. It originally consisted of the 10th, 8th and 90th Rifle Divisions, and on June 26th, the 22nd NKVD Motor Rifle Division was added to the corps. It fought in Riga in early July and was destroyed near Talinn in August 1941. It was reformed in October 1942 as part of the North Caucasus Front and consisted of the 43rd, 59th, and 106th Rifle Brigades. It fought as part of the 51st Army in south Ukraine and Crimea in 1944. It was part of the reconquest of LIthuania in October 1944 and fought in the Battle of Memel.<cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 在敌对行动爆发时，该军驻扎在立陶宛的波罗的海军区。它最初由第10步兵师、第8步兵师和第90步兵师组成，在6月26日增加了第22内务人民委员部机械化步兵师。7月初，它参加了里加战役，并于1941年8月在塔林附近被消灭。该军于1942年10月作为北高加索方面军的一部分重建，由第43、59和106步兵旅组成。1944年，它作为第51集团军的一部分参加了乌克兰南部和克里米亚的战斗，并参与了1944年10月收复立陶宛的战役以及梅梅尔战役。<cr><cr>Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert, 《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，Presidio Press，1985<cr><cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 10th Rifle Division was formally created in June 1922. The division seems to have been deactivated at some point after 1922 but was reactivated in September 1939 and participated in the Soviet invasion of Poland and the Soviet occupation of the Baltic States. At the start of Operation Barbarossa the division was part of the 8th Army on the border with East Prussia. From April 1942 to December 1944 the division was engaged in the Siege of Leningrad. From June to August 1944 it took part in the Vyborg-Petrozavodsk Offensive as part of 115th Rifle Corps.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第10步兵师于1922年6月正式成立。该师似乎在1922年后某个时期被解散，但在1939年9月重新组建，并参加了苏联入侵波兰和占领波罗的海国家的行动。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师隶属于与东普鲁士接壤的第8集团军。<cr>指挥官报告：从1942年4月至1944年12月，该师参与了列宁格勒围城战；1944年6月至8月期间，作为第115步兵军的一部分，参加了维堡-彼得罗扎沃茨克攻势。<cr>本文由Chris Munson提供

text: The 10th Romanian Infantry Division was attached to the Romanian II Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. It was one of a handful of Romanian units not withdrawn to Romania after the Siege of Odessa and was assigned to garrison duties. Over the next two years it was assigned to various Romanian and German Corps. It was not part of the Battle of Stalingrad but was serving in the Crimea as part of Army Group A.<cr><cr>John Ellis, World War II A Statistical Survey<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第10罗马尼亚步兵师在巴巴罗萨行动开始时隶属于罗马尼亚第二军。它是少数几个没有在敖德萨围城战后撤回罗马尼亚的罗马尼亚部队之一，并被分配守备任务。接下来的两年里，它先后被分配到不同的罗马尼亚和德国军中。虽然它并未参与斯大林格勒战役，但作为A集团军群的一部分，在克里米亚服役。<cr>资料来源：John Ellis, 《第二次世界大战统计调查》<cr><cr>词条由Chris Munson提供<cr><cr>

text:
The 10th Tank Corps was formed April - May 1942 in the Moscow Military District.<cr>The 10th Tank Corps went to Western Front reserves in late May, and remained
in Western Front or 16th Army of Western Front until September. In the early winter the corps was withdrawn from Western Front and in January 1943 sent south and assigned to Southwestern Front. 10th Tank Corps was part of the Front Mobile Group 'Popov' which was cut off and almost annihilated by Manstein's counter-attack in February 1943. The remnants of the corps were withdrawn into STAVKA Reserves in March 1943. Between March and July 1943 the corps was extensively reformed and re-equipped as part of 66th Army (later 5th Guards Army). When 4th Panzer Army attacked the southern face of the Kursk salient on 5 July, 10th Tank Corps was one of the first reserve units to react to the attack.<cr>The 10th Tank Corps took part in the battles around Kharkov in August and then the advance to the Dnepr River and across it during the fall and early winter of 1943. During these months the Corps was reinforced with 390th Antitank Battalion (12 85mm towed guns) . In November 1943 the 10th Tank Corps went into STAVKA Reserves, it remained in reserves, in the Kiev or Moscow Military Districts, until 21 September 1944. While in reserve, the corps underwent considerable organizational changes. By 21 September 1944 when the corps was committed with the Baltic Fronts in the offensive to liberate Latvia and Lithuania and take Riga.<cr>After fighting through the autumn in the Baltic, 10th Tank Corps was assigned to 5th Guards Tank Army on 20 December, with only 63 tanks and SUs left. In the same month, 326th Guards SU Regiment left the corps and was replaced, first by 1207th SU Regiment, and then, from February 1945 on, by 381st Guards Heavy SU Regiment (ISU-122s) . Both SU regiments were in the corps when the East Prussia Operation started on 14 January, the corps had 117 tanks and 84 SUs -full strength in the self-propelled artillery. By the time 10th Tank Corps reached the Baltic coast with 5th Guards Tank Army on 26 January, just 64 armored vehicles were left running in the corps. After another month of fighting, 10th Tank Corps was removed from 5th Guards Tank Army on 1 March and went into STAVKA Reserves for the rest of the war in Europe.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第10坦克军于1942年4月至5月在莫斯科军区组建。该坦克军于5月下旬进入西方面军预备队，并一直留在西方面军或其下属的第16集团军，直到9月。初冬时分，该坦克军从西方面军撤出，并于1943年1月被调往西南方面军。第10坦克军是“波波夫”方面军机动部队的一部分，在1943年2月曼施坦因的反攻中几乎全军覆没。<cr><cr>该坦克军残部在1943年3月撤入最高统帅部预备队。从1943年3月至7月，该坦克军作为第66集团军（后为第5近卫集团军）的一部分进行了大规模重组和重新装备。当第4装甲集团军于1943年7月5日对库尔斯克突出部南翼发动攻击时，第10坦克军是最早作出反应的预备部队之一。<cr><cr>该坦克军参加了1943年8月哈尔科夫周围的战斗，并在秋季和初冬期间参与了向第聂伯河推进并渡过该河的行动。在此期间，该军得到了第390反坦克营（配备12门85毫米牵引炮）的增援。<cr><cr>1943年11月，第10坦克军进入最高统帅部预备队，并一直留在基辅或莫斯科军区的预备队中，直到1944年9月21日。在此期间，该军经历了相当大的组织变革。到1944年9月21日，该军被投入到波罗的海方面军发起的解放拉脱维亚和立陶宛并夺取里加的攻势中。<cr><cr>经过秋季在波罗的海地区的战斗，第10坦克军于12月20日被分配给第5近卫坦克集团军，此时该部队只剩下63辆坦克和SU。同月，第326近卫SU团离开该军，并先后由第1207SU团和从1945年2月起的第381近卫重型SU团（ISU-122）替换。当东普鲁士行动于1月14日开始时，两个SU团都在该军中，该军拥有117辆坦克和84辆SU——自行火炮满编。到1月26日第5近卫坦克集团军与第10坦克军到达波罗的海沿岸时，该军只剩下64辆装甲车辆在运行。经过另一个月的战斗，第10坦克军于3月1日被移出第5近卫坦克集团军，并进入最高统帅部大本营预备队直到欧洲战争结束。<cr>苏联二战战斗序列 第二卷 作者：查尔斯·C·夏普

text:
The 10th Tank Division was formed July 1940 in Kiev Special Military District. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
19th Tank Regiment
20th Tank Regiment
10th Motorized Rifle Regiment
10th Reconnaissance Battalion
10th Motorized Pontoon Battalion<cr>
10th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr>Originally, this division was part of 4th Mechanized Corps with 8th Tank Division. By 1 October, 10th Tank Division had almost 300 BT7 tanks and participated in the only corps-division manuevers held by any mechanized forces in the Soviet Army in 1940-41. In February 1941 10th Tank Division was assigned to the 15th Mechanized Corps, then forming in the western Ukraine.<cr>In the spring of 1941 the division started receiving modern tanks. By 22 June it had 63 KVs (100% of authorized), 38 T-34s, 51 T-28s, 181 BT-7s, 22 T- 26s, 8 OT-26s, and 56 BA-10 and 27 BA-20 armored cars. The division was also much better equipped with 'soft' vehicles than normal in the Red Army at this time. While overall units were short up to 80% of trucks and tractors authorized, 10th Tank Division had almost 80% of their authorized trucks. Another 382 trucks were supposed to be mobilized from the 'civilian economy' within 48 hours after war started, but in the event, never appeared. In personnel, the division was missing 25% of the technicians and non-commissioned officers required, but had 333 reservist sergeants assigned in May, 1941 for training to make up the lack.<cr>10th Tank Division fought under 15th Mechanized Corps HQ in the great tank battles of June and July 1941 in the Ukraine. In his after-action report, the division commander noted that the KV heavy tanks were almost impervious, even to 'direct hits by aerial bombs' BUT the division was so short of tractors and trained mechanics that most of its armor was lost to breakdown rather than enemy action. When 15th Mechanized Corps HQ was disbanded in August, 10th Tank Division became the mobile reserve for 40th Army south of Kiev.<cr>On 31 August the division reported that it had only 750 men and 14 tanks left. It was pulled into reserve in early September 1941, before it was caught in the Kiev encirclement. At Chuguev the cadre of 10th tank Division was used to form 133rd Tank Brigade.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第10坦克师于1940年7月在基辅特别军区组建。1941年6月22日，该师包括：
<cr>
第19坦克团
第20坦克团
第10摩托化步兵团
第10侦察营
第10机械化舟桥营
<cr>
第10防空营
<cr>最初，这个师是第四机械化军的一部分，与第八坦克师同属。到1941年10月1日，第十坦克师几乎拥有300辆BT-7快速坦克，并参加了苏联军队在1940年至1941年间唯一一次由机械化部队组织的军师级演习。<cr>1941年春天，该师开始接收新型坦克。到6月22日，它装备了63辆KV（占授权数量的100%）、38辆T-34、51辆T-28、181辆BT-7快速坦克、22辆T-26、8辆OT-26和56辆BA-10以及27辆BA-20装甲车。该师的“软”车辆装备也比当时红军平均水平要好得多。尽管总体上部队缺少授权数量高达80%的卡车和拖拉机，第十坦克师却拥有接近其授权数量80%的卡车。<cr>另外382辆卡车应在战争开始后48小时内从民用经济中动员起来，但最终并未出现。在人员方面，该师缺少所需技术人员和非士官军官的25%，但在1941年5月为训练而分配了333名预备役军士。<cr>第10坦克师于1941年6月和7月在乌克兰参加了大规模的坦克战役，当时隶属于第15机械化军司令部。师长在其战后报告中指出，KV重型坦克几乎坚不可摧，甚至直接遭受空袭炸弹的打击也不例外，但该师缺乏拖拉机和训练有素的技术人员，导致大部分装甲车辆因故障而非敌方行动而损失。当第15机械化军司令部于8月解散时，第10坦克师成为位于基辅以南第40集团军的机动预备队。<cr>8月31日该师报告称仅剩下750名士兵和14辆坦克。它在9月初被调入预备队，避免了基辅助围圈套。<cr>车臣部队在楚格乌夫利用第10坦克师的骨干力量组建了第133坦克旅。<cr>苏联战斗序列 第一卷查尔斯·C·夏普编著

text: The 110th Infantry Division was with Army Group Center in the initial attack on the Soviet Union and, after a number of desperate battles (including Vilna, Smolensk, Vyazma, and Klin), penetrated to the Volga in December 1941. Pushed back by the Russian winter offensive of 1941-42, it remained on the central sector of the Eastern Front for the rest of its existence. In 1942, the III/252nd Infantry Regiment and the I/254th Infantry Regiment were disbanded. After taking part in the defensive battles of 1942, where it suffered significant losses, it participated in the defense of Rzhev and the subsequent withdrawal from the Rzhev salient in March 1943. It suffered heavy losses at Bryansk in the summer of that year and the 252nd Grenadier Regiment had to be disbanded; the 321st Divisional Group, however, was attached to the 110th Infantry Division. Remaining in the line, it was destroyed near Bobruisk in the Russian summer offensive of 1944. The divisions last commander, Lieutenant General Eberhard Kurowski, was taken prisoner when the division was smashed.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第110步兵师在德国中央集团军群对苏联的初始攻击中参战，并在一系列激烈的战斗（包括维尔纽斯、斯摩棱斯克、维亚兹玛和基林）后，于1941年12月推进至伏尔加河。在1941-42年的俄罗斯冬季攻势下被击退后，它在整个存在期间都驻守在东线中央战区。1942年，第252步兵师团第三营和第254步兵师团第一营被解散。参与了1942年的防御战斗并遭受重大损失后，该师参加了列日的防御以及随后于1943年3月从列日突出部撤退。同年夏天在布良斯克遭受严重损失后，第252掷弹兵师团不得不被解散；然而，第321师属集团则被编入了第110步兵师。继续驻守前线，在1944年的俄罗斯夏季攻势中于鲍里斯哥夫附近被消灭。该师最后的指挥官、少将埃伯哈德·库罗夫斯基在师团被摧毁时成为战俘。<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷 1-290步兵师在二战中的表现，塞缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text:
The division was first formed 20 September 1939 at Sverdlovsk. Mobilized before the beginning of Operation Barbarossa, by June 1941 the division (first formation) formed part of the 61st Rifle Corps in the 20th Army, in the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (Stavka Reserve) around Moscow, the 20th Army occupying a defensive position around Kaluga. The division was destroyed with its corps during the Siege of Mogilev in July 1941. The division was officially disbanded on 19 September 1941.

On 4 September 1941, the 4th Moscow People's Militia Rifle Division, which had originally been raised in the Kuibyshev district of Moscow in July 1941, was renumbered as the new 110th Rifle Division, beginning its second formation. Its composition changed to the regular army subunits to include:

1287, 189, 1291 Rifle Regiments
971 Artillery Regiment
695 AA Artillery Battalion
470 Reconnaissance Company
859 Separate Signal Battalion
493 Medical Battalion
332 Separate Chemical Defence Company
329 Auto-transport Company<cr>
It was assigned as part of the 24th, 49th, 21st, and 33rd Armies, participating in the defensive and offensive operations around Moscow Operation Mars at the end of 1942 as part of the Red Army's Kalinin Front, and later in 1943 the Rzhev-Vyazma offensives, and the Orel offensive operation (Operation Kutuzov), after the Battle of Kursk. From the Rzhev battles to October 1944, the division was commanded by Major General Georgy Borisovich Peters, its former deputy commander.

On 10 April 1943, the 110th Rifle Division was renamed the 84th Guards Koracheyev Rifle Division.

The third formation of the division was on 5 May 1943, with the same unit numbers as the second formation. On 6 April 1945, commanded by Colonel Sergey Mikhailovich Tarasov, it participated in the encirclement of Konigsberg, located at the northern sector. In that assault, the division was accompanied by its two sister divisions of 69th Rifle Corps, 50th Army: the 153rd Rifle Division, on its right flank, and the 324th Rifle Division on its left flank.<cr><cr>
translation:
该师于1939年9月20日在斯维尔德洛夫斯克首次组建。在巴巴罗萨行动开始前动员，到1941年6月，第一个编成的该师成为第61步兵军下属单位，隶属于最高统帅部大本营预备队（大本营预备队），驻扎在莫斯科附近的卡卢加地区防御阵地内。该师及其所属军在1941年7月莫吉廖夫围城战中被消灭。该师于1941年9月19日正式解散。

1941年9月4日，第4莫斯科人民民兵步兵师（该师于1941年7月在莫斯科库比雪夫区组建）改番号为新成立的第110步兵师，开始第二次编成。其编制变更为包括正规军下属单位：

1287、189、1291 步兵团
971 炮兵团
695 高射炮兵营
470 侦察连
859 通信独立营
493 医疗营
332 化学防御独立连
329 汽车运输独立连<cr>

该师作为第24、第49、第21和第33集团军的一部分被部署，在1942年底莫斯科地区的火星行动中参与了防御和进攻作战，隶属于红军加里宁方面军。1943年，它参加了勒热夫-维亚兹马攻势以及奥廖尔攻势（库图佐夫行动）。在库尔斯克战役之后，从勒热夫的战斗到1944年10月，该师由少将乔治·鲍里索维奇·彼得斯指挥，他曾是该师的副指挥官。

1943年4月10日，第110步兵师改名为第84近卫科拉切耶夫步兵师。

该师的第三次编组是在1943年5月5日，与第二次编组时使用相同的单位编号。1945年4月6日，在上校谢尔盖·米哈伊洛维奇·塔拉索夫指挥下，它参加了对柯尼斯堡北部地区的包围行动。在这次突击中，该师得到了第69步兵军第50集团军中的两个兄弟单位的支援：右侧是第153步兵师，左侧是第324步兵师。<cr><cr><cr>

text: The 111th Infantry Division fought in the early campaigns of Army Group South in 1941, including Zhitomir, Kiev and the Donetz, and took part in the Caucasus campaign and subsequent withdrawal (1942-43), including both battles for Rostov.<cr>The 111th Infantry also fought in the Kuban campaign, including the Battle of Novorossiysk, where an ambitious Soviet amphibious landing was checked in fierce fighting. Later transferred to the Mius sector, it took heavy losses in the Battle of Taganrog and fought in the battles of the lower Dnieper, where it performed exceptionally well. Meanwhile, it was reorganized as a Type 44 division in late 1943. Sent to the Crimea in early 1944, it was trapped when the Russians overran the peninsula. The 117th Infantry Regiment managed to escape by sea with the 50th Infantry Division, but the rest of the 111th was lost when its transport ships failed to arrive. When Sevastopol fell Major General Erich Gruner tried to surrender the division but was executed by the Russians, along with many of his men.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第111步兵师参加了德国南方集团军群在1941年的早期战役，包括日托米尔、基辅和顿涅茨克地区，并参与了高加索战役及随后的撤退（1942-1943年），其中包括罗斯托夫两场战役。<cr>第111步兵师还参加了库班战役，包括诺沃罗西斯克之战，在这场激烈的战斗中，苏联雄心勃勃的两栖登陆行动被阻止了。后来转移到米乌斯地区，在塔甘罗格战役中遭受重大损失，并参与了第聂伯河下游地区的战斗，在那里表现出色。与此同时，该师在1943年底重组为44型师。1944年初被派往克里米亚，当苏联军队占领半岛时被困在那里。第117步兵团与第50步兵师一起乘船逃脱，但其余的第111师因运输船只未到达而损失殆尽。塞瓦斯托波尔陷落后，埃里希·格鲁纳少将试图向苏军投降，但他被苏联人处决了，他的许多部下也遭此厄运。<cr><cr>德国战斗序列 第1-290步兵师在二战中的表现，塞缪尔·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text: The headquarters of the 111th Rifle Corps was formed in early November 1943 under the command of Major General Boris Rozhdestvensky, who led it for the rest of the war, part of the 54th Army of the Volkhov Front. Corps troops, formed along with the headquarters, included the 551st Separate Communications Battalion and the 3907th Field Postal Station. Upon formation, it was assigned the 44th and 288th Rifle Divisions and the 53rd Rifle Brigade. The 53rd Rifle Brigade transferred to the 115th Rifle Corps in December. The corps fought in the Leningrad-Novgorod Offensive in January and February 1944, recapturing Chudovo, Shimsk, Soltsy, Dno, and Porkhov in cooperation with the 119th Rifle Corps.<cr>During January, the 288th went into front reserve and the 18th and 80th Rifle Divisions joined the corps. In late January, the corps advanced toward Chudovo against the German 21st Infantry Division, capturing the town with a three-pronged attack by the 44th Rifle Division and the 14th and 53rd Rifle Brigades. The 18th and 80th were transferred in February, while the 288th returned to the corps, which was joined by the 225th Rifle Division. The corps rejoined 54th Army on 11 February after the army headquarters was relocated to the left flank of the front. The Volkhov Front was disbanded by an order of 13 February and the corps and army transferred to the Leningrad Front . In conjunction with the 14th Guards Rifle Corps of the 1st Shock Army, the 111th attacked the town of Dno late on 23 February, but both corps were repulsed by German counterattacks. On the next day, a renewed assault by the 44th and 288th Divisions and attached 16th Tank Brigade of the 111th and a rifle division, brigade, and tank regiment of the 14th Guards took the town. The corps fought in the recapture of Porkhov on 26 February, then fought with the army in unsuccessful attempts to break the Panther Line. It would include the 44th, 225th, and 288th Divisions until July. The 54th Army transferred to the 3rd Baltic Front in April. The 393rd Field Vehicle Repair Base was formed by 1 June as a corps unit.<cr>From mid-to-late July, the corps fought in the Pskov-Ostrov Offensive. With the 67th Army, the corps fought near the Tiupe and Gauja Rivers, then in the Riga Offensive in September, during which it helped recapture Riga.<cr> After the Riga Offensive, the corps, with the 189th and 196th Divisions and the 14th Fortified Region, was made responsible for the defense of the eastern coast of the Parnu Bay and Riga Bay from Ranna in southern Estonia to Sildze?i in northern Latvia and garrisoning Parnu, Ainazi, Salacgriva, and other large settlements along the coastline by an order of 21 October. The corps and the 14th Fortified Region were headquartered at Parnu, while the 196th was at Ainai and the 189th at Kodara. While on garrison duty, the corps conducted combat training in preparation for participation in the blockade of the Courland Pocket.<cr>The corps planned for an operation to break through the German line between Rasas and the Abava river, defended by the 81st Infantry Division, from 25 April. On the night of 6-7 May, the German troops began withdrawing from the defensive line towards the north and northwest, covered by small rearguard detachments. The corps, with the 189th and 196th Divisions, marched to the area of Talsi and Dundaga on 9 and 10 May to collect and disarm the surrendered German forces of the 207th Security Division and other units of Army Group Courland.<cr><cr>
translation: 第111步兵军司令部于1943年11月初在少将鲍里斯·罗日杰斯特温斯基的指挥下成立，他带领该军直到战争结束。该军是沃尔霍夫方面军第54集团军的一部分。<cr>军部与司令部一同组建，包括独立通信营第551和野战邮局第3907。组建完成后，它被分配了第44步兵师、第288步兵师以及第53步兵旅。<cr>第53步兵旅于12月转隶至第115步兵军。<cr>该军参加了1944年1月至2月的列宁格勒-诺夫哥罗德进攻战役，与第119步兵军合作重新夺回楚多沃、希姆斯克、索尔茨、德诺和波尔霍夫。<cr>一月期间，第288步兵师进入方面军预备队，而第18和第80步兵师加入该集团军群。在一月底，该集团军群向楚多沃推进，对抗德国第21步兵师，并通过第44步兵师以及第14和53步兵旅的三路进攻占领了该镇。第18和第80步兵师于二月转移，而第288步兵师返回集团军群，后者加入了第225步兵师。该集团军群于2月11日重新加入第54集团军，此前集团军司令部迁移到方面军左翼。根据2月13日的命令，沃尔霍夫方面军被解散，该集团军群和集团军转移到列宁格勒方面军。与第一突击集团军的第14近卫步兵军协同作战，第111师于2月23日晚攻击了德诺镇，但两个集团军均遭到德国反击部队的击退。次日，第44和第288步兵师以及第111师附属的第16坦克旅、一个步兵师、一个步兵旅和一个坦克团重新发起进攻占领了该镇。该集团军群参与了2月26日夺回波尔霍夫的战斗，然后与集团军一起在试图突破豹式防线的努力中失败。直到7月，它包括第44、第225和第288步兵师。第54集团军于四月转移到第三巴尔蒂克方面军。到6月1日，393野战车辆修理基地作为集团军群单位成立。<cr>从7月中旬至月底，该集团军群参加了普斯科夫-奥斯特罗夫攻势。与第67集团军一起，该集团军群在提乌佩河和高亚加河附近作战，然后于9月参加里加攻势，在此期间帮助夺回了里加。<cr> 里加攻势后，该军负责保卫爱沙尼亚南部的兰纳至拉脱维亚北部的西尔策之间的帕鲁湾和里加湾东岸，并根据10月21日的命令驻守帕鲁、阿伊纳齐、萨拉克里瓦和其他沿海大型居民点。该军和第14加固区总部设在帕鲁，而第196师则位于阿伊纳齐，第189师位于科达拉。在执行守备任务期间，该军进行了战斗训练以准备参加库尔兰包围圈的封锁行动。<cr>该军计划从4月25日起，在拉斯和阿巴瓦河之间的德国防线上发动突破行动，该防区由第81步兵师防守。5月6日至7日夜间，德国部队开始向北和西北方向撤退，并由小规模后卫部队掩护。5月9日至10日，该军与第189师、第196师行进至塔尔西和邓达加地区，收集并解除库尔兰集团军群第207治安师和其他单位投降的德军武装。<cr><cr>

text: The 112th Infantry Division took part in the Russian invasion as part of Army Group Center and was involved in the battles of Bobruisk, Kiev, Bryansk, and Moscow, where it suffered terribly from the extreme cold. Utterly unequipped for winter, the 112th Infantry reported 400 cases of frostbite in each regiment as early as November 17.<cr>Despite its casualties the 112th Infantry fought on, opposing the 1941-42 Russian winter offensive as well as fighting in the defensive battles on the central sector in 1942 and early 1943, especially around Bryansk and Orel. It suffered heavy casualties during the Kursk offensive and was caught up in the retreats after the defeat of Operation 'Citadelle', including the battles of Belgorod and Kiev (1943). Classified as a Kampfgruppe as early as August 1943, it was officially downgraded to become Division Group 112 on November 2, 1943. The division headquarters became Staff, Corps Detachment B, which included the 112th, 255th and 332nd Divisional Groups. It was largely destroyed at Cherkassy (Korsum) in February 1944 and was dissolved shortly thereafter. Its remnants were absorbed by the 57th and 88th Infantry Divisions.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation:
第112步兵师参加了中央集团军群的俄罗斯入侵行动，并参与了鲍里斯拉夫、基辅、布良斯克和莫斯科等地的战斗，在这些战斗中，严寒给该师带来了极大的痛苦。完全未作冬季准备的第112步兵师在11月17日就报告每个团有400例冻伤病例。<cr>尽管伤亡惨重，第112步兵师仍然继续作战，不仅对抗了1941-42年的俄罗斯冬季攻势，还参加了1942年和1943年初在中央战区的防御战斗，尤其是在布良斯克和奥廖尔周边地区。该师在库尔斯克战役中遭受了重大伤亡，并且在“堡垒”行动失败后的撤退过程中也参与了别尔哥罗德和基辅（1943年）等地的战斗。<cr>早在1943年8月就被归类为战斗群，第112步兵师于1943年11月2日正式降级成为第112师团。该师司令部成为了B军部直属指挥部，其中包括了第112、第255和第332师团。<cr>该师在1944年2月的切尔卡瑟（科尔松）战役中被大量摧毁，并很快解散。其残余部队被并入了第57步兵师和第88步兵师。

德国战斗序列 第一卷 二战中的第1至第290步兵师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text: The 112th Rifle Division was established at Vyazma prior to 7.41 and wiped out there 10.41. Recreated at Novosibirsk 4.42, fought at Stalingrad, Kiev, Korosten, Zhitomir, and in Poland and Germany. With 6th Army of the 1st Ukrainian Front 5.45.<cr><cr>
translation: 第112步兵师于1941年7月前在维亚兹玛建立，同年10月在那里被消灭。1942年4月在新西伯利亚重建，参加了斯大林格勒、基辅、科罗斯坚、日托米尔以及波兰和德国的战斗。1945年5月隶属于第一乌克兰方面军的第6集团军。<cr><cr>

text: The 113th Infantry Division remained in Germany until July 1941, when it was sent to the 6th Army on the Russian Front. After fighting in the Battle of Kiev, however, it was sent to the Balkans to perform occupation duties. The III/268th Infantry Regiment was sent to the Afrika Korps in May 1942 and became the III/155th Rifle Regiment. Meanwhile, in early 1942, the rest of the 113th Infantry Division was transferred back to the southern sector of the Russian Front. It was with the 6th Army in the battles around Taganrog (February 1942), Kharkov-Izyum (May-June), the Don Bend battles (July) and in the Stalingrad street fighting beginning in August 1942. It was surrounded with General Paulus at Stalingrad in November 1942. The 113rd Infantry Division was destroyed on January 20, 1943.<cr>A new 113th Infantry was created in Brittany in the spring of 1943. It was sent to Army Group Center that summer but did not prove to be a particularly effective combat division. In the autumn of 1943, it suffered heavy casualties in the Dnieper withdrawal and was broken up on November 2, 1943. About one-third of the unit was assigned to the 337th Infantry Division, while the rest was used to form Division Group 113 of Corps Detachment G. This unit was destroyed at Bobruisk in July 1944. The 113th Infantry Division, meanwhile, officially ceased to exist on November 2, 1943.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第113步兵师直到1941年7月都驻扎在德国，随后被派往俄罗斯前线的第六集团军。经过基辅战役后，该师又被调往巴尔干地区执行占领任务。第268步兵师第三团于1942年5月被派往非洲装甲集群，并改组为第155步兵师第三团。与此同时，在1942年初，第113步兵师的其余部分被调回俄罗斯前线南部战区。该师参加了塔甘罗格（1942年2月）、哈尔科夫-伊久姆（1942年5月至6月）以及顿河弯道战役（7月），并在斯大林格勒巷战中作战，从1942年8月开始。该师在1942年11月与保卢斯将军一起被包围在斯大林格勒。第113步兵师于1943年1月20日被消灭。<cr>新组建的第113步兵师于1943年春季在布列塔尼成立，同年夏天被派往中央集团军群，但并未证明是一个特别有效的战斗师。1943年秋季，在第聂伯河撤退中遭受了严重损失，并于1943年11月2日解散。大约三分之一的部队被分配给第337步兵师，其余部分则用于组建G军属部下的第113师团群。该单位在1944年7月鲍里斯克战役中被消灭。<cr>与此同时，第113步兵师于1943年11月2日正式解散。<cr>德国二战陆军战斗序列 第一卷：第1至第290步兵师作者：萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: The 113th Rifle Division was established at Rylsk 8.39 and wiped out at Minsk 7.41. Recreated at Moscow from 5th Moscow People's Militia Division 7.41, fought at Moscow, Vyazma, and Rogan. With 57th Army of the 3rd Ukrainian Front 5.45.<cr><cr>
translation: 第113步兵师于1939年8月在罗尔斯克成立，于1941年7月在明斯克被消灭。1941年7月在莫斯科重建，参加了莫斯科、维亚兹马和罗戈任的战斗。1945年5月隶属于第57集团军（第三乌克兰方面军）。<cr><cr>

text:
On 25 December 1944, the 114th Guards Airborne Division was converted to infantry and became the 114th Guards Rifle Division. Its first commander was Vasily Polikarpovich Ivanov.

On 10 January 1945, the 39th Guards Rifle Corps was transferred to Hungary. During Operation Spring Awakening, the division created defensive positions on the eastern bank of the Danube from Dunavecse to Rackeve. On 23 March, the division captured Papa, for which it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner. It was on the Austrian border by 1 April and captured Zillingdorf. The division attacked on the corps' right flank during the Vienna Offensive. After the capture of Vienna, the division fought in the Prague Offensive.<cr><cr>

text: The 119th Rifle Division was originally raised at Krasnoyarsk in 1939 as a motor rifle division until the following year when it was reorganized as a standard Red Army rifle division, and served for the duration of WWII in that role. It saw very limited service in the Winter War against Finland. Following the German invasion in 1941 the first two formations of the division distinguished themselves on the battlefield, and were raised to the status of Guards Rifle divisions: the 17th Guards following the Battle of Moscow; and the 54th Guards for its successes in Operaton Uranus. The division was formed for a third time in early 1943 and served for the duration of the war in the north-central sectors of the front, taking part in the offensive that drove the Nazi forces out of the Baltic States and winning a decoration for the liberation of Riga.<cr><cr>
translation: 第119步兵师最初于1939年在克拉斯诺亚尔斯克组建，起初为摩托化步兵师。到第二年，该师重组为标准红军步兵师，并以这种编制参加了整个二战。它在对抗芬兰的冬季战争中仅有限参战。随着德国人在1941年的入侵，该师最初的两个建制部队在战场上表现出色，被提升为近卫步兵师：第17近卫步兵师因莫斯科保卫战有功；第54近卫步兵师则因为在天王星行动中的成功而获此殊荣。该师于1943年初第三次组建，并在整个战争期间在前线的北中部地区服役，参与了将纳粹部队驱逐出波罗的海国家的攻势，并因解放里加而获得了一枚勋章。<cr><cr><cr>
