text: The 132nd Infantry Division crossed into southern Russia in July 1941. The division fought in the drive to the Dnieper, in the huge Battle of Kiev, in the push to the Crimea, and in the siege of Sevastopol. It later took part in the assault that caused the fall of this giant Soviet naval fortress in the summer of 1942, occupied the Kertsch peninsula in August, and was subsequently shifted to the northern sector of the Eastern Front in October 1942. It remained with the 18th Army of Army Group North for the next two and a half years.<cr>In late 1943 or early 1944, it was reorganized as a Type 44 division, with three grenadier regiments of two battalions each. It fought in the siege of Leningrad, in the subsequent retreat from the city, and in the defense of the Narva River. In July 1944, the 132nd Infantry suffered heavy casualties in the Russian summer offensive and was forced into the Courland Pocket in September 1944. It took part in the six battles of the Courland Pocket, where all Soviet attempts to crush Army Group North were checked. It suffered such heavy losses in these battles, however, that the 437th Grenadier Regiment and the III/132nd Artillery Regiment had to be disbanded. The division was still in Courland when the war ended. It surrendered on May 8, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第132步兵师于1941年7月进入南俄。该师参加了向第聂伯河推进的战斗、巨大的基辅战役、克里米亚攻势以及塞瓦斯托波尔围城战。它后来参与了1942年夏季导致这座巨大苏联海军要塞陷落的突击行动，在8月份占领了刻赤半岛，并于同年10月转移到东线北部战区，隶属于北方集团军群第18集团军，接下来两年半时间里一直驻守在此。<cr>1943年末或1944年初，该师重组为一种44型师，拥有三个掷弹兵团（每个团下辖两个营）。它参加了列宁格勒围城战、从城市撤退的战斗以及纳尔瓦河防御战。1944年7月，在苏联夏季攻势中第132步兵师遭受了重大伤亡，并于同年9月被迫进入库尔兰包围圈。该师参与了库尔兰包围圈内的六次战役，这些战役阻止了所有苏军试图击溃北方集团军群的尝试。然而，由于在这些战斗中的巨大损失，第437掷弹兵团和第132炮兵团第三营不得不解散。当战争结束时该师仍驻守库尔兰地区，并于1945年5月8日投降。<cr>德国二战陆军编成 第一卷：第1至第290步兵师，萨缪尔·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text: The 134th Infantry Division was more or less continuously engaged on the central sector of the Russian Front from June 1941 until it was destroyed in July 1944. It fought at Bialystok, Bobruisk, Kiev, and Bryansk, and was with the 2nd Army in the battles around Orel (south of Moscow). It suffered heavy casualties when it was overrun near Livny in December 1941. The division lost much of its artillery when the Russians broke into the rear of the 2nd Army, and on December 12, General Halder, the chief of the Army General Staff, reported it unfit for combat because of a lack of supplies. It nevertheless remained in the line and fought in the Orel sector until the spring of 1943. In March 1944, it absorbed what was left of the 390th Field Training Division. It took part in the defensive battles around Gomel and Bryansk in the summer and autumn of 1943. It was on the front line in June 1944, when the Soviet summer offensive smashed Army Group Center. The 134th was encircled near Bobruisk and was destroyed there, along with much of the 9th Army, on June 29, 1944. Lieutenant General Ernst Philipp, the last division commander, committed suicide rather than surrender to the Russians.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text: The 137th Infantry Division crossed into Russia with Army Group Center in June 1941 and remained with that army group throughout its existence. It fought in the battles of the Bialystok, Smolensk, and the Yelnya Bend, in the final drive on Moscow, and against the 1941-42 Russian winter offensive, where it suffered such heavy casualties that its 449th Infantry Regiment had to be disbanded. Later it fought at Juchnow (1942), Spass-Demyansk (1942), Kursk (1943), and the battles of the central Dnieper. Badly understrength after over two years of almost continuous action, during which five of its original nine infantry battalions had suffered such heavy losses that they had to be disbanded, the 137th was withdrawn from combat in late 1943, and was downgraded to Divisiongruppe 137 on November 2. The staff of the division became Staff, 271st Infantry Division. Division Group 137 was assigned to Corps Detachment E and remained on the Eastern Front until December 16, 1943, when it was disbanded.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text:
The 139th Rifle Division was established at Kozelsk in September 1939, on the basis of a regiment of the 81st Rifle Division. It fought in the Winter War with Finland. It initially consisted of the 718th, 609th, and 364th Rifle Regiments. Fighting as part of 8th Army, it was defeated at the Battle of Tolvajrvi on 12 December 1939. It was serving with 37th Rifle Corps, 6th Army, Kiev Special Military District, on 22 June 1941. It was wiped out during the Battle of Uman in August 1941.

Force Composition 2 October 1939

364th Rifle Regiment
609th Rifle Regiment
718th Rifle Regiment
354th Light Artillery Regiment<cr><cr>
Second Formation
It was recreated from 9th Moscow People's Militia Rifle Division (In 1941, residents of Zamoskvorechye formed the Twelfth Militia Division of Kirovsky District (Zamoskvorechye District). It was destroyed again at Vyazma in October 1941.

Third Formation
It was recreated at Cheboksary in January 1942. Fought at Kursk and Gdynia. It received a large number of volunteers from Siberia before participating in the Battle of Kursk. A popular song was written about a platoon of the division 'Na Bazimyannoy Visote (On a nameless height) featured in the film 'Tishina' (Silence) that documented the events of a defence of a height at the village of Rubezhenka, Kuybyshevsky rayon, Kaluga Oblast, when the platoon defended against an attack by a German battalion estimated at a strength of 200 on 14 September 1943. There were only two survivors from the platoon, but the height was held. It was serving with the 49th Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front in May 1945.<cr><cr>

text: The 13th Army (1st formation) headquarters was formed in May 1941 in the Western Special Military District, starting on 5 May in Mogilev in accordance with the decision of Central Committee of the Communist Party and Sovnarkom of the USSR No.1113-460cc. dated 23 April 1941. It was intended to comprised 21st, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_Rifle_Corps, and 44th Rifle Corps. In the beginning of June Lieutenant General Petr Filotov arrived to take command. From the beginning of Operation Barbarossa the Army included the 21st Rifle Corps, 50th Rifle Division, the 8th Anti-Tank Artillery Brigade and a number of other separate units. From the end of June 1941 the Army conducted defensive operations in the Minsk Fortified Region, towards Borisov and on the Dnieper river. The formation conducted operations as part of the Soviet Western and Central Fronts. Parts of the Army held up the Wehrmacht advance for almost three weeks near Mogilyev. The 172nd Rifle Division under Major General Mikhail Romanov especially distinguished itself in the combat. Parts of the Army participated in the Battle of Smolensk from 10 July to 10 September 1941. During September and October 1941 the Army was operating as part of the Bryansk Front and included the 6th Rifle Division.<cr>The Army fought as part of the Central Front in the Battle of Kursk in July 1943 under General N.P. Pukhov, numbering four corps with twelve rifle divisions (including the 75th Guards Rifle Division). The Army finished its war service in Germany within the 1st Ukrainian Front in 1945, consisting of the 24th Rifle Corps (117th Rifle Division, 380th Rifle Division, 395th Rifle Division), 27th Rifle Corps (6th Guards Rifle Division and 121st Guards Rifle Division), 102nd Rifle Corps (147th Rifle Division and 172nd Rifle Divisions, which took part in the Battle of Halbe), 17th Artillery Division, and many other smaller artillery and other formations.<cr><cr>

It was intended to comprised 21st, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_Rifle_Corps, and 44th Rifle Corps. In the beginning of June Lieutenant General Petr Filotov arrived to take command. text: The 13th Guards Rifle Corps was formed from 30 October to 15 November 1942 in Ranenburg, Tambov Oblast. The corps' fighting way began in December 1942 in the Battle of Stalingrad. Part of 2nd Guards Army on 1 December 1942. On 1 February 1943, still with 2nd Guards Army, the corps consisted of 3rd Guards Rifle Division, 49th Guards Rifle Division, and . By December 1, 1943, 295th Rifle Div had joined the corps.<cr>Later the corps helped liberate Novocherkassk, Donbass, Kherson, Crimea, Belarus and Lithuania. It took part in the capture of East Prussia and Knigsberg. The combat history of the corps finished on the Baltic Sea. 42 awards of Hero of the Soviet Union were made to personnel attached to the corps. During the assault and capture of the walled city of Koenigsberg the name 'Konigsberg' was conferred on the corps (1945).<cr><cr>
translation: 第13近卫步兵军于1942年10月30日至11月15日在坦博夫州的兰内堡成立。该军的战斗历程始于1942年12月在斯大林格勒战役中。1942年12月1日，该军隶属于第2近卫集团军。<cr>1943年2月1日，仍然属于第2近卫集团军时，该军包括第3近卫步兵师、第49近卫步兵师和<cr><cr>。到1943年12月1日，第295步兵师加入了该军。<cr>后来该军帮助解放了诺沃切尔卡斯克、顿巴斯、赫尔松、克里米亚、白俄罗斯和立陶宛，并参与了东普鲁士和柯尼斯堡的占领。该军的战斗历史在波罗的海结束。<cr><cr>与该军相关的人员共获得42次苏联英雄称号。<cr>

text: On 19 January 1942, the 87th Rifle Division was officially awarded Guards status and was re-designated as the 13th Guards Rifle Division.<cr>In May 1942, the 13th Division was involved in the Soviet counter-offensive at Kharkov, where they fought on its northern axis, thus escaping the encirclement and destruction of a substantial portion of the Soviet forces engaged, followed by the Russian defeat. During this offensive, the division suffered more than fifty-percent casualties, most of which were sustained in the repelling of fierce German counter-attacks.<cr>On 13 September of that year, German infantry divisions made their first advance into Stalingrad, marking the opening salvos of the Battle of Stalingrad. By the end of the day the German 71st Infantry Division had reached the city centre, north of the Tsaritsa Gorge. A Stavka directive ordered the 13th Guards Division (in the midst of its resupply and reinforcement) to the Volga River and Stalingrad.<cr>The battle at the Mamaev Kurgan began approximately three weeks after the brutal fighting between the German and Russian infantrymen had begun in the outskirts of Stalingrad, on 15 September. During this portion of the battle, the division fought several Wehrmacht divisions for control of the park's central hilltop summit, which changed hands multiple times. Meanwhile, other divisional units fought in different sectors of Stalingrad. The division was in the midst of the combat throughout the city in the remains of the bombed-out buildings and factories, on the slopes of the Mamaev Kurgan hills. Most accounts state that of the 10,000 men of the division that crossed the Volga into the Battle of Stalingrad, only between 280 and 320 of them survived the struggle.<cr>Following the Soviet victory at Stalingrad and the destruction of the German 6th Army, the 13th Guards are again pulled from the lines for re-fit and re-supply. Alongside the 5th Guards Army (Voronezh Front), the division was held in reserve south of Kursk, in order to counter the forthcoming German offensive there Operation Citadel. The original intention was for these two formations to counter-attack the Germans after the German assault had been ground down by the front line Soviet units, but both formations were committed to prevent a possible breakthrough. After several days of continuous fierce fighting (including the tank battle at Prokhorovka, in which the 13th Rifles' small number of armored units participated in), they successfully ground the elite Waffen-SS formations to a standstill. Meanwhile, the rifle battalions on the 13th held the line around Oboyan, repelling attacks from trenches.<cr>Shortly thereafter, the 13th Rifles advanced south-westwards, where they participated in the Red Army's assault to liberate Ukraine from German control. The division took part in the Poltava-Kremenchuk Operation [ru] in which they gained control of the town of Poltava after extremely fierce fighting, it was liberated on 23 September 1943. This is indicated by the designation of 13th Guards Rifle Division, Poltava (given in September 1943), which shows that the division was cited for their actions in seizing Polatava. After Poltava the division took part in the battle of the Dnieper. It was assigned to accomplish a false crossing of the Dnieper River to confuse the Germans and allow for crossings further north and south. Elements of the division crossed the river on floats and rafts to reach the island of Peschanny to the north-west of Kremenchuk where German infantry had occupied the west side of the island and had to be dislodged in hand-to-hand combat.<cr>During the Red Army's final drive into Germany, starting with Operation Bagration beginning on 22 June 1944, the Division was a part of the 32nd Guards Rifle Corps or was under direct command of the 5th Guards Army (2nd Ukrainian Front). This force drove the Germans back through northern Ukraine and central Poland in to the northern regions of Germany itself. By the end of January 1945, the 1st Ukrainian Front, including the 13th Rifles, had reached the southern outskirts. Here, they participated in the Battle of Berlin where they combating for both objectives: Berlin itself and the Teltov Canal. The capture of the latter objective gave the Red Army a river crossing of the Elbe River, allowing the Russians to assault the heart of the Third Reich.<cr><cr>
translation: 1942年1月19日，第87步兵师正式被授予近卫称号，并重新命名为第13近卫步兵师。<cr>1942年5月，在苏联在哈尔科夫的反攻中，第13师参与了北部轴线的战斗，从而避免了苏军主力部队的大规模包围和毁灭，随后是俄罗斯军队的失败。在这次进攻期间，该师遭受了超过百分之五十的伤亡，其中大部分是在击退德军猛烈反击的过程中造成的。<cr>同年9月13日，德国步兵师首次向斯大林格勒推进，标志着斯大林格勒战役的开始。当天结束时，德国第71步兵师已到达城市中心，位于茨瓦尼察峡谷以北。最高统帅部下达指令，命令正在补给和增援中的第13近卫师前往伏尔加河及斯大林格勒。<cr>在马马耶夫丘陵的战斗大约开始于德国与俄罗斯步兵在外围地区激烈交战后的三周后，即9月15日。在这场战役的部分中，该师与其他几个德军师争夺公园中央山顶的控制权，这一区域多次易手。与此同时，其他部队在斯大林格勒的不同区域作战。整个城市内，在被轰炸破坏的大楼和工厂残骸以及马马耶夫丘陵山坡上都留下了战斗痕迹。大多数记录显示，该师10,000名士兵中有280至320人在这场战役中幸存下来。<cr>在苏联取得斯大林格勒战役胜利并消灭德国第6集团军之后，第13近卫师再次被从前线撤出进行整备和补给。该师与第5近卫集团军（沃罗涅日方面军）一起，在库尔斯克以南地区作为预备队部署，准备应对即将在那里的德军“堡垒行动”进攻。最初计划是这两支部队将在前线苏军部队消耗德国军队后发起反击，但为了防止可能的突破，两支部队都被投入了战斗。经过数天连续激烈的战斗（包括普罗霍罗夫卡坦克战，在这场战斗中第13步兵师的小部分装甲单位也参与其中），他们成功地将精锐的武装党卫军部队压制住。<cr>与此同时，第13师的步兵团在奥波扬地区坚守防线，击退了从战壕发起的攻击。<cr>不久之后，第13步兵师向西南推进，在红军解放乌克兰的突击行动中发挥了作用。该师参加了波尔塔瓦-克雷门丘格战役 [ru] ，在极其激烈的战斗后占领了波尔塔瓦镇，并于1943年9月23日将其解放。这表明第13近卫步兵师（波尔塔瓦）的称号是在1943年9月授予的，以表彰该师夺取波尔塔瓦的行动。在波尔塔瓦之后，该师参加了第聂伯河战役。它被分配执行一次假渡河任务，以迷惑德国人并为北部和南部的真正渡河创造条件。该师的部分部队乘坐浮桥和木筏到达克雷门丘茨西北方向的佩什纳尼岛，在那里德军步兵占领了岛屿西侧，并需要通过肉搏战将其驱逐。<cr>在红军最后进军德国的过程中，从巴格拉季昂行动开始于1944年6月22日，该师隶属于第32近卫步兵军或直接接受第5近卫集团军（第二乌克兰方面军）的指挥。这支力量将德军赶回了北部乌克兰和波兰中部，并深入德国北部地区。到1945年1月底，第一乌克兰方面军包括第13步兵师在内的部队已经到达柏林南部郊区，在那里他们参加了柏林战役，为两个目标而战：柏林本身和特尔托夫运河。后者的目标使红军获得了易北河的渡口，允许俄国人进攻第三帝国的心脏。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 13th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 13th Light Division. The Hungarian Government reluctantly agreed to support the Germans 1942 summer offensive Fall Blau and allocated the division as part of the Hungarian Second Army to the task. Each light division in the Second Army was reinforced with three battalions from sister divisions in Hungary but nonetheless each division was only slightly larger than half the size of its German counterparts. Second Army's role in the offensive was to guard the German northern flank on the Don River. During the Stalingrad Campaign the Second Army suffered over 60% casualties but was generally able to retreat in good order. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 13th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 13th Infantry Division. The division was disbanded in November of 1944.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第13匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖2个步兵团（每个团有3个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多兵力以支持东线作战，并且大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本保持不变。该旅更名为第13轻型师。匈牙利政府勉强同意在1942年的夏季攻势（蓝色行动）中支援德国，并将该师分配给匈牙利第二集团军的任务。第二集团军中的每个轻型师都从匈牙利的兄弟部队得到三个营的增援，但即便如此，每个师仍然只有其德军同行的一半左右规模。在此次进攻中，第二集团军的角色是保卫德国北部顿河沿岸的侧翼。在斯大林格勒战役期间，第二集团军遭受了超过60%的伤亡率，但仍能有组织地撤退。<cr>参考文献：Nigel Thomas 博士和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利陆军》<cr>词条提供：Chris Munson% c<cr>

text: The 13th Mechanized Corps was formed in March 1941 in Bielsk Podlaski as part of the 10th Army in the Western Special Military District. Major General Pyotr Akhlyustin commanded the corps, Major General Vasily Ivanov was its deputy commander for combat troops, and Colonel Ivan Grizunov was its chief of staff.<cr>The corps was alerted on the night of 22 June. At 0200 in the morning corps headquarters moved into the forest 15 kilometers southwest of Bielsk Podlaski. The first staff echelon of the 2nd Rifle Corps from Minsk moved into the 13th Mechanized Corps' former headquarters at Bielsk Podlaski. On the morning of 22 June, the motorized infantry of the 6th and 13th Mechanized Corps began to prepare positions on the Narew from Zoltki to Suraz and onwards to Topczewo, Bransk, and Gmina Bocki. The 13th Mechanized Corps fought the vanguard of the German IX Army Corps.<cr>The 25th Tank Division's reconnaissance battalion joined the battle before the rest of the division. At Bransk the battalion blocked the advance of German units. Despite having armored vehicles, the battalion could not resist superior German troops for long. The battalion was cut to pieces and pushed back to the Nurzec. Akhlyustin sent in the 18th Motorcycle Regiment to help the battalion. Regimental commander Captain Alexey Gromov took about a hundred motorcycles and three tanks to Bransk, but only the vanguard reached the city. The regiment suffered heavy losses, losing two out of four company commanders.<cr>By 1000 on 23 June, the 25th Tank Division was holding positions at Men, Bereznitsa, and Bransk. Its motor rifle regiment was at Raysk, Proneviche, and Gatki. The 31st Tank Division held positions at Voytki, Lyubeyki, and Andrianki. The 208th Motorized Division was at Nowosady, Hajnowka, and Lipin. Corps headquarters was in the forest north of Golody. On 23 June, the counterattack at Bransk involved all the forces of the 25th Tank Division and 18th Motorcycle Regiment, as well as the 208th Motorized Division's 760th Motorized Regiment. The town twice was recaptured and then lost.<cr>The 25th and 31st Tank Divisions retreated towards the Bialowieza Forest and the 208th Motorized Division moved from the Narew to Svislach and to Bialystok. On 28 June German troops advancing from Bielsk and Hrodna linked up in the Berestovitsa area, splitting the Bialystok pocket into several smaller pockets. The 208th Motorized Division retreated to Vawkavysk. Corps headquarters and separate groups were consolidated into a unit led by Akhlyustin. On 28 July, after moving through 500 kilometers of German-held territory, Akhlyustin was killed crossing the Sozh River at the positions of the 132nd Rifle Division.<cr><cr>
translation: 第13机械化军于1941年3月在别利亚斯克波多利斯基作为西部特别军事区的第10集团军的一部分组建。少将彼得·阿赫柳斯丁指挥该军，副司令瓦西里·伊万诺夫负责战斗部队，参谋长为伊万·格里祖诺夫上校。<cr>该军在6月22日晚接到警报。 6月23日凌晨2点，军司令部转移到别利亚斯克波多利斯基西南15公里处的森林中。第2步兵军（来自明斯克）的第一梯队进入第13机械化军原来的总部所在地别利亚斯克波多利斯基。<cr>6月22日上午， 第6和第13机械化军的摩托化步兵开始在纳雷夫河从佐尔茨基到苏拉兹并延伸至托普切沃、布兰斯克和博奇基地区准备阵地。第13机械化军与德国第九集团军先头部队交战。<cr>25坦克师 的侦察营加入战斗，但其余部队尚未参战。在布兰斯克，该营阻止了德军单位的推进。尽管拥有装甲车辆，该营无法长时间抵抗优势德军。该营被分割包围并被迫撤退到努尔泽茨河。阿赫柳斯丁派遣第18摩托车团增援该营。<cr>团长格罗莫夫上尉率领约一百辆摩托车和三辆坦克前往布兰斯克，但只有先头部队到达城市。该团遭受了重大损失，失去了四名连长中的两名。6月23日中午，第25坦克师在梅恩、别尔热尼察和布兰斯克一线据守。其摩托化步兵团则位于雷斯基、普罗内维奇和加茨基。第31坦克师驻扎在沃伊特基、柳贝耶基和安德里安基。第208摩托化师则位于诺沃萨迪、哈尼沃卡和利平。军司令部位于戈洛季北部的森林中。6月23日，布兰斯克反攻涉及了第25坦克师的所有部队以及第18摩托车团，并且还动用了第208摩托化师的第760摩托化团。该镇两次被重新夺回又丢失。<cr>第25和第31坦克师撤退至比亚韦斯托克森林，而第208摩托化师则从纳雷夫河转移到斯维斯拉克河，并最终到达比亚韦斯托克。6月28日，德军部队从别列斯克和戈梅林推进，在别尔热诺维奇地区会合，将比亚韦斯托克包围圈分割成几个较小的包围圈。第208摩托化师撤退至瓦科维斯基。军司令部和其他独立单位被整合为一个由阿赫利乌丁指挥的部队。<cr>7月28日，在穿越了500公里德占区后，阿赫利乌丁在索日河畔132步兵师阵地前渡河时阵亡。

text: The 13th Panzer Division crossed into Russia with Army Group South in June 1941. The division was very heavily engaged, almost from the beginning. It fought in the battles of Lubin and Uman, in the Stalin Line breakthrough at Hulsk, in the drive on and encirclement of Kiev, in the Battle of the Chernigovka Pocket, and in the capture of Rostov.<cr>By November 1941, its divisional commander and two of its regimental commanders were suffering from nervous exhaustion. After helping halt the Soviet winter offensive of 194142 on the Mius River, the 13th Panzer took part in von Kleist's drive on the Caucasus oilfields in 1942, where it crossed the Terek River and pushed to within fifteen miles of Grozny. Most of the division escaped isolation in the Kuban before the Russians retook Rostov, although part of it was cut off and had to be evacuated later via the Crimea. By this time, it had only eighteen operational tanks left. Reunited under the command of the resurrected 6th Army, the 13th Panzer was reinforced with a battalion of Panthers, new model PzKw IVs and several excellent self-propelled tank destroyers. It fought in the lower Dniepr battles in the Ukraine, where it fought near Kharkov and Zaporozhye, and only had seven tanks left when it was surrounded at Melitopol, along with the 336th Infantry Division and the 15th Luftwaffe Field Division. Outnumbered more than 7 to 1, the 13th Panzer led the ensuing breakout on August 30, 1943, and reached German lines on September 2. The battered division remained in the line and covered the retreat from Stalino. It then fought its way back to the Dnieper, fought in the Battle of the Nikopol Bridgehead, and in the subsequent retreat to Krivoy Rog.<cr>The 13th Panzer was partially rebuilt in early 1944, and was rushed back to the front, where it took part in the Cherkassy relief attempt in February and the retreats to the Bug and Dniester (Dnestr). It suffered heavy losses when the Romanians defected in September 1944. The division had only 40 tanks left when the battle began and lost almost all of them. Withdrawn to reform in October, the 13th absorbed the 110th Panzer Brigade and was back in action on the southern sector of the Eastern Front in November. Most of the division (3,000 men and seventeen PzKw IV and Panther tanks and thirty-five self-propelled guns and eight assault guns) was encircled at Budapest in December and was destroyed when the German garrison tried unsuccessfully to break out of the city on February 11, 1945. The remnants of the division (300 to 500 men) were reformed under the command of Lieutenant Colonel of Reserves Wilhelm Schning. This kampfgruppe was used to form the nucleus of Panzer Division Feldherrnhalle 2, which was activated on February 2, 1945. This division was unofficially referred to as the 13th Panzer Division, but it was not. The 13th Panzer officially ceased to exist in March.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第13装甲师于1941年6月随南方集团军群进入俄罗斯。该师几乎从一开始就投入了激烈的战斗，参加了卢布林和乌曼战役，在胡尔斯克突破斯大林防线的战斗中作战，并参与了对基辅的进攻和包围、切尔尼戈夫卡包围圈之战以及罗斯托夫的占领。<cr>到1941年11月，该师的师长和两名团级指挥官都因神经衰弱而病倒。在帮助阻止苏联于1941-42年的冬季攻势后，在米乌斯河畔，第13装甲师参加了克莱斯特将军对高加索油田的进攻行动，在此期间它越过了特列克河，并推进到了格罗兹内的十五英里范围内。该师大部分部队在库班地区避免了孤立，但在苏联重新占领罗斯托夫后，部分部队被切断并不得不通过克里米亚撤离。此时，该师只剩下十八辆可操作的坦克。<cr>重组并在复活的第6集团军指挥下，第13装甲师得到了一个豹式营、新型四号坦克和几辆优秀的自行反坦克炮的增援。它参加了乌克兰第聂伯河下游的战斗，在此期间它在哈尔科夫和扎波罗热附近作战，并且在梅利托波尔被包围时只剩下七辆坦克，与第336步兵师和第15空军野战师一起被困。<cr>面对7比1以上的劣势兵力，第13装甲师于1943年8月30日领导了随后的突围行动，并在9月2日到达德军防线。这支疲惫不堪的部队继续坚守阵地并掩护从斯大林诺撤退。然后它重新夺回了第聂伯河，在尼科波尔桥头堡之战中作战，以及后续撤退至克里沃伊罗格。<cr>第13装甲师于1944年初部分重建，并迅速返回前线，参加了2月切尔卡瑟解围行动以及撤退至布格河和德涅斯特河的战斗。当罗马尼亚军队在1944年9月倒戈时，该师遭受了重大损失。战斗开始时，该师只剩下40辆坦克，并几乎全部丧失。10月被撤出重组后，第13装甲师吸收了第110装甲旅，并于11月重新投入东线南部战区的战斗。该师大部分兵力（约3000人、十七辆PzKw IV和豹式坦克以及三十五门自行火炮和八门突击炮）在12月布达佩斯战役中被包围，当德军守备部队于1945年2月11日试图从城市突围时失败，该师被消灭。第13装甲师残部（约300至500人）由预备役上校威廉·施宁领导重组，并用于组建“统帅堂”装甲师第2师的核心力量。“统帅堂”装甲师第2师于1945年2月2日激活。该师非正式地被称为第13装甲师，但实际上并非如此。官方的第13装甲师在3月份停止存在。<cr>德国战斗序列 第三卷 - 二战中的德军装甲、摩托化步兵和武装党卫军师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text: Part of 12th Army in Kiev Military District at the outbreak of hostilities, the corps consisted of 44th, 48th and 192nd Mountain Rifle Divisions. It was destroyed in the Kiev Pocket in August 1941. It was reformed in 1943 and consisted of 392nd Rifle Division and 94th Rifle Brigade. It fought as part of 1st Ukrainian Front in the crossing of the Dnepr at Bukrin in September 1943. If fought in the Balkans in 1944 and was at Nis, Yugoslavia in October, 1944. <cr><cr><cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 作为冲突爆发时基辅军区第12集团军的一部分，该军由第44、48和192山地步兵师组成。它于1941年8月在基辅包围圈中被消灭。该军于1943年重组，包括第392步兵师和第94步兵旅。它作为第1乌克兰方面军的一部分，在1943年9月布克林渡过第聂伯河时作战。1944年在巴尔干地区作战，并于1944年10月驻扎在南斯拉夫的尼什。<cr><cr><cr><cr>波里耶，罗伯特和康纳，阿尔伯特，《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，普雷斯迪奥出版社，1985<cr><cr>条目由斯图尔特·金提供

text: The 13th Rifle Division was formed in July 1922 on the basis of the 1st Dagestan Rifle Brigade. It participated in the Soviet invasion of Poland in 1939. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was stationed at the border area Zambra - Snyadovo, as part of the 5th Rifle Corps, 10th Army, itself part of the Western Front. The division was engaged on the first day and on June 23rd it retreated toward Bia?ystok and on June 24th it took up the defence of the river Narev. On June 26th the division received an order to retreat to Supraselskuyu Forest, where the division by now was reduced to several unorganized groups. During late June - early July 1941 small groups from the division attempted to break through to the east but were dispersed. The division was formally disbanded on September 19, 1941. It was reformed later that year. During the Sandomierz-Silesian Offensive, the division helped capture D?browa Grnicza on January 27th. For its actions, it was awarded the honorific 'D?browa'. The division fought for the remainder of the war and was with the 1st Ukrainian Front when hostilities ended.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第13步兵师成立于1922年7月，基于第一达吉斯坦步兵旅。该师参加了苏联于1939年入侵波兰的行动。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，它驻扎在赞布腊-斯尼亚多沃边境地区，属于西方方面军第10集团军下的第5步兵军。该师在第一天即投入战斗，并于6月23日撤退至比亚韦斯托克方向，在6月24日防守纳雷夫河。6月26日，该师接到命令撤退到苏普拉谢森林区，在那里此时已缩减为几个无组织的小队。1941年6月底至7月初，该师的小分队试图向东突围但被击散。该师于1941年9月19日正式解散，并在同年重组。在桑多梅日-西里西亚攻势中，该师帮助占领了德布罗瓦格尼察，并因此获得“德布罗瓦”荣誉称号。该师继续战斗直至战争结束，在第1乌克兰方面军服役时停火。<cr> <cr> <cr> <cr> 克里斯·芒森提供

text: The 13th Romanian Infantry Division was attached to the German XXX Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. As with most Romanian infantry divisions it was withdrawn to Romania after the Siege of Odessa. In August of 1942 it left Romania to participate in Fall Blau as part of the Romanian V Corps. Much of the division was encircled and captured during the Battle of Stalingrad. It participated in the defense of Romania in 1944 and was largely disarmed by the Soviets after Romania canceled its alliance with Germany.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第13罗马尼亚步兵师在巴巴罗萨行动开始时隶属于德国第30军。与其他大多数罗马尼亚步兵师一样，该师在敖德萨围城战后撤回了罗马尼亚境内。1942年8月，它离开罗马尼亚，作为罗马尼亚第5军参加了蓝色行动。该师的大部分部队在斯大林格勒战役中被包围并被俘虏。1944年，它参与了防御罗马尼亚，并且在罗马尼亚取消与德国结盟后，该师基本上被苏联解除武装。<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>词条由克里斯·芒森提供

text:
The 13th Tank Corps was formed in April 1942 at Stalingrad.<cr>The 13th Tank Corps had a short but eventful history as a tank corps. It formed up near Stalingrad with one heavy tank brigade of KV tanks and two brigades equipped with T-34s and T-60 or T-70 light tanks. As soon as it went into combat in early June, however, the Soviet command began switching out tank brigades. First to go, on 5 June, was the 65th (Heavy) Tank Brigade. Next, on 16 June 88th Tank Brigade was replaced by 158th Tank Brigade, and 167th Tank Brigade added. 158th Tank Brigade, in turn, was removed from the corps on 5 July, then 85th and 167th Tank Brigades on 19 July.<cr>All of these changes were prompted by heavy losses. 13th Tank Corps was fighting across southern Russia against the German 6th and 4th Panzer Armies, and as a tank brigade was shot up in combat, it was replaced by a fresh brigade. At the end of July, all the brigades were removed from the corps HQ and replaced, so that on 4 August 1942 the corps consisted of:
6th Guards Tank Brigade
1st, 2nd Tank Battalions
6th Guards Motorized Rifle Battalion
13th Tank Brigade
88th, 89th Tank Battalions - total 42 T-34s
13th Motorized Rifle Battalion
254th Tank Brigade
655th Tank Battalion - 2 cos, each 10 T-34s
656th Tank Battalion - 1 co with 10 T-34s,
2 cos each 9 T-70s
194th Motorized Rifle-Machinegun Battalion
38th Motorized Rifle Brigade
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Battalions<cr>Fighting in 1st Tank Army on the approaches to Stalingrad, 13th Tank Corps continued to suffer heavy casualties. On 2 September 56th Tank Brigade was added to improve the corps' tank strength, and on 7 September 6th Guards Tank Brigade was replaced by 39th Tank Brigade. All of this was evidence more of
panic than reinforcement, since the tank brigades had all either been hastily formed or already shot up in battle. By 1 November all the corps' subordinate units had been removed except 13th Tank Brigade, and the 13th Tank Corps was reformed as 13th Mechanized Corps.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第13坦克军于1942年4月在斯大林格勒成立。该坦克军虽然存在时间不长，但经历丰富。它在斯大林格勒附近组建时拥有一个装备KV重型坦克的装甲旅和两个装备T-34中型坦克及T-60或T-70轻型坦克的装甲旅。<cr>然而，自6月初投入战斗以来，苏联指挥部开始频繁更换装甲旅。首先在6月5日撤换的是第65（重）装甲旅。接着，在6月16日，第88装甲旅被第158装甲旅替换，并增加了第167装甲旅。<cr>随后，第158装甲旅于7月5日离开该军，而第85和第167装甲旅则在7月19日撤出。所有这些变动都是由于严重损失所致。<cr>第13坦克军与德国第6和第4装甲集团军作战，在南部俄罗斯境内展开战斗。每当一个装甲旅遭受重创后，就会被新的装甲旅替换。<cr>截至7月底，该军的所有装甲旅都被移出司令部并替换为新部队，因此在1942年8月4日，第13坦克军的编制如下：<cr>第6近卫坦克旅<cr>第1、第2坦克营<cr>第6近卫机械化步兵营<cr>第13坦克旅<cr>第88、第89坦克营（共42辆T-34）<cr>第13机械化步兵营<cr>第254坦克旅<cr>第655坦克营（两个连，每连10辆T-34）<cr>第656坦克营（一个连配备10辆T-34，另外两个连各9辆T-70）<cr>第194机械化步兵机枪营<cr>第38机械化步兵旅<cr>第1、第2、第3步兵营在斯大林格勒外围与第1坦克集团军作战时，第13坦克军继续遭受严重伤亡。9月2日，第56坦克旅被加入以增强该军的坦克实力；9月7日，第6近卫坦克旅被第39坦克旅替换。所有这些都更多地表明了恐慌而非增援，因为所有的坦克旅要么是仓促组建的，要么已经在战斗中损失惨重。到11月1日，除了第13坦克旅外，该军的所有下属单位都被移除，并将第13坦克军重组为第13机械化军。<cr>苏联战斗序列 二战卷二<cr>Charles C. Sharp

text:
The 13th Tank Division was formed 19 July 1940 from 15th Light Tank Brigade in Transbaikal Military District with:<cr>
25th Tank Regiment
26th Tank Regiment
13th Motorized Rifle Regiment
13th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
13th Reconnaissance Battalion
13th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
13th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>The 13th Tank Division was formed as part of 5th Mechanized Corps. The Red Army had stationed large armored forces in the Transbaikal, watching the Japanese, ever since the mid-1930s, so this unit had the advantage of relatively experienced cadre, and was almost full strength in armor by 1 October 1940, with over 300 light tanks. Unfortunately, no modern tanks were shipped to the Transbaikal, so when 13th tank Division was alerted to move west in May 1941 with the rest of 16th Army, it still had no modern equipment, only T-26s, BT-5 or BT-7, or light T-37 and T-38 amphibious tankettes.<cr>Originally intended to go to the Ukraine, 16th Army was rerouted to the Smolensk area after the Germans attacked. Since part of 5th Mechanized Corps was already engaged in the south, 13th Tank Division ended up under a truncated Corps HQ and 20th Army west of Smolensk, and on 6 - 7 July took part in the Orsha Counteroffensive against 3rd Panzer Group. Since the Soviet units were already short of trucks and prime movers, and had left much of their support scattered on railroads from Smolensk to Kiev, this battle amounted to a Charge of the Light Brigade by unsupported Soviet light tanks with neither artillery nor air support against German tank, infantry, and antitank gun lines.<cr>Officially, 13th Tank Division was not disbanded until August, but after 10 July it was little more than a slightly-motorized rifle regiment with a handful of light tanks.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第13坦克师于1940年7月19日从外贝加尔军区的第15轻型坦克旅组建而成：<cr>
第25坦克团
第26坦克团
第13机械化步兵营
第13机械化榴弹炮营
第13侦察营
第13机械化浮桥营
第13防空营<cr><cr>第13坦克师作为第5机械化军的一部分组建。自1930年代中期以来，红军一直在外贝加尔地区部署大量装甲部队以监视日本军队，因此该单位拥有相对有经验的骨干，并且到1940年10月1日时，其装甲力量已接近满编，拥有超过300辆轻型坦克。不幸的是，没有现代坦克被运送到外贝加尔地区，所以当第13坦克师于1941年5月接到命令与第16集团军一起向西调动时，它仍然没有任何现代化装备，只有T-26、BT-5或BT-7快速坦克以及轻型两栖坦克T-37和T-38。<cr>最初计划前往乌克兰的第16集团军在德军发动攻击后被重新部署到斯摩棱斯克地区。由于第5机械化军的一部分已经在南部作战，第13坦克师最终隶属于一个截短的军司令部和位于斯摩棱斯克以西的第20集团军，并于7月6日至7日参加了奥尔沙反攻战对抗第3装甲集群。由于苏联部队已经缺少卡车和牵引车，并且将大部分支援力量分散在从斯摩棱斯克到基辅的铁路线上，这场战斗相当于一支没有炮兵或空中支援、由未受支持的苏军轻型坦克组成的“轻骑兵冲锋”对德军坦克、步兵和反坦克炮线发起攻击。<cr>官方上，第13坦克师直到8月才被解散，但自7月10日起，它实际上只是一支拥有少量轻型坦克的小规模机械化步兵营。<cr><cr>苏联战斗序列 第一卷 作者：查尔斯·C·肖普

text: The 140th Rifle Division was established at Uman Sep 1939. Wiped out at Nikolayev Aug 1941. Recreated from the 13th Moscow People's Rifle Division at Moscow Jul 1941. Wiped out at Vyazma Oct 1941. Recreated at Kanasch Jan 1942. Inactivated Aug 1942. Recreated at Novorossiysk Nov 1942. Fought at Kursk, Zhitomir, Lvov, in the Carpathians, and at Prague. With 38th Army of the 4th Ukrainian Front 5.45.<cr><cr>

text: The 145th Rifle Division was established at Belgorod prior to Jun 1941. Fought at Smolensk; wiped out at Roslavl Aug 1941. Recreated at Balachna Jan 1942. Fought at Chelm and Vitebsk, then in the Baltic lands and Poland.<cr><cr>

text: The 146th Rifle Division was formed for the first time as a standard Red Army rifle division in mid-1939, as part of a major build-up of the Army prior to the start of World War II. After the start of the German invasion in 1941 it defended the approaches to Kiev for several months until being surrounded and destroyed in September. A second formation began in January 1942, and the new division spent the following year on a relatively quiet sector before joining the offensives that would drive the German invaders from north-central Russia, Lithuania, and Poland. The 146th ended the war fighting in the streets of Berlin, after compiling an enviable record of service.<cr><cr>
translation: 第146步兵师首次于1939年中期作为标准红军步兵师组建，这是在二战爆发前对军队进行大规模扩充的一部分。1941年德国入侵开始后，该师保卫基辅周边地区数月，直至9月被包围并消灭。<cr>指挥官报告：第146步兵师于1942年1月重建，在接下来的一年里驻守相对平静的战区，并参与了驱逐德国侵略者、收复俄罗斯中部、立陶宛和波兰的攻势。该师在战争结束前还在柏林市区作战，建立了令人羡慕的服务记录。<cr>步兵师<cr>

text: The 14th Air Army was first formed from the Air Forces of the Volkhov Front in June 1942, and in 1943 participated in the Novgorod-Luga operation. In February 1944 it was dispersed, with the command staff assigned to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (RVGK) and its units to other air armies. Reformed in April 1944, when it served with the 3rd Baltic Front, it was again dispersed in November 1944, with its staff again been allocated to the Stavka Reserve and its units to other formations.<cr><cr>
translation: 第14空军集团军于1942年6月从沃尔霍夫方面军的航空兵中组建，并在1943年参加了诺夫哥罗德-卢加战役。1944年2月，该集团军解散，指挥机构被分配到最高统帅部大本营预备队（RVGK），其部队则被分配给其他空军集团军。<cr>1944年4月重建后，它在第3个波罗的海方面军服役。同年11月再次解散，其指挥机构再次被分配到最高统帅部预备队，而其部队则被分配给其他编制单位。<cr> <cr>

text: Formed 2/14/43 from 21st Mountain Cavalry Division, it was part of VII Guards Cavalry Corps. The division fought at Chernigov in September 1943 and in the Kalinkovichi-Mozyr Offensive in January 1944. It was awarded the honorific 'Mozyr' as a result of its performance in this battle. It participated in the Lublin-Brest Offensive in June 1944, and was awarded the honorific 'Lublin'. In 1945, it was part of the East Pomeranian Offensives in February 1945 and was near Berlin at the end of the war. <cr><cr>The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II: volume V - Book B Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Trafford, 2009 <cr><cr> Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert,The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King

text: The 14th Guards Rifle Division was reformed as an elite infantry division of the Red Army on January 24, 1942, based on the 1st formation of the 96th Rifle Division, which was officially a mountain unit at the time, and served in that role until after the end of WWII. It was in Southern Front when it was redesignated and was soon assigned to the 57th Army. It was encircled during the German counterattack in the Second Battle of Kharkov in May and its first commander was made a prisoner of war, later dying in German captivity. A cadre of the division managed to escape and was sent to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command for rebuilding. In July it joined the 63rd Army and took part in the attacks against the Italian 8th Army that created the bridgehead south of the Don River near Serafimovich during August. In October, now in 21st Army of Don Front, it was active in two probing attacks against the Romanian forces now containing the bridgehead which inflicted severe casualties in advance of the Soviet winter counteroffensive. At the start of that offensive the division was in 5th Tank Army, but was soon transferred to 1st Guards Army and then to the 3rd Guards Army when that was formed. It was under this Army as it advanced into the Donbass in late winter before returning to 57th Army during most of 1943, fighting through east Ukraine and across the lower Dniepr by the end of the year. After being briefly assigned to 53rd Army in December it was moved to 5th Guards Army in February, 1944 where it remained for the duration, mostly in the 33rd Guards Rifle Corps. It saw action in the Uman-Botosani Offensive and won its first decoration, the Order of the Red Banner, as it advanced, before being involved in the frustrating battles along the Dniestr River on the Romanian border. In late spring, 1944 the division was redeployed north becoming part of 1st Ukrainian Front and taking part in the Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive into Poland. The 14th Guards made a spectacular advance across Poland during the Vistula-Oder Offensive and was awarded the Order of Lenin for its part in the liberation of Sandomierz. On January 22, 1945 its commander suffered mortal wounds in the fighting for a bridgehead over the Oder River. In the drive on Berlin in April the division and its regiments won further honors and decorations.<cr><cr>
translation: 第14近卫步兵师于1942年1月24日作为红军精锐步兵师重建，基于当时正式为山地部队的第96步兵师第一编成。该师在南方方面军时被重新指定，并很快被分配给第57集团军。它在德国反攻哈尔科夫第二战役中被包围，其首任指挥官成为战俘并在德国囚禁期间去世。该师的一部分成功逃脱并被送往最高统帅部预备队重建。7月，它加入第63集团军，并参与了8月份对意大利第八集团军的攻击，在塞拉芬维奇附近的顿河以南建立了桥头堡。10月，现在在顿河方面军第21集团军中，该师参加了两次试探性进攻，针对包围桥头堡的罗马尼亚部队，造成了严重的伤亡，为苏联冬季反攻做准备。在此次反攻开始时，该师隶属于第5坦克集团军，但很快被调至第1近卫集团军，并于第3近卫集团军建立后转到该集团军。它是在这个集团军的指挥下推进到顿巴斯地区，在晚冬时节返回第57集团军，并在1943年大部分时间里继续作战，穿越东乌克兰并横跨第聂伯河下游，直到年底。之后，它于12月被短暂分配给第53集团军，并于1944年2月转至第5近卫集团军，在那里一直待到战争结束，主要隶属于第33近卫步兵军。该师参加了乌曼-博托沙尼攻势，并在推进过程中首次获得红旗勋章。随后，它参与了沿罗马尼亚边境德涅斯特河的令人沮丧的战斗。1944年晚春，该师被重新部署到北方，成为第1乌克兰方面军的一部分，并参加了进入波兰的利沃夫-桑多梅日攻势。在维斯瓦-奥得攻势中，第14近卫师在波兰境内取得了惊人的进展，并因参与解放桑多梅日而获得列宁勋章。1945年1月22日，其指挥官在奥得河桥头堡的战斗中受致命伤。4月份，在进攻柏林的过程中，该师及其团获得了进一步的荣誉和勋章。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: The 14th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. The brigade participated in the German invasion of Yugoslavia in 1941. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 14th Light Division. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 14th Light Division was merged with other units and disbanded.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第14匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖两个步兵团（每个团有3个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。该旅参加了德国于1941年入侵南斯拉夫的行动。1942年1月，德军要求匈牙利提供更多东线兵力，大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而其编制表基本没有变化。该旅更名为第14轻型师。在斯大林格勒战役后对匈牙利陆军进行的一次总体重组中，第14轻型师与其他部队合并并解散。<cr>资料来源：Dr. Nigel Thomas 和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利军队》<cr>条目由 Chris Munson 提供

text: The 14th Mechanized Corps was formed in March 1941 at Kobryn under the command of Major General Stepan Oborin as part of the 4th Army in the Western Special Military District.<cr>The 205th Motorized Division deployed forward under attack from German aircraft on the morning of 22 June. The 30th Tank Division's 61st Tank Regiment concentrated west of Pruzhany by 0900. The division formed two columns, reinforced by artillery. The German artillery bombardment on the morning of 22 June destroyed much of the 22nd Tank Division's fuel, supplies, and ammunition at Brest. Air raids on the corps headquarters destroyed its radio, severing communications. Oborin moved the command post to the prearranged location in the forest around Tevli. As a result of the loss of communications, the corps was not alerted until German troops had already started to cross the Bug River. A tank battalion from the 22nd Tank Division was sent towards the river and was unable to stop the crossing. By the end of the morning, the combat units of the two tank divisions were around Zhabinka. At 1200, the 30th Tank Division sent a tank regiment into a counterattack against German amphibious tanks crossing the Lesnaya River to the north of Brest, which was repulsed by German air attacks. Oborin put the 14th Mechanized Corps on the defensive and ordered a counterattack with the entire corps the next morning. Attacking on the morning of 23 June, the 200 T-26s of the 22nd and 30th destroyed numerous German tanks but suffered heavier losses.<cr>The German forces continued their attack, inflicting heavy losses on the 22nd Tank Division and killing Puganov. The 30th Tank Division was broken through by the advance. Pruzhany and Kobrin were captured by German troops. Oborin was wounded and flew to Moscow to receive treatment, but he was arrested for desertion and later shot. After that, Tutarinov became the corps commander. The corps retreated towards Pinsk to the east. Until 28 June the corps held the Kalita-Omgovichi-Voloshevo line, blocking the German advance on the Warsaw Highway. During the fighting corps commissar Ivan Nosovsky was killed and Tutarinov wounded and evacuated. Now Bogdanov took command of the corps, which began withdrawing towards Osipovichi. By 1 July the corps had been reduced to 1,825 men with two T-26s. The corps was across the Dnieper by 3 July. The corps left the operational army on 30 June.<cr><cr>
translation: 第14机械化军于1941年3月在科布林成立，由少将斯捷潘·奥博林指挥，隶属于西部特别军事区的第4集团军。22日清晨，第205摩托化师在德国飞机攻击下向前推进。到上午9时，第30坦克师的第61坦克团集中在普鲁尚西以西。该师组建了两列纵队，并得到炮兵增援。22日清晨，德军炮兵对布列斯特的第22坦克师燃料、补给和弹药进行了猛烈轰炸，造成大量损失。空袭摧毁了机械化军司令部的电台，切断了通信联系。奥博林将指挥部转移到特夫利周围预先安排好的森林位置。由于通讯中断，该军直到德军开始渡过布格河时才得到警报。第22坦克师的一个坦克营被派往河边，但未能阻止德军渡河。到上午结束时，两个坦克师的战斗部队集中在扎宾卡附近。中午12点，第30坦克师派出一个坦克团对向北渡过列斯纳亚河的德国两栖坦克进行反击，遭到德机空袭而被击退。奥博林将第14机械化军转入防御，并命令全军于次日清晨发起反攻。6月23日清晨，第22和第30师的200辆T-26坦克摧毁了大量德国坦克，但自身也遭受了更重的损失。<cr>德军继续发动攻击，给第22坦克师造成了重大损失，并击毙了普加诺夫。第30坦克师被突破。普鲁尚和科布林被德军占领。奥博林负伤后飞往莫斯科接受治疗，但因擅离职守被捕并随后遭枪决。之后图塔里诺夫成为军长。该军向东撤退至宾斯克。截至6月28日，该军坚守卡利塔-奥姆戈维奇-沃洛谢沃一线，阻击德军沿华沙公路的推进。战斗中，军政委伊万·诺索夫斯基阵亡，图塔里诺夫负伤并被后送。现在博加诺夫接管了该军，开始撤退至奥斯皮奥维奇方向。到7月1日，该军仅剩1825人和两辆T-26坦克。该军于7月3日前进至第聂伯河对岸。该军在6月30日脱离作战集团军。<cr>指挥官报告：

text: Sent to Russia in 1941, the 14th Motorized Division was on the Eastern Front from the first day of the invasion until the fall of Berlin. It was part of Army Group Centre (later Army Group North) from beginning to end. In 1941, the 14th was prominent in the Battle of Vitebsk, the battles of encirclement at Vyazma-Bryansk, and the drive on Moscow. In late October 1941, it helped establish the Kalinin bridgehead on the upper Volga, between Moscow and Leningrad. The division spent 1942 in the Rzhev sector and played a part in the withdrawal from the Rzhev salient in 1943, and was then sent to Nevel, on the northern flank of the 4th Army.<cr>In July 1943, it was withdrawn, demotorized, and converted into a three-regiment infantry division, adding a new 101st Grenadier Regiment in the process; however, all of its grenadier regiments were reduced to two battalions. The unit was redesignated 14th Infantry Division on June 30 and was returned to the Eastern Front, where it fought at Bryansk (September 1943) and Vitebsk (October 1943-June 1944). It was the only division in the reserve of the 4th Army when Army Group Center was smashed in July 1944; as such, it escaped total destruction but was reduced to battle group strength. The remnants of the 14th Division fought on the Narew in northern Poland (August 1944-January 1945) and East Prussia (February-May 1945) until the end. It surrendered to the Soviets near Stuthof on the Frischen Nehrung, East Prussia, in May 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation:
1941年被派往俄罗斯的第14摩托化师从入侵的第一天起就一直在东线作战，直到柏林陷落。该师始终隶属于中央集团军群（后来是北方集团军群）。在1941年，第14摩托化师在维捷布斯克战役中表现突出，并参与了围绕维亚兹马-布良斯克的包围战以及向莫斯科的推进。1941年10月下旬，该师帮助建立了加里宁桥头堡，在莫斯科和列宁格勒之间的伏尔加河上游地区。第14摩托化师在1942年驻扎在热季夫地区，并参与了1943年的热季夫突出部撤离行动；随后被调往第四集团军北部翼的内夫尔。1943年7月，该师撤出战斗序列，取消摩托化并改编为一个拥有三个团的步兵师，在此过程中增加了新的第101掷弹兵团；然而，所有其掷弹兵团都被削减到两个营。该单位于6月30日重新命名为第14步兵师，并被送回东线作战，在布良斯克（1943年9月）和维捷布斯克（1943年10月至1944年6月）进行了战斗。当中央集团军群在1944年7月遭到重创时，它是第四集团军预备队中唯一一个师；因此，它避免了彻底毁灭但被削减到战斗群规模。第14师的残部在波兰北部纳雷夫河（1944年8月至1945年1月）和东普鲁士（1945年2月至5月）作战直至战争结束。该师于1945年5月在东普鲁士弗里施海湾区的斯图特霍夫附近向苏联投降。

参考文献：德国战斗序列第3卷 - 二战中的装甲、装甲掷弹兵和武装党卫军师，萨缪尔·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text: The 14th Panzer Division fought in the drive across the Ukraine, the Battles of Kiev, Kholm, Dnepropetrovsk, the Chernigovka Pocket (on the Sea of Azov), and in other battles on the southern sector, where it suffered serious losses. After the Russian winter offensive of 194142 had been checked, the division fought at Kharkov in May and in the drive across the Don and the Volga.. It was surrounded with the 6th Army in Stalingrad in November 1942, and was destroyed there in January 1943.<cr>The 14th Panzer Division was resurrected in Brittany, France, in the summer of 1943 and returned to southern Russia in time to take part in the Battle of Kiev that autumn. In more or less continuous retreat after that, it fought at Krivoi Rog, Kirovograd, and in the Dnieper battles, and suffered such heavy losses in the withdrawal from that river that it had to be rebuilt in the summer of 1944. That September it was sent to the northern sector of the front and was soon isolated in the Courland Pocket. After Berlin fell, elements of the 14th Panzer (along with parts of the 11th Infantry and 12th Panzer Divisions) were returned to Germany on the last available shipping before Army Group Courland capitulated, and thus it escaped Russian captivity. These units were selected because they had been the 'firefighters' of the army group when the Russians tried unsuccessfully to crush the pocket six times in the winter of 194445.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第14装甲师参加了在乌克兰的攻势、基辅战役、霍尔姆战役、第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克战役以及亚速海切尔尼戈夫卡包围圈和其他南部战线上的战斗，在这些战斗中该师遭受了严重损失。经过1941至1942年的俄罗斯冬季攻势后，该师于1942年5月在哈尔科夫作战，并参加了穿越顿河和伏尔加河的攻势。同年11月，第14装甲师与第六集团军一起在斯大林格勒被包围，在1943年1月被消灭。<cr>第14装甲师于1943年夏天在法国布列塔尼复活，并及时返回南部俄罗斯参加当年秋天的基辅战役。此后基本上处于撤退状态，该师参加了克里沃伊罗格、基罗斯夫卡和第聂伯河战役，在从这条河流撤离时遭受了如此严重的损失，以至于必须在1944年夏天重建。<cr>同年9月，它被派往前线北部地区，并很快在库尔兰包围圈中孤立起来。柏林陷落后，第14装甲师的部分部队（连同第11步兵师和第12装甲师的某些部分）在陆军集团军库尔兰投降前通过最后一班船返回德国，从而避免了被苏联俘虏的命运。<cr>这些单位之所以被选中是因为它们曾在1944至1945年冬季六次试图粉碎包围圈时成为陆军集团军的“救火队”。<cr>参考文献：《德国战斗序列 第三卷：二战中的装甲师、装甲掷弹兵师和武装党卫军师》萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text: The corps began the conflict as a part of 9th Army and was destroyed in August 1941. The corps was reformed in fall 1941 and participated in the Second Battle of Kharkov as part of 6th Army. It suffered heavy casualties and was disbanded after that battle. It was reformed in January 1944 as part of 59th Army and consisted of 191st and 378th Rifle Divisions. It participated in the Novogorod-Luga Operation and the crossing of the Dvina at Daugavpils. It was awarded the title of 'Stalin' for its performance in the 1944 campaigns. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军最初作为第9集团军的一部分参战，并于1941年8月被消灭。该军在1941年秋季重建，作为第6集团军参加了第二次哈尔科夫战役，在此役中伤亡惨重并解散。它于1944年1月再次重建，成为第59集团军的一部分，由第191步兵师和第378步兵师组成。该军参与了诺沃格罗德-卢加行动以及在道加瓦皮尔斯渡过迪维纳河的作战。由于其在1944年战役中的表现，它被授予“斯大林”称号。<cr>指挥官报告: Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert, 红军战斗序列：伟大卫国战争, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 14th Romanian Infantry Division was attached to the German XXX Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. As with most Romanian infantry divisions it was withdrawn to Romania after the Siege of Odessa where it was assigned to the Romanian IV Corps. During the Battle of Stalingrad it was assigned to the Romanian II Corps.<cr><cr>John Ellis, World War II A Statistical Survey<cr>Charles D. Pettibone, The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II Volume VII - Germany's and Imperial Japan's Allies & Puppet States<cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text:
The 14th Tank Corps was formed in May 1942 in the North Caucasus Military District with:
138th Tank Brigade
139th Tank Brigade<cr>The 14th Tank Corps is one of the 'shadow' units of the Soviet Army. While official documents confirm that it was formed and appeared in STAVKA Reserves as of 1 June, it was not completely formed until mid-July, and then in the middle of battle against the German advance across the southern Don river. The corps was formed from local resources by North Caucasus Military District and the Caucasus Fronts, which meant it was chronically short of equipment and troops throughout its brief existence. Soviet histories of the fighting in the Caucasus make no mention of the corps, which probably indicates that it never managed to get completely formed or operate as a corps. In mid-July the corps was complete by the 1942 Tank Corps standards, with:<cr>136th Tank Brigade
138th Tank Brigade
139th Tank Brigade
21st Motorized Rifle Brigade<cr>All of the component brigades had been formed locally in the North Caucasus, and by 28 July the corps had a total of just 15 tanks in it! By the end of August the subordinate brigades had been removed or destroyed, and 14th Tank Corps was a HQ only in STAVKA Reserves. The staff and HQ troops were moved to
Moscow, where on 26 November they officially formed the HQ of 6th Mechanized Corps.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp

第14坦克军于1942年5月在北高加索军区成立，包括：
第138坦克旅
第139坦克旅<cr>第14坦克军是苏军中的“影子”部队之一。官方文件确认该部队于6月1日组建并进入最高统帅部预备队，但实际上直到7月中旬才完全组建完毕，并在与德军穿越顿河南部的战斗中仓促成立。该军由北高加索军区和高加索方面军利用当地资源组建而成，这意味着其在整个短暂存在期间都严重缺乏装备和人员。苏方关于高加索战役的历史记录中未提及该军，这可能表明它从未完全组建或作为一支部队运作。7月中旬，按照1942年坦克军的标准，第14坦克军已全部成立，包括：
第136坦克旅
第138坦克旅
第139坦克旅
第21摩托化步兵旅<cr>所有组成部队均在北高加索当地组建。到7月28日，该军仅有15辆坦克！到8月底，下属各旅已被移除或被消灭，第14坦克军仅作为最高统帅部预备队中的司令部存在。指挥部和司令部人员被调往
莫斯科，在那里于11月26日正式组建了第6机械化军的司令部。<cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普著《二战苏军战斗序列 第二卷》

text:
The 14th Tank Division was formed July 1940 from 55th Light Tank Brigade at Narofominsk in Moscow Military District as part of 7th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
27th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - all light tanks
28th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - all light tanks
14th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
14th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1 light, 1 medium bn
14th Reconnaissance Battalion
14th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
14th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>The 14th Tank Division , not being stationed in the western border districts facing the Germans, did not have priority for equipment and personnel. Therefore, it remained little more than an expanded tank brigade until early 1941, with only about 200 light BT tanks by 1 October 1940. By 22 June 1941 the division had its full complement of tanks, over 350, on hand, but all were old light tanks, mostly BT-5 and BT-7.<cr>With the rest of 7th mechanized Corps, 14th Tank Division was under
Western Front near Smolensk by 1 July. On 6 - 7 July the division took part in the counter-attack at Orsha, where it lost most of its tanks. After 7th Mechanized Corps HQ was disbanded in mid-July, the division became a separate unit under the Yartsevo Direction Group of Western Front. Early in August 1941, 14th Tank Division was pulled back to Moscow Military District and disbanded. The personnel from the two tank regiments were used to form 27th and 28th Tank Brigades.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: The 153rd Field Training Division was sent to the Crimea in late 1942, it controlled the 23rd, 76th, and 257th Reserve Grenadier Regiments until the following spring, when it was converted into a field training unit. As such, it was no longer part of the Replacement Army, but came under the direct control of Army Group A and later Army Group South. In early 1944, as the Soviets neared the Crimea, the 153rd Field Training was evacuated to the lower Dnieper and became involved in combat southwest of Odessa. It remained on the line, fighting as an infantry division, and in September was routed near Bucharest, Romania, suffering heavy casualties in the process.<cr>Later the 153rd fought in Hungary and on December 14 was reorganized into the composition shown above. Its artillery regiment, however, had only one battalion. Later that month, the 153rd Grenadier was trapped, along with the 1st and 23rd Panzer Divisions, between the Danube and Lake Balaton. The 153rd held the town of Szekesfehervar for several days but was finally overrun on December 24, 1944. Remnants of the division escaped to form a battle group of approximately regimental strength. It was redesignated 153rd Grenadier Division in February 1945, and was still resisting as a part of the 1st Panzer Army (in the Deutsch-Brod Pocket and surrounded by the Red Army) when the war ended.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第153训练师于1942年末被派往克里米亚，控制了第23、76和257掷弹兵团直至次年春天。随后该师转为野战训练单位，不再隶属于后备军，而是直接归北方集团军群和后来的南方集团军群指挥。1944年初，随着苏联军队逼近克里米亚，第153训练师撤至第聂伯河下游地区，并在敖德萨西南部参与战斗。该师继续作为步兵师作战，在9月于罗马尼亚布加勒斯特附近被击溃，过程中遭受了严重伤亡。<cr>之后第153掷弹兵师在匈牙利作战，12月14日重组为上述编制。其炮兵团只有一个营。当月晚些时候，第153掷弹兵师与第1和第23装甲师一起被困于多瑙河和巴拉顿湖之间。<cr>该师坚守塞克什费赫尔瓦城数天后，终于在1944年12月24日被击溃。残部逃出并重组为一个团级战斗群。1945年2月重新编为第153掷弹兵师，并作为第1装甲集团军的一部分（位于德意志-布罗德包围圈内，被红军包围）继续抵抗直至战争结束。<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷：二战中的第1至第290步兵师，塞缪尔·W·米奇厄姆少校

text:
The 153rd Rifle Division was formed in the Ural Military District. On 22 June 1941 when the German Operation Barbarossa began, it was serving with the 51st Rifle Corps of the 22nd Army. By 29 June 1941, after the effective destruction of the 37th Rifle Division, a composite regiment (20th Rifle Regiment) formed mostly from 37th Rifle Division rear units (Tyl) was attached to the division.

The 153rd Rifle Division was one of the first divisions to be designated a Guards formation, becoming 3rd Guards Rifle Division on September 18, 1941, due to 'its combat record in Belarus and Smolensk'. It was reformed for the second time in February 1942, and later became the 57th Guards Rifle Division in December 1942, after fighting with the 63rd Army.

Reformed for the third time, during the East Prussian Offensive, on 6 April 1945 the Division, which was with the 69th Rifle Corps, 50th Army, was one of the divisions in the encirclement around Knigsberg, located at the northwest sector. The division to the right was the 216th Rifle Division, and to the left was the 110th Rifle Division. They attacked German positions and broke through the second defense line.<cr><cr>

第153步兵师成立于乌拉尔军区。1941年6月22日，德国巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师隶属于第51步兵军的第22集团军。到1941年6月29日，在有效摧毁了第37步兵师后，由第37步兵师后勤部队（图尔）组成的混成团（第20步兵团）加入该师。

第153步兵师是首批被指定为近卫编队的师之一，于1941年9月18日成为第3近卫步兵师，原因是“其在白俄罗斯和斯摩棱斯克地区的战斗表现”。该师第二次重组发生在1942年2月，并于1942年12月，在与第63集团军作战后，成为第57近卫步兵师。

第三次重组期间，在东普鲁士攻势中，1945年4月6日，隶属于第69步兵军、第50集团军的该师是包围哥尼斯堡地区的一个师之一。其右侧为第216步兵师，左侧为第110步兵师。他们攻击了德军阵地，并突破了第二道防线。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 154th Infantry Division was formed in 1939 as the III Replacement Troop Command. In November 1939 it was designated Replacement Division 154. The unit consisted of Saxon and Sudeten Germans and initially contained the 4th, 223rd, 255th and 256th Infantry Regiments and various support troops. In September 1942 it was redesignated the 154th Reserve Division and sent to northern Poland where it continued to train soldiers of the IV Military District. Some elements of the division saw combat as early as March 1944. The entire division was briefly committed in the summer of 1944 to the Ukraine, White Russia and southern Poland after the collaspe of Army Group Centre. In the fall of 1944 the division was withdrawn to reorganize and was designated the 154th Field Training Division. In April 1945 it was redesignated the 154th Infantry Division and was in eastern Germany when the Soviets launched their final offensive. On April 17, 1945 the division was overrun near Oderberg and ceased to exist with substantially all personnel being killed or taken prisoner by the Soviets.<cr><cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, German Order of Battle: 1st-290th Infantry divisions in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text: The 5th Cosseria Italian Infantry Division was formed in January 1942 as a garrison division. The division consisted of the 277th and 278th Infantry Regiments, the 156th Artillery Regiment and various support troops. The division was one of seven dispatched as reinforcements to the Eastern Front with the Italian 8th Army in the summer of 1942. In Russia the division was prmarily engaged in anti-partisan duties and as a reserve for the 8th Army. The division found itself, along with the rest of the 8th Army, stretched along a 160 mile section of the Don River between the Hungarian Second Army and Romanian 3rd Army on the German left flank at the start of Operation Little Saturn. By January 1943 the division was down to 1,300 survivors and was disbanded.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text: The 15th Guards Rifle Division was reformed as an elite infantry division of the Red Army in February, 1942, based on the 1st formation of the 136th Rifle Division, and served in that role until well after the end of WWII. The division had already distinguished itself during the Winter War with Finland in 1940 and had been decorated with the Order of Lenin; soon after its redesignation it also received its first Order of the Red Banner. It was in Southern Front as this time but was soon moved to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command where it was assigned to 7th Reserve Army in May, then to 28th Army in Southwestern Front in June, then to 57th Army in Stalingrad Front in July. It remained in that Army for the rest of the year, with one brief exception, until it was transferred to Don Front's 64th Army in January, 1943 during the closing stages of the battle of Stalingrad. In March this Army became 7th Guards Army and was railed to the northwest, joining Voronezh Front south of the Kursk salient. In the battle that followed the 15th Guards assisted in the defeat of Army Detachment Kempf, then took part in the summer offensive into Ukraine, winning one of the first battle honors at Kharkov. It remained in either 7th Guards or 37th Army into the spring of 1944. It saw action in the Nikopol-Krivoi Rog Offensive and was awarded the Order of Suvorov before being involved in the frustrating battles along the Dniestr River on the Romanian border. In June the division became part of 34th Guards Rifle Corps in 5th Guards Army and was redeployed north becoming part of 1st Ukrainian Front and taking part in the Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive into Poland. The 15th Guards made a spectacular advance across Poland during the Vistula-Oder Offensive and was further decorated with the Order of Kutuzov for forcing a crossing of the Oder River. It then saw action in the drive on Berlin in April and the Prague Offensive in May, winning a further battle honor and an unusual second Order of the Red Banner in the process. <cr><cr>
translation: 第15近卫步兵师于1942年2月作为红军精锐步兵师重建，基于原第136步兵师的首次组建。该师在冬季战争中已经表现出色，并获得列宁勋章；重新编组后不久又获得了第一个红旗勋章。当时它隶属于南方方面军，但很快被调往最高统帅部预备队，在5月加入第7预备集团军，6月转隶西南方向第28集团军，7月则进入斯大林格勒方向的第57集团军，并在该集团军中一直待到年底，仅有一个短暂例外。1943年1月，它被调往顿河方面军第64集团军，在斯大林格勒战役后期阶段。同年3月，该师所在的第28集团军改组为第7近卫集团军，并向西北方向移动，加入沃罗涅日方面军南部的库尔斯克突出部南侧。在随后的战斗中，第15近卫步兵师协助击败了坎普夫集群，然后参加了夏季进攻乌克兰的行动，在哈尔科夫赢得了第一个战役荣誉。该师一直留在第7近卫集团军或第37集团军直到1944年春季。它参与了尼科波尔-克里沃罗格攻势，并获得苏沃洛夫勋章；之后在罗马尼亚边境沿德涅斯特河的令人沮丧的战斗中发挥作用。6月，该师成为第5近卫集团军下属第34近卫步兵军的一部分，并被重新部署到北方，加入第1乌克兰方面军并参加了利沃夫-桑多梅日攻势进入波兰。第15近卫师在维斯瓦-奥得河进攻行动中横扫波兰，因强渡奥得河而荣获库图佐夫勋章。该师随后参加了4月的柏林攻势和5月的布拉格攻势，在此过程中又获得了一项战斗荣誉，并罕见地第二次获得了红旗勋章。 <cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: The 15th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 15th Light Division. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 15th Light Division was merged with other units and disbanded.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第15匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖两个步兵团（每个团有三个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多东线兵力，大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本保持不变。该旅更名为第15轻型师。在斯大林格勒战役后对匈牙利陆军进行的一次总体重组中，第15轻型师与其他部队合并并解散。<cr><cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas 和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利军队》<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>克里斯·芒森提供

text: he 15th Infantry Division remained in France until after the fall of Stalingrad, but in early February 1943, the High Command ordered the division to embark for Russia. On February 9, it was on the Atlantic coast; nine days later it was back in action on the Eastern Front, where it remained for the rest of the war. After fighting at Kharkov and in the Donets as part of the i>4th Panzer Army, the division suffered heavy losses at the Battle of Dnepropetrovsk in the summer of 1943. Reorganized as a six grenadier battalion unit, it fought in the battles of the southern Ukraine (including Krivoy Rog and Uman) and, in August 1944, was encircled at Kischinev, Romania, west of the lower Dnestr. It broke out, but suffered such serious losses that it had to be completely rebuilt. All of its grenadier regiments were reduced to two understrength battalions. Nevertheless, the 15th Infantr-now at battle group strength-was back in the line by October, opposing the Soviet advance through northern Hungary and Slovakia. By March 1945 it was reportedly in remnants. The next month it was surrounded-along with most of Army Group Center-in the large pocket at Deutsch-Brod (just north of Brunn [Brno] and east of Prague) and was there when the war ended. It surrendered to the Soviets on May 5.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第15步兵师一直留在法国直到斯大林格勒陷落之后，但在1943年2月初，最高指挥部命令该师前往俄罗斯。2月9日，它还在大西洋沿岸；九天后，它重新投入东线战场，并在那里作战直至战争结束。作为第4装甲集团军的一部分，该师在哈尔科夫和顿涅茨地区进行了战斗，在1943年夏季的第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克战役中遭受了重大损失。重组为六个掷弹兵营单位后，它参加了南部乌克兰（包括克里沃伊罗格和乌曼）的战斗，并于1944年8月在罗马尼亚基什尼奥夫被包围，位于德涅斯特河下游西岸。虽然成功突围，但遭受了严重损失，不得不完全重建。所有掷弹兵团都缩减为两个不足额营。尽管如此，第15步兵师（现已降级为战斗群）于10月重新投入匈牙利北部和斯洛伐克的苏军攻势中作战。到1945年3月，该师据说只剩下残部。下个月，它在德式-布罗德的大包围圈内被包围——与中央集团军群的大部分部队一起——位于布拉格东北方向、布拉恩[Brno]以东。战争结束时，该师向苏联投降，于5月5日放下武器。<cr><cr>德国二战步兵师战斗序列 第1-290师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text:
The 15th Mechanized Division was formed in May 1940 from 15th Rifle Division in Odessa Military District with:<cr>
47th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
321st Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
14th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd Tank Bns - 30 light tanks each
203rd Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
Reconnaissance Battalion
Antitank Battalion
Antiaircraft Battalion
Sapper Battalion<cr>
Even though 15th was one of the first four Mechanized Divisions formed, because it was formed from a Motorized Rifle Division with only 50 tanks, the 15th Mechanized was never brought up to strength in armor. In July 1940 it formed part of 2nd Mechanized Corps, but on 1 October 1940 still had lessthan 100 old light tanks on hand in the division. On 22 June 1941, 15th Mechanized Division had nearly full strength in personnel, artillery, and heavy weapons, but the 14th Tank Regiment was little more than a reinforced
battalion, with about 60 old BT tanks.<cr> 15th Mechanized Division fought under 2nd Mechanized Corps in retreat across southern Ukraine throughout June, July, and early August 1941. In mid- August 15th Mechanized Division was officially redesignated 15th Rifle Division by adding the 676th Rifle Regiment and removing 14th Tank Regiment, which formed the cadre for 14th Tank Brigade.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第15机械化军于1940年5月在敖德萨军区的第15步兵师基础上组建，包括：
第47摩托化步兵团
第1、2、3步兵营
第321摩托化步兵团
第1、2、3步兵营
第14坦克团
第1、2坦克营（每营各30辆轻型坦克）
第203摩托化榴弹炮团
第1、2、3营
侦察营
反坦克营
防空营
工兵营

尽管第15机械化军是首批组建的四个机械化军之一，但由于它是由只有50辆坦克的摩托化步兵师改编而成，因此其装甲力量从未达到满编。1940年7月，该军成为第2机械化军的一部分，但直到1940年10月1日，该军手上仍不足100辆老旧轻型坦克。<cr><cr>到1941年6月22日，第15机械化军在人员、炮兵和重武器方面几乎满编，但第14坦克团不过是一个加强营，拥有约60辆旧BT坦克。

从1941年6月至8月初，第15机械化军在第2机械化军指挥下，在乌克兰南部地区撤退作战。到8月中旬，第15机械化军正式改编为步兵师，并加入第676步兵团，同时解散了第14坦克团，后者成为第14坦克旅的基础。

Charles C. Sharp《苏联战斗序列 第一卷》

text: 15th Rifle Corps participated in the Winter War as part of 13th Army but was part of 5th Army in Kovel in Ukraine in June 1941. The corps had two distinguished commanders: at the oubreak of hostilities, its leader was Hero of the Soviet Union Ivan Ivanovich Fedyuninsky, who was given command of 42nd Army in July. Then, Hero of the Soviet Union and future Marshal Kirill Semyonovich Moskalenko took command and led the corps in a successful breakout from the Kiev Pocket in September 1941. The corps was disbanded after that battle. It was reformed in fall 1942 and consisted of 8th, 74th and 148th Rifle Divisions. It served again with 13th Army in the Battle of Kursk. Later, it was the principal attack corps in the Lvov-Sandomierz Operation in July 1944, at which time 322nd and 336th Rifle Divisions had joined the corps. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 第15步兵军参加了冬季战争，当时隶属于第13集团军。但在1941年6月，该军位于乌克兰科韦利，属于第5集团军。<cr>该军曾有两位杰出的指挥官：在敌对行动爆发时，其领导人是苏联英雄伊万·伊万诺维奇·费德尤宁斯基。他在7月被任命为第42集团军的指挥官。随后，另一位苏联英雄、未来的元帅基里尔·谢苗诺维奇·莫斯卡连科接任该军，并在1941年9月成功带领部队从基辅包围圈中突围。<cr>该军在此战后解散。它于1942年秋季重组，包括第8步兵师、第74步兵师和第148步兵师。该军再次隶属于第13集团军，在库尔斯克战役中服役。后来，它成为1944年7月利沃夫-桑多梅日行动中的主要攻击部队，此时第322步兵师和第336步兵师已加入该军。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 《红军在伟大卫国战争中的战斗序列》, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 15th Rifle Division was formed from the Inzensk Revolutionary Division in April 1919. The division was reformed as the 15th Motorized Division in September 1939 and took part in the occupation of Romanian Bessarabia and Nothern Bukovina in June and July 1940. At this time the division consisted of the 47th Motor Rifle Regiment, 321st Rifle Regiment, 14th Tank Regiment, 203rd Artillery Regiment and various support troops.<cr>At the start of Operation Barbarossa the division was part of the Odessa Military District. It first engaged Axis forces on June 24th, 1941 and retreated to the Dnestr River. In July 1941 the division was caught in the encirlement at Uman and largely destroyed although the divisional commander, Colonel Laskin, eventually escaped captivity. Some elements of the division escaped the encirlement in September 1941 and the division reverted to the 15th Rifle Division. The 676th Mountain Rifle Regiment of the 192nd Mountain Rifle Division was added as its third rifle regiment. It remained in southern Russian and took part in defending the Donbass region in the area near Artemovsk.<cr>The division took part in the Battle of Voronezh in the summer of 1942 and in the subsequent Voronezh-Kastornensk Operation to liberate the city in 1943. On the night of July 5th, 1943 reconnaissance units of the division captured a prisoner who showed that the German troops would launch an attack on Kursk during the same day. The division fought in the Battle of Kursk .<cr>Subsequent operations included the Chernigov-Pripyat and Gomel-Rechitsa Offensives in 1943, the Kalinkovichi-Mozyr Operation, Operation Bagration, the liberation of Baranovichi in 1944, the East Pomeranian Offensive, and the Battle of Berlin in 1945.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第15步兵师于1919年4月由因岑斯克革命师改编而成。该师在1939年9月重组为第15机械化师，并参加了1940年6月至7月占领罗马尼亚比萨拉比亚和北部布科维纳的行动。此时，该师包括第47摩托化步兵团、第321步兵团、第14坦克团、第203炮兵团以及各种支援部队。<cr>在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师隶属于敖德萨军区。它于1941年6月24日首次与轴心国军队交战，并撤退至德涅斯特河。1941年7月，该师在乌曼被包围并大部分被消灭，尽管师长拉斯金上校最终逃脱了俘虏的命运。该师的部分部队于1941年9月逃离了包围圈，恢复为第15步兵师，并加入了来自第192山地步兵师的第676山地步兵团作为第三支步兵团。该师驻扎在南部俄罗斯地区，并参加了保卫顿巴斯地区的战斗，在阿特莫夫斯克附近作战。<cr>1942年夏天，该师参与了沃罗涅日战役，并随后参加了解放该城市的沃罗涅日-卡斯特伦斯基行动。1943年7月5日夜，该师侦察部队俘获了一名德军士兵，表明德国军队将在同一天对库尔斯克发起攻击。该师参加了库尔斯克会战。<cr>后续作战包括1943年的切尔尼戈夫-普里皮亚季和戈梅利-雷奇察攻势、卡林科维奇-莫日尔行动、巴格拉季昂行动、解放巴拉诺维奇的战斗（1944年）、东波美拉尼亚攻势以及1945年的柏林会战。<cr>资料来源: 克里斯·芒森

text: The 15th Romanian Infantry Division was attached to the Romanian III Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. As with most Romanian infantry divisions it was withdrawn to Romania after the Siege of Odessa. The division was one of six Romanian infantry divisions encircled during the Battle of Stalingrad that became known as the General Lascar Group. On the 22nd of November 1942, refusing calls to surrender, out of food and down to 40 rounds per gun, the Group transmitted its last message and was destroyed.<cr><cr>John Ellis, World War II A Statistical Survey<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第15罗马尼亚步兵师在巴巴罗萨行动开始时隶属于罗马尼亚第三军。与其他大多数罗马尼亚步兵师一样，该师在敖德萨围城战后被撤回罗马尼亚境内。该师是六个在斯大林格勒战役中被包围的罗马尼亚步兵师之一，这些部队被称为拉斯卡尔将军集团。1942年11月22日，拒绝投降要求、弹尽粮绝的情况下，该集团发送了最后一封电报后被消灭。<cr>资料来源：John Ellis, 《第二次世界大战统计调查》<cr><cr>克里斯·芒森提供

text:
The 15th Tank Corps was formed in May 1942 at Moscow with:<cr><cr>96th Tank Brigade
228th, 331st Tank Battalions - T-34s and T-60s
96th Motorized Rifle Battalion
96th Machine-Gun Battalion
105th Tank Brigade
303rd, 304th Tank Battalions
105th Motorized Rifle Battalion
113th Tank Brigade
317th, 318th Tank Battalions
113th Motorized Rifle Battalion
17th Motorized Rifle Brigade - (Not assigned until June 1942)
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Battalions<cr><cr>The 15th Tank Corps was immediately assigned to 3rd Tank Army as that HQ formed in Moscow Military District in May from 58th Army. The army went into action in July in the Kozelsk Operation, one of several disastrous offensives launched by the Soviet commands on the northern half of the front in the summer of 1942. After this fiasco, 15th Tank Corps went into reserve for extensive rebuilding. From August to November 1942 the corps re-equipped with all T-34 and T-70 tanks.<cr>The corps went back into action at the end of December with 3rd Tank Army and fought through the advance that liberated Kharkov. Unfortunately, that action was followed by Manstein's counter-attack which virtually destroyed 3rd Tank Army. By early March 15th Tank Corps was back in reserve as a tankless remnant. The Corps went back to Moscow Military District, where it was both rebuilt and reinforced. By 1 July 1943 it was back under 3rd Guards Tank Army.<cr>On 14 July 1943 the 3rd Guards Tank Army went over to the offensive with Bryansk Front. Because of the...'persistent and aggressive actions...' of the tank units, on 26 July 1943 all the tank corps in the 3rd Guards Tank Army received their Guards designations, and 15th Tank Corps became 7th Guards Tank Corps.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp

第15坦克军于1942年5月在莫斯科成立，编成如下：
第96坦克旅
第228、331坦克营——T-34和T-60坦克
第96摩托化步兵营
第96机枪营

第303、304坦克营

第113坦克旅
第317、318坦克营
第113摩托化步兵营
第17摩托化步兵旅——（未分配，直到1942年6月）
第1、2、3步兵营

该坦克军立即被编入在莫斯科军区于5月成立的第3坦克集团军司令部。该集团军于7月在科泽尔斯克行动中投入战斗，在1942年夏季苏联北部战线指挥官发起的一系列灾难性攻势之一中参战。在这场失败之后，第15坦克军进入预备状态进行大规模重建。从1942年8月至11月，该军重新装备了全部T-34和T-70坦克。

该军于12月底再次投入战斗，在第3坦克集团军的指挥下解放哈尔科夫。不幸的是，这次行动之后曼施坦因发起反攻，几乎摧毁了第3坦克集团军。到1943年3月初，第15坦克军又成为一支无坦克的残部进入预备状态。该军返回莫斯科军区，在那里重建并得到加强。截至1943年7月1日，它再次隶属于第3近卫坦克集团军。

1943年7月14日，第3近卫坦克集团军在布良斯克方面军的指挥下发起进攻。由于“持续且积极的行动”，该集团军内的所有坦克军于1943年7月26日获得近卫称号，第15坦克军成为第7近卫坦克军。

The 15th Tank Divison was formed July 1940 in Kiev Special Military District as part of 8th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
29th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns
30th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns

15th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>This division was quickly brought up to authorized strength in personnel and tanks, having close to 300 light tanks by 1 October 1940. In February 1941, 15th Tank Division was shifted to the newly-formed 16th Mechanized Corps in the western Ukraine. By 22 June 1941 15th Tank Division was nearly full strength in manpower, but had only 75 old T-28 medium tanks, no heavy or modern tanks, and about 280 old light tanks. The division was short almost 30% of the authorized trucks and tractors. In August 1941, 15th Tank Division was disbanded.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

第15坦克师于1940年7月在基辅特别军区组建，隶属于第8机械化军，其编制如下：<cr>

text: The 160th Rifle Division was established at Gorki from the 6th Moscow People's Militia Rifle Division Jun 1941. Second formation with same number while first still existed, formed Nov 1941. Fought at Kharkov and Stalingrad. Became the 89th Guards Rifle Division Apr 1943. Created for third time at Gydnia Mar 1945. With 70th Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第160步兵师于1941年6月在高尔基从第6莫斯科人民民兵步兵师建立。同年11月，以同样番号建立了第二支建制部队，而第一支部队仍然存在。该师参加了哈尔科夫和斯大林格勒的战斗。1943年4月成为第89近卫步兵师。1945年3月在格丁尼亚第三次建立。1945年5月隶属于第二白俄罗斯方面军的第70集团军。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 161st Infantry Division first saw action in the invasion of Russia in June 1941, fighting at Bialystok, Smolensk, Vyazma, Klin, and Rzhev, and suffered heavy casualties against the Russian winter offensive before Moscow. It remained in the Rzhev salient until October 1942, before being withdrawn to northern France to rest and refit in the winter of 1942-43.<cr>Returning to action on the southern zone of the Eastern Front after the fall of Stalingrad, it fought at Kharkov (1943) and again sustained heavy losses at Dnepropetrovsk in the autumn of 1943, where it was reduced to battle group strength. It nevertheless took part in the withdrawal from the lower Dnieper Bend. On November 10, 1943, the Staff of the 161st Infantry Division became Staff, Corps Detachment A and assumed control of the remnants of the 161st, 293rd, and 355th Infantry Divisions (which were now designated division groups). Corps Detachment A was redesignated 161st Infantry Division on July 27, 1944. The new division included the 50th, 371st, and 866th Grenadier Regiments (two battalions each), the 241st Artillery Regiment, and the 241st Fusilier Battalion. The other divisional units bore the number 161. All of these units were destroyed in the vicinity of Jassy, Romania, in August and September 1944.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第161步兵师首次参战是在1941年6月入侵苏联的行动中，参加了比亚韦斯托克、斯摩棱斯克、维亚兹马、克林和日兹德拉等地的战斗，并在莫斯科附近的俄罗斯冬季攻势中遭受了重大伤亡。该师一直驻守在日兹德拉突出部直到1942年10月，之后撤退到法国北部，在1942-43年的冬天休整并进行整补。<cr>在斯大林格勒沦陷后重返东线南部战区作战时，参加了哈尔科夫（1943）的战斗，并于1943年秋季在第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克再次遭受重大损失，被削弱到战斗群规模。尽管如此，它仍然参与了从低地第聂伯河弯撤离的行动。<cr>1943年11月10日，第161步兵师指挥部改组为A军直属队，并接管了第161、293和355步兵师（现在被指定为师群）的残部。A军直属队于1944年7月27日重新命名为第161步兵师。<cr>新组建的师包括第50掷弹兵团、第371掷弹兵团和第866掷弹兵团（每个团两个营）、第241炮兵团以及第241轻步兵团。其他师属单位都标有“161”编号。所有这些部队都在1944年8月和9月的雅西地区被消灭。<cr>德国二战陆军战斗序列卷一：第1至第290步兵师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校
