text:
The 161st Rifle Division first formed from July 1 to Aug. 28, 1940, at Mogilev in the Western Special Military District based on cadres from 143rd Rifle Division and the 342nd and 356th Reserve Regiments, under the command of Colonel Alexey Mikhaylov. At the opening of Operation Barbarossa the division was in the same district.<cr><cr>On June 22, 1941, 161st Rifle Division was in transit from Drutyskie Camp in Mogilev Oblast to join 44th Rifle Corps near Minsk. Caught up in the confused fighting east of that city, it fought in 13th Army under both 44th and 2nd Rifle Corps. In August it was reassigned to 20th Army of Western Front, and on the 15th it reported the following strength figures: 695 officers; 787 NCOs; 5,306 men plus 400 replacements just received; 5,464 rifles; 32 SMGs; 20 HMGs; 74 LMGs; 1 AAMG; 12 76mm guns; and no antitank guns, howitzers or mortars. The division distinguished itself in the Battle of Smolensk for its stubborn defensive fighting and local counterattacks, and it was withdrawn to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command in September. On Sept. 18, in recognition of its earlier distinctions and its success in the Yelnya Offensive, the 161st became the fourth of the original four rifle divisions raised to the status of Guards on that date.<cr><cr>A division commander was finally assigned at the beginning of July, when the division was assigned to 3rd Reserve Army in the Reserve of the Supreme High Command. On July 10 this army became the 2nd formation of the 60th Army and joined Voronezh Front. In August the 161st was moved to 38th Army in the same Front, and on Dec. 18 became part of 18th (Separate) Rifle Corps, which in Feb. 1943 formed the basis for the 69th Army, but within a month the division was moved to 40th Army. During these months the division was participating in the winter counteroffensive that partly surrounded and destroyed German 2nd Army, and as this ground to a halt in the spring it found itself well into what became known as the Kursk salient.

In preparation for the Battle of Kursk, 40th Army was in the first echelon of the Voronezh Front defenses, but west of 6th Guards Army, which took the brunt of the German assault, and therefore saw little action. In August the division became part of 47th Rifle Corps. During the Battle of the Dniepr, on Sept. 23, the 161st forced a crossing of the river at Zarubentsy, becoming part of the Bukrin Bridgehead, and 32 men were awarded the Gold Star of the Hero of the Soviet Union. At the end of 1943 the division was moved to 18th Army, still in the same (now renamed 1st Ukrainian) Front, and in April, 1944, was once again moved to that front's 38th Army. Just before the Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive in July the 161st became part of 1st Guards Army, and it was here that it won the honorific 'Stanislavskihk' for liberating the Polish town of Stanislav during that operation. In August, 1st Guards Army was reassigned to 4th Ukrainian Front, and apart from a few weeks back again in 18th Army, the division served in that army and that front for the duration as part of 107th Rifle Corps. It ended the war with the official title of 161st Rifle, Stanislav, Order of the Red Banner, Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky Division.<cr><cr>
translation:
第161步兵师于1940年7月1日至8月28日在莫吉廖夫的西部特别军区组建，该军区基于第143步兵师和两个预备团（第342团和第356团）的骨干力量。在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师仍在同一军区。<cr>1941年6月22日，第161步兵师从莫吉廖夫州杜特斯基营地转移到明斯克附近的第44步兵军。由于在该城东部的混乱战斗中被卷入，它在第13集团军作战，并先后隶属于第44和第2步兵军。<cr>8月，该师被重新分配到西方方面军的第20集团军，在8月15日报告了以下兵力数字：695名军官；787名士官；5,306名士兵加上刚刚接收的400名补充人员；5,464支步枪；32支冲锋枪；20挺重机枪；74挺轻机枪；1挺高射机枪；12门76毫米炮；没有反坦克炮、榴弹炮或迫击炮。<cr>该师在斯摩棱斯克战役中因顽强的防御作战和局部反击而脱颖而出，并于9月被撤至最高统帅部预备队。9月18日，为了表彰其之前的荣誉以及在叶连纳攻势中的成功，第161步兵师成为第四支从最初的四支步兵师中晋升为近卫师的部队。<cr>该师在7月初终于被任命为师长，并于最高统帅部预备队的第3预备集团军中编入。7月10日，该集团军成为第60集团军的第二组建，并加入沃罗涅日方面军。8月，第161师转隶同一方面的第38集团军，在12月18日成为第18（独立）步兵军的一部分，后者于1943年2月构成了第69集团军的基础。然而在一个月内该师又被调往第40集团军。在这几个月里，该师参与了冬季反攻行动，部分包围并消灭了德国第2集团军。随着春季攻势停滞不前，该师发现自己深入到了后来被称为库尔斯克突出部的地区。

为库尔斯克战役做准备时，第40集团军是沃罗涅日方面军第一梯队的防御力量，但位于第6近卫集团军西侧，后者承受了德国突击的主要压力，因此该集团军几乎没有参与战斗。8月，该师成为第47步兵军的一部分。在第聂伯河战役中，9月23日，第161师在扎鲁别茨强行渡过了河流，成为了布克林桥头堡的一部分，并有32名士兵被授予苏联英雄金星奖章。到1943年底，该师转移到了第18集团军，仍然在同一（此时改名为第一乌克兰）方面军内，在1944年4月又被调往该方面军的第38集团军。在7月初发起利沃夫-桑多梅日攻势之前，第161师成为第1近卫集团军的一部分，并在此期间因解放波兰城镇斯坦尼斯瓦夫而获得了“斯坦尼斯拉夫斯基”荣誉称号。8月，第1近卫集团军被重新分配到第四乌克兰方面军，在此之后除了短暂回到第18集团军外，该师一直在该集团军和该方面军内服役，并成为第107步兵军的一部分。战争结束时，该师的官方名称为第161步兵斯坦尼斯拉夫斯基红旗波将金师。<cr> <cr>

text: The 162nd Infantry Division took part in the first campaigns in Russia and was continuously engaged from June 1941 until the first winter offensive was checked in early 1942, fighting at Bialystok, Smolensk, Vyazma, and Rzhev, among other battles. The 162nd suffered serious losses at Kalinin (near Moscow) in December 1941, and continued to serve on the central sector of the Eastern Front until the spring of 1942.<cr>At this point, the 162nd Infantry Division was taken out of the line and partially disbanded. Most of its survivors were transferred to the 129th Infantry Division. The divisional staff, however, was sent to Stettin, where it was placed in charge of volunteers from the former Soviet Union. Its commander at this time was Major General Professor Doctor Oscar Ritter von Niedermayer, a well-known specialist in foreign affairs. Perhaps for this reason the 162nd was selected to train Ost (Eastern) battalions, which were established by the order of the High Command in late 1941. These troops--including people from Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazak, Turkestan, Iran, Afghanistan, and other--all volunteered to fight in German service against communism. After they left the 162nd, these battalions (collectively called 'Turks') were sent to other active divisions. The 162nd was reformed as a combat unit on May 21, 1943, when it was designated the 162nd (Turkestan) Infantry Division. It initially set up training operations in Poland in August 1943, but was soon was transferred to Slovenia, where it simultaneously conducted training and anti-partisan operations along the Ljubljana-Trieste railroad.<cr>Early in 1944 the 162nd was transferred to Italy, where it surrnedered to the British in 1945. Many of its personnel were turned over to the Russians after the war and disappeared.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第162步兵师参加了在俄罗斯进行的第一批战役，并从1941年6月一直战斗到1942年初冬攻势被遏制。该师曾在比亚韦斯托克、斯摩棱斯克、维亚兹马和日兹赫等地作战，以及其他许多战场中遭受严重损失。1941年12月在加里宁（靠近莫斯科）的战斗中，第162步兵师又蒙受了重大伤亡，并一直驻守东线中央战区直到1942年初。<cr>此时，第162步兵师被撤出前线并部分解散。其大部分幸存者被调往第129步兵师。而该师的指挥部则被派往什切青，并负责管理来自前苏联地区的志愿者。当时指挥官是少将教授博士奥斯卡·冯·尼德迈尔，他是一位著名的外国事务专家。<cr>或许正因为如此，第162步兵师被选中训练东方营（Ost），这些部队由最高统帅部在1941年末下令建立。这些部队包括来自格鲁吉亚、亚美尼亚、阿塞拜疆、哈萨克斯坦、突厥斯坦、伊朗、阿富汗及其他地区的人员，他们志愿为德国军队作战反对共产主义。<cr>离开第162步兵师后，这些营（统称为“土耳其人”）被派往其他活跃的部队。该师于1943年5月21日重组为战斗单位，并被指定为第162（突厥斯坦）步兵师。它最初在波兰设立训练行动，在1943年8月，但很快就被转移到斯洛文尼亚，在那里同时进行培训和反游击队作战，特别是在卢布尔雅那-的里雅斯特铁路沿线。<cr>1944年初，第162步兵师被调往意大利，在1945年向英国人投降。战后许多人员被移交给苏联并从此消失。<cr>德国战斗序列：从第1到第290步兵师（二战）<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham Jr. 著，第一卷

text: The 162nd Rifle Division was formed with 5600 men on 1 June 1941 in Kharkov Military District, established at Artemovsk prior to Jun 1941. Wiped out at Vyazma Oct 1941. Recreated at Verchniy Ufalev Jan 1942. Inactivated Jul 1942. Recreated at Tashkent from the Central Asia NKVD Division Oct 1942. Fought near Baranov, in Poland, and in the Berlin Operation. With 70th Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front May 1945.162nd Rifle Division
translation: 第162步兵师于1941年6月1日在哈尔科夫军区组建，该师在1941年6月前已先期建立于阿尔捷莫夫斯克。该师于1941年10月在维亚兹玛被消灭。1942年1月在乌法上重建。1942年7月停编。同年10月，从中亚内务人民委员部师在塔什干重建第162步兵师。该师参加了巴诺夫（波兰）附近的战斗以及柏林战役。1945年5月隶属于第二白俄罗斯方面军的第70集团军。

text:
The 163rd Mechanized Division was formed 1 July 1940 from 163rd Rifle Division in Leningrad Oblast, as part of 1st Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
529th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
729th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
81st Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns
365th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
Reconnaissance Battalion
Antitank Battalion
Antiaircraft Battalion
Sapper Battalion<cr><cr>The 163rd Mechanized Division was very nearly full-strength in armor by 22 June 1941, but with all older BT-5 and BT-7 light tanks. At the end of June the division was ordered south from its peacetime station near Pskov, and went into action against 4th Panzer Group at Daugavpils on 2 - 3 July.<cr>
Like most other Soviet divisions equipped with the older light tanks in 1941, the 163rd quickly lost all of its tanks through enemy action, air attack, or, most commonly, mechanical breakdowns. After mid-August, the division was being used as a regular rifle division in 11th and then in 34th Army in the forested swamps around Lake Ilmen. In mid-September 1941 163rd Mechanized Division was converted officially into 163rd Rifle Division by disbanding the tank regiment and adding 1318th (reserve) Rifle Regiment to the division.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

第163机械化军于1940年7月1日由列宁格勒州的第163步兵师改编而成，隶属于第一机械化军：<cr>
第529摩托化步兵团
第1、2、3步兵营

第1、2、3步兵营

第1、2、3营

反坦克营
防空营
工兵营<cr>@在1941年6月22日之前，第163机械化军的装甲部队几乎满编，但全部是老旧的BT-5和BT-7轻型坦克。6月底该部从战前驻地普斯科夫附近南下，在7月2日至3日期间与第四装甲集团军在道加瓦皮尔斯交火。<cr>
如同1941年装备旧式轻型坦克的大多数苏联部队一样，第163机械化军很快因敌方行动、空袭或最常见的机械故障而损失了所有坦克。8月中旬之后，该部被用作常规步兵师，在第11集团军和随后在第34集团军中作战，驻扎在伊利姆湖周围的森林沼泽地区。1941年9月中旬，第163机械化军正式改编为第163步兵师，解散了坦克团，并加入了第1318（预备）步兵团。<cr>

text:
The 166th Rifle Division was formed at Tomsk in September 1939. It was commanded by Colonel Alexey Holzinev. On 22 June 1941, the division was in its summer quarters south of Yurga. The division hastily moved to Tomsk and was reequipped with new uniforms, weapons and ammunition. On 26 June, the first train of the division left for Smolensk. The division became part of the 24th Army and by mid-July was defending the Bely-Dorogobuzh-Yelnya area. On 19 July, two battalions of the 517th Rifle Regiment and the 499th Artillery Regiment engaged in battle with German troops at Lake Shchuchye. Days later, Soviet troops began counterattacks in the Smolensk area. The division was initially part of Group Khomenko but was transferred to Group Kalinin on 22 July. Along with the 91st Rifle Division, the 166th was to attack towards Dukhovshchina. On 24 July, it reached Lelimovo but was forced to withdraw to the area between Pakikino and Pochinok.

The division continued to attack and in early August captured Gutarovo, only 32 kilometers from Yartsevo. On 11 August, the 517th and 735th Rifle Regiments broke through German defences and provided a corridor for Ivan Boldin's group to escape from its encirclement. Colonel Mikhail Dodonov became the division commander on 31 August. In late September, the depleted division was moved to the second echelon to receive replacements. On 2 October, the German troops began Operation Typhoon and the division was forced to take up positions at Kholm-Zhirkovsky. On 4 October, Western Front decided to withdraw from the Gzhatsk defensive line, but the division could not retreat. On 7 October, the division was encircled in the Vyazma Pocket. Only 517 soldiers from the division escaped from the encirclement. A number of soldiers from the division became partisans in the area. The division was officially disbanded on 27 December 1941. 

Poirer and Connor, in their Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, 1985, write that it was established at Tomsk prior to June 1941. Wiped out Vyazma Oct 1941.<cr><cr>The division was reformed from the 437th Rifle Division in January 1942 at Chebarkul. The division was mostly composed of soldiers from Chelyabinsk and Sverdlovsk Oblasts, Bashkortostan and Kazakhstan. It was commanded by Major General Fyodor Shchekotsky. Between 29 January and 16 February 1942, the division was transported to Lyubim.

Fought at Kursk and in Kurland. With 6th Guards Army of the Kurland Group (Leningrad Front) May 1945.<cr><cr>

text:
The 167th Rifle Divison was formed at Balashov in the Volga Military District in July 1940, under the command of Kombrig Vasily Rakovsky. Just before the beginning of Operation Barbarossa, the June 1941 German invasion of the Soviet Union, the division became part of the 63rd Rifle Corps. After the beginning of Operation Barbarossa, the division and its corps were sent to the front, joining the 21st Army of the Reserve of the High Command (Stavka reserve). From 28 June, the 167th fought in defense of positions between Rogachev and Zhlobin. During the Battle of Smolensk the division repulsed German attempts to cross the Dnieper. Launching a counterattack, it advanced to the line of the Drut River and remained there until 12 August, when it was withdrawn to the army reserve. Relocated to the area of Dovsk, the division defended the latter as part of the 67th Rifle Corps, fighting in encirclement from 13 August. Due to its loss of contact with the 67th Rifle Corps, the 167th returned to the control of the 63rd Rifle Corps from 14 August. In the encirclement, Rakovsky decided to destroy heavy weapons and ordered the division to escape in groups. He led a group of 25 others out of the encirclement with their weapons in the sector of the 155th Rifle Division of the Bryansk Front on 18 September; about 2,500 men of the division escaped the encirclement. The units that escaped encirclement were disbanded and their men used to reinforce other units.

On 16 December 1941, the 438th Rifle Division was formed in the Ural Military District. On 23 January 1942, it became the 167th Rifle Division (Second Formation). The division was recreated at Ssucho Lug in February 1942 and fought near Bryansk and at Kursk. The division fought in the Battle of the Dnieper. Division personnel Major Fyodor Bruy, Junior lieutenant Alexander Bondarev, Sergeant major Arkady Chepelev, Senior sergeant Alexey Gabrusev, Sergeant Andrian Zhuravlev and Private Dmitry Yemelyanov, among others, were awarded the title Hero of the Soviet Union for their actions during the battle. The division fought in the Carpathians and in Hungary. The division was with the 1st Guards Army of the 4th Ukrainian Front in May 1945. The division ended the war with the honorifics 'Sumy-Kiev Twice Red Banner'.<cr><cr>
translation:
第167步兵师于1940年7月在伏尔加河军区的巴拉萨沃成立，由科莫布拉格瓦西里·拉科夫斯基指挥。巴巴罗萨行动开始前，在1941年6月德国入侵苏联之前，该师成为第63步兵军的一部分。巴巴罗萨行动开始后，该师及其所属军被派往前线，加入最高统帅部预备队的第21集团军。从6月28日起，第167师在罗加切夫和日洛宾之间防御阵地。在斯摩棱斯克战役期间，该师击退了德军试图渡过第聂伯河的企图，并发起反攻推进至德鲁特河一线，直到8月12日被撤回集团军预备队。重新部署到多夫斯基地区后，该师作为第67步兵军的一部分防御后者，在包围圈中作战，从8月13日起。由于与第67步兵军失去联系，第167师于8月14日起归第63步兵军指挥。在包围圈中，拉科夫斯基决定销毁重武器，并命令该师分组突围。9月18日，在布良斯克方面军的第155步兵师辖区，他带领25人小组携带武器从包围圈中逃脱；大约有2,500名士兵成功逃离了包围圈。逃出包围圈的部队被解散，其人员用于增援其他单位。

1941年12月16日，第438步兵师在乌拉尔军区组建。1942年1月23日，该师改称为第167步兵师（第二次组建）。该师于1942年2月在苏乔卢格重建，并参加了布良斯克附近的战斗和库尔斯克的战斗。该师还参与了第聂伯河战役。少校费奥多尔·布鲁伊、中尉亚历山大·邦达列夫、军士长阿尔卡季·切佩列夫、上士阿列克谢·加布鲁舍夫、下士安德烈·朱拉韦利和士兵迪米特里·叶梅利亚诺夫等人员因在战斗中的表现被授予苏联英雄称号。该师还参加了喀尔巴阡山脉的战斗以及匈牙利的战斗。1945年5月，该师隶属于第4乌克兰方面军的第1近卫集团军。<cr>该师以“苏梅-基辅两次红旗”荣誉称号结束战争。

text: The 168th Infantry Division was formed in December 1939 as part of the 7th Wave. It contained the 417th and 429th Infantry Regiments, 248th Light Artillery Battalion and various support units. The 168th was attached to the German Sixth Army in Army Group South during Operation Barbarossa. The division contained the 417th, 429th and 442nd Infantry Regiments, the 248th Artillery Regiment and various support units. In August 1942 two Nebelwerfer batteries were attached to the artillery regiment. In November 1943 the division was merged with the 223rd Infantry Division. The division was almost destroyed at the Baranov bridgehead and was reformed in Silesia. The division was captured by the Russians in January 1945 near Glatz in Lower Silesia.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text: The 168th Rifle Division was established at Sortovala prior to 12.39, fought in Winter War. With 7th Army on 22 June 1941, fought near Leningrad and Stalingrad. With 22nd Army of the RVGK 5.45.<cr><cr>

text: The 169th Rifle Division was formed as an infantry division of the Red Army beginning in late August, 1939, as part of the pre-war Soviet military build-up. It saw service in the occupation force in western Ukraine in September. The German invasion found it still in Ukraine, fighting back to the Dniepr until it was nearly destroyed. The partly-rebuilt division fought again at Kharkov, then was pulled back into reserve and sent deep into the Caucasus where it fought south of Stalingrad throughout that battle. Following another major redeployment the division helped in the liberation of Oryol, and the following race to the Dnieper. In 1944 and 1945 it was in 1st and 2nd Belorussian Fronts, participating successfully in the offensives that liberated Belarus, Poland, and conquered eastern Germany. It ended the war on the Elbe River.<cr><cr>
translation: 第169步兵师于1939年8月下旬作为红军的步兵师组建，是战前苏联军事扩张的一部分。该师在9月被部署到占领西部乌克兰的部队中。德国入侵时，它仍在乌克兰作战，一直抵抗至第聂伯河附近，几乎被消灭。部分重建后，该师再次参与了哈尔科夫战役，随后被调入预备队，并深入高加索地区，在斯大林格勒南部持续战斗。经过另一次重大调动，该师帮助解放了奥廖尔，并参加了向第聂伯河的冲刺。1944年和1945年，它在白俄罗斯第一方面军和第二方面军服役，成功参与了解放白俄罗斯、波兰以及征服东德的攻势行动。战争结束时，该师驻扎在易北河附近。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 16th Air Army began forming on 8 August 1942 during the Battle of Stalingrad and originally included the 220th Fighter Aviation Division (IAD) and 228th Assault Aviation Division (ShAD) of the 8th Air Army, as well as two separate aviation regiments. Around the end of August and the beginning of September, the 283rd IAD and 291st Mixed Aviation Division (SAD) arrived from the Reserve of the Supreme High Command. On 4 September, the army had 152 serviceable aircraft, composed of Yakolev Yak-1 and Lavochkin-Gorbunov-Gudkov LaGG-3 fighters, Ilyushin_Il-2 Shturmovik ground attack aircraft, and Petlyakov Pe-2 dive bombers.<cr>It took part in Operaton Uranus, the counteroffensive that successfully cut off German troops in Stalingrad, as part of the Don Front during November and December 1942, under the command of Major General Sergei Rudenko. On 19 November, when the offensive began, the army had a total of 249 serviceable aircraft.<cr>It was involved in the Battle of Kursk , and was part of the 1st Belorussian Front for the liberation of Belarus, the Lublin-Brest Offensive, and the assault on Berlin.<cr><cr>
translation: 第16空军集团军于1942年8月8日在斯大林格勒战役期间开始组建，最初包括来自第8空军集团军的第220战斗机航空师和第228突击航空师以及两个独立航空团。到8月底和9月初，从最高统帅部预备队调来了第283战斗机航空师和第291混合航空师。9月4日，该集团军拥有152架可服役飞机，包括雅克-1、拉格-3战斗机，伊尔-2强击机以及佩-2俯冲轰炸机。<cr>它参与了天王星行动（成功切断斯大林格勒德军的反攻），作为顿河方面军的一部分，在1942年11月和12月期间，由少将谢尔盖·鲁登科指挥。当进攻于11月19日开始时，该集团军共有249架可服役飞机。<cr>它还参与了库尔斯克战役，并作为第1白俄罗斯方面军的一部分解放白俄罗斯、进行卢布林—布列斯特攻势以及对柏林的突击。<cr><cr>

text: The Sixteenth Army took part in the Battle of France. It was then deployed with Army Group North during Operation Barbarossa, the German invasion of the Soviet Union. It fought its way into northern Russia where in January 1942 part of it was encircled by the Soviets near Demyansk. Hitler forbade a withdrawal and the Army was re-supplied by air until a land corridor was opened in April 1942. It was subsequently involved in the siege of Leningrad. The Soviets relieved Leningrad in January 1944.<cr>On February 19, 1944, the Soviet 2nd Baltic Front launched a fresh set of attacks against the German 16th Army around Kholm. The Soviet 22nd Army made good progress in the initial assault. These attacks greatly diminished the 16th Army. It, along with the 18th Army was cut off in the Courland Peninsula when the Soviets launched their summer and autumn offensives of 1944. It stayed trapped there until the end of the war. After the war, 250,000 German troops trapped in the Courland Pocket were marched into captivity, many were never heard from again.<cr><cr>
translation: 第16集团军参加了法国战役。随后在巴巴罗萨行动中，它被部署到北方集团军群参与德国入侵苏联的行动。该集团军一路向北俄罗斯推进，在1942年1月其部分兵力在德梅伊安斯克附近遭到苏军包围。希特勒禁止撤退，并通过空投补给第16集团军，直到1942年4月开辟出一条陆地走廊。随后该集团军参与了列宁格勒的围城战。苏联于1944年1月解除了对列宁格勒的包围。<cr>1944年2月19日，苏军第2波罗的海方面军在霍尔姆地区对德军第16集团军发起新一轮突击。苏军第22集团军在最初的突击中取得显著进展。这些攻击大大削弱了第16集团军。<cr>当苏联于1944年夏季和秋季发动攻势时，它与第18集团军一起被切断在库尔兰半岛上，直到战争结束才得以解脱。战后，被困在库尔兰包围圈内的25万德军士兵被押送至战俘营，许多人从此杳无音信。<cr><cr><cr>1944年2月19日，苏军第2波罗的海方面军在霍尔姆地区对德军第16集团军发起新一轮突击。苏军第22集团军在最初的突击中取得显著进展。这些攻击大大削弱了第16集团军。<cr>当苏联于1944年夏季和秋季发动攻势时，它与第18集团军一起被切断在库尔兰半岛上，直到战争结束才得以解脱。战后，被困在库尔兰包围圈内的25万德军士兵被押送至战俘营，许多人从此杳无音信。<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: Soon after the commencement of Operation Barbarossa a crisis situation developed on the Western Front sector of the frontline, and on 26 June 1941 16th Army was ordered to redeploy to the area of Orsha - Smolensk. However, the breakthrough of the German 11 Panzer Division in the direction of Ostrov during the afternoon of 26 June required an emergency response. Lieutenant-General Lukin took part of the 109th Motorised Division directly from disembarkation from the trains and directed them towards the enemy. The units involved were designated 'Group Lukin.'<cr>On 1 July 1941 16th Army consisted of the 32nd Rifle Corps (with the 46th and 152nd Rifle Divisions), two artillery regiments, and the 5th Mechanised Corps (13th and 17th Tank Divisions and the 109th Mechanised Division). 126th Corps Artillery Regiment and the 112th Separate Anti-aircraft Artillery Battalion.<cr>Most of the 16th Army began concentrating in the region of Smolensk, but the 5th Mechanised Corps was transferred to the 20th Army and participated in the counterattack at Lepel 6-9 July. On 9 July a status report from the army chief of staff said that the command group, 32nd Rifle Corps, and some units of 5th Mechanised Corps were still at peacetime establishment strength. About this time the separate 57th Tank Division from the Far East joined the army, and on 20 July elements of the 129th Rifle Division arrived as well.<cr>The Army HQ was disbanded on 8 August 1941 after encirclement (the Battle of Smolensk (1941)) just west of Smolensk as part of the Western Front.<cr>As part of a restructuring of the forces of Western Front, on 10 August 1941 the second formation of 16 Army was created from forces in the Yartsevo area and placed under the command of Major-General Konstantin Rokossovsky. In September 1941, he was tasked with defending the Volokolamsk Highway, and preventing any advance by German forces towards Moscow. By late November, 16th Army had gradually been forced back to the line Krasnaya Polyana-Kryukovo-Istra, but here it held firm until the Red Army went over to the offensive in December. In January 1942 the Army conducted an offensive on the Gzhatsk axis.<cr>In the second half of January 1942, the forces of 16 Army were transferred to the command of 5th Army, and 16 Army Headquarters was deployed to the area of Sukhinichi, where the Army HQ took command of some of the troops and defensive positions of 10th Army. By February the frontline positions in the Sukhinichi area had stabilized.<cr>On 15 July 1942, Rokossovsky was transferred to take command of the Bryansk Front as part of new command arrangements made by Soviet High Command in response to the disastrous Battle of Voronezh (1942). He was replaced by Lieutenant-General Hovhannes Bagramyan.<cr>On 11 August 1942 German forces mounted a surprise offensive on the southern flank of Western Front, splitting 61st Army from 16th Army, which was not taking part in the Rzhev-Sychevka Offensive Operation. The German forces threatened Bagramyan's left flank and he reacted quickly, moving his forces to counter the German threat and halting their advance on 9 September.<cr>Until May 1943 the troops of the Army conducted defensive and offensive battles on the Zhizdrinsky District axis. On 1 May 1943, on the basis of Stavka directives of 16 April 1943, the army was reorganized into the 11th Guards Army in the Western Front.<cr>16th Army was formed for the third time on 10 July 1943 in the Far Eastern Front and was based on the Special Rifle Corps. From the spring of 1945 the Army was responsible for the defense of the Soviet state border with Japan on the island of Sakhalin, and also along the mainland coast of the Tatar Strait from Sovetskaya Gavan to Nikolaevsk-on-Amur.<cr><cr>
translation:
巴巴罗萨行动开始不久，西方面军前线就出现危机。1941年6月26日，第16集团军接到命令调往奥尔沙-斯摩棱斯克地区。然而，在当天下午，德国第11装甲师在奥斯托夫方向突破，需要紧急应对。卢金中将指挥部分刚从火车上下来的第109摩托化师直接投入战斗，并向敌人发起进攻。这些部队被命名为“卢金集团”。

1941年7月1日，第16集团军包括第32步兵军（辖第46和第152步兵师）、两个炮兵团、以及第5机械化军（辖第13和第17坦克师及第109摩托化师）。此外还有第126集团军炮兵团和第112独立防空高射炮营。

大部分的第16集团军开始在斯摩棱斯克地区集结，但第5机械化军被调往第20集团军，并参与了7月6日至9日在列佩尔的反击战。7月9日，集团军参谋长报告称指挥组、第32步兵军以及部分第5机械化军仍保持和平时期的编制规模。大约在这个时候，远东独立第57坦克师加入该集团军，而7月20日，第129步兵师的部分部队也抵达。

由于被包围（斯摩棱斯克战役），第16集团军司令部于1941年8月8日在斯摩棱斯克西面的西方方面军内解散。作为西方方面军重组的一部分，1941年8月10日，第16集团军第二次组建完成，由雅尔策沃地区的部队组成，并交由康斯坦丁·罗科索夫斯基少将指挥。1941年9月，他被赋予保卫沃尔科拉姆斯公路的任务，并阻止德军向莫斯科推进。到11月下旬，第16集团军逐渐退守至克拉斯诺波利亚纳-克鲁科沃-伊斯特拉一线，在此坚守直至红军于12月转入进攻。1942年1月，该集团军在格扎茨克方向发动攻势。<cr><cr>1942年1月下旬，第16集团军的部队被转交给第5集团军指挥，第16集团军司令部部署至苏欣奇地区，在那里接管了部分第10集团军的部队和防御阵地。到2月，苏欣奇地区的前线位置趋于稳定。<cr><cr>1942年7月15日，罗科索夫斯基被调任指挥布良斯克方面军，这是苏联最高统帅部为应对1942年沃罗涅日战役的惨败而做出的新指挥安排的一部分。他由霍瓦赫·巴格拉米扬中将接替。<cr><cr>1942年8月11日，德军在西方方面军南部翼发起突袭进攻，使第61集团军与未参与热季夫-斯切夫卡攻势的第16集团军分离。德军威胁巴格拉米扬左翼，他迅速反应，调动部队应对德军威胁，并于9月9日阻止了其推进。<cr><cr>直到1943年5月，该集团军的部队在日兹德拉区轴线上进行了防御和进攻战斗。1943年5月1日，根据最高统帅部1943年4月16日的指示，该集团军重组为西方方面军第11近卫集团军。<cr>第16集团军第三次于1943年7月10日在远东方面军中组建，并以特别步兵军为基础。从1945年春季开始，该集团军负责保卫苏联在日本萨哈林岛以及鞑靼海峡大陆海岸索维etskaya Gavan到尼古拉耶夫斯科耶-阿穆尔边界的国界。<cr>第16集团军

text: Formed 2/14/43 from 112th Cavalry Division, it was part of VII Guards Cavalry Corps. It inherited the title of 'Bakshir' from 112th Cavalry Division. The division fought at Chernigov in September 1943 and in the Kalinkovichi-Mozyr Offensive in January 1944. It was awarded the honorific 'Mozyr' as a result of its performance in this battle. It participated in the Lublin-Brest Offensive in June 1944, and was awarded the honorific 'Lublin'. In 1945, it was part of the East Pomeranian Offensives in February 1945 and was near Berlin at the end of the war. <cr><cr>The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II: volume V - Book B Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Trafford, 2009 <cr><cr> Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert,The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 成立于1943年2月14日，由第112骑兵师改编而成，并成为第七近卫骑兵军的一部分。该师继承了“巴库什”这一称号。它于1943年9月在切尔尼戈夫作战，并参加了1944年1月的卡林科维奇-莫吉廖夫进攻战役，因其在这场战斗中的表现而获得“莫吉廖夫”的荣誉称谓。该师还参与了1944年6月的卢布林-别列斯攻势，并因此获得了“卢布林”的荣誉称谓。在1945年，它参加了2月份的东波美拉尼亚攻势，并且在战争结束时靠近柏林。<cr>参考文献：《第二次世界大战中各国军队组织与战斗序列：苏联社会主义共和国联盟卷V-B》（Trafford出版社，2009年）<cr>Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert，《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，Presidio Press出版社，1985年<cr>词条由Stewart King提供

text: The 16th Guards Rifle Division was reformed as an elite infantry division of the Red Army in February, 1942, based on the 1st formation of the 249th Rifle Division, and served in that role until well after the end of WWII. It was in Kalinin Front when it was redesignated and remained in the northern half of the front throughout the war. In the summer it was assigned to Western Front's 30th Army to the north of the Rzhev salient and took part in the stubborn and costly struggle for the village of Polunino just east of that town in August. It returned to the fighting in March, 1943 in the followup to the German evacuation of the salient, then was reassigned to the new 11th Guards Army, where it would remain for the duration of the war. During the summer offensive against the German-held salient around Oryol it assisted in the liberation of Karachev and received its name as an honorific. By December, after fighting through western Russia north of Smolensk the division was in 1st Baltic Front, attacking south towards Gorodok and winning the Order of the Red Banner in an ultimately unsuccessful effort to seize Vitebsk. By the start of the offensive against Army Group Center in the summer of 1944 the 16th Guards had been redeployed with its Army to the south of Vitebsk as part of 3rd Belorussian Front, where it would remain for the duration. Driving westward during Operation Bagration the division helped to liberate the key city of Orsha and then drove on towards Minsk. With its Army it advanced through Lithuania to the border with East Prussia, being further decorated with the Order of Suvorov for its crossing of the Neman River. As part of the East Prussian Offensive the 16th Guards entered that heavily-fortified region and helped gradually break the German resistance there, particularly at Insterburg and Konigsberg, ending the fighting at Pillau. <cr><cr>
translation:
第16近卫步兵师于1942年2月在红军中重组，基于原第249步兵师的第一组建制，并一直服役至第二次世界大战结束之后。该师当时隶属于加里宁方面军，在重新指定番号后，整个战争期间都驻扎在前线的北部地区。夏季时，它被分配到西方面军第30集团军，在热季突出部以北作战，并参与了8月对普卢尼诺村艰难且代价高昂的争夺战。1943年3月，该师在德国撤离突出部之后重返战斗，并随后被重新指定给新成立的第11近卫集团军，在那里一直服役至战争结束。

在夏季攻势中，该师协助解放了卡恰夫并因此获得荣誉番号。到12月，经过西斯摩棱斯克地区的激烈战斗后，该师隶属于第一波罗的海方面军，并向戈罗多克方向发起进攻，尽管最终未能占领维捷布斯克，但仍获得了红旗勋章。

在1944年夏季对中央集团军群发动攻势开始时，第16近卫步兵师已随其集团军重新部署至维捷布斯克以南地区，并成为第三白俄罗斯方面军的一部分，在那里一直服役至战争结束。在巴格拉季昂行动中向西推进期间，该师帮助解放了关键城市奥尔沙，并继续朝明斯克方向进攻。与所属集团军一起，它穿越立陶宛并向东普鲁士边境挺进，并因跨越涅曼河而获得苏沃洛夫勋章的进一步表彰。作为东普鲁士进攻的一部分，第16近卫师进入该重兵设防地区，并帮助逐渐瓦解了德国人的抵抗，特别是在因斯特堡和柯尼斯堡，最终在皮劳结束了战斗。 <cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: The 16th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 16th Light Division. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 16th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 16th Infantry Division. In January of 1944 the Hungarian First Army to which the division was subordinate, mobilized to defend Hungary's northern Carpathian frontier against the advancing Red Army. The division was disbanded in May 1944.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第16匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖两个步兵团（每个团有三个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有七个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多东线兵力，大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本没有变化。该旅更名为第16轻型师。在斯大林格勒战役后对匈牙利陆军进行的一般重组中，第16轻型师与其他部队合并，并改名为第16步兵师。1944年1月，在上级匈牙利第一集团军的指挥下，该师动员起来防御匈牙利北部喀尔巴阡山脉边境，对抗推进中的红军。该师于1944年5月解散。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas 和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利陆军》<cr>条目由 Chris Munson 提供

text: The 16th Motorized Division fought in the battles in the Ukraine in 1941, helping to break the Stalin Line in July, in the Battle of Kiev, and in the drive on Moscow. It spent the winter of 1941-42 fighting in the vicinity of Kursk. The following June, it added the 116th Panzer Battalion (formerly I/1st Panzer Regiment) to its table of organization. The division was transferred back to the southern sector in 1942, fighting in the Battle of Voronezh and in the drive to the Caucasus before being shifted north, to cover the large gap between the 1st and 4th Panzer armies in the vast wilderness south of Stalingrad. The recon battalion penetrated to within twenty miles of Astrakhan, the furthest eastward advance of any German unit during the entire war. The 16th Panzer Grenadier fought against the Russians in the winter of 1942-43, before being transferred to the newly reconstituted 6th Army in the spring of 1943. It did not take part in the Battle of Kursk but did fight in the retreat to the Mius, suffering heavy casualties in the fighting around Zaporozhe. It also fought in the battles of Taganrog, Krivoy Rog, Novo, Uman and others. The following spring it bore very heavy losses in the withdrawal from the lower Dnieper, after which the remnants of the 16th Panzer Grenadier were then transported to France, where they were merged with the much larger 179th Reserve Panzer Division to form the 116th Panzer Division.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第16摩托化师于1941年在乌克兰的战斗中作战，帮助德军在7月突破斯大林防线，在基辅战役和向莫斯科推进的过程中发挥了作用。该师在1941至1942年的冬季期间，在库尔斯克附近地区作战。次年6月，它将第116装甲营（原属第一装甲团）编入编制表中。1942年，该师被调回南部战区，在沃罗涅日战役和向高加索的推进中作战，并随后北移，填补了斯大林格勒以南广袤荒野中的第1和第4装甲集团军之间的巨大缺口。侦察营深入至阿斯特拉罕市附近20英里处，这是德国部队在整个战争期间最东端的一次推进。该师在1942至1943年的冬季与俄国人作战后，在春季被调往新重组的第6集团军，并参加了从扎波罗热附近的战斗中遭受重大伤亡的撤退行动。它还参与了塔甘罗格、克里沃伊罗格、诺沃乌曼等战役。次年春天，该师在从第聂伯河下游地区撤离时蒙受了巨大损失，之后第16装甲掷弹兵师残部被运往法国，并与规模更大的第179预备装甲师合并重组为第116装甲师。<cr>德国战斗序列卷三 - 二战中的德军装甲、装甲掷弹兵和武装党卫军师<cr>萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: The 16th Panzer Division Division was in action on the southern sector of the Russian Front from July 1941. It was almost continuously engaged, fighting in the Ukraine campaign, the Battle of Kiev, the Donets battles, against the Russian winter offensive of 1941-42, and in the drive across the Don and to the Volga. During the Bacaklesa encirclement (May 1722, 1942), the 16th Panzer Division captured 31,500 Russians and sixty-nine tanks and 224 other vehicles. It was, however, seriously depleted by casualties in the street fighting in Stalingrad in September and October 1942. As of mid-November 1942, the division had only 4,000 men left. It was ordered to pull out of the line and withdraw to the Donetz to refit. It was in the middle of this maneuver on November 19, 1942, when Stalin's massive offensive struck. The main thrust cut across 16th Panzers line of march, cutting the division in half. The division staff, 79th Panzer Grenadier Regiment, most of the 64th Panzer Grenadier Regiment, and the 16th Panzer Artillery Regiment were cut off in the Stalingrad Pocket when the pinchers closed on November 23. The rest of the divisionincluding the 2nd Panzer Regiment; the 16th Tank Destroyer Battalion; the I/64th Panzer Grenadier Regiment; and the 16th Panzer Engineer Battalionmanaged to escape to the west. Under the command of Colonel Rudolf Sickenius, it fought on as a separate battle group. The rest of the division remained surrounded with 6th Army in the Stalingrad Pocket, and was forced to surrender there on February 2, 1943.<cr>A second 16th Panzer Division was formed in the spring of 1943 and sent to Italy until late in the year, when it was returned to the Eastern Front just in time to take part in the counteroffensive against Kiev. The 16th Panzer suffered heavy losses at Kiev and in the withdrawal across the northern Ukraine. It also tried unsuccessfully to relieve the pocket at Cherkassy. In the fall of 1944 the 16th Panzer was engaged west of the Vistula. It fought in the retreat through Poland and was at battle group strength in east Germany and Czechoslovakia (around Lauban and Brno [Brunn]) when Hitler shot himself on April 30, 1945. The division managed to disengage from the Russians and broke into three groups: one infiltrated through the mountains and forests and reached Karlsbad, Germany, where it surrendered to the U.S. 3rd Army; one was forced to surrender to the Red Army at Troppau on May 18; and the third reached Pilsen and capitulated to the Americans. This last group, however, was promptly handed over to the Soviets.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第16装甲师于1941年7月在俄罗斯方面军南部战区投入战斗。该师几乎一直持续作战，参加了乌克兰战役、基辅助围战、顿涅茨克地区战役、对抗1941-42年的苏联冬季攻势以及穿越顿河向伏尔加河推进的行动。在巴卡列萨包围圈（1942年5月17日至22日）中，第16装甲师俘获了31,500名苏军士兵和69辆坦克及224辆其他车辆。<cr>然而，在1942年9月至10月的斯大林格勒市区战斗中，该师严重减员。截至1942年11月中旬，该师只剩下4,000名士兵。它被命令撤出前线并撤离至顿涅茨克地区整补。<cr>在11月19日的这一行动过程中，斯大林的大规模攻势突然发起。主要突击部队切断了第16装甲师的行军路线，将其一分为二。该师指挥部、第79装甲掷弹兵团、大部分第64装甲掷弹兵团以及第16装甲炮兵团被围困在斯大林格勒包围圈内，直到11月23日钳形攻势合拢。<cr>其余部队包括第2装甲团；第16坦克歼击车营；第64装甲掷弹兵团的I营；和第16装甲工兵营成功向西逃出。在鲁道夫·席肯尼乌斯上校指挥下，它作为独立战斗群继续作战。<cr>其余部队仍然被围困在斯大林格勒包围圈内，并被迫于1943年2月2日在该地投降。<cr>第二次世界大战中的1943年春天，第16装甲师在德国重组，并被派往意大利直到年底。之后该师返回东线，在对抗基辅的反击战中及时参战。第16装甲师在基辅遭受了重大损失，并且在撤退穿越乌克兰北部时也蒙受了巨大伤亡。它还试图解救切尔卡瑟包围圈，但未能成功。1944年秋天，该师在维斯瓦河西岸作战。它参加了从波兰的撤退战斗，在东德和捷克斯洛伐克（劳巴恩和布尔诺附近）以战斗群规模存在时，希特勒于1945年4月30日自杀。该师成功脱离了苏联军队，并分为三组：一组穿越山脉和森林到达德国卡尔斯巴德并向美国第3集团军投降；另一组被迫在特罗帕乌向红军投降；第三组抵达皮尔森并向美军投降，但很快被移交给苏联。[Brunn]<cr><cr>《二战中的装甲师、装甲掷弹兵师及武装党卫军师：德国战斗序列卷三》，萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: At the outbreak of hostilities the corps was in Kaunas as part of 11th Army. It consisted of 5th, 33rd, 133rd, and 188th Rifle Divisions. It was destroyed in the first week of the war. It was reformed in April 1943 as part of 18th Army in Novorossiysk and consisted of 227th, 339th, and 383rd Rifle Divisions in January 1944. It fought in the Taman Peninsula and the Crimean Offensive through 1943 and 1944. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 在敌对行动爆发时，该军作为第11集团军的一部分驻扎在考纳斯。它由第5、第33、第133和第188步兵师组成。战争的第一周内被消灭。该军于1943年4月在新罗西斯克重建，并成为第18集团军的一部分，到1944年1月时包括第227、第339和第383步兵师。它参加了塔曼半岛作战和克里米亚攻势，直到1943年底和1944年初。<cr>指挥官报告: Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军战斗序列在伟大的卫国战争中, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 16th Rifle Division was formed in 1918. At the start of Operation Barbarossa the division was part of the 27th Army in the Northwestern Front. It was destroyed at Mga during the German drive on Leningrad. The division was ordered reformed in December 1941 and for propoganda reasons given the name 'Lithuanian' as large numbers of Lithuanian nationals in Russian service had either deserted or surrendered since the start of the invasion. Lithuanian refugees were urged to join. Most of the divisions officers had trained at the infantry academy in Vilnius.<cr>By February 1943 formation and training were complete and the division entered the line near Oryol in time to fight at Battle of Kursk. The division suffered over 4,000 casulaties and after the Russian victory was posted to northern Russia. The division participated in the recapture of Belarus and Lithuania. While in Lithuania its ranks were filled with Lithuanian forced conscripts. In August 1944 it helped repel German counter-attacks during the Siauliai Offensive. In January 1945 the division was sent to reduce the Germans trapped in the Courland Pocket. It was there when the war ended.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第16步兵师成立于1918年。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师隶属于西北方面军的第27集团军。在德国进攻列宁格勒期间，该师在姆加被消灭。该师于1941年12月接到重建命令，并为了宣传目的而冠以“立陶宛”之名，因为自入侵开始以来，在俄方服役的大批立陶宛国民要么逃亡，要么投降。<cr>到1943年2月，组建和训练工作完成，该师进入奥廖尔附近的一线部队，及时参加了库尔斯克战役。该师伤亡超过4000人，并在取得俄罗斯胜利后被调往北俄地区。该师参与了白俄罗斯和立陶宛的收复行动。当其驻扎在立陶宛时，其兵员中包括被迫征召的立陶宛人。<cr>1944年8月，在锡拉乌利斯攻势期间，该师帮助击退德军反攻。<cr>1945年1月，该师被派往消灭困守在库尔兰包围圈中的德军。战争结束时，该师仍驻扎在那里。

text:
The 16th Tank Corps was formed in June 1942 in the Moscow Military District.<cr>The 16th Tank Corps was actually formed under Bryansk Front HQ with units from both Moscow and Volga Military Districts. In August the Corps was sent south and assigned to 1st Guards Army. In desperate counter-attacks to take pressure off the defenders in Stalingrad, 16th Tank Corps lost heavily: tanks drove into unreconnoitered minefields, attacks were poorly coordinated and supported, and the corps and its subordinate units woefully inexperienced. The corps took part briefly in the tightening of the ring around Stalingrad in November, but again suffered heavy losses and was withdrawn into the Volga Military District to refit in December 1942. There, in January 1943, the 16th Tank Corps became one of the first units assigned to 2nd Tank Army as that HQ formed, and the corps fought under 2nd Tank (later: 2nd Guards Tank) Army for the rest of the war. In the spring of 1943 16th Tank Corps , like most of the Soviet tank units, was in reserve being built up to the 1943 Tank Corps' standard.<cr>The 16th Tank Corps fought both on the defensive and in the counter-attacks that ended the German's Kursk offensive against Central Front, and then in the advance to the Dnepr throughout August-September 1943. During these months, the 16th Tank Corps received an Antiaircraft Regiment which did not complete forming until after it was assigned to the Corps! By September this unit was complete as the 1721st Antiaircraft Regiment, while the 614th Antitank regiment had been redesignated as the 298th Guards Antitank Regiment. During the last half of 1943, the corps suffered from heavy tank casualties against German defenses and a general wearing down of all the units from continuous combat and movement. The corps did not really get a chance to rest and refit until after the Korsun Shevchenkovskii and Uman Operations ended and the entire 2nd Tank Army went into STAVKA Reserve in June 1944.<cr>When the 16th Tank Corps went back into action in July 1944, after a fast refit, all three tank brigades had 3 tank battalions with T-34/85 tanks.<cr>After reaching the suburbs of Warsaw, 16th Tank Corps was back in reserve in
October 1944, when 283rd Guards Light Artillery Regiment (24 76mm towed guns) was added to the corps. In recognition of its combat exploits in the advance to Warsaw and earlier actions, on 21 November 1944 16th Tank Corps became 12th Guards Tank Corps - the highest-numbered Guards Tank Corps designated during World War Two.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第16坦克军于1942年6月在莫斯科军区组建。<cr>实际上，该坦克军是在布良斯克方面军司令部下，由来自莫斯科和伏尔加河两个军区的部队组成的。8月份，该军被调往南方，并划归第1近卫集团军指挥。为了减轻对斯大林格勒守军的压力，在绝望的反击中，第16坦克军遭受了重大损失：坦克驶入未侦察过的雷区，进攻协调和支援都很差，部队及其下属单位经验不足。<cr>该军在11月短暂参与了收紧斯大林格勒包围圈的行动，但再次蒙受重大伤亡，并于1942年12月撤至伏尔加河军区整补。在那里，第16坦克军于1943年1月成为首批被分配给第2坦克集团军（该司令部正在组建）的部队之一，并在余下的战争中一直在第2坦克集团军（后来：第2近卫坦克集团军）指挥下作战。<cr>1943年春天，像大多数苏联坦克部队一样，第16坦克军处于预备状态，正在加强以达到1943年坦克军的标准。第16坦克军在库尔斯克战役中既参与了中央方面军的防御作战，也参加了反击德军攻势的行动，并于1943年8月至9月期间继续推进至第聂伯河。在这几个月里，第16坦克军接收了一个防空团，但该团直到被分配到坦克军后才完成组建！到了9月，这个单位已经作为第1721防空团完整建立起来，而第614反坦克团则重新命名为第298近卫反坦克团。在1943年下半年，由于持续的战斗和调动，该军遭受了严重的坦克损失，并且所有部队都出现了普遍的损耗。直到1944年6月，在科尔松谢夫琴科夫斯基行动和乌曼行动结束后，整个第2坦克集团军才被最高统帅部大本营转入预备队，第16坦克军才有机会休息和整补。<cr>当第16坦克军在1944年7月重新投入战斗后，在快速整补期间，三个坦克旅都配备了3个装备T-34/85坦克的坦克营。<cr>在推进至华沙郊区之后，第16坦克军于1944年10月再次转入预备队，并加入了第283近卫轻炮兵团（配备24门76毫米牵引式火炮）。鉴于其在推进至华沙和之前行动中的战斗功绩，在1944年11月21日，第16坦克军被授予“第12近卫坦克军”的称号——这是二战期间编号最高的近卫坦克军。<cr>查尔斯·C·夏普的《苏联二战战斗序列 第二卷》

text:
The 16th Tank Division was formed in July 1940 from 4th Light Tank Brigade in Odessa Military District as part of 2nd Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
31st Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Tank Bns
32nd Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Tank Bns
16th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
16th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1 light, 1 medium bn
16th Reconnaissance Battalion
16th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
16th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>Because 2nd Mechanized Corps was formed from only one tank brigade plus some separate tank battalions, this division was very understrength in armor throughout 1940, with less than 200 light tanks on hand by October. By shifting resources, 16th Tank Division did get all the BT-5 and BT-7 tanks, which somewhat simplified maintenance. Also, the corps received some T-34 and KV tanks for training purposes early in 1941, but they all went to 11th Tank Division. When war started on 22 June, 16th Tank Division had only about 150 BT-5 and BT-7 light tanks.<cr>The 16th Tank Division fought under 2nd Mechanized Corps across south Russia into the Donbass by August, when 2nd Mechanized Corps HQ was disbanded. By that time, there was so little left of 16th Tank Division that the remnants were evacuated to the rear and disbanded by 1 September 1941.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: The 170th Infantry Division took part in the advance across the Ukraine and southern Russia. It fought at Odessa in July and August, and in October attacked across the Tartar trench and the Perekop Isthmus, pursued the Russians across the Crimea, and took part in the Siege of Sevastopol.<cr>n July 1942, the 170th participated in the attacks that resulted in the fall of this Soviet naval fortress. That summer, as part of von Manstein's 11th Army, the 170th Infantry was transported to the northern sector of the Eastern Front for the attack on Leningrad but was tied down in heavy defensive fighting instead. Later it faced the Russian winter offensive of 1942-43 and successfully defended a sector of the German corridor east of Leningrad against heavy Soviet attacks. The following month, the division absorbed the remnants of the 9th and 10th Luftwaffe Field Divisions. The division remained with Army Group North throughout 1943 and suffered heavy losses when the Russians finally broke the siege of Leningrad in January 1944. After the retreat through Estonia, the 170th was shifted to the central sector of the Eastern Front in July and helped check the Soviet summer offensive of 1944, although it was unable to help the major portions of the German 4th and 9th Armies, which were encircled in White Russia. The 170th Infantry, meanwhile, was returned to Army Group North and took part in the Battle of Narva and the retreat through Latvia. It absorbed the 1065th Grenadier Regiment and the 1034th March Battalion in October, but still had only six under-strength grenadier battalions. At battle group strength, it was sent to East Prussia, where it ended up on the Hela peninsula, across from Danzig. The division finally surrendered to the Soviets in May 1945, when the war ended. Elements of the 170th had been evacuated by sea to Kiel, however, and these surrendered to the British on May 11.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第170步兵师参加了在乌克兰和南部俄罗斯的推进行动。该师于7月和8月参与了敖德萨战役，在10月进攻穿过鞑靼战壕和佩雷科普地峡，追击俄军穿越克里米亚，并参与了塞瓦斯托波尔围城战。<cr>1942年7月，第170步兵师参加了导致这座苏联海军要塞陷落的攻击。那年夏天，作为曼施泰因第11集团军的一部分，第170步兵师被运送到东线北方战区进攻列宁格勒，但最终却陷入激烈的防御战斗中。后来它面对了1942-43年的苏联冬季攻势，并成功地在列宁格勒以东的德国走廊区域抵御了苏军猛烈的攻击。次月，该师吸收了第9和第10空军野战师的残部。整个1943年，该师都隶属于北方集团军群，在1944年1月苏联最终突破列宁格勒包围时遭受了重大损失。在通过爱沙尼亚撤退后，第170步兵师于7月被转移到东线中央战区，并帮助遏制了1944年的苏军夏季攻势，尽管它无法帮助德国第4和第9集团军的主要部分，后者被困在白俄罗斯地区。与此同时，第170步兵师返回北方集团军群并参加了纳尔瓦战役以及通过拉脱维亚的撤退行动。该师于10月吸收了第1065掷弹兵团和第1034行军营，但仍只有六个战斗力不足的掷弹兵营。以战斗群规模，它被派往东普鲁士，在赫拉半岛驻扎，对面是但泽。最终在1945年5月战争结束时向苏联投降。然而，该师的部分部队通过海上撤退到基尔，并于5月11日向英国人投降。<cr>德国二战陆军战斗序列卷一：第1-290步兵师，萨缪尔·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text:
The 170th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in 1939 and was assigned to the 62nd Rifle Corps, 22nd Army, Stavka Reserve (RVGK). At the start of the war it was in transit from the Urals Military District.

The Division was close to 100% strength, but short of transport for heavy equipment, and in early July took up defensive positions on the east bank of the Dvina River. This sector was soon in total disarray, the Division was lucky to escape encirclement, and the original Divisional Commander, T K Silkin, was reported missing, presumed killed in action. In late July the division was assigned to the 51st Rifle Corps and absorbed remnants of the 98th Rifle Division and 112th Rifle Division, and by the end of August had an establishment of about 300 men. 

In September 1941 the Division was transferred to the 24th Reserve Army for rebuilding but was disbanded in October 1941 due to lack of equipment.

The Division was reformed in Molotov in early 1942, based on the forming 439th Rifle Division. In April it was assigned to the 34th Army of the Northwestern Front. The Division fought at Demyansk, Kursk, in Operation Bagration, and finished the war near Elbing, assigned to the 48th Army, 3rd Belorussian Front.



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson

text:
The 172nd Soviet Rifle Division was formed in 1939 and was assigned to the 61st Rifle Corps, 20th Army, Stavka Reserves, located near Tula.

At the start of the war, the 172nd Rifle Division Division was close to 75% strength, but was lacking in support services and transport for heavy equipment. In early July 1941 the Division was rushed forward to take up defensive positions on the Dnieper, near Mogilev, and by 25th of July had been surrounded and completely destroyed. The Divisional Commander, M T Romanov, was wounded trying to break out of the encirclement.

The Division was reformed for a second time in October 1941, based on the 3rd Crimean Motorised Militia Division, and assigned to the 51st Army, then the Coastal Army, and destroyed at Sevastopol in July 1942.

The Division was reformed for a third time in October 1942, in Moscow, and fought at Pavlograd, Kursk, and Kielce. Ended the war with the 102nd Rifle Corps, 13th Army, 1st Ukrainian Front in May 1945.

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner and the Order of Suvorov (2nd Class).




Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第172苏联步兵师成立于1939年，并被分配到位于图拉附近的最高统帅部预备队中的第61步兵军和第20集团军。

战争开始时，该步兵师的兵力接近75%% s，但支援服务和重型装备运输不足。1941年7月初，该师被迅速调往第聂伯河附近的莫吉廖夫地区布防，并于7月25日被包围并完全消灭。师长M·T·罗曼诺夫在试图突破包围时受伤。

该师于1941年10月第二次重建，基于第三克里米亚机械化民兵师，并分配给第51集团军和海岸集团军，在1942年7月塞瓦斯托波尔战役中被消灭。

该师于1942年10月第三次在莫斯科重建，并参加了帕夫洛格勒、库尔斯克和基耳采的战斗。战争结束时，它隶属于第102步兵军、第13集团军和第一乌克兰方面军，在1945年5月。

该师被授予红旗勋章和苏沃罗夫勋章（二级）。

text:
The 173rd Soviet Rifle Division was formed in July 1940 and was assigned to the 8th Rifle Corps, 26th Army, Southwestern Front. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was at about 50% strength. Whilst the Division was reasonably well established, due to the quick Axis advance, and being located close to the border, it never had a chance to get to full strength. The Division was wiped out in the Uman pocket in August 1941.

In September 1941 the Division was recreated for a second time in Moscow, from the 21st Militia Division. The Division suffered heavy losses and in October 1941 was withdrawn to be rebuilt. The Division distinguished itself in the battle for Stalingrad and in March 1943 was renamed the 77th Guards Rifle Divisions.

The Division was recreated for the 3rd time at Staritsa, from the 150th Rifle Brigade, and ended the war assigned to the 31st Army, 1st Ukrainian Front.



 
 
Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第173苏联步兵师成立于1940年7月，并被分配至西南方面军的第26集团军中的第8步兵军。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师大约有50% s的实力。尽管该师已经相对稳定，但由于轴心国快速推进且靠近边境，它从未有机会达到满编状态。该师在1941年8月的乌曼包围圈中被消灭。

1941年9月，该师第二次在莫斯科重建，由第21民兵师改编而成。该师遭受了重大损失，并于1941年10月撤出以重建。该师在斯大林格勒战役中表现出色，并于1943年3月被改名为第77近卫步兵师。

该师第三次在斯塔里察重建，由第150步兵旅改编而成，并最终被分配至第一乌克兰方面军的第31集团军。

text:
The 174th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in 1940 and was assigned to the 62nd Rifle Corps, 22nd Army, Stavka Reserves. At the start of the war it was in transit from the Urals Military District.

The Division was close to 100% strength, but short of transport for heavy equipment, and in early July took up defensive positions on the east bank of the Dvina River. This sector was soon in total disarray, the Division was lucky to escape encirclement, and by the end of August had an establishment of about 400 men. The division was rebuilt, assigned to the 30th Army, where it distinguished itself in the Winter Offensive. The Division was renamed the 20th Guards Division in March 1942.

The Division was reformed for the second time in Starobelsk in April 1942, based on the 130th Motorised Rifle Brigade, under the command of S I Karapetian, and in October 1942 was renamed the 46th Guards Rifle Division in October 1942.

The Division was reformed for the third time in Kaluga in April 1943, based on the 28th Rifle Brigade. The Division fought at Kursk, Belorussia, and in East Prussia and finished the war assigned to the 31st Army, 1st Ukranian Front.



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第174苏联步兵师成立于1940年，并被分配到最高统帅部预备队的第62步兵军、第22集团军。战争开始时，该师正在从乌拉尔军区调动。

该师接近满员（约100% s），但缺乏重型装备运输工具，在7月初在迪维纳河东岸占据了防御阵地。这一区域很快陷入混乱，该师幸运地避免了被包围的命运，并到8月底时只剩下大约400人。该师重建后被分配给第30集团军，在冬季攻势中表现出色。1942年3月，该师更名为第20近卫师。

该师于1942年4月在斯塔罗别尔斯克第二次重组，基于第130摩托化步兵旅，并由S.I.卡拉佩蒂安指挥，同年10月改名为第46近卫步兵师。

该师于1943年4月在卡卢加第三次重组，基于第28步兵旅。该师参加了库尔斯克战役、白俄罗斯战役和东普鲁士战役，并最终被分配给第31集团军、第一乌克兰方面军结束战争。

Nigel Askey, 巴巴罗萨行动 第三卷

感谢 John Tomlinson

text:
The 175th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in July 1940 and was assigned to the 64th Rifle Corps, North Caucasus Military District, near Nalchik.

 At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was at peacetime strength, about 50%. It was held back to finish mobilizing and in July 1941 was assigned to the Southwestern Front Reserves where it remained till August. It was then assigned to the 37th Army for the defense of Kiev and was wiped out in the Kiev pocket in September 1941.

In March 1942 the Division was recreated for a second time at Tyumen , fought at Stalingrad, assigned to the 64th Army, and suffered heavy causalities, It was deactivated in September 1942.

 Recreated again for the third time at Sverdlovsk in late 1942, the Division fought at Demyansk and in Belorussia. It finished the war assigned to 47th Army of the 1st Belorussian Front.

 
 
Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

Courtesy of J Tomlinson
translation:
第175苏联步兵师成立于1940年7月，并被分配到北高加索军区的第64步兵军，靠近纳尔奇克。

在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师处于平时编制水平，约为50%。它被保留下来完成动员工作，在1941年7月被分配给西南方面军预备队，并一直留在那里直到8月。然后它被分配给第37集团军以保卫基辅，并在1941年9月的基辅包围圈中被消灭。

1942年3月，该师在图尔任第二次重建，参加了斯大林格勒战役，被分配到第64集团军，并遭受了严重伤亡。它于1942年9月被解散。

第三次重建发生在1942年底的斯维尔德洛夫斯克，该师参加了德米扬斯克和白俄罗斯地区的战斗。战争结束时，它被分配给第一白俄罗斯方面军第47集团军。

text:
The 176th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in July 1940 and was assigned to the 35th Rifle Corps, 9th Army, Southern Front. 

 At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was at peacetime strength, about 50%. Located on the Rumanian border at the start of hostilities, the Division was able to make an orderly retreat, and despite suffering heavy causalities, survived 1941 intact, in reserve to the Southern Front.

In October 1943 the Division was renamed the 129th Guards Rifle Division.

The Division was formed for a second time at Maselkaya, from the 65th and 80th Naval Rifle Brigades, and finished the war assigned to 31st Army of the 1st Ukrainian Front.

 
 
Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA

text:
The 178th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in 1939 at Omsk in the Siberian Mlitary District. At the start of the war, the Division was close to full strength, and was assigned to the 53rd Rifle Corps, 24th Army, Stavka Reserve (RVGK).

text:
The 179th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in August 1940 from the 1st Lithuanian Infantry Division and was assigned to the 29th Rifle Corps, 11th Army, Northwestern Front. At the start of the war the Division had non standard equipment and was still forming. Many of the soldiers were not sympathetic to the Soviet cause and the Division was classed as unreliable. Despite this the Division kept its cohesion in combat though by August 1941 it was down to 300 men. It finished the year assigned to the 22nd Army of the Kalinin Front.

At the end of the war it was assigned to the 4th Shock Army, Leningrad Front.




 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 
 

 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson

战后，该师被分配到列宁格勒方面军下的第4突击集团军。

text: The 17th Air Army was formed in October 1942 on the basis of the Air Forces of the Southwestern Front. It included a mixed air corps, two fighter, one ground-attack, one bomber, and one night bomber division. It immediately took part in the Battle of Stalingrad. On 19 November 1942 during the Battle of Stalingrad it was under the command of General Major Stepan Krasovsky. On 1 April 1943, as part of the Southwestern Front, it comprised the 3rd Mixed Aviation Corps (207th Fighter Aviation Division, 290th Assault Aviation Division), 7th Mixed Aviation Corps (202nd Bomber Aviation Division, 235th Fighter Aviation Division), 9th Mixed Aviation Corps (305th, 306th Assault Aviation Division, 295th Fighter Aviation Division), 244th Bombardment Aviation Division, 262nd Night Bomber Aviation Division, 39th, 132nd Bomber Aviation Regiments, 208th, 637th Attack Aviation Regiments, 282nd Mixed Aviation Regiment, 371st Transport Aviation Regiment, 10th, 50th Reconnaissance Aviation Squadrons, 34th Fire Correction Squadron. From March 1943 until the end of the war Vladimir Sudets commanded the 17th Air Army. From 1943-45 it participated in the Ostrogozhsk-Rossoh, Left and Right Bank Ukraine operations, and the capture of Romania, Bulgaria, Yugoslavia, Hungary, and Austria. Over 200,000 sorties were flown.<cr><cr>
translation: 第17空军集团军成立于1942年10月，基于西南方面军的航空兵力量。它包括一个混合航空军、两个战斗机师、一个强击机师、一个轰炸机师和一个夜间轰炸机师。该部队立即参加了斯大林格勒战役。1942年11月19日，在斯大林格勒战役期间，由少将斯捷潘·克拉索夫斯基指挥。1943年4月1日，作为西南方面军的一部分，它包括第3混合航空军（第207战斗机航空师、第290强击机航空师）、第7混合航空军（第202轰炸机航空师、第235战斗机航空师）、第9混合航空军（第305和306强击机航空师、第295战斗机航空师），以及第244轰炸机航空师、第262夜间轰炸机航空师，还有第39和132轰炸机航空团、第208和637强击机航空团、第282混合航空团、第371运输航空团，以及第10和50侦察航空中队、第34火力校正中队。从1943年3月到战争结束，弗拉基米尔·苏德茨少将指挥第17空军集团军。从1943年至1945年，它参加了奥斯特罗戈日斯克-罗斯霍战役、左岸和右岸乌克兰作战行动以及罗马尼亚、保加利亚、南斯拉夫、匈牙利和奥地利的占领行动。共执行了超过20万次飞行任务。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: On 22 June 1941, the 17th Army was part of Army Group South (Heeresgruppe Sd) when Nazi Germany launched Operation Barbarossa (Case Barbarossa) and invaded the Soviet Union. From 1 July, the Hungarian 'Fast Moving Army Corps' (Gyorshadtest) was subordinated to the 17th Army.<cr>The 17th Army was engaged in some very heavy fighting with Soviet forces in southern Russia. Along with 1st Panzer Army, the 17th Army encircled Soviet forces near Uman in central Ukraine during the Battle of Uman. Approximately 100,000 Soviet troops were captured.<cr>Afterwards, the 17th Army and other German formations encircled even more Soviet troops during the Battle of Kiev. Approximately 450,000 were captured and, afterwards, Marshal of the Soviet Union (Marshal Sovietskovo Soyuza) Semyon Budyonny was dismissed from duty.<cr>After Kiev, the German focus shifted towards Moscow and the Battle of Moscow. Army Group South was ordered to resume the offensive, with the objective of capturing Rostov-on-Don, the gateway to the Caucasus oil fields, and Kharkov a major center of heavy industry for the Soviet Union.<cr>In 1942, Army Group South was to spearhead the German summer offensive in Russia known as Fall Blau. The 17th Army was to give flank protection to 1st Panzer Army as it struck towards the Don River. From June to July, the German 17th Army, the Italian Expeditionary Corps in Russia, and the Romanian 3rd Army were organized as 'Army Group Ruoff' (Heeresgruppen Ruoff).<cr>In August 1942, what he considered slow progress, caused German dictator Adolf Hitler to re-organize his forces. Hitler sub-divided Army Group South into two new army groups: Army Group A (Heeresgruppe A) and Army Group B (Heeresgruppe B). Army Group A included the 17th Army, the 1st Panzer Army, and the 4th Panzer Army. Army Group B included the 2nd Army, the Sixth Army, theItalian 8th Army, and the Hungarian 2nd Army. By October 1942, the Romanian 3rd Army and the Romanian 4th Army were added to further bolster Army Group B.<cr>While Army Group B struck towards Stalingrad, Army Group A and the 17th Army attacked towards the Caucasus oilfields in what was to be known as the Battle of the Caucasus. However, by December with Soviet forces en-circled the 6th Army at Stalingrad, Army Group B withdrew from Southern Russia but 17th Army was ordered to hold the Kuban bridgehead. Hitler demanded a three-mile road and rail bridge across the Strait of Kerch in spring 1943 to support a push through the Caucasus to Persia, although the Cable Railway (Aerial tramway) which went into operation on July 14 with a daily capacity of one thousand tons was adequate for the defensive needs of the 17th Army in the Kuban bridgehead. Because of frequent earth tremors, vast quantities of extra-strength girders would be required, and their transport would curtail shipments of military material to the Crimea.<cr>By October 1943, the 17th Army was forced to retreat from the Kuban Bridgehead across the Kerch Strait to Crimea. During the following months, the Red Army pushed back the German Army (Heer) in the southern Ukraine. In November 1943, they eventually cut off the land-based connection of 17th Army through the Perekop Isthmus.<cr>Hitler forbade a sea evacuation of 17th Army because he thought the Soviets could use the Crimea to launch air attacks against Romanian oil refineries. However, by the end of 1943, the Soviet began landing troops in Kerch Strait and, by 10 April 1944, moving troops near the Sivash and together with an attack at the Perekop Isthmus forced 17th Army to fall back to Sevastopol. The German Supreme Command of the Armed Forces (Oberkommando der Wehrmacht, or (OKW)) intended to hold Sevastopol as a fortress, much as the Red Army had done during the first battle for the Crimea from 1941 to 1942. Inadequate repair to the defenses of Sevastopol made this impossible and, on 9 May 1944, Sevastopol fell in less than one month after the start of the battle.<cr>The Army lost much of its heavy equipment in the Crimea. Considerable losses were suffered in terms of men lost in battle and losses associated with the sea evacuation.<cr>he Army was subsequently reorganized and continued to fight on the Eastern Front, including in the Battle of Bautzen.<cr><cr>
translation: 1941年6月22日，第17集团军是南方集团军群（Heeresgruppe Sd）的一部分，当纳粹德国发动巴巴罗萨行动并入侵苏联时。从7月1日起，匈牙利“快速移动军”（Gyorshadtest）被划归给第17集团军指挥。<cr>第17集团军在南部俄罗斯与苏军进行了激烈的战斗。 与第1装甲集团军一起，第17集团军在乌克兰中部乌曼附近包围了苏军，在乌曼战役中俘获了约10万名苏军士兵。<cr>之后，第17集团军和其他德军部队在基辅战役中又包围并俘虏了大约45万名苏军士兵。战后，苏联元帅（Marshal Sovietskovo Soyuza）斯米尔诺夫被解除职务。<cr>基辅之战结束后，德国的焦点转向莫斯科和莫斯科战役。 南方集团军群接到命令重新发起攻势，目标是占领顿河门户罗斯托夫以及苏联重工业中心哈尔科夫。<cr>1942年，南方集团军群将领导德军在俄罗斯的夏季攻势——蓝色行动（Fall Blau）。 第17集团军将为第1装甲集团军提供侧翼掩护，后者向顿河方向进攻。从6月到7月，德国第17集团军、意大利远征军和罗马尼亚第3集团军被组织成鲁夫夫集团军群（Heeresgruppen Ruoff）。1942年8月，由于认为进展缓慢，德国独裁者阿道夫·希特勒重组了他的部队。希特勒将南方集团军群分为两个新的集团军群：A集团军群（Heeresgruppe A）和B集团军群（Heeresgruppe B）。A集团军群包括第17集团军、第1装甲集团军和第4装甲集团军。B集团军群包括第2集团军、第6集团军、意大利第8集团军以及匈牙利第2集团军。<cr>到1942年10月，罗马尼亚第3集团军和第4集团军被加入以进一步增强B集团军群的力量。<cr>虽然B集团军群向斯大林格勒发起进攻，A集团军群和第17集团军则攻击高加索油田，在这场被称为高加索战役的战斗中。然而，到12月，随着苏联军队在斯大林格勒包围了第6集团军，B集团军群从南俄罗斯撤退，但第17集团军被命令坚守克里木桥头堡。<cr>希特勒要求在1943年春季修建一条跨越刻赤海峡的三英里长的道路和铁路大桥，以支持通过高加索到波斯的推进。然而，电缆铁路（空中缆车）于7月14日投入运营，每天可运输一万吨物资，足以满足第17集团军在克里木桥头堡的防御需求。<cr>由于频繁的地壳震动，需要大量额外强度的梁架，并且其运输将限制向克里米亚运送军事物资。<cr>到1943年10月，第17集团军被迫从刻赤海峡对面的克里木桥头堡撤退。在接下来的几个月中，红军迫使德国陆军（Heer）从乌克兰南部后撤。<cr>到1943年11月，他们最终切断了通过别列科普地峡与第17集团军之间的陆上联系。希特勒禁止第17集团军从海上撤离，因为他认为苏联可能会利用克里米亚对罗马尼亚的炼油厂发动空袭。然而，到1943年底，苏联开始在刻赤海峡登陆部队，并于1944年4月10日将部队部署至锡瓦什湖附近，同时与佩雷科普地峡的攻击相结合，迫使第17集团军撤退至塞瓦斯托波尔。德国国防军最高统帅部（Oberkommando der Wehrmacht，简称OKW）打算像苏联红军在1941年至1942年克里米亚第一次战役中所做的那样，将塞瓦斯托波尔作为要塞坚守。但是，塞瓦斯托波尔防御工事的修复不足使得这一计划无法实现，并且在战斗开始不到一个月后的1944年5月9日，塞瓦斯托波尔失陷。<cr>该集团军在克里米亚损失了大量的重型装备。在人员伤亡和海上撤离过程中也遭受了重大损失。<cr>该集团军随后进行了重组，并继续在东线作战，包括巴统战役中。<cr>

text:
The 17th Guards was one of four Guards rifle divisions created in Kalinin Front on the same date, March 17, 1942, (along with 20th, 21st and 22nd Guards) in recognition of their role in driving in the left flank of Army Group Center during the winter of 1941-42. When formed, its order of battle was as follows:

45th Guards Rifle Regiment from 365th Rifle Regiment
48th Guards Rifle Regiment from 421st Rifle Regiment
52nd Guards Rifle Regiment from 634th Rifle Regiment
26th Guards Artillery Regiment from 349th Artillery Regiment
22nd Guards Antitank Battalion from 230th Antitank Battalion
16th Guards Sapper Battalion from 224th Sapper Battalion<cr>
The division was part of 22nd Army when it was formed, and remained in Kalinin Front, in either that army or the 41st Army for the next year. In early 1943 it was transferred to 5th Guards Rifle Corps in 39th Army, and remained under those commands for the duration.

In late 1943 the division, along with the rest of 39th Army, was transferred to Western Front, and took part in the campaign to liberate Smolensk. The division was the first Soviet unit to enter the city of Dukhovshchina after it was abandoned by German XXVII Army Corps on the night of September 16/17 and received its name as an honorific.

During Operation Bagration the 17th Guards, now under 3rd Belorussian Front, advanced into the southern Baltic States. At the time of the German surrender the division was in East Prussia, near Knigsberg. <cr><cr>
translation:
第17近卫步兵师是1942年3月17日在加里宁方面军中成立的四个近卫步兵师之一（其他三个分别是第20、第21和第22近卫步兵师），以表彰它们在1941-1942年冬季驱逐中央集团军群左翼时所起的作用。该师成立之初的战斗序列如下：

来自第365步兵师的第45近卫步兵团
来自第421步兵师的第48近卫步兵团
来自第634步兵师的第52近卫步兵团
来自第349炮兵师的第26近卫炮兵团
来自第230反坦克营的第22近卫反坦克营
来自第224工兵营的第16近卫工兵营<cr>

该师成立时隶属于第22集团军，并在接下来的一年内一直留在加里宁方面军，要么是在第22集团军中，要么是在第41集团军中。1943年初，它被转移到第5近卫步兵军中的第39集团军，并在此后继续接受这些指挥。

1943年末，该师连同整个第39集团军一起被调往西方面军，参与解放斯摩棱斯克的战役。该师是第一个进入德国XXVII集团军群在16/17夜间弃守的杜霍夫什奇纳城的苏联部队，并因此获得荣誉称号。

巴格拉季昂行动期间，在第三白俄罗斯方面军指挥下，第17近卫步兵师推进到波罗的海南部诸国。德国投降时，该师位于东普鲁士靠近柯尼斯堡的地方。<cr><cr>

text: The 17th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 17th Light Division. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 17th Light Division was merged with other units and disbanded.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第17匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人在少将指挥下，拥有2个步兵团（每个团有3个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团配有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多东线兵力，大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本没有变化。该旅更名为第17轻型师。在斯大林格勒战役后对匈牙利陆军进行的一般重组中，第17轻型师与其他部队合并并解散。<cr><cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas 和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利军队》<cr>Chris Munson 提供

text: The 17th Infantry Division was in the forefront of Army Group Centers last thrusts toward Moscow in the winter of 194142. (Earlier it had fought at Brest-Litovsk, Bialstok and Gomel, among other places.) The 17th was exhausted after the Soviet winter offensive and was sent to France to rest and rebuild in the summer of 1942. It returned to Russia in February 1943, after the fall of Stalingrad brought the German southern sector to the verge of collapse. In the spring of 1943 it took part in the battles around Juchnov and Gshatsk. After the German defeat at Battle of Kursk in July, the 17th Infantry fought on the Mius, the lower Dnieper, at the Nikopol Bridgehead and in the southern Ukraine, where it again suffered heavy casualties. It was reorganized as a Type 44 division (with six grenadier battalions) in October 1943. It was defending in southern Poland in late 1944 and was smashed on the Vistula in January 1945. In March, it was defending the Hirschberg-Bad Warmbrunn zone of Silesia and consisted of the 95th Grenadier Regiment (two battalions), the 1246th Grenadier Regiment, the 17th Division Fusilier Regiment and assorted divisional troops. (The 1246th Grenadier Regiment consisted of the Staff and students of the Army NCO School at Bruenn [Brno], which the division had absorbed.) The division absorbed elements of the defunct 88th and 291st Infantry Divisions that same month. Remnants of this veteran division were surrounded in Czechoslovakia in late April 1945 and surrendered there.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text: The 17th Mechanized Corps was formed in March 1941 at Baranovichi under the command of Mikhail Petrovich Petrov. It was part of the Western Special Military District's reserve at Slonim. The corps included the 27th and 36th Tank Divisions, and the 209th Motorized Division. The 17th Mechanized Corps was a cadre-strength formation equipped with only 36 tanks, which included 24 BT tanks, a T-26 tank, and eleven T-37, T-38, and T-40 amphibious tanks.<cr>Following the German invasion of the Soviet Union, the 17th Mechanized corps fought in the Battle of Bia?ystok-Minsk. The corps was initially stationed in the rear but was moved forward to Baranovichi to stop the German advance. On 26 June it fought in defensive battles around Baranovichi, Stowbtsy, and Minsk. Its positions were broken through by the German XLVII Army Corps (Motorized). The outnumbered 17th Mechanized Corps was unable to offer much resistance to the attack and its remnants retreated eastwards to the Berezina, where they linked up with other Soviet units. By 3 July it was still mostly fighting on the western bank of the Dnieper. It suffered heavy losses in the fighting and on 5 July was allocated to the 21st Army after being ordered to Babruysk on the previous day.<cr>On 7 July the corps' strength returns (lists of equipment) showed no armored vehicles. On 14 July the 16th Army was ordered to attack south towards Gorki alongside the 17th Mechanized Corps to destroy the German advance troops. The corps increased its resistance as it retreated, fighting against the German 10th Panzer Division as it advanced towards Pochinok on 16 July. On 18 July, the 16th Army was again ordered to attack south towards Gorki with the corps. On 21 July the corps ordered to withdraw to the Sukhinichi area with 4th Army. On 24 July it was regrouping from Yartsevo to support the 16th Army with a strength of 1,600, according to Western Front commander Semyon Timoshenko's situation report on that day. The corps became the 147th Tank Brigade on 1 August. Its 27th and 36th Tank Divisions were disbanded on the same date.<cr><cr>
translation: 第17机械化军于1941年3月在巴拉诺维奇成立，由米哈伊尔·彼得罗夫指挥。该军隶属于西方特别军区的斯洛尼姆预备队。该军包括第27和第36坦克师以及第209摩托化师。第17机械化军是一个只有36辆坦克（其中包括24辆BT坦克、一辆T-26坦克和十一辆T-37、T-38和T-40两栖坦克）的编制单位。<cr>随着德国入侵苏联，第17机械化军参加了比亚韦斯托克—明斯克战役。该军最初驻扎在后方，但被调往前移到巴拉诺维奇以阻止德军推进。6月26日，它在巴拉诺维奇、斯特沃茨和明斯克周围进行了防御战。其阵地被德国第47机械化军突破。兵力不足的第17机械化军无法对进攻提供有效抵抗，残部向东撤退至别列津纳河与苏军其他部队会合。<cr>到7月3日，它仍在第聂伯河西岸作战。在战斗中遭受了重大损失后，该军于7月5日被分配给第21集团军，并接到命令前往前一天指定的巴布鲁伊斯克。7月7日，该军的兵力恢复情况（装备清单）显示没有装甲车辆。7月14日，第16集团军被命令与第17机械化军一起向戈尔基方向发起攻击，以消灭德国前进部队。该军在撤退过程中加强了抵抗，在7月16日与推进至波奇诺克的德军第10装甲师交战。7月18日，第16集团军再次被命令与该军一起向戈尔基方向发起攻击。7月21日，该军接到撤退到苏金奇地区的命令，并在同一天与第4集团军汇合。7月24日，它从雅尔采沃重新编组以支援第16集团军，兵力为1,600人，根据西方方面军指挥官谢苗·蒂莫申科当天的情况报告。该军于8月1日改编为第147坦克旅。其第27和第36坦克师在同一天被解散。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: In June 1941, the 17th Panzer Division struck into Russia with Army Group Centre, fighting at Brest-Litovsk, the Minsk encirlement, in the Dniepr crossings, at Smolensk, and in the Battle of Moscow. It destroyed 100 Russian tanks in a single day-July 9, 1941-at Orsha, during the Dnieper crossing operations. That winter it was pushed back to Orel and remained there until December 1942, when it was transferred to the southern sector of the front. Although it was poor shape (it only had thirty tanks left and all of its armored cars had been destroyed), it took part in the attempt to relieve Stalingrad, but was itself encircled and had to fight its way out. It nevertheless acquitted itself very well, destroying twenty-one Soviet tanks in a single day in temperatures of minus 22 degrees Fahrenheit. By Christmas Eve 1942, the 17th was down to a strength of eight tanks and one anti-tank gun, and one of its regiments was commanded by the lieutenant.<cr>It was taken out of the line shortly thereafter and was partially rebuilt. It received fifty new tanks and the 297th Army Motorized Anti-Aircraft Battalion, which later became the 27th (Flak) Tank Destroyer Battalion, which was added to its table of organization on January 12, 1943. Sent back to the front almost immediately, it took part in Manstein's Kharkov counteroffensive in March, it fought at Kursk (July), and in the subsequent retreats from the Donets, the Dniepr bend, and the northern Ukraine. In March 1944, it was encircled with the 1st Panzer Army, but again broke out. It took part in the retreat across eastern Poland and, in September 1944, was still resisting west of the Vistula. In late 1944, the 17th Panzer Division was reorganized again-this time as a regimental-sized Kampfgruppe. The Staff, 39th Panzer Regiment, was used to form the 108th Panzer Brigade, and the division was left with a single tank battalion. The seriously depleted and understrength 63rd Panzer Grenadier Regiment was dissolved and used to form the III/40th Panzer Grenadier Regiment-a bicycle unit. All of the division support units were reduced to companies, and the 27th Panzer Artillery Regiment became the 27th Panzer Artillery Battalion. The 17th Panzer Division nevertheless opposed the Russian drive west of the Vistula River in the winter of 1944-45, fought in the disastrous Battle of the Baranov Bridgehead and at Goerlitz, and ended the war in the Deutsch-Brod pocket east of Prague. It surrendered to the Russians near Olmuetz on May 11, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation:
1941年6月，第17装甲师随中央集团军群进入俄罗斯境内，在布列斯特-立托夫斯克、明斯克包围战、第聂伯河渡口作战、斯摩棱斯克以及莫斯科战役中参战。在1941年7月9日于奥尔沙进行的第聂伯河渡口作战中，该师一天内就摧毁了100辆苏联坦克。<cr>那年的冬天，它被推回到奥廖尔，并一直驻守到1942年12月。随后，它被调往前线南部战区。尽管当时部队状况不佳（只剩下30辆坦克，所有装甲车都被摧毁），该师还是参与了解救斯大林格勒的行动，但自身也被包围，不得不奋力突围。<cr>然而，它表现得非常出色，在零下22华氏度的气温中一天内就摧毁了21辆苏联坦克。到1942年平安夜时，第17装甲师仅剩下8辆坦克和一门反坦克炮，其中一个团由一名少校指挥。<cr>该师不久后撤出一线，并部分重建。它接收了五十辆新坦克和第297摩托化防空营，后者后来成为第27（高射炮）歼击坦克营，在1943年1月12日编入编制表中。几乎立即被送回前线，参加了曼斯坦因在哈尔科夫的反攻行动（3月），库尔斯克战役（7月），以及从顿涅茨河、第聂伯河弯道和乌克兰北部撤退。1944年3月，它与第1装甲集团军一起陷入包围圈，但再次突围成功。参加了东波兰地区的撤退，并在1944年9月仍于维斯瓦河西抵抗。1944年底，第17装甲师重新编组为团级战斗群。第39装甲团指挥部被用来组建第108装甲旅，该师仅剩下一个坦克营。严重减员的第63装甲掷弹兵团解散，并用于组建第40装甲掷弹兵团第三营——一个自行车单位。所有支援单位都被削减为连级规模，第27装甲炮兵团成为第27装甲炮兵营。尽管如此，该师在1944-45年冬季仍对抗着维斯瓦河西的俄国人进攻，在巴诺夫桥头堡灾难性战役和戈尔利茨战斗中作战，并最终在德布罗德包围圈（布拉格以东）结束战争。它于1945年5月11日在奥洛穆茨附近向俄国人投降。
<cr><cr>德国战斗序列卷三 - 二战中的装甲师、装甲掷弹兵师和武装党卫军师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: Hero of the Soviet Union and future marshal Ivan Stepanovich Konev commanded this corps in 1932-33. The corps was at Chernovtsy in June 1941 as part of 12th Army and consisted of 60th and 96th Mountain Rifle and 164th Rifle Divisions. It was part of the Uman Pocket in August and was destroyed. It was reformed in North Caucasus Front in May 1943 and fought in the Proskurov-Chernovtsy Operation as part of 1st Guards Army. Wikipedia says 17th Rifle Corps was part of 25th Army in the Khabarovsk region of the Far East Military District from 1943-1945. <cr><cr> <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 苏联英雄、未来的元帅伊万·斯捷潘诺维奇·科涅夫在1932-33年指挥该军。该军于1941年6月驻扎在切尔诺夫策，隶属于第12集团军，并由第60山地步兵师、第96山地步兵师和第164步兵师组成。8月份它成为乌曼包围圈的一部分并被消灭。该军于1943年5月在北高加索方面军中重建，并作为第1近卫集团军参加了普罗斯库罗夫-切尔诺夫策战役。维基百科称，从1943年至1945年，第17步兵军是远东军区第25集团军的一部分。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 17th Rifle division was formed in October 1918 from the 1st Vitebsk Rifle Division and 2nd Smolensk Rifle Division by order of the Military council of the Smolensk Defensive Region. The division participated in the Russian Civil War in Lithuania, Ukraine and Belorussia. After that the division participated in the PolishSoviet War. The division was disbanded in 1930 and its elements used to form the 17th, 136th and 137th Rifle Divisions. It was reformed in 1939 from the 49th Rifle Regiment. By December 1940 the division was brought to full strength and participated in the Winter War.<cr>At the start of Operation Barbarossa the division was part of the 10th Army in the area of Vitebsk and Polotsk. It consisted of the 55th, 271st and 278th Rifle Regiments, 20th Artillery Regiment, 390th Howitzer Regiment and various support units. By the end of June 1941 the division was surrounded in the area east of Minsk. Though the division was destroyed in late June 1941 it was not officially disbanded until September 1941.<cr>In October 1941 the division was reformed from the 17th Moscow People's Militia Rifle Division. It participated in the Moscow. In July 1943 it was part of the Orel Counter-offensive and in June 1944 Operation Bagration. From February to April 1945 the division participated in the East Prussian Offensive ending the war there as part of the occupation forces.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第17步兵师成立于1918年10月，由军事委员会下令从第1维捷布斯克步兵师和第2斯摩棱斯克步兵师组建。该师参加了在立陶宛、乌克兰和白俄罗斯的俄国内战。之后，该师参与了波苏战争。该师于1930年解散，其部分单位被用于组建第17、第136和第137步兵师。1939年，该师从第49步兵团重组而成。到1940年12月，该师已达到满编，并参加了冬季战争。<cr><cr>在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师是第10集团军的一部分，在维捷布斯克和波洛茨克地区活动。它由第55、第271和第278步兵团，第20炮兵团，第390榴弹炮团以及各种支援单位组成。到1941年6月底，该师在明斯克以东地区被包围。<cr><cr>尽管该师于1941年6月下旬被消灭，但它直到同年9月才正式解散。<cr><cr>1941年10月，该师从第17莫斯科人民民兵步兵师重组而成。它参加了莫斯科保卫战，在1943年7月参与了奥廖尔反攻行动，并在1944年6月参加了巴格拉季昂行动。<cr><cr>从1945年2月至4月，该师参加了东普鲁士进攻战役，并作为占领部队结束了战争。

text:
The 17th Tank Corps was officially formed on 19 June 1942 in the Moscow Military District with:
66th Tank Brigade
215th, 216th Tank Battalions - total 23 KVs, 27 T-60s
66th Motorized Rifle Battalion
67th Tank Brigade
217th, 218th Tank Battalions - total 45 T-34s, 20 T-60s
67th Motorized Rifle Battalion
174th Tank Brigade
380th, 381st Tank Battalions - total 45 T-34s, 20 T-60s
174th Motorized Rifle Battalion
3lst Motorized Rifle Brigade
39th Mine-Engineer Company
85th (Tank) Repair Base
92nd (Motorized Vehicle) Repair Base<cr>Just a week after it officially formed up, 17th Tank Corps was moved to Voronezh and assigned to Bryansk Front reserves. It was committed in attacks with 40th and 60th Armies against German forces around Voronezh July to September 1942. As usual for Soviet tank corps in the summer of 1942, these attacks resulted in severe tank losses to little effect. On 6 October the corps went back to Volga Military District for complete refitting. It remained there until December, and during this time all the tank brigades were re-equipped to the July 1942 standard with 32 T-34 and 21 T-70 tanks each. On 15 December 17th Tank Corps went into the attack with 1st Guards Army in the 'Malyy Saturn' ('Little Saturn') Offensive. At that time the corps had 98 T-34s and 70 T-70s. As a result of this offensive the Italian 8th Army was annihilated and the Germans pushed away from Stalingrad so that Don Front could finish the destruction of the isolated German 6th Army. In recognition of its contributions
to the Soviet successes, on 3 January 1943 17th Tank Corps became 4th Guards Tank Corps.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp

第17坦克军于1942年6月19日在莫斯科军区正式成立，包括：
第66坦克旅

第174摩托化步兵营
第31摩托化步兵旅
第39工兵连
第85（坦克）修理基地
第92（机动车辆）修理基地<cr>仅仅一周后，第17坦克军被调往沃罗涅日，并分配给布良斯克方面军预备队。该部队于1942年7月至9月与德国军队在沃罗涅日附近进行攻击行动，支援第40集团军和第60集团军。如同苏联坦克军通常情况一样，在1942年夏季的这些攻势中，严重损失了大量坦克却收效甚微。1942年10月6日，该军返回伏尔加河军区进行全面整备。它一直留在那里直到12月，并在此期间所有坦克旅都重新装备为1942年7月的标准配置，每旅配备32辆T-34和21辆T-70轻型坦克。12月15日，第17坦克军在“小土星”攻势中支援第1近卫集团军进行攻击行动。此时该军拥有98辆T-34和70辆T-70。由于此次进攻，意大利第8集团军被彻底摧毁，并迫使德军从斯大林格勒撤退，使得顿河方面军能够消灭孤立的德国第6集团军。作为对苏联胜利贡献的认可，1943年1月3日，第17坦克军成为第4近卫坦克军。<cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普《二战苏军战斗序列》第二卷
