text: The 17th Tank Division was formed in July 1940 at Crossing 77 with the 5th Mechanized Corps from the 37th Light Tank Brigade. It also included the 199th Flamethrower and 526th Transport Battalions. The 17th Tank Division's structure in 1941 included the 33rd and 34th Tank Regiments, the 17th Motor Rifle Regiment, the 17th Howitzer Artillery Regiment, the 17th Reconnaissance Battalion, the 17th Transport Battalion and the 17th Maintenance Battalion. The division was commanded by Major General Ilya Alekseyenko. On 1 March 1941 Colonel Ivan Korchagin took command. Beginning on 12 June 1941 the division was relocated to Izyaslav. <cr>After the German invasion of the Soviet Union, the division moved with the corps to Smolensk. The division was 60% Ukrainian in early July, and German troops attributed its reportedly poor performance to its ethnic composition. On 6 July, the division had 413 tanks, including 237 BT tanks and 130 T-26 tanks. The remainder were flamethrower or amphibious tanks. The division fought in the 5th Mechanized Corps' counterattack towards Senno and Lepel. The division was placed in the corps' first echelon during the counterattack. When it reached the region south of Senno, the division, reinforced by 6 KV-1 and 10 T-34 tanks, ran into the 17th Panzer Division. The counterattack failed with heavy losses. The division was encircled in the Smolensk Pocket, in which it defended the Dnieper line to the west of the city. The division fought against the 17th and 18th Panzer Divisions, which were attempting to establish positions on the southern bank of the river. On 25 July, the division had three KV tanks, four T-34s, 73 BT tanks, 28 T-26s, 16 KhT-26 flamethrower tanks, for a total of 124 tanks. On the night of 31 July to 1 August, the division and the rest of the corps escaped the Smolensk Pocket through the gap in the German encirclement line. <cr>On 28 August, it was converted into the 126th Tank Brigade. The brigade was destroyed in the Vyazma Pocket in October. It was not officially disbanded until 22 August 1942. <cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack
translation: 第17坦克师于1940年7月在77号渡口组建，由第5机械化军和第37轻型坦克旅组成。该师还包括第199火焰喷射器营和第526运输营。1941年的第17坦克师结构包括第33和第34坦克团、第17摩托化步兵团、第17榴弹炮炮兵团、第17侦察营、第17运输营和第17后勤营。该师由伊利亚·亚历山德罗夫少将指挥，1941年3月1日，伊万·科尔察金上校接任指挥官职务。从1941年6月12日起，该师被转移到伊扎斯拉夫。<cr><cr>德国入侵苏联后，该师随军前往斯摩棱斯克。7月初，该师60%的成员是乌克兰人，德军认为其表现不佳的原因在于其民族构成。7月6日，该师拥有413辆坦克，包括237辆BT坦克和130辆T-26坦克，其余为火焰喷射器或两栖坦克。该师参加了第5机械化军在森诺和列佩尔方向的反攻行动，并被部署于反攻的第一梯队。当其到达森诺以南地区时，得到6辆KV-1重型坦克和10辆T-34坦克增援后，与第17装甲师遭遇。反攻失败并遭受重大损失。该师在斯摩棱斯克包围圈中被围困，并在城市西边的第聂伯河防线上进行防御。该师对抗试图在河流南岸建立阵地的第17和第18装甲师。7月25日，该师拥有3辆KV-1重型坦克、4辆T-34坦克、73辆BT坦克、28辆T-26坦克以及16辆KhT-26火焰喷射器坦克，总计124辆坦克。在7月31日晚至8月1日夜间，该师和其余部队通过德军包围线的缺口逃离了斯摩棱斯克包围圈。<cr>8月28日，该师被改编为第126坦克旅。该旅在维亚兹马包围圈中被消灭，并于1942年8月22日正式解散。<cr><cr><cr><cr> 入库感谢NotOneStepBack

text:
The 180th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in September 1940 from elements of 2 Estonian Peoples Army Divisions and was assigned to the 22nd Rifle Corps, 27th Army, Northwestern Front. At the start of the war the Division was at about 50% strength, and some of the equipment was non standard eg of British or Swedish manufacture, with ammunition limited. By July 1941 the Division was assigned to the 11th Army where it fought at Staraya Russa and Demyansk.

In May 1942 the Division was renamed as the 28th Guards Rifle Division.

The Division was formed for a second time at Cherepovets in June 1942 from the 41st Rifle Brigade. It fought at Kiev, Trgu Frumos, and Budapest. The division was part of the 53rd Army of the 2nd Ukrainian Front in May 1945. 

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, the Order of Suvorov 2nd class and the Order of Kutuzov 2nd class. 





Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 

Courtesy of J Tomlinson
translation:
第180苏联步兵师成立于1940年9月，由两个爱沙尼亚人民军步兵师的部分部队组建，并被分配到西北方面军的第27集团军下的第22步兵军。战争开始时该师大约有50% s的实力，部分装备是非标准的，例如英国或瑞典制造的，弹药有限。1941年7月，该师被调至第11集团军，在斯塔罗亚鲁萨和德米扬斯克作战。

1942年5月，该师更名为第28近卫步兵师。

第二次组建于1942年6月在切列波韦茨，由第41步兵旅改编而成。该师参加了基辅、特古弗鲁莫斯和布达佩斯的战斗。1945年5月，该师隶属于第二乌克兰方面军的第53集团军。

该师被授予红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫二级勋章以及库图佐夫二级勋章。

尼格尔·阿斯基，《巴巴罗萨行动》，第三卷A

感谢J汤姆林森

text:
The 181st Soviet Rifle Division was formed in September 1940 from elements of 2 Latvian Peoples Army Divisions and was assigned to the 24th Rifle Corps, 27th Army, Northwestern Front. At the start of the war the Division was at about 50% strength, and much of the equipment was non standard. Reinforcements were naturally hard to mobilise. The Division suffered heavy losses and by the end of September had been officially disbanded. 
 
The Division was reformed at Stalingrad in 1942 and by August had been wiped out at Kalach.
 
The Division was reformed for the 3rd time at Chelyabinsk in February 1942, with the renaming of the depleted 10th NKVD Rifle Division to 181st 'Stalingrad' of the Order of Lenin Rifle Division.
 
The Division fought at Demyansk, and at Korosten, and ended the war assigned to the 6th Army, 1st Ukrainian Front. 
 

 
Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 
 
 Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第181苏联步兵师成立于1940年9月，由两个拉脱维亚人民军步兵师的部分部队组建，并被分配到西北方面军的第27集团军下属的第24步兵军。战争开始时该师大约有50% s的实力，很多装备是非标准的。增援自然难以动员。该师遭受了重大损失，并于9月底正式解散。

1942年在斯大林格勒重建该师，并于8月在卡拉萨被彻底消灭。

1942年2月，第181“斯大林格勒”步兵师（列宁勋章）在车里雅宾斯克第三次重建，由残存的第10内务人民委员部步兵师更名而来。

该师参加了德梅扬斯克和科罗斯坦的战斗，并于战争结束时被分配到第一乌克兰方面军下属的第一集团军。

text: The 182nd Infantry Division has a complicated lineage. The division was originally formed in late 1939 as the 182nd Replacement and Training Division which was part of the Replacement Army. In December 1939 the division was in Lodz Poland but by July 1941 the division was in Nancy France. In July 1942 the division was designated the 182nd Infantry Division. Around this time some of the division was removed and used to form the 182nd Reserve Division and the remaining units of the 182nd Infantry Division were designated the Gumbel Division. In August 1942 the Gumbel Division was renamed again and designated the Karl Division. In September 1942 the 182nd Reserve Division was designated the Nanzig Division. In March 1943 the Karl division became the 282nd Infantry Division. In October 1942 the Nanzig Division was designated the 462nd Infantry Division but in November 1942 part of this division was removed and a new 182nd Reserve Division was formed. In November 1944 the division was reformed in Slovakia and designated the 182nd Training Division.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第182步兵师有着复杂的编成历史。该师最初于1939年底作为第182补充与训练师组建，属于补充集团军的一部分。1939年12月，该师位于波兰洛兹，但到1941年7月已移至法国南锡。1942年7月，该师被指定为第182步兵师。大约在同一时期，部分单位从该师中抽调出来组建了第182预备师，剩余的第182步兵师则被称为贡贝尔师。1942年8月，贡贝尔师再次改名并被指定为卡尔师。1942年9月，第182预备师被指定为南日格师。1943年3月，卡尔师成为第282步兵师。1942年10月，南日格师被指定为第462步兵师，但同年11月该师的部分单位又被抽调出来组建了一个新的第182预备师。1944年11月，该师在斯洛伐克重组并被指定为第182训练师。<cr>参考文献：George F. Nafziger, 《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>条目由Chris Munson提供

text:
The 182nd Soviet Rifle Division was formed in September 1940 from elements of 2 Estonian Peoples Army Divisions and was assigned to the 22nd Rifle Corps, 27th Army, Northwestern Front. At the start of the war the Division was at about 50% strength, and much of the equipment was non standard. By July 1941 the Division was assigned to the 11th Army where it remained for the rest of the year.

The Division showed some natural reluctance to fight for the Soviet cause but under the circumstances performed reasonably well in 1941. 

The Division ended the war assigned to the 43rd Army, 2nd Belorussian Front.




Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 

Courtesy of J Tomlinson
translation:
第182苏联步兵师成立于1940年9月，由两个爱沙尼亚人民军步兵师的部分部队组建，并被分配到西北方面军的第27集团军下的第22步兵军。战争开始时该师大约有50% s的实力，许多装备是非标准的。到了1941年7月，该师被分配到第11集团军，在那里一直待到年底。

该师在为苏联事业而战方面表现出一些自然的迟疑，但在当时的情况下，它在1941年的表现还算不错。

战争结束时，该师被分配到第二白俄罗斯方面军下的第43集团军。

尼格尔·阿斯基，《巴巴罗萨行动》，第三卷A

text: The 183rd Infantry Division was not involved in heavy fighting on the Eastern Front until October 1941, when it took part in the Battle of Vyazma. The 183rd was also engaged in fierce combat in the latter stages of the advance on Moscow. It remained on the central sector until after the Rzhev withdrawal, fighting in the defensive battles of 1942 and the first eight months of 1943. It suffered so many casualties that its 343rd Grenadier Regiment had to be disbanded.<cr>Transferred to the southern zone of operations in September 1943, the division suffered heavy losses in the Kiev fighting that autumn and on November 2, 1943, its Staff was redesignated Corps Detachment C (Korps-Abteilung C). It controlled the former 183rd, 217th, and 339th Infantry Divisions (now Division Groups 183, 217, and 339), as well as the 219th Artillery Regiment, 219th Tank Destroyer Battalion, 219th Engineer Battalion, 219th Signal Battalion, and 219th Field Replacement Battalion. The new command fought at Zhitomir, Tarnopol, and the Brody Pocket in Belorussia (July 1944). Here it broke out of the pocket and most of its survivors escaped. Withdrawn from the combat zone after Brody, the 183rd was rebuilt at the Dllersheim Maneuver Area (Wehrkreis XVII, formerly Austria) as a Volksgrenadier unit. Most of its personnel were inexperienced, poorly trained Austrians from the 564th Grenadier Division. It absorbed Shadow Division Doellersheim on August 3 and was officially activated on September 15, 1944. The fighting caliber of the 183rd declined considerably after that, although it continued to achieve creditable results. (Its subordinate units retained their old numbers, although the grenadier regiments were reduced from three to two battalions.)<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

第183步兵师在1941年10月之前没有参与东线的激烈战斗，直到参加维亚兹马战役。该师还在进攻莫斯科后期阶段进行了激烈的战斗，并一直驻守中央战区，直至1942年的撤退行动（即日洛韦撤退）。它参加了1942年的防御作战以及1943年前八个月的防御作战。由于伤亡惨重，其第343掷弹兵团不得不解散。

1943年9月被调往南部战区后，该师在当年秋天基辅助战斗中遭受了重大损失，并于1943年11月2日将其指挥部重新指定为C军属部队（Korps-Abteilung C）。它控制着原第183、217和339步兵师（现分别为第183、217和339师群），以及第219炮兵团、第219歼击坦克营、第219工兵营、第219通信营和第219野战补充营。新指挥官参加了扎波罗热、塔尔诺波尔和白俄罗斯布罗迪包围圈（1944年7月）的战斗，在这里它突破了包围圈，大多数幸存者得以逃脱。

text:
The 183rd Soviet Rifle Division was formed in September 1940 from elements of 2 Latvian Peoples Army Divisions and was assigned to the 24th Rifle Corps, 27th Army, Northwestern Front. At the start of the war the Division was at about 50% strength, and much of the equipment was non standard. Reinforcements were hard to mobilise. The Division suffered heavy losses and by mid August 1941 had practically ceased to exist. The division was withdrawn to be re-built and by the end of 1941 was assigned to the 29th Army, Kalinin Front.

The Division fought at Rzhev, Kursk and Lvov and by 1944 it was assigned to the 101st Rifle Corps, 38th Army, 4th Ukrainian Front. It ended the war in the Carpathians.





Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 

 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson

该师参加了列日、库尔斯克和利沃夫的战斗，到1944年时被分配到第4乌克兰方面军下第38集团军的第101步兵军。战争结束时该师位于喀尔巴阡山脉地区。

text:
The 184th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in September 1940 from the 2nd Lithuanian Infantry Division and was assigned to the 29th Rifle Corps, 11th Army, Northwestern Front. Most of the soldiers were not sympathetic to the Soviet cause and the Division was classed as very unreliable. The Division was disbanded by mid August 1941 without having seen any significant combat.

The Division was reformed in the Crimea in October 1941, based on the 4th Crimea Militia Division, assigned to the 51st Army, and was destroyed there in November, 1941.

The Division was reformed for the third time and by 1944 it was assigned to the 45th Rifle Corps, 5th Army. Units of 184th Rifle Division were the first Soviet soldiers to reach the prewar frontier on 17 August 1944. The Division ended the war fighting in Manchuria.





 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 
Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第184苏联步兵师于1940年9月由第二立陶宛步兵师改编而成，并被分配到西北方面军的第29步兵军和第11集团军。大多数士兵对苏维埃事业并不忠诚，该师被认为非常不可靠。该师在1941年8月中旬解散，未参与任何重要战斗。

该师于1941年10月在克里米亚重组，基于第四克里米亚军民兵师，并被分配到第51集团军，在同年11月被消灭。

该师第三次重组后，至1944年被分配给第45步兵军和第5集团军。第184步兵师的部队是第一批于1944年8月17日到达战前边界的苏军部队。该师在满洲地区作战结束战争。

Nigel Askey, 巴巴罗萨行动，第三卷A

text:
The 185th Mechanized Division was formed March 1941 from 185th Rifle Division in Moscow Military District as part of 21st Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
257th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
280th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
145th Tank Regiment - 0 tanks
695th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
Reconnaissance Battalion
Antiaircraft Battalion
Antitank Battalion
Sapper Battalion<cr>
The entire 21st Mechanized Corps never received any tanks before the war started, and trucks were so short most of the infantrymen were on foot. The division had 90% of its assigned personnel, but up to 3/4 of them had just arrived between April and June 1941 - there was no time for any unit, or even individual training before the division went into battle.<cr>
Tankless and practically truckless, 185th 'Mechanized' Division went into action at Daugavpils against 4th Panzer Group on 26 June. Six weeks later it officially converted into 185th Rifle Division by adding 1319th (reserve) Rifle Regiment to the remnants of the original 'mechanized' division.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text:
The 185th Soviet Rifle Division was formed at Belgorod in November 1939 and in March 1941 was redesignated the 185th Mechanised Division, assigned to the 21st Mechanized Corps.

The 185th Mechanised Division was rushed into action, suffered very heavy casualties, was withdrawn to be rebuilt in August 1941, and redesignated back to the 185th Rifle Division.

The 185th Soviet Rifle Division was rebuilt by September, 1941, assigned to the 30th Army, Kalinin Front and fought in the defense of Moscow.

In January 1945 the Division was assigned to the 77th Rifle Corps, 47th Army, 1st Belorussian Front and finished the war close to Berlin.




 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第185苏联步兵师于1939年11月在别洛戈罗德组建，并于1941年3月被重新指定为第185机械化军，隶属于第21机械化军。

第185机械化军迅速投入战斗，遭受了非常严重的伤亡，在1941年8月撤退重建并重新指定回第185步兵师。

第185苏联步兵师于1941年9月重建，并被分配给第30集团军、加里宁方面军，参与了莫斯科防御战。

1945年1月，该师被分配给第77步兵军、第47集团军、第一白俄罗斯方面军，并在接近柏林的地方结束了战争。


Nigel Askey, 巴巴罗萨行动 第三卷

text:
The 186th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in 1939 and was assigned to the 62nd Rifle Corps, 22nd Army, Stavka Reserve (RVGK). At the start of the war it was in transit from the Ural Military District.

The Division was close to 100% strength and in early July took up defensive positions on the east bank of the Dvina River. This sector was soon in total disarray, the Division was lucky to escape encirclement, and by the end of August had an establishment of about 2,000 men.

In September 1941 the Division was rebuilt with reservists and survived the year defending Moscow as part of the Kalinin Front.

The Division finished the war assigned to the 46th Rifle Corps, 65th Army, on the Oder River in Germany.

Note : A second 186th Rifle Division was formed in September 1941 and renamed the 205th Rifle Division in June 1943.



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB

text:
The 187th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in 1939 and was assigned to the 45th Rifle Corps, Stavka Reserve (RVGK), located in the Kharkov Military District. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was at about 50% strength.

The Division quickly received mobilised reserves and was assigned to the 21st Army. In mid July 1941 it was committed into the counter attack against Army Groups Center, suffered heavy casualties, and the remnants were wiped out in the Kiev pocket in September 1941.

The Division was reformed in October 1941, assigned to the 1st Red Banner Army in the Far East, where it remained for the remainder of the war. For a time it was known as the Grodelkovskaya Rifle Division.

 
 

Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson

第187苏联步兵师成立于1939年，并被分配至位于哈尔科夫军区的最高统帅部预备部队（RVGK）下的第45步兵军。在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师大约有50% s的实力。

该师迅速接收了动员后的预备队，并被分配给第21集团军。1941年7月中旬，它被投入到对抗中央集团军群的反击中，遭受了严重伤亡，在同年9月基辅包围圈中残部也被消灭。

该师于1941年10月重建，并被分配至远东地区的第1红旗集团军，直至战争结束都驻扎在那里。一段时间内，它被称为格罗德洛夫斯基步兵师。

text:
The 188th Soviet Rifle Division was formed at Kaunas in March 1941 and was assigned to the 16th Rifle Corps, 11th Army, Northwestern Front. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was at about 70% strength. Despite receiving reinforcements the Division suffered heavy casualties and by mid July, 1941 was down to about 2,000 men. By the end of the year it was assigned to the 34th Army of the Northwestern Front.

The Division fought in central Russia and in the liberation of Ukraine and Moldova. It was with the 82nd Rifle Corps of the 37th Army in Bulgaria in May 1945. 

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner and the Order of the October Revolution.



 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 

 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第188苏联步兵师于1941年3月在考纳斯组建，并被分配到西北方面军的第11集团军中的第16步兵军。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师大约有70% s的实力。尽管得到了增援，但该师伤亡惨重，到1941年7月中旬只剩下约2,000人。到年底，该师被分配给西北方面军的第34集团军。

该师在俄罗斯中部作战，并参与了乌克兰和摩尔多瓦的解放行动。1945年5月，该师隶属于保加利亚第37集团军中的第82步兵军。

该师荣获红旗勋章和十月革命勋章。

The 189th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in April 1941 and was assigned to the Reserves of the Southwestern Front. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was at about 50% strength. The Division was wiped out in the Uman pocket in August 1941.

text: Formed in November 1939 in Military Region (Wehrkreis) VI, the 18th Army was part of the offensive into the Netherlands (Battle of the Netherlands) and Belgium (Battle of Belgium) during Fall Gelb and later moved into France in 1940. The 18th Army was then moved East and participated in Operation Barbarossa in 1941.<cr>The Army was a part of the Army Group North until early 1945, when it was subordinated to Army Group Kurland. In October 1944, the army was encircled by the Red Army offensives and spent the remainder of the war in the Courland Pocket.<cr><cr>
translation: 第18集团军成立于1939年11月的第六军事地区（Wehrkreis VI），参加了入侵荷兰（荷兰战役）和比利时（比利时战役）的攻势，在黄色方案期间，后来在1940年进入法国。第18集团军随后被调往东线，并参与了1941年的巴巴罗萨行动。<cr>该集团军是北方集团军群的一部分，直到1945年初才转隶给库尔兰集团军群。1944年10月，该集团军被红军的攻势包围，在库尔兰包围圈中度过了战争剩余时间。<cr><cr>

text: The 18th Army was formed on 21 June 1941 on the basis of HQ Kharkov Military District and armies of the Kiev Special Military District.<cr>The Army's commander in 1941 was General-Lieutenant Ilya Smirnov. The Army composition on the beginning of the war was the 16th Mechanized Corps (15th Tank Division, 39th Tank Division, 240th Mechanized Tank Division, 64th Fighter Air Division, 45th Mixed Air Division), 17th Rifle Corps (96th Mountain Rifle Division, 60th Mountain Rifle Division, 164th Rifle Division), 18th Mechanised Corps (47th Tank Division, 218th Mechanized Division), 55th Rifle Corps (130th Rifle Division, 160th Rifle Division, 189th Rifle Division, 4th Independant Brigade).<cr>It was caught soon after the start of Operation Barbarossa in 1941 in a huge encirclement south of Kiev along with the Soviet 6th Army and 12th Army. This encirclement was part of the Battle of Uman. A further formation was shattered during the Battle of the Sea of Azov in September-October 1941.<cr>On 1 October 1943 the army consisted of 20th Rifle Corps (8th Guards Rifle Brigade, 81st and 83rd Naval Rifle Brigades), 55th Guards Rifle Division, 89th Rifle Division, 176th, 318th, 414th Rifle Divisions, 107th Rifle Brigade, 255th Naval Infantry Brigade, 10th Guards Separate Antitank Battalion, artillery, armoured forces, and engineers.
translation: 第18集团军成立于1941年6月21日，基于哈尔科夫军区司令部和基辅特别军事区的部队。<cr>该集团军在1941年的指挥官是少将伊利亚·斯米尔诺夫。战争初期，集团军编成包括第16机械化军（第15坦克师、第39坦克师、第240机械化坦克师、第64战斗机航空师、第45混合航空师）、第17步兵军（第96山地步兵师、第60山地步兵师、第164步兵师）、第18机械化军（第47坦克师、第218机械化师）和第55步兵军（第130步兵师、第160步兵师、第189步兵师、第4独立旅）。<cr>巴巴罗萨行动开始不久，该集团军在基辅以南地区被纳入苏联第6集团军和第12集团军的大包围圈中。这一包围圈是乌曼战役的一部分。另外一支编成在亚速海战役（1941年9月至10月）期间被击溃。<cr>到1943年10月1日，该集团军包括第20步兵军（第8近卫步兵旅、第81和第83海军步兵旅）、第55近卫步兵师、第89步兵师、第176、第318、第414步兵师、第107步兵旅、第255海军步兵旅、第10近卫独立反坦克营，以及炮兵、装甲部队和工兵。

text: The 18th Guards Motor Rifle Division was formed originally as 133rd Rifle Division at Novosibirsk or Biysk in 1939. The division was part of 1st Shock Army on 1 December 1941 during the Battle of Moscow. It was redesignated as the 18th Guards Rifle Division in March 1942 with the 51, 53, 58 Guards Rifle Regiments and 52 Guards Artillery Regiment. The division fought in the East Prussian Offensive. The unit became 30th Guards Mechanised Division in 1945 as part of the 11th Guards Army.<cr><cr>
translation: 第18近卫机械化步兵师最初成立于1939年，当时名为第133步兵师，在新西伯利亚或比斯克。该师于1941年12月1日作为第1突击集团军的一部分参加莫斯科防御战。<cr><cr>1942年3月，该师被重新命名为第18近卫步兵师，并编入了第51、53、58近卫步兵团和第52近卫炮兵团。该师参加了东普鲁士进攻行动。<cr><cr>1945年，该单位成为第30近卫机械化师，隶属于第11近卫集团军。<cr> <cr>

text: The 18th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 18th Light Division. In March of 1943 the division was sent from Hungary to join the Hungarian Occupation Group assigned to security duties in occupied Russia. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 18th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 18th Reserve Division. In January of 1944 the Hungarian First Army to which the division was subordinate, mobilized to defend Hungary's northern Carpathian frontier against the advancing Red Army. The division was disbanded in August 1944.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第18匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖两个团（每个团有三个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多东线兵力，大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本保持不变。该旅更名为第18轻型师。1943年3月，该师从匈牙利调往匈牙利占领集团，负责在被占领的俄罗斯执行治安任务。斯大林格勒战役后，作为对匈牙利军队的一般重组的一部分，第18轻型师与其他部队合并，并更名为第18预备师。1944年1月，在该师隶属下的匈牙利第一集团军动员起来，以防御红军进攻的北部喀尔巴阡山边境。该师于1944年8月解散。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr>条目由Chris Munson提供

text: As part of Hoth's 3rd Panzer Group, the 18th Motorized Division fought in the Bialystok and Minsk encirclements, in the drive on Leningrad, and at Volchov, among others. It was badly mauled in the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42, losing 9,000 men and dropping to a strength of 741 combat effectives by December 22. Soon after it was put into reserve behind the northern sector of the front.<cr>In March 1942, however, it was back in the line and took part in the rescue of II Corps at Demyansk. Remaining on the northern sector in the defensive battles of 1942 and 1943, where it held a sector of the front near Tichvin, the 18th Panzer Grenadier also fought around Demyansk and Lake Ilmen and at Staraya Russa. On June 23, 1943, it added the 118th Panzer Battalion (which was equipped with assault guns), and it was redesignated 18th Panzer Grenadier Division. That autumn, it was sent to Army Group Centre, where it fought in the unsuccessful defense of Smolensk that fall. In the spring of 1944 it was officially cited for distinguished action in the central Dnieper fighting. The 18th Panzer Grenadier was virtually destroyed in the Russian summer offensive of 1944. Encircled in the Bobruisk Pocket, divisional commander Lieutenant General Karl Zutavern committed suicide, rather than surrender to the Russians. The tiny remnants of the burned-out division that escaped the destruction of the 4th Army were sent to Silesia, where they were temporarily absorbed by the 105th Panzer Brigade. The division was rebuilt as a Kampfgruppe in November and early December 1944, and absorbed both the 105th and 103rd Panzer Brigades. It had four panzer grenadier battalions, a panzer battalion and three artillery battalions, but no tank destroyer or engineer battalions. Its tank battalion was equipped with obsolete PzKw IVs. It returned to the Eastern Front in East Prussia in December and was decimated there in the winter fighting of 1944-45. Evacuated by sea to northern Germany, it fought in the battles of Seelow Heights and Berlin, where it was finally destroyed. Most of its survivors fell into Communist hands.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text: The 18th Panzer Division first saw action in Russia, crossing the Bug in underwater tanks originally designed for Operation Sea Lion (the invasion of Britain). It spent the rest of 1941 fighting in a number of battles, including the Minsk encirlement, Smolensk, the Dniepr crossings, Kiev, Roslavl, Bryansk, Moscow, and Orel, all on the central sector of the Russian Front. It also opposed the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42, near the Soviet capital. Casualties were heavy. During the first sixty days of the campaign, it lost almost 6,000 men-more than one-third of its pre-invasion strength. By July 9, the division had only eighty-three operational tanks-39 percent of its strength just three weeks before. By late July, only twelve of its panzers were operational, compared to 212 on June 21. The division nevertheless acquitted itself very well in the winter fighting of 1941-42.<cr>On June 15, 1942, the division was reorganized and lost several units, including the 18th Panzer Regiment, which was disbanded. The divisions only remaining tank unit was redesignated 18th Panzer Battalion. Its table of organization and equipment strength was reduced from more than 17,000 men to about 14,000. This was all academic, however; its actual strength was less than 7,000. The division, however, did receive one new unit: the 292nd Army Anti-Aircraft Battalion.<cr>In the summer of 1942, the much-reduced division was sent to the southern sector of the Eastern Front, where it took part in the initial advances on Stalingrad, but it was soon returned to Army Group Center, with which it fought in the defensive battles of 1942-43. The 18th Panzer Division was virtually destroyed in the Battle of Kursk. It went into the battle with 5,432 combat effectives but lost 4,028 men in the next ten days. The division commander disbanded his supply and rear area units and sent their men to the front. By mid-September, the division had four panzer grenadier battalions, but they only averaged 130 men each. In autumn 1943, the 18th was fighting around Kiev, and in the fall suffered such heavy losses in the counteroffensive west of Kiev (in the Bryansk, Orscha and Vitebsk sectors) that it had to be disbanded on September 29, 1943. Low morale was a factor in this decision. Its Headquarters and its artillery were used to help form the 18th Artillery Division.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第18装甲师首次在俄罗斯参战，使用专门设计用于海狮行动（入侵英国）的水下坦克穿越布格河。它在1941年的剩余时间里参加了多次战役，包括明斯克包围战、斯摩棱斯克、第聂伯河渡口、基辅、罗斯拉夫利、布良斯克、莫斯科和奥廖尔等地的战斗，所有这些都在俄罗斯中央战区进行。该师还对抗了苏联在1941-42年冬季发起的攻势，在距离苏联首都不远的地方作战。伤亡惨重。在战役最初的六十天里，它损失了近6000人——超过其入侵前实力的三分之一。到7月9日，该师只有83辆可操作坦克——仅比三周前少了39%的实力。到了晚些时候的7月，仅有12辆装甲车可以使用，而6月21日时有212辆。然而，在1941-42年冬季作战中，该师表现得非常出色。<cr>指挥官报告：1942年6月15日，该师进行了重组，并解散了第18装甲团等多个单位。其唯一的坦克部队被重新指定为第18装甲营。编制表和装备实力从超过17000人减少到约14000人。然而，这都是理论上的；实际上它的兵力不到7000人。不过该师确实接收了一个新单位：第292集团军防空营。1942年夏天，兵力大减的第18装甲师被派往东线南部战区，在进攻斯大林格勒初期阶段参战。但很快又被调回中央集团军群，并参与了该集团军群在1942-43年的防御作战。第18装甲师几乎在库尔斯克战役中被消灭，出战时有5,432名战斗人员，但在接下来的十天内损失了4,028人。师长解散了他的补给和后方单位，并将这些部队的人派到前线。至9月中旬，该师仅剩四个装甲掷弹兵营，但每个营平均只有130人。1943年秋天，第18装甲师在基辅附近作战，在基輔以西的反攻中（布良斯克、奥尔沙和维捷布斯克地区）遭受了严重损失，不得不于1943年9月29日解散。低士气是这一决定的因素之一。其司令部和炮兵被用来帮助组建第18炮兵师。<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham Jr., German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII

text:
The 18th Rifle Division was formed in November 1918 at Arkhangelsk with troops from Archangel, Belsky and Kotlassky areas. In the spring of 1920 the division was part of the Western Front and took part in the invasion of Poland. After being defeated at the Battle of Warsaw the division retreated to East Prussia where it was briefly interned. From November 1939 to March 1940 the division was part of the Winter War with Finland. The division led the attack on Uoma-Kitilya-Impilahti-Sortavala and was subsequently encircled near Lemeti and defeated. In early 1940 due to the loss of its banner and heavy losses the division was disbanded. The remains of the division were reassigned to the 71st Rifle Division. Today the divisions banner is in a museum collection in Finland. The division was reestablished at Kazan in August 1939 from the Ulyanovsk-based 86th Rifle Division as the 111th Rifle Division. In 1940 it was renamed as the 18th Rifle Division.<cr>At the start of Operation Barbarossa the division was stationed in Kazan and consisted of the 97th, 208th and 316th Rifle Regiments, 12th Howitzer Regiment, 381st Separate Tank Battalion and various support units. The division was immediately ordered west and took up positions south of Orsha on the left bank of the Dneper River covering the area from Orsha to near Shklow. Here the division found itself surrounded. Elements of the division was able to break out of the ring on in July and August 1941. The division was officially disbanded in September 1941.<cr>The division was reformed once again in September 1941 from the 18th Division of the Moscow People's Militia. It then fought at the Battle of Moscow becoming the 11th Guards Rifle Division in January 1942.<cr>A new 18th Rifle Division was formed in February 1942 at Ryazan in the Moscow Military District from a cadre of the 16th Sapper Brigade. The division was in reserve as part of the Stalingrad Front by July 1942 and assigned to the 4th Tank Army. In August 1942 the division was involved in intense fighting in a small bend of the Don River north-west of Stalingrad where it sustained heavy casualties. Due to its significant losses the division was put in reserve in September 1942. After spending three months in the Moscow Military District rebuilding near Tambov the division was sent to the Volkhov Front and before the end of 1942 was assigned to the 2nd Shock Army. In mid-January 1943 the division broke through the German encirclement, breaking the Siege of Leningrad and joining the forces of the Leningrad Front. The 18th Rifle Division is credited with capturing the first Tiger Tank. The division would participate in the Svir-Petrozavodsk Offensive. In late September 1944 the division was assigned to the Soviet-Finish border southwest of Sortavala. The division was placed in the STAVKA reserves in mid-November 1944 and assigned to the 19th Army's 132nd Rifle Corps. Reassigned to the 2nd Belorussian Front the division participated in the East Pomeranian Offensive and fought at Danzig, Poland.
The division remained in Poland as part of the Northern Group of Forces and was disbanded in June 1946.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation:
第18步兵师成立于1918年11月，在阿尔汉格尔斯克组建，由阿尔汉格尔、贝尔斯基和科特拉斯基地区的部队组成。1920年春天，该师隶属于西方方面军，并参加了入侵波兰的行动。在华沙战役中被击败后，该师撤退到东普鲁士并短暂被拘留。从1939年11月到1940年3月，该师参与了与芬兰的冬季战争。该师领导了对乌奥马-基蒂利亚-因皮拉赫蒂-索塔瓦拉的攻击，并在莱梅蒂附近遭到包围和击败。1940年初由于失去旗帜并遭受重大损失，该师被解散。该师剩余部队重新分配给第71步兵师。今天，该师的旗帜收藏于芬兰的一个博物馆中。1939年8月，该师在喀山重建为第111步兵师，由乌里扬诺夫斯克基地的第86步兵师改编而成。1940年改名为第18步兵师。<cr>巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师驻扎在喀山，并包括第97、208和316步兵团，第12榴弹炮团，第381独立坦克营以及各种支援单位。该师立即被命令向西移动，在奥尔沙以南的第聂伯河左岸布防，覆盖从奥尔沙到谢夫洛夫附近的区域。在这里，该师发现自己被包围了。<cr>在1941年7月和8月期间，该师的部分部队能够突破包围圈。该师于1941年9月正式解散。<cr>巴巴罗萨行动结束后，该师于1941年9月从莫斯科民兵第18师重建，并参加了莫斯科战役，在1942年1月成为第11近卫步兵师。1942年2月，第18步兵师在莫斯科军区的梁赞从第16工兵旅的核心组建而成。该师于1942年7月成为斯大林格勒方面军预备队的一部分，并被分配给第4坦克集团军。1942年8月，该师参与了顿河畔斯大林格勒西北部一小段弯曲河道的激烈战斗，在此过程中遭受了重大伤亡。由于损失严重，该师于1942年9月成为预备队。在莫斯科军区重建三个月后，该师被派往沃尔霍夫方面军，并于1942年底被分配给第2突击集团军。1943年1月中旬，该师突破了德国的包围圈，解除了列宁格勒的围困，并加入了列宁格勒方面军的力量。第18步兵师因俘获第一辆虎式坦克而受到赞誉。该师参加了斯维里-彼得罗扎沃茨克攻势。1944年9月底，该师被分配到索塔瓦拉西南部的苏芬边境地区。1944年11月中旬，该师被最高统帅部大本营作为预备队，并被分配给第19集团军的第132步兵军。重新部署至第2白俄罗斯方面军后，该师参加了东波美拉尼亚攻势，并在波兰的但泽作战。

该师于1946年6月解散前一直驻扎在波兰北部集团军群内。<cr>Chris Munson 提供

text: The 18th Romanian Infantry Division did not participate in the opening phase of Operation Barbarossa and remained in Romania. In January of 1942 it was assigned, less its 90th Infantry Regiment, to the German XI Corps. It was one of four Romanian infantry divisions not withdrawn to Romania after the Siege of Odessa. In January of 1943 it was serving with the German4th Panzer Army.<cr><cr>John Ellis, World War II A Statistical Survey<cr>Charles D. Pettibone, The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II Volume VII - Germany's and Imperial Japan's Allies & Puppet States<cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text: The 18th Tank Corps was formed in June 1942 in the Moscow Military District.<cr>While it was forming, 18th Tank Corps moved to Voronezh, where it temporarily included 217th Antiaircraft Regiment, but it never went into combat with this unit. Early in July 18th Tank Corps was assigned to 5th Tank Army in Bryansk Front, and then to 60th Army in Voronezh Front. In the uncoordinated Soviet tank actions around Voronezh the corps suffered heavy losses, and in October was withdrawn into Volga Military District, where the most damaged subordinate brigades were removed and replaced by new units. In November 1942 the corps was assigned to Southwestern Front.<cr>The 18th Tank Corps was in 1st Guards Army at the start of 'Malyy Saturn' Offensive on 15 December, and then part of the Southwestern Front Mobile Group known as 'Group Popov' in February 1943, when the badly-worn corps was almost annihilated at the beginning of Manstein's panzer counter-attack. At that time, in addition to the units above, the corps also contained the 1st Armored Car Battalion.<cr>In late February 1943 the remnants of 18th Tank Corps, almost completely without equipment, went into STAVKA reserves to be completely rebuilt. The corps was assigned to Steppe District (later Steppe Front) of STAVKA Reserves from April to 5 July 1943. On 6 July the corps was assigned to 5th Guards Tank Army.<cr>The 18th Tank Corps was on the right of 5th Guards Tank Army at the great tank battle at Prokhorovka on 12 July 1943. Even with support from 10th Antitank Brigade, fighting Tigers with T-70s and T-34s was costly. On 12 and 13 July, the corps lost one-third of its tanks, and when fighting died down on 17 July it took the rest of the month to repair enough tanks to rebuild the corps. In August 18th Tank Corps took part in the battles to recover Kharkov, with the 78th Motorcycle Battalion and 106th Guards Mortar Battalion (8 BM-13 launchers) being added to the units already commanded.<cr>In November 1943 the 18th Tank Corps was supposed to be turning in all the T-70 light tanks and equipping each tank brigade with 65 T-34s, but because of the continuous combat since August, the tank brigades only averaged 40 tanks each including almost 25% T-70s. By November 1943 also, 36th Guards Heavy Tank Regiment had been removed from the corps and replaced by 1543rd Heavy SU Regiment with SU-152s. By 15 December the corps only had 37 tanks left, and even by adding 1438th SU Regiment (SU-85s) the corps could not be brought up to any decent armored strength. After attacking through the Kirovograd Operation (January 1944) , Korsun-Shevchenkosvskii (January-February) and Uman (March) the corps was practically wrecked. On 9 March 1944 there were just 9 T-34s and 8 SU guns left in 18th Tank Corps.<cr>On 27 May 1944 18th Tank Corps was removed from 5th Guards Tank Army, under which it had fought since July 1943, and became a separate unit in 2nd Ukrainian Front. By this time 1543rd Heavy SU Regiment had been removed from the corps, but in July, preparing for the Lvov-Sandomir Operation, 363rd Guards Heavy SU Regiment (ISU-122s) was added to the corps, and in August 1944 18th Tank Corps received 452nd Light Artillery Regiment with 24 76mm towed guns. For the rest of the war, 452nd and 1000th Regiments were used and designated as either Light Artillery or Antitank Regiments, since they were equipped almost alike, each with 24 76mm guns. In November 1944 18th Tank Corps became part of 3rd Ukrainian Front reserves, and fought under that Front until the end of the war. The corps ended the war in Hungary in May 1945.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第18坦克军于1942年6月在莫斯科军区组建。<cr>在组建期间，该坦克军迁至沃罗涅日，并临时编入了第217防空团，但从未与该单位一同参战。7月初，第18坦克军被分配给布良斯克方面军的第5坦克集团军，随后又被调往沃罗涅日方面的第60集团军。在苏联坦克部队围绕沃罗涅日进行的一系列不协调行动中，该军遭受了重大损失，并于10月撤至伏尔加河军区，在那里最受损的下属旅被移除并替换为新单位。1942年11月，该军被分配给西南方面军。<cr>在“小土星行动”开始时（1942年12月15日），第18坦克军隶属于第1近卫集团军，并于1943年2月成为西南方面军机动部队的一部分，即“波多夫斯基集群”，该集群几乎被曼施坦因的装甲反攻摧毁。当时，除了上述单位外，该军还编有第1装甲车营。<cr>1943年2月底，第18坦克军残部在几乎没有装备的情况下进入最高统帅部大本营预备队进行全面重建。从1943年4月到7月5日，该军被分配给最高统帅部预备队的斯捷普区（后来成为斯捷普方面军）。7月6日，该军被分配给第5近卫坦克集团军。<cr>第18坦克军在1943年7月12日普罗霍罗夫卡的大规模坦克战役中位于第5近卫坦克集团军的右侧。即使有第10反坦克旅的支持，用T-70和T-34对抗虎式坦克代价高昂。<cr>7月12日至13日，该军损失了三分之一的坦克，在7月17日战斗结束后，整个8月份才修复足够的坦克以重建部队。8月，第18坦克军参加了收复哈尔科夫的战役，加入了第78摩托化营和第106近卫迫击炮团（配备8门BM-13火箭发射器）。<cr>到1943年11月，第18坦克军本应交出所有T-70轻型坦克，并为每个装甲旅装备65辆T-34，但由于自8月以来的连续战斗，各装甲旅平均只有40辆坦克，其中包括近25%的T-70。到1943年11月，第36近卫重型坦克团已被移出该军，并由配备SU-152的第1543重型自行火炮团取代。<cr>截至12月15日，该军只剩下37辆坦克，即使加上第1438自行火炮团（装备SU-85），也无法达到任何合理的装甲力量。在经过基洛夫格勒行动（1944年1月）、科尔松谢夫琴科夫斯基战役（1月至2月）和乌曼战役（3月）的攻击后，该军几乎被摧毁。<cr>到1944年3月9日，第18坦克军只剩下9辆T-34和8门自行火炮。1944年5月27日，第18坦克军从第5近卫坦克集团军中撤出，并成为第2乌克兰方面军的一个独立单位。此时，该军已将第1543重型SU团移除，但在准备利沃夫-桑多梅日行动时，于7月加入了第363近卫重型SU团（ISU-122）。8月，第18坦克军接收了第452轻炮兵团，该团装备有24门76毫米牵引式火炮。在战争剩余时间里，第452和第1000团被用作轻炮兵或反坦克部队，因为它们的装备几乎相同，每团都有24门76毫米火炮。1944年11月，第18坦克军成为第3乌克兰方面军预备队的一部分，并在该方面军指挥下作战直至战争结束。该军于1945年5月在匈牙利结束了其战时任务。<cr>苏联二战战斗序列 第二卷作者：查尔斯·C·夏普

The 190th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in March 1941 and was assigned to the Reserves of the Southwestern Front. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was at about 50% strength. The Division was wiped out in the Uman pocket in August 1941.

The Division was reformed in October 1941, assigned to the 25th Army in the Far East where it spent the remainder of the war.

The Division was sometimes known as the Poltavskaya (Poltava) Rifle Division.

text:
The 191st Soviet Rifle Division was formed in April 1941 and was assigned to the Leningrad Military District. At the start of Operation Barbarossa the Division was still forming and it was at about 55% strength. 

The Division was assigned to the Luga Operations Group in July 1941. It suffered very heavy casualties in the defence of Leningrad and had to be withdrawn to be rebuilt. By November 1941 the Division was assigned to the 4th Army.

text:
The Soviet 193rd Rifle Division was established in the Kharkov Military District on March 14, 1941. By June 22, 1941 it was still forming near Kamenka in the Kiev Military District and was at close to 50% strength. The Division fought at Rozhits and Kivertsy and by July 8th it was down to 3,500 men. It was destroyed in the Kiev pocket. 

It's Commander, Col. A.K. Berestov, escaped the pocket, and went on to command the 124th Rifle Division, until his death in July 1942.

The division was reformed at Sorochinsk, in the South Urals Military District, in early 1942 and was held in reserve until committed at Stalingrad in September 1942, where it suffered very heavy casualties. In November, 1942 the Division was withdrawn from the field to be rebuilt. 

The rebuilt division was assigned to the 65th Army in February 1943; it was under the command of Lieutenant General Pavel Batov, part of Colonel General K. K. Rokossovski's Central Front. The 193rd would remain under these commanders for the duration of the war.

The Division fought at Kursk, in Operation Bagration, participated in the liberation of Danzig, and finished the war on the Oder river.

The Division was awarded the honorific of Dnepr, Red Banner, Order of Lenin, Order of Suvorov, and Order of Kutuzov.



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 

Steen Ammentrop, The Generals.

Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
苏联第193步兵师于1941年3月14日在哈尔科夫军区成立。到1941年6月22日，该师仍在基洛夫军区的卡缅卡附近组建，接近50%% s实力。该师在罗日希茨和基韦尔斯基作战，并于7月8日减员至3,500人，在基辅包围圈中被消灭。

其指挥官A.K.别列斯托夫上校逃出了包围圈，并继续指挥第124步兵师，直至1942年7月去世。

该师于1942年初在南乌拉尔军区的索罗钦斯基重建，并一直作为预备队直到1942年9月被投入斯大林格勒战役，在此遭受了严重损失。1942年11月，该师从战场撤出以重建。

重建后的第193步兵师于1943年2月被分配给第65集团军，并由列宁格勒方面军的副司令巴托夫中将指挥，隶属于科涅夫大将的中央方面军。在整个战争期间，该师一直在这两位指挥官手下服役。

该师参加了库尔斯克战役、巴巴罗萨行动和但泽解放战，并在奥得河畔结束了战争。

该师获得了第聂伯红旗勋章、列宁勋章、苏沃洛夫勋章和库图佐夫勋章的荣誉。

text: The 196th Infantry Division was formed in November 1939 as part of the 7th Wave. It contained the 340th and 345th Infantry Regiments, 223rd Light Artillery Battalion and various support units. In September 1940 the division was on garrison duty in Norway. It had gained the 362nd Infantry Regiment but its 345th Infantry Regiment had been sent to the 199th Infantry Division. The artillery battalion had been upgraded to the 223rd Artillery Regiment. By late 1943 elements of the division were being sent to Army Group Centre in Russia. By July 1944 the bulk of the division was in Russia although some elements remained in Norway. In September 1944 the division was largely destroyed. text: The 197th Infantry Division, was sent to the central sector of the Russian Front in July 1941, and remained there throughout the rest of its existence. It fought at Smolensk, played a prominent role in the minor battle of encirclement at Roslavl in August, defended a sector near Vyazma in September, and took part in the battles around Moscow in December 1941 and January 1942. Engaged in skirmishing and the defensive battles of Army Group Center in 1942, the 197th also took part in the Rzhev withdrawal in early 1943. By April 30, it was down to four grenadier battalions, and the 321st Grenadier Regiment had been disbanded. The division was involved in the fighting west of Smolensk in the fall of 1943, and most of it was destroyed in the huge Soviet summer offensive of 1944. The division broke up that July near Vitebsk, along with much of the 3rd Panzer Army and the bulk of the 4th Army. The last commander of the 197th Infantry Division, Colonel Hans Hahne, is still missing and was presumably killed. The divisional staff, however, was pulled out of the battle after Hahne disappeared on June 24 and was used to form Staff, Corps Detachment H.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text: The 198th Infantry Division was formed in November 1939 as part of the 7th Wave. It contained the 305th, 308th and 326th Infantry Regiments, 235th Light Artillery Battalion and various support units. In January 1940 the artillery battalion was upgraded to the 235th Artillery Regiment. In May 1940 one battalion from the 326th Regiment was detached for garrison duty in Copenhagen but was replaced. In April 1941 the division participated in the invasion of Greece. During Operation Barbarossa the division was attached to the 11th Army in Romania. In the summer of 1944 the division was withdrawn to France and rebuilt with the Bohemian Shadow Division. By November 1944 the division had been pushed back into Germany and absorbed numerous independent units including the 1432nd Fortress Infantry Battalion, 40th Fortress Machine Gun Battalion, 8th Ship's Company Battalion and one company from the 687th Naval Artillery Battalion. The division subsequently withdrew to the Neckar River in southern German where it was taken prisoner by the Americans. <cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第198步兵师成立于1939年11月，属于第七波组建的部队。该师包括第305团、第308团和第326团，以及第235轻炮营和其他支援单位。1940年1月，炮兵营升级为第235炮兵团。1940年5月，从第326团中抽调一个营前往丹麦守备，但随后被替换。1941年4月，该师参加了入侵希腊的行动。在巴巴罗萨行动期间，该师隶属于罗马尼亚境内的第11集团军。1944年夏季，该师撤至法国并重建，与波希米亚影子师合并。到1944年11月，该师被推回德国境内，并吸收了多个独立单位，包括第1432要塞步兵营、第40要塞机枪营、第8舰艇连和来自第687海军炮兵团的一个连队。随后，该师撤退至南部德国的内卡河地区并被美军俘虏。<cr>参考文献：George F. Nafziger, 《二战期间德军战斗序列：步兵》<cr>条目由Chris Munson提供

The 198th Soviet Rifle Division was formed in October 1941 from the remnants of the 198th Mechanised Division and the newly raised 1027th and 1029th Rifle Regiments. It was assigned to the 23rd Army, Northern Front.

It was with the 10th Guards Army of the Kurland Group (Leningrad Front) in May 1945.

text:
The 199th Soviet Rifle Division was established in the Ukraine, in March, 1941, assigned to the Southwestern Front. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was approximately 50% (6,700 men) in strength and by August, 1941, it was down to 1,900 men. It was one of the few rifle divisions that did not suffer the fate of encirclement in 1941.

The Division fought at Lake Ilmen and Kharkov and was disbanded in September 1942. 

The Division was recreated at Kalinin from the 126th and 128th Rifle Brigades, in February 1943. It fought at Smolensk and in East Prussia. With the 49th Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front in May 1945.



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 

Courtesy John Tomlinson
translation:
第199苏联步兵师于1941年3月在乌克兰成立，并被分配到西南方面军。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师大约有50%（6700人）的兵力，到了1941年8月，人数减少至1900人。它是1941年未遭受包围命运的少数步兵师之一。

该师参加了伊利门湖和哈尔科夫的战斗，并于1942年9月解散。

该师在1943年2月从第126步兵旅和第128步兵旅重组而成，驻扎在加里宁。它参加了斯摩棱斯克和东普鲁士的战斗，在1945年5月与第二白俄罗斯方面军的第49集团军一起作战。

尼格尔·阿斯基，《巴巴罗萨行动》，第三卷A

text: The 19th Guards Rifle Division was formed from the first formation of the 366th Rifle Division on March 17, 1942. At this time it was in the 52nd Army of Volkhov Front, taking part in the Lyuban Offensive Operation, which was planned to encircle and defeat the enemy forces laying siege to Leningrad. However, just at that time the German 18th Army was in the process of cutting off the Soviet Lyuban grouping in a pocket, and over the following months the division was nearly destroyed. Enough survivors emerged from the swamps in June and July to rebuild the unit, and it fought in the Second Sinyavino Offensive before it was shifted south into Kalinin Front to take part in the battle and siege of Velikiye Luki in December. In the summer of 1943 the 19th Guards fought in the battles for Smolensk, and won its first battle honor, 'Rudnya'. in September. During the offensive in the summer of 1944 it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner for its successes in the fighting around Vitebsk. It was further honored in February, 1945, with the Order of Lenin for its role in the victories in East Prussia. In the summer the division was moved by rail with its 39th Army to the Far East and saw action in the Soviet invasion of Manchuria in August, winning its second battle honor, 'Khingan', for its services.<cr><cr>
translation: 第19近卫步兵师于1942年3月17日由第366步兵师的第一个编成单位组建而成。当时它隶属于沃尔霍夫方面军的第52集团军，参与了卢班进攻战役，旨在包围并击败围攻列宁格勒的德军部队。然而，在此期间，德国第18集团军正在切断苏联卢班集群的包围圈，并在接下来的几个月中，该师几乎被消灭殆尽。6月和7月间，从沼泽地里幸存下来的人数足以重建该单位，并参与了第二次辛纳维诺进攻战役。随后它被转移到加里宁方面军，在12月参加了对韦利卡亚卢基的战斗与围攻。在1943年夏天的斯摩棱斯克战役中，第19近卫步兵师赢得了它的第一个荣誉称号“鲁德尼亚”。同年9月，由于其在维捷布斯克地区的战斗中的成功表现，在1944年夏季攻势期间被授予红旗勋章。该师于1945年2月因在东普鲁士的胜利中所起的作用而获得列宁勋章进一步荣誉。夏天时，该师随第39集团军通过铁路转移到远东，并参与了苏联入侵满洲的战役，在8月份赢得了它的第二个荣誉称号“兴安岭”。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: The 19th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 19th Light Division. The Hungarian Government reluctantly agreed to support the Germans 1942 summer offensive Fall Blau and allocated the Hungarian Second Army to the task. Each light division in the Second Army was reinforced with three battalions from sister divisions in Hungary but nonetheless each division was only slightly larger than half the size of its German counterparts. Second Army's role in the offensive was to guard the German northern flank on the Don River. During the Stalingrad Campaign the Second Army suffered over 60% casualties but was generally able to retreat in good order. By 1943 the division was part of the Hungarian Occupation Group assigned to security duties in occupied Russia. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 19th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 19th Reserve Division. In January of 1944 the Hungarian First Army to which the division was subordinate, mobilized to defend Hungary's northern Carpathian frontier against the advancing Red Army. The division was disbanded in August 1944.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第19匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括约9500人，下辖一名少将、2个团（每个团有3个营和一个机枪连）以及一个炮兵团（拥有7个炮兵连）和其他支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多兵力参加东线作战，大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本没有变化。该旅更名为第19轻型师。匈牙利政府勉强同意支持德军在1942年夏季的蓝色行动，并将匈牙利第二集团军分配给此任务。第二集团军的任务是在进攻中保护德国北部顿河沿岸的侧翼。在斯大林格勒战役期间，第二集团军伤亡超过60%% c，但总体上能够有秩序地撤退。到1943年，该师成为匈牙利占领部队的一部分，被分配到占领区执行治安任务。作为对斯大林格勒之后的重新组织，第19轻型师与其他单位合并，并更名为第19预备师。1944年1月，在上级匈牙利第一集团军指挥下，该师动员起来保卫匈牙利北部喀尔巴阡山脉边境免受红军进攻。该师于1944年8月解散。<cr><cr>Nigel Thomas 博士和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利陆军》<cr><cr>Chris Munson 提供

text: Sent to Russia in 1941, the 19th Panzer Division fought in the Bialystock, Minsk and Smolensk encirclements, at Nevel, and in the Battle of Moscow. Losses were so heavy that two of its three panzer battalions had to be disbanded. It nevertheless remained on the central sector in the defensive battles of 1942 and was sent to the critical southern sector in late 1942.<cr>In January 1943, it escaped to Army Group Don after the 8th Italian Army, which it had been supporting, collapsed. The division took part in the Donets battles of early 1943, the Kharkov counteroffensive of March 1943, and the Battle of Kursk offensive of July 1943, and suffered heavy casualties in these battles and in the subsequent retreats. It was fighting near Kiev in November 1943, at Zhitomir in December, and was heavily engaged in the withdrawal through the northern Ukraine in March 1944. It formed part of General Hube's 'Floating Pocket' in March and April. Rushed north after Army Group Centre was crushed, the 19th and two other panzer divisions surprised and destroyed the III Soviet Tank Corps north of Warsaw and thus halted the Russian summer offensive of 1944. It was cited for this action. In autumn 1944, the 19th Panzer was resisting west of the Vistula. Now at battle group strength, the division retreated through southern and eastern Poland, fought in the Baranov Bridgehead battles on January 1945, and the subsequent retreat through Warthegau, Silesia and southern Germany, and ended the war in the Deutsch-Brod pocket east of Prague.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第19装甲师于1941年被派往俄罗斯，参加了比亚韦斯托克、明斯克和斯摩棱斯克的包围战，在涅夫勒作战，并参与了莫斯科战役。损失惨重，其三个装甲营中有两个不得不解散。尽管如此，该师仍在1942年的防御战斗中留在中央战区，并于1942年末被派往关键的南部战区。<cr>第19装甲师在1943年1月逃离了支持的第8意大利集团军崩溃后的北方集团军群。该师参加了1943年初的顿涅茨克战役、1943年3月的哈尔科夫反击战以及1943年7月的库尔斯克攻势，并在这些战斗和随后的撤退中遭受了重大伤亡。<cr>第19装甲师于1943年11月在基辅附近作战，在12月在日托米尔作战，于1944年3月在北部乌克兰的大规模撤退中进行了激烈战斗。该师是胡贝将军的“浮动包围圈”中的组成部分，在3月和4月期间。<cr>第19装甲师在中央集团军群被摧毁后匆忙北上，与另外两个装甲师一起出乎意料地消灭了位于华沙北部的苏联第三坦克军，并因此阻止了俄罗斯1944年的夏季攻势。该师因这一行动而受到表彰。<cr>1944年秋季，第19装甲师在维斯瓦河西侧抵抗。此时已降至战斗群规模，该师撤退通过波兰南部和东部地区，在1945年1月的巴诺夫桥头堡战役中作战，并随后从沃特加、西里西亚到德国南部的大规模撤退中作战，最终于普拉格以东的德意志-布罗德包围圈结束战争。<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham Jr., 《二战中的装甲师、装甲掷弹兵师和武装党卫军师：德国战斗序列卷三》

text: The 19th Rifle Division was originally formed in 1922 as a territorial unit. In 1923 it was renamed the 19th Voronezh Rifle Division. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it consisted of the 32nd, 282nd and 315th Rifle Regiments, 90th Artillery Regiment, 103rd Howitzer Regiment and various support units. It entered combat against the Germans on July 19, 1941 near Yelnya as part of the 24th Army of the Western Front. It participated in the Elninskaya Offensive, the Battle of Moscow, Rzhev Offensive in 1942, the Rzhev-Sychevka Offensive, Third Battle of Kharkov and Belgord-Kharkov Offensive in 1943 as part of the 7th Guards Army. The division also participated in the Poltava-Kremenchuk Offensive, Pyatihatskoy Offensive, Bereznegovatoe-Snigirevskaya Offensive, Odessa, Chisinau and Izmail Offensives, Belgrade Offensive and Bratislava-Brnovskoy Offensive. In 1944 its combat path took it through Romania, Bulgaria, Yugoslavia, Hungary, and Czechoslovakia where it ended the war. The division was awarded the Order of Suvorov 2nd degree in January 1945.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第19步兵师最初成立于1922年，作为地方部队。1923年改名为第19沃罗涅日步兵师。在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师由第32团、第282团和第315团组成，并包括第90炮兵团、第103榴弹炮团以及各种支援单位。它于1941年7月19日在叶连纳附近与德军交战，当时隶属于西方方面军的第24集团军。<cr>该师参与了以下战役：<cr>埃伦斯卡亚攻势、莫斯科会战、1942年的日兹赫夫攻势、1943年的日兹赫夫-西切夫卡攻势、第三次哈尔科夫战役和别尔哥罗德-哈尔科夫攻势。<cr>此外，该师还参与了波尔塔瓦-克列缅丘格攻势、皮亚季哈茨基攻势、别尔热涅沃-斯尼吉雷夫斯基攻势、敖德萨攻势、奇什蒂纳乌攻势、伊斯梅尔攻势、贝尔格莱德攻势和布拉迪斯拉发-布罗诺夫斯基攻势。<cr>1944年，该师的战斗路径经过罗马尼亚、保加利亚、南斯拉夫、匈牙利和捷克斯洛伐克，并在那里结束战争。该师于1945年1月被授予苏沃罗夫勋章二级奖章。<cr>克里斯·芒森提供<cr><cr>第19步兵师的战斗历程显示了其在二战东线战场上的广泛参与和卓越贡献。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text:
The 19th Tank Corps HQ was formed in December 1942.<cr>The 19th Tank Corps formed up and trained in Bryansk Front reserves from February to April 1943, and then was transferred to Central Front. It was one of the first reserve units moved to counter the German 9th Army's attack on the northern flank of the Kursk salient in July, by which time the improvised Armored Car Battalion had been replaced by 91st Motorcycle Battalion in the corps. 19th Tank Corps suffered heavy losses in the Battle of Kursk, and in
late July was sent back to Moscow Military District, where it spent two months reforming to the 1943 Tank Corps standard. The corps went to the South Front in September.<cr> The 19th Tank Corps fought across southern Russia with South Front (in October 1943 renamed 4th Ukrainian Front) until the spring of 1944. While the basic composition of the corps remained the same, the assigned SU regiments fluctuated depending on the mission. In October-November 1943 as the corps took part in the Melitopol Operation, 1452nd SU Regiment (SU-85s) was part of the corps. In April - May 1944 when the corps was the Mobile Group for the break in to the Crimea, the corps had two SU Regiments.<cr> After the fall of the Crimea, 19th Tank Corps went into STAVKA Reserve, and then back to Moscow Military District in June 1944. At this time the tank brigades were probably re-equipped with T-34/85 tanks all or in part, because the corps was generally built up while in reserve. It went back to the front in the Baltic in early July.<cr> Even after it was committed in the Baltic, 19th Tank Corps continued to receive reinforcements. The 19th Tank Corps remained in the Baltic theater until the end of the war in May 1945.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第19坦克军司令部于1942年12月成立。该坦克军从1943年2月至4月在 Bryansk 方面军的预备队中编成并训练，随后被调往中央方面军。<cr>它是最早一批用于对抗德国第9集团军对库尔斯克突出部北翼进攻的预备部队之一，在此之前，该坦克军中的临时装甲车营已被替换为第91摩托化步兵营。在库尔斯克战役中，第19坦克军遭受了重大损失，并于7月下旬被调回莫斯科军区，在那里花费两个月时间重组至1943年标准的坦克军编制。<cr>该军于9月前往南方面军。<cr>从1943年10月至1944年春季，第19坦克军与南方面军（1943年10月改名为第4乌克兰方面军）一起在南部俄罗斯作战。尽管该军的基本编制保持不变，但分配给它的自行火炮团会根据任务的不同而有所变化。<cr>1943年10月至11月，在梅利托波尔行动中，第1452自行火炮团（SU-85）是该坦克军的一部分。在1944年4月至5月期间，当该坦克军作为进入克里米亚突破的机动部队时，它拥有两个自行火炮团。<cr>克里米亚沦陷后，第19坦克军被调至最高统帅部预备队，并于1944年6月返回莫斯科军区。此时，坦克旅可能全部或部分重新装备了T-34/85坦克，因为该坦克军在预备队期间得到了加强。<cr>它于7月初重返波罗的海战区。<cr>即使是在被投入波罗的海战区后，第19坦克军仍继续获得增援。直到1945年5月战争结束，第19坦克军一直留在波罗的海战区。<cr>参考文献：Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp

text:
The 19th Tank Division was formed December 1940 in Kiev Special Military District as part of 9th Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
37th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Tank Bns - each 20 to 30 light tanks
38th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Tank Bns - each 20 to 30 light tanks
19th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
19th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1 light, 1 medium bn
19th Reconnaissance Battalion
19th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
19th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>This was one of the two divisions formed separately, between the two great 'waves' of Soviet armored formations of July 1940 and February-March 1941. In February 1941 19th Tank Division became part of the newly-formed 22nd Mechanized Corps and moved to near the border, at Rovno.<cr>On 22 June 1941 the division was nearly at full strength for personnel, with 9347 men present for duty. However, it was short almost 50% of the NCOs authorized, and over 33% of the offiicers and technicians. The two tank regiments had a total of 34 BT tanks, 122 T-26s, and 7 OT-26s. The howitzer regiment had all of its authorized guns, but the division had only 20% of its
trucks and a little over half the tractors required. This meant that in the initial marches, most of the division was on foot and could not keep up with the tanks, and when tanks broke down there was no way to recover them. The division went into battle on 24 June, and by 26 June 1941 had only 4 working tanks left, and had lost half the howitzers in the division.<cr>Fighting under 22nd Mechanized Corps throughout June and July to mid- August, the division was reduced to less than 1500 men and less than a halfdozen
armored cars and light tanks by 20 August. Shortly afterwards, 19th Tank Division was disbanded.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

这是在1940年7月和1941年2月至3月苏联装甲部队的两次大规模组建之间单独成立的两个师之一。1941年2月，第19装甲师成为新组建的第22机械化军的一部分，并转移到靠近边境的罗夫诺。

1941年6月22日，该师人员几乎满编，有9347人服役。然而，它缺少近50%授权的士官和超过33%的军官及技术人员。两个坦克团共有34辆BT坦克、122辆T-26坦克和7辆OT-26坦克。榴弹炮团拥有所有授权火炮，但该师只有20%的卡车和略多于一半所需的拖拉机。这意味着在最初的行军中，大多数部队都是步行前进，无法跟上坦克的速度；当坦克出现故障时也无法回收。

该师于1941年6月24日投入战斗，并到1941年6月26日只剩下4辆可工作的坦克，损失了半数的榴弹炮。在整个6月至7月中下旬，在第22机械化军指挥下作战后，该师人数减少至不到1500人，装甲车和轻型坦克不足六辆。

不久之后，第19装甲师被解散。苏联战斗序列 第一卷 作者：查尔斯·C·肖普

text: The 1st Air Army was formed on May 10, 1942, within the Soviet Western Front.<cr>When it was formed, the 1st Air Army was made up of two fighter aviation divisions (with four fighter aviation regiments each), two mixed aviation divisions (with two fighter aviation regiments, two assault aviation regiments and one bombing regiment each) a training aviation regiment, a long-range reconnaissance aviation regiment, a communications squadron, and a night close-range bombing aviation regiment.<cr>In March 1943, the Air Army also included the French Normandie Niemen squadron, which was later reorganized into a regiment. In 1942, the 1st Air Army fought alongside the troops of the Western Front, supporting them near Yukhnov, Gzhatsk and Rzhev. The Air Army later participated in the Rzhev-Sychevka, Rzhev-Vyazma, Oryol, Smolensk, Belarusian, Memel and East Prussian offensive operations.<cr>Throughout the war, the 1st Air Army made 290,000 sorties. Five of the Air Army's formations where reorganized as 'Guards Units', 50 formations were given 'honourable titles', 44 formations received various awards, 145 pilots and navigators received the title 'Hero of the Soviet Union' and over 17,000 of its servicemen were also given various medals and decorations.<cr><cr>
translation: 苏联西方面军于1942年5月10日组建了第1空军集团军。@PH0@组建时，第1空军集团军包括两个歼击航空兵师（每个师有四个歼击机团），两个混合航空兵师（每个师有两个歼击机团、两个强击机团和一个轰炸机团）、一个训练航空兵团、一个远程侦察航空兵团、一个通信中队以及一个夜间近距离轰炸航空兵团。@PH1@1943年3月，空军集团军还包括法国诺曼底-尼缅中队，该中队后来重组为一个团。在1942年，第1空军集团军与西方面军的部队并肩作战，在尤赫诺夫、热季茨克和列日附近提供支援。之后，空军集团军参与了列日-斯切夫卡、列日-维亚兹马、奥廖尔、斯摩棱斯克、白俄罗斯、梅梅尔和东普鲁士进攻战役。@PH2@在整个战争期间，第1空军集团军执行了29万次飞行任务。空军集团军中有五个单位被重组为“近卫”部队，50个单位获得了“荣誉称号”，44个单位获得各种奖励，145名飞行员和领航员获得了“苏联英雄”的称号，超过17,000名官兵也获得了各种勋章和奖章。@PH3@

text: The corps was formed in April 1941 and consisted of the 1st, 204th, and 211th Airborne Brigades. In 1941, it fought as a part of Southwestern Front to defend Kiev. It was destroyed with the collapse of the Kiev pocket in August and was reformed in December 1941. It was assigned to Western Front. Between December and February 1942, it participated in airborne operations in the central region, culminating in an unsuccessful operation to seize airfields in the Demyansk Pocket that reduced the corps to about 900 effectives. In August, it was reorganized into the 37th Guards Rife Division. The corps was reformed in fall 1942, and in December it was used to form two new guards airborne divisions, the 4th Guards Airborne Division and the 9th Guards Airborne Division. <cr><cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King

text:
The 1st Artillery Division of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (RGK) in October 1942 with the Southwestern Front, under the command of Colonel Vikenty Mazur. It was composed of the 274th, 275th, and 331st Howitzer, the 1162nd and 1166th Gun, and the 468th, 501st, and 1189th Anti-Tank (Tank Destroyer) Artillery Regiments. In addition to its regiments, the division included the organic 816th Separate Reconnaissance Artillery Battalion and the 45th Separate Corrective Aviation Squadron. It was sent into combat on 9 November in the area of Kletskaya and Serafimovich, supporting the 21st Army of the Southwestern Front in the final stage of the Soviet defensive phase of the Battle of Stalingrad. From the second half of November to January 1943, the units of the 1st Artillery, operationally subordinated to the 24th and 65th Armies of the Don Front, provided artillery support in the encirclement and defeat of the German troops in the Stalingrad area.

After the Battle of Stalingrad, the 1st Artillery was transferred to the Central Front during February, where it was subordinated to the 65th Army and later the 70th Army. The division was reorganized on 20 February 1943, with its regiments combined into three brigades one howitzer, one gun, and one anti-tank (tank destroyer). In recognition of its 'courage and heroism', the division was converted into the 1st Guards Artillery Division RGK on 1 March 1943.<cr><cr>
translation:
1942年10月，最高统帅部预备队（RGK）的第一炮兵师在西南方面军服役，由维克托尼·马祖尔上校指挥。该师包括第274、275和331炮兵旅，第1162和1166野战炮兵旅以及第468、501和1189反坦克（坦克歼击车）炮兵团。此外，该师还包括独立侦察炮兵营第816和独立校正航空中队第45。它于11月9日在克列茨卡亚和塞拉菲莫夫地区投入战斗，支援西南方面军的第21集团军，在苏联斯大林格勒保卫战防御阶段的最后阶段作战。

从11月下旬到1943年1月，第一炮兵师在操作上隶属于顿河方面军的第24和65集团军，为包围并击败斯大林格勒地区的德军提供了炮兵支援。 

经过斯大林格勒战役后，第一炮兵师于1943年2月被转移到中央方面军，在那里它最初隶属于第65集团军，后来转隶给第70集团军。该师在1943年2月20日进行了重组，其团合并为三个旅：一个榴弹炮、一个野战炮和一个反坦克（坦克歼击车）旅。为了表彰它的“勇气与英雄主义”，该师于1943年3月1日被改编为最高统帅部预备队的第一近卫炮兵师。

text: The First Baltic Front was a major formation of the Red Army during the Second World War. It was commanded by Army General Andrey Yeryomenko, succeeded by Army General Ivan Bagramyan. It was formed by renaming the Kalinin Front in October 12, 1943, and took part in several important military operations, most notably Operation Bagration in the summer of 1944. The 1st Baltic Front also assisted in lifting the Siege of Leningrad on January 27, 1944, as well as in Operation Samland, at that time known as the Samland Group, captured Knigsberg in April 1945.<cr><cr>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Baltic_Front
translation: 第一个波罗的海方面军是苏联红军在第二次世界大战期间的一个主要部队。该方面军由陆军元帅安德烈·叶里门科指挥，后由陆军元帅伊万·巴格拉米扬接任。它成立于1943年10月12日，当时将加里宁方面军改名为第一个波罗的海方面军，并参与了多次重要军事行动，最著名的是1944年夏季的巴格拉季昂行动。此外，该方面军还协助解除了列宁格勒的围困（1944年1月27日），并在“萨姆兰特”行动中发挥了作用，在当时被称为萨姆兰特集团，并于1945年4月占领了柯尼斯堡。<cr><cr><cr>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Baltic_Front

text: Initially, the Belorussian Front was created on 20 October 1943 as the new designation of the existing Central Front. It was placed under the command of General Konstantim Rokossovsky, who had been commanding the Central Front. It launched the Gomel-Rechitsa Offensive in 1943 and then the Kalinkovichi-Mozyr Offensive in 1944.<cr>It was then renamed the 1st Belorussian Front (1BF) on 17 February 1944 following the Dniepr-Carpathian Offensive. A few days later, on 21 February, the Rogachev-Zhlobin Operation commenced, which continued until 26 February. The next operation was the Bobruysk Offensive, part of Operation Bagration, and on 26 June the attacks of 1BF encircled Bobruisk, trapping 40,000 troops of the German 41st Panzer Corps (part of 9th Army). From 18 July-2 August the Front was part of the Lublin-Brest Offensive. From 2 August to 30 September, the Front was engaged cleaning out Germans to the east of the Vistula (during which the Battle of Radzymin took place from 1-10 August). Its 8th Guards, 28th, 47th, 65th, 69th, and 70th Armies were involved at Radzymin. Later during that same period, on 14 September, 1BF with the support of Polish forces it captured Praga, a suburb of Warsaw.<cr>The next attack was the Warsaw-Poznan Operation, a part of the Vistula-Oder Offensive. On 13 January, 1BF began an offensive toward Schlossberg in East Prussia, against which they met stiff resistance from the 3rd Panzer Army.The 1st Belorussian Front opened its attack on the German Ninth Army from the Magnuszew and Pulawy bridgeheads at 08:30 on 14 January, again commencing with a heavy bombardment. The 33rd and 69th Armies broke out of the Pulawy bridgehead to a depth of 30 km, while the 5th Shock and 8th Guards Armies broke out of the Magnuszew bridgehead. The 2nd and 1st Guards Tank Armies were committed after them to exploit the breach. On 25 January, the Front cut off the fortress city of Poznan which held 66,000 Germans, and continued its 80 km a day advance, leaving the 8th Guards Army to lay siege to the city, which they finally took on 23 February. While Adolf Hitler dealt with home issues in Germany, Stalin had defeated the German Army near Warsaw.<cr>Along with the 1st Ukrainian Front, 1BF then stormed Berlin in the climatic Battle of Berlin.They finished the encirclement of Berlin on 25 April when units of the 1BF and 1UF met at Kietzen west of Berlin. After heavy street by street and house to house fighting, General Helmuth Weidling, the commander of Berlin's garrison, met with Marshal Vasily Chuikov and surrendered Berlin unconditionally at 15:00 hours local time on 2 May.<cr><cr>Wikipedia 1st Belorussian Front
translation: 最初，白俄罗斯方面军于1943年10月20日成立，是原有中央方面军的新名称。该方面军由康斯坦丁·罗科索夫斯基将军指挥，他曾领导中央方面军。它发起了戈梅利-雷奇察攻势（1943年）和卡林科维奇-莫吉廖夫攻势（1944年）。<cr>随后，在第聂伯河-喀尔巴阡山脉攻势之后的1944年2月17日，该方面军更名为第一白俄罗斯方面军（1BF）。几天后，即2月21日，罗加切夫-兹洛宾行动开始，并持续到2月26日。接下来是鲍里斯拉夫攻势，属于巴格拉季昂行动的一部分，在6月26日，1BF的攻击包围了鲍里斯拉夫，俘获了4.1装甲军（隶属于第9集团军）的4万名士兵。<cr>从7月18日至8月2日，该方面军参与了卢布林-别列津纳攻势。从8月2日至9月30日，该方面军在维斯瓦河以东清理德军（期间发生了拉迪米奇战役，时间为8月1日至10日）。其第8近卫集团军、第28集团军、第47集团军、第65集团军、第69集团军和第70集团军参与了拉迪米奇战役。同一时期稍晚，在9月14日，1BF在波兰军队的支援下占领了华沙郊区普拉加。<cr>下一次攻击是华沙-波兹南行动，这是维斯瓦-奥得进攻战役的一部分。1月13日，第1白俄罗斯方面军开始向东普鲁士的施洛斯贝格发动攻势，在此过程中遭遇了来自第3装甲集团军的顽强抵抗。1月14日上午8点30分，第1白俄罗斯方面军从马格努谢夫和波乌亚两个桥头堡出发，对德国第九集团军发起了攻击，并以猛烈炮击开始进攻。第33集团军和第69集团军突破了波乌亚桥头堡并向纵深推进了30公里，而第5突击集团军和第8近卫集团军则从马格努谢夫桥头堡突破。随后，第2和第1近卫坦克集团军被投入战斗以利用突破口。1月25日，方面军切断了拥有6.6万名德国守军的要塞城市波兹南，并继续每天推进80公里，在此期间留下第8近卫集团军围攻该城，最终于2月23日攻克。当阿道夫·希特勒忙于处理德国内部事务时，斯大林在华沙附近击败了德国军队。<cr>随后，与第1乌克兰方面军一起，第1白俄罗斯方面军发起了对柏林的进攻，在决定性的柏林战役中攻占了这座城市。他们在4月25日完成了对柏林的包围圈，当时第1白俄罗斯方面军和第1乌克兰方面军的部队在柏林以西的凯岑会师。经过激烈的逐街逐屋战斗后，柏林守备司令赫尔穆特·魏德林将军与瓦西里·楚伊科夫元帅会面，并于5月2日当地时间下午3点无条件投降。

text: The 1st Cavalry Division fought in the battles of Minsk, Gomel, and Kiev (1941), and was used in anti-partisan operations in the Pripjet marshes. text:
The 1st Guards Airborne Division was formed in accordance with an order from 8 December 1942 from the 4th Airborne Corps headquarters and the 1st Airborne Brigade.<cr> 
The division became part of the Special Group commanded by Mikhail Khozin. In mid-February 1943, it was concentrated south of Zaluceni. Its objective was to advance into a breach in the German lines in the 1st Shock Army offensive zone. In March, the division fought in the Staraya Russa operation, but was unable to capture the town. In August, it made another attempt and cut the Staraya Russa-Kholm road on 18 August. It then advanced to the Porus River at the villages of Chirikov and Kotov. The division entrenched in positions there. After the end of the fighting, it was sent to the rear to rest and refit; in September, it was transferred to the Steppe Front.<cr>
It fought in the capture of Left-bank Ukraine in the area east of Kremenchug. On 9 October, it crossed the Dnieper near Moldavan Island and the villages of Soloshino and Perevolochna. October 9, 1943, crossed the Dnieper near the island of Moldovans, Soloshino, Perevolochna, advancing in the second echelon of the 37th Army. From October to December, the division advanced towards Krivoy Rog and Kirovograd.<cr>
In January and February 1944, the division fought in the Korsun-Shevchenkovsky Offensive and took part in the encirclement of German troops around Zvenigorod. The division was awarded the honorific 'Zvenigorod' for its actions during the fighting on 13 February. Between March and April, it fought in the Uman-Botosani Offensive. During the offensive, the division reached the Dniester and Dubasari. During the summer it fought in the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive. During the offensive, it advanced in the second echelon of 53rd Army towards Focsani. On 31 August, it entered Bucharest. At the end of September, the division reached the Hungarian border northwest of Arad. On 6 October, it launched an offensive from there during the Battle of Debrecen and reached the Tisza. The division crossed the Tisza in November during the Budapest Offensive.<cr>
By February 1945, the division was positioned on the Hron. It fought in the Bratislava-Brno Offensive in April and the Prague Offensive in May.<cr><cr>
translation:
第1近卫空降师于1942年12月8日根据第四空降军司令部和第一空降旅的命令组建。<cr>

该师成为米哈伊尔·霍津指挥的特别小组的一部分。1943年2月中旬，它在扎卢岑尼以南集结。其任务是在第1突击集团军进攻区域内的德军防线缺口处推进。3月，该师参加了斯塔罗亚鲁萨行动，但未能占领该镇。8月，它再次尝试，并于8月18日切断了斯塔罗亚鲁萨至霍尔姆的道路。随后，它推进到普罗斯河畔的奇里科夫和科托夫村。该师在这些位置上构筑防御工事。战斗结束后，它被送往后方休整和整补；9月，它被转移到顿斯克方面军。<cr>

该师参加了左岸乌克兰地区的占领行动，在克雷门丘格以东地区作战。10月9日，它在莫尔达万岛附近以及索洛什尼科夫村和佩列沃洛奇纳村附近渡过第聂伯河，并作为第37集团军第二梯队推进。从10月至12月，该师向克里沃伊罗格和基罗斯拉夫方向推进。<cr>
1944年1月和2月，该师参加了科尔松-舍甫琴科夫斯基进攻战役，并参与了在兹韦尼哥罗德附近包围德国军队的行动。由于其在2月13日战斗中的表现，该师被授予“兹韦尼哥罗德”荣誉称号。3月至4月期间，它参加了乌曼-波托恰尼进攻战役，在此次进攻中，该师推进至德涅斯特河和杜巴塞里。夏季时，该师参加了雅西-奇普利纳进攻战役，并在53集团军的第二梯队向福克桑推进。8月31日，它进入布加勒斯特。9月底，该师到达阿腊德西北部的匈牙利边境。10月6日，在德布勒森战役中从那里发起攻势并推进至蒂萨河。<cr>10月底，该师在布达佩斯进攻战役期间渡过蒂萨河。<cr><cr><cr>到1945年2月，该师部署于赫龙河。它参加了4月的布拉迪斯拉发-布尔诺进攻战役和5月的布拉格进攻战役。<cr><cr><cr>

text: On August 6, 1942, the army formed from the 2nd Reserve Army with five Guards Rifle Divisions, the 37th, 38th, 39th, 40th and 41st. On August 9, the army was incorporated into Southeastern Front. On August 18, it was transferred to the Stalingrad Front (renamed Don Front on September 30).<cr>On October 16, 1942, the headquarters of the army transferred into Stavka reserve and its troops transferred to the 24th Army. On 25 October 1942 the army was disbanded, its headquarters was converted to the field management of the 2nd formation of Southwestern Front according to the Stavka directive of 22 October 1942.<cr>On November 5, 1942, 1st Guards Army was reformed from 63rd Army according to the Stavka directive of November 1. The army was a part of Southwestern Front. When the German troops were making their attack on Stalingrad, the First Guards Army was facing the Italian Eighth Army in the upper part of the Don River. The Army participated in Stalingrad strategic offensive Operation Uranus. As the right flank of the front shock group, 1st Guards Army with 5th Tank Army created the appearance of the Stalingrad encirclement 'boiler'.<cr>On December 5, 1942, 1st Guards Army is split, its left wing being renamed 3rd Guards Army of the Southwestern Front.<cr>The 1st Guards Army was created on December 8, 1942, according to the Stavka directive of December 5, 1942. The troops of the army was formed from the part of the operational group of Southwestern Front, and the headquarters of the army formed of management of 4th Army Reserve. It is composed of units of the right wing of the previous version of the 1st guard army and some reinforcement units : the 4th Guards Rifle Corps, the 6th Guards Rifle Corps, the 153rd Rifle Division, and the 18th Tank Corps. After the German relief operation was held, the 1st Guards Army, along with the 6th Army and 3rd Guards Army, launched an attack in Operation Little Saturn. During the operation the Soviets defeated the Italian Eighth Army and gained a respectable amount of territory. By the end of the year, the 1st Guards Army was outside Millerovo.<cr>The 1st Guards Army also took part in Operation Saturn, where the Red Army successfully drove back Army Group South to the Donets Basin in the Ukraine. The 1st Guards Army was part of the Soviet Southwestern Front, and took part in the victorious Soviet pushing into Germany in 1943 to 1945. Also, in 1943, the 1st Guards Army was the first unit of the soviet army to operate the new T-34/85 tank. Among its units when the war ended in 1945 was the 81st Rifle Division. In August, the 1st Guards Army became the headquarters of the Kiev Military District.<cr><cr>
translation: 1942年8月6日，由第二预备集团军改编而成的军队成立，下辖五个近卫步兵师：第37、38、39、40和41师。8月9日，该集团军被编入东南方面军。8月18日，它被转移到斯大林格勒方面军（9月30日改名为顿河方面军）。<cr>1942年10月16日，该集团军司令部转入最高统帅部预备队，其部队转交给第24集团军。根据1942年10月22日的最高统帅部指令，在10月25日解散了该集团军，其司令部被改编为西南方面军第二组建的野战管理机构。<cr>1942年11月5日，第一近卫集团军根据11月1日的最高统帅部指令由第63集团军改编而成，隶属于西南方面军。当德军部队对斯大林格勒发动攻击时，第一近卫集团军面对的是意大利第八集团军，在顿河上游地区。该集团军参与了斯大林格勒战略进攻天王星行动。作为前线突击集团的右翼，第一近卫集团军与第五坦克集团军共同制造了斯大林格勒包围圈“锅炉”的假象。<cr>1942年12月5日，第一近卫集团军被分割，其左翼改名为西南方面军第三近卫集团军。<cr>第1近卫集团军成立于1942年12月8日，根据最高统帅部大本营于1942年12月5日的指令组建。该集团军部队由西南方面军作战群的一部分组成，而其司令部则由第4集团军预备队管理机构构成。它包括前一版本第1近卫集团军右翼单位和一些增援单位：第4近卫步兵军、第6近卫步兵军、第153步兵师以及第18坦克军。在德军解围行动结束后，第1近卫集团军与第6集团军及第3近卫集团军一起，在“小土星”行动中发起攻击。在此期间，苏军击败了意大利第八集团军，并占领了一定数量的土地。到年底时，第1近卫集团军已位于米列罗沃之外。<cr>第1近卫集团军还参加了“土星”行动，在此行动中红军成功将南方集团军群驱逐至乌克兰的顿涅茨盆地。第1近卫集团军隶属于苏联西南方面军，并参与了苏军从1943年到1945年的胜利推进，进入德国境内。<cr>此外，在1943年，第1近卫集团军成为首个操作新T-34/85坦克的苏军单位。当战争于1945年结束时，其下属单位包括第81步兵师。<cr>在八月，第1近卫集团军成为了基辅军区司令部。<cr>司令部

text:
In recognition of its 'courage and heroism, the 1st Artillery Division was converted into the 1st Guards Artillery Division RGK on 1 March 1943. The 1st Guards Artillery Division included the 1st Guards Gun, 2nd Guards Howitzer, and 1st Guards Light Artillery Brigades, which in turn included the 201st and 205th Guards Gun, 169th and 203rd Guards Howitzer, and 167th, 200th, and 206th Guards Light Artillery Regiments. During the defensive phase of the Battle of Kursk, the division supported the 13th and 70th Armies with massed artillery fire, helping to repulse German tank and infantry attacks.

It received the Glukhov honorific on 31 August. In October the division was assigned to the 1st Ukrainian Front. In July of 1944 the division was assigned to the 7th Artillery Corps.

From 16 April to 20 May 1944 3rd Guards Light Artillery Brigade commander Colonel Viktor Zhagala temporarily commanded the division after Arkady Volchek was wounded. 76th Rifle Corps Artillery commander Colonel Viktor Khusid (promoted to major general on 18 November 1944) was appointed to lead the division on 21 May, while it was part of the 1st Ukrainian Front. The division then fought in the Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive. The division was redesignated as the 1st Guards Breakthrough Artillery Division in November 1944, reflecting its role of providing artillery concentrations for offensives. In 1945 the division fought in the Sandomierz-Silesian Offensive, the Lower Silesian Offensive, the Berlin Offensive, and the Prague Offensive, and in fighting for the cities of Szydlw, Kielce, Steinau, Lben, Sprottau, Cottbus, and Dresden.<cr><cr>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Guards_Breakthrough_Artillery_Division
translation:
为表彰其“勇气与英雄主义”，第1炮兵师于1943年3月1日改编为近卫第1炮兵师。该师包括第1近卫榴弹炮旅、第2近卫加农炮旅和第1近卫野战炮兵旅，其中又包含第201和205近卫榴弹炮团、第169和203近卫加农炮团以及第167、200和206近卫野战炮兵团。在库尔斯克防御阶段，该师支援了第13军和第70军，以密集的炮火击退了德军坦克和步兵的进攻。

该师于8月31日获得格卢霍夫荣誉称号。10月份，该师被分配给第1乌克兰方面军。1944年7月，该师被分配到第7炮兵军。

从1944年4月16日至5月20日，由于阿尔卡季·沃尔切克负伤，第3近卫野战炮兵旅指挥官维克多·扎加拉少校临时指挥该师。1944年11月18日晋升为中将的维克托·库希德少校于5月21日在第1乌克兰方面军内被任命为该师指挥官，随后参加了利沃夫-桑多梅日攻势。该师于1944年11月重新编组为近卫第1炮兵突破师，反映了其在进攻中提供集中火力的角色。1945年，该师参与了桑多梅日-西里西亚攻势、下西里西亚攻势、柏林攻势和布拉格攻势，并参加了什切青、基尔采、施泰瑙、利本、斯普劳塔乌、科特布斯和德累斯顿等城市的战斗。<cr> <cr> https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Guards_Breakthrough_Artillery_Division

text: Formed 11/26/1941 from 5th Cavalry Division as part of I Guards Cavalry Corps, it was part of Southwestern Front reserve. It was awarded the honorific titles 'Stavropol' and 'Zhitomir' in December 1943. Fought in the Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive and the Dniepr-Carpathian Offensive in 1944 and in the Battle of Berlin in 1945 as part of 1st Ukrainian Front. <cr><cr>Pettibone, Charles D., The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II: volume V - Book B Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Trafford, 2009<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 1941年11月26日由第5骑兵师改编而成，隶属于第一近卫骑兵军，并作为西南方面军预备队。该部队于1943年12月获得“斯大林诺”和“日托米尔”的荣誉称号。参加了1944年的利沃夫-桑多梅日进攻战役和第聂伯河-喀尔巴阡山进攻战役，以及1945年作为第一乌克兰方面军参加的柏林战役。<cr>资料来源：Pettibone, Charles D., 二战中军事力量的组织与战斗序列：卷V - 书B 苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟，Trafford, 2009<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text:
The 1st Guards Mechanized Corps was formed in November 1942 in the Tambov region during the re-establishment of the Mechanized Corps as a formation in the Red Army. It was then assigned to the Southwestern Front which was under the command of General Nilolai F. Vatutin to participate in the encirclement of German Army Group A in Operation Saturn, which was undertaken during the Battle of Stalingrad.<cr>The corps consisted of the following units:<cr><cr>Combat Units
1st Guards Mechanized Rifle Brigade
2nd Guards Mechanized Rifle Brigade
3rd Guards Mechanized Rifle Brigade
16, 17, 18, 19 Guards Tank Regiments (combined into the 9th Guards Tank Brigade by 1945)
116th Guards Artillery Regiment
1504th Guards Anti-Tank Regiment
267th Mortar Regiment
407th Guards Mortar Battalion<cr><cr>Support Units
54th Guards Signalling Battalion
Corps Train<cr><cr>Changes to unit organization
The 116th Guards Artillery Regiment had been replaced by the 382nd Guards, 1453rd, and 1821st self-propelled gun regiments by 1945.
The 1504th Guards Anti-Tank Regiment was no longer with the corps in 1945.
The 11th Guards Motorcycle Battalion and 1699th Anti-Aircraft Regiment had been added to the corps by 1945.<cr><cr>
