text:
The 1st Guards Special Rifle Corps was created on 4 October 1941 by special request of the STAVKA supreme command, in an area of the city of Mtsensk (the Oryol Oblast). Initially its structure included the 6th Guards Rifle Division, 5th Airborne Corps, 4th Tank Brigade, 11th Tank Brigade, the Tula military school, several Border Guard Regiments, two artillery regiments, two rocket artillery battalions and the 6th reserve aviation group. Major General Dmitri Lelyushenko was appointed the commander of the corps. The corps was given several tasks: to destroy the nearby enemy, to break through into Oryol, to slow the progress of the German tank armies, and to block the way to Tula.<cr>The Soviet government and STAVKA command highly valued the efforts and sacrifices of the 1st Guards Rifle Corps in the Oryol-Bryansk defensive operation, which took place from 4 to 18 October 1941. On 11 November the National Commissioner of Defense renamed the 4th Tank Brigade, which played a vital role in the battle of Mtsensk, the 1st Guards tank brigade. The Commander of the brigade, Colonel Mikhail Katukov, was eventually promoted to commander of the Soviet 1st Guards Tank Army, and was twice awarded the Hero of the Soviet Union award.<cr><cr>On 12 October 1941, by the order of STAVKA supreme command, the corps was transformed into the 26th Army. On 25 October 1941, its field HQ was disbanded, and its constituent formations were transferred to the 50th Army of the Bryansk Front.<cr>A new 1st Guards Rifle Corps was formed on 31 December 1941. Its first commander, Col. Afanasii Sergeevich Gryaznov, was appointed the same day; he would be promoted to Major General ten days later. As of 1 February it was under the direct command of Northwestern Front, with the following units in its order of battle:

7th Guards Rifle Division
14th, 15th, 52nd Rifle Brigades
72nd Naval Rifle Brigade
203rd, 204th and 205th Ski Brigades
878th Corps Artillery Regiment (re-designated 37th Guards Artillery Regiment later that month, with 4 batteries of 4 122mm guns each.)<cr><cr>The Corps saw action around the Demyansk Pocket for most of 1942, with a number of rifle brigades under command, but also with 7th Guards Rifle and 37th Guards Artillery under command as well. In October the Corps headquarters went into the Reserve of the Supreme High Command, where it was assigned to the 1st Reserve Army, which later became the 2nd Guards Army. For the duration of the war it served as an administrative command, with no assigned support units.<cr><cr>

1941年10月4日，根据最高统帅部大本营的特别要求，在奥廖尔州姆岑斯克市的一个区域成立了第1近卫特种步兵军。最初该部队包括第6近卫步兵师、第5空降军、第4坦克旅、第11坦克旅、图拉军事学校、几个边防团、两个炮兵团、两个火箭炮营和第6预备航空大队。少将德米特里·列柳申科被任命为该军的指挥官。该军承担了多项任务：消灭附近的敌人，突破奥廖尔，减缓德国坦克集团军的推进，并封锁通往图拉的道路。<cr>苏联政府和最高统帅部大本营高度评价第1近卫步兵军在奥廖尔-布良斯克防御行动中的努力与牺牲。该行动于1941年10月4日至18日进行。11月11日，国防人民委员将在这场姆岑斯克战役中发挥关键作用的第4坦克旅改名为第1近卫坦克旅。该旅指挥官米哈伊尔·卡图科夫上校最终被任命为苏联第1近卫坦克集团军的指挥官，并两次获得苏联英雄称号。<cr>根据最高统帅部大本营于1941年10月12日下达的命令，该军被改编为第26集团军。1941年10月25日，其野战司令部解散，组成部队转隶布良斯克方面军的第50集团军。<cr>一个新的第1近卫步兵军于1941年12月31日成立。其首任指挥官阿法纳西·谢尔盖维奇·格拉兹诺夫少校当天被任命；十天后他将晋升为少将。自1942年2月1日起，该部队直接隶属于西北方面军，并拥有以下战斗序列单位：

第七近卫步兵师
第14、15旅和第52旅
第72海军步兵旅
第203、204和205滑雪旅
第878军炮兵团（当月改称第37近卫炮兵团，下辖4个营，每营装备4门122mm火炮。）<cr><cr>该集团军在1942年大部分时间里参与了德梅耶斯克包围圈的战斗，指挥多个步兵旅，并且还指挥第七近卫步兵师和第三十七近卫炮兵团。十月间，司令部进入最高统帅部预备队，在那里被分配给第一预备集团军，该集团军后来成为第二近卫集团军。在整个战争期间，它作为行政指挥部存在，没有分配支援单位。<cr><cr>

text:
On 22 June 1941 the 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division was part of the 7th Mechanised Corps, alongside the 14th and 18th tank divisions in the Moscow Military District, assigned to the 20th Army.
23 June 1941, the 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division was replenished to the full strength of 10831 men. It was the first Soviet formation to use T-34 tanks, at Borisov, on June 30, 1941.
11 July 1941, after suffering heavy losses, the 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division was moved to the reserve of 20th army and placed north of Orsha, and was completely encircled by the German forces 14 July 1941.
25 July 1941, the elements of 6th and 175th motor rifle regiments of 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division break encirclement near Mogilev, but have suffered more losses in the heavy rearguard fighting by 30 July 1941. During that period, heavy personnel flow left few if any of the initial combatants.
By 5 August 1941, remnants of the 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division were wiped out after being encircled again in Smolensk region, in unclear circumstances.
5 August 1941, the 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division was re-formed anew within 20th army, 18 August 1941 renamed 1st armoured division and on September 21, 1941, it was renamed the 1st Guards Moscow Motor Rifle Division. The division was renamed (again) as the 1st Guards Rifle Division, in January 1943.
30 August 1941, the 1st armoured division was participating in the Yelnya Offensive, forcing back 28th Jager Division. Due heavy losses, the division was stopped advancing 10 September 1941 and was withdrawn to behind of Vop River.
18 September 1941, the 1st armoured division was withdrawn to Mozhaysk for replenishment and subordinated directly to Stavka.
30 September 1941, the 1st Guards Moscow Motor Rifle Division was assigned to 40th army and sent to Sumy region. After initial advances, the 1st Guards Moscow Motor Rifle Division started to retreat 6 October 1941 as First Battle of Kharkov was being lost by Soviet forces. After losing Sumy 10 October 1941, the division was withdrawn to the reserve and sent back to Moscow.
21 October 1941, the division was assigned to 3rd army and arrived to Naro-Fominsk. The 1st Guards Moscow Motor Rifle Division lost 70% of personnel in urban warfare before retreating from Naro-Fominsk 25 October 1941. Attempt to re-take Naro-Fominsk 28 October 1941 have failed. The division remained in Naro-Fominsk area until end of November 1941.
29 January 1942, the division liberated the village of Myatlevo in cooperation with the 415th Rifle Division during the winter counteroffensive in front of Moscow.
In 1942, the 1st Guards Moscow Motor Rifle Division was participating in Battle of Rzhev.
In July 1943, the 1st Guards Rifle Division was participating in Operation Kutuzov, in October 1943 - in Bryansk offensive, and in December 1943 - in Haradok offensive.
In JanuaryJuly 1944, the 1st Guards Rifle Division was advancing in Vitebsk - Minsk direction with heavy fighting, and was awarded 'Minsk' honorific 13 July 1944.
In November 1944, the division invaded East Prussia in Gusev area, and finally stormed Knigsberg in April 1945.
21-26 April 1945, the 1st Guards Rifle Division ended the war by storming Baltiysk as part of 11th Guards Army of the 3rd Belorussian Front.<cr><cr>
translation: 1941年6月22日，第1莫斯科机械化步兵师隶属于莫斯科军区的第7机械化军，在该军区内与第14和第18坦克师一起被分配给第20集团军。1941年6月23日，第1莫斯科机械化步兵师补充至满员人数10831人。这是第一个使用T-34坦克的苏联部队，在鲍里斯夫（Borisov）于1941年6月30日首次投入使用。1941年7月11日，遭受重大损失后，第1莫斯科机械化步兵师被调至第20集团军预备队，并部署在奥尔沙以北地区，在1941年7月14日完全被德军包围。1941年7月25日，第1莫斯科机械化步兵师的第6和第175机械化团的部分部队在莫吉廖夫附近突破了包围圈，但在激烈的后卫战斗中至1941年7月30日又遭受更多损失。在此期间，大量人员流动使得最初的作战人员几乎全部撤离。到1941年8月5日，在斯摩棱斯克地区再次被包围后，第1莫斯科机械化步兵师的残部在不明情况下被消灭。1941年8月5日，第1莫斯科机械化步兵师在第20集团军内重新组建，并于1941年8月18日改名为第1装甲师，在1941年9月21日再次更名为第1近卫莫斯科机械化步兵师。该师于1943年1月被再度改名为第1近卫步兵师。1941年8月30日，第1装甲师参与叶连尼亚攻势，迫使第28猎兵师后撤。由于遭受重大损失，该师在1941年9月10日停止推进，并撤至沃普河（Vop）以西地区。1941年9月18日，第1装甲师被调往莫扎伊斯克进行补充，并直接隶属于最高统帅部大本营。1941年9月30日，第1近卫莫斯科机械化步兵师被分配给第40集团军，并被派往苏缅地区。在初步推进后，该师于1941年10月6日开始撤退，因为苏联军队正在失去第一次哈尔科夫战役的胜利。1941年10月10日，在失去苏缅之后，该师被调至预备队并返回莫斯科。1941年10月21日，该师被分配给第3集团军，并抵达纳罗-福米诺斯克地区。在城市战中损失了70%的人员后，该师于1941年10月25日从纳罗-福米诺斯克撤退。<cr>1941年10月28日再次尝试夺回纳罗-福米诺斯克失败。该师一直驻扎在纳罗-福米诺斯克地区直到1941年11月底。<cr>1942年1月29日，该师与第415步兵师合作解放了梅特列沃村，在莫斯科前方的冬季反攻中获得“明斯克”荣誉称号。在1942年，第1近卫莫斯科机械化步兵师参加了热季战役。<cr>1943年7月，该师作为第1近卫步兵师参加库图佐夫行动；10月-布良斯克攻势；12月-哈拉多克攻势。<cr>1944年1月至7月，该师在维捷布斯克-明斯克方向推进，并于1944年7月13日获得“明斯克”荣誉称号。<cr>1944年11月，该师入侵东普鲁士的古谢夫地区；最终于1945年4月攻占柯尼斯堡。1945年4月21日至26日，作为第3白俄罗斯方面军中的第11近卫集团军的一部分，该师以强攻方式结束战争，夺取巴尔蒂斯克。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: The 1st Guards Romanian Infantry Division was formed in 1940 and was intended to be an elite division in the Romanian Army. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was attached to the Romanian V Army Corps at the southern end of the front. It participated in the 73 day Siege of Odessa. At the end of 1941 it was transferred from the front to Romania where it remained until the Soviets threatened Romania in 1944. It was decimated in the defensive battles that followed and disbanded. In the Spring of 1945 it was again mobilized under Soviet control and sent to Czechoslavkia.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第1近卫罗马尼亚步兵师成立于1940年，旨在成为罗马尼亚军队中的精锐部队。在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师被编入罗马尼亚第五军，在战线的南部端点。它参加了持续73天的敖德萨围城战。到1941年底，该师从前线调往罗马尼亚，并一直留在那里直到1944年苏联威胁到罗马尼亚。在随后的防御战斗中，该师几乎被消灭并解散。1945年初，在苏军控制下再次动员起来，并被派往捷克斯洛伐克。<cr>参考资料：Chris Munson 提供

text: On 8 December 1942, the 26th Tank Corps became the 1st Guards Tank Corps for its actions at Stalingrad. The 216th Tank Brigade became the 15th Guards, the 19th became the 16th Guards, the 157th became the 17th Guards and the 14th Motor Rifle Brigade became the 1st Guards.<cr>On 27 January 1943, the corps was awarded the honorific 'Don' for its actions. Alexey Rodin was promoted to Lieutenant general and became commander of the 2nd Tank Army in early February. 6th Army Tank Troops commander Major General Alexander Kukushkin took command. During February and March, the corps fought in the Third Battle of Kharkov. It defended positions north of Pavlohrad and fled to escape an encirclement on 24 February. On 25 April, Kukushkin was killed during an enemy air raid. 2nd Guards Army Tank Troops commander Major General Mikhail Panov took command. During the summer it fought in Operation Kutuzov. From October 1943, it fought in Belarus during the Gomel-Rechitsa Offensive. The corps captured Rechytsa in November and cut off the German line of retreat west of Gomel. For its actions, the corps was awarded the Order of the Red Banner on 18 November.<cr>The corps fought in the Kalinkovichi-Mozyr Offensive in January 1944. The corps captured Kalinkavichy on 14 January after outflanking defending German troops. On 15 January, the corps was awarded the Order of Suvorov 2nd class for its actions. From June, the corps fought in Operation Bagration. On 24 June, the corps advanced through the gap made by the advance of the 65th Army. By 27 June, the corps linked up with elements of the 9th Tank Corps, completing the encirclement of five German 9th Army divisions in the Bobruysk Offensive. The corps continued to advanced towards Pukhavichy and Osipovichi. On 3 July, the corps was on the southeastern outskirts of Minsk and helped complete the encirclement of the German 4th Army around Minsk. After the capture of Minsk, the corps advanced toward Baranovichi and Brest. The corps helped capture Slonim.<cr>From mid-November 1944, the corps was part of the 2nd Belorussian Front. From January 1945, the corps fought in the East Prussian Offensive. During the offensive, the corps helped capture Plonsk and Tuchola. On 19 February, the corps was awarded the Order of Lenin for its capture of Plonsk. At the end of March, the corps fought in the capture of Gda?sk during the East Pomeranian Offensive. From April, the division fought in the Berlin Offensive. It reached the Baltic coast near Rostock and Ribnitz at the end of the war.<cr><cr>
translation: 1942年12月8日，由于在斯大林格勒的行动，第26坦克军被改编为第1近卫坦克军。第216坦克旅成为第15近卫坦克旅，第19坦克旅成为第16近卫坦克旅，第157坦克旅成为第17近卫坦克旅，第14摩托化步兵旅则成为第1近卫摩托化步兵旅。<cr>1943年1月27日，该军因其行动而获得“顿河”荣誉称号。亚历山大·罗季翁被晋升为中将，并于2月初担任第2坦克集团军指挥官。6集团军坦克部队指挥官少校将军亚历山大·库库什金接任指挥。<cr>2月和3月，该军参加了第三次哈尔科夫战役。它保卫了帕夫洛格勒以北的阵地，并于2月24日撤退以避免被包围。<cr>4月25日，库库什金在敌机空袭中阵亡。第2近卫集团军坦克部队指挥官少校将军米哈伊尔·帕诺夫接任指挥。<cr>夏季期间，该军参加了库图佐夫行动。从1943年10月开始，它在白俄罗斯的戈梅利-列奇察攻势中作战。该军于11月占领了列奇察，并切断了德国向戈梅利西线撤退的道路。<cr>由于其行动，该军被授予红旗勋章，日期为11月18日。该军参加了1944年1月的卡林科维奇-莫吉廖夫进攻。1月14日，该军绕过防守的德国军队后占领了卡林科维奇，并于次日因行动出色被授予苏沃罗夫勋章二级奖章。从6月开始，该军参加了巴格拉季昂行动。6月24日，该军通过第65集团军突破的缺口前进。到6月27日，该军与第9坦克军的部分部队会合，完成了鲍里斯哥夫进攻中对五个德国第9集团军师的包围圈。随后，该军继续向普卡霍维奇和奥西波维奇推进。7月3日，该军抵达明斯克东南郊外，并帮助完成对围困在明斯克周围的德军第4集团军的包围圈。占领明斯克后，该军向巴拉诺维奇和布列斯特方向前进并协助占领了斯洛尼姆。<cr>从1944年11月中旬开始，该军成为第2白俄罗斯方面军的一部分。<cr>从1945年1月起，该军参加了东普鲁士进攻。在此次攻势中，该军协助占领了普隆斯克和图霍拉。<cr>2月19日，因攻占普隆斯克的贡献，该军被授予列宁勋章。<cr>3月底，该军参与了东波美拉尼亚进攻期间对格但斯克的攻克。从4月开始，该师参加了柏林攻势。在战争结束时，它抵达了罗斯特克和里宾茨附近的波罗的海沿岸。

text: The first commander of the Hungarian First Army was Lieutenant-General (or Altbornagy according to the Hungarian army rank) Vilmos Nagy. After 30 August 1940, under Nagy, the Hungarian First Army took part in Hungary's annexation and occupation of northern Transylvania. This region of Romania was awarded to Hungary as a condition of the Second Vienna Award.<cr>From 1940 to mid-1944, the Hungarian First Army saw little action other than occupation duties.<cr>By 30 April 1944, the Hungarian First Army was used to bolster Army Group South Ukraine. This army group was pushed back during the Second Battle of Trgu Frumos in May 1944. The Hungarians were placed in defensive positions north of the 4th Romanian Army and south of Army Group North Ukraine.<cr>From 13 July to 29 July 1944, the Hungarian First Army fought against the Soviet Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive. At this time the Hungarians were attached to the German 1st Panzer Army commanded by Colonel-General (Generaloberst)Gotthard Heinrici, which, in turn, was part of Army Group North Ukraine.<cr>Later in 1944, Soviet troops entered Romania, Bulgaria, and Hungary. The Romanians capitulated. The Bulgarians capitulated. The Hungarians tried to capitulate twice, but unsuccessfully. In the end, the Hungarian First Army continued its precarious existence.<cr>On 28 December, a newly formed Hungarian government, under acting Prime Minister Bla Mikls, officially declared war against Nazi Germany. But the Germans and the pro-German Hungarians in Hungary fought on against the Soviets. However, there are indications that some elements of the Hungarian First Army went over to the Soviets at about this time. Bla Mikls had been the commander of the Hungarian First Army from 1 August 1944 to 16 October 1944.<cr>Between 1 January and 16 February 1945, most of what remained of the Hungarian First Army was overrun, bypassed, or destroyed about 200 kilometers north of Budapest when the 40th Soviet Army advanced through the area. But, even after this, the Hungarian First Army did not cease to exist. The remnants fought on as an attachment to Heinrici's German First Panzer Army. Fighting as they went, they moved progressively westward into Slovakia. The army was not officially disbanded until 8 May 1945, the end of the war.<cr><cr><cr>Photo courtesy Slobodsky family archive.
translation: 匈牙利第一集团军的第一任指挥官是中将（根据匈牙利军队的军衔称为Altbornagy）维尔莫斯·纳吉。从1940年8月30日起，在纳吉的领导下，匈牙利第一集团军参与了匈牙利吞并和占领北特兰西瓦尼亚地区的行动。这一罗马尼亚地区是根据第二次维也纳仲裁案授予匈牙利的。<cr>从1940年至1944年中期，除了驻守任务外，匈牙利第一集团军几乎没有参与其他军事行动。<cr>到1944年4月30日，匈牙利第一集团军被用来加强南方乌克兰集团军群。该集团军在5月份的第二次特鲁日弗鲁莫斯战役中被迫后撤。匈牙利部队被部署在第4罗马尼亚集团军以北和北方乌克兰集团军群以南。<cr>从1944年7月13日至29日，匈牙利第一集团军参加了苏联的利沃夫-桑多梅日攻势。此时，匈牙利部队隶属于由大将（Generaloberst）戈特哈德·海尼里希指挥的德国第1装甲集团军，该集团军又是北方乌克兰集团军群的一部分。<cr>到了1944年晚些时候，苏联军队进入了罗马尼亚、保加利亚和匈牙利。罗马尼亚投降了。保加利亚也投降了。匈牙利试图两次投降但未成功。最终，匈牙利第一集团军继续其岌岌可危的存在状态。<cr>12月28日，在代理总理贝拉·米克洛什领导下的新政府正式对纳粹德国宣战。然而，德军和亲德的匈牙利军队仍在对抗苏联人。不过，有迹象表明，大约在这个时候，匈牙利第一集团军的一些部队转向了苏联一方。贝拉·米克洛什从1944年8月1日至10月16日担任匈牙利第一集团军指挥官。<cr>1945年1月1日至2月16日期间，匈牙利第一集团军的残部在布达佩斯以北约200公里处被苏军第40集团军击溃、绕过或消灭。但即便如此，匈牙利第一集团军并未停止存在。剩余部队作为附庸加入海因里希指挥的德国第一装甲集团军，并且边打边向西撤退至斯洛伐克境内。该集团军直至1945年5月8日战争结束时才正式解散。<cr>照片来源：Slobodsky家族档案馆

text: The 1st Hungarian Cavalry Brigade was formed in 1938. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was assigned to the Hungarian Mobile Corps or Gyorshadtest which in turn was part of the Carpathian Group. The Carpathian Group invaded Ukrainian Galicia on June 29th, 1941. Shortly thereafter the Carpathian Group was disbanded and the Hungarian VIII Corps was assigned occupation duties while the 1st Hungarian Cavalry Brigade, still part of the the Hungarian Mobile Corps, continued the drive deep into the Soviet Union. The brigade along with the rest of the Corps were recalled to Hungary in October of 1941. Shortly after arriving home the 1st and 2nd Hungarian Cavalry Brigades were merged into the 1st Hungarian Cavalry Division. In September 1944 the division was renamed the 1st Hussar Division.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr>Charles D. Pettibone, The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II Volume VII - Germany's and Imperial Japan's Allies & Puppet States<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第1匈牙利骑兵旅成立于1938年。在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，它被分配给匈牙利摩托化军或Gyorshadtest，后者又属于喀尔巴阡集团。喀尔巴阡集团于1941年6月29日入侵乌克兰加利西亚。不久之后，喀尔巴阡集团解散，第8匈牙利军负责占领任务，而第1匈牙利骑兵旅仍属匈牙利摩托化军，继续深入苏联境内推进。该旅及其所属的军于1941年10月被召回匈牙利。回国不久后，第1和第2匈牙利骑兵旅合并为第1匈牙利骑兵师。1944年9月，该师更名为第1骠骑师。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas 和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《二战中的皇家匈牙利陆军》<cr>Charles D. Pettibone，《二战中军事组织和战斗序列 第七卷 - 德国及其盟友与傀儡国家》<cr>词条由 Chris Munson 提供

text: The 1st Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 1st Light Division. In January of 1943 the division was transferred to Russia for security duties with the Hungarian Occupation Group. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 1st Light Division was merged with other units and disbanded.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第1匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖两个步兵团（每个团有3个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多东线兵力，大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本保持不变。该旅更名为第1轻型师。1943年1月，该师被调往俄罗斯执行治安任务，隶属于匈牙利占领集团。在斯大林格勒战役后对匈牙利陆军进行的一次总体重组中，第1轻型师与其他部队合并并解散。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas 和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利军队》<cr><cr>词条由 Chris Munson 提供

text: The 1st Hungarian Motorized Brigade was formed in 1938. The brigade participated in the German Invasion of Yugoslavia in early 1941. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was assigned to the Hungarian Mobile Corps or Gyorshadtest which in turn was part of the Carpathian Group. The Carpathian Group invaded Ukrainian Galicia on June 29th, 1941. Shortly thereafter the Carpathian Group was disbanded and its Hungarian VIII Corps was assigned occupation duties while the 1st Motorized Brigade, still part of the the Hungarian Mobile Corps, continued the drive deep into the Soviet Union. The brigade along with the rest of the Corps were recalled to Hungary in October of 1941. By this time the brigade had lost most of its armor. In early 1942 the brigade was reorganized and became the 1st Armored Division.<cr>The Hungarian Government reluctantly agreed to support the Germans 1942 summer offensive Fall Blau and allocated the division as part of the Hungarian Second Army to the task. Second Army's role in the offensive was to guard the German northern flank on the Don River. During the Stalingrad Campaign the Second Army suffered over 60% casualties but was generally able to retreat in good order with the 1st Armored Division being the last unit in the Hungarian Second Army to withdraw from the fighting in February 1943.<cr>In September 1944 the division was part of the Third Hungarian Army defending Hungary's southern border. The division was one of the defenders of the Hungarian capital when In November 1944 the Russians commenced their 102 day Siege of Budapest. The division was disbanded in February 1945 when the city surrendered.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

In early 1942 the brigade was reorganized and became the 1st Armored Division.<cr>The Hungarian Government reluctantly agreed to support the Germans 1942 summer offensive Fall Blau and allocated the division as part of the Hungarian Second Army to the task. Second Army's role in the offensive was to guard the German northern flank on the Don River. During the Stalingrad Campaign the Second Army suffered over 60% casualties but was generally able to retreat in good order with the 1st Armored Division being the last unit in the Hungarian Second Army to withdraw from the fighting in February 1943.<cr>In September 1944 the division was part of the Third Hungarian Army defending Hungary's southern border. The division was one of the defenders of the Hungarian capital when In November 1944 the Russians commenced their 102 day Siege of Budapest. The division was disbanded in February 1945 when the city surrendered.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text: The 1st Hungarian Mountain Brigade was formed in September of 1939. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was assigned to the Hungarian VIII Corps which in turn was part of the Carpathian Group. The Carpathian Group invaded Ukrainian Galicia on June 29th, 1941. Shortly thereafter the Carpathian Group was disbanded and the Hungarian VIII Corps was assigned occupation duties however the 1st Hungarian Mountain Brigade was back in Hungary by the end of 1941. It did not participate further in the fighting until Russian armies approached the Carpathian Mountains and Hungary proper in 1944. The brigade surrendered to Soviet forces in Styria, Austria in May of 1945.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr>Charles D. Pettibone, The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II Volume VII - Germany's and Imperial Japan's Allies & Puppet States<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第1匈牙利山地旅成立于1939年9月。在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，它被分配给匈牙利第8军，该军又属于喀尔巴阡集团。喀尔巴阡集团于1941年6月29日入侵乌克兰加利西亚。不久之后，喀尔巴阡集团解散，匈牙利第8军被分配了占领任务，但第1匈牙利山地旅在1941年底之前回到了匈牙利。直到1944年苏联军队接近喀尔巴阡山脉和匈牙利本土时，该旅才再次参与战斗。该旅于1945年5月向奥地利施蒂利亚的苏军投降。<cr>参考文献：<cr>Nigel Thomas 博士与 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利陆军》<cr>Charles D. Pettibone，《第二次世界大战中军事力量的组织和战斗序列 第七卷 - 德国及其盟友和傀儡国家》<cr><cr><cr>词条由 Chris Munson 提供<cr>

text: In June 1941, the 1st Infantry Division crossed into Russia with Army Group North and was heavily engaged in the Baltic States during the drive on Leningrad. By October 1941, its strength had been reduced by two-thirds; nevertheless, it continued to fight on the northern sector of the Russian Front, primarily as a part of the 18th Army, for more than two years. During this time, it took part in the Battle of Lake Peipus, the Battles of Lake Ladoga, and the Battle of the German Corridor (east of Leningrad), as well as the siege of Leningrad itself. In October 1943, the 1st Infantry was attached to Army Group South and fought in the Battle of Krivoi Rog in the Dniepr campaign in southern Russia. Later it saw action in the Ukraine and was encircled with the 1st Panzer Army between the Bug and the Dnestr rivers in March 1944. In the subsequent breakout it formed the rear guard of the XXXXVI Panzer Corps and suffered heavy casualties. Later, after a period of rest and rebuilding, it was sent to the central sector in August 1944. The survivors of the 1st Infantry remained with Army Group Center and ended the war fighting the Soviets in the division's home territory of East Prussia, including the battles of Schlossberg, Knigsberg, Samland, and Pillau.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 1941年6月，第1步兵师随北方集团军群进入俄罗斯，并在进攻列宁格勒的过程中，在波罗的海国家进行了激烈战斗。到1941年10月，其兵力已减少三分之二；然而，它继续在俄罗斯前线北部地区作战，主要隶属于第18集团军，持续了两年多时间。在此期间，它参与了佩普斯湖战役、拉多加湖系列战役以及德国走廊（列宁格勒以东）战役，并参加了对列宁格勒的围攻。1943年10月，第1步兵师被调至南方集团军群，在德涅斯特河畔克里沃伊罗格战役中作战。之后它在乌克兰地区参战，并于1944年3月与第1装甲集团军一起被困在布格河和德涅斯特河之间。在随后的突围行动中，它成为第46装甲军后卫部队并遭受了重大损失。稍后，在休整重建一段时间后，它被派往中央战区作战，直到1944年8月。第1步兵师的幸存者继续留在中央集团军群，并在东普鲁士（该师的故乡）与苏联军队作战，包括施洛斯贝格、柯尼斯堡、萨姆兰和皮劳等战役。<cr>德国二战战斗序列卷一：第1至290步兵师，山缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: The 1st Mechanized Corps was initially formed in March 1940 it was attached to the Leningrad Military District, and held in reserve near the Pskov Fortified Region. It was under the command of Major General Mikhail Chernyavski when the German Operation Barbarossa began in June 1941. It initially comprised the 1st and 3rd Tank Divisions, and the 168th Mechanized Division. On 22 June 1941, 1st Mechanized Corps consisted 31,439 Men, 1037 Tanks, 239 Armored Cars, 148 Artillery Pieces, 146 Mortars, 4730 Vehicles, 246 Tractors & 467 Motorcycles including lighter models T-26, BT-7, & T-28's.<cr>After the invasion began the Leningrad Military District was renamed Northern Front, Commanded by Lieutenant General Markian Popov. The front fielded 14th Army, 7th Army, 23rd Army, the 65th Rifle Corps & the Leningrad Military District forces including the 2nd Division of NKVD troops. The 1st Mechanized Corps was heavily engaged in the first battles of Operation Barbarossa, particularly during the Baltic Operation (1941). On 29 June 1941 the 1st Mechanized Corps was ordered to reinforce new defenses anchored on the Velikaya River near Ostrov on the former Stalin Line after the spectacular advances by Georg-Hans Reinhardt's XLI Panzer Corps which had crossed the Daugava River. However it was unable to hold the line. On 11 July 1941 Col P Poluboiarov, Northwestern Front armoured directorate reported that the 1st Mechanized Corps had at the present moment fewer than 100 Tanks remaining. Pskov and Ostrov were captured within weeks & Leningrad invested. On 2 August 1941 Colonel Limarenko, Chief of Staff of the 1st Mechanized Corps reported that the Corps 'possessed no T-34 or Kv-1s when sent into action 20 were delivered only after combat began. The 1st Mechanized Corps was disbanded in August 1941, although 1st Tank Division remained in 14th Army.<cr><cr>
translation: 第1机械化军最初于1940年3月组建，随后被编入列宁格勒军区，并在普斯科夫要塞地区附近作为预备力量部署。当德国的巴巴罗萨行动于1941年6月开始时，该军由少将米哈伊尔·切雷亚夫斯基指挥。最初，它包括第1坦克师、第3坦克师和第168机械化师。1941年6月22日，第1机械化军共有31,439人、1037辆坦克（包括T-26、BT-7快速坦克及T-28）、239辆装甲车、148门火炮、146具迫击炮、4730辆车辆、246台拖拉机和467辆摩托车。<cr>入侵开始后，列宁格勒军区改名为北方方面军，由少将马基安·波波夫指挥。该方面军建制包括第14集团军、第7集团军、第23集团军、第65步兵军以及列宁格勒军区部队，其中包括内务人民委员部第2师。在巴巴罗萨行动的初期战斗中，特别是巴尔蒂克行动（1941）期间，第1机械化军投入了大量兵力。1941年6月29日，在乔治-汉斯·莱因哈特的第41装甲军突破道加瓦河后，该军接到命令增援在奥斯特罗夫附近的维捷茨卡亚河上的新防线。然而它未能守住这条防线。1941年7月11日，西北方面军装甲总监波卢鲍亚罗夫上校报告称，第1机械化军目前剩余坦克不足100辆。普斯科夫和奥斯特罗夫在几周内被占领，列宁格勒被包围。1941年8月2日，第1机械化军参谋长林马连科上校报告说，该军在投入战斗时没有T-34或KV-1坦克，只有20辆是在战斗开始后才送达的。第1机械化军于1941年8月被解散，尽管第1坦克师仍留在第14集团军内。<cr>第1机械化军在巴巴罗萨行动初期遭受了重大损失，并最终被解散。<cr>第1机械化军虽然被解散，但其部分力量重组为第1坦克师。

text:
The 1st Mechanized Division was formed from the 1st Rifle Division in May 1940 in Moscow Military District.<cr>
The 1st was one of the earliest Mechanized Divisions formed, and even though it was assigned to 7th Mechanized Corps, it retained some of the personality of the 1st 'Moscow Proletariat' Rifle Division, which had been a Parade or showpiece unit permanently stationed in Moscow.<cr>
By 22 June 1941 the 1st Mechanized was actually stationed just outside of Moscow in Vyazma, with 12,000 men (actually overstrength in authorized personnel), 100% of authorized artillery and heavy weapons, and 225 BT-7M tanks in the tank regiment - the newest and most modern 'light tanks' available in quantity.<cr>
Before the rest of 7th Mechanized Corps, 1st Mechanized Division was alerted to move to the front on the morning of 22 June. On the way forward through Orsha (west of Smolensk) the division added 10 KVs and 30 T-34s from Tank Training units in Western Military District. When the division went into battle for the first time 26 - 30 June, it also had under command a battalion of students from the Borisov Tank-Technical School. Because of these additions, the Germans mistakenly thought that this division had been authorized a special complement of heavy and medium tanks not found in other mechanized divisions. To add to the confusion, German intelligence variously identified the unit as the 'Moscow' division, the 'Stalin Guards' division, or the 'Moscow Guards' division.<cr>
For a time in August 1941, both the Germans and the Red Army (unofficially)identified it as the 1st Tank Division - chiefly because it still had a functioning tank regiment after almost all the other tank and mechanized divisions in Western Front had been destroyed.<cr>7th Mechanized Corps staff was used to form a new headquarters for 16th Army near Smolensk in early July, so 1st Mechanized Division became an independant 'fire brigade' unit for Western Front, fighting frequently under either 16th or 20th Army command east of Smolensk throughout July and August, 1941. Its division commander, Col A. I. Lizyukov, was one of the first wartime recipients of the Hero of the Soviet Union medal - the Soviet equivalent of the Medal of Honor or Victoria Cross.<cr>
By 15 September, 1st Mechanized Division was in Western Front reserveswith 45 tanks total and 600 riflemen left in each motorized rifle regiment. In recognition of the division's combat record - in persistant survivability, if not strategic success - on 21 September 1941 1st Mechanized Division became the 1st Guards Motorized Division.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第1机械化军于1940年5月在莫斯科军区从第1步兵师改编而成。<cr>
第1机械化军是最早组建的机械化部队之一，尽管它被分配到第7机械化军中，但仍保留了部分“莫斯科无产者”步兵师的传统特色，后者一直是驻扎在莫斯科的一支阅兵或展示单位。<cr>
截至1941年6月22日，第1机械化军实际上驻扎在莫斯科外围的维亚兹马，拥有超过编制人数的1.2万人、全部授权火炮和重武器以及坦克团中的225辆BT-7M轻型坦克——这是当时可大量获得的最新最现代化的轻型坦克。<cr>
在6月22日早晨接到前往前线命令时，第1机械化军比第7机械化军其他部队提前行动。行进途中经过斯摩棱斯克以西的奥尔沙时，该部从西部军区的坦克训练单位中增加了10辆KV和30辆T-34坦克，并且还指挥着来自鲍里斯夫坦克技术学校的1个学生营。由于这些增援，德国人错误地认为这支部队被授权拥有其他机械化部队所没有的重型和中型坦克编制。为了增加混乱，德军情报部门将该部误称为“莫斯科”师、“斯大林近卫”师或“莫斯科近卫”师。<cr>
1941年8月期间，德国人和红军（非官方）都将它视为第1坦克师——主要是因为几乎所有的其他坦克和机械化部队在西方面军中被消灭后，该部仍然拥有一个运作中的坦克团。<cr>1941年7月初，第7机械化军的司令部被用来在斯摩棱斯克附近为第16集团军建立一个新的总部。因此，第1机械化师成为独立的“救火队”单位，在西方面军作战，并经常在第16或第20集团军指挥下于斯摩棱斯克以东地区进行战斗，直到同年7月和8月。<cr>第1机械化师的师长A. I. 利兹尤科夫上校是第一次世界大战期间获得苏联英雄勋章的第一批人员之一——这是苏联版的荣誉勋章或维多利亚十字勋章。<cr>截至9月15日，第1机械化师在西方面军预备队中拥有总计45辆坦克和每个摩托化步兵团剩下600名步兵。<cr>鉴于该师的战斗记录——尽管战略上没有成功，但在持续生存能力方面表现出色，1941年9月21日，第1机械化师被改编为第1近卫摩托化师。<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: The 1st Moscow Rifle Division was formed from a single regiment in September 1939 and reformed as the 1st Moscow Motor Rifle Division in January 1940. Its honorific title was 1st Moscow Proletariat Red Banner Rifle Division. Training was complete by June 1940 and the division took part in the Soviet occupation of the Baltic States. After several months on occupation duty the division returned to Russia. At the start of Operation Barbarossa the division was assigned to the 20th Army in the Moscow Military District. The division was rapidly replenished to its full complement of 10,831 men. On June 30, 1941 at Borisov the division was the first Russian unit to use T-34 tanks against the Germans invaders.<cr>In July 1941 the division was encircled near Mogilev. Some elements escaped only to be encircled near Smolensk the following month and destroyed. The division was reformed almost immediately in August 1941 as the 1st Tank Division and in September 1941 was renamed the 1st Guards Moscow Motor Rifle Division. The division was severely mauled in October 1941 in street fighting at Naro-Fominsk.<cr>The division fought in the Battle of Rzhev in 1942. The division was again renamed in January 1943 becoming the 1st Guards Rifle Division. The division fought in many other engagements throughout 1944 and crossed into East Prussia in November 1944. In April 1945 it participated in the storming of Knigsberg and then Baltiysk.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第1莫斯科步兵师于1939年9月由一个团组建，并于1940年1月重组为第1莫斯科机械化步兵师。其荣誉称号是“第1莫斯科无产阶级红旗步兵师”。训练在1940年6月完成，该师参加了苏联占领波罗的海国家的行动。几个月的驻防任务后，该师返回俄罗斯。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师被分配给莫斯科军区内的第20集团军。<cr>1941年6月30日，在博里索夫，该师成为第一个使用T-34坦克对抗德国入侵者的苏联部队。<cr><cr>1941年7月，该师在莫吉廖夫附近被包围。一些单位逃脱后于当月在斯摩棱斯克再次被围并被消灭。<cr><cr>该师几乎立即在1941年8月重组为第1坦克师，并于同年9月改名为“第1近卫莫斯科机械化步兵师”。1941年10月，该师在纳罗-费奥多罗夫斯克的巷战中遭受重创。<cr><cr>该师参加了1942年的列日战役。1943年1月，该师再次改名为“第1近卫步兵师”。该师于1944年参与了多次战斗，并在同年11月进入东普鲁士。<cr><cr>1945年4月，该师参加了对柯尼斯堡和巴尔提斯克的进攻。<cr><cr>本文由克里斯·芒森提供

text: In June 1941, the 1st Mountain Division crossed into Russia as part of Army Group South, and on July 15-16 broke through the Stalin Line. During this battle, the division lost 31 men killed and 74 wounded, but killed several hundred Russians and captured 281 more. It also captured 100 machine guns, eight guns, a tank and three airplanes. Two days later, it was fighting on the Bug, where it held a twenty-seven mile front with only two infantry regiments. As the Soviet forces tried to escape from Vinniza, the division was able to take 10,000 prisoners, but was unable to block the escape of 30,000 more.<cr><cr>Later, the 1st Mountain took part in the Battle of the Uman Pocket (where it suffered 759 casualties), and by the end of the month, the divisions strength had dropped from 17,801 men to 13,636. It had also lost about 500 of its 6,487 horses. The division nevertheless launched a major assault across the Dnieper River at Berislav, where it built a bridge 431 meters long. It took part in the capture of Kiev and the subsequent liquidation of the Kiev Pocket, then pushed south to help capture Stalino (now Donetsk, Ukraine) in September, and took part in the encirclement of Mogila Tokmak (also known as the Chernigovka Pocket and the Battle of the Sea of Azov) from October 5 to 10. During this battle, the Red Army lost 100,000 men captured and 212 tanks and 672 guns captured or destroyed. From September 6 to October 10, 1941, however, the 1st Mountain Division had lost 573 men killed and 1,975 wounded. Even more seriously, 75 percent of its vehicles had broken down or were in need of major overhauls. The division nevertheless took part in the drive on and retreat from Rostov and helped defend the Mius River Line against Stalin's winter offensive of 1941-42.<cr><cr>By May 1942, it was with the III Panzer Corps and fought in the Battle of Kharkov and in the eastern Donetz. Later, it was at the spearhead ofGeneral von Kleist's Caucasus campaign, but was checked in the high mountains. After the disaster of Stalingrad, Kleists Army Group A was forced to retreat into the Kuban, and the 1st Mountain Division was involved in the first of a long series of withdrawals and rear-guard actions on the road back to Germany. In April 1943, the division was withdrawn from the front and sent to Serbia and northern Greece, where it was rebuilt and engaged in anti-partisan operations. Later it was reported on the Greco-Albanian frontier, and subsequently in western Serbia, Bosnia, Croatia and Montenegro. The division was still fighting south of Belgrade in October 1944. Following the loss of this city, it fought in Hungary (November 1944March 1945) and in the Austrian Alps. It was redesignated 1st Volks Mountain Division on March 12, 1945, but with no change to its table of organization. The 1st Mountain Division ended the war as part of Army Group South, fighting the Russians in central Styria. It ended up in Soviet captivity in May 1945.German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII
translation: 1941年6月，第1山地师作为南方集团军群的一部分进入俄罗斯，并于7月15日至16日突破了斯大林防线。在这场战斗中，该师阵亡31人，受伤74人，但杀死了数百名苏联士兵并俘虏了281人。它还缴获了100挺机枪、8门火炮、一辆坦克和三架飞机。两天后，该师在布格河作战，在仅有两个步兵旅的情况下守住了长达二十七英里的战线。当苏军试图从文尼察逃走时，第1山地师俘虏了10,000人，但未能阻止另外30,000人的逃脱。<cr>随后，该师参与了乌曼包围圈战役（在此期间损失了759名士兵），到月底其兵力从17,801人下降到了13,636人。它还失去了大约500匹马中的6487匹。<cr>尽管如此，该师还是在别里斯拉夫发动了一次大规模突击，横跨第聂伯河，并建造了长达431米的桥梁。它参与了基辅的占领以及随后对基辅包围圈的肃清行动，然后向南推进帮助占领斯大林诺（现为乌克兰顿涅茨克），并在9月参加了莫吉拉-托卡马克（也称为切尔尼戈夫卡包围圈和亚速海战役）从10月5日至10日。在这场战斗中，红军失去了10万名被俘士兵、212辆坦克和672门火炮的缴获或摧毁。<cr>然而，从1941年9月6日至10月10日，第1山地师损失了573名阵亡士兵和1,975名受伤士兵。更严重的是，其车辆中有75%已经损坏或需要重大维修。<cr>尽管如此，该师还是参与了对罗斯托夫的进攻以及从罗斯托夫撤退，并帮助防御米乌斯河防线以抵御斯大林1941-42年的冬季攻势。到1942年5月，该师隶属于第III装甲军，在哈尔科夫战役和东顿巴斯地区作战。后来，它成为克莱斯特将军高加索攻势的先锋部队，但在高山地带遭到阻止。在斯大林格勒灾难之后，克莱斯特的A集团军群被迫撤退到库班地区，第1山地师参与了从苏联领土返回德国的一系列撤退和后卫行动中的第一次。1943年4月，该师从前线撤出，并被派往塞尔维亚和希腊北部，在那里重建并参加了反游击作战。之后它出现在希腊-阿尔巴尼亚边境地区，随后在西塞尔维亚、波斯尼亚、克罗地亚和黑山活动。直到1944年10月，该师仍在贝尔格莱德以南作战。失去这座城市后，它在匈牙利（1944年11月至1945年3月）以及奥地利阿尔卑斯山区作战。1945年3月12日，该师被重新命名为第1人民山地师，但编制未变。到战争结束时，第1山地师作为南方集团军群的一部分，在施蒂利亚中部与苏联红军作战。它在1945年5月落入苏军战俘营中。《二战德国战斗序列 第二卷：291至999步兵师、命名步兵师及特殊部队》

text: The 1st Panzer Division crossed into the Soviet Union when Operation Barbarossa began on June 22, 1941, with a strength of approximately 155 tanks. It formed part of Army Group Norths 4th Panzer Group (later Army) and took part in the annihilation of the Soviet III Armored Corps at Dubysa in June. The 1st Panzer was seriously depleted by casualties, and by August 16 had only forty-four serviceable tanks; nevertheless it took part in the drive on Moscow (it came to within twenty miles of the Soviet capital) and opposed the Russian winter offensive, where it was surrounded and forced to break out. By February 18, the 1st Panzer Regiment had only eighteen operational tanks; most of the regiment was used to form two ad hoc ski companies. The division nevertheless fought in the critical Rzhev salient and helped save the 9th Army, which was nearly surrounded.<cr><cr>In early July, the 1st and 2nd Panzer Divisions surrounded and destroyed or captured 218 Soviet tanks, 592 guns, and 1,300 anti-tank guns near Pushkeri. In a two day period in August, the division destroyed sixty-five superheavy KV-1 and KV-2 tanks and wiped out a Soviet penetration. Greatly reduced by losses, the 1st Panzer was withdrawn for resting and refitting in January 1943. Initially it was sent to Amiens, France, but spent that summer in Greece. Here it was brought up to full strength; by autumn it had a full battalion of PzKw V (Tiger) tanks and about 100 PzKw VI (Panther) tanks. When Italy defected to the Western Allies in September 1943, the 1st Panzer Division played a major role in subduing the Italian 11th Army, which put up little resistance. In October 1943, it returned to the Russian Front, fighting on the southern sector, took part in the Battle of the Kiev Salient and the counteroffensive west of Kiev (NovemberDecember 1943).<cr><cr>It also spearheaded the attempt to rescue the XI and XXXXII Corps, which were surrounded at Cherkassy in February 1944. It could not penetrate the last six miles to the pocket but was still successful in saving half the trapped Germans. The next month the 1st Panzer rescued the 96th and 291st Infantry Divisions from the Soviet spring offensive of 1944. Casualties were again heavy and, as of March 14, 1944, the divisions panzer grenadier battalions were at 25 percent of their authorized strengths, and the 1st Panzer Regiment had fewer than sixty operational tanks. The division nevertheless remained in the line and fought in the battles of the Dnieper Bend, the north Ukraine, and eastern Poland in 1944. Retreating behind the Vistula, it was transferred to Hungary and was cited for its counterattack against the Russians at Debrecen. Most of the division was trapped and destroyed at Szekesfehervar, Hungary, in December 1944, when the 6th Army collapsed; despite its losses, however, the remnants of the 1st Panzer Division continued fighting on the southern sector of the Eastern Front until the end of the war. The division then extricated itself from the Red Army and surrendered to the Americans at Mauerkirchen in Upper Bavaria on May 8, 1945. The Americans dissolved the division five days later. Most of its soldiers were released and sent home by the end of July.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第1装甲师于1941年6月22日巴巴罗萨行动开始时进入苏联境内，当时拥有约155辆坦克。它隶属于北方集团军群的第4装甲集群（后来成为集团军），参与了在6月份摧毁苏军第三装甲集团军的杜比萨战役。第1装甲师因伤亡严重而实力大减，到8月16日只剩下44辆可服役坦克；然而，该师仍参加了进攻莫斯科（距离苏联首都仅20英里）的行动，并对抗了俄罗斯冬季攻势，在此过程中被包围并被迫突围。至2月18日，第1装甲团仅有18辆可以使用的坦克；该团大部分兵力用于组建两个临时滑雪营。尽管如此，该师仍参加了关键的热季突出部作战，并帮助挽救了几乎被包围的第9集团军。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>7月初，第1和第2装甲师在普斯克雷附近包围并摧毁或俘获了218辆苏联坦克、592门火炮以及1300门反坦克炮。8月期间，在两天内该师摧毁了65辆重型KV-1和KV-2坦克，并消灭了一支苏军突入部队。由于损失惨重，第1装甲师于1943年1月被撤出休整并补充兵员。最初它被派往法国阿米埃，但那个夏天却驻扎在希腊，在那里恢复了满编状态；到秋天时拥有一个完整的虎式坦克营和大约100辆豹式坦克。当意大利于1943年9月倒向西方盟国时，第1装甲师在镇压几乎没有抵抗的意军第11集团军中发挥了重要作用。<cr><cr>1943年10月，该师重返苏联战场，在南部战区作战，并参加了基辅突出部战役以及基辅以西的反攻（1943年11月至12月）。<cr> <cr>它还主导了营救被围困在切尔卡瑟的第十一军和第四十二军的行动，时间是1944年2月。尽管未能突破最后六英里到达包围圈，但仍然成功拯救了一半被困的德军。下个月，第1装甲师从苏联1944年的春季攻势中救出了第96步兵师和第291步兵师。伤亡再次严重，截至1944年3月14日，该师的装甲掷弹兵团仅达到其授权编制的25%，而第1装甲团拥有的坦克不足六十辆。尽管如此，该师仍然坚守在前线，并参加了1944年的第聂伯河弯道战役、北乌克兰战役和东波兰战役。撤退到维斯瓦河后，它被转移到匈牙利，并因在德布勒森对俄反击战中的表现而受到表彰。大部分部队在1944年12月的锡盖特塞盖什堡战役中被困并被消灭，当时第六集团军崩溃；尽管损失惨重，但第1装甲师残部仍在东线南部继续战斗直到战争结束。该师随后从红军手中脱身，并于1945年5月8日在上巴伐利亚的马厄尔基兴向美军投降。五天后，美军解散了该师；大部分士兵在7月底获释并返回家园。<cr><cr>德国战斗序列卷三 - 二战中的装甲、装甲掷弹兵和武装党卫军师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text: 1st Panzer Group (Panzergruppe 1), which was attached to Field Marshal Gerd von Rundstedt's Army Group South at the beginning of Operation Barbarossa. At the start of Operation Barbarossa in June 1941, Panzer Group 1 included the III, XIV and XLVIII Army Corps (mot) with five panzer divisions and four motorized divisions (two of them SS) equipped with 799 tanks. Panzer Group 1 served on the southern sector of the Eastern Front against the Red Army and was involved the Battle of Brody which involved as many as 1,000 Red Army tanks. On October 6, 1941, Panzer Group 1 was enlarged to the 1st Panzer Army.<cr><cr>
translation: 第1装甲群（装甲群1），在巴巴罗萨行动初期隶属于格尔德·冯·伦斯德特元帅的南方集团军群。1941年6月巴巴罗萨行动开始时，第1装甲群包括第III、XIV和XLVIII摩托化军，辖5个装甲师和4个摩托化师（其中2个是党卫军），装备有799辆坦克。第1装甲群在东线南部地区对抗红军，并参与了布罗迪战役，该战役中多达1000辆红军坦克参战。1941年10月6日，第1装甲群扩编为第1装甲集团军。<cr><cr>

text: Part of the 10th Army in the Western Front, it consisted of the 2nd and 8th Rifle Divisions. It was encircled in the Minsk Pocket and was destroyed in June 1941. The corps was reformed in to the North Caucasus Front in August 1942 and its subsequent history is unclear. <cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 隶属于西方方面军的第10集团军，由第2步兵师和第8步兵师组成。它在明斯克包围圈中被合围，并于1941年6月被消灭。该军于1942年8月重组为北高加索方面军，其后续历史不详。<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 1st Romanian Armored Division was formed in April of 1941. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was assigned to the Romanian Cavalry Corps. As with most Romanian units it was withdrawn to Romania after the Siege of Odessa. In late 1942 the division was deployed to Southern Russia with Army Group B The first armored regiment had been reequipped with imported German tanks, primarily the PzKw 35t, PzKw III and PzKw IV. The 2nd Armored Regiment, equipped with obsolete Renault R-35 tanks, was left behind in Romania in the role of training unit. After its losses in the Battle of Stalingrad the division was out of action for more than a year as it waited for replacement equipment from Germany and did not see action again until February of 1944.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Picture: 'Armata Romana in al doilea razboi mondial', Meridiane, 1995<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第1罗马尼亚装甲师成立于1941年4月。在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师被分配给罗马尼亚骑兵军。与其他大多数罗马尼亚部队一样，在敖德萨围城战后撤回了罗马尼亚境内。1942年底，该师被部署到南方集团军群B的南俄地区。第1装甲团已经重新装备了进口的德国坦克，主要是PzKw 35t、PzKw III和PzKw IV型。第2装甲团则配备了老旧的雷诺R-35坦克，并留在罗马尼亚作为训练单位。<cr>指挥官报告：在斯大林格勒战役中的损失后，该师因等待德国提供的替换装备而停战超过一年，直到1944年2月才再次参战。<cr>插图：《罗马尼亚军队在第二次世界大战中》，Meridiane出版社，1995年<cr>词条由Chris Munson提供<cr>

text: The 1st Romanian Cavalry Brigade was attached to the Romanian VI Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. In March of 1942 it was reorganized as the 1st Romanian Cavalry Division. As the 1st Cavalry Division it participated in the Stalingrad Campaign where much of the division was encircled and destroyed. By April of 1943 the surivors, with only 189 horses and one tank remaining, had returned to Romania. It was envisioned the division would be transformed into an armored cavalry or motorized cavalry division but due to a lack of tanks and vehicles this was only partially complete prior to Romania's signing an armistice with Russia in 1944.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第1罗马尼亚骑兵旅在巴巴罗萨行动开始时隶属于罗马尼亚第六军。1942年3月，该部队重组为第1罗马尼亚骑兵师。作为第1骑兵师，它参加了斯大林格勒战役，在此期间大部分兵力被包围并消灭。到1943年4月，幸存者仅剩下189匹马和一辆坦克，并返回了罗马尼亚。原计划将该师改造成装甲骑兵或摩托化骑兵师，但由于缺乏坦克和其他车辆，直到1944年罗马尼亚与苏联签署停战协定之前，这一改造只部分完成。<cr>Chris Munson 提供

text: The 1st Romanian Infantry Division did not participate in the opening phase of Operation Barbarossa and remained in Romania. It was activated in September of 1941 and assigned to the V Romanian Army Corps. At the end of 1941 it was assigned to the German 1st Panzer Army to assist in repeling Soviet winter counterattacks. In 1942 it particpated in the German summer campaign Fall Blau. The division was down to a few hundred survivors after the Battle of Stalingrad and returned to Romania. When the Soviets threatened Romania in 1944 it was again activated and participated in many defensives battles until it was merged with other units in late 1944.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第1罗马尼亚步兵师没有参加巴巴罗萨行动的初期阶段，留在了罗马尼亚。该师于1941年9月被激活，并编入第5罗马尼亚军。到1941年底，它被分配给德国第1装甲集团军，协助抵御苏联的冬季反攻。在1942年的德军夏季攻势“蓝色行动”中，该师参与了作战。经过斯大林格勒战役后，该师仅剩下几百名幸存者，并返回罗马尼亚。当苏联军队于1944年威胁到罗马尼亚时，该师再次被激活并参加了许多防御性战斗，直到同年年底与其他部队合并。<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>词条由克里斯·芒森提供

text: The 1st Shock Army was formed as part of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (RVGK, the Stavka reserve) at Zagorsk (now Sergiyev Posad) in the Moscow Military District in November 1941. Taking part in the Battle of Moscow in December 1941, on 1 December the Army consisted of the 133rd Rifle Division, 29th, 44th, 47th, 50th, 55th, 56th, 71st, and 84th Rifle Brigades, 17th Cavalry Division, two tank battalions, an artillery regiment of the Stavka reserve, and other support units.[2] All the rifle brigades were formed from the naval personnel of the Pacific Fleet.<cr>1st Shock Army was then airlifted to Staraya Russa and fought at Demyansk in 1942. Fighting in the north-central areas of the front, the 1st Shock Army again fought near Staraya Russa in 1944. From 1942 through 1944, the army took part in many attacks such as the Leningrad-Novgorod, Pskov-Ostrov, Tartu, and Riga offensives. Fighting through the Baltic States, the 1st Shock Army finished the war as part of the Courland Group of Forces that had trapped the German Army Group Kurland in the northern reaches of Latvia.<cr><cr>
translation: 第1突击集团军于1941年11月在莫斯科军区的扎戈尔斯克（现为谢尔吉耶夫波萨德）作为最高统帅部大本营预备队（RVGK，即大本营预备队）的一部分组建。该集团军参加了1941年12月的莫斯科战役，在12月1日由第133步兵师、第29、44、47、50、55、56、71和84步兵旅、第17骑兵师、两个坦克营、一个大本营预备队炮兵团和其他支援单位组成。[2]所有步兵旅都是由太平洋舰队的海军人员组建而成。<cr>随后，该突击集团军被空运至斯塔罗亚罗斯拉瓦并参加了1942年的德米扬斯克战役。在前线北部中央地区作战时，第1突击集团军于1944年再次在斯塔罗亚罗斯拉瓦附近作战。从1942年至1944年间，该集团军参与了多次进攻行动，如列宁格勒-诺夫哥罗德、普斯科夫-奥斯特罗夫、塔尔图和里加攻势等。穿越波罗的海国家后，第1突击集团军在战争结束时成为库尔兰兵力群的一部分，该兵力群将德国陆军库尔兰集团军困于拉脱维亚北部地区。<cr><cr>

text: The 1st Slovak Infantry Division was part of the Slovakian Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. It was disbanded in August of 1941 and elements were used to form the Mobile Division (aka Fast Division). The Mobile Division was in turn disbanded in August of 1943 and a new 1st Slovak Infantry Division formed from its elements. After being mauled at Melitopolin the Southern Ukraine the division was disbanded in the summer of 1944 and its personnel assigned to construction units.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第1斯洛伐克步兵师在巴巴罗萨行动开始时隶属于斯洛伐克军。该师于1941年8月解散，其部分兵力用于组建快速师（又称摩托化师）。快速师又于1943年8月解散，新的第1斯洛伐克步兵师由其残部重组而成。在南乌克兰梅利托波尔受重创后，该师于1944年夏季再次被解散，其人员被分配到工兵部队。<cr>感谢克里斯·芒森提供资料

text: The 1st SS Panzer Division crossed into southern Russia with Army Group South in July 1941. It advanced along the Black Sea coast in August, took part in the opening phases of the Crimean campaign, and was devastated in the Battle of Rostov during the Soviet winter offensive of 194142. After seeing some action in the summer of 1942, the Leibstandarte was pulled out of the line and sent to northern France in August.<cr>Returned to the Eastern Front in the spring of 1943, the division took part in the Kursk offensive and suffered heavy casualties in the Battle of Kharkov (1943) before being transferred to northern Italy.<cr>Returning to southern Russia in the autumn, the 1st SS was involved in heavy combat west of Kiev, at Tarnopol, and in the Dnieper battles. It unsuccessfully tried to prevent the encirclement of the 1st Panzer Army in 1944. The division was itself surrounded at Skala in the spring of that year and suffered ruinous losses in the ensuing breakout.<cr>THe division was sent to Belgium and fought in the west until after the Ardennes offensive. The division was subsequent withdrawn and sent to Hungary, where it fought in the unsuccessful Lake Balaton counterattack. Hitler, displeased with the failure of one of the Leibstandartes attacks, ordered it to remove the Adolf Hitler cuffband from the uniforms of its troops. The division responded by sending him a pile of their medalsin a latrine bucket. The survivors of the division retreated into Austria in 1945, and fought in the Battle of Vienna. It ended the war on the southern sector of the Eastern Front, although most of the men of the division managed to surrender to the Americans.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第1装甲师于1941年7月随南方集团军群进入俄罗斯南部。8月，该师沿着黑海海岸推进，并参加了克里米亚战役的初期阶段，在苏联冬季攻势（1941-42）中的罗斯托夫战役中遭受重创。<cr>在1942年夏季经历了一些战斗后，该师于8月被调离前线并送往法国北部。<cr>1943年春天重返东线战场时，该师参加了库尔斯克攻势，并在1943年的哈尔科夫战役中遭受了重大伤亡，随后被转移到意大利北部。<cr>秋天返回俄罗斯南部后，第1装甲师在基辅以西、塔尔诺波尔和第聂伯河战役中进行了激烈战斗。它试图阻止第一装甲集团军在1944年被包围的努力未果。<cr>该师自己也在当年春天的斯卡拉战役中被包围，并在随后的突围行动中遭受了毁灭性的损失。<cr>该师后来被派往比利时，在西线作战，直到阿登攻势之后。该师随后撤出并被送往匈牙利，在那里参加了失败的巴拉顿湖反击战。<cr>希特勒因不满莱布维茨攻击未果而命令其部队从制服上移除阿道夫·希特勒袖标。该师则通过将他们的勋章放在便桶中寄给希特勒来回应这一命令。<cr>1945年，该师的幸存者撤退到奥地利，并参加了维也纳战役。它在东线南部战区结束了战争，尽管大多数士兵最终向美国人投降了。<cr><cr>德国战斗序列第3卷——二战中的装甲、装甲掷弹兵和武装党卫军师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text: The 1st Tank Army was first formed within the Stalingrad Front from 38th Army in July 1942, under the command of Major General Kirill Moskalenko. The army was encircled and partially destroyed, and was disbanded as a result in August 1942, its headquarters becoming the Southeastern Front headquarters.<cr>The 1st Tank Army was formed a second time on 30 January 1943 (order No.46021) from the headquarters of the 29th Army, under the command of famous armoured troops commander Lieutenant General of Tank Troops Mikhail Katukov, personally appointed by Stalin. The army was transferred to the Northwestern Front. 3rd Mechanized Corps (later to become 8th Guards Mechanized Corps) and 6th Tank Corps (later to become 11th Guards Tank Corps) joined it on formation, and served with the army throughout the war. It was quickly transferred to Voronezh Front for the defense of the Kursk salient's southern shoulder. It was awarded a Guards title and became the 1st Guards Tank Army in April 1944, and Katukov was promoted to Colonel General.<cr><cr>
translation: 第1坦克集团军于1942年7月在斯大林格勒方面军内组建，由第38集团军改编而成，由少将基里尔·莫斯卡连科指挥。该集团军被包围并部分被消灭，结果于同年8月解散，其司令部成为东南方面军的司令部。<cr>第1坦克集团军第二次于1943年1月30日（命令编号46021）在第29集团军司令部基础上重建，由著名装甲部队指挥官坦克兵上将米哈伊尔·卡图科夫直接任命为总指挥。该集团军被调往西北方面军。<cr>组建时加入了第3机械化军（后来成为第8近卫机械化军）和第6坦克军（后来成为第11近卫坦克军），并在整个战争期间与集团军共同作战。它很快被转移到沃罗涅日方面军，为库尔斯克突出部南翼的防御做准备。该集团军于1944年4月获得近卫称号，并更名为第1近卫坦克集团军，卡图科夫晋升为大将。

text:
The 1st Tank Corps was formed in March 1942 in the Moscow Military District, started receiving units in April 1942 in the same District.<cr>The first Corps commander was Major General M. E. Katukov, the commander of 4th Tank Brigade when it became 1st Guards Tank Brigade in 1941, and later commander of 1st Guards Tank Army. The 1st Tank Corps went right to Bryansk Front in May, before receiving any unit training or any other supporting units. It was badly chewed up trying to attack the flank of German panzer forces south and east of Voronezh, and by late August was assigned to 5th Tank Army with only 89th Tank Brigade left in the corps.<cr>The 1st Tank Corps was part of the 'Mobile Group' of 5th Tank Army that seized Kalach-na-Don and surrounded the 6th German Army at Stalingrad, unfortunately, the actual seizure of Kalach was done by 26th Tank Corps, so that unit received the 'Guards' designation, not 1st Tank Corps. In January 1943 the 1st Tank Corps went into reserve, first in Volga Military District (east of Stalingrad) and then, in March, it shifted to Western Front reserves near Moscow. While in reserve the corps was stripped of its supporting elements, leaving just the brigades.<cr>In June 1943 the Soviet High Command began rebuilding the Corps for the anticipated campaigns of the late summer. When llth Guards Army went over on the attack north of Orel in July, 1st Tank Corps was assigned to it as part of the Army Mobile Group.<cr>The 1st Tank Corps fought under Bryansk Front through the summer of 1943. Since Bryansk Front had no major breakthroughs in which to commit the tank corps, in September it added two more support units.<cr> In January-March 1944 1st Tank Corps fought under llth Guards Army in 1st Baltic Front, sometimes with 2nd Guards Heavy Tank Regiment (KV-85 tanks) attached. In late March 1944 the corps went into STAVKA Reserves to prepare for the major operations planned for the summer. While in the reserves in April-May 1944, the corps was completely re-equipped with new tanks and the antitank and SU units in the corps were reorganized.<cr>The 1st Tank Corps formed the Mobile Group for 6th Guards Army in June-July 1944, and formed its own Corps Forward Detachment to lead the advance deep into the German rear.<cr>Even while the fighting was going on in the Baltic, 1st Tank Corps was
being reinforced. In August 1944 the corps received 354th Guards Heavy SU Regiment (21 ISU-122s) and in September 1944 the 120th Light Artillery Regiment (24 76mm guns) was added. These were the last additions to 1st Tank Corps, which ended the war in May 1945 in East Prussia with 3rd Belorussian Front.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第1坦克军于1942年3月在莫斯科军区组建，同年4月开始接收部队。<cr>第一任军长是少将M.E.卡图科夫，他在1941年担任第4坦克旅指挥官时该旅改编为第1近卫坦克旅，并于后来成为第1近卫坦克集团军的指挥官。第1坦克军在5月直接被派往布良斯克方面军，在没有接受任何单位训练或支援部队的情况下。它试图攻击德国装甲部队在沃罗涅日南面和东面的侧翼，但遭受了严重损失，并于8月下旬被分配到第5坦克集团军，此时该军只剩下第89坦克旅。<cr>第1坦克军是第5坦克集团军“机动编队”的一部分，后者夺取了顿河畔卡拉萨并包围了在斯大林格勒的德军第6集团军。不幸的是，实际占领顿河畔卡拉萨是由第26坦克军完成的，因此该部队获得了“近卫”称号，而不是第1坦克军。<cr>1943年1月，第1坦克军进入预备队，在伏尔加军区（斯大林格勒以东）和随后在3月转移到莫斯科附近的西方面军预备队。在预备期间，该军被剥夺了支援部队，只剩下旅级单位。<cr>1943年6月，苏联最高统帅部开始重建坦克军，为预期的夏季末期战役做准备。当第11近卫集团军于7月在奥廖尔北部发起进攻时，第1坦克军被分配给它作为集团军机动编队的一部分。<cr>第1坦克军在布良斯克方面军作战直到1943年夏天。由于布良斯克方面军没有重大突破来投入坦克军，在9月又增加了两个支援单位。 1944年1月至3月，第1坦克军在第11近卫集团军指挥下隶属于第1波罗的海方面军作战，有时会与第2近卫重型坦克团（KV-85坦克）协同。1944年3月底，该军进入最高统帅部预备队以准备夏季计划中的重大行动。在1944年4月至5月期间处于预备队时，该军完全换装了新坦克，并重新组织了反坦克和SU单位。<cr>第1坦克军于1944年6月至7月成为第6近卫集团军的机动部队，并组建了自己的军先遣队以深入德国后方推进。<cr>即使在波罗的海地区战斗仍在进行时，第1坦克军也在不断得到加强。1944年8月该军接收了第354近卫重型SU团（21辆ISU-122），同年9月又增加了第120炮兵团（24门76毫米火炮）。这些是第1坦克军在战争结束前的最后增援，它于1945年5月在第3白俄罗斯方面军中结束了在东普鲁士的最后一战。<cr>查尔斯·C·夏普著《二战苏联战斗序列 第二卷》

text: On October 20, 1943, the Voronezh Front was renamed to the 1st Ukrainian Front. This name change reflected the westward advance of the Red Army in its campaign against the German Wehrmacht, leaving Russia behind and moving into Ukraine.<cr>During 1944, the front participated with other fronts in the battles of Korsun-Shevchenkovsky, and the battle of Hube's Pocket in Ukraine. It conducted the Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive, during which the Front was controlling the Soviet 1st Guards Tank Army, 3rd Guards Tank Army, 4th Tank Army, 3rd Guards, 5th Guards Army, 13th, 38th, and 60th Armies. It then took part in the battle for Ternopil'.<cr>In 1945 the front participated in the Vistula-Oder Offensive, and conducted the Silesian and Prague Operations, and the siege of Breslau. It also participated in the Berlin operations in Germany and Poland. The front also conducted the major part of the Halbe Encirlement, in which most of the German 9th Army was destroyed south of Berlin. By this time the Polish 2nd Army was operating as part of the Front. Finally 1st Ukrainian Front provided the defence against the counter-attacks by Armee Wenck which aimed to relieve Berlin and the 9th Army. The Prague Offensive was the final battle of World War II in Europe.<cr><cr>
translation: 1943年10月20日，沃罗涅日方面军更名为第1乌克兰方面军。这一名称变更反映了红军在对抗德国国防军的战役中向西推进的情况，从俄罗斯境内推进到了乌克兰。<cr>1944年，该方面军与其他方面军一起参加了科尔松-舍甫琴科夫斯基战役和乌赫捷列包围圈战役。它还进行了利沃夫-桑多梅日进攻行动，在此期间，第1近卫坦克集团军、第3近卫坦克集团军、第4坦克集团军、第3近卫集团军、第5近卫集团军、第13集团军、第38集团军和第60集团军均受方面军指挥。随后该方面军参加了特伦恰夫战役。<cr>1945年，该方面军参与了维斯瓦河-奥得河进攻行动，并进行了西里西亚和布拉格作战以及布雷斯劳的围攻战。它还参与了德国和波兰境内的柏林作战。该方面军还在哈勒包围圈中发挥了主要作用，在此期间，德军第9集团军大部分被消灭在柏林以南地区。<cr>此时，波兰第2集团军也作为方面军的一部分进行行动。最后，第1乌克兰方面军提供了防御阵地，抵御了文克陆军的反攻，后者试图解救柏林和第9集团军。布拉格进攻是欧洲战场上的第二次世界大战的最后一战。<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>

text:
The 200th Soviet Rifle Division was established at Belokorovichi, Ukraine, in March, assigned to the Southwestern Front. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was at approximately 50% strength and was wiped out at Kiev, in September 1941. 

Recreated at Busulusk in February 1942 by renaming the 425th Rifle Division. Fought in Belorussia, at Gydnia, and at Berlin. With the 49th Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front in May 1945. 



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 

Courtesy John Tomlinson

text:
The 201st Rifle Division was formed as an Red Army national unit during August 1941 in Gorki, Moscow Military District from the remains of the 24th Territorial Rifle Corps, and assigned to the 33rd Army.<cr>
It was originally designated as the 201st Latvian Rifle Division, as the basis of the division was the 76th Independent Latvian Rifle Regiment. By December 1941 the division had 10,348 personnel, of whom 51% were ethnic Latvians, 26% ethnic Russians, 17% Jews and 6% others.<cr> 
The first combat the division experienced was during the counter-offensive at Moscow in the areas of Naro-Fominsk and Borovsk where it suffered 55% casualties. It also fought in the battle for Staraya Russa (from 16 February 1942 until 4 April), and for the Demyansk bridgehead. By June 1942 only 36% of the division were Latvian-speaking, and a year later this figure was reduced to 32%.<cr> 
The division was renamed as the 43rd Guards Rifle Division in October 1942 and was known as the Latvian Guards.<cr>
A new 201st Rifle Division was raised from the 27th Rifle Brigade at Shlisselburg, near Leningrad, in November 1943, assigned to the 23rd Army. It served in the Leningrad and Baltic coast areas. 



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa Vol IIIB

translation: 第201步兵师是在1941年8月于莫斯科军区的戈尔基市成立的一个红军全国性部队，由第24领土步兵军残部组建，并分配给第33集团军。<cr>最初它被命名为第201拉脱维亚步兵师，因为该师的基础是独立第76拉脱维亚步兵团。到1941年12月，该师共有10,348名人员，其中51%为拉脱维亚人，26%为俄罗斯人，17%为犹太人，其余6%为其他民族。<cr>该师首次经历的战斗是在莫斯科反攻期间，在纳罗-福明斯克和博罗夫斯基地区遭受了% c伤亡。它还参加了从1942年2月16日至4月4日的斯塔罗伊鲁萨战役，以及德米扬斯克桥头堡的战斗。到1942年6月，只有36%的师员会讲拉脱维亚语，一年后这一比例降至32%。<cr>该师于1942年10月被重新命名为第43近卫步兵师，并被称为拉脱维亚运兵师。<cr>一个新的第201步兵师在1943年11月从列宁格勒附近的什利谢利堡的第27步兵旅组建，分配给第23集团军。它服务于列宁格勒和波罗的海沿岸地区。<cr><cr>尼格尔·阿斯基，《巴巴罗萨行动》第三卷<cr>条目由56ajax提供

text:
The 202nd Mechanized Division was formed in February - March 1941 near Riga in Baltic Special Military District as part of 12th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
645th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
682nd Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
125th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - all T-26 tanks
652nd Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
281st Reconnaissance Battalion - included 1 company of T-26 tanks
151st Antiaircraft Battalion
189th Antitank Battalion
371st Sapper Battalion<cr>
The 202nd Mechanized Division had almost all of its assigned artillery and heavy weapons on 22 June 1941, but only about 200 light T-26 tanks, and less than a third of the trucks and tractors required to move its men and equipment. The biggest problem for the division, however, was that it had only 50% of its authorized radios, the divisional signal battalion was short 2/3 of its assigned technicians, and when the Germans attacked the division's elements were scattered over 60 km apart! When 12th Mechanized Corps went into battle, the division simply could not organize itself fast enough to join the tank divisions. As a result, the 125th Tank Regiment was taken from the division and added to 28th Tank Division on 26 June, to try to make up for tank losses in that unit.<cr>
In late July 202nd Mech, which was now effectively only a 'semi motorized' rifle division, was assigned directly to llth Army. In late August, by adding 1317th (Reserve) Rifle Regiment to the division, it was officially converted into 202nd Rifle Division.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第202机械化军于1941年2月至3月在里加附近波罗的海特别军事区组建，隶属于第12机械化军，编成如下：
645摩托化步兵团
第1、2、3步兵团
682摩托化步兵团
第1、2、3步兵团
125坦克团
第1、2、3、4坦克营——全部为T-26坦克
652摩托化榴弹炮团
第1、2、3营
281侦察营——包括一个装备T-26坦克的连
151防空营
189反坦克营
371工兵营

截至1941年6月22日，第202机械化军几乎拥有其分配的所有火炮和重型武器，但只有约200辆轻型T-26坦克，并且缺少三分之一的卡车和拖拉机以移动人员和装备。该军最大的问题是无线电设备仅为其授权数量的一半，信号营技术人员短缺三分之二，当德军发动攻击时，其各部之间相距达60公里！在第12机械化军投入战斗时，该军无法迅速组织起来加入装甲师。结果，在6月26日，从该军抽调了125坦克团并将其编入第28装甲师，以弥补该单位的坦克损失。

7月下旬，此时实际上仅剩半摩托化步兵师的第202机械化军被直接分配给第11集团军。到8月底，在加入第1317（预备）步兵团后，它正式改编为第202步兵师。
——查尔斯·C·夏普《苏联战斗序列 第一卷》

text:
The 202nd Rifle Division was formed in August 1941 from the scattered remnants of the 202nd Mechanised Division and with the inclusion of the newly raised 1317th Rifle Regiment. By September 1941 it was attached to the 11th Army, Northwestern Front.

The Division fought Sol'tsa, Kiev, and Korsun and ended the war assigned to the 27th Army of the 3rd Ukrainian Front.



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第202步兵师成立于1941年8月，由第202机械化师的残部重组而成，并加入了新组建的第1317步兵团。到1941年9月，该师隶属于西北方面军下的第11集团军。

该师参加了索尔察、基辅和科尔松战役，并在战争结束时被分配给第三乌克兰方面军下的第27集团军。

尼格尔·阿斯基，《巴巴罗萨行动》，卷III-A

text: In June 1942 the 203rd Security Brigade became the 203rd Security Division. In October 1942 it consisted of the 608th and 613th Security Regiments and several smaller Ost units . In October 1944 the 203rd Security Division became the 203rd Infantry Division. It consisted of the 608th, 613th and 930th Grenadier Regiments, the 203rd Artillery Regiment and various support units. The division was largely destroyed on the Narev River in southern German in March 1945. The survivors served on the Vistula River with the 2nd Army.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text:
The 203rd Rifle Division, an infantry division of the Soviet Union's Red Army, started forming in the Kuban near Labinsk, from February 1942. In August 1942 the division moved to the front and built defensive positions on the Don northwest of Vyoshenskaya 

The Division's first offensive operation, whilst initially successful, ended in disaster as the enemy counterattacked and the Division retreated in disarray. The Divisional and Regimental commanders were relieved of their command.

The Division fought at Stalingrad, the Donbass, Odessa and Budapest, amongst others.

Awarded the Order of the Red Banner and the Order of Suvorov, 2nd Class.


Entry courtesy 56ajax
translation:
第203步兵师是苏联红军的一个步兵师，于1942年2月在库班靠近拉宾斯克开始组建。1942年8月，该师前往前线，在顿河西北部的维约申斯卡亚附近建立了防御工事。

该师首次进攻行动虽然初期取得成功，但最终因敌军反攻而告终，并且部队陷入混乱中撤退。师长和团级指挥官被解除职务。

该师参加了斯大林格勒、顿巴斯、敖德萨和布达佩斯等战役。

获得红旗勋章和苏沃洛夫勋章二级奖章。

text:
The 204th Mechanized Division was formed March 1941 from 9th Armored Car Brigade at Volkovysk in Western Special Military District as part of llth Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
700th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
706th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
Tank Regiment - 1st Tank Bn only
657th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
2 bns - each 4 76mm cannon, 8 122mm howitzers
1 battery of 4 152mm howitzers
Reconnaissance Battalion
Antitank Battalion
Antiaircraft Battalion
Sapper Battalion<cr>
The 204th Mechanized Division had only 1 battalion of 44 light BT-5 tanks, but was full strength in armored cars left over from 9th Armored Car Brigade. Unfortunately, the division had almost no tractors and less than 15% of its authorized trucks, so the rifle regiments were largely on foot and the howitzer regiment, which was understrength, couldn't even move the pieces it had. Just to complete the dismal story of the unit, on the first day of the war, while trying to move to the front, the 204th was caught by the Luftwaffe and lost over 50% of its remaining equipment. The rest of the division was overrun and destroyed in the Bialystok pocket and was removed from the Soviet order of battle in early July.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text:
The 204th Rifle Division of the Soviet Union should have been formed from the 204th Mechanised Division, except that this division was lost in the Bialystok pocket and deleted from the Soviet Order of Battle by early July 1941.

The Division was then formed at Blagoveshchensk, Far East, Nov 1941 and assigned to the 2nd Red Banner Army.

In July 1942 the Division was transferred to the 64th Army and fought at Stalingrad. The Division was renamed the 77th Guards Rifle Divisions in March, 1943. 

The Division was then recreated from 37th Rifle Brigade at Nelidovo Jul 1943. Fought at Kursk, in Belorussian Offensive and in Courland. With the 51st Army of the Kurland Group (Leningrad Front) May 1945. 

 

Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 
Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

Courtesy John Tomlinson

该师随后于1941年11月在远东的布拉戈维申斯克组建，并被分配给第2红旗集团军。

1942年7月，该师转隶至第64集团军，在斯大林格勒作战。1943年3月，该师更名为第77近卫步兵师。

随后于1943年7月在内利多沃从第37步兵旅重建该师。参加了库尔斯克战役、白俄罗斯攻势和库尔兰防御战。1945年5月隶属于库尔兰集团军群（列宁格勒方面军）的第51集团军。

The 205th Soviet Rifle Division started forming in the Far East from October 1941. In July 1942 it was assigned to the 64th Army at Stalingrad where it was overrun and destroyed by October 1942.

text: The 206th Infantry Division was involved in the Russian campaign from the beginning. It fought at Duenaberg, Velikije-Luka and Kalinin, and, along with the 26th Infantry Division, took Rzhev on the Volga River between Moscow and Leningrad in October 1941; however, the division was shattered by Russian counterattacks near Moscow from December 22, 1941 to January 4, 1942. Later that month it was briefly surrounded, along with the XXIII Corps, south of Lake Volga.<cr>In the spring of 1942, the 312th Infantry Regiment was disbanded, along with three infantry battalions, and the 206th Tank Destroyer and 206th Reconnaissance Battalions were combined to form a single schnelle battalion. The division remained with Army Group Center for the rest of its existence, taking part in the defensive battles around Rzhev (1942-43), the Rzhev withdrawal in March 1943, and the Battle of Smolensk (August 1943), among others. The 312th Grenadier Regiment was reconstituted in April 1944 (from elements of the 52nd Security Division), but the other grenadier regiments were reduced to two battalions each. As part of LIII Corps, 3rd Panzer Army, the division was crushed by the massive Soviet summer offensive of 1944. Encircled at Vitebsk and ordered to stay there by Adolf Hitler himself, the divisional commander, Lieutenant General Alfons Hitter, ordered a breakout on his own responsibility. Only a few of the division's 12,000 men managed to escape, however; the division was overwhelmed and destroyed on June 28. General Hitter was among those taken prisoner. On July 18, 1944, the demobilization office officially declared the historic East Prussian 301st, 312th, and 413th Grenadier Regiments disbanded and the 206th Infantry Division dead.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第206步兵师从一开始就参与了俄罗斯战役。它在杜纳堡、维利亚基-卢卡和加里宁作战，并与第26步兵师一起，在1941年10月，占领了位于莫斯科和列宁格勒之间的伏尔加河畔的热季夫；然而，该师从1941年12月22日至1942年1月4日，在莫斯科附近被苏联反攻击溃。当月晚些时候，它与第XXIII军一起在伏尔加湖以南地区短暂被包围。<cr>1942年春天，第312步兵团和三个步兵营被解散，第206坦克歼灭营和第206侦察营合并成一个快速营。该师余生都隶属于中央集团军群，并参与了热季夫周围防御战（1942-43年）、1943年3月的热季夫撤退以及1943年8月的斯摩棱斯克战役等战斗。<cr>第312掷弹兵团在1944年4月重建（从第52治安师中抽调），但其他掷弹兵团则被削减为两个营。作为第LIII军，第3装甲集团军的一部分，该师在1944年的苏联夏季攻势中遭到重创。<cr>在维捷布斯克被包围并接到阿道夫·希特勒亲自下达的留在原地命令后，师长阿尔丰斯·希特勒将军下令自行突围。然而只有少数人员成功逃脱；该师于6月28日被彻底击溃和消灭。阿尔丰斯·希特勒将军也被俘虏。<cr>1944年7月18日，动员办公室正式宣布解散历史悠久的东普鲁士第301、312和413掷弹兵团，并宣告第206步兵师覆灭。德国战斗序列 第一卷：第1至第290步兵师在二战，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少将

text:
The 206th Rifle Division was an infantry division of the Red Army, which began forming in March 1941, as a reserve division for what was to become the Southern Front.

 When the German invasion began it was only at 40% strength, still organizing well away from the front, near Krivoi Rog. The Division was sent North to the Kiev Fortified Sector where it was completely destroyed in the Kiev pocket in September, 1941. 

A small group led by the commander, Colonel Gorshkov, managed to escape, along with another led by the divisional chief of staff, Lt. Col. P. I. Kulizhski. It was not officially stricken from the Soviet order of battle until 27th December 1941.

 The 206th was reformed in early 1942 and went on to have a distinguished military history. It fought at Battle of Kursk, Korsun where it suffered heavy casualties, Uman, Budapest and Vienna amongst others. It lost 2 commanders due to military action and was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov, Kutuzov and Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky. 

Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA

text:
The 207th Rifle Division was partly formed for the first time as a standard Red Army rifle division in the spring of 1941 but was disbanded by June 1941.

The second 207th Rifle Division began forming in April, 1942, in the North Caucasus Military District, based on a cadre from the 52nd Rifle Brigade. In August it was thrown into a series of desperate and costly counter attacks against the north flank of the German 'corridor' at Stalingrad. It suffered very heavy casualties and was disbanded.

The third 207th Rifle Division was formed on June 6, 1943, in the 5th Army in Western Front, based on a cadre from the 40th Rifle Brigade and the 2nd formation of the 153rd Rifle Brigade. It was involved in the battles for Smolensk, Riga and Berlin, amongst others.

The 207th Rifle Division ended the war with the official title of 207th Rifle, Pomerania, Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov, Division. 



Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第207步兵师首次部分组建于1941年春季，作为标准的红军步兵师，但该师在同年6月被解散。

第二个第207步兵师开始于1942年4月，在北高加索军区组建，基于第52步兵旅的核心人员。8月份，该师被迫参与了一系列针对斯大林格勒北部德军“走廊”的绝望且代价高昂的反击战，遭受了非常严重的伤亡并被解散。

第三个第207步兵师于1943年6月6日在西方方面军第5集团军组建，基于第40步兵旅和第153步兵师第二次组建的核心人员。该师参与了斯摩棱斯克、里加和柏林等战役。

战争结束时，第207步兵师获得了“波美拉尼亚”、“红旗勋章”和“苏沃洛夫勋章”的正式称号。

text:
The 208th Mechanized Division was formed March 1941 near Gainovka in Western Special Military District as part of 13th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
435th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
760th Motorized Rifle Regiment

Antiaircraft Battalion
Antitank Battalion
Sapper Battalion<cr>
The 208th Mechanized Division had a full strength howitzer regiment, -antiaircraft and antitank battalions - at least in weapons. Unfortunately, it had no tanks at all, and was missing most of its other motorized transport. As a result, ithin a few days after the war started, the division was stripped out of 13th Mechanized Corps and fought directly under 10th Army as a regular rifle division. The division was destroyed in the Minsk pocket, but a core of the unit, hiding in the forests east of Minsk, formed 208th Partisan Regiment. The 578th Howitzer Regiment was detached from the rest of the division when the pocket closed, and elements of it fought with 5th Mechanized Corps near Orsha in late June and early July, before the regiment was dissolved and its elements used to reinforce other artillery units.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text:
The 208th Rifle Division was a Soviet infantry division in the Red Army during World War II. It began Operation Barbarossa as the 208th Mechanized Division under Colonel V.I. Nichiporovich and was part of the 13th Mechanized Corps, 10th Army, Western Front.

The division was trapped and destroyed in the Minsk pocket.

 Unusually, Colonel Nichiporovich managed to keep a large group of men together after the destruction of his division during the border battles, and kept on the fight as 'Detachment No.208,' one of the first units of the Soviet partisans in Belorussia. 

The Division is listed as being assigned to the 25th Army, Far East, as of November 1941.

In 1942 the Division, under Col. K. M. Vysokoboinikov, was part of the 64th Army which fought in the Battle of Stalingrad.
On 6 April 1945, now under the title 'Siberian,' it was part of the divisions of the encirclement of Knigsberg, located at the northwest sector as part of 124th Rifle Corps, 43rd Army. 


Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIA 
Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第208步兵师是苏联红军在第二次世界大战期间的一个步兵师。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师为第208机械化军，在尼奇皮罗维奇上校的指挥下，隶属于第13机械化军、第10集团军、西方面军。

该师被围困并在明斯克包围圈中被消灭。

不同寻常的是，尼奇皮罗维奇上校在边境战斗中成功地将大量人员组织起来，并以“第208分队”的名义继续作战，成为白俄罗斯最早的一支苏联游击队之一。

该师于1941年11月被分配给远东地区的第25集团军。

1942年，在维索科博伊尼科夫上校的指挥下，该师隶属于参加斯大林格勒战役的第64集团军。

1945年4月6日，改名为“西伯利亚”的该师作为包围柯尼斯堡行动的一部分，隶属于第124步兵军、第43集团军西北方向的部队。

text:
The 209th Mechanized Division was formed March 1941 in Western Special Military District as part of 17th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
Motorized Rifle Regiment
Motorized Rifle Regiment
Howitzer Regiment
Antitank Battalion
Antiaircraft Battalion
Sapper Battalion<cr>
The 209th Mechanized Division had a full-strength howitzer regiment and most of the heavy weapons for the rifle regiments, but not a single tank or armored car, and very few vehicles of any kind. In addition, like the entire the division was desparately short of NCOs and experienced officers, and had had no time to train the men that were on hand before the war started. The division was officially disbanded 19 September 1941.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第209机械化军于1941年3月在西方特别军事区组建，隶属于第17机械化军，编制如下：<cr>
摩托化步兵团
摩托化步兵团
榴弹炮团
反坦克营
防空营
工兵营<cr>
第209机械化军拥有完整的榴弹炮团和大部分步兵团所需的重武器，但没有一辆坦克或装甲车，并且几乎没有其他类型的车辆。此外，整个部队极度缺乏士官和有经验的军官，在战争开始前也没有时间对在编人员进行训练。该部于1941年9月19日正式解散。<cr><cr>
查尔斯·夏普《苏联战斗序列 第一卷》

text: The 20th Army was first formed in the Orel Military District in June 1941. On 22 June 1941 the Army was part of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command and was located west of Moscow.<cr>On 27 June 1941 it was proposed to Joseph Stalin that the Soviet armies (13th, 19th, 20th, 21st, and 22nd Armies) would defend the line going through the Daugava-Polotsk-Vitebsk-Orsha-Mogilev-Mazyr as part of the Reserve Front.<cr>Committed as part of Western Front in defensive battles in Belarus, Battle of Smolensk, and Vyazma. By 5 August 1941 the army had been seriously reduced. The strength of the 289th Rifle Division had fallen to 285 men, 17 machine guns, and one anti-tank gun, the 73rd Rifle Division to 100 men and 4 to 5 machine guns, 144th Rifle Division to 440 men, and 153rd Rifle Division to 750 men. The Army HQ was disbanded having been encircled and destroyed in the Vyazma Pocket.<cr>Reestablished in November 1941 from Operational Group Liziukov. Reformed November 1941 for the Battle of Moscow, comprising 331st and 350th Rifle Divisions, and three separate brigades. Fought as part of the Western Front. In 1942-43 it operated on the Rzhev-Vyazma bridgehead, and took part in the Rzhev-Vyazma offensive operation. In 1944 it became part of the Stavka Reserve and was then reassigned to Kalinin Front and Leningrad Front. It was disbanded in April 1944 by being dispersed within the formations of 3rd Baltic Front.<cr><cr>
translation: 第20集团军成立于1941年6月的奥廖尔军区。1941年6月22日，该集团军作为最高统帅部预备队的一部分，位于莫斯科以西。<cr>1941年6月27日，建议约瑟夫·斯大林将苏联的第13、19、20、21和22集团军部署为预备方面军，在达乌加瓦-波洛茨克-维捷布斯克-奥尔沙-莫吉廖夫-马兹尔一线进行防御。<cr>作为西方方面军的一部分，参加了白俄罗斯的防御战役、斯摩棱斯克战役以及维亚兹玛战役。到1941年8月5日，该集团军的实力已经严重削弱。第289步兵师的人数减少到了285人，拥有17挺机枪和一门反坦克炮；第73步兵师人数减少至100人，拥有4到5挺机枪；第144步兵师人数为440人；第153步兵师人数为750人。集团军司令部在维亚兹玛包围圈中被合围并摧毁。<cr>1941年11月，从利齐科夫作战群重建了该集团军，并于同年11月为了莫斯科战役重新组建，包括第331和第350步兵师以及三个独立旅。作为西方方面军的一部分参战。<cr>1942-43年，它在热季夫-维亚兹玛桥头堡作战，并参与了热季夫-维亚兹玛进攻战役。<cr>1944年，该集团军成为最高统帅部预备队的一部分，随后被重新分配到加里宁方面军和列宁格勒方面军。它于1944年4月解散，并分散在第3个巴尔蒂克方面军的编制中。<cr><cr>

text: The 20th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 20th Light Division. The Hungarian Government reluctantly agreed to support the Germans 1942 summer offensive Fall Blau and allocated the Hungarian Second Army to the task. Each light division in the Second Army was reinforced with three battalions from sister divisions in Hungary but nonetheless each division was only slightly larger than half the size of its German counterparts. Second Army's role in the offensive was to guard the German northern flank on the Don River. During the Stalingrad Campaign the Second Army suffered over 60% casualties but was generally able to retreat in good order. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 20th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 20th Infantry Division. In September 1944 the division was part of the Third Hungarian Army defending Hungary's southern border.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第20匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖两个步兵团（每个团有三个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有七个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多兵力以参加东线作战，并且大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本没有变化。该旅更名为第20轻型师。匈牙利政府勉强同意支持德军在1942年夏季的攻势——蓝色行动，并将匈牙利第二集团军投入任务中。第二集团军中的每个轻型师都从匈牙利国内的兄弟部队得到三个营的增援，但即便如此，每个师仍然只有其德国同行的一半左右规模。第二集团军在进攻中的角色是保卫德军北线顿河沿岸的安全。在斯大林格勒战役期间，第二集团军伤亡超过60%，但仍能有组织地撤退。作为战后对匈牙利军队进行重组的一部分，第20轻型师与其他部队合并，并更名为第20步兵师。1944年9月，该师成为第三匈牙利集团军的一员，在保卫匈牙利南部边境的战斗中。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr>% c<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>
