text: The 23rd SS Panzergrenadier Division began its career as the SS Volunteer Legion 'Niederlande'. It was formed in Krakow (Krakau), Poland, from Dutch volunteers who joined the SS to fight communism. Initially it consisted of the 1st and 2nd SS Volunteer Panzer Grenadier Regiments 'Nederland', as well as a two battalion artillery regiment, tank destroyer, engineer and field replacement battalions, a reconnaissance company and a signal company. It distinguished itself in its first action (on the northern sector of the Eastern Front) where, in June 1942, it attacked and destroyed a much larger Soviet force, taking 3,500 prisoners in the process, including General Andrey Vlasov, the future commander of the Russian Liberation Army (ROA). The Legion was then shifted north, where it took part in the Siege of Leningrad and in the Second Battle of Lake Lagoda.<cr>The Legion was sent back to the Netherlands in early 1943 to rest, recruit and expand. It was upgraded to the 4th SS Volunteer Panzer Grenadier Brigade on October 23, 1943, and its panzer grenadier regiments became the 48th SS Volunteer Panzer Grenadier Regiment 'General Seyffardt' and the 49th SS Volunteer Panzer Grenadier Regiment 'De Ruiter', respectively. The Dutch Legion/Brigade served in the Balkans until December 1943, when it was sent to the Leningrad sector. It joined the III Panzer Corps and fought in the Siege of Oranienbaum, in the retreat from Leningrad, in the fierce battles on the Narva, and in the first battles of the Courland Pocket. The 48th SS Volunteer Panzer Grenadier Regiment and most of the divisions artillery regiment were destroyed in Operation Bagration (JuneJuly 1944). The division was transported to Stettin, Pomerania, by ship in early 1945, and, on February 10, was upgraded to divisional status as the 23rd SS Volunteer Panzer Grenadier Division 'Nederland', although without any change to its table of organization and equipment and without any reinforcements. (It had only about 1,000 men left at this time, and its 48th SS Volunteer Regiment had been reduced from a strength of 2,000 men to eighty men.) It was sent to the Oder sector and was trapped in the huge Halbe Pocket southeast of Berlin. Here it surrendered to the Soviets on or about April 29, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第23党卫军装甲掷弹兵师最初名为“荷兰”志愿军团。该师在波兰克拉科夫（克拉科夫）组建，由加入武装党卫军以抗击共产主义的荷兰志愿者组成。起初它包括第一和第二“荷兰”志愿装甲掷弹兵团、一个拥有两个营的炮兵团、坦克歼击车、工兵及补充营、侦察连和通信连。在它的首次行动中（东线北部战区），该师于1942年6月攻击并消灭了一支规模大得多的苏联部队，在此过程中俘获了3500人，其中包括未来的俄罗斯解放军指挥官安德烈·弗拉索夫将军。随后该军团被调往北方，参加了列宁格勒围城战和第二次拉多加湖战役。<cr>该军团于1943年初被派回荷兰休整、招募和扩充。它在1943年10月23日升级为第4武装党卫军志愿装甲掷弹兵旅，并且其两个装甲掷弹兵团分别更名为“塞夫塔特将军”团（第48武装党卫军志愿装甲掷弹兵团）和“德鲁伊特”团（第49武装党卫军志愿装甲掷弹兵团）。荷兰军团/旅在巴尔干地区服役至1943年12月，之后被调往列宁格勒战区。它加入了第3装甲军，并参与了奥兰宁鲍姆围城战、从列宁格勒撤退的战斗、纳尔瓦河畔的激烈战斗以及库尔兰包围圈初期的战斗。在巴格拉季昂行动（1944年6月至7月）中，第48武装党卫军志愿装甲掷弹兵团及其大部分炮兵团被消灭。该师于1945年初通过船只运往波美拉尼亚什切青，并于2月10日升级为第23武装党卫军志愿装甲掷弹兵师“荷兰”，尽管编制表和装备没有变化，也没有增援。（此时它只剩下约1,000人，其第48武装党卫军志愿团从原来的2,000人减少到仅剩80人。）该师被派往奥得河战区，并在柏林东南的大哈尔贝包围圈中被困。大约于1945年4月29日向苏联投降。<cr>德国战斗序列第3卷 - 二战中的装甲、装甲掷弹兵和武装党卫军师，山姆·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text:
The 23rd Tank Corps was formed April 1942 in Southwestern Front as 3rd Mechanized Corps.<cr>The 23rd Tank Corps was formed with experienced tank brigades, at least:130th and 131st were both formed from the 8th Tank Division in 1941, and 6th Tank Brigade was formed from the 6th Tank Division. Unfortunately, in its first actions in the Battle of Kharkov in May, the Soviet command switched brigades back and forth between direct support missions in the rifle armies and operational missions with the tank corps. At various times in May and June 1942 23rd Tank Corps not only controlled its 'own' tank brigades, but also 57th, 65th, or 114th Tank Brigades.<cr>At that time the entire 4th Tank Army only had a handful of tanks left. As tank brigade remnants were evacuated to the rear to reform, 23rd Tank Corps was moved to 1st Tank Army in late July.<cr>From late August to October 1942, 23rd Tank Corps was under 62nd Army, acting as a 'holding HQ' for shot-up tank brigades.<cr>Finally, in October 1942 the corps was evacuated across the Volga into the tank training areas of Volga Military District. There, in November - December 1942, the corps was rebuilt. In late December it went back to the front in
Southwestern Front reserves.<cr>The 23rd Tank Corps took part in operations in the Donbass with Southwestern Front and 3rd Guards Army. As a result of the heavy casualties suffered in these battles, the corps went into reserve in Southwestern Front in March 1943. It remained in reserve until August 1943, when the advance to the Dnepr River began. By that time the corps had been built up to the 1943 standard.<cr>The 23rd Tank Corps kept these same components for the rest of 1943 and most of 1944, only adding a third tank battalion to each tank brigade late in 1943 and gradually replacing the light tanks in the brigades with all T-34s. The corps also spent the rest of the war in the southern portion of the front, with either 2nd or 3rd Ukrainian Front. From July to Octoberl944 the 23rd Tank Corps was paired with 5th Guards Cavalry Corps in Gorshkov's Cavalry Mechanized Group for the lasi-Kishinev Operation and the advance through Rumania into Hungary. In November the corps received its first structural change in over a year when 1669th Light Artillery Regiment (24 76rnm guns) was assigned. The 23rd Tank Corps ended the war in May 1945 in 2nd Ukrainian Front reserves in Austria.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第23坦克军于1942年4月在西南方面军中组建，当时是第3机械化军。该坦克军由有经验的坦克旅组成，至少包括：第130和第131坦克旅均成立于1941年的第8坦克师；第6坦克旅则来自第6坦克师。不幸的是，在5月哈尔科夫战役中的首次行动中，苏联指挥官在步兵师与坦克军之间来回调动这些坦克旅执行直接支援任务或作战任务。从1942年5月至6月期间，第23坦克军不仅控制了其“自己的”坦克旅，还一度控制了第57、第65和第114坦克旅。<cr>当时整个第4坦克集团军只剩下少量坦克。随着坦克旅残部被撤往后方重组，第23坦克军于7月下旬转移到第1坦克集团军。从8月下旬到10月，该坦克军隶属于第62集团军，在伏尔加河军事区的坦克训练区域充当“驻留司令部”，接收受损严重的坦克旅。<cr>最终在1942年10月，该部队被撤过伏尔加河进入伏尔加河军事区的坦克训练区域。在那里，从1942年11月至12月期间，该军得以重建。到12月下旬，它返回前线，在西南方面军预备队中。<cr>第23坦克军参加了与西南方面军和近卫第3集团军在顿巴斯地区的行动。由于这些战斗中的严重伤亡，该部队于1943年3月进入西南方面军的预备队。直到1943年8月进攻第聂伯河时才重新投入作战。<cr>到那时为止，该部已经重建至1943年的标准配置。第23坦克军在1943年余下的时间和大部分1944年都保持了相同的编制，仅在1943年末为每个装甲旅增加了第三个坦克营，并逐渐用T-34替换旅中的轻型坦克。该军在整个战争期间都在前线的南部地区作战，隶属于第2或第3乌克兰方面军。从1944年7月到10月，第23坦克军与戈尔什科夫骑兵机械化集团下的第5近卫骑兵军配合作战，在拉西-基希涅夫行动中以及通过罗马尼亚进入匈牙利的推进过程中协同作战。直到11月，该军才在一年多后首次进行编制调整，分配了第1669轻型炮兵团（24门76毫米火炮）。第23坦克军于1945年5月结束战争时驻扎在奥地利，隶属于第2乌克兰方面军的预备队。<cr><cr>苏联二战战斗序列第二卷 查尔斯·C·肖普

text:
The 23rd Tankd Division was formed February 1941 from 6th and 22nd Tank Brigades in Baltic Special Military District as part of 12th Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
45th Tank Regiment
46th Tank Regiment
23rd Motorized Rifle Regiment
23rd Motorized Howitzer Regiment
23rd Motorized Pontoon Battalion
23rd Reconnaissance Battalion
23rd Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>Formed from existing tank brigades, by 22 June 1941 23rd Tank Division was at nearly full strength in personnel, artillery, heavy weapons, and had over 75% of its authorized trucks - a much better percentage than normal in Soviet motorized units in 1941. Unfortunately, it only had about half its authorized tanks, and of the 230 tanks, all were light BT and T-26 tanks and 16% of them were in need of repair before the war even started. In other specific shortages, the divisional reconnaissance battalion had no headquarters or staff organized, and there were less than 20% of the authorized armored cars available.<cr>23rd Tank Division was ordered to counterattack German advancing units on the first day of the war in the Baltic. In moving to the front, the division came under heavy air attacks. To build up more armor for the attack, 28th Tank Division's 55th Tank regiment was added to the division late on 23 June. In the ensuing tank battles throughout 24 June, most of the tanks in all three tank regiments were either destroyed or overrun by the German armor.<cr>23rd Tank Division remained in the Soviet order of battle under 12th Mechanized Corps until early August, when it was officially disbanded.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第23装甲师成立于1941年2月，由波罗的海特别军区的第6和第22坦克旅组建，隶属于第12机械化军。<cr>截至1941年6月22日包括：<cr><cr>第45坦克团<cr>第46坦克团<cr>第23摩托化步兵团<cr>第23摩托化榴弹炮团<cr>第23摩托化浮桥营<cr>第23侦察营<cr>第23防空营<cr><cr>由现有坦克旅组建，到1941年6月22日，第23装甲师在人员、炮兵和重武器方面已接近满编，并拥有超过75%的授权卡车数量——这比当时苏联摩托化部队通常的比例要好得多。不幸的是，它只有大约一半的授权坦克，其中230辆坦克全部是轻型BT和T-26坦克，且有16%需要在战争开始前进行维修。<cr>此外，在具体短缺方面，师侦察营没有组织总部或参谋人员，并且仅有不到20%的授权装甲车可用。<cr>第23装甲师被命令在波罗的海地区对德军推进部队发起反击。在前往前线的过程中，该师遭到了猛烈的空袭。<cr>为了加强进攻力量，第28装甲师的第55坦克团于6月23日晚加入该师。<cr>在整个6月24日的坦克战斗中，三个坦克团中的大多数坦克要么被摧毁，要么被德军装甲部队击溃。<cr>第23装甲师一直留在苏联战斗序列中的第12机械化军直到8月初，然后正式解散。<cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普《苏联战斗序列 第一卷》

The 240th Mechanized Division was formed in March-April 1941 at Kupyansk in Kharkov Military District with:<cr>

text: The 243rd Rifle Division was one of a series of 15 divisions formed from cadres of NKVD border troops as standard Red Army rifle divisions, very shortly after the German invasion, in the Moscow Military District. It served in the heavy fighting around Smolensk in Smolensk, then later in the defensive operations around Kalinin. It then saw extensive service in the severe fighting around Rzhev, before being moved south in the winter of 1942-43. In the following winter the division was recognized for its role in the liberation of Nikopol, receiving that place name as an honorific. After battling through Ukraine, Romania, Hungary and Austria, the 243rd completed a very complex combat path by ending the war in Manchuria and earning a second honorific.<cr><cr>
translation: 第243步兵师是由内务人民委员部边防部队的骨干组建而成的15个红军标准步兵师之一，德国入侵后不久在莫斯科军区成立。该师参加了斯摩棱斯克地区的激烈战斗，随后又参与了加里宁地区防御作战。之后，它在热季夫周边的严重战斗中经历了长期服役，并于1942-43年冬季被调往南方。次年冬天，由于其在尼科波尔解放中的作用，该师获得了以该地名作为荣誉名称的认可。经过乌克兰、罗马尼亚、匈牙利和奥地利的激战后，第243步兵师通过在中国东北结束战争并获得第二个荣誉名称完成了复杂的战斗历程。<cr><cr>

text:
The division began organizing on June 26, 1941, in the Urals Military District. It was one of a series of rifle divisions numbered in the 240260 range that were built on cadres taken from the NKVD.<cr><cr>The division was assigned to 31st Army of Reserve Front until October, giving its troops more time to form up and train than many other divisions in that period. During that month it was assigned to 22nd Army in Kalinin Front, which was rebuilding after being partly overrun by the Germans in September. In December the 249th was transferred again to 27th Army, which was soon renamed 4th Shock Army.<cr><cr>The division led the attack of its Army in January 1942, advancing over 100 km through deep snow and without regular supplies until capturing the German supply base at Toropets on January 21. For its efforts in this offensive, the 249th Rifle Division was re-designated as the 16th Guards Rifle Division on February 16.<cr><cr>A new division, originally designated the 423rd Rifle Division, then the 2nd Estonian Rifle Division, began forming on Feb. 10, 1942 in the Chelyabinsk Oblast of the Urals Military District. On Feb. 28 it was finally re-designated as the 249th Estonian Rifle Division. The division stayed in the Urals until September, then was shipped to the Moscow Military District where it joined the 7th Estonian and the 19th Guards Rifle Divisions to form the 8th Estonian Rifle Corps. The 249th remained in that Corps for the duration.<cr><cr>In November the corps was assigned to Kalinin Front, and reinforced 3rd Shock Army in its attack against German Third Panzer Army in and around the city of Velikiye Luki. Its first battle was costly, and in spite of receiving the 162nd Machinegun Battalion and a training battalion as replacements in December, by the end of the battle on Feb. 1, 1943, the 249th was at about 50% strength, with a total of 4,213 officers and men. The division and its corps remained directly under Front command (in October Kalinin Front became 2nd Baltic Front) for the remainder of the year, attacking alongside 4th Shock Army towards Vitebsk in the Battle of Nevel in November and December.

In February, 1944, 8th Corps was reassigned to the reserves of Leningrad Front, following the breaking of the German siege and that Front's advance towards the Baltic States. Once the 249th entered Estonia it could draw on the local population for replacements. By August it was at a strength of 7,946 officers and men, making it a very strong rifle division for that stage of the war. In September, 8th Corps became part of 8th Army, which was clearing the coasts of Estonia and Latvia as well as the islands offshore. On Oct. 6, the 1st Battalion of the 925th Rifle Regiment, along with the 328th Reconnaissance Company, staged an amphibious assault on one of these islands, mounted on US Lend Lease DUKW amphibious trucks of the 283rd Special Purpose Truck Battalion. During this year the division as a whole was awarded the honorific 'Tartu' for assisting in the liberation of that city, as well as the Order of the Red Banner on October 22.<cr><cr>In February, 1945, 8th Corps returned to 2nd Baltic Front, now in Lithuania. On Mar. 17 a strength return showed the 249th still with 8,996 officers and men, nearly twice the strength of the average 1945 Red Army rifle division. They spent the last two months of the war helping to keep guard over the German forces trapped in the Kourland Pocket.<cr><cr>
translation:
该师于1941年6月26日在乌拉尔军区开始组建。它是系列步兵师之一，编号在240至260之间，由内务人民委员部抽调骨干建立。<cr><cr>该师被分配给预备方面军的第31集团军直到10月，在这段时间里其部队有更多时间集结和训练，比当时许多其他师都多。<cr><cr>在那个月中它又被调往加里宁方面军的第22集团军，该集团军正在重建，因为9月份被德军部分突破。到12月，第249步兵师再次转隶给第27集团军，后者不久改名为突击第4集团军。<cr><cr>在1942年1月，该师领导了其集团军的进攻，穿越超过100公里深雪地带，在没有正常补给的情况下前进，并于1月21日占领德军补给基地托罗佩茨。<cr><cr>由于在此次攻势中的努力，第249步兵师被重新指定为近卫第16步兵师，日期为2月16日。<cr><cr><cr>一个新的师，最初编号为第423步兵师，然后是第2爱沙尼亚步兵师，在1942年2月10日在乌拉尔军区的车里雅宾斯克州开始组建。到2月28日它最终被重新指定为第249爱沙尼亚步兵师。<cr><cr><cr>该师一直留在乌拉尔直到9月，然后被调往莫斯科军区，在那里与近卫第19步兵师和第7爱沙尼亚步兵师一起组建了第8爱沙尼亚步兵军。第249师在该军中服役至战争结束。11月，该军被分配到加里宁方面军，并加强了第3突击集团军对德国第3装甲集团军在维捷布斯克和周边地区的攻击。它的首次战斗代价高昂，在尽管于12月接收了第162机枪营和一个训练营作为补充后，截至1943年2月1日的战斗结束时，第249师的实力约为50% s%，总共有4,213名军官和士兵。该师及其军在当年余下的时间里继续直接受方面军指挥（加里宁方面军于10月成为波罗的海第二方面军），与第4突击集团军一起，在11月至12月的内夫尔战役中向维捷布斯克发起攻击。

1944年2月，第8军被重新分配到列宁格勒方面军的预备队中，在德军包围圈被打破后，该方面军向波罗的海国家推进。当第249步兵师进入爱沙尼亚时，可以利用当地人口进行补充。到了8月，其兵力达到7,946名官兵，成为当时非常强大的步兵师。9月，第8军成为了第8集团军的一部分，该集团军正在清理爱沙尼亚和拉脱维亚的海岸线以及附近的岛屿。10月6日，第925步兵团第1营与第328侦察连在美军租借法案提供的DUKW两栖卡车支援下，在其中一个岛上发动了登陆作战。这一年中，该师整体获得了“塔尔图”荣誉称号，以表彰其协助解放该城市，并于10月22日获得红旗勋章。<cr><cr>1945年2月，第8军返回波罗的海第二方面军，此时位于立陶宛境内。3月17日的一次兵力统计显示，第249步兵师仍有8,996名官兵，几乎是当时平均红军步兵师兵力的两倍。在战争最后两个月里，他们帮助守卫着困于库尔兰包围圈中的德军。<cr>

text: The 24th Army headquarters, formed from Headquarters Siberian Mlitary District; under General Staff instructions of 25 June 1941 arrived on 28 June 1941 at Vyazma, and was assigned six Siberian rifle divisions of the high command reserve (RVGK). The 24th participated in the Yelnya Offensive, August-September 1941. It was disbanded 10 October 1941, having been destroyed in the Vyazma Pocket.<cr>Reformed from 9 December 1941 to 4 January 1942 when it was redesignated as 1st Reserve Army. The army was assigned the 385th Rifle Division for less than a month. The army remained in the Moscow Defense Zone through April 1942 with no assigned forces.<cr>Reformed again on 20 May 1942, from an Operational Group under the command of Major General Aleksei Grechkin while assigned to the Southern Front. The army was concentrated in the area of Salsk, Rostov Oblast. The army was then transferred to the North Caucasus Front on 28 July. In early August the units assigned were transferred to the 12th and 37th Armies, and its headquarters relocated to Grozny, Chechen Republic, where it was assigned to the Transcaucasian Front. The army was disbanded on 23 August and the headquarters personnel were used to form the 58th Army on August 28, 1942.<cr>Soon afterwards reformed again as part of the Stalingrad Front from 9th Reserve Army on 1 September 1942. The army participated in the Battle of Stalingrad as part of both the Stalingrad and Don Fronts. In March-April 1943 relocated to the Voronezh area and was assigned to the Steppe Military District as part of the STAVKA reserves for rebuilding. Was redesignated 4th Guards Army in May 1943.<cr><cr>
translation: 第24集团军司令部，由西伯利亚军区司令部组建；根据总参谋部于1941年6月25日的指示，在1941年6月28日抵达维亚兹马，并被分配了来自最高统帅部预备队（RVGK）的六个西伯利亚步兵师。第24集团军参加了1941年8月至9月的叶连纳攻势。该集团军于1941年10月10日解散，因为在维亚兹马包围圈中被消灭。<cr><cr>从1941年12月9日至1942年1月4日重建，并重新命名为第1预备集团军。该集团军在莫斯科防御区一直驻扎到1942年4月，期间没有分配任何部队。<cr><cr>再次于1942年5月20日在南方方面军司令部的少将亚历山大·格雷琴金指挥下的一个作战群基础上重建。该集团军集中在罗斯托夫州萨尔斯基地区的区域。随后在7月28日转移到北高加索方面军，并于8月初，所分配的部队被转移至第12和第37集团军，其司令部迁移到车臣共和国格罗兹尼市，并被分配给外高加索方面军。该集团军于8月23日解散，司令部人员用于组建第58集团军，时间为1942年8月28日。<cr><cr>不久之后，从第9预备集团军在1942年9月1日在斯大林格勒方面军基础上重建。该集团军参加了斯大林格勒战役，并作为斯大林格勒和顿河方面军的一部分参与了战斗。于1943年3月至4月转移到沃罗涅日地区，并被分配给外高加索军区，作为最高统帅部预备队进行重建。在1943年5月重新命名为第4近卫集团军。<cr><cr>

text: The 24th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In the fall of 1941 the brigade was one of five brigades reduced in size and stripped of their artillery that was assigned to the Hungarian Occupation Group for security duties on the Eastern Front. At this time it was redesignated the 124th Hungarian Infantry Brigade but in February of 1942 was redesignated the 124th Light Division. In May of 1943 the unit became the 24th Light Division. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 24th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 24th Infantry Division. In January of 1944 the Hungarian First Army to which the division was then subordinate, mobilized to defend Hungary's northern Carpathian frontier against the advancing Red Army.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第24匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖两个步兵团（每个团有三个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有七个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1941年秋季，该旅是五个被削减规模并剥离了炮兵的旅之一，这些旅被分配给匈牙利占领集团执行东线方面的治安任务。此时，它被重新命名为第124匈牙利步兵旅，但于1942年2月又被改名为第124轻师。1943年5月，该单位成为第24轻师。作为斯大林格勒战役后对匈牙利陆军进行的一般重组的一部分，第24轻师与其他部队合并，并更名为第24步兵师。1944年1月，在当时下属的匈牙利第一集团军动员下，该师准备防御匈牙利北部喀尔巴阡山脉边境以抵御进犯的红军。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas 和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利陆军》<cr>条目由 Chris Munson 提供

text: The 24th Infantry Division crossed into Russia in June 1941, fought its way across eastern Galacia and the Ukraine and into the Crimea with von Manstein's 11th Army, and took part in the Siege of Sevastopol for several months. With the 22nd Air Landing Division it was involved in the amphibious assault that led to the fall of the city in early July 1942. Transferred to Army Group North with the 11th Army, the division helped repulse the Russian counteroffensives in the Lake lImen area in the latter part of 1942. The 24th remained in the northern sector of the Eastern Front for the remainder of the war. It was reorganized as a Type 44 division in September 1943, when each of its grenadier regiments were reduced to two battalions each. It was part of the 18th Army when the Soviets broke the Siege of Leningrad in mid-January 1944. Unlike several other divisions, the 24th kept its composure and was later officially cited for its bravery in the withdrawal through the Baltic States. In July 1944 it held its line against the Russian summer offensive, withdrew into western Latvia at its own pace in October 1944, and fought in the six battles of the Courland Pocket (1944-45).<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第24步兵师于1941年6月进入俄罗斯，穿越东加利西亚和乌克兰，并与曼施泰因的第11集团军一起进入克里米亚。该师参与了塞瓦斯托波尔围城战数月。与第22空降师一起，它参加了导致这座城市于1942年7月初陷落的两栖突击行动。随后被调往北方集团军群，在第11集团军的帮助下，该师在1942年下半年帮助击退了俄罗斯在伊利门湖地区的反攻。在整个战争期间，第24步兵师一直驻守在东线北部战区。1943年9月，它被重组为Type 44型师，每个掷弹兵团都缩减到两个营。当苏联打破列宁格勒围城战时（1944年1月中旬），该师隶属于第18集团军。与其他几个师不同，第24步兵师保持了冷静，并在后来因从波罗的海国家撤退中的英勇表现而获得官方表彰。1944年7月，它坚守住了防线，抵御了俄罗斯夏季攻势，在同年10月以自己的节奏撤入拉脱维亚西部，并参加了库尔兰包围圈内的六场战役（1944-45）。<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷 1至290步兵师在二战中的表现，山姆·米奇安 Jr.

text: The corps was created after the occupation of Latvia in 1940 as the Latvian Territorial Corps, and it consisted of the 181st and 183rd Rifle Divisions. It was part of 27th Army. It was disbanded in July and reformed in spring 1943 as part of 60th Army and consisted of 121st Guards, 112th, 140th, 149th, 287th, and 328th Rifle Divisions. It fought at Kursk, in Operation Polkovodets Rumyantsev, and at the liberation of Kiev. In 1944 it became part of 13th Army and fought in the Lvov-Sandomierz Operation. In 1945, as part of 3rd Guards Army, it fought in the Berlin Strategic Offensive<cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军成立于1940年占领拉脱维亚之后，当时称为拉脱维亚地方军，并由第181步兵师和第183步兵师组成。它隶属于第27集团军。该军于7月解散，在1943年春季重组为第60集团军的一部分，包括第121近卫、第112、第140、第149、第287和第328步兵师。它参加了库尔斯克战役、波罗金采夫·鲁缅采夫行动以及解放基辅的战斗。在1944年，该军成为第13集团军的一部分，并参与了利沃夫-桑多梅日攻势。1945年作为第3近卫集团军的一部分，参加了柏林战略进攻作战。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军战斗序列在伟大卫国战争中的变化, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 24th Rifle Division was formed from volunteers in July 1918 as the 1st Simbirsk Infantry Division. In November of the same year it was renamed as the 24th Simbirsk Rifle Division. During the Russian Civil War it was active in the Volga region, Southern Ural Mountains, Polissya and Volhynia. In 1922 it was renamed as the 24th Samaro-Simbirsk Iron Rifle Division. In 1924 it was once again renamed becoming the 24th Samaro-Ulyanovsk Iron Rifle Division. During the Winter War the division distinguished itself during the breaking of the Mannerheim Line on the Karelian isthmus.<cr>The division was active in the fighting from the first days of Operation Barbarossa. It took part in the Kiev and then in heavy fighting in Belarus. The division was disbanded in December 1941. In February 1942 a new 24th Rifle Division was formed in the area of Vologda as part of the 17th Guards Rifle Corps. The Division participated in the Battle of Stalingrad, the Donbass offensive operation, in Zhytomyr - Berdychiv, Khmelnytskyi - Chernivtsi, Lviv - Sandomierz, East - Carpathian, Western - Carpathian, Moravia - Ostrava and the Prague offensive operations. The division ended the war near Prague and was disbanded in July 1945.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第24步兵师成立于1918年7月，当时称为第1西比利亚步兵师。同年11月改名为第24西比利亚步兵师。在俄罗斯内战期间，该师活跃于伏尔加河地区、南乌拉尔山脉、波利西亚和沃林尼亚。1922年更名为第24萨马拉-西比利亚钢铁步兵师。1924年再次改名为第24萨马拉-乌里扬诺夫斯克钢铁步兵师。在冬季战争期间，该师在卡累利阿地峡突破曼纳海姆防线时表现出色。<cr>巴巴罗萨行动开始后，该师即投入战斗，在基辅和白俄罗斯的激烈战斗中发挥了重要作用。1941年12月该师被解散。1942年2月，新的第24步兵师在沃洛格达地区重新组建，并隶属于第17近卫步兵军。<cr>该师参加了斯大林格勒战役、顿巴斯进攻作战、日托米尔-别列兹涅夫、赫梅利尼茨基-切尔诺维策、利沃夫-桑多梅日、东喀尔巴阡山、西喀尔巴阡山、摩拉维亚-奥斯特拉发和布拉格进攻作战。<cr>该师在战争结束时靠近布拉格，并于1945年7月被解散。

text:
The 24th Tank Corps was formed in April 1942 at Voroshilovgrad in the Kharkov Military District.<cr>The 24th Tank Corps was another corps, like the 2lst, 22nd, and 23rd, formed
in Southwestern Theater from existing tank units in the spring of 1942 with their numbers out of sequence. Quite possibly, like the others, 24th Tank Corps was originally known as a Mechanized Corps, but in the earliest Soviet records it is referred to as a Tank Corps. Like the other corps on the southern front, the command played 'musical brigades' with the corps HQ in May and June as the German summer offensive started. 2nd Tank Brigade was quickly removed from the brigade, and it was late June before the corps composition stabilized.<cr>Note that all three of the corps' tank brigades had a good cadre of experienced personnel: 54th and 130th were both formed from prewar Tank Divisions, and 4th Guards had distinguished itself in the Battle of Moscow. In addition, by October at the latest the corps had picked up a good collection of supporting
units.<cr>The 24th Tank Corps was in reserve when the Stalingrad Counteroffensive started on 19 November. In mid-December the corps went into the attack with 1st Guards Army. Operating as an independent Mobile Group, 24th Tank Corps broke deep into the German rear and overran the airfield at Tatsinskaya - the main base for the airlift supplying 6th Army in Stalingrad. While the air supply operations had certainly not been succeeding before this, the raid broke the back of the Luftwaffe effort. Counterattacks by panzers forced most of the corps to abandon their equipment and 'exfilitrate' back to Russian lines, but the corps' exploits in the raid earned it the honorific title: 'Tatsinskaya' and redesignation as 2nd Guards Tank Corps on 26 December 1942.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第24坦克军于1942年4月在哈尔科夫军区的沃罗希洛夫格勒组建。第24坦克军是像第21、22和23坦克军一样，在1942年春季从现有的坦克部队中组建起来的另一个坦克军，其番号并不连续。很可能与其他几个坦克军一样，第24坦克军最初被称为机械化军，但在最早的苏联记录中它被称作坦克军。<cr>与南部战线上的其他军队一样，该部在5月和6月进行了“旅调换”行动，随着德国夏季攻势的开始，指挥部频繁调动。第2坦克旅很快就被移出了编成，直到6月下旬部队编制才稳定下来。<cr>值得注意的是，该军的所有三个坦克旅都拥有大量经验丰富的人员：第54和第130坦克旅都是由战前的坦克师组建而成，而第4近卫坦克旅在莫斯科保卫战中表现出色。此外，最迟至10月，该部已经集结了一大批支援单位。<cr>当斯大林格勒反攻于1942年11月19日开始时，第24坦克军处于预备状态。12月中旬，该部在第1近卫集团军的指挥下发起攻击行动。作为独立机动集群作战，第24坦克军深入德军后方，并占领了塔茨斯基空军基地——这是向斯大林格勒围困中的第6集团军提供空运补给的主要基地。<cr>虽然在此之前空运行动肯定没有成功，但这次袭击彻底摧毁了德国空军的努力。装甲部队的反击迫使该部大部分人员放弃装备并“撤退”回苏联战线，但在此次突袭中表现出色后，该部获得了荣誉称号：“塔茨斯基”，并于1942年12月26日被重新命名为第2近卫坦克军。<cr>苏联战斗序列 二战卷二 查尔斯·C·肖普著

text: The 250th Infantry Division consisted of Spanish soldiers who volunteered to fight for Germany against the communists. It was 14,000 strong when it was mustered in at the Grafenwoehr Troop Maneuver Area in July 20, 1941. Quickly sent into action at Novgorod on the northern sector of the Russian Front, the so-called 'Blue Division' fought very well in all of its engagements. In the Novgorod-Leningrad-Lake Ilmen battles of late 1941-early 1942, the Spanish Fascist volunteers played a major role in turning back the Russian winter offensive in the northern sector but lost 8,000 men killed, wounded, captured, or incapacitated by frostbite. After receiving replacements from Spain, it continued in action with Army Group North, fought at Volchov, and lost another 3,200 men in the Second Battle of Lake Ladoga in January and February 1943. Here its Fusilier battalion lost 90 percent of its soldiers, but the division again held its positions against massive Soviet attacks. The 250th continued to serve in northern Russia and in the siege of Leningrad until October 1943. At that time Spanish dictator Francisco Franco requested that the division be returned to Spain; however, about half of its veteran warriors volunteered for service in the Waffen-SS and continued to fight against the Russians until the end of the war. The Blue Division was officially disbanded on October 20, 1943.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第250步兵师由西班牙志愿者组成，他们自愿为德国对抗共产主义作战。该师于1941年7月20日在格拉芬沃赫演习区组建时有14,000人。很快被派往诺夫哥罗德北部战线的战斗中，被称为“蓝色师”的西班牙部队在所有战役中表现出色。<cr>在1941年末至1942年初的诺夫哥罗德-列宁格勒-伊利门湖战役中，“蓝色师”在对抗苏联冬季攻势时发挥了重要作用，但自身也损失了8,000人（阵亡、受伤、被俘或冻伤）。<cr>从西班牙补充兵员后，该师继续随北方集团军群作战，在沃尔乔夫和1943年1月至2月的第二次拉多加湖战役中又损失了3,200人。其中其步枪营损失了90%的士兵，但整个师仍然坚守阵地对抗苏联的大规模进攻。<cr>第250师继续在北俄罗斯服役，并参与列宁格勒围城战直到1943年10月。此时西班牙独裁者弗朗西斯科·佛朗哥请求将该师撤回西班牙；然而，大约一半的老兵志愿加入武装党卫军并继续对抗苏联直至战争结束。<cr>“蓝色师”于1943年10月20日正式解散。<cr>参考文献：德国战斗序列第一卷：二战中的第1至第290步兵师，山姆·W·米查姆少校

text: The 250th Rifle Division began forming within days of the start of the German invasion on June 26, 1941, at Vladimir, in the Moscow Military District, based on a cadre of 1,500 officers and men of the NKVD Internal Troops.The division was first assigned to 30th Army in Western Front.<cr><cr>The 250th was almost immediately committed to heavy fighting north of Smolensk. After about two weeks of combat, the division had lost about half its strength. As well, by Aug. 5 the tank battalion was down to eight T-34s, one T-26, two BT-7s and six BT-5s, when the division was transferred to 29th Army. By early October the 250th had lost all its armor, and was reduced to 500 men fighting at Olenino.<cr><cr>While retreating to the Kalinin area from Rzhev, the division became part of the newly formed Kalinin Front, under command of Col. Gen. Ivan Konev. On October 15 the 250th was ordered to 'stubbornly defend' its sector, alongside the 220th Rifle Division. On the 18th, Konev reported that both divisions were falling back under German pressure. On October 21, the two divisions were assigned to 22nd Army.<cr><cr>The 250th spent the winter in Kalinin Front, and in April 1942 was reassigned to the newly-forming 53rd Army in Northwestern Front, where it remained in the vicinity of Demyansk until February 1943. After a brief posting to 1st Shock Army in the same Front, in early March the 250th got new orders to re-deploy to the new 2nd Reserve Army, in the Yelets, Lepetsk and Lebedian regions. In April, 2nd Reserve became the 63rd Army, assigned to Bryansk Front, and the division was also assigned to 35th Rifle Corps, where it would remain for the duration. In this Front (Belorussian Front after October 20) the 250th would take part in the difficult fighting through Bryansk and towards the Dniepr River until February 1944.<cr><cr>On February 18, 63rd Army was dissolved, and 35th Rifle Corps was reassigned to 3rd Army, where it would remain for the duration. At the outset of Operation Bagration, on June 23, 35th Rifle Corps, under command of Major General Viktor Zholudev, formed one of the two assault corps of 3rd Army, packed into less than ten kilometres of front opposite the northern half of the sector held by the German 134th Infantry Division. On the second day of the offensive, at 0400 hours, the assault force unleashed a massive 2-hour bombardment on the defenders in the Rogachev area. As the weather cleared towards evening, further lines were taken, and the 9th Tank Corps prepared to exploit a breakthrough. Northwest of Bobruysk on June 26, the tankers cut the road to Mogilev behind the German XXXV Corps, with 35th and 41st Rifle Corps close behind and the 134th Infantry shattered and in flight. On the following day Bobruysk was surrounded, along with most of German 9th Army, and it fell to the 250th to help clear and liberate the city, for which the men and women of the division received the name of that city as an honorific. On Aug. 9, the 250th was also awarded the Order of Suvorov II Class.<cr><cr>Also, in August, the division, along with its army and corps, were transferred to 2nd Belorussian Front, where it would remain for the next six months, assisting in the liberation of the remainder of Belorussia and eastern Poland. It was still in this front at the outset of the Vistula-Oder Offensive in January 1945, but in February was reassigned to 3rd Belorussian Front, fighting in East Prussia. In April, 3rd Army was once again reassigned, this time to back to 1st Belorussian Front, in preparation for the assault on the German capital. When the shooting stopped, the division was in the enemy's lair of Berlin, and the final full title of its men and women was '250th Rifle, Bobruysk, Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov Division'.<cr><cr>
translation: 第250步兵师于1941年6月26日德国入侵开始后的几天内在莫斯科军区的弗拉基米尔市组建，基于内务人民委员部内部部队的1500名军官和士兵。该师最初被分配给西方方面军的第30集团军。<cr>第250步兵师几乎立即就被投入斯摩棱斯克北部的激烈战斗中。经过大约两周的战斗，该师损失了约一半的实力。此外，到8月5日，坦克营只剩下8辆T-34、1辆T-26、2辆BT-7和6辆BT-5，随后该师被转移到第29集团军。<cr>到10月初，第250步兵师已经失去了所有的装甲车辆，并且只有约500人在奥列宁诺作战。<cr>在从热季夫撤退至加里宁地区时，该师成为新成立的加里宁方面军的一部分，由上将伊万·科涅夫指挥。10月15日，第250步兵师被命令“坚决防御”其防区，并与第220步兵师并肩作战。<cr>18日，科涅夫报告称两支部队都在德军的压力下撤退。10月21日，这两支师被分配给第22集团军。第250师在1941至1942年冬季驻扎于加里宁方面军，4月被调往新组建的西北方向第53集团军，在德梅伊扬斯克附近驻守到1943年2月。之后短暂派驻同一方面的第1突击集团军，3月初接到新的调动命令，前往叶列茨、列佩茨克和莱贝季扬地区的新编第2预备集团军。4月，第2预备集团军改称第63集团军，并被分配到布良斯克方面军，该师也被分配至第35步兵军，在此驻守直到战争结束。在这一方面军（10月后称为白俄罗斯方面军）中，第250师参与了从布良斯克向第聂伯河艰难推进的战斗，直至1944年2月。<cr>指挥官报告：<cr>第250师于1943年2月至1944年2月期间在白俄罗斯方面军服役。2月18日，第63集团军解散，第35步兵军被调至第3集团军，并一直留在那里。在巴格拉季昂行动开始时，即6月23日，在少将维克多·佐留德夫的指挥下，第35步兵军成为第3集团军两个突击军之一，部署在不足10公里宽的战线上，面对德国第134步兵师占据的北部半区。进攻第二天凌晨4点，突击部队对罗加乔夫地区的防守者进行了2小时的大规模炮击。随着天气转晴，傍晚时分占领了更多阵地，第9坦克军准备利用突破进行扩张。6月26日，在鲍里斯拉夫西北方向，坦克兵切断了德国第35军后方通往莫吉廖夫的道路，第35步兵军和第41步兵军紧随其后，而德军第134步兵师被击溃并仓皇逃窜。次日，鲍里斯拉夫及其周边地区被包围，包括大部分德国第9集团军在内。250师帮助清理并解放了这座城市，为此该师官兵获得了以城市命名的荣誉称谓。8月9日，250师还荣获苏沃洛夫勋章二级奖章。<cr><cr><cr><cr>此外，在8月，该师连同其所在的集团军和军一起被转移到了第2白俄罗斯方面军，在那里停留了接下来的六个月，协助解放白俄罗斯剩余地区及东波兰。在1945年1月开始的维斯瓦-奥得河攻势初期，它仍然在这个方面军内，但在2月又被重新分配到第3白俄罗斯方面军，在东普鲁士作战。4月时，该集团军再次被重新分配，这次是回到第1白俄罗斯方面军，为进攻德国首都做准备。战斗结束后，该师位于敌方巢穴柏林，其最终完整的称号是“第250步兵波布鲁斯克红旗苏沃洛夫勋章师”。<cr> <cr>

text: The 251st Infantry Division was formed in August 1939 as part of the 4th Wave. It contained the 451st, 459th and 471st Infantry Regiments, 251st Artillery Regiment and various support units. The division was part of the XXIII Army Corps in Army Group North at the start of Operation Barbarossa. In November 1943 the division was disbanded. It was reformed in September 1944 from the 'E' Corps Detachment. The new division had the 184th, 448th and 451st Grenadier Regiments, 186th Artillery Regiment and various support units. In January 1945 the division was destroyed near the Warka bridgehead in Poland. It was disbanded in March 1945.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation:
第251步兵师成立于1939年8月，属于第四波组建的部队。该师包括第451团、第459团和第471团，第251炮兵团以及各种支援单位。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师隶属于北方集团军群下的第XXIII军。

1943年11月，该师被解散。1944年9月，它从“E”军属部队重组而成，新编成的师包括第184掷弹兵团、第448掷弹兵团和第451掷弹兵团，第186炮兵团以及各种支援单位。

1945年1月，该师在波兰瓦尔卡桥头堡附近被消灭。同年3月，该师解散。

参考文献：George F. Nafziger, 《二战期间德国战斗序列中的步兵》

text:
On the order of Stavka, the 251st Rifle Division was one of the first 10 Rifle Divisions created from NKVD cadre in late June 1941. L.P. Beria was personally responsible for raising these divisions. The division was established at Kolomna in the Moscow Military District, finished formation on 13th July, and was assigned to the 30th Army. The division lacked trained personnel, equipment and transport and was considered to be of low combat value. The division fought at Smolensk and was trapped in the Vyazma pockrt, but successfully broke out with heavy losses.

The division was formed for a second time in November 1941, based on the 2,000 men that had escaped the pocket. In late 1942 the division was assigned to the 20th Army, Western Front, and participated in Operation Mars where it suffered heavy casualties. In June 1944, assigned to the 5th Guards Rifle Corps, 39th Army, the division fought in Operation Bagration, where it was awarded the honorific of Vitebsk for the liberation of that city. It fought in Courland and ended the war assigned to the 2nd Guards Army, 3rd Belorussian Front.

It had also been awarded the Order of the Red Banner and Order of Suvorov.



 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

David Glantz, Colossus Reborn
 
Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
根据最高统帅部大本营的命令，第251步兵师是1941年6月底由内务人民委员部骨干创建的首批10个步兵师之一。L.P. 贝利亚亲自负责组建这些部队。该师在莫斯科军区科洛姆纳成立，于7月13日完成编成，并被分配给第30集团军。由于缺乏训练有素的人力、装备和运输工具，该师被认为战斗值较低。该师参加了斯摩棱斯克战役，并被困在维亚兹马包围圈内，但成功突围并遭受了重大损失。

1941年11月，该师基于从包围圈中逃脱的2000人第二次组建。1942年底，该师被分配给西方方面军第20集团军，并参加了火星行动，在此过程中遭受了严重伤亡。1944年6月，该师被分配给第5近卫步兵军、第39集团军，并参加了巴格拉季昂行动，在解放维捷布斯克市后获得了“维捷布斯克”的荣誉称号。该师在库尔兰作战，并于战争结束时被分配给了第2近卫集团军、第3白俄罗斯方面军。

此外，该师还获得了一级红旗勋章和苏沃洛夫勋章。

text: The 252nd Infantry Division was formed in August 1939 as part of the 4th Wave. It contained the 452nd, 461st and 472nd Infantry Regiments, 252nd Artillery Regiment and various support units. The division was part of the XXXXIII Army Corps in Army Group Centre at the start of Operation Barbarossa. By February 1943 the 452nd Regiment had been replaced by the 7th Regiment and the 472nd Regiment was disbanded and its survivors distributed to the other two regiments. In September 1943 the division consisted of the 7th and 461st Grenadier Regiments, 252nd Artillery Regiment and various support troops. In July 1944 the 472nd Regiment was reformed. The division was taken prisoner by the Russians near Danzig.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text:
On the order of Stavka, the 252nd Rifle Division was one of the first 10 Rifle Divisions created from NKVD cadre in late June 1941. L.P. Beria was personally responsible for raising these divisions. The division was established at Serpukhovin the Moscow Military District, finished formation on 13th July, and was assigned to the 29th Army. The division fought at Smolensk and suffered heavy casualties and in October 1941 was assigned to the 39th Army in the defense of Kalinin where it fought with some distinction. The following year the division fought in the battles around Rzhev and in July 1942 barely escaped entrapment.

The division was withdrawn to be rebuilt and in October was assigned to the Don Front at Stalingrad, but by November it was depleted and was withdrawn into the Reserve. The Division fought with success in the Stalingrad counter offensive but by January 1943 was assigned to mopping up operations. In April the division was reorganised and fought successfully at Kharkov where it was awarded the honorific of 'KHARKOV' . In January 1944, assigned to the 53rd Army, it fought in the liberation of Uman and pursued the Axis forces to the Danube. It fought in the capture of Bratisalva for which it was awarded the honorific of 'BRATISLAVA' and ended the war linking up with the U.S. 2nd Infantry Division near Pilsen.

A highly distinguished Division, it had been awarded the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov and Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky.



 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

David Glantz, Colossus Reborn
 
Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
根据最高统帅部大本营的命令，第252步兵师是1941年6月下旬从内务人民委员部骨干中组建的首批十个步兵师之一。L.P. 贝利亚亲自负责建立这些师。该师在莫斯科军区的瑟普霍夫成立，在7月13日完成编组，并被分配给第29集团军。该师参加了斯摩棱斯克战役，遭受了重大伤亡，并于1941年10月被调往第39集团军保卫加里宁，在那里表现出色。

次年，该师在热季夫周围的战斗中作战，并且在1942年7月险些陷入包围。该师撤出重建，并于10月被分配给斯大林格勒顿河方面军，但到11月时兵力已耗尽并转入预备队。该师成功参加了斯大林格勒反攻战，但在1943年1月又被调往清剿行动。4月，该师重组并在哈尔科夫作战，并因此获得“哈尔科夫”荣誉称号。1944年1月，被分配给第53集团军的该师参加了乌曼解放战役，并追击轴心国部队至多瑙河。该师在布拉迪斯拉发的占领中表现出色并因此获得“布拉迪斯拉发”荣誉称号，战争结束时与美国第2步兵师在皮尔森附近会合。

这是一支非常杰出的师，曾被授予红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫勋章和博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基勋章。

text:
The 253rd Soviet Rifle Division started forming on the 10th July at Volchansk in the Odessa Military District. It completed formation on the 15th of August and was assigned to the Southern Front. It was not a strong formation and was destroyed at Krivoi Rog and was disbanded on the 19th September, 1941.

The Division was formed for a second time in October 1941 and was assigned to the 37th Army and then in January the 38th Army. The division was trapped and destroyed at Izyum in May 1942.

The Division was formed for a third time in September 1942 at Chapaevsk and assigned to the Voronezh Front. It fought along the Dnieper and at Kalinkovichi and ended the war assigned to the 3rd Guards Army of the 1st Ukrainian Front. 



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第253苏联步兵师于1941年7月10日在敖德萨军区沃尔恰ansk开始组建。该师于8月15日完成组建，并被分配给南方方面军。该部队实力不强，在克里沃伊罗格被消灭，于1941年9月19日解散。

该师在1941年10月第二次组建，并被分配给第37集团军，然后在1942年1月被分配给第38集团军。该师在1942年5月的伊久姆战役中被困并被消灭。

该师于1942年9月第三次在恰帕耶夫斯克组建，并被分配给沃罗涅日方面军。它参加了第聂伯河地区的战斗，在卡林科维奇作战，最终被分配给第一乌克兰方面军第3近卫集团军结束战争。

text: The 254th Infantry Division was formed in August 1939 as part of the 4th Wave. It contained the 454th, 474th and 484th Infantry Regiments, 254th Artillery Regiment and various support units. text:
On the order of Stavka, the 254th Rifle Division was one of the first 10 Rifle Divisions created from NKVD cadre in late June 1941. L.P. Beria was made personally responsible for raising these divisions. The division was established at Tetnitsky Camp, north of Tula, in the Moscow Military District, finished formation on 13th July, and was assigned to the 11th Army, Northwestern Front. The division was rushed to Staraya Russa without it's artillery and many of its machine guns and fought with distinction. The division fought at Demyansk and at the end of 1942 was assigned to the 27th Army, Northwestern Front.

In 1944 The Division was the first Soviet Unit to cross into Romanian territory and it's last major action was the Battle of Bautzen in 1945, near Dresden, assigned to the 52nd Army. On the 21st April, 1945, its commanding officer, Major General M.K. Puteiko, one of the youngest Soviet Generals at that time, died from wounds, and now lies in a cemetery in L'vov.

A highly distinguished Division with many Heroes of the Soviet Union, it had been awarded the honorific of 'CHERKASSY', Order of Lenin, Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov, Order of Kutuzov and Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky.



 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

David Glantz, Colossus Reborn

A.A. Maslov, Fallen Soviet generals
 
Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
根据最高统帅部大本营的命令，第254步兵师是1941年6月底从内务人民委员部骨干中组建的第一个十个步兵师之一。L.P. 贝利亚被指定负责建立这些师。该师在图拉北部的特滕茨基营地成立，在莫斯科军区完成编组，于7月13日结束组建，并分配给第11集团军，西北方面军。该师没有炮兵和许多机枪就被紧急调往斯塔罗亚罗斯萨作战，并表现出色。该师在德米扬斯克作战，到1942年底被分配给第27集团军，西北方面军。

1944年，该师成为第一个进入罗马尼亚领土的苏联部队，其最后一个主要行动是1945年的包岑战役，靠近德累斯顿，并被分配给第52集团军。1945年4月21日，其指挥官M.K. 普特耶科少将，在当时是最年轻的苏联将军之一，因伤去世，现在安葬在利沃夫的公墓中。

这是一支非常杰出的师，拥有许多苏联英雄称号，并被授予“切尔卡斯基”荣誉称号、列宁勋章、红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫勋章、库图佐夫勋章和博格丹·赫梅尔尼茨基勋章。

text: The 255th Infantry Division was formed in August 1939 as part of the 4th Wave. It contained the 455th, 465th and 475th Infantry Regiments, 255th Artillery Regiment and various support units. text: In June 1941, the 256th Infantry Division invaded Russia, where it was almost continuously engaged for the next three years. It fought at Bialystok, Nevel, Velikije Luki, Kalinin, and Rzhev (December 1941-January 1942). In the last ten days of December 1941, it held its line near Moscow against odds of ten to one or even higher odds. A month later it was instrumental in saving the XXIII Corps, which the Soviets had surrounded west of Rzhev. Remaining on the central sector of the Russian Front, it held a defensive sector east of Smolensk and took part in the Rzhev withdrawal, but apparently was not present at the Battle of Kursk . The 256th suffered heavy losses at the Battle of Smolensk in the autumn of 1943 and, as part of the 3rd Panzer Army, was destroyed at Vitebsk by the Soviet summer offensive of 1944. The remnants of the division became Divisiongruppe 256 of Corps Detachment H on July 21. They later ended up in the 280th Grenadier Regiment of the 95th Infantry Division.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 1941年6月，第256步兵师入侵俄罗斯，在接下来的三年里几乎一直参战。该师参加了比亚韦斯托克、涅夫勒、维列茨耶卢基、加里宁和热季夫（1941年12月至1942年1月）等地的战斗。在1941年最后十天，它在莫斯科附近坚守阵地，面对的是十比一甚至更高的敌军优势。一个月后，该师在热季夫以西帮助解救了被包围的第23军。留在俄罗斯方面军中央战区，它守卫斯摩棱斯克东面的一个防御地带，并参与了热季夫撤退行动，但似乎并未参加库尔斯克会战。1943年秋季在斯摩棱斯克战役中遭受重大损失后，作为第3装甲集团军的一部分，在1944年的苏联夏季攻势中被消灭于维捷布斯克。该师残部于7月21日成为H集群的第256步兵群，并最终并入了第95步兵师下的第280掷弹兵团。<cr>德国二战陆军战斗序列卷一：第1至第290步兵师，萨缪尔·W·米奇安 Jr.

text:
On the order of Stavka, the 257th Rifle Division was one of the first 10 Rifle Divisions created from NKVD cadre in late June 1941. L.P. Beria was made personally responsible for raising these divisions. The division was established near Tula in the Moscow Military District, finished formation on 10th July, and was assigned to the 34th Army. The Division took part in the unsuccessful Staraya Russa counter offensive and was smashed. The commander of the 34th Army Kuzma Kachanov was arrested on the 12th September and executed.

The Division started forming for a second time on the 8th November 1941 in the Moscow Military District and on the 25th December was assigned to the 3rd Shock Army, Northwestern Front, and soon after the Kalinin Front. In early 1942, short of equipment and supplies the Division pushed towards, but was unable to take, Velikie Luki, which did not fall until 1943. In April 1943, the Division was renamed the 91st Gurads Rifle Division.

In June 1943 the Division was formed for the third time at Krymskaya, based on 9th and 60th Rifle Brigades and the 62nd Naval Rifle Brigade and finished the war assigned to the 4th Shock Army in Courland.



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 

David Glantz, Colossus Reborn

Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
根据最高统帅部大本营的命令，第257步兵师是1941年6月下旬从内务人民委员部骨干中组建的首批10个步兵师之一。L.P.贝利亚被指定负责这些师的建立工作。该师在图拉附近的莫斯科军区成立，于7月10日完成编组，并分配给第34集团军。该师参加了未能成功的斯塔罗亚鲁萨反攻行动并遭受重创。第34集团军司令库兹马·卡恰诺夫于9月12日被捕并于当日被处决。

该师从1941年11月8日起在莫斯科军区开始第二次组建，并于12月25日分配给西北方面军的第3突击集团军，随后又转隶加里宁方面军。1942年初，在装备和补给不足的情况下，该师向维捷布斯克推进但未能占领该地，直到1943年才被攻克。1943年4月，该师更名为第91近卫步兵师。

1943年6月，该师在克里木斯卡亚第三次组建，基于第9和第60步兵旅以及第62海军步兵旅，并最终分配给库尔兰的第4突击集团军结束战争。

text: The 258th Infantry Division crossed into Russia in mid-1941, and fought and at Brest, Bialystok, Bobruisk, Yelnya, and Vyazma-Bryansk as well as in the battles around Moscow. The 258th continued to serve with Army Group Center until late summer 1943, and took part in the defensive battles at Jucknov, Gshatsk and Orel. It was also involved in the Kursk offensive. During the retreat from Kursk and Orel, the division defended 9th Army's supply depot at Kromy against heavy odds, withstood fifteen major Soviet attacks, and frustrated the Russian attempt to seize the depot. Later in the year the Prussian division was transferred to the southern sector of the Eastern Front. It took part in the Mius and Dnieper retreats and was at battle group strength by October 1943. It fought in the Nikopol Bridgehead and was routed in March 1944, during the withdrawal from the lower Dnieper bend, where three of its grenadier battalions were destroyed. That August, it was encircled west of the lower Dnieper and was virtually destroyed at Jassy, Romania, in early September. Those few soldiers who managed to escape were sent to Division Group 387, and the 258th Infantry was disbanded.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第258步兵师于1941年中期进入俄罗斯，参加了布列斯特、比亚韦斯托克、鲍里斯拉夫、叶连纳和维亚兹马-布良斯克等地的战斗，以及莫斯科周围的战役。该师继续在中央集团军群服役至1943年夏末，并参与了尤克诺夫、格沙茨克和奥廖尔的防御战。它还参加了库尔斯克攻势。在从库尔斯克和奥廖尔撤退期间，该师保卫了第9集团军位于克罗马的补给站，抵挡住了重重困难，击退了15次主要苏联进攻，并挫败了俄罗斯夺取补给站的企图。同年晚些时候，普鲁士师被转移到东线南部战区。它参加了米乌斯河和第聂伯河的撤退行动，在1943年10月时已处于战斗群规模。该师参与了尼科波尔桥头堡的战斗，并在1944年3月从第聂伯河弯曲部撤退期间被击溃，其中三个掷弹兵营被消灭。同年8月，它在下第聂伯河西侧被包围，在罗马尼亚雅西几乎全军覆没。少数成功逃脱的士兵被派往第387师群，而第258步兵师则解散。<cr>德国战斗序列 第1-290步兵师在二战中的表现<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text:
The 258th Soviet Rifle Division, a Uzbek National Division, started forming on the 10th July, 1941, with resources from the Central Asia Military District. On the 15th August it was assigned to the 50th Army (Commander A Yermakov executed for dereliction of duty in November), fought with some good fortune and distinction at Bryansk, Roslavl and Tula and by January 1942 was redesignated the 12th Guards Rifle Division. 

The division was recreated for a second time and by the middle of 1942 it was assigned to the 5th Tank Army. By the end of the year it was assigned to the 24th Army, Don Front, and fought at Stalingrad.

It ended the war assigned to the 25th Army of the Far Eastern Front.<cr><cr>

第258苏联步兵师，一个乌兹别克民族师，于1941年7月10日开始在中亚军区组建。8月15日被分配给第50集团军（指挥官A·叶尔马科夫因玩忽职守罪于11月被执行枪决），该师在布良斯克、罗斯拉夫利和图拉等地作战，表现出色，并于1942年1月被重新指定为第12近卫步兵师。

text: The 25th Cavalry Division was a mounted division of the Red Army that served for just over a year in the Great Patriotic War. It was formed in the summer of 1941 and served in the region south and west of Leningrad during the following months against the advance of Army Group North during Operation Barbarossa. It survived a German armored counterattack before being pulled back into the reserves in September. In January 1942, it was assigned to the Mobile Group of 2nd Shock Army to take part in the Lyuban Offensive Operation. This offensive aimed to encircle and destroy the German forces besieging Leningrad; in the event, 2nd Shock was itself encircled and forced to break out as individuals and small groups from May into July. The 25th Cavalry was disbanded, and its survivors were used to help rebuild the badly depleted 19th Guards Rifle Division, while the 25th's commanding officer took over the latter division.<cr><cr>
translation: 第25骑兵师是苏联红军在伟大卫国战争中服役超过一年的马步师。该师于1941年夏季组建，并在接下来几个月内，在列宁格勒南部和西部地区对抗北方集团军群发起的巴巴罗萨行动进攻。它经受住了一次德国装甲反攻后，于9月被撤至预备队。<cr>1942年1月，该师被分配给第2突击集团军机动部队，参与卢班攻势作战。此次攻势旨在包围并消灭围困列宁格勒的德军；最终，第2突击集团军自身遭到合围，并从5月至7月间被迫以个人和小分队形式突围。<cr>第25骑兵师被解散，其幸存者用于帮助重建严重减员的第19近卫步兵师，而该师指挥官则接管了后者。<cr>第25骑兵师<cr><cr>

text: The 25th Guards Rifle Division was formed in the period from 24 April 1942 to 12 July 1942, pursuant to Directive GShKA N org/2/783669 on 16 April 1942, by converting the 2nd Guards Rifle Brigade, ex 71st Naval Rifle Brigade, station Sonkovo, Kalinin region. 1112 July 1942 the Division left the place of formation for the Voronezh Front, arrived in the front, and from 22 July 1942 until 4 August 1942 it built the defence line on the eastern bank of the river Bityug. Participated in the battles to establish a bridgehead on the river Don north of the city Korotoyak in August 1942, Ostrogozh-Rossoshanskij, Voronezh-Kastornoye, Kharkov offensive and defensive operations. It took part in the operations to take cities of Budapest and Bratislava.<cr><cr>
translation: 第25近卫步兵师成立于1942年4月24日至7月12日，根据总参谋部于1942年4月16日发布的GShKA N org/2/783669号指令，由原海军步兵旅（第71海军步兵旅）改编而成，驻地为加里宁区的松科沃。1942年7月11日至12日期间，该师离开组建地点前往沃罗涅日方面军，并于8月抵达前线。从1942年7月22日至8月4日，它在比图格河东岸构筑了防御工事线。参与了1942年8月在科托亚克以北顿河上建立桥头堡的战斗、奥斯特罗戈热-罗斯霍斯卡耶、沃罗涅日-卡斯托诺耶攻势和哈尔科夫防御行动。它还参加了夺取布达佩斯和布拉迪斯拉发城市的作战行动。<cr><cr>

text: The 25th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 25th Light Division. In March of 1943 the division was sent from Hungary to join the Hungarian Occupation Group assigned to security duties in occupied Russia. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 25th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 25th Infantry Division. In January of 1944 the Hungarian First Army to which the division was then subordinate, mobilized to defend Hungary's northern Carpathian frontier against the advancing Red Army. In August 1944 the division was part of a reactivated Hungarian Second Army defending Northern Transylvania from the invading Red Army. The division was disbanded in April 1945.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第25匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖两个步兵团（每个团有三个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有七个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多东线兵力，大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本没有变化。该旅更名为第25轻型师。1943年3月，该师从匈牙利调往匈牙利占领集团，负责在被占领的俄罗斯执行治安任务。斯大林格勒战役后，为重组匈牙利军队，第25轻型师与其他部队合并，并更名为第25步兵师。1944年1月，在该师隶属下的匈牙利第一集团军动员起来，以防御进逼的红军。1944年8月，该师成为重新组建的匈牙利第二集团军的一部分，负责在北特兰西瓦尼亚抵御入侵的红军。该师于1945年4月解散。<cr>资料来源：Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, 《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利陆军》<cr>@@"条目由Chris Munson提供"

text: The 25th Mechanized Corps was formed in March 1941 at Kharkov in the Kharkov Military District. The corps included the 50th and 55th Tank Divisions, and the 219th Motorized Division. The 50th Tank Division was formed at Kharkov, the 55th at Chuguyev, and the 219th Motorized Division at Akhtyrka. The corps was commanded by Major General Semyon Krivoshein.<cr>The 25th Mechanized Corps was part of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command on 22 June 1941. Between 24 and 29 June it deployed by rail to the Kiev region. The corps was originally to support the 19th Army and was assigned to it on 30 June. The corps was slow in deploying forward from Kharkov. As a result, the 23rd Mechanized Corps supported the 19th Army instead. During the first half of July, it was assigned to support the 21st Army to replace the mechanized corps destroyed in the border battles. Between 3 and 8 July the corps moved to the Novozybkov region. The corps included 163 older model tanks on 1 July (6 BT tanks and 157 T-26 tanks) and was reinforced by 64 T-34 medium tanks by 13 July. On 13 July, the corps was ordered to concentrate the 219th Motorized Division in the Rudnia, Borkhov, and Pribor region, 15 to 25 kilometers to the west of Gomel. The 50th Tank Division was to attack along the Bykhov and Bobruisk axis from its positions. 300 tanks of the corps launched heavy unsuccessful attacks in cooperation with the 67th Rifle Corps against Heinz Guderian's forces south of Bykhov.<cr>On 16 July, the corps was in the Krichev area, according to Western Front commander Semyon Timoshenko. On 18 July, the 50th Tank Division was in the Voshchanka and Aleshnia region, 40 to 50 kilometers wast of Rogachev and 15 to 20 kilometers east of Dovsk, according to Timoshenko's situation report. Its 10-tank detachment and a motorized company had reportedly destroyed 70-80 wheeled vehicles, 10 tanks, and killing up to 500 German soldiers in the Mahsevskaya Sloboda region from 17 July. The 219th Motorized Division was in the Chechersk and Voronovka area. The 55th Tank Division was at Novozybkov. According to Timoshenko's 21 July report, the corps was attacking. The 50th Tank Division was on the southern outskirts of Obidovichi, the 219th Motorized Division was unsuccessfully attempting to capture Maly Propoysk with its motor rifle regiment, and the 55th Tank Division was still at Novozybkov. On 22 July the corps was ordered to capture Propoysk. On 23 July it was fighting for Propoysk. The corps suffered heavy losses in its attacks and regrouped on 24 July. Between 25 and 27 July it resumed the offensive. The corps shifted back to defense on 31 July. On 10 August, the 55th Tank Division became the 8th and 14th Separate Tank Battalions. On 14 August a Stavka directive ordered the corps command and control units along with those of the 20th Rifle Corps to form the Bryansk Front headquarters.<cr><cr>
translation:
第25机械化军于1941年3月在哈尔科夫的哈尔科夫军区成立。该军包括第50坦克师、第55坦克师和第219摩托化师。第50坦克师在哈尔科夫组建，第55坦克师在丘古耶夫组建，第219摩托化师在阿赫图尔卡组建。该军由少将谢苗·克里沃舍因指挥。

<cr>第25机械化军是最高统帅部预备队的一部分，在1941年6月22日属于轴心国一方。从6月24日至29日，该军通过铁路部署到基辅地区。最初该军是为了支援第19集团军而组建，并于6月30日被分配给它。由于从哈尔科夫向前推进缓慢，因此由第23机械化军代替支援第19集团军。在7月上半月，该军被分配去支援第21集团军以替换在边境战斗中被消灭的机械化军。从7月3日至8日，该军转移到诺沃兹比科夫地区。到7月1日，该军包括163辆较旧型号坦克（其中包含6辆BT坦克和157辆T-26坦克），并在7月13日前得到64辆T-34中型坦克的增援。

在7月13日，该军被命令将第219摩托化师集中到鲁德尼亚、博尔科夫和普里博尔地区，在戈梅利以西15至25公里处。第50坦克师从其位置出发沿比霍夫和鲍里斯方向发动攻击。该军的300辆坦克与第67步兵军合作，对海因茨·古德里安在比霍夫南部的力量发起了沉重但未成功的进攻。<cr>7月16日，根据西方面军司令谢苗·铁木辛哥的报告，该军位于克里切夫地区。7月18日，第50坦克师位于沃什昌卡和亚列什尼亚地区，距离罗加乔夫以西40至50公里，距多夫斯克以东15至20公里，根据铁木辛哥的情报报告，该师的一个拥有10辆坦克的分队以及一个摩托化连在马赫塞夫斯卡亚村区域从7月17日开始摧毁了70到80辆轮式车辆、10辆坦克，并击毙多达500名德国士兵。第219摩托化师位于切彻尔斯克和沃罗诺夫卡地区，第55坦克师位于诺沃兹比科夫。根据铁木辛哥7月21日的报告，该军正在发动进攻。第50坦克师在奥比多维奇以南郊区，第219摩托化师试图用其摩托步兵团夺取马里普罗波伊斯克但未成功，而第55坦克师仍位于诺沃兹比科夫。7月22日该军接到命令要占领普罗波伊斯克。7月23日该军在争夺普罗波伊斯克。该军在进攻中遭受了重大损失，并于7月24日重新集结。从7月25日至27日，该军恢复攻势。7月31日该军转为防御态势。8月10日，第55坦克师被改编为第8和第14独立坦克营。8月14日，最高统帅部下达命令要求该军司令部及控制单位与第20步兵军的相应单位一起组建布良斯克方面军司令部。<cr><cr>第55坦克师于7月31日被改编为第8和第14独立坦克营。8月14日，最高统帅部下达命令要求该军司令部及控制单位与第20步兵军的相应单位一起组建布良斯克方面军司令部。<cr><cr>

text: The 25th Motorized Division was sent to the Russian Front in June 1941, and served on the central sector for the next three years. It fought in the 2nd Panzer Group's battles at Zhitomir, Uman, Kiev, Bryansk, and Tula (south of Moscow). It spent January 1942 to June 1943 in the Bryansk/Orel sector, took heavy casualties at Kursk in July, and fought at Smolensk in October 1943. Meanwhile, on June 23, 1943, it was redesignated the 25th Panzer Grenadier Division. From November 1943 to June 1944, it held part of 4th Army's sector near Orscha. In the summer of 1944, the 25th Panzer Grenadier suffered heavy losses in the encirclement east of Minsk. The parts of the division which escaped were assigned to the 107th Panzer Brigade.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第25摩托化师于1941年6月被派往俄罗斯方面军，并在接下来的三年里驻守中央战线。它参加了第2装甲集群在日托米尔、乌曼、基辅、布良斯克和图拉（莫斯科以南）的战斗。从1942年1月至1943年6月，该师驻扎在布良斯克/奥廖尔地区，在1943年7月库尔斯克战役中伤亡惨重，并于1943年10月参加了斯摩棱斯克的战斗。与此同时，第25摩托化师于1943年6月23日被改编为第25装甲掷弹兵师。从1943年11月至1944年6月，该师驻守在奥尔沙附近的第4集团军战区的一部分。1944年夏天，在明斯克以东的包围圈中，第25装甲掷弹兵师遭受了重大损失。逃脱的部分被分配给第107装甲旅。<cr>德国战斗序列 第3卷 - 二战中的德军装甲、装甲掷弹兵和武装党卫军师萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: At the outbreak of hostilities, the corps was part of 19th Army deployed near Kiev. It comprised the 127th, 134th and 162nd Rifle Divisions. The army was assigned to Western Front and participated in the Battle of Smolensk. At this time, Hero of the Soviet Union Alexander Gorbatov was deputy commander, having just been rehabilitated after a 1936 sentence in the Gulag for 'counter-revolutionary activities'. The corps was dissolved in July 1941. It was briefly reformed in August and served as the basis of 52nd Army in Southwest Front. The corps was reformed once again in February 1943 as part of 69th Army and consisted of 4th and 41st Rifle Divisions and 77th Guards Rifle Division. It participated in the Lvov-Sandomierz Operation and the Carpathian Offensive in 1944 and the Vistula-Oder Offensive and the Berlin Strategic Offensive in 1945. <cr><cr><cr><cr> <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 在冲突爆发时，该军隶属于部署在基辅附近的第19集团军。它包括第127步兵师、第134步兵师和第162步兵师。该集团军被分配给西方方面军，并参加了斯摩棱斯克战役。此时，苏联英雄亚历山大·戈尔巴托夫是副指挥官，刚刚在古拉格服刑8年后因“反革命活动”而平反。该军于1941年7月解散，在同年8月短暂重组并成为西南方面军第52集团军的基础。该军再次于1943年2月作为第69集团军的一部分重建，包括第4步兵师、第41步兵师和第77近卫步兵师。它参加了1944年的利沃夫-桑多梅日进攻战役和喀尔巴阡山脉攻势以及1945年的维斯瓦河—奥得河攻势和柏林战略进攻行动。<cr>指挥官报告：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军在伟大卫国战争中的战斗序列, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 25th Rifle Division was formed in 1918 at the beginning of the Russian Civil War. Shortly after the start of Operation Barbarossa in June 1941 Stavka Order #20466 attached the 25th Rifle Division to the 14th Rifle Corps, 9th Army, Southern Front. It took part in the Siege of Odessa and was evacuated by sea in October 1941 prior to the city's fall. The division arrived in Sevastopol in time to prepare for the defence of the port against the oncoming German offensive. The division was destroyed during the following Siege of Sevastopol in July 1942. The division was subsequently reformed in the Arkhangelsk Military District in 1943. It did not see any further action in the Second World War.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第25步兵师成立于1918年，即俄罗斯内战初期。巴巴罗萨行动开始后不久，在1941年6月，最高统帅部命令第20466号令将第25步兵师编入第14步兵军、第9集团军、南方方面军。<cr>该师参加了敖德萨围城战，并于1941年10月在城市陷落前经海路撤出。随后，该师及时抵达塞瓦斯托波尔，准备防御港口以应对即将到来的德国攻势。<cr>第25步兵师在接下来的塞瓦斯托波尔围城战中被消灭，时间是1942年7月。<cr>该师于1943年在阿尔汉格尔斯克军区重建。它没有再参加第二次世界大战中的任何行动。<cr>词条提供：克里斯·芒森

text:
The 25th Tank Corps was formed in June 1942 in the Moscow Military District.<cr>The 25th Tank Corps moved to Bryansk Front area at Voronezh in late June and then, on 5 July, was assigned to 5th Tank Army. The 25th was roughly handled in the tank battles around Voronezh, but not caught up in the German advance to the Don and the Volga Rivers. Instead, 25th Tank Corps remained in the Voronezh area until December, when it was shifted south and took part in the 'Malyy Saturn' Operation with 1st Guards Army. By January 1943 the 25th Tank Corps was part of Southwestern Front's Mobile Group with additional supporting units.<cr>Unfortunately, between the continuous advances and fighting from December to February and Manstein's counterattack in late February and March 1943, 25th Tank Corps suffered almost 90% losses and in March 1943, went into STAVKA Reserves to be rebuilt and refitted. In July, the corps went back into action with 11th Guards Army in the Bryansk Front.<cr>The 25th Tank Corps fought only briefly in the summer offensives that started in July-August after Kursk, and by late August was back in reserve in the Moscow Military District. There it remained until October 1943, probably reequipping all the tank brigades with T-34 tanks in 3 tank battalions each. In late October 1943 it was sent to 1st Ukrainian Front, with which it remained for the rest of the war. At that time the corps included additional supporting units.<cr>In the fighting after the liberation of Kiev on the right bank of the Dnepr 25th Tank Corps fought under 13th and 60th Armies west of Kiev. By March 1944 the corps' SU regiments had been changed.<cr>The 25th Tank Corps was part of 1st Cavalry Mechanized Group for the
Lvov-Sandomir Operation in July 1944. In September 1944 the corps received 296th Guards Light Artillery Regiment (24 76mm guns) At the end of 1944, as the Front prepared for the Vistula-Oder Operation, 25th Tank Corps converted 746th Antitank Battalion into the 746th Heavy SU Regiment (ISU-122s).<cr>As a result of the operations in January 1945 that advanced the corps to the Oder River, the 746th was redesignated as 262nd Guards Heavy SU Regiment. This was the last change in organization made to the corps during the war. 25th Tank Corps ended the war in May 1945 near Berlin, after taking part in the Berlin Operation in the first echelon of 1st Ukrainian Front.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第25坦克军于1942年6月在莫斯科军区组建。该部队于6月下旬转移到沃罗涅日的布良斯克方面军区域，并于7月5日被分配给第5坦克集团军。<cr>第25坦克军在沃罗涅日附近的坦克战斗中遭受重创，但没有卷入德国向顿河和伏尔加河推进的攻势。相反，该坦克军一直留在沃罗涅日地区直到12月，并于此时被转移到南方并参加了“小土星行动”，与第1近卫集团军协同作战。<cr>到1943年1月，第25坦克军成为西南方面军机动部队的一部分，并有额外的支援单位。遗憾的是，在从12月至次年2月连续推进和战斗期间以及曼施坦因在1943年2月下旬至3月发起反攻时，该坦克军遭受了近90%的损失，并于1943年3月进入最高统帅部大本营预备队进行重建。<cr>7月，该部队与第11近卫集团军一起在布良斯克方面军投入战斗。它仅短暂参与了从7月至8月开始的夏季攻势，在8月下旬又回到了莫斯科军区的预备队中。<cr>直到1943年10月，它可能一直在为每个坦克营配备T-34坦克，并于该月被派往第1乌克兰方面军。此后，该部队一直留在那里直至战争结束，并包括额外的支援单位。<cr>在解放基辅后，在第聂伯河右岸作战期间，第25坦克军隶属于第13集团军和第60集团军，位于基辅以西地区。到1944年3月，该部的SU团已经进行了调整。第25坦克军于1944年7月在利沃夫-桑多尔行动期间隶属于第1机械化骑兵集团。1944年9月，该军接收了第296近卫轻炮兵团（装备有24门76毫米火炮）。到1944年底，随着方面军为维斯瓦河-奥得河行动做准备，第25坦克军将第746反坦克营改编为第746重型自行火炮团（ISU-122）。<cr>由于1945年1月的作战行动推进该军到达奥德河畔，第746团被重新指定为第262近卫重型自行火炮团。这是战争期间该军组织上的最后一次变更。第25坦克军于1945年5月在柏林附近结束战争，在第一次梯队中参与了第一乌克兰方面军的柏林行动。<cr>苏联二战战斗序列 第二卷作者：查尔斯·C·夏普

50th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Tank Battalions, equipped as above
25th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
25th Howitzer Regiment
25th Reconnaissance Battalion
25th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
25th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>This division, along with the rest of 13th Mechanized Corps, was 'completely understrength' on 22 June 1941, according to the Western Front's deputy commander. 25th Tank Division was the best equipped unit in 13th mech, but it only had 247 T-26 tanks, most in dire need of major repairs. The reconnaissance
battalion was missing trucks and motorcycles, and antiaircraft battalion had no equipment or weapons. While the howitzer regiment was fully equipped with guns, it had almost no trucks or tractors to pull them, and the gun crews were all away in training camps when the Germans attacked! The division was directly in front of 2nd Panzer Group's advance south of Minsk, and was officially disbanded on 4 July 1941 - one of the first divisions stricken from the Red Army order of battle, in the war.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第25坦克师成立于1941年2月至4月，在西方特别军区的戈梅利，由第44轻型坦克旅改编而成，并隶属于第13机械化军：<cr>
第49坦克团
第1、2、3、4坦克营
每个营 = 两个连，每连配备17辆T-26 + 1辆HQT-26，共35辆坦克/营
第50坦克团
第1、2、3坦克营，装备同上
第25摩托化步兵师
第1、2、3营
第25榴弹炮团
第25侦察营
第25机械化舟桥营
第25防空营<cr><cr>根据西方方面军副指挥官的说法，在1941年6月22日，包括该师在内的整个第13机械化军都“严重缺员”。尽管第25坦克师是第13机械化军中装备最好的单位，但它只有247辆T-26坦克，大多数急需大修。侦察营缺少卡车和摩托车，防空营没有任何设备或武器。虽然榴弹炮团完全配备了火炮，但几乎没有卡车或拖拉机来牵引这些火炮，并且炮兵部队都在训练营中接受培训！该师直接位于明斯克以南的第2装甲集团军进攻路线前，在1941年7月4日被正式解散——这是战争初期从红军战斗序列中撤销的第一个师之一。<cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普著《苏联战斗序列 第一卷》

text: he 260th Infantry Division was formed from reserve units in August 1939 as part of the 4th Wave during the general mobilization of the German Army. Its soldiers came from Baden and Wrttemberg. It contained the 460th, 470th and 480th Infantry Regiments, 260th Artillery Regiment and various support units. In October 1939 it was sent to the Upper Rhine and spent most of the Battle of France in OKH reserve. The division was on occupation duty in France until July of 1941 when it was sent to the Eastern Front.<cr>In the summer of 1943 the 470th Grenadier Regiment (most infantry regiments in the German Army by this point were designated grenadier regiments) was disbanded after heavy losses and an additional battery composed of five captured Russian 152mm howitzers joined the artillery regiment. In April 1944 the 470th Grenadier Regiment was reformed and the division now consisted of three regiments with two battalions each plus a divisional fusilier battalion. The division was surrounded and destroyed in the Minsk Offensive and never reformed.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, German Order of Battle Volume I: 1st-290th Infantry Divisions in WWII<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第260步兵师于1939年8月由预备部队组建，作为德国陆军总动员第四波的一部分。其士兵来自巴登和符腾堡地区。该师包括第460、470和480步兵团，第260炮兵团以及各种支援单位。1939年10月，该师被派往上莱茵河，并在法国战役期间大部分时间处于陆军总司令部预备队状态。直到1941年7月，该师一直在法国执行占领任务。<cr>1943年夏天，由于遭受严重损失，第470掷弹兵团被解散，炮兵连增加了一个由5门缴获的苏联152毫米榴弹炮组成的炮兵连。1944年4月，第470掷弹兵团重建，该师现在包括三个团，每个团有两个营，另有一个师属步枪营。<cr>在明斯克攻势中，该师被包围并被消灭，从未重建。<cr>资料来源：George F. Nafziger，《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham，《二战中的德国战斗序列第一卷：第1至290步兵师》<cr>感谢Chris Munson提供条目

text:
The 260th Rifle Division started forming on the 2nd July 1941 at Kalinin and on the 15th August was assigned to the 50th Army, Bryansk Front. The division was trapped in the Bryansk pocket and whilst 1000 men escaped the division was officially disbanded by the 17th November, 1941. 

The division was raised for the 2nd time at Volokolamsk near Moscow, from the 55th Rifle Brigade, in May 1942. In September it was assigned to the Don Front where the commander was demoted for lack of military success. It fought with some success at Stalingrad. In July 1943 it fought at Bryansk, Gomel and assisted in the capture of Kovel.

In 1944 The Division fought in Operation Bagration, in the capture of Warsaw and Berlin and ended the war assigned to the 77th Rifle Corps near Berlin.

A distinguished Division , it had been awarded the honorific of 'KOVEL', Order of the Red Banner and Order of Suvorov.



 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 


Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第260步兵师于1941年7月2日在加里宁开始组建，并于8月15日被分配给布良斯克方面军的第50集团军。该师被困在布良斯克包围圈内，尽管有1000名士兵逃脱，但该师还是于1941年11月17日正式解散。

该师于1942年5月在莫斯科附近的沃尔科拉姆斯克从第55步兵旅重新组建。同年9月被分配给顿河方面军，在此期间指挥官因军事成绩不佳而被降职。该师在斯大林格勒的战斗中取得了一定的成功。1943年7月，它参加了布良斯克、戈梅利的战斗，并协助占领了科韦尔。

1944年，该师参与了巴格拉季昂行动，在华沙和柏林的攻占中发挥了作用，并在战争结束时被分配给第77步兵军，驻扎在柏林附近。

这是一支杰出的部队，曾获得“科韦尔”荣誉称号、红旗勋章和苏沃洛夫勋章。

text:
The 261st Rifle Division began forming on 18 July 1941 at Berdiansk in the Odessa Military District. It was made up from a combination of reservists, militia, and volunteers, and its basic order of battle was as follows:

974th Rifle Regiment
976th Rifle Regiment
978th Rifle Regiment
809th Artillery Regiment<cr>
The division went into Southern Front in August, first as part of 6th Army, but was reassigned to 12th Army, in the same Front, by September 1. It remained with that Army up to at least August 1942 but then was assigned to the Transcaucasian Front's Black Sea Group of Forces. It then spent much of the later part of World War II, from January 1, 1943,[8] onwards with the small 45th Army of the Transcaucasian Front, which was guarding the Soviet borders with Turkey.<cr><cr>

第978步兵团

text: The 262nd Infantry Division was formed in August 1939 from Austrian reservists as part of the 4th Wave. It contained the 462nd, 482nd and 486th Infantry Regiments, 262nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 262nd Artillery Regiment and various support units. The division was stationed in the Saar during the Polish Campaign. The division remained there until after the fall of France in 1940.<>The division was part of the IV Army Corps in Army Group South at the start of Operation Barbarossa. By early 1943 the infantry regiments were reduced from three to two battalions each and the artillery regiment added a Nebelwerfer battery. The division fought in the Battle of Kursk and suffered heavy casualties. In February 1944 the division was disbanded and most elements combined with other units to form 'D' Corps Detachment and the remainder of the division was distributed to other units throughout the Army.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, German Order of Battle Volume I: 1st-290th Infantry Divisions in WWII<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第262步兵师成立于1939年8月，由奥地利预备役人员组成，属于第四波组建部队。该师包括第462团、第482团和第486团，第262侦察营，第262炮兵团以及各种支援单位。在波兰战役期间，该师驻扎在萨尔地区，并一直留在那里直到1940年法国沦陷之后。<cr>巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师隶属于南方集团军群的第四军。到1943年初，步兵团从三个营缩减为两个营，炮兵团增加了一个喷烟者火箭炮连。该师参加了库尔斯克战役，并遭受了严重伤亡。1944年2月，该师被解散，大部分单位与其它部队合并组成“D”军直属队，其余部分则分配到集团军的其他单位。<cr><cr><cr>乔治·F·纳夫齐格，《二战德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>塞缪尔·W·米查姆，《二战德国战斗序列第一卷：第1至第290师》<cr><cr>克里斯·芒森提供

text: The 262nd Rifle Division began forming at Vladimir in the Moscow Military District as the 16th NKVD Mountain Division on 26 June 1941. It used 1,500 NKVD troops as a cadre, and was transferred to the Red Army as the 262nd Rifle Division before 10 July. Without completing its formation, on the night of 19-20 July the division was moved to the Mozhaysk area as part of the Reserve Front's 33rd Army. A week later it was transferred to the Northwestern Front's 34th Army. Later that month, it suffered heavy losses in the Staraya Russa counterattack.<cr><cr>In the second half of October, it moved east to the Kalinin Front's 31st Army, which was preparing for the Soviet winter counteroffensive in the Battle of Moscow. The division fought in the Kalinin Defensive Operation and the Kalinin Offensive during the winter campaign.<cr><cr>In 1943 it became part of the 43rd Army. Until 15 September, the division fought in defensive battles near Demidov, then fought in the Dukhovshchina-Demidov Offensive. The division remained with the Kalinin Front, which became the 1st Baltic Front on 20 October. In October and November, the 262nd fought in the advance on Vitebsk during the Belorussian Strategic Offensive as part of the army's 1st Rifle Corps. It then defended positions on the approaches to Vitebsk, rejoining the 39th Army on 15 December.<cr><cr>The army became part of the 3rd Belorussian Front for Operation Bagration in June 1944, and remained with the front until April 1945. On 23 June 1944, at the start of Operation Bagration, it was part of the army's 84th Rifle Corps. It subsequently advanced into Lithuania during the Vilnius Offensive and the Kaunas Offensive during the summer. On 12 August the 262nd was awarded the Order of Suvorov 2nd class for its actions in the capture of Kaunas. The division fought in the Memel Offensive in October. From January 1945, the division moved into East Prussia, attacking towards Tilsit in the Insterburg-Koenigsberg Offensive. The division spent the last months of the war in the Samland Group of Forces near Konigsberg.<cr><cr>In April, the division and the rest of the 39th Army were withdrawn to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command and moved to the Soviet Far East in May and June in preparation for the Soviet invasion of Manchuria. The 262nd was transported to the Choibalsan area by rail, then marched 400 kilometres (250 mi) to concentration areas south of Tamsagbulag. At the beginning of the invasion on 9 August, the division was part of the 39th Army's 113th Rifle Corps in the Transbaikal Front. The 262nd fought in the Khingan-Mukden Offensive Operation of the invasion.<cr><cr>
translation: 第262步兵师于1941年6月26日在莫斯科军区的弗拉基米尔开始组建，最初为内务人民委员部（NKVD）第16山地师。该师使用了1,500名内务人民委员部部队作为骨干，并在7月10日前转隶红军，成为第262步兵师。尚未完成编组的该师于7月19日至20日夜间被调往莫扎伊斯克地区，加入预备方面军第33集团军。一周后又被转移到西北方面军第34集团军。当月晚些时候，在斯大利亚罗斯卡反攻中遭受了重大损失。<cr><cr>在十月的下半段，该师向东转移至加里宁方面军第31集团军，后者正在为莫斯科战役中的苏联冬季反攻做准备。该师参加了加里宁防御行动和加里宁进攻行动，在冬季战役期间作战。<cr><cr>1943年，该师成为第43集团军的一部分。直到9月15日，该师在德米多夫附近进行防御战斗，随后参加杜霍夫什奇纳-德米多夫攻势。该师继续留在加里宁方面军内，后者于10月20日改名为第一波罗的海方面军。<cr><cr>在十月和十一月期间，第262步兵师参加了白俄罗斯战略进攻中的维捷布斯克推进行动，并作为集团军的第一步兵军的一部分作战。随后该师保卫了接近维捷布斯克地区的阵地，并于12月15日重新加入第39集团军。<cr>该师于1944年6月成为第3白俄罗斯方面军的一部分，参与巴格拉季昂行动，并一直留在该方面军直到1945年4月。在巴格拉季昂行动开始时的1944年6月23日，它隶属于集团军的第84步兵军。随后，在夏季期间，该师参加了维尔纽斯进攻和考纳斯进攻。1944年8月12日，由于夺取考纳斯的表现，第262师被授予苏沃罗夫勋章二级奖章。该师在10月份参与了梅梅尔攻势。从1945年1月开始，该师进入东普鲁士，在因斯特堡-柯尼斯堡攻势中向提格里斯推进。战争最后几个月里，该师驻扎在靠近柯尼斯堡的萨姆兰集团军群附近。<cr><cr>4月份，第262师和其余第39集团军被调往最高统帅部预备队，并于5月和6月转移到苏联远东地区，为苏联入侵满洲做准备。第262师通过铁路运送到楚鲁巴尔桑地区，然后行军400公里（250英里）到达坦萨格布尔加以南的集结区。<cr><cr>在8月9日入侵开始时，该师隶属于第39集团军的第113步兵军，在外贝加尔方面军。第262师参加了入侵期间的兴安-沈阳进攻作战。<cr><cr>

text: The 263rd Infantry Division was formed in August 1939 as part of the 4th Wave. It contained the 463rd, 483rd and 485th Infantry Regiments, 263rd Artillery Regiment and various support units. The division was part of the IX Army Corps in Army Group Centre at the start of Operation Barbarossa. In April 1943 the 483rd Grenadier Regiment (most infantry regiments in the German Army by this point were designated grenadier regiments) was disbanded and its two battaltions added to the other two regiments in the division so that each now had three battalions. By this time the division also had two companies of Ost infantry from the 263rd Ost Battalion assigned to it. In May 1944 the 483rd Grenadier Regiment was reformed by taking one battalion from each of the other two regiments so that the division now had three regiments with two battalions each. The division surrendered to the Russians in Courland in May 1945.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation:
第263步兵师成立于1939年8月，属于第四波组建的部队。该师包括第463、483和485步兵团，第263炮兵团以及各种支援单位。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师隶属于中央集团军群下的第九军。

1943年4月，第483掷弹兵团（此时德国陆军中的大多数步兵团都已改称为掷弹兵团）被解散，其两个营分别加入另外两个团中，使得每个团都有三个营。到这个时候，该师还从第263东方营分配了两个东方步兵连。

1944年5月，第483掷弹兵团重组，通过将其他两个团中的一个营抽调出来重新组建而成，这样该师现在有三个团，每个团有两个营。该师于1945年5月在库尔兰向苏联人投降。<cr>参考文献：George F. Nafziger,《二战期间德国战斗序列中的步兵》<cr>词条由Chris Munson提供

text: The 264th Rifle Division began forming on 10 July 1941 at Poltava in the Kharkov Military District. Its basic order of battle included the 1056th, 1058th, and the 1060th Rifle Regiments. The division was barely formed and lacked much of its equipment when it was sent to the front on nine trains at the end of July. By 30 July, it was taking positions defending the line of the Dnieper near Kaniv, south of Kiev. By 5 August, the 264th was part of the Southwestern Front's 26th Army. It was trapped in the Kiev pocket in early September and destroyed almost immediately in the pocket. The 264th was officially disbanded on 19 September.<cr><cr>The second formation of the 264th began forming in February 1942 in the Ural Military District, including the basic order of battle as the first formation. By the time its commander was assigned on 1 May, the division had been relocated to the Moscow Military District. In May, it was assigned to the Moscow Defence Zone for training, and in August the 264th joined the 3rd Tank Army, part of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command behind the Western Front near Moscow. The division was part of the army's mobile group for several front-level offensives in 1942, which occasionally stretched the German defenses but never broke through. Thus, these actions were mostly ignored by Soviet accounts. The division fought in heavy fighting through the fall of 1942 around Rzhev, Sychyovka, and Zhizdra. On 20 October 1942, it was converted into the 48th Guards Rifle Division for its actions.<cr><cr>The division was formed for a third time on 20 July 1943 with the 35th Army in the Far Eastern Front. It included the same rifle regiments as the previous formations, and spent the entire war with the 35th Army. On 8 August 1945, the army was with the 1st Far East Front for the Soviet invasion of Manchuria, which began the next day. While other units of the army engaged in a speedy advance through the Japanese line, the 264th spent the entire campaign systematically reducing Japanese fortifications in and around Hutou in conjunction with the 109th Fortified Region. By the end of the invasion, the 264th was so far behind the rest of the army that it was assigned to the 87th Rifle Corps in the front reserves. For its actions, the division was awarded the honorific 'Ussuri.'<cr><cr>
translation:
第264步兵师于1941年7月10日在哈尔科夫军区的波尔塔瓦开始组建。其基本战斗序列包括第1056、1058和1060步兵团。该师在7月底尚未完全形成，装备不足的情况下就被派往前线，分乘九列火车出发。到7月30日，它正在卡尼夫附近部署兵力，防御第聂伯河一线，位于基辅以南地区。至8月5日，第264步兵师成为西南方面军第26集团军的一部分。9月初被围困在基辅包围圈内，并几乎立即被消灭。该师于9月19日正式解散。

第二组建的第264步兵师从1942年2月开始在乌拉尔军区组建，包括与第一次组建相同的战斗序列。到5月1日指挥官任命时，该师已迁至莫斯科军区。5月份被分配给莫斯科防御区进行训练，并于8月加入第3坦克集团军，成为最高统帅部预备队的一部分，在西方面军后方靠近莫斯科地区。该师参加了1942年几次战线级别的进攻行动，这些行动偶尔会拉伸德国防线但从未突破成功。因此，苏联方面的记录大多忽略了这些行动。从1942年秋季开始，该师在列日、斯奇科夫卡和吉兹德拉地区进行了激烈的战斗。至1942年10月20日，由于其表现，第264步兵师被改编为第48近卫步兵师。该师于1943年7月20日第三次在远东方面军第35集团军内组建。它包括与前两次编组相同的步兵团，并在整个战争期间都隶属于第35集团军。<cr>1945年8月8日，该集团军随第1远东方面军参加苏联对满洲的入侵行动，次日开始进攻。<cr>在其他部队迅速突破日军防线的同时，第264师与第109要塞区协同作战，在整个战役期间系统地摧毁了胡头及其周边地区的日军工事。<cr>到入侵结束时，该师远远落后于集团军的其他单位，被分配给方面军预备队中的第87步兵军。<cr>指挥官报告：由于其行动，该师荣获“乌苏里”荣誉称谓。<cr> <cr>

text:
The 265th Rifle Division began forming on 26 June 1941 in the Moscow Military District as the 17th NKVD Mountain Division. It was one of the fifteen NKVD divisions that began forming on 26 June and was transferred to the Red Army in early July. The 265th, whose major subunits included the 450th, 941st, and 951st Rifle Regiments, the 798th Artillery Regiment, and the 224th Anti-Tank Battalion, remained in the Moscow Military District at least until 10 July, and later that month moved to Leningrad with a 1500-man cadre of NKVD personnel. In early August it joined the 23rd Army, fighting in the Continuation War north of Leningrad on the Karelian Isthmus. On 26 August, its first Red Army commander, Major Ivan Prytkov, was assigned to the division.


On 14 October, the division was transferred to the Neva River front, south of the city. In November it became part of the 8th Army, which was part of the Volkhov Front from early 1942. In November 1943, the 265th was withdrawn to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command and from February 1944 was either part of the Leningrad Front or the 3rd Baltic Front until the end of 1944. Between June and July, it was part of the 21st Army's 110th Rifle Corps for the Svir-Petrozavodsk Offensive on the Karelian Isthmus, which eventually forced Finland out of the war. In August the 265th became part of the 3rd Baltic reserves, and in October it was with the 3rd Shock Army's 7th Rifle Corps in the 2nd Baltic Front. Just before the Vistula-Oder Offensive began in January 1945, the division transferred to the 1st Belorussian Front. It fought in the advance through Poland and in the Battle of Berlin in April and May 1945. During the war, the division was awarded the honorific 'Vyborg'.<cr><cr>
translation:
第265步兵师于1941年6月26日在莫斯科军区开始组建，最初为内务人民委员部（NKVD）的第17山地师。它是从6月26日开始组建的十五个内务人民委员部师之一，并在7月初转隶红军。该师的主要下属单位包括第450、941和951步兵团，第798炮兵团以及第224反坦克营。至少到7月10日为止，该师一直驻扎在莫斯科军区；当月晚些时候，它带着一个由1500名内务人民委员部人员组成的骨干前往列宁格勒。8月初，该师加入北方列宁格勒以北卡累利阿地峡的继续战争中的第23集团军作战。

10月14日，该师被调往涅瓦河前线，位于城市南部。11月份，它成为第8集团军的一部分，而后者从1942年初开始隶属于沃尔霍夫方面军。1943年11月，第265步兵师撤至最高统帅部预备队，并于1944年2月至年底期间要么属于列宁格勒方面军，要么属于波罗的海第三方面军。

从6月到7月，该师隶属于第21集团军的第110步兵军，在卡累利阿地峡进行斯维里-彼得罗扎沃茨克攻势作战，最终迫使芬兰退出战争。8月份，第265步兵师成为波罗的海第三方面军预备队的一部分；10月，它隶属于第三突击集团军的第7步兵军，在波罗的海第二方面军中。

在1945年1月开始的维斯瓦河-奥得河攻势之前，该师被调往第一白俄罗斯方面军。它参加了波兰境内的推进作战，并于1945年4月至5月期间参与了柏林战役。在整个战争期间，该师获得了“ Vyborg ”这一荣誉称谓。
