text: The 266th was first formed between 26 June and 2 July 1941 at Kaluga in the Moscow Military District as the 26th NKVD Mountain Division. By 2 July, it was transferred to the Red Army as the 266th Rifle Division. In early August, the 266th joined the 21st Army of the Bryansk Front. In late August, the 2nd Panzer Group advanced south across the Desna River, breaking through the 21st Army. At this time the division was part of the army's 66th Rifle Corps and suffered heavy losses. It was disbanded on 30 August.<cr><cr>The 467th Rifle Division started forming in the Stalingrad Military District on 14 December 1941. On 22 December the division was redesignated as the 266th Rifle Division at Kuybyshev in the Volga Military District. After it was redesignated, the division was moved a short distance west to the Volga River area near Stalingrad. It remained there, forming and training under the Stalingrad Military District, until April 1942, when it was assigned to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (RVGK). In late April, the 266th joined the Southwestern Front's 6th Army. On 12 May, when the Kharkov offensive in the Second Battle of Kharkov began, the 266th was an assault unit and had the most success in its initial attacks. As a result, it was farther into the pocket when the German counterattack surrounded the army in the Izyum Pocket in late May. The division never made it out and the pocket was mopped up between 26 and 28 May. The 266th was officially disbanded on 30 May.<cr><cr>The 266th was reformed for a third time on 26 August 1942 in Kuybyshev Oblast, part of the Volga Military District. The 266th remained in the district until October, when it was assigned to the 4th Reserve Army in the Reserve of the Supreme High Command. On 10 November, the division went to the front with the army, which became the 2nd Guards Army and was assigned to the Southwestern Front. Just before it fought in Operation Little Saturn in December, the division transferred to the 3rd Guards Army's 14th Guards Rifle Corps.<cr><cr>In late February 1943, the division was with the 5th Tank Army. By the end of March 1943, it was back with the 3rd Guards Army. After April, the 266th was part of the 32nd Rifle Corps. On 5 September, the division fought in the recapture of Artemovsk during the Donbass Strategic Offensive, and it was later awarded the honorific 'Artemovsk'. In late October, the army became part of the 4th Ukrainian Front. On 13 February 1944, the division was awarded the Order of Suvorov, 2nd class. In late February, it was transferred to the 3rd Ukrainian Front's 6th Army with the 32nd Rifle Corps. The 266th became part of the 46th Army in March and transferred to front reserves in May. In June, it joined the 5th Shock Army. It fought in the Second JassyKishinev Offensive with the army and moved into the RVGK with the army in September.<cr><cr>In late October, the division transferred with the 26th Guards Rifle Corps to the 1st Belorussian Front, where it fought for the rest of the war. In January 1945, during the VistulaOder Offensive, the division loaded 30 men into each of its 18 US 2.5 ton trucks, added enough 'collected vehicle' to motorize most of the 1006th Rifle Regiment heavy weapons, and used this improvised motor rifle force to support tank units pursuing retreating German troops across Poland. By this time most of the division artillery had been motorized with half-tracks, including both Lend-Lease US M3A1s and captured German vehicles. The division fought in the Battle of Berlin from April 1945. In the battle, it was with the 5th Shock Army's 26th Guards Rifle Corps, part of the 1st Belorussian Front.<cr><cr>

text: The 267th Infantry Divison fought at Brest-Litovsk, Bialystok, Bobruisk, Yelnya, Vyazma, and north of Moscow. It suffered greatly in the Soviet winter offensive of 194142. The division had lost so many horses from the cold, the lack of supplies, and lack of fodder that when it did have to retreat on December 17, 1941, it had to leave all of its artillery behind. It nevertheless remained in the line and fought in the defensive battles of Gshatsk, Juchnov and Spass-Demensk in 1942. It remained in the Spass-Demensk sector until August 1943, when it was sent back to Bryansk in September. From October 1943 to June 1944, it defended Mogilev and fought in all the major battles of Army Group Center until July 1944. At that time it was encircled and smashed near Minsk, along with the bulk of the 4th Army. The remnants of the division were finally destroyed near Memel on August 13. Its last commander, Lieutenant General Otto Drescher, was killed that day. The Horsehead Division was officially declared dissolved shortly afterwards.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第267步兵师参加了别雷、比亚韦斯托克、鲍里斯波尔、叶连纳、维亚兹玛以及莫斯科北部的战斗。在1941至1942年的苏联冬季攻势中，该师遭受了巨大损失。由于严寒、补给不足和饲料短缺，该师失去了大量马匹，在1941年12月17日撤退时不得不留下所有炮兵装备。尽管如此，它仍然坚守在前线，并参加了1942年的格什茨克、尤赫诺夫和斯帕斯-德梅内斯克的防御战斗。该师一直驻守在斯帕斯-德梅内斯克地区，直到1943年8月才被调往布良斯克，于同年9月抵达。从1943年10月至1944年6月，它保卫了莫吉廖夫，并参加了中央集团军群的所有主要战役，直至1944年7月。此时，该师在明斯克附近被包围并摧毁，与第四集团军的大部分一同覆灭。该师残部最终于8月13日在梅梅尔附近被消灭。其最后一位指挥官奥托·德雷舍少将也在当天阵亡。马头师正式宣布解散不久之后。<cr><cr>德国战斗序列第1卷：二战中的第1至290步兵师，萨缪尔·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text:
The division began forming from reservists on 10 July 1941 at Stary Oskol, part of the Orel Military District. Its basic order of battle included the 844th, the 846th, and the 848th Rifle Regiments, as well as the 845th Artillery Regiment. By mid-August, the 268th had been assigned to the 52nd Army, defending the Volkhov River line near Leningrad, where it remained until early 1942. The division's positions were located in impassable swampy forests, and as a result it held a front of 34 kilometers in October 1941. From January 1942, the division fought in the Lyuban Offensive Operation, initially as part of the 2nd Shock Army Operations Group, attacking across the Volkhov. The Soviet attack achieved a breakthrough, and in February the 267th was transferred to General Korovnikov's Operational Mobile Group of the 59th Army, which was attempting to exploit the breakthrough by advancing into the rear of the German troops besieging Leningrad. A German counterattack in the spring cut off the 2nd Shock Army and the 59th Army, and the division was trapped in the swamps west of Volkhov. It took several months for the German forces to completely clear the pocket, but by 1 June the division had only 2687 men, 964 officers, and 773 non-commissioned officers. After the pocket was eliminated, the 267th was officially disbanded on 30 July 1942.

The division was reformed on 12 September 1942 at Serpukhov, part of the Moscow Military District, with the same basic order of battle as the previous division. In mid-September the 267th was transferred to the Moscow Defence Zone for training, and in late November it was sent to the front as part of the 6th Army of the Voronezh Front. At the end of 1942 the division moved south with the 6th Army to the Southwestern Front, and fought in the Soviet offensive in early 1943 towards Kharkov and the northern Donbass. The 267th remained with the 6th Army until September 1943, and was usually part of the 15th Rifle Corps. In September, the division was withdrawn to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (RVGK), but returned to the front a month later in the 28th Army of the 4th Ukrainian Front. It was transferred to the 5th Shock Army's 63rd Rifle Corps in November, and in January 1944 was withdrawn to the RVGK with the 63rd Corps.

In February, the corps and the 267th joined the 51st Army, with which they fought in the Crimean Offensive in May 1944. After the recapture of Crimea, the 51st Army became part of the RVGK and moved north to the 1st Baltic Front. By 27 July, the division was fighting at Siauliai during the Siauliai Offensive. On 15 August, the division was fighting off armored counterattacks from the Grossdeutschland Division and the 4th and 12th Panzer Divisions at Auce. From late August to the end of the war, the 267th was part of the army's 1st Guards Rifle Corps. In February 1945, the army transferred to the 2nd Baltic Front, and it spent the last weeks of the war blockading German troops trapped in the Courland Pocket.<cr><cr>
translation:
该师于1941年7月10日在奥廖尔军区的斯塔里奥斯科尔从预备役人员开始组建。其基本战斗序列包括第844、第846和第848步兵团，以及第845炮兵团。到八月中旬，第268师被分配给保卫列宁格勒附近沃尔霍夫河防线的第52集团军，并一直驻守至1942年初。该师的位置位于难以通行的沼泽森林中，在1941年10月时，其防御正面长达34公里。从1942年1月起，该师参加了卢班进攻战役，最初作为第2突击集团军作战小组的一部分，攻击越过沃尔霍夫河。苏联攻势取得了突破，2月份，第268师被转移到科罗文诺夫将军指挥的第59集团军机动部队中，后者试图利用这一突破向围困列宁格勒的德军后方推进。春季德国反攻切断了第2突击集团军和第59集团军，该师被困在沃尔霍夫西面的沼泽地中。德军花了数月时间才完全肃清包围圈，但到6月1日时，该师只剩下2687名士兵、964名军官和773名非委任军官。在包围圈被消灭后，第268师于1942年7月30日正式解散。

该师于1942年9月12日在莫斯科军区的瑟普霍夫重组，与之前的师拥有相同的战斗序列。九月中旬，第267师被转移到莫斯科防御区进行训练，并在十一月下旬作为沃罗涅日方面军第6集团军的一部分前往前线。到1942年底，该师随同第6集团军向西南方向移动，在1943年初的苏联攻势中参与了进攻哈尔科夫和北部顿巴斯地区的战斗。直到1943年9月，第267师一直隶属于第6集团军，并通常属于第15步兵军。九月份，该师被调往最高统帅部预备队（RVGK），但一个月后返回前线，成为第4乌克兰方面军第28集团军的一部分。十一月，该师转隶至第5突击集团军的第63步兵军，并于1944年1月再次被调回RVGK，随同第63步兵军。

二月，该军和第267师加入第51集团军，在其中参与了1944年5月的克里米亚攻势。在克里米亚重获控制后，第51集团军成为方面军预备队，并向北转移到波罗的海第一方面军。到7月27日，该师正在参加锡拉乌利斯攻势中的锡拉乌利斯战斗。8月15日，该师在奥采与大德意志装甲师和第4、第12装甲师进行反装甲反击作战。从八月末至战争结束，第267师成为集团军第一近卫步兵军的一部分。<cr>二月，该集团军转隶波罗的海第二方面军，并在最后几周内封锁了困于库尔兰包围圈中的德军部队。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 268th Infantry Division invaded Russia on June 22, 1941, and spent the rest of its career on the Russian Front. Here it fought in the Brest-Litovsk sector, at Bialystok, Smolensk, in the Battle of the Yelnya Bend, at Vyazma, before Moscow, against the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42, in the defensive actions of 1942, and in the Rzhev withdrawal. In the summer of 1943 it suffered such heavy losses in the Battle of Kursk and the associated retreat (including the battles of Bryansk and Mogilev) that it was down to battle group strength by October. It was downgraded to Division Group 268 on November 2, 1943. Simultaneously, it was attached to the 36th Motorized Division.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第268步兵师于1941年6月22日入侵俄罗斯，并在苏联方面军度过其整个服役生涯。该师曾在别雷-立陶宛、比亚韦斯托克、斯摩棱斯克作战，在叶连纳河弯战役中参战，还在维亚兹马和莫斯科外围战斗过。此外，它还参与了1941至1942年冬季苏联的攻势以及1942年的防御行动，并在热季从列夫撤退。1943年夏季，在库尔斯克会战及其相关撤退（包括布良斯克和莫吉廖夫战役）中，该师遭受了严重损失，到10月时仅剩战斗群规模。1943年11月2日，它被降级为第268步兵师团，并同时隶属于第36摩托化师。<cr>德国二战步兵师战斗序列 第1至290师，山姆·米奇姆著

text:
The division began forming on 26 June 1941 at Mozyr in the Western Front as the 12th NKVD Mountain Division with a cadre of border guards. It was almost immediately redesignated the 268th Rifle Division and transferred to the army, and by 10 July it moved back to Moscow to keep ahead of the German advance. Its basic order of battle included the 942nd, 947th, and the 952nd Rifle Regiments, as well as the 799th Artillery Regiment. In late July, the 268th was moved to the Leningrad Front, where it was assigned to the 8th Army around 1 August. After six weeks the division was transferred to the 55th Army, defending positions along the Neva River, where it remained until September 1942. In January 1943, just before Operation Iskra, which eased the Siege of Leningrad, the division was in front reserves. At the beginning of the offensive on 12 January, the 136th Rifle Division and the 268th, supported by tanks and artillery, captured a bridgehead between Shlisselburg and Gorodok 1 that was approximately 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) wide and 3 kilometres (1.9 mi) deep.

In the spring of 1943, the 268th was moved back to the 55th Army, and in May became part of the 67th Army. It absorbed troops from the disbanded 55th Naval Rifle Brigade in September. On 21 January 1944, the division attacks towards the Mga station and captured it. During the Vyborg-Petrozavodsk Offensive north of Leningrad in June and July, the division was part of the 21st Army's 110th Rifle Corps. After the end of the first phase of the offensive, which forced Finland to leave World War II, the 110th Rifle Corps and the division were relocated to the 42nd Army in the Baltics by August. The division spent last two months of the war in the spring of 1945 blockading trapped German forces in the Courland Pocket.<cr><cr>
translation:
该师于1941年6月26日在西方方面军的莫吉廖夫开始组建，最初为第12边防军山地师。几乎立即被改编为第268步兵师，并转隶集团军。到7月10日，该师返回莫斯科以避开德军攻势。其基本战斗序列包括第942、947和952步兵团以及第799炮兵团。7月下旬，第268师被调往列宁格勒方面军，并于8月1日前后编入第8集团军。六周之后，该师转隶保卫涅瓦河沿岸阵地的第55集团军，直至1942年9月。1943年1月初，在“火花”行动开始前（此行动缓解了列宁格勒围城战），该师被编入方面军预备队。在1月12日攻势开始时，第136步兵师和第268师，在坦克和炮兵支援下，夺取了什利谢利堡与戈罗德科1之间宽约5公里（3.1英里）、纵深约3公里（1.9英里）的桥头堡。

1943年春季，该师被调回第55集团军，并于5月编入第67集团军。同年9月吸收了解散中的第55海军步兵旅的部分兵力。1944年1月21日，该师进攻姆加车站并夺取之。在列宁格勒以北的维堡-彼得罗扎沃茨克攻势期间（6月至7月），该师编入第21集团军的第110步兵军。第一阶段攻势结束后，迫使芬兰退出第二次世界大战，第110步兵军和该师于8月被调往波罗的海地区的第42集团军。在1945年春季最后两个月中，该师封锁了库尔兰包围圈内的德军部队。<cr><cr><cr>编制：第268步兵师<cr><cr>

text: The 269th Infantry Division crossed into Russia with Army Group North on June 22 and played a major role in the XXXX Panzer Corps annihilation of the Russian III Armored Corps on the Dubysa. The division was down to 40 percent of its authorized strength by October, but still fought well in the Battle of the Volkhov, southeast of Leningrad, in early 1942. Meanwhile, it disbanded its III/469th, III/489th and II/490th Infantry Battalions.<cr>In the winter of 1942-43, the 269th was sent to Norway to rest and refit and remained on occupation duty at Bergen for more than a year and a half. In October 1944, it returned to the European mainland via Denmark and fought in the Vosges Mountains and in the Battle of the Colmar Bridgehead on the Western Front, where it was again reduced to battle group strength. In January 1945, it was transferred to southern Poland. (By now its 490th Grenadier Regiment had been disbanded and the other two regiments had only two battalions each.) The 269th Infantry fought in Silesia and was in the vicinity of Dresden as the only division in 4th Panzer Army's reserve when Berlin fell. A sizable number of its survivors thus managed to surrender to the Western Allies instead of to the Russians.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第269步兵师于1941年6月22日随北方集团军群进入俄罗斯，并在杜比萨河畔与XXXX装甲军一起摧毁了苏联第三装甲集团军，发挥了重要作用。该师到10月份已减员至编制的40%，但仍积极参与了1942年初沃尔霍夫战役中的战斗，该战役位于列宁格勒东南方向。与此同时，它解散了第3/469步兵团、第3/489步兵团和第2/490步兵团。<cr>1942-1943年的冬季，第269师被派往挪威休整并补充兵员，并在卑尔根驻扎了一年半以上。1944年10月，它经丹麦返回欧洲大陆，在孚日山脉作战，并参与了西线科尔马桥头堡战役，再次减员至战斗群规模。1945年1月，该师被调往波兰南部。<cr>到此时，其第490掷弹兵团已被解散，其余两个团每个仅剩两个营。<cr>1月，该师在西里西亚作战，并作为第四装甲集团军预备队中唯一一个师，在柏林陷落时位于德累斯顿附近。因此，许多幸存者得以向西方盟国投降，而不是苏联。<cr>@PH0@<cr>@PH2@@德国二战步兵师战斗序列 第1-290师，塞缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text:
The 269th Rifle Division began forming on 13 July 1941 from reservists at Kolomna, part of the Moscow Military District. Its basic order of battle included the 1018th, 1020th, and the 1022nd Rifle Regiments, as well as the 836th Artillery Regiment. By 5 August, the division had been moved to Teplukha, and assigned to the 24th Army of the Reserve Front. In mid-August the 269th was transferred to the newly formed 50th Army, but by the end of August the division was part of the 3rd Army in the Bryansk Front. Colonel Andrey Chekharin became division commander in early September. The 269th was encircled during Operation Typhoon and Chekharin was reported missing, presumably killed, during a breakout attempt on 20 October. The division served in roughly the same positions, covering the southern flank of the Moscow defenses, until late 1943.

From late 1943 to early 1944, the division slowly advanced towards the Dnieper as part of the Belorussian Front. The 269th fought in Operation Bagration as part of the 3rd Army's 41st Rifle Corps during the summer of 1944. On 21 July, it received the Order of the Red Banner for its actions. The division then fought in the southern Baltic states in late 1944 as part of the 2nd Belorussian Front and the 3rd Belorussian Front. During April and May 1945 it participated in the Battle of Berlin as part of the 1st Belorussian Front.<cr><cr>
translation:
第269步兵师于1941年7月13日开始在莫斯科军区科洛姆纳从预备役人员中组建。其基本战斗序列包括第1018、1020和1022步兵团，以及第836炮兵团。到8月5日，该师被转移到特普卢赫，并分配给预备方面军的第24集团军。在八月中旬，第269师被调往新成立的第50集团军，但到了8月底，该师成为布良斯克方面军第3集团军的一部分。安德烈·切卡林上校于9月初接任师长职务。在台风行动中，第269师遭到包围，切卡林在10月20日的一次突围尝试中失踪，据推测已阵亡。<cr><cr>该师大致在同一位置服役，覆盖莫斯科防御的南翼，直到1943年底。

从1943年底到1944年初，该师作为白俄罗斯方面军的一部分缓慢推进至第聂伯河。在1944年夏季，第269师作为第3集团军第41步兵军的一部分参加了巴格拉季昂行动，并于7月21日因行动表现获得红旗勋章。<cr><cr>该师随后在1944年底作为白俄罗斯第二方面军和第三方面军的一部分，在波罗的海南部地区作战。1945年4月至5月，它参加了作为白俄罗斯第一方面军一部分的柏林战役。<cr>第269步兵师<cr>@PH1@@

text: 26th Army was a part of the Southwestern Front and defended the Soviet-German border between Przemysl and the Carpathian Mountains in June 1941. The Army was located on the eastern bank of San river manning the 8th Fortified District. The 26th Army commander was Lt.Gen. F.Ya. Kostenko.<cr>The 26th Army consisted of the 8th Rifle Corps, with the 99th Rifle Division, 173rd Rifle Division, and the 72nd Mountain Rifle Division, the 8th Fortified District, a number of artillery units (the 2nd Anti-Tank Brigade, 233rd Corps Artillery Regiment, 236th Corps Artillery Regiment, and the 28th Independent Anti-Aircraft Squadron, the 8th Mechanised Corps with the 12th Tank Division, 34th Tank Division, and the 7th Mechanized Division), and the 17th Pontoon-Bridge Regiment on 22 June 1941. Headquarters was at Borislav.<cr>The Germans attacked the junction between 6th Army and 26th Army. On 23 June General Kirponos ordered 26th Army armour troops (8th Mechanized Corps) to move to Brody out of the command of Kostenko. Meanwhile, German assault created a twenty-mile breach on 24 June. During the night from 26th to 27 June, 6th and 26th retreated from frontier fortifications. The 26th Army and 12th Army now held a line from Ostropol to Bar. On 10 July Kostenko's Army together with 6th Army and 12th Army became threatened by south eastern swing of Kleist's 1st Panzer Group, which could cut them off from Dnieper river. On 20 July two Rifle Corps of 26th Army attacked in northern direction towards the Dnieper. Only small part of the 26th Army with its commander reached the Dnieper. Most of its units were destroyed or captured by Germans.<cr>The 26th Army was quickly rebuilt in October 1941 by subsequent reinforcements and included elements of the 1st Guards Special Rifle Corps and now defended the Dnieper river at Kaniev and Rzhishchev south-west of Kiev. 6th and 12th Army ended up in Uman Pocket. 26th Army tried to relieve those armies and attacked in the Boguslav-Zwenigorodka direction. It didn't work. In September 26 Army itself became surrounded in the Kiev Pocket. The Soviets tried to break out, 26th Army was supposed to attack on Lubny. General Kostenko escaped from the encirclement with quite a large group of his soldiers. The army was disbanded and the remaining forces were assigned to the 50th Army.<cr>The third time, 26th Army formed in November 1941 in the Volga Military District. On 18 December it was assigned to the newly formed Volkhov Front. In late December 1941 the army was redesignated as the 2nd Shock Army.<cr>Commander: Lieutenant General G.G. Sokolov (November - December 1941).<cr>The army was reformed for the fourth time within the Karelian Front in March-April 1942. On 1 January 1943 the army comprised 27th, 54th, 186th, and 263rd Rifle Divisions, 61st, 67th, 80th, and 85th Naval Infantry Brigades, artillery, and other units.<cr>Commander in 1943-1945 was Major General (later Lieutenant General) Lev Skvirsky.<cr>The army ended the war in Romania and was assigned to the Southern Group of Forces. The army along with most of its subordinate units were disbanded in 1947. The 25th Guards and 23rd Mechanized Divisions were reassigned to the Ukraine.<cr><cr>
translation: 第26集团军是西南方面军的一部分，在1941年6月保卫着普热梅希尔和喀尔巴阡山脉之间的苏联-德国边境。该集团军驻扎在桑河东岸，负责守卫第8工事区。第26集团军指挥官为少将F.Ya.科斯特尼科夫。<cr>1941年6月22日，第26集团军包括第8步兵军（下辖第99步兵师、第173步兵师和第72山地步兵师）、第8工事区、多个炮兵单位（第2反坦克旅、第233军属炮兵团、第236军属炮兵团以及第28独立防空中队）和第8机械化军（下辖第12装甲师、第34装甲师和第7机械化师），还有第17舟桥团。司令部位于博里斯拉夫。<cr>德国人攻击了第6集团军与第26集团军之间的结合部。6月23日，基尔波诺斯将军命令第26集团军的装甲部队（即第8机械化军）撤至布罗迪，脱离科斯特尼科夫指挥。与此同时，德军突击在6月24日造成了长达20英里的缺口。<cr>从6月26日至27日夜间，第6和第26集团军从边境工事中撤离。此时，第26集团军与第12集团军共同守卫着奥斯特罗波尔至巴的防线。7月10日，科斯特尼科夫指挥下的第26集团军连同第6集团军和第12集团军受到克莱斯特第1装甲集群从东南方向包抄的威胁，该行动可能切断他们与第聂伯河之间的联系。<cr>7月20日，第26集团军中的两个步兵军向北进攻，朝第聂伯河推进。只有小部分第26集团军及其指挥官抵达了第聂伯河。其大部分单位被德军消灭或俘虏。第26集团军在1941年10月迅速重建，通过后续增援包括了第一近卫特种步兵军的部分兵力，并且在基辅西南的卡尼夫和日兹希切夫地区防守第聂伯河。第六集团军和第十二集团军最终被困于乌曼包围圈内。第26集团军试图解救这些部队并从博古斯拉夫-泽维尼戈罗德方向发起攻击，但没有成功。<cr>在9月，第26集团军自身也被困于基辅包围圈中。苏联人试图突围，第26集团军被命令进攻卢布内。科斯特енко将军带领相当数量的士兵从包围圈中逃脱。该集团军解散，剩余部队被分配给第50集团军。<cr>第三次重建是在1941年11月在伏尔加河军区组建第26集团军。12月18日，它被分配到新成立的沃尔霍夫方面军。1941年底，该集团军重新指定为第二突击集团军。<cr>指挥官：少将G.G.索科洛夫（1941年11月至12月）<cr>第四次重建是在1942年3月至4月期间在卡累利阿方面军内进行的。到1943年1月，该集团军包括第27、54、186和263步兵师，第61、67、80和85海军陆战旅，炮兵和其他单位。<cr>指挥官：少将（后晋升为中将）列夫·斯克维尔斯基（1943-1945年）<cr>该集团军在罗马尼亚结束战争，并被分配给南方集团军。该集团军及其大部分下属单位于1947年解散。第25近卫步兵师和第23机械化师被重新分配到乌克兰。

text: The 26th Guards Rifle Division was reformed as an elite infantry division of the Red Army in April, 1942, based on the 1st formation of the 93rd Rifle Division, and served in that role until after the end of WWII. It would soon after provide the headquarters cadre for the 8th Guards Rifle Corps. It was soon assigned, with its Corps, to 20th Army of Western Front and saw extensive fighting, while also suffering extensive casualties, in two campaigns against the German 9th Army in the Rzhev salient through the rest of 1942. The division, again with 8th Guards Corps, joined the 11th Guards Army when it was formed in April, 1943 and, apart from a brief reassignment in early 1944, remained under those commands for the duration of the war. During that summer the division took part in the liberation of Bryansk. By December, after fighting through western Russia north of Smolensk it was in 1st Baltic Front, attacking south towards Gorodok and won the name of that city as a battle honor. By the start of the offensive against Army Group Center in the summer of 1944 the 26th Guards had been redeployed with its Army to the south of Vitebsk as part of 3rd Belorussian Front, where it would remain for the duration. Driving westward during Operation Bagration the division advanced north of Orsha and then helped to seize a crossing over the Berezina River for which it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner. It continued to advance through Lithuania to the border with East Prussia later that year. As part of the East Prussian Offensive the 26th Guards entered that heavily-fortified region in the winter of 1945 and helped gradually break the German resistance there, particularly at Insterburg and Knigsberg, winning the Order of Suvorov for its part in the battle for the former place. The division ended the war at Pillau.<cr><cr>
translation: 第26近卫步兵师于1942年4月在红军中重建，基于第93步兵师的第一个编制，并一直服役到第二次世界大战结束。不久之后，该师为第8近卫步兵军提供了司令部人员。随后，它与所属的军被分配给西方方面军的第20集团军，在1942年下半年在热季突出部对德军第9集团军的两次战役中进行了大量战斗，并遭受了重大伤亡。该师再次与第8近卫步兵军一起加入于1943年4月组建的第11近卫集团军，除了1944年初短暂重新分配外，一直隶属于这些部队直到战争结束。在那年的夏天，该师参与了解放布良斯克的行动。到12月份，在西俄罗斯斯摩棱斯克以北作战后，它被调往第1巴尔干方面军，向戈罗德克发起进攻，并因此获得了该城市的荣誉称号。在1944年夏季对中央集团军群发动攻势开始时，第26近卫师已与所属的集团军一起重新部署到维捷布斯克以南，成为第3白俄罗斯方面军的一部分，在那里一直驻扎到最后。在巴格拉季昂行动期间向西推进，该师在奥尔沙北部前进，并帮助夺取了别列津纳河上的渡口，因此获得了红旗勋章。同年晚些时候，它继续向东普鲁士边境推进，穿越立陶宛。作为东普鲁士攻势的一部分，第26近卫师于1945年冬季进入该地区，在因斯特堡和柯尼斯堡等地逐渐瓦解了德军的抵抗，并因此获得了苏沃洛夫勋章。该师在皮劳结束了战争。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: The 26th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 26th Light Division. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 26th Light Division was merged with other units and disbanded.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第26匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖两个步兵团（每个团有三个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多东线兵力，大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本没有变化。该旅更名为第26轻型师。在斯大林格勒战役后对匈牙利陆军进行的一次总体重组中，第26轻型师与其他部队合并并解散。<cr>参考文献：Nigel Thomas 博士和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利军队》<cr>条目由 Chris Munson 提供

text: The 26th Infantry Division got its first serious test in the Russian campaign of 1941, where it performed well. It distinguished itself when it crossed the Volga between Moscow and Leningrad, and stormed Rzhev, along with the 206th Infantry Division. It was heavily engaged against the Russian winter offensive of 1941-1942. Although relatively undamaged in the defensive fighting on the central sector in 1942, the 26th again suffered heavy casualties in the Battle of Kursk , Hitlers last major offensive on the Eastern Front. Shortly thereafter, it was reorganized as three two-battalion regiments. It opposed the Soviet offensive after the failure of the Kursk operation, fought at Orel (1943) and in the defense of Smolensk, and conducted itself brilliantly in the defense of Kovel in July 1944.<cr>Although it managed to escape destruction in the Russian summer offensive that smashed Army Group Center that year, the division was finally overrun near the East Prussian border in September 1944, and had to be withdrawn from the line. It was rebuilt in September and October 1944, in the Warthelager Maneuver Area in western Poland, where it was fleshed out with naval and Luftwaffe personnel, and recruits from Westphalia and the Rhineland formerly assigned to the 582nd Volksgrenadier Division. Its grenadier regiments were reduced from three to two battalions each and its reconnaissance battalion became a fusilier company. Redesignated a Volksgrenadier division on September 17, it was sent to the Luxembourg sector of the Western Front in November. The new Volksgrenadier division suffered heavy casualties in the Battle of the Bulge, where it took part in the siege of Bastogne as part of the XXXXVII Panzer Corps of the 5th Panzer Army. It also performed well in this campaign. At the end of the offensive the division had a combat strength of only 1,782 men; nevertheless, it remained in action and opposed the Allied drive on Pruem in February 1945. It finished the war on the Western Front and surrendered to the Americans in the Harz Mountains in May 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation:
第26步兵师在1941年的俄国战役中首次接受了严峻考验，并表现出色。该师在跨越伏尔加河，从莫斯科到列宁格勒之间时表现突出，并与第206步兵师一起猛攻了日兹德拉。它还积极参与了1941-1942年冬季的俄国人反攻作战。尽管在1942年的中央战区防御战斗中受损较小，但在库尔斯克战役中再次遭受重大伤亡。库尔斯克战役是希特勒在东线发动的最后一场大规模攻势。<cr>不久之后，该师重组为三个由两个营组成的团。它对抗了苏联在库尔斯克行动失败后的进攻，在奥廖尔（1943年）作战，并参与了斯摩棱斯克的防御战。此外，还在1944年7月科韦利的防御中表现出色。<cr><cr>尽管该师在当年的俄罗斯夏季攻势中幸免于难，但在1944年9月靠近东普鲁士边境的地方被突破，不得不撤出前线。该师在1944年9月至10月期间，在波兰西部瓦尔塔训练区重建，并补充了海军和空军人员以及原属第582国民掷弹兵师的威斯特法伦和莱茵地区的征召兵员。其掷弹兵团从每个团三个营减少到两个营，侦察营则改编为步枪连。该师于9月17日重新编为国民掷弹兵师，并在11月被派往西线卢森堡地区。新组建的国民掷弹兵师在突出部战役中遭受了严重伤亡，在第5装甲集团军第XXXXVII装甲军对巴斯通的围攻中发挥了作用。该师在这场战役中的表现也相当出色。进攻结束时，该师仅有1782名战斗人员；然而，它仍然继续作战，并于1945年2月在普鲁姆地区对抗盟军推进。该师最终在西线投降，地点是哈茨山脉，在1945年5月。

参考文献：德国二战陆军编成 第一卷 1至290步兵师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: The 26th Mechanized Corps was formed in March 1941 in the North Caucasus Military District. The corps included the 52nd and 56th Tank Divisions, and the 103rd Motorized Division (the former 103rd Rifle Division). The corps headquarters and the 56th Tank Division were at Armavir, the 52nd Tank Division at Mineralnye Vody, and the 103rd Motorized Division at Voroshilovsk. The corps was commanded by Major General Nikolai Kirichenko. It became part of the 19th Army. On 1 June, the units of the corps were equipped with 86 BT tanks and T-26 tanks, and 15 T-37, T-38, and T-40 amphibious tanks.<cr>On 22 June, Operation Barbarossa, the German invasion of the Soviet Union began. Between 28 and 29 June the corps was sent to the Kiev region with the 19th Army. The corps initially consisted of about 200 tanks and received reinforcements. It moved north with the 19th Army on 2 July. The corps was transferred to the 24th Army in the Dorogobuzh region southwest of Vyazma in early July. The corps was ordered to prepare fortified defensive lines northeast of Vyazma. On 8 July the corps was disbanded before it saw action as a result of the reorganization of Red Army mechanized forces. The 52nd and 56th Tank Divisions became the 101st and 102nd Tank Divisions. The 103rd Motorized Division became the 103rd Tank Division. All three divisions became part of the 24th Army's reserve. In mid-July, the Soviet General Staff decided to disband the mechanized corps as a result of combat experienced in the first weeks of the war, and planned to reform the corps headquarters as a rifle corps. On 16 July the 107th Rifle Division, 108th Rifle Division, 6th People's Militia Division, 19th Rifle Division, and the 444th Rifle Regiment, with artillery units, were ordered to become part of the rifle corps. The order was countermanded the next day and the rifle corps was never created.<cr><cr>
translation: 第26机械化军于1941年3月在北高加索军区组建。该军包括第52坦克师和第56坦克师，以及第103摩托化师（原第103步兵师）。军司令部和第56坦克师驻扎在阿玛维尔，第52坦克师位于米纳列尔内沃迪，第103摩托化师则位于沃罗希洛夫斯克。该军由少将尼古拉·基里琴科指挥，并成为第19集团军的一部分。<cr>6月1日，该军部队装备了86辆BT坦克和T-26坦克，以及15辆T-37、T-38和T-40两栖坦克。<cr>6月22日，巴巴罗萨行动开始，德国入侵苏联。6月28日至29日，该军被派往基辅地区与第19集团军会合。最初该军拥有约200辆坦克，并得到增援。7月2日，该军随同第19集团军向北移动。7月初，该军被调至维亚兹马西南的多罗戈布日地区的第24集团军。该军接到命令，在维亚兹马东北方向准备坚固防御阵地。7月8日，由于红军机械化部队重组，该军在未参战前解散。第52坦克师和第56坦克师分别改编为第101坦克师和第102坦克师。第103摩托化师改编为第103坦克师。这三个师均成为第24集团军预备队的一部分。7月中旬，苏联总参谋部决定解散机械化军，并计划重组该军司令部作为步兵军。7月16日，第107步兵师、第108步兵师、第6人民民兵师、第19步兵师和第444步兵团，连同炮兵单位，被命令成为步兵军的一部分。<cr>次日该命令被撤销，步兵军从未建立。

text:
The 26th Tank Corps was formed in July 1942 at Moscow with:<cr>
19th Tank Brigade:
-236th, 237th Tank Battalions
-19th Motorized Rifle Battalion
157th Tank Brigade:
-346th, 347th Tank Battalions (T-34s and T-60s)
-157th Motorized Rifle Battalion
216th Tank Brigade:
-452nd , 453rd Tank Battalions
-216th Motorized Rifle Battalion
14th Motorized Rifle Brigade<cr><cr>The 26th Tank Corps formed up slowly, and was not assigned to an operational HQ until August 1942, when it went to 5th Tank Army. In September 1942 the 56th Motorcycle Battalion was added to the corps, and on 19 November 26th Tank Corps was part of the Mobile Group of 5th Tank Army when the Stalingrad Offensive Operation began. It was the Forward Detachment of 26th Tank Corps that seized the bridge at Kalach-na-Don, completing the encirclement of the German 6th Army in Stalingrad. In honor of this feat the corps received the honorific title: 'Donskikh' and was redesignated as the 1st Guards Tank Corps on 8 December 1942.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp

text:
The 26th Tank Division was formed in February 1941 at Minsk as part of 20th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
51st Tank Regiment - 0 tanks
52nd Tank Regiment - 0 tanks
26th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
26th Howitzer Regiment - 1 light bn only<cr><cr>The 26th Tank Division had barely started organizing when the war started. Formed without a base of equipment or personnel from a tank brigade or cavalry division, this 'tank' division had no tanks, no armored cars, no heavy howitzers, no antiaircraft guns, few trucks, and virtually no unit training. Effectively, it was a rifle regiment with a battalion of howitzers attached. By l July the Soviet high command was officially listing the division as 'without equipment', acknowledging that it was no longer had a combat value. The division strength report of 7 July showed just 3800 men and 5 guns in the 'division'. it was destroyed in the Minsk pocket and officially disbanded in mid-July 1941.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第26坦克师于1941年2月在明斯克组建，隶属于第20机械化军：<cr>
第51坦克团 - 0辆坦克
第52坦克团 - 0辆坦克
第26摩托化步兵团
第1、2、3营
第26榴弹炮团 - 只有轻型营<cr><cr>该师刚刚开始组建，战争就爆发了。它没有以坦克旅或骑兵师为基础的装备和人员，实际上是一个“无坦”师，既没有坦克也没有装甲车，没有重榴弹炮、防空炮，只有少量卡车，并且几乎没有进行过单位训练。实际上，这只是一个附带一个榴弹炮营的步兵团。到7月1日，苏联最高统帅部正式将该师列为“无装备”，承认它已不再具有战斗价值。7月7日的师编制作战报告仅显示有3800人和5门火炮在所谓的“师”中。该师在明斯克包围圈被消灭，并于1941年7月中旬正式解散。<cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普《苏联战斗序列 第一卷》

text:
The 270th Rifle Division began forming on 10 July 1941 at Melitopol, part of the Odessa Military District. The division was assigned to the Southern Front's 12th Army by late August. In September, it was transferred to the 6th Army of the Southwestern Front. In January 1942, the 270th participated in the Barvenkovo-Lozovaya Offensive.<cr><cr>During the initial attack in the Second Battle of Kharkov, the 270th was assigned to Army Group Bobkin. The German attack in the Second Battle of Kharkov trapped Soviet forces in this bulge, which became known as the Izyum pocket. The 270th was among the divisions wiped out, and was officially disbanded on 25 May.<cr><cr>The 270th was begun forming in July 1942, part of the Arkhangelsk Military District. It had left the Arkhangelsk Military District for the Voronezh Front's 6th Army.<cr><cr>At the end of 1942, the 270th became part of the 18th Separate Rifle Corps. From 18 January, the division fought in the Ostrogozhsk-Rossosh Offensive, capturing Novy Oskol. At the beginning of February, the corps became the 69th Army. The 270th fought in Operation Star, the advance on Kharkov, entering Kharkov Oblast on 3 February. On 9 February, it captured Volchansk and developed the attack towards the city. The 270th participated in the capture of Kharkov on 16 February and began advancing on Bogodukhov. The division fought in the Third Battle of Kharkov. At the end of March, it was withdrawn to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command.<cr><cr>In July, the division was moved north in the RVGK and became part of the 6th Guards Army on 6 July, fighting in the Battle of Kursk and on the outskirts of Belgorod during the Belgorod-Khar'kov Offensive Operation. On 27 July, the 270th was withdrawn to the RVGK and transferred to the Kalinin Front. At the end of August, it became part of the front's 43rd Army, remaining there until February 1944. In September 1943, the division fought in the Smolensk Operation and the Dukhovshchina-Demidov Offensive. On 22 September, it was awarded the honorific 'Demidov'.<cr><cr>In the fall, the division advanced westwards into Belarus, fighting northeast of Vitebsk from October. On 14 February, the division transferred back to the RVGK and became part of the 103rd Rifle Corps. In early June, it was relocated to the Novokhovansk area south of Nevel. On 12 June, the division and its corps joined the 6th Guards Army of the 1st Baltic Front just before Operation Bagration began in late June. The division participated in the Vitebsk-Orsha Offensive and the Polotsk Offensive in June and July. For its actions in the capture of Polotsk, the division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner on 23 July. Continuing the offensive, the 270th advanced into Latvia, fighting in the Rezhitsa-Dvinsk Offensive, the Siauliai Offensive, the Baltic Offensive, the Riga Offensive, and the Battle of Memel from July to November.

In December, the division began blockading German troops trapped in the Courland Pocket on the Baltic coast. On 12 February 1945, the division was transferred to the 22nd Guards Rifle Corps of the 10th Guards Army, part of the 2nd Baltic Front. A month later it shifted to the 6th Guards Army's 84th Rifle Corps. On 17 April, the corps transferred to the 4th Shock Army, still in the Courland Group of Forces, defending positions southeast of Libau until the end of the war.<cr><cr>
translation:
第270步兵师于1941年7月10日在梅利托波尔开始组建，隶属于敖德萨军区。该师在8月下旬被分配给南方方面军的第12集团军。9月份，它被转移到西南方向第6集团军。1942年1月，第270步兵师参加了巴尔文科沃-洛佐瓦亚攻势。<cr>在第二次哈尔科夫战役初期攻击中，第270步兵师被分配给鲍布金集团军群。德国人在第二次哈尔科夫战役中的进攻将苏联军队困在一个突出部内，形成了伊久姆包围圈。第270步兵师是被消灭的部队之一，并于5月25日正式解散。<cr>1942年7月，第270步兵师在阿尔汉格尔斯克军区开始组建。它离开了阿尔汉格尔斯克军区，加入了沃罗涅日方面军的第6集团军。<cr>到1942年底，第270步兵师成为第18独立步兵军的一部分。从1月18日起，该师参加了奥斯特罗戈热斯克-罗斯霍夫攻势，占领了诺维奥斯科尔。2月初，该军成为了第69集团军。第270步兵师参与了“星辰”行动，即向哈尔科夫的推进，在2月3日进入了哈尔科夫州。2月9日，它占领了沃尔昌斯克，并继续攻击这座城市。2月16日，该师参加了哈尔科夫的夺取，并开始向博戈杜霍夫推进。第270步兵师参与了第三次哈尔科夫战役。<cr>3月底，它被撤回最高统帅部预备队。7月，该师被调往北方的预备队方面军（RVGK），并于7月6日成为第6近卫集团军的一部分，在库尔斯克战役中作战，并在别尔哥罗德-哈尔科夫进攻行动期间参与了别尔哥罗德外围地区的战斗。7月27日，该师被撤回预备队方面军并转隶加里宁方面军。8月底，它成为前线第43集团军的一部分，直至1944年2月。1943年9月，该师参加了斯摩棱斯克行动和杜霍夫什奇纳-德米多夫进攻行动。9月22日，该师被授予“德米多夫”荣誉称号。

秋季，该师向西推进进入白俄罗斯，在维捷布斯克东北部作战从10月开始。2月14日，该师返回预备队方面军并成为第103步兵军的一部分。6月初，它被重新部署到内夫尔以南的诺沃霍瓦斯基地区。6月12日，在巴格拉季昂行动即将于月底展开之前，该师及其所属步兵军加入波罗的海第一方面军的第6近卫集团军。

在6月至7月期间，该师参加了维捷布斯克-奥尔沙进攻和波洛茨克进攻。由于其在夺取波洛茨克中的行动，该师于7月23日被授予红旗勋章。继续推进，第270师进入拉脱维亚，在雷吉察-迪纳普进攻、希奥利艾进攻、波罗的海进攻、里加进攻以及梅梅尔战役中作战，从7月至11月。

1945年12月，该师开始封锁波罗的海沿岸库尔兰包围圈内的德军。1945年2月12日，该师被调至第22近卫步兵军，隶属于第二波罗的海方面军下的第10近卫集团军。<cr>一个月后，它又转移到了第6近卫集团军的第84步兵军。<cr>4月17日，该军转隶第4突击集团军，在库尔兰集团军群内继续防守利巴瓦东南方向的位置直到战争结束。<cr> <cr>

text: The 271st Infantry Division was formed as part of the 10th Wave for the invasion of France but with France's rapid defeat its formation was halted. In November 1943 it was reformed in Holland with the 977th, 978th and 979th Grenadier Regiments, 271st Artillery Regiment and various support units. In May 1944 the division was stationed on the southern coast of France. Around this time the 666th and 681st Ost Battalions transferred to the division. In August 1944 the division was destroyed in Normandy. In September 1944 as part of the 32nd Wave the 576th Volksgrenadier Division was redesignated the 271st Volksgrenadier Division. It contained two regiments, the 977th and 978th Grenadier Regiments with two battalions each. Part of the division was sent to Budapest in February 1945. The division was later captured by the Russians in Moravia.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第271步兵师是在第十波入侵法国时组建的，但由于法国迅速战败，其组建工作被叫停。1943年11月，该师在荷兰重组，包括第977掷弹兵团、第978掷弹兵团、第979掷弹兵团、第271炮兵团以及各种支援单位。1944年5月，该师驻扎在法国南部海岸。大约在同一时期，第666和第681东区营被调入该师。1944年8月，该师在诺曼底被消灭。1944年9月，在第三十二波中，第576国民掷弹兵师改称为第271国民掷弹兵师。它包括两个团，即第977和第978掷弹兵团，每个团有两个营。该师的一部分于1945年2月被派往布达佩斯。后来该师在摩拉维亚被俄国人俘获。<cr>参考文献：George F. Nafziger,《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>条目由Chris Munson提供

text:
The 271st Rifle Division began forming in Orel on the 10th of July 1941, from reserves of the Orel Military District. In early August it was assigned to the 51st Army in the defence of the Crimea where it suffered heavy casualties. It was evacuated from the Taman peninsula in November 1941.

In March 1942 the division was assigned to the 47th Army, returned to the Crimea and was destroyed by May 1942. Remnants of the Division were used to rebuild the division and it was designated as an Azerbaijani National Division.

In late 1942 the division was assigned to the 58th Army of the North Caucasus Front, and in 1943 was assigned to 44th Army of the Southern Front. It fought in the Donbass, the Carpathian mountains and ended the war in Czechoslovakia with the 38th Army.

It fought with some distinction as it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner and Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky.



 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 


Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第271步兵师于1941年7月10日在奥廖尔开始组建，由奥廖尔军区的预备队提供。8月初被分配给保卫克里米亚的第51集团军，在那里遭受了重大伤亡。该师在1941年11月从塔曼半岛撤出。

1942年3月，该师被分配给第47集团军，并返回克里米亚，到1942年5月已被消灭。该师的残部被用来重建该师，并将其指定为阿塞拜疆国民师。

1942年底，该师被分配给北高加索方面军的第58集团军，在1943年又被分配给南方方面军的第44集团军。它参加了顿巴斯战役、喀尔巴阡山脉战斗，并在捷克斯洛伐克与第38集团军结束了战争。

由于表现出色，该师被授予红旗勋章和博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基勋章。

Nigel Askey, 巴巴罗萨行动 第三卷

感谢 John Tomlinson

text:
The 272nd Rifle Division began forming at Tikhvin on the 10th of July 1941, from reserves of the Leningrad Military District. In late July it was assigned to the 7th Army in Karelia where it remained until Finland was knocked out of the war in September 1944.

In January 1945 the division was assigned to the 19th Army, in East Prussia and ended the war assigned to the 2nd Shock Army.

text:
The 273rd Rifle Division began forming at Dnepropetrovsk on the 10th of July 1941, from reserves of the Odessa Military District. It took some time to complete formation as it lacked automatic and heavy weapons. In late August it was assigned to the 6th Army and then the 12th Army and by the end of September it had been destroyed in the vicinity of Dnepropetrovsk.

The division was raised for a second time in February 1942 in the Ural Military District. By the middle of the year it was assigned to the Moscow Defense Zone, afterwards the Voronezh Front and then the Don Front in the Battle of Stalingrad.

In July 1943 the Division was assigned to the Bryansk Front and fought in the Battle of Smolensk where it was awarded an honorific for the capture of Bezhitsa.

In 1944 the Division was suffering from manpower shortages and it's last significant combat operation was the Siege of Breslau in 1945.

The Division fought with distinction as it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky and honorific BEZHITSA



 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 


Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第273步兵师于1941年7月10日在顿涅茨克彼得罗夫斯克开始组建，由敖德萨军区的预备队提供。由于缺乏自动武器和重武器，其组建花费了一段时间。到8月底，该师被分配给第6集团军，随后是第12集团军，并于9月末在顿涅茨克彼得罗夫斯克附近被消灭。

该师于1942年2月在乌拉尔军区第二次重建。同年中旬，它被分配到莫斯科防御区，之后是沃罗涅日方面军，然后是在斯大林格勒战役中的顿河方面军。

1943年7月，该师被分配给布良斯克方面军，并参加了斯摩棱斯克战役，在贝热季萨的占领中获得荣誉称号。

1944年，该师因人手不足而遭受损失。其最后一次重要的作战行动是1945年的布雷斯劳围城战。

该师表现出色，获得了红旗勋章、波格丹·赫梅利尼茨基勋章和贝热季萨荣誉称号。

text:
The 274th Rifle Division began forming at Zaporozhye on the 10th of July 1941, from reserves of the Odessa Military District. It took some time to complete formation and it never received its full complement of anti tank guns and artillery. In late August it was assigned to the 12th Army and then lost a rifle regiment to the 15th Rifle Division. The Division was smashed by the 1st Panzer Group, and suffered heavy casualties with the remnants used as replacements for the 4th Rifle Division.

The division was raised for a second time in May 1942 in the Moscow Military District. By the middle of the year it was assigned to the Moscow Defense Zone, afterwards the Kalinin Front and then the Western Front.

In September 1943 the Division was assigned to the 31st Army and led the attack for the recapture of Yartsevo.

The Division ended the war assigned to the 61st Rifle Corps, 69th Army, 1st Belorussian Front.

The Division fought with distinction as it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov and honorific YARTSEVO



Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 


Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第274步兵师于1941年7月10日在扎波罗热开始组建，由敖德萨军区的预备队组成。完成组建花费了一段时间，并且该师从未完全获得其反坦克炮和火炮的完整编制。8月下旬，它被分配给第12集团军，随后将一个步兵团调给了第15步兵师。该师被第1装甲集群摧毁，遭受了严重伤亡，剩余部队用于补充第4步兵师。

该师于1942年5月在莫斯科军区第二次组建。到当年中期，它被分配给莫斯科防御区，之后是加里宁方面军，然后是西方面军。

1943年9月，该师被分配给第31集团军，并领导了夺回雅尔采沃的进攻。

战争结束时，该师隶属于第61步兵军、第69集团军和第1白俄罗斯方面军。

该师英勇作战，荣获红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫勋章以及荣誉称号“雅尔采沃”

Nigel Askey, 巴巴罗萨行动 第三卷

感谢 John Tomlinson

text:
The 275th Rifle Division began forming at Novomoskovsk , north of Dnepropetrovsk on the 10th of July 1941, from reserves of the Odessa Military District. Due to the German advance it completed its formation as part of the North Caucasus Military District. In late August it was assigned to the 6th Army and then the 37th Army. 

In 1942 it avoided the disaster at Kharkov and retreated all the way into the Caucasus in a very depleted state, taking up defensive positions along the Terek and Baksan rivers. Along with the 37th Army, it was destroyed by the 3rd Panzer Corps in October 1942.

The division was raised for a second time in July 1943 in the Transbaikal. It was assigned to the Far East and in 1945 took part in the Soviet invasion of Manchuria.



 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 


Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第275步兵师于1941年7月10日在诺沃莫斯科夫克开始组建，该地位于第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克以北，由敖德萨军区的预备部队组成。由于德国军队推进迅速，它在高加索军区内完成了组建工作。8月下旬被分配给第6集团军，随后又转隶至第37集团军。

1942年，该师避开了哈尔科夫灾难，并一路撤退到高加索地区，在极度虚弱的状态下沿特erek河和巴克斯安河布设防御阵地。与第37集团军一起，于1942年10月被第3装甲军消灭。

该师在1943年7月再次组建于外贝加尔地区，并被分配到远东方向，在1945年参加了苏联入侵满洲的行动。

Nigel Askey, 巴巴罗萨行动，第三卷

text:
The 276th Rifle Division began forming near Orel on the 10th of July 1941, from reserves of the Orel Military District. Still incomplete it was rushed to the Crimea and finished forming at Simferopol with the 51st Army. After heavy fighting it was withdrawn to the Caucasus in November 1941. In February 1942 it returned to the Crimea and was destroyed in the German offensive in May 1942.

The division was raised for a second time in August 1942 as a Georgian National Division, at Kutaisi, and was assigned to the 9th and then the 18th Army. The Division fought at Terek River and Temryuk, in the Carpathian Mountains and ended the war in Czechoslovakia with the 38th Army. 

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner and the honorific TEMRYUK.





 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 


Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第276步兵师于1941年7月10日在奥廖尔附近的军区预备队中开始组建。尚未完全编成，该师就被紧急调往克里米亚，并在辛菲罗波尔与第51集团军一起完成了组建工作。经过激烈战斗后，该师于1941年11月撤至高加索地区。1942年2月，该师再次返回克里米亚，在1942年5月的德军攻势中被消灭。

1942年8月，该师在库塔伊西第二次组建，并编入第9集团军和随后的第18集团军。该师参加了特列布河、特姆尼科夫以及喀尔巴阡山脉的战斗，并最终随第38集团军在捷克斯洛伐克结束战争。

该师荣获红旗勋章，并获得荣誉称号TEMRYUK。

——内维尔·阿斯基，《巴巴罗萨行动》，第三卷

text:
The 277th Rifle Division began forming in Dmitriev on the 10th of July 1941, from reserves of the Orel Military District. In early August, missing heavy weapons and transport, it was rushed into combat with the 51st Army and destroyed in the Kiev pocket. 

The division was raised for a second time near Stalingrad, in December 1941, by redesignating the barely formed 486th Rifle Division. In 1942 the Division participated in the battle of Kharkov and in defensive operations as it retreated towards Stalingrad, during which time it suffered heavy casualties. 

 In 1943 the Division participated in the elimination of the Battle of Stalingrad pocket and was then assigned to the Western Front. 

In 1944 the Division took part in Operation Bagration and the advance into the Baltic states. By March 1945 it was down to 2700 personnel when it was withdrawn into Reserve and then moved to the Far East for the invasion of Manchuria.

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov, Order of Kutuzov and the honorific ROSLAVL.



 Nigel Askey, Operation Barbarossa, Vol IIIB 


Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第277步兵师于1941年7月10日在德米特里耶夫开始组建，由奥廖尔军区的预备队提供。8月初，由于缺少重武器和运输工具，该师被迫与第51集团军一起投入战斗，并在基辅包围圈中被消灭。

该师于1941年12月在斯大林格勒附近重建，通过重新指定刚刚组建的第486步兵师实现。1942年，该师参加了哈尔科夫战役以及撤退至斯大林格勒期间的防御作战，在此过程中遭受了重大伤亡。

1943年，该师参与消灭了斯大林格勒包围圈，并随后被分配到西方面军。

1944年，该师参加了巴格拉季昂行动和向波罗的海国家推进的战斗。至1945年3月，人员减少到2700人时，该师被撤出预备队并转移到远东地区准备入侵满洲国。

该师获得了红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫勋章、库图佐夫勋章和荣誉称号ROSLAVL。

尼格尔·阿斯基，《巴巴罗萨行动》，第三卷

约翰·汤姆林森提供

text:
The 278th Rifle Division began forming in Livny on the 10th of July 1941, from reserves of the Orel Military District. In the middle of August, it was assigned to the 50th Army of the Bryansk Front and by mid October had been trapped and destroyed in the Bryansk pocket. 

The division was raised for a second time near Stalingrad, in January 1942, by renaming the 4 week old 471st Rifle Division. In mid 1942 the Division was assigned to the Moscow Military District to complete formation, then the 38th Army Southwestern Front and fought in defensive operations as it retreated towards Stalingrad, during which time it suffered heavy casualties. The Division fought in the Battle of Stalingrad, and in mopping up operations, where it was reduced to 50% strength. In January 1943 it was renamed as the 60th Guards Rifle Division.

The Division was raised for the third time in July 1943, assigned to the 36th Army of the Transbaikal Front and then fought in the invasion of Manchuria where it was awarded the honorific of KHINGAN.

text:
The 279th Rifle Division began forming near Gorky on the 2nd of July 1941, from the 6th Reserve Rifle Brigade of the Moscow Military District. In the middle of August, it was assigned to the 50th Army of the Bryansk Front and by mid October had been trapped and destroyed in the Bryansk pocket. The remnants were used to reinforce the 154th Rifle Divison and the 279th Rifle Division was officially disbanded on the 15th of November 1941.

The division was raised for a second time at Balakhna, in June 1942, with reserves drawn from the Urals and Central Asia. In January 1943 the Division was assigned to the 3rd Guards Army near Stalingrad then back into Reserves. 

In January 1944 it was part of the 51st Army in the Crimea where it received a commendation for the capture of Simferopol. By July 1944 the Division was part of the 1st Baltic Front and ended the war in Courland.

The Division received the Order of the Red Banner and the honorific LYSYCHANSK.



Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第279步兵师于1941年7月2日在高尔基附近开始组建，由莫斯科军区的第6预备步兵旅改编而成。8月中旬，该师被分配给布良斯克方面军的第50集团军，并在10月中旬被困并消灭于布良斯克包围圈中。剩余部队用于增援第154步兵师，第279步兵师正式解散于1941年11月15日。

该师于1942年6月在巴拉赫纳第二次组建，后备人员来自乌拉尔和中亚地区。1943年1月，该师被分配给斯大林格勒附近的第3近卫集团军，然后又回到预备队。

1944年1月，该师成为克里米亚的第51集团军的一部分，并因占领辛菲罗波尔而获得嘉奖。到1944年7月，该师成为波罗的海第一方面军的一部分，并在库尔兰结束战争。

该师获得了红旗勋章和LYSYCHANSK荣誉称号。

text: On 22 June 1941 the 27th Army consisted of the 22nd and 24th Rifle Corps, 16th and 67th Rifle Divisions, 3rd Separate Rifle Brigade, two artillery regiments, and two anti-tank regiments. It became part of Northwestern Front on the outbreak of Operation Barbarossa.<cr>From 30 June 1941 to 1 July 1941 elements of the 22nd Territorial Rifle Corps manned the hills around Porkhov taking up defensive positions to the south and south-west. On 7-8 July 1941 battles took place with advanced German reconnaissance elements and on 9 July 1941 in the evening a clash with the attack from the area in the direction of Shmoilova Porkhov and Bukhara Dedovichi.<cr>During the fighting, 9-10 July 1941 mass desertions of the 22nd Corps' Estonian personnel took place to the Germans. Among the famous defectors was the Deputy Chief of Operations, Division Staff 180th Rifle Division, Ain-Ervin Mere. On 10 July 1941 the 111th Motorized Division broke the defense of the 182nd Rifle Division On 11 July it finally left the city, and partly moved to the east bank of the river Shelon, and took up defensive positions. On 12 July 1941 the 182nd Rifle Division was fighting against troops of the enemy trying to break through to Dno.<cr>On 15 August to 17 August 1941the 22nd Territorial Rifle Corps, participated in an counterattack, from the area Parfino at Staraya Russa, corps troops liberated most of the city, but failed to take it completely. 20-21 August 1941 some units left Staraya Russa and re-crossed the eastern shore of the Lovat. 22 September 1941 the headquarters of the 22nd Territorial Rifle Corps was disbanded.<cr>From June to October 1941 the 27th Army fought on the Dvina River, during the Staraya Russa offensive, and at Kholm and Demyansk. By 1 November 1941 the army's forces had been reduced to the 23rd and 33rd Rifle Divisions, the 613th Artillery Regiment of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (RVGK), the 28th Tank Division, and three Battalions of engineers.<cr>In December 1941 it was renamed the 4th Shock Army.<cr>The army was formed for a second time in May 1942, within the Northwestern Front, consisting of five rifle divisions. In April 1943 it was moved into Stavka reserve. From July 1943, it participated in many famous battles, assigned to the Steppe Front, then the Voronezh Front, in the Belgorod-Kharkov operation and the Bukrina bridgehead. From October 1943, it fought in the Kiev offensive (with 1st Ukrainian Front). Thereafter, assigned to the 2nd and 3rd Ukrainian Front, it was part of the Zhitomir-Berdichev Offensive, the Korsun-Shevchenkovsky Offensive, Uman-Botoshany, Iassy-Kishinev Offensive, the Battle of Debrecen, and the Vienna Offensive.<cr><cr>
translation: 1941年6月22日，第27集团军由第22步兵军和第24步兵军、第16步兵师和第67步兵师、第3独立步兵旅、两个炮兵团和两个反坦克团组成。巴巴罗萨行动爆发时，它成为西北方面军的一部分。<cr>从1941年6月30日至7月1日，第22边防步兵军的部分部队在波尔霍夫周围的山丘上占据南部和西南部的防御阵地。1941年7月7-8日，与德军侦察部队发生战斗；1941年7月9日晚，与来自什莫伊洛娃、波尔霍夫和布哈拉·德多维奇方向的进攻部队交战。<cr>在战斗期间，1941年7月9日至10日，第22步兵军中的爱沙尼亚人员大量投敌。其中一位著名叛徒是副作战主任兼第180步兵师参谋部成员艾恩-埃里温·梅雷。1941年7月10日，第111摩托化师突破了第182步兵师的防御阵地；11日，该师最终撤离城市，并部分转移到谢尔隆河东岸，占据新的防御位置。1941年7月12日，第182步兵师与试图突破至德诺的敌军部队作战。<cr>从1941年8月15日至17日，第22边防步兵军参与了帕尔菲诺地区针对斯塔罗亚·鲁萨地区的反击行动；该军部分部队解放了大部分城市，但未能完全占领。1941年8月20-21日，一些单位从斯塔罗亚·鲁萨撤离，并重新渡过洛瓦特河东岸。<cr>1941年9月22日，第22边防步兵军司令部被解散。从1941年6月到10月，第27集团军在德维纳河沿岸作战，在斯塔罗波尔斯卡进攻中参战，并参加了霍尔姆和德米扬斯克的战斗。到1941年11月1日，该集团军的力量已缩减为第23步兵师、第33步兵师、最高统帅部预备队（RVGK）中的第613炮兵团、第28坦克师和三个工兵营。<cr>1941年12月，它被改名为第4突击集团军。<cr>该集团军于1942年5月在西北方面军内第二次组建，由五个步兵师组成。1943年4月，它被调入最高统帅部预备队。<cr>从1943年7月起，它参加了许多著名战役，隶属于顿斯克方面军，然后是沃罗涅日方面军，在别尔哥罗德-哈尔科夫行动和布克林桥头堡作战中。从1943年10月开始，它在基辅助攻战（隶属第1乌克兰方面军）。此后，被分配给第2和第3乌克兰方面军，参加了日托米尔-别列斯切夫斯基进攻、科尔松-舍甫琴科夫斯基进攻、乌曼-博托沙尼行动、伊萨克-奇什古尔进攻战、德布勒森战役以及维也纳攻势。

text:
The division draws its history from the 75th Naval Rifle Brigade formed in the end of 1941. As part of the 3rd Shock Army, Kalinin Front in 1942 the brigade participated in the Demiansk operations - the Moscow counteroffensive. For its fighting performance it became the 3rd Guards Rifle Brigade in March 1942, having spent all its time in reserve, became the 27th Guards Rifle Division in April-May 1942. With a view to the preservation of fighting and revolutionary traditions of earlier formations, the name 'Omsk' which 27th Rifle Division had during the Russian Civil War had earlier was given to the new division. In the late summer of 1942, it was rushed south to help stop the German offensive into the northern Caucasus and Stalingrad. It took part in the destruction of the German 6th Army during the winter of 1942/43. During World War II the division was part of the 4th Tank Army, 1st Guards Army, the 24th Army, the 66th Army, the 65th Army and since February 1943 the 62nd Army. In April 1942 the 62nd Army became the 8th Guards Army. In July 1942 the division was part of Kalinin Front's 58th Army, alongside 16th Guards Rifle Division and two other rifle divisions. The division was back with the 8th Guards Army of the 1st Belorussian Front in May 1945.

The division participated in the Battle of Stalingrad, Izyum-Barvenkovo, Donbass, Zaporozhye, Nikopol-Krivoi Rog, Bereznegova-Snigirovka, Odessa, Lublin-Brest, Poznan, Kustrin, East Prussia Offensive and the Berlin offensive operation. For services in battle the division was awarded the honorific 'Novobug' in March 1944, then awarded the Order of the Red Banner and Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky 2nd degrees. Over 10 thousand of its soldiers were awarded awards and medals, and 7 were awarded the Hero of the Soviet Union. Its commanders included Colonel Konstantin Vindushev (1942), and Viktor Glebov (19421945), Glebov was originally a colonel but was made a general-major in November 1942.<cr><cr>
translation:
该师的历史可以追溯到1941年底成立的第75海军步兵旅。作为加里宁方面军第三突击集团军的一部分，该旅在1942年参加了德米扬斯克行动——莫斯科反攻。由于其出色的战斗表现，该旅于1942年3月被改编为第3近卫步兵旅，并且自成立以来一直在预备队中待命。到1942年4月至5月期间，它被改编为第27近卫步兵师。为了保留早期部队的战斗和革命传统，“鄂木斯克”这一名称（该师在俄国内战时期使用的名字）被赋予了新组建的师。1942年晚秋，该师被紧急调往南方，以阻止德国向北高加索和斯大林格勒发动进攻。它参与了摧毁德军第6集团军的冬季行动（1942/43）。在第二次世界大战期间，该师隶属于第四坦克集团军、第一近卫集团军、第二十四集团军、第六十六集团军、第六十五集团军以及自1943年2月起隶属第六十二集团军。1942年4月，第六十二集团军被改编为第八近卫集团军。1942年7月，该师隶属于加里宁方面军的第五十八集团军，与第十六近卫步兵师和其他两个步兵师并肩作战。到1945年5月，该师又回到了第一白俄罗斯方面军第八近卫集团军。

该师参加了斯大林格勒战役、伊久姆-巴尔文科沃战役、顿巴斯战役、扎波罗热战役、尼科波尔-克里沃罗格战役、别列任戈瓦-斯尼吉罗夫卡战役、敖德萨战役、卢布林-布列斯特战役、波兹南战役、库斯特林战役、东普鲁士进攻和柏林进攻行动。由于在战斗中的贡献，该师于1944年3月获得“诺沃布格”荣誉称号，并被授予红旗勋章和博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基二级勋章。超过一万名士兵获得了奖章，其中七人荣获苏联英雄称号。该师的指挥官包括康斯坦丁·温杜舍夫少校（1942年）和维克多·格尔波夫少校（1942-1945年），格尔波夫最初是少校，但在1942年11月被晋升为少将。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: The 27th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 27th Light Division. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 27th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 27th Infantry Division although as late as August 1944 it remained listed on the rolls as the 27th Light Division. In January 1944 the Hungarian First Army to which the division was then subordinate, mobilized to defend Hungary's northern Carpathian frontier against the advancing Red Army. In August 1944 the division was part of a reactivated Hungarian Second Army defending Northern Transylvania from the invading Red Army. The division was disbanded in April 1945.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第27匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖两个步兵团（每个团有三个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有七个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多东线兵力，大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本保持不变。该旅更名为第27轻型师。在斯大林格勒战役后对匈牙利陆军进行的一般重组中，第27轻型师与其他单位合并，并改名为第27步兵师，尽管迟至1944年8月，它仍被列为第27轻型师。1944年1月，在当时下属的匈牙利第一集团军动员下，该师准备防御匈牙利北部喀尔巴阡山脉边境免受红军进攻。1944年8月，该师成为重新组建的匈牙利第二集团军的一部分，负责在北方特兰西瓦尼亚地区抵御入侵的红军。该师于1945年4月解散。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas 和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利陆军》<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The corps was formed in March 1941 in Mary in the Central Asian Military District. The corps included the previously formed 9th Tank Division at Mary, and the new 53rd Tank Division at Kyzyl-Arvat, as well as the new 221st Motorized Division at Samarkand. The corps was commanded by Major General Ivan Yefimovich Petrov.<cr>On 22 June 1941, Operation Barbarossa, the German invasion of the Soviet Union, began. At the time the corps was equipped with 356 tanks. On 25 June the corps was alerted for movement to the west. On 27 June the first echelon of the 9th Tank Division moved west by rail, followed by the rest of the division. Moving through Tashkent and Orenburg, the division's first echelon reached Voronezh on 8 July. On 8 July, the Soviet General Staff decided to disband the mechanized corps and reorganize the tank divisions as a result of heavy tank losses in the first days of the war. The division's headquarters arrived at Voronezh on 10 July. The 27th Mechanized Corps was to become part of the 28th Army at Kirov. Unloading was to be carried out at the Fayansovaya railway station to the north of Kirov. The trains transporting the corps began to arrive at the station the next day, unloading only at night due to German air superiority. Many trains were delayed due to damage to the railway tracks, including one tank battalion that was stuck at Bryansk station for three days. By 15 July, the concentration of the 9th Tank Division had been completed with 208 tanks (mostly T-26s and BT-7s). At the same time the 9th Tank Division had become the 104th Tank Division, the 53rd Tank Division the 105th Tank Division, and the 221st Motorized Division the 106th Tank Division. The corps was disbanded on 15 July, and the 106th Tank Division became the 106th Motorized Division on 19 July.<cr><cr>
translation: 该军于1941年3月在玛丽的中亚军区成立。该军包括此前在玛丽组建的第9坦克师，以及新近在基兹尔-阿拉瓦特建立的第53坦克师和在撒马尔罕建立的新第221摩托化师。该军由伊凡·叶菲莫维奇·彼得罗夫少将指挥。<cr>1941年6月22日，巴巴罗萨行动开始，即德国入侵苏联。当时该机械化军装备有356辆坦克。6月25日，该机械化军接到向西调动的命令。6月27日，第9坦克师第一梯队通过铁路向西移动，其余部队随后跟进。经过塔什干和奥伦堡，该师的第一梯队于7月8日到达沃罗涅日。7月8日，苏联总参谋部决定解散机械化军，并重组坦克师以应对战争初期的严重损失。第9坦克师司令部于7月10日抵达沃罗涅日。第27机械化军将并入基洛夫地区的第28集团军。卸载将在基洛夫北部的法亚纳索娃火车站进行。第二天，运输该机械化军的列车开始到达车站，并仅在夜间卸货以避开德国的制空权。许多列车因铁路轨道受损而延误，包括一个坦克营在布良斯克站滞留了三天。到7月15日，第9坦克师集结完毕，拥有208辆坦克（主要是T-26和BT-7）。同时，第9坦克师改名为第104坦克师，第53坦克师改名为第105坦克师，第221摩托化师改名为第106坦克师。该机械化军于7月15日解散，第106坦克师在7月19日改为第106摩托化师。<cr><cr>

text: The 27th Panzer Division was apparently formed in two echelons-part of the divisional base (including the artillery regiment) was formed in France in the summer and autumn of 1942 and then was sent to Voronezh, Russia, in the rear area of the 2nd Army. Here it was joined by Brigade Michalik-which mainly consisted of the 140th Panzer Grenadier Regiment (formerly of the 22nd Panzer Division)-to form the 27th Panzer Division, which was activated on October 1, 1942. The new divisions total strength was slightly less than 3,000 men. It was nevertheless broken up into as many as seven battle groups and was scattered over the entire southern sector of the Eastern Front. The 127th Panzer Engineer Battalion was trapped and destroyed at Stalingrad and never joined the rest of the unit. Other elements of the new division fought on the Don, in the retreat from Stalingrad, and in the battles south of Kharkov. Still other parts were attached to the Hungarian 2nd Army and the 8th Italian Army. By January 1, 1943, the division had lost half of its grenadiers and only had eleven tanks left (excluding twenty which had been appropriated by Headquarters, 2nd Army.) By February 8, the divisions estimated strength was 1,590. The 27th Panzer Division was disbanded on or about March 3, 1943, after the Soviet winter offensive of 1942-43 had been stopped. Most of its equipment and survivors were absorbed by the 7th Panzer Divison, although the men of the 127th Panzer and 127th Panzer Signal Battalions were sent to France and assigned to the 24th Panzer Division.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第27装甲师似乎分两个梯队组建——该师的部分基础部队（包括炮兵团）于1942年夏秋在法国形成，然后被派往俄罗斯沃罗涅日的第二集团军后方区域。在这里，它与米哈尔斯基旅汇合，后者主要由原属第22装甲师的第140装甲掷弹兵团组成，从而组建了第27装甲师，并于1942年10月1日正式激活。新编成的师总兵力略低于3,000人。尽管如此，它还是被拆分成多达七个战斗群，并分散在整个东线南部战区。第127装甲工兵团在斯大林格勒被围困并消灭，从未加入其余部队。该师其他部分则在顿河作战，在从斯大林格勒撤退时以及哈爾科夫以南的戰鬥中作戰，并有部分被编入匈牙利第二集团军和意大利第八集团军。到1943年1月1日，该师失去了半数掷弹兵，只剩下十一辆坦克（不包括已被第二集团军司令部征用的二十辆）。截至2月8日，该师估计兵力为1,590人。第27装甲师于1943年3月初左右解散，在苏联冬季攻势被阻止后。其大部分装备和幸存人员被并入第七装甲师，尽管第127装甲团和第127装甲通信营的士兵被派往法国，并编入第二十四装甲师。<cr>德国战斗序列卷三——二战中的装甲、装甲掷弹兵及武装党卫军师<cr>萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: Formed as part of 5th Army in Southwestern Front in June 1941, the corps consisted of 87th, 124th and 135th Rifle Divisions. It participated in the Battle of Kiev and was destroyed in August 1941. It was briefly reformed in April 1943 and the headquarters was used as the basis for 18th Independent Rifle Corps, which was part of 13th Army and fought from Lvov to Berlin. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 1941年6月作为西南方面军第5集团军的一部分组建，该军由第87、第124和第135步兵师组成。它参加了基辅会战，并于1941年8月被消灭。该部曾在1943年4月短暂重建，其司令部成为独立第18步兵军的基础，后者隶属于第13集团军，从利沃夫一路战斗到柏林。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 《红军伟大卫国战争战斗序列》，Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 27th Rifle Division was formed in November 1918 during the Russian Civil War. It later fought in the war with Poland shortly after World War I and suffered heavy losses. The division returned to Poland in 1939 and took part in the joint Nazi and Soviet Invasion of Poland as part of the 3rd Army's 4th Rifle Corps.<cr>At the start of Operation Barbarossa on 22 June 1941, the division was again part of 4th Rifle Corps in the Western Special Military District which quickly became the Western Front. The division was attacked by the German 162nd and 256th Infantry Divisions. Its regiments fought separately as they retreated eastwards towards Sok?ka. By June 24th the division had lost 40% of its personnel and the following day unsuccessfully tried to defend the Swis?ocz river line. In accordance with orders, it defended the line until the end of the day when it was annihilated. Only small groups of soldiers from the division survived to reach Soviet lines in July and early August. The division was officially disbanded on September 19, 1941.<cr>The division was reformed in August 1941 at Arkhangelsk and renamed the Rebolsky Direction Division in September 1941. The division subsequently fought against the Finnish Army. The division was subordinated to the 26th Army of the Karelian Front in May 1942 and was deployed in the far north of Russia until the end of 1944. The unit completed the war with the 19th Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front in May 1945.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第27步兵师成立于1918年11月的俄国内战期间。该师后来参加了第一次世界大战后不久与波兰的战争，并遭受了重大损失。该师于1939年返回波兰，作为西部特别军区第三集团军第四步兵军的一部分参与了纳粹德国和苏联对波兰的联合入侵。<cr>巴巴罗萨行动开始时（1941年6月22日），该师再次隶属于西部方面军辖区内的第四步兵军。德军第162步兵师和第256步兵师对该师进行了攻击。其团级单位在撤退至索科尔卡的过程中各自为战。<cr>到6月24日，该师已损失了40%的人员，并于次日试图防守斯维斯洛奇河防线未果。根据命令，该师一直坚守到当天结束时被彻底摧毁。只有少数士兵在7月和8月初到达苏军阵地幸存下来。<cr>该师于1941年9月19日正式解散。<cr>1941年8月，该师在阿尔汉格尔斯克重建，并于同年9月更名为雷博尔斯基方向师。该师随后与芬兰军队作战。该师于1942年5月隶属于卡累利阿方面军的第26集团军，在俄罗斯北部地区一直战斗到1944年底。<cr>该单位在1945年5月作为第二白俄罗斯方面军第19集团军的一部分完成了战争。<cr><cr>克里斯·芒森提供

text: The 27th Tank Corps tarted forming in June 1942, but never completed forming as a tank corps. Possibly the corps HQ controlled, at least for training, 219th Tank Brigade and 19th Motorized Rifle Brigade, which were both in Moscow Military District in July-September 1942. In September 1942, HQ 27th Tank Corps was used to form the cadre for 1st Mechanized Corps, the initial composition of which included 219th Tank Brigade and 19th Mechanized Brigade (formed by adding 9th Tank Regiment to 19th Motorized Rifle Brigade).<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. text:
The 27th Tank Division was formed in February - March 1941 near Baranovichi in Western Military District as part of 17th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
53rd Tank Regiment - 0 tanks
54th Tank Regiment - 0 tanks
27th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
27th Motorized Howitzer Regiment - 1 light bn only<cr><cr>The 17th Mechanized Corps has the melancholy distinction of being the most poorly equipped unit of all the poorly-equipped and half-formed mechanized corps in the Red Army on 22 June 1941. 27th Tank Division was missing most of the support elements from the division: it had a few light armored cars, but few trucks or tractors, no maintenance units formed yet, no antiaircraft guns, and no tanks. text:
The 280th Rifle Division began forming in Tula on the 2nd of July 1941, from reserves of the Moscow Military District. In the middle of August, it was assigned to the 50th Army of the Bryansk Front and by mid October had been trapped and destroyed in the Bryansk pocket. The commanding officer, S.E. Danilov was captured when his headquarters was overrun and perished in German captivity in March 1944.

The division was raised for a second time near Stalingrad, in December 1941, took some time to complete formation and by the end of 1942 was assigned to the 48th Army of the Bryansk Front. In mid 1943 the Division fought with distinction at the Battle of Kursk and was then assigned to the 1st Ukrainian Front, where it remained for the rest of the war. The division ended the war in the Carpathian Mountains. 

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov and honorifics of KONOTOP and KOROSTEN.



Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第280步兵师于1941年7月2日在图拉开始组建，由莫斯科军区的预备队提供人员。8月中旬，该师被分配给布良斯克方面军下的第50集团军，并在10月中旬被围困并消灭于布良斯克包围圈中。指挥官S.E.丹尼洛夫在其司令部被突破时被俘，在德国战俘营中于1944年3月去世。

该师于1941年12月在斯大林格勒附近再次组建，完成编组花费了一段时间，并于1942年底被分配给布良斯克方面军下的第48集团军。1943年中期，该师在库尔斯克战役中表现出色，并随后被分配给第1乌克兰方面军，在那里一直待到战争结束。该师最终在喀尔巴阡山脉结束了战争。

该师获得了红旗勋章、苏沃罗夫勋章以及科诺托普和科尔松的荣誉称号。

text: The 281st Security Division served behind the northern sector of the Russian Front in 1941. After major Russian breakthroughs in the winter offensive in 1941-42, the 281st was encircled at Kholm on January 28, 1942. Its commander, Major General Theodor Scherer, became commandant of the 'fortress' and held it against overwhelming odds with only 5,000 men until May 5, when it was relieved. Remarkably, he performed this task without artillery of any kind, although he did rely heavily on air support when weather permitted. The 281st Security was engaged in line of communications duties for Army Group North during the next few weeks, but its 368th Security (now Grenadier) Regiment was again in action in the battles of Demyansk from November 1942 until February 1943.<cr>The following autumn, the 281st was again heavily engaged against the Russians on the northern sector of the front and was finally smashed by the Soviet summer offensive of 1944. It rebuilt as an infantry division at the end of the year. As of January 1945 (when it became the 281st Infantry), the division consisted of the 322nd, 368th, and 418th Grenadier Regiments (two battalions each), the 281st Artillery Regiment, the 281st Fusilier Company, the 281st Tank Destroyer Company (equipped with captured tanks), the newly-formed 281st Engineer Battalion, the 822nd Signal Battalion, and the 281st Field Replacement Battalion. The new infantry division, meanwhile, was withdrawn from Courland and was sent to the Vistula. It fought in the withdrawal from West Prussia and Pomerania, and ended up on the Oder River. Along with the rest of the 3rd Panzer Army, it surrendered to the Western Allies in May 1945. Contrary to its supposed rear-area mission, the 281st spent much of its time on the front line, rather than in the communications zone.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第281治安师于1941年在俄罗斯方面军北部战区后方服役。在1941-42年的冬季攻势中，苏军取得重大突破后，第281治安师于1942年1月28日在霍尔姆被包围。<cr>其指挥官、少将西奥多·舍雷尔成为“要塞”的司令，并仅凭5,000人对抗压倒性的优势，直到5月5日才得以解围。令人惊讶的是，在任何炮兵支援都不存在的情况下（尽管在天气允许时他大量依赖空中支援），他完成了这一任务。<cr>接下来的几周内，第281治安师继续为北方集团军群执行后勤线任务，但其第368治安团（现改称掷弹兵团）再次于1942年11月至1943年2月间在德梅扬斯克战役中参战。次年秋天，第281师再次在前线北部地区与俄国人激烈交战，并最终被苏联1944年的夏季攻势摧毁。该师年底重建为步兵师。截至1945年1月（此时改称第281步兵师），该师包括第322掷弹兵团、第368掷弹兵团和第418掷弹兵团（每个团有两个营）、第281炮兵团、第281燧发枪连、装备被俘坦克的第281歼击坦克连、新成立的第281工兵营、第822通信营以及第281野战补充营。新的步兵师从库尔兰撤出，调往维斯杜拉河地区，并参与了从中普鲁士和波美拉尼亚撤离的战斗，最终驻守在奥得河畔。该师与第三装甲集团军其他部队一起，在1945年5月向西方盟国投降。<cr>注：有关德军战斗序列的资料请参阅《二战中的第1至290步兵师：德国战斗序列第一卷》，作者萨缪尔·W·米查姆。

text:
The 281st Rifle Division began forming on 10 July 1941 at Leningrad from reservists. The division's basic order of battle included the 1062nd, 1064th, and the 1066th Rifle Regiments, as well as the 816th Artillery Regiment. It was brought up to strength in July by around 3,000 untrained civilians from Leningrad volunteer 'fighter battalions.' On 13 August, it was sent to the defensive line at Kingisepp, south of the city. For most of the rest of the year, the 281st was a 'fire brigade', directly subordinated to the Leningrad Front. On 17 December, the division transferred to the 54th Army, which was fighting to the east of the Volkhov River. The 281st fought in the Volkhov area as part of the 54th Army, which became part of the Volkhov Front.

After the Leningrad-Novgorod Offensive ended the Siege of Leningrad in February 1944, the Volkhov Front was disbanded, and the division became part of the 8th Army. The 282nd fought in the Narva area but was soon transferred to the 98thRifle Corps. The 98th Rifle Corps became part of the 23rd Army, and the division fought in the Vyborg-Petrozavodsk Offensive, a Soviet attack in the Karelian Isthmus during the summer of 1944, which resulted in the withdrawal of Finland from the war in September. After spending September in the Reserve of the Supreme High Command, the 281st and the 98th Rifle Corps moved south to become part of the 2nd Shock Army. The 282nd fought in the East Prussian Offensive and the East Pomeranian Offensive in early 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第281步兵师于1941年7月10日在列宁格勒开始组建，由预备役人员组成。该师的基本战斗序列包括第1062、1064和1066步兵团以及第816炮兵团。7月份，从列宁格勒志愿者“战士营”中征召了约3,000名未经训练的平民以补充兵力。<cr><cr>8月13日，该师被派往金吉塞普南面防御线。在接下来的一年里，第281步兵师大部分时间作为“救火队”，直接隶属于列宁格勒方面军。12月17日，该师转隶到正在沃尔霍夫河以东作战的第54集团军。第281步兵师作为第54集团军的一部分，在沃尔霍夫地区作战，并成为沃尔霍夫方面军的一员。<cr><cr>在列宁格勒-诺夫哥罗德攻势于1944年2月结束列宁格勒围城战后，沃尔霍夫方面军解散，该师转隶到第8集团军。第281步兵师在纳尔瓦地区作战，但很快被调往第98步兵军。<cr><cr>第98步兵军成为第23集团军的一部分，该师参加了维堡-彼得罗扎沃茨克攻势，在1944年夏季的卡累利阿地峡苏攻中发挥了作用，并导致芬兰在同年9月退出战争。经过9月份最高统帅部预备队的休整后，第281步兵师和第98步兵军南下成为第2突击集团军的一部分。<cr><cr>第281步兵师参加了东普鲁士攻势和波美拉尼亚攻势，在1945年初作战。<cr><cr><cr>第282步兵师在纳尔瓦地区作战，但很快被调往第98步兵军。<cr><cr>第98步兵军成为第23集团军的一部分，该师参加了维堡-彼得罗扎沃茨克攻势，在1944年夏季的卡累利阿地峡苏攻中发挥了作用，并导致芬兰在同年9月退出战争。经过9月份最高统帅部预备队的休整后，第282步兵师和第98步兵军南下成为第2突击集团军的一部分。<cr><cr>第282步兵师参加了东普鲁士攻势和波美拉尼亚攻势，在1945年初作战。<cr>

text: The 282nd Rifle Division's first formation was formed in the summer of 1941 and destroyed in the Bryansk pocket in the fall of that year. The 282nd was quickly reformed in December 1941 in Siberia and moved west in the spring of 1942. The division fought in the Demyansk Pocket for the next year, and during Operation Bagration advanced into the Baltic states in the summer of 1944. Due to losses the 282nd spent the last months of 1944 in reserve and after receiving reinforcements reentered combat in January 1945, fighting in the Sandomir-Silesian Offensive, the Silesian Offensives, and the Prague Offensive before being disbanded after the end of the war in the summer of 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第282步兵师的第一个编制成立于1941年夏季，并在同年秋季布良斯克包围圈中被消灭。该师于1941年12月在西伯利亚迅速重建，并于1942年春季向西推进。接下来的一年，该师参加了德梅耶斯克包围圈的战斗，在巴格拉季昂行动期间，于1944年夏季进入波罗的海国家。由于损失严重，第282步兵师在1944年末处于预备状态，并在获得增援后于1945年1月重新投入战斗，参加了桑多梅日-西里西亚进攻、西里西亚攻势和布拉格攻势，直至战争结束于1945年夏季解散。<cr><cr>

text:
The 283rd Rifle Division began forming from reservists on 15 July 1941 at Shchigry in the Orel Military District. Its basic order of battle included the 856th, 858th, and 860th Rifle Regiments, as well as the 848th Artillery Regiment. In early September, it was sent to the front, where it was assigned to Arkady Yermakov's operational group of the Bryansk Front. In October, during Operation Typhoon, the German assault on Moscow, the 283rd was transferred to the 3rd Army, with which it served during the rest of the war with only one small interruption. After the Bryansk Front was disbanded, the division became part of the Southwestern Front in late 1941. In February 1942, the 848th Artillery Regiment became the 9th Guards Artillery Regiment. The division was later transferred back to the new formation of the Bryansk Front, with which it served until October 1943. In late 1943, the 283rd fought in the operations that forced the German Army Groups Center to retreat back to the Dnieper.

In February 1944, the division briefly transferred to the 1st Belorussian Front's 50th Army, but a month later it returned to the 3rd Army. At this point the division had suffered so much attrition that each rifle battalion had only two rifle companies, one machine gun company, and one mortar company. The division fought in Operation Bagration in June and July as part of the 80th Rifle Corps. In late July the 3rd Army moved to the 2nd Belorussian Front, advancing into the Baltic states. The 3rd Army became part of the 3rd Belorussian Front in February 1945. In late April, the 3rd Army became part of the 1st Belorussian Front, and the 283rd was assigned to the 41st Rifle Corps, serving as the front reserve in the Berlin Offensive.<cr><cr>
translation:
第283步兵师于1941年7月15日在奥廖尔军区的什奇格里从预备役人员开始组建。其基本战斗序列包括第856、858和860步兵团，以及第848炮兵团。九月初，该师被派往前线，并加入布良斯克方面军亚历山大·叶尔马科夫的作战群。十月期间，在台风行动中，即德军对莫斯科的突击时，第283步兵师转隶第三集团军，直至战争结束仅短暂中断一次。在布良斯克方面军解散后，该师于1941年末成为西南方面军的一部分。1942年二月，第848炮兵团改组为第九近卫炮兵团。之后，该师被调回新组建的布良斯克方面军，并一直服役至1943年十月。1943年底，第283步兵师参加了迫使中央集团军群撤退到第聂伯河的作战行动。

1944年二月，该师短暂转隶第一白俄罗斯方面军第三十集团军，但一个月后又返回第三集团军。此时该师已遭受严重消耗，每个步兵营仅剩两个步兵连、一个机枪连和一个迫击炮连。六月至七月期间，在巴格拉季昂行动中，第283步兵师作为第八十步兵军的一部分参战。七月底，第三集团军转隶第二白俄罗斯方面军，向波罗的海国家推进。1945年二月，第三集团军成为第三白俄罗斯方面军的一部分。四月下旬，第三集团军成为第一白俄罗斯方面军的一部分，并第283步兵师被分配给第四十一步兵军，在柏林攻势中作为方面军预备队参战。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 284th Rifle Division began service as a standard Red Army rifle division shortly after the German invasion. Moved to the front soon after, it helped defend the Soviet lines west of the Ukrainian capital for more than a month, but was then destroyed in the encirclement of Kiev. A new division was formed in early 1942. It served in the early fighting against the German summer offensive of 1942 until its losses forced it to be withdrawn for rebuilding. In September it was redeployed, and played a leading role in defending the northern part of the central city and Mamayev Kurgan hill in the Battle of Stalingrad, and later in the reduction of the trapped German 6th Army during Operation Ring, for which it was raised to Guards status as the 79th Guards Rifle Division shortly after the battle ended. A third 284th was raised a few months later. It served on the quiet fronts of the Far East for most of the rest of the war before fighting briefly against the Japanese in Manchuria in August, 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第284步兵师在德国入侵后不久开始服役，很快就被调往前线。该师帮助保卫了乌克兰首都基辅导西的苏联防线超过一个月，但在基辅包围圈中被消灭。一个新的师于1942年初组建。它参加了对抗德军1942年夏季攻势的早期战斗，直到损失严重被迫撤退重建。9月，该师重新部署，并在斯大林格勒战役中发挥了重要作用，保卫了市中心北部和马马耶夫高地，在后来的“环”行动中进一步削弱被围困的德国第6集团军时也起到了关键作用，战后不久即升格为近卫部队，成为第79近卫步兵师。几个月后又组建了一个新的第284步兵师。该师在战争剩余时间里主要驻守较为平静的远东前线，直到1945年8月短暂参加了对日本的战斗。<cr><cr>

text:
The 285th began forming on 2 July 1941 at Kostroma, part of the Moscow Military District. Its basic order of battle included the 1013th, 1015th, and 1017th Rifle Regiments, as well as the 835th Artillery Regiment. While still forming in early September, the 285th was assigned to the 54th Army, also forming to the east of Leningrad. The division was transferred to the 4th Army for its first combat in the Tikhvin Defensive and Tikhvin Offensive operations between October and December.

By the beginning of 1942 the 285th had been transferred back to the 54th Army, which became part of the Volkhov Front, holding positions on the Volkhov River to the east and southeast of Leningrad. In February 1944, the front was disbanded after the LeningradNovgorod Offensive ended the Siege of Leningrad, and the 54th Army became part of the Leningrad Front. The division was transferred to the 3rd Baltic Front's 67th Army in April 1944. The division served with the 67th Army or the 1st Shock Army fighting in the Baltic states until October, when it transferred to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command. The 285th was subsequently transferred to the 21st Army of the 1st Ukrainian Front, with which it moved south.<cr><cr>

As part of the 21st Army's 55th Rifle Corps, the division fought in the VistulaOder Offensive and the Silesian Offensives in early 1945. The 285th remained with the army until the end of the war.
translation: 第285师于1941年7月2日在莫斯科军区的科斯特罗马开始组建。其基本战斗序列包括第1013团、第1015团和第1017团，以及第835炮兵团。在九月初仍在组建期间，该师被分配给正在列宁格勒以东地区组建的第54集团军。<cr><cr>到1942年初，第285师又被调回第54集团军，后者成为沃尔霍夫方面军的一部分，在列宁格勒东南方向和东部地区的沃尔霍夫河沿岸驻防。在1944年2月，随着列宁格勒-诺夫哥罗德进攻战役结束对列宁格勒的围困后，该方面军被解散，第54集团军成为列宁格勒方面军的一部分。<cr><cr>第285师于1944年4月被调至第三波罗的海方面军的第67集团军。该师与第67集团军或第一突击集团军在波罗的海诸国作战，直到10月被调到最高统帅部预备队。<cr><cr>随后，第285师被调至第一乌克兰方面军的第21集团军，并随其向南推进。<cr><cr><cr>作为第21集团军第55步兵军的一部分，该师参加了1945年初的维斯瓦-奥得进攻战役和西里西亚进攻战役。<cr><cr>直到战争结束，该师一直隶属于第21集团军。<cr>
