text: This division was formed on March 15, 1942, from the remains of the 213th Infantry Division, a recently disbanded Landwehr unit. (The 286th received those personnel still on active duty.) The division served with Army Group Center throughout the rest of the war. It was used primarily in the rear area, protecting important installations and conducting anti-partisan operations. Its main base was Orscha, which was also its headquarters. It saw front-line duty against the Russian summer offensive of 1944, and suffered heavy casualties. At battle group strength, it fought in Narev, Memel, and Samland and on the Oder. On December 17, 1944, it was reorganized and redesignated the 286th Infantry Division. It now included the 926th, 927th and 931st Grenadier Regiments (two battalions each), the 286th Artillery Regiment (three battalions), the 286th Signal Battalion and the 286th Field Replacement Battalion. On April 17, 1945, it was reorganized yet again. The combat units of the division were sent to Swinemuende and placed under the command of Staff, Division Raegener, an ad hoc unit which was now renamed the 286th Training Division (Ausbildung-Division 286). The former staff of the 286th remained in Samland and became Special Administrative Division Staff 619. The 286th, meanwhile, joined the 9th Army on the Oder and took part in the defense of Berlin. It was destroyed when the Russians captured the city (April 25-May 3, 1945).<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 该师于1942年3月15日由解散的第213步兵师残部组建而成。（第286师接收了仍在服役的人员。）该师在整个战争期间隶属于中央集团军群，主要部署在后方区域，保护重要设施并进行反游击作战。其主要基地和司令部均设于奥尔沙。它参加了1944年夏季苏军攻势的一线战斗，并遭受重大伤亡。以战斗群规模，它参与了纳雷夫、梅梅尔、萨姆兰以及奥得河的战斗。1944年12月17日，该师重组并改称为第286步兵师。此时包括第926掷弹兵团（每团两个营）、第927掷弹兵团（每团两个营）、第931掷弹兵团（每团两个营），第286炮兵团（三个营），第286通信营和第286野战补充营。1945年4月17日，该师再次重组。战斗部队被派往施韦因穆登，并由临时组建的拉根纳尔师司令部指挥，改称为第286训练师（Ausbildung-Division 286）。原第286师指挥部留在萨姆兰并成为特别行政分队司令部619。与此同时，该师加入奥得河畔的第9集团军，并参与了柏林防御战。在苏军占领柏林期间（1945年4月25日至5月3日），该师被消灭。<cr><cr>德国二战战斗序列第一卷：第1至第290步兵师，塞缪尔·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text:
The 287th Rifle Division began forming around 10 July 1941 at Yelets, part of the Orel Military District. Its basic order of battle included the 866th, 868th, and 870th Rifle Regiments, as well as the 851st Artillery Regiment. While still forming, the division was assigned its commander on 20 July and became part of the Bryansk Front reserves on 15 August. At the end of September, the division, possibly still trying to complete its formation, was trapped in the Bryansk pocket after the 2nd Panzer Group broke through the Soviet lines. On 3 October, the division was moved up from the reserve by rail and its eleven trains were unloaded at Brasovo station, 75 kilometers south of Bryansk. Between 3 and 5 October the division conducted unsuccessful counterattacks. The 287th was virtually destroyed by mid-October, but was not officially disbanded until 27 December.<cr><cr>The second formation of the 287th began forming in late December at Lipetsk with the same basic organization as the first formation, and quickly became part of the Bryansk Front while still forming. Its first units were formed from the remnants of the 287th's first formation that had escaped from the Bryansk pocket. The 287th joined the 3rd Army in January, and was assigned its commander in late February. The division fought in battles on the Bryansk Front and in May 1943 was transferred to the 63rd Army, still on the same front.

In October, the army was transferred to the Belorussian Front, and on 20 December the 287th was transferred to the 13th Army. The division subsequently became part of the army's 24th Rifle Corps. By April 1944, its divisional anti-tank battalion was equipped with older model 76 mm M1936 or 76 mm M1939 (USV) guns. In July the division transferred to the army's 102nd Rifle Corps. The 287th transferred to the 38th Army's 67th Rifle Corps in November, and from December 1944 to the war's end was part of the 3rd Guards Army's 76th Rifle Corps. The division fought in the Berlin Offensive from late April 1945. On 25 April, its commander, Major General Iosif Pankratov, was killed by a large mine blast. By the end of the war, the division's honorifics were 'Novograd-Volynsky, twice Order of the Red Banner, Orders of Suvorov, Kutuzov, and Bogdan Khmelnitsky.<cr><cr>
translation:
第287步兵师于1941年7月10日左右在奥廖尔军区的叶列茨开始组建。其基本战斗序列包括第866、868和870步兵团，以及第851炮兵团。该师还在组建期间，指挥官于7月20日被任命，并于8月15日成为布良斯克方面军预备队的一部分。到9月底，该师可能仍在试图完成组建工作，在第二装甲集团突破苏联防线后被困在布良斯克包围圈内。10月3日，该师从预备队中调出并乘火车前往布拉斯沃车站卸载，该站位于布良斯克以南75公里处。10月3日至5日期间，该师进行了几次未成功的反击行动。到10月中旬，第287步兵师几乎被消灭，但直到12月27日才正式解散。

第二次组建的第287步兵师于1941年12月底在利佩茨克开始组建，其基本组织结构与第一次相同，并且在仍在组建期间就成为布良斯克方面军的一部分。该师的第一批单位由从布良斯克包围圈中逃脱的第一组建残部组成。第287步兵师于1月加入第三集团军，并于2月底被任命指挥官。该师参加了布良斯克方面军的战斗，直到1943年5月才转隶第六十三集团军，仍在同一战区作战。

十月，集团军被转移到白俄罗斯方面军，12月20日，第287师转隶至第13集团军。随后该师成为该集团军第24步兵军的一部分。到1944年4月，其反坦克营装备了较老型号的ZIS-3（76毫米M1936）或SU-76（76毫米M1939）自行火炮上的76毫米火炮。7月该师转隶至第102步兵军。11月，第287师被转移到第38集团军的第67步兵军，在1944年12月至战争结束期间成为第3近卫集团军第76步兵军的一部分。该师参加了从1945年4月下旬开始的柏林攻势。4月25日，其指挥官伊奥西夫·潘克拉托夫少将被一枚大型地雷爆炸致死。到战争结束时，该师获得了“诺夫哥罗德-沃林斯基，两次荣获红旗勋章，苏沃洛夫勋章、库图佐夫勋章和赫梅利尼茨基勋章”的荣誉称号。<cr><cr>第287师<cr><cr>

text:
The 288th Rifle Division began forming on 13 July 1941 at Yaroslavl, part of the Moscow Military District, from reservists. Its basic order of battle included the 1012th, 1014th, and 1016th Rifle Regiments, as well as the 834th Artillery Regiment. The division was moved north within a month and in mid-August was assigned to the new 52nd Army, forming east of Leningrad in the swampy Volkhov area. The overstretched division held a front of 46 kilometers in the Volkhov area by mid-October. In early January 1942, the division was transferred to the 4th Army, still in the Volkhov Front. In November 1943 it was transferred to the 54th Army's 111th Rifle Corps. After the end of the Siege of Leningrad in January 1944, the division advanced into the Baltic states in the spring and summer.

In August the 288th was transferred to the 1st Shock Army in Latvia and in late October became part of the 42nd Army's 123rd Rifle Corps. From January 1945, the division was part of the 22nd Army 14th Guards Rifle Corps, blockading German troops trapped in the Courland Pocket on the Baltic coast of Lithuania. In March the 14th Guards Rifle Corps was transferred to the Courland Group of Forces of the 2nd Baltic Front, with which it ended the war in May with the surrender of the German Army Group Courland.<cr><cr>
translation:
第288步兵师于1941年7月13日在雅罗斯拉韦尔开始组建，该地属于莫斯科军区，由预备役人员组成。其基本战斗序列包括第1012团、第1014团和第1016团，以及第834炮兵团。一个月内，该师被调往北方，并于8月中旬被分配到新成立的第52集团军，在列宁格勒以东的沃尔霍夫沼泽地区组建。截至10月中旬，这个兵力不足的师在沃尔霍夫地区防守了长达46公里的正面。1942年1月初，该师被调往仍在沃尔霍夫方面军内的第4集团军。1943年11月，它又被转移到第54集团军下属的第111步兵军。

在列宁格勒围城战结束后的1944年1月，该师进入波罗的海国家，在春季和夏季推进。8月，第288步兵师被调往拉脱维亚的第1突击集团军，并于10月下旬成为第42集团军下属的第123步兵军的一部分。从1945年1月起，该师成为第22集团军下属的第14近卫步兵军的一部分，在立陶宛波罗的海沿岸封锁了被围困在库尔兰包围圈内的德军部队。3月，第14近卫步兵军被调往第二波罗的海方面军的库尔兰兵力群，并于5月随着德国北方集团军群的投降结束了战争。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text:
The 289th Rifle Division began forming from reservists on 10 July 1941 at Lubny. Its basic order of battle included the 1044th, 1046th, and 1048th Rifle Regiments, as well as the 281st Artillery Regiment. At the beginning of August, the division was assigned to the Southwestern Front's 26th Army. The division arrived at the 26th Army's positions from 2 to 5 August, taking up a defense along the Dnieper southeast of Kiev. The division fought in the Battle of Kiev and was destroyed in the Kiev pocket in September, along with most of the 26th Army. While the division was officially disbanded on 19 September, its commander and some remnants escaped to provide a cadre for the division's second formation.<cr><cr>The division's second formation was formed on 15 October 1941 from the 5th Rifle Brigade. The 5th Rifle Brigade had been redesignated on 5 October 1941 from the Murmansk Rifle Brigade, which was also called the Grivnik Brigade. The Murmansk Rifle Brigade was originally formed in July 1941. The brigade fought alongside the Soviet 88th Rifle Division against the Finnish J-Group of the Finnish III Corps and the German SS North during Operation Barbarossa. They beat back both forces, forcing the Finno-German troops to retire to the city of Kestenga, near Lake Topozero in September 1941. The brigade consisted of some local militia, the 242nd Rifle Regiment of the 104th Rifle Division and probably an artillery battalion of the same division.

The division fought in Karelia for the rest of the war. In April 1942 it became part of the 32nd Army. From June to August 1944 it fought in the Svir-Petrozavodsk Offensive, during which it fought in the recapture of southern Karelia. The advances made in the offensive resulted in the Finnish ending the Continuation War in September. After the end of the Continuation War, the division became part of the 4th Rifle Corps of the Belomorsky Military District at Belomorsk by May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
第289步兵师于1941年7月10日在卢布内从预备役人员开始组建。其基本战斗序列包括第1044团、第1046团和第1048团，以及第281炮兵团。8月初，该师被分配给西南方面军的第26集团军。该师于8月2日至5日抵达第26集团军的位置，在基辅东南方向的第聂伯河沿岸进行防御。该师参加了基铺战役，并在9月份与大部分第26集团军一起在基辅包围圈中被消灭。虽然该师正式解散日期为9月19日，但其指挥官和一些残部逃脱，成为第二次组建的基础。<cr><cr>该师的第二次组建于1941年10月15日从第5步兵旅开始。第5步兵旅在1941年10月5日被重新命名为摩尔曼斯克步兵旅，也被称为格里夫尼克旅。摩尔曼斯克步兵旅最初于1941年7月组建。该旅与苏联第88步兵师一起，在巴巴罗萨行动期间对抗芬兰第三军的J集团和德国武装党卫军北方师。他们击退了两支敌军，迫使芬德联军撤退到靠近托波泽罗湖的城市凯斯特加纳。该旅由一些地方民兵、第104步兵师的第242团以及可能来自同一师的一个炮兵团组成。

该师在 Karelia 继续作战直至战争结束。1942年4月，它成为第32集团军的一部分。从1944年6月至8月，它参加了 Svir-Petrozavodsk 进攻，在此期间参与了南部 Karelia 的收复行动。<cr>此次进攻取得的进展导致芬兰在9月份结束了继续战争。继续战争结束后，该师于1945年5月成为白海军区别洛莫尔斯克驻地第4步兵军的一部分。<cr><cr>

text: The 28th Army was formed in June 1941 from the Arkhangelsk Military District. It included the 30th and 33rd Rifle Corps, 69th Motorised Division, artillery and several other units. The Army Commander was Lieutenant General Vladimir Kachalov (previously commander of the Arkhangelsk Military District). Members of the army's Military Council were Brigade Commissioner Vasily T. Kolesnikov, and Army Chief of Staff Major General Pavel G. Egorov.<cr>On 14 July 1941, the order creating the Reserve Front gave the 28th Army's composition as nine divisions, one gun, one howitzer, and four corps artillery regiments, and four anti-tank artillery regiments.<cr>It participated in the Battle of Smolensk and was encircled in the Smolensk Pocket and destroyed. Army headquarters was disbanded on 10 August. Subordinate units that broke out were used to form the Reserve Front, along with units from other armies.<cr>General Kachalov was killed by artillery fire on 4 August 1941 during the breakout from the encirclement. He was buried in the village of Stodolische. Lacking accurate information regarding his death, Stalin allowed him to be named as a traitor and sentenced to death in absentia. Only on 23 December 1953, well after the war ended, did the Supreme Court overturn the order.<cr>The army was subsequently reformed again in November 1941 and September 1942. The third formation began on September 9, from forces assigned to the Stalingrad Military District and Southeastern Front, and was tasked with defending the port city of Astrakhan on the Caspian Sea's northern coast, as well as the lower reaches of the Volga. The army was under the command of Lt. Gen. V.F. Gerasimenko, with Corps Commissar A.N. Melnikov and chief of staff Mjr. Gen. S.M. Rogachevsky making up the rest of the army's Military Council. On its formation it was under the direct command of the STAVKA, but on September 30 it was subordinated to the Stalingrad Front.<cr>As of November 19, the army's ration strength was 64,265 men, with 47,891 men assigned to its combat forces. It fielded 1,196 guns and mortars and 80 tanks (10 heavy, 26 medium and 44 light).<cr>On 1 July 1944 the army comprised the 3rd Guards Rifle Corps (50th, 54th and 96th Guards Rifle Divisions), 20th Rifle Corps (48th and 55th Guards Rifle Divisions, 20th Rifle Division), the 128th Rifle Corps (61st, 130th, and 152nd Rifle Divisions) artillery units including the 3rd Corps Artillery Brigade, 157th Cannon Artillery Brigade, 377th Cannon Artillery Regiment, 530th Fighter Anti-Tank Artillery Regiment, 1st Mortar Brigade (from the 5th Breakthrough Artillery Division), 133rd and 316th Guards Mortar Regiments, 12th Anti-Aircraft Artillery Division (836th, 977th, 990th, 997th Anti-Aircraft Artillery Regiments), 607th Anti-Aircraft Artillery Regiment, tank forces, engineers, and other troops.<cr><cr>
translation: 第28集团军成立于1941年6月，由阿尔汉格尔斯克军区组建。该集团军包括第30步兵军、第33步兵军、第69摩托化师、炮兵和其他一些单位。集团军司令为列宁格勒方面军前指挥官瓦列里·卡查洛夫少将。军事委员会成员有旅政委瓦西里·科列斯尼科夫和集团军参谋长帕维尔·叶戈罗夫中将。<cr>1941年7月14日，建立预备方面军的命令将第28集团军编成公布为九个师、一个加农炮团、一个榴弹炮团以及四个军属炮兵团和四个反坦克炮兵团。<cr>该集团军参加了斯摩棱斯克战役，并在斯摩棱斯克包围圈中被消灭。司令部于8月10日解散，突围出来的下属单位与其他军队的部队一起组建了预备方面军。<cr>卡查洛夫将军于1941年8月4日在突破包围圈时遭炮火击毙，葬在斯托多利谢村。由于缺乏关于他死亡的确切信息，斯大林允许将他定为叛徒，并缺席判处死刑。直到1953年12月23日，在战争结束后很久，最高法院才推翻了这一命令。<cr>该集团军于1941年11月和1942年9月再次重组。第三次组建始于1942年9月9日，由斯大林格勒军区和东南方面军的部队组成，并负责保卫里海北部海岸上的港口城市阿斯特拉罕以及伏尔加河下游地区。集团军由少将V.F.杰拉斯梅尼科夫指挥，军政委A.N.梅利尼科夫和参谋长中将S.M.罗加乔夫斯基构成军事委员会的其余部分。组建之初直接隶属于最高统帅部大本营，但于9月30日转隶斯大林格勒方面军。<cr>截至1942年11月19日，集团军的给养人数为64,265人，其中47,891人被分配到作战部队。该集团军拥有1,196门火炮和迫击炮以及80辆坦克（包括10辆重型、26辆中型和44辆轻型）。<cr>至1944年7月1日，该集团军编成第3近卫步兵军（第50、54和96近卫步兵师）、第20步兵军（第48和55近卫步兵师以及第20步兵师）、第128步兵军（第61、130和152步兵师）炮兵部队包括第3军炮兵团、第157榴弹炮团、第377榴弹炮营、第530战斗机反坦克炮兵营、来自第5突破炮兵师的第1迫击炮团、第133和第316近卫迫击炮营以及第12防空高射炮师（包括第836、977、990和997防空高射炮营）和第607防空高射炮营，坦克部队、工兵和其他部队。<cr>

text: In June, the 28th Light Division struck into Russia with Army Group Centre, and fought at Smolensk and in the drive on Moscow, where it suffered heavy casualties. In November, the 28th Division was transferred to France, where it was converted into a Jger division.<cr>Early in 1942, the 'new' 28th reappeared on the Eastern Front, this time on the southern sector, and fought on the Kerch peninsula and in the final assault on the naval fortress of Sevastopol in the Crimea. Transferred to the northern sector with von Manstein's 11th Army, the Jger troops were earmarked for attachment to Finland, but they were held up by order of Field Marshal Georg von Kchler, who committed them to action with his Army Group North near Demyansk in late 1942. In January and February 1943, the 28th fought in the Second Battle of Lake Ladoga and remained in the northern zone until mid-1944. Meanwhile, the 28th Jger absorbed the https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Luftwaffe_Field_Division on February 20, 1944. In July, the division was attached to Group von Saucken and tried to prevent the encirclement of the bulk of the 4th Army near Minsk, but failed. Assigned to the tactically bankrupt Army Group Center, the 28th Jger suffered heavy losses in the retreat into Poland, where it took part in the fighting near the old Brest-Litovsk fortress in the Polish marchland. It was pushed back into East Prussia in September 1944, and fought there for eight months. The remnants of the division, less than a thousand men, ended the war in the Heiligenbeil Pocket. It surrendered to the Russians on May 8, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. Mitcham Jr.

text: The corps was formed for the assault on Viipuri during the Winter War. At the outbreak of hostilities in June 1941, it was stationed along the border in Belarus and consisted of 6th and 42nd Rifle Divisions. Elements of both divisions were present during the defense of the Brest-Litovsk Fortress. The corps headquarters was disbanded in July 1941. The corps was reformed in July 1943 at Kursk as part of 70th Army and took part in the Battle of Kursk , the Lublin-Brest Offensive, and the Berlin Strategic Offensive. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King

text: The 28th Rifle Division was known as the 2nd Consolidated Rifle Division during the Russian Civil War before being renamed the 28th Rifle Division. It was subsequently renamed the 28th Highland Mountain Division in the 1930's. In September 1936 it was renamed once again becoming the 28th Highland Mountain Division named for S. Ordzhonikidze and in July 1940, the 28th Red Banner Mountain Rifle Division named for S. Ordzhonikidze. The division was destroyed during the Kiev in September 1941. The division was reformed at Archangelsk. In November 1942 it fought at Velikie Luki and at the Battle of Trgu Frumos. The division was disbanded in October 1945.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

The 28th Tank Corps was formed in July 1942 near Stalingrad with:<cr>

32nd Motorized Rifle Brigade<cr><cr>The 28th Tank Corps was formed in the worst possible circumstances, with brigades that had all been smashed in combat and hurriedly reformed, and sent into action barely formed in front of a major German offensive across the Don River in front of Stalingrad. Going into action under the equally-raw 1st Tank
Army HQ in July, in less than a month 28th Tank Corps was reduced to just 39th and 55th Tank Brigades, and those had few if any tanks left. By 1 September the remnants of the corps were sent back into Stalingrad Front reserves. On 18 September, near Nizhne-Povolzhiya in Stalingrad Military District, the staff of 28th Tank Corps began reforming as 4th Mechanized Corps.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp

text:
The 28th Tank Division was formed in February 1941 from 27th Light Tank Brigade in the Baltic Special Military District. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
55th Tank Regiment
56th Tank Regiment
28th Motorized Rifle Regiment
28th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
28th Reconnaissance Battalion -
28th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
28th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>The 28th Tank Division is famous in Soviet Army lore because of its leadership. The division commander. Colonel Chernyakovskii, went on to become the youngest Front commander in the Red Army (he rose from Colonel to Colonel-General in 3 years ! ) , and the commander of 55th Tank Regiment was one of the
first Heroes of the Soviet Union in the war. The division was nearly complete in artillery and personnel, but had no modern tanks and only 230 light tanks, mostly BT-5 and BT-7 types, and a 'handful' of old T-28 medium tanks, on 22 June 1941.<cr>The 28th Motorized Rifle regiment was separated from the rest of the division and went into battle independantly along the Baltic coast. The remainder of the division suffered heavy casualties from German air attacks in the first days of the war, so 125th Tank Regiment, from 202nd Mechanized Division, was placed under 28th Tank's command on 26 June and served with the division from then on. Retreating across the Baltic states, on 14 September the division HQ also took control of 3rd NKVD Motorized Rifle Regiment.<cr>In November 1941 the remnants of the division were reorganized as 241st Rifle Division.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: The 290th Infantry Division invaded the Soviet Union with the LVI Panzer Corps of Army Group North in June 1941. It was an effective fighting unit. The 290th Infantry spearheaded the initial attack into Russia and played a major role in the capture of Dvinsk. In August it fought in the First Battle of Lake lImen and was surrounded in the Demyansk Pocket in January 1942. The divisions freedom of action was not restored until February 1943. It then fought at Dno, Lake Ladoga, and the Battle of Nevel that winter. By the fall of 1943, the division was down to six grenadier battalions and its tank destroyer and reconnaissance battalions had been consolidated into a single schnelle battalion. The division suffered heavy losses in the Leningrad withdrawal and was isolated in the Memel by October. Its 503rd Grenadier Regiment was disbanded that fall, and it was down to four grenadier battalions and three artillery battalions. It remained in the Courland Pocket, holding off several Soviet attacks, until March 1945, when it boarded ships and was sent to Neutief on the Frische Nehrung in East Prussia. It both inflicted and suffered heavy casualties in the last Soviet attempts to crush the Army of East Prussia. The 290th Infantry Division remained isolated in East Prussia until the end of hostilities and surrendered to the Red Army in May 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第290步兵师于1941年6月随北方集团军群的LVI装甲军入侵苏联，是一支有效的战斗部队。该师在初期进攻俄罗斯时担任先锋，并在占领德维纳过程中发挥了重要作用。8月，它参加了第一次伊利门湖战役，在1942年1月被包围于德梅耶斯克包围圈中。直到1943年2月，该师的行动自由才得以恢复。随后，它参与了多诺、拉多加湖和内夫尔冬季战役。到1943年秋季，该师只剩下六个掷弹兵营，其坦克歼击车营和侦察营被合并为一个快速营。在列宁格勒撤退中遭受重大损失后，该师于10月被孤立在梅梅尔。同年秋天，它的第503掷弹兵团被解散，仅剩下四个掷弹兵营和三个炮兵营。直到1945年3月，它一直坚守库尔兰包围圈，并击退了多次苏联进攻。该师于1945年3月登船前往东普鲁士弗里施海湾区的纽蒂夫。在苏军最后几次试图摧毁东普鲁士集团军时，第290步兵师既造成了重大伤亡也遭受了重大损失。直到战争结束，它一直被孤立在东普鲁士，并于1945年5月向红军投降。<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷：二战中的第1至第290步兵师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text:
The 290th Rifle Division began forming on 12 July 1941 at Kalyazin in the Moscow Military District from reservists. Its basic order of battle included the 878th, 882nd, and the 885th Rifle Regiments, as well as the 827th Artillery Regiment. After only five weeks, the division was assigned to the 50th Army. In late September, the division was encircled in the Bryansk pocket by Operation Typhoon, the German advance on Moscow. The division's remnants broke out from the pocket by 23 October. On 27 November the 827th Artillery Regiment was removed from the division and replaced by the 1420th Artillery Regiment on 22 January 1942. In May, the 290th transferred to the Western Front's 10th Army. During the last four months of 1943, the division was part of the 33rd Army, 49th Army, and the 68th Army, as it advanced from Smolensk to the Mogilev-Orsha line on the Dnieper. At the end of the year, the 290th transferred back to the 10th Army, but in spring 1944 it was moved to the 49th Army. The division fought in Operation Bagration and was awarded the Order of Kutuzov, 2nd class, for recapturing Grodno. By August it began to outrun its supply lines, and received 1200 rear area conscripts and militia from Grodno, and 380 newly drafted civilians from areas it advanced through as replacements. 

In September, the 290th was transferred to the 3rd Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front, with which it fought in the Vistula-Oder Offensive and the East Pomeranian Offensive in early 1945. At the very end of the war, the 3rd Army was transferred to the 1st Belorussian Front, and became part of the front reserve during the Battle of Berlin. By the end of the war, the division's honorifics were 'Mogilev, Order of the Red Banner, Orders of Suvorov and Kutuzov.'<cr><cr>
translation:
第290步兵师于1941年7月12日在莫斯科军区的卡利亚津从预备役人员开始组建。其基本战斗序列包括878团、882团和885团，以及827炮兵团。仅五周后，该师就被分配给第50集团军。9月下旬，在台风行动中，德军向莫斯科推进时，该师被包围在布良斯克包围圈内。到10月23日，该师残部成功突围。11月27日，827炮兵团从该师撤出，并于1942年1月22日由第1420炮兵团替换。5月，第290步兵师转隶到西方方面军的第10集团军。在1943年的最后四个月里，该师隶属于第33集团军、第49集团军和第68集团军，在从斯摩棱斯克推进至第聂伯河莫吉廖夫-奥尔沙线的过程中作战。年末，第290步兵师再次转隶到第10集团军，但在1944年春季被调往第49集团军。该师参加了巴格拉季昂行动，并因重新夺回格罗德诺而获得库图佐夫二级勋章。

8月开始，该师的补给线逐渐紧张，从格罗德诺征召了1200名二线地区新兵和民兵作为补充人员，同时在推进过程中还征用了380名新征募的平民。9月，第290步兵师被调往第二白俄罗斯方面军的第3集团军，在该方面军的维斯瓦河-奥得河攻势和东波美拉尼亚攻势中作战。战争末期，第3集团军转隶到第一白俄罗斯方面军，并成为柏林战役中的预备队之一。到战争结束时，该师获得了“莫吉廖夫、红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫勋章和库图佐夫勋章”的荣誉称号。

text: On June 22-23, the first two days of the invasion, the 291st penetrated forty-four miles in the first thirty-four hours-an astonishing total for a non-motorized infantry division in combat. It soon loosely surrounded Riga and repulsed several desperate attempts by the Soviet garrison to break out of the city. Although casualties were heavy, the division held its line, and contained and eventually helped destroy the Russian garrison. Later that year, it took the major Soviet naval base at Liepaja after a bitter struggle.<cr>Remaining with Army Group North, the 291st fought in the Battle of Volkhov (January-March 1942) before being transferred to the Velikie Luki sector of Army Group Center in late 1942. It held a sector of the line here for several months. During the winter of 1942-43, three of its grenadier battalions were disbanded and the remnants were merged together to form a single ski battalion. In October 1943, it joined Army Group South, fought at Kiev, suffered heavy losses in the retreat through the northern Ukraine and, as part of the 1st Panzer Army, again suffered heavy losses in the Kamenets-Podolsky ('Hube Pocket') battles of 1944. (During these battles, the 1st Panzer Army was surrounded but-brilliantly led by General Hube-it formed a 'floating pocket' and broke out, despite the efforts of several Soviet armies to destroy it.)<cr>The 291st was rebuilt as a 1944 type division in February 1944, when each of its grenadier regiments was reduced to two battalions. It also absorbed the 1st Reserve Grenadier Regiment of the 141st Reserve Division. Several months later, on September 10, 1944, it also absorbed the 1135th Grenadier Brigade. Although still greatly reduced in numbers, the 291st took part in the retreat across eastern Poland and fought in the Vistula campaign of late 1944. The veteran infantry division was finally smashed on January 27, 1945, when it tried unsuccessfully to block the Soviet advance into Silesia. The following month, the remnants of the Elk Division were placed under the command of a special staff, directed by Colonel Georg Heinlein (commander of the 504th Grenadier Regiment) and were absorbed by the 6th Infantry Division.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 6月22日至23日，入侵的前两天，第291师在最初的34小时内推进了约44英里——对于一个非摩托化步兵师来说，这是一个惊人的战绩。它很快松散地包围了里加，并击退了苏联守备部队几次绝望的突围尝试。尽管伤亡惨重，该师坚守住了阵地，并最终帮助摧毁了俄罗斯守备部队。同年晚些时候，在一场激烈的战斗后，第291师占领了列瓦达的主要苏联海军基地。<cr><cr>之后，它一直隶属于北方集团军群，在沃尔霍夫战役（1942年1月至3月）中作战，然后在1942年底被调往中央集团军群的维捷布斯克地区。在这里坚守了一段时间。<cr><cr>1942-1943年的冬天，该师解散了三个掷弹兵营，并将剩余部队合并成一个滑雪营。1943年10月，它加入南方集团军群，在基辅助战中作战，撤退时在乌克兰北部遭受重大损失，作为第1装甲集团军的一部分，在卡缅斯克-波多利斯基（“胡贝包围圈”）战役中再次遭受重大损失。<cr><cr>（在这场战斗中，第1装甲集团军被包围了——但由胡贝将军指挥得当——它形成了一个‘漂浮的包围圈’并成功突围，尽管几支苏联军队试图将其摧毁。）第291师于1944年2月重建为1944型步兵师，当时每个掷弹兵团都缩减到只有两个营。该师还吸收了第141预备师的第1预备掷弹兵团。几个月后，在1944年9月10日，它又吸收了第1135掷弹兵旅。<cr><cr>尽管人数仍然大幅减少，但第291师参与了从东波兰撤退，并参加了1944年末的维斯瓦河战役。这支部队在1945年1月27日试图阻止苏联军队进入西里西亚时被彻底击溃。<cr><cr>次月，埃尔克师残部由特别指挥部指挥（该指挥部由第504掷弹兵团团长乔治·海因莱因上校领导），并被第6步兵师吸收。<cr><cr><cr>资料来源：《二战中的命名步兵师和特殊师——德国战斗序列卷二 291至999师》，山缪尔·W·米奇姆少校。<cr>

text:
With the inclusion of regular Red Army cadre, the 291st Rifle Division was formed from the barely raised 11th Moscow Militia Division on the 12th of July 1941, at Rybinsk.

Barely a month later the Division was engaged in the defense of Leningrad, assigned to the 23rd and then 55th Army until 1943.

With the lifting of the siege the Division was assigned to the 67th and then 21st Army, fighting its way across Poland, Germany and into Czechoslovakia.

The Division was awarded the Order of the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Kutuzov and the honorific GATCHINA.

text: The 292nd Infantry Division crossed the Bug River with Army Group Center in June 1941, it fought at Brest and Bialystok, in the Battle of the Yelnya Bend, at Vyazma, and in the subsequent drive on Moscow. It helped check the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42, took part in the defensive actions of 1942 (including Gshatsk and Vjasma), the Rzhev withdrawal (1943), the Battle of Kursk (where it sustained heavy casualties), and Gomel. It took part in the fighting on the Sozh and the Pripjet (Pripyet) marshes, Pinsk, Ostrow, and Narev, and in theretreat in to Poland. Down to battle group strength, it retreated through Poland and was destroyed in the Heiligenbeil Pocket in East Prussia in March 1945. Its survivors were absorbed by other divisions on the Hela peninsula that same month.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. text:
The 292nd Rifle Division started forming on the 2nd July 1941 from reservists in the Moscow Military District. Only partially formed the Division was rushed north for the defense of Leningrad in August 1941. The Division took part in battles on the Volkhov river and at Tikhvin but suffered such heavy casualties it was disbanded in November 1941.

The Division was raised for the third time in July 1943 from reserves of the Transbaikal Front. It spent the remainder of the war in the Soviet Far East and took part in the invasion of Manchuria.

text: The 293rd Infantry Division crossed into Russia on June 22 and fought at Brest-Litovsk, Pinsk, Gomel, Kiev, and Bryansk and against the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42. It occupied a sector near Mzensk (not far from Orel) from February to September 1942, and a zone in the vicinity of Bolchov (also near Orel) until June 1943. It fought in the Battle of Kursk in July and at Bryansk in August, and suffered heavy losses at Kharkov in September. Remaining in the line at Kampfgruppe strength, the 293rd fought at Krementschug and Uman in October and November. The battered division was downgraded to Division Group 293 on November 2, 1943, and was assigned to Corps Detachment A. It was finally destroyed at Jassy, Romania, in August and September 1944.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. text:
The 293rd Soviet Rifle Division had a fortunate history in that it was on the periphery of a number of major military disasters in 1941/42 but escaped the fate of being encircled and destroyed.

The Division started forming on the 18th July 1941, at Sumy, from reservists in the Kharkov Military District. The Division was rushed into the defense of Kiev in August 1941 but avoided being trapped in the Kiev pocket and spent the winter in the vicinity of Kursk. 

In 1942 the Division was involved in fighting around Kharkov, assigned to the 21st Army, and once again avoided being trapped, like some of its fellow divisions. The Division retreated all the way to the Don and was withdrawn into Reserve into the Southern Urals, as it was down to about 1,500 men. In October 1942 the Division was back to near full strength and fought with some distinction at Stalingrad. For this it was renamed the 66th Guards Rifle Division in January 1943.

The Division was raised for the second time in July 1943 from reserves of the Transbaikal Front. It spent the remainder of the war in the Soviet Far East and took part in the invasion of Manchuria.

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner.



Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第293步兵师在1941至1942年间经历了幸运的历史，尽管它位于多次重大军事灾难的边缘地带，但最终避免了被包围和消灭的命运。

该师于1941年7月18日在苏米从哈尔科夫军区的预备役人员中组建。该师在1941年8月匆忙投入基辅防御战，但未陷入基辅包围圈，并在库尔斯克附近度过了冬季。

1942年，该师参与了哈尔科夫周边地区的战斗，隶属于第21集团军，再次避免了被围困的命运。该师撤退至顿河地区，并因兵力减少到约1500人而转入预备队，在乌拉尔南部休整。1942年10月，该师恢复了接近满员的状态，并在斯大林格勒战役中表现出色。为此，它于1943年1月被改编为第66近卫步兵师。

该师第二次组建是在1943年7月从远东方面军的预备役人员中招募而成。剩余战争期间一直在苏联远东地区作战，并参与了满洲国入侵行动。

该师荣获红旗勋章。

text: The 294th Infantry Division crossed into southern Russia in the summer of 1941 and was involved in the drive on Kiev, in the capture of Kharkov and the Donetz, and in the checking of the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42. Remaining with Army Group South, it was used to stabilize the 3rd Romanian Army in the fall of 1942, and suffered heavy casualties when the Romamans collapsed and set up the Stalingrad debacle.<cr>The bulk of the 8th Luftwaffe Field Division was attached to the 294th in late 1942 during the retreat from the Volga. Remaining in the line, the 294th Infantry fought on the Mius and at Stalino, and was later encircled at Taganrog in August, and again sustained heavy losses in the ensuing breakout. After this, the veteran division was reorganized. It absorbed the remnants of the 333rd Infantry Division and now included the 513rd and 514th Grenadier Regiments (two battalions each), Divisional Group 333 (with the 679th and 680th Regimental Groups), the 333rd Fusilier Battalion, the 333rd Artillery Regiment, the 294th Artillery Regiment, the combined 294th Tank Destroyer/Reconnaissance Battalion, and the usual divisional supply units. The 294th Infantry Division returned to the front and fought in the Nikopol Bridgehead and at Odessa. It was again surrounded and finally destroyed at Kischinev, Romania, west of the lower Dnestr, on August 26, 1944. The few soldiers that escaped the disaster were on leave or in medical facilities. They were attached to the 333rd Infantry Division, which absorbed them when the 294th Infantry Division was officially disbanded on October 9, 1944.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第294步兵师于1941年夏季进入南俄，并参与了对基辅的进攻、哈尔科夫和顿涅茨河地区的占领，以及对抗苏联在1941-1942年冬季发动的攻势。该师一直隶属于南方集团军群，在1942年秋季被用于稳定第3罗马尼亚集团军的战线，并在罗马尼亚军队崩溃导致斯大林格勒灾难时遭受了重大伤亡。<cr>大部分第8空军野战师于1942年末在从伏尔加河撤退期间并入第294步兵师。该师继续坚守前线，在米乌斯河和斯塔里诺夫作战，并于同年8月在塔甘罗格被包围，再次遭受重大损失。之后，这支部队重新整编，吸收了第333步兵师的残部，包括两个掷弹兵团（每个团有两个营）：第513掷弹兵团和第514掷弹兵团、第333师团群（包含第679团群和第680团群）、第333轻步兵团、第294炮兵团、联合的第294歼击坦克/侦察营，以及通常的师级补给单位。该师重返前线，在尼科波尔桥头堡和敖德萨作战，并于1944年8月26日在罗马尼亚下德涅斯特河以西的基希讷乌再次被包围并最终被消灭。少数幸存士兵当时正在休假或在医疗设施中，他们随后被编入第333步兵师，在该师吸收了这些人员后，第294步兵师于1944年10月9日正式解散。<cr>德国战斗序列 第二卷 291-999 步兵师、命名步兵师和特殊部队在二战中的运用，萨缪尔·W·米奇姆少校

text:
The 294th Rifle Division started forming on the 10th July 1941 at Lipetsk, from reservists in the Orel Military District. The Division was given 2 months to complete formation and then moved north for the defense of Leningrad in September 1941. The Division took up positions east of the city in the Volkhov river area. In March 1942 the divisional commander, A.A. Kichkailov, was killed in action and the division suffered heavy casualties.

In May 1943 the division was assigned to the 52nd Army with which it remained till the end of the war. The Division fought in the Ukraine, Poland, Germany and Czechoslovakia

text: The 295th Infantry Division was formed in February 1940 as part of the 8th Wave. It contained the 516th, 517th and 518th Infantry Regiments, 295th Artillery Regiment and various support units. The division was part of the IV Army Corps in Army Group South at the start of Operation Barbarossa. The division was destroyed at Stalingrad in January 1943. In March 1943 it was sent to Norway where it served as a static fortress division. Over the next few months it expanded to two regiments with four battalions each. text:
The 295th Rifle Division started forming on the 10th July 1941 at Chuguyev, from reservists in the Kharkov Military District, and by August was defending Kiev. The Division was trapped and destroyed in the Kiev pocket, although one infantry regiment did escape.

The Division was formed for a second time near Kursk, in October 1941 and was assigned to the 37th Army of the Southern Front. In June 1942 the division performed defensive operations and retreated into the Caucasus, all the way to the Terek River. With the Axis retreat the division distinguished itself in the pursuit and the recapture of Kherson in late 1943.

In 1944 the Division fought in the Ukraine and late that year, assigned to the 32nd Rifle Corps, 5th Shock Army ended the war in Berlin. 

A highly decorated Division, it was awarded the Order of Lenin, Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov and the honorific KHERSON.





Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第295步兵师于1941年7月10日在丘古耶夫开始组建，由哈尔科夫军区的预备役人员组成，并在8月份防守基辅。该师被困并在基辅包围圈中被消灭，尽管有一个步兵团成功逃脱。

该师于1941年10月在库尔斯克附近第二次组建，并被分配给南方方面军第37集团军。1942年6月，该师执行防御任务并撤退至高加索地区，一直撤到特erek河。随着轴心国的撤退，该师在追击和重新占领赫尔松的过程中表现出色，时间是在1943年末。

1944年，该师在乌克兰作战，并于当年晚些时候被分配给第32步兵军、第5突击集团军，在柏林结束战争。

这是一支获得多项荣誉的师级部队，曾获列宁勋章、红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫勋章以及赫尔松荣誉称号。

text:
The 296th Rifle Division was formed in early July 1941 in the Odessa Military District and in August was assigned to the 9th Army of the Southern Front. In March 1942 the Division was assigned to the 37th Army and avoided destruction at Kharkov. The Division was pursued by Axis forces all the way into the Caucasus and by August 1942, had suffered such heavy casualties that it was disbanded. The remnants were used as reinforcements for the 242nd Rifle Division.
 
The Division was formed for a 2nd time in July 1943, in Georgia, and spent the rest of the war on the Turkish or Iranian border.

text: The 297th Infantry Division first saw action in Russia with Army Group South in July 1941. It fought at Zhitomir (July), Uman (August), Kiev (September), Kharkov (November), and Rostov (November-December), and opposed the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42. In 1942, it was with the 6th Army in the Battle of Kharkov, in the clearing of the Izyum Pocket, in the drive across the Don, and in the Battle of Voronezh. It was subsequently encircled at Stalingrad with the 6th Army and destroyed there on January 25, 1943. <cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. text:
The 297th Rifle Division started forming on the 2nd July 1941 at Lubny, from reservists in the Kharkov Military District and later on elements of the Kremenchug Militia Division, and by September was assigned to the defense of Kiev. The Division was lucky to escape the Kiev pocket and in October was assigned to the 21st Army in the Kursk sector.

In May 1942 the Division was initially held in reserve during the 2nd Battle of Kharkov but suffered such heavy casualties in defensive operations and the subsequent retreat that it was disbanded in July 1942.

The Division was formed for a second time on the 25th July 1943 from the 253rd Rifle Brigade and was assigned to the 33rd Rifle Corps of the Southwestern Front. The Division fought with some distinction, including the siege of Budapest, and ended the war fighting near Vienna, assigned to the 46th Army.

A decorated Division, it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky and the honorifics KIROVOGRAD and SLAVYANSK.





Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第297步兵师于1941年7月2日在卢布内开始组建，由哈尔科夫军区的预备役人员和克雷门楚格民兵师的部分成员组成。到9月份，该师被分配至基辅防御任务。幸运的是，该师成功逃离了基辅包围圈，并在10月份被调往库尔斯克地区的第21集团军。

1942年5月，该师最初作为预备队参与第二次哈尔科夫战役，但在防御作战和随后的撤退中遭受严重伤亡，最终于1942年7月解散。

第297步兵师于1943年7月25日再次组建，由第253步兵旅组成，并被分配至西南方面军第33步兵军。该师在战斗中有出色表现，包括布达佩斯围城战，并最终在维也纳附近作战，隶属于第46集团军。

作为荣誉部队，该师获得红旗勋章、博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基勋章以及基洛夫格勒和斯拉夫扬斯克的荣誉称号。

text:
The 298th Rifle Division started forming on the 2nd July 1941, at Kalinin, from reservists in the Moscow Military District and by September was assigned to the 13th Army, Bryansk Front. When the Axis resumed the drive on Moscow, the Division was trapped in the Bryansk pocket and destroyed. 

The Division was formed for a second time in January 1942, at Barnaul, in the Siberian Mlitary District and was assigned to the 50th Army of the Western Front. As the Axis closed in on Stalingrad the Division was transferred south to the Stalingrad sector where it fought with distinction in the Soviet offensive. The Division was assigned to the 21st Army in mopping up the pocket and in March 1943 was renamed the 80th Guards Rifle Division.

The Division was formed for a third time in July 1943, in the Transbaikal Front, and in 1945 was assigned to the 36th Army where it took part in the invasion of Manchuria. For this action it was awarded the honorific of 'KHINGAN'.

translation:
第298步兵师于1941年7月2日开始在加里宁组建，由莫斯科军区的预备役人员组成，并于9月被分配给布良斯克方面军的第13集团军。当轴心国重新发动对莫斯科的攻势时，该师被困在布良斯克包围圈中并被消灭。

该师于1942年1月在巴尔瑙勒再次组建，位于西伯利亚军区，并被分配给西部方面军的第50集团军。当轴心国逼近斯大林格勒时，该师被调往南部的斯大林格勒战区，在苏联攻势中表现出色。该师随后被分配给第21集团军进行清剿包围圈的任务，并于1943年3月改名为第80近卫步兵师。

该师第三次组建是在1943年7月，位于外贝加尔方面军，并在1945年被分配给远东第一方面军的第36集团军，参加了入侵满洲的行动。为此行动，该师获得了“兴安”的荣誉称号。

text: The 297th Infantry Division was involved in the initial invasion of southern Russia in June 1941, and was almost continuously engaged after that, fighting at Zhitomir and Kiev, in the Donets, and at Kursk (1941). It held a sector in the vicinity of Livny (east of Orel) from January 1942 to August 1943. That fall it fought in the Battles of Bryansk and Gomel in 1943, and distinguished itself as a good combat division, although three of its infantry battalions had to be disbanded due to heavy casualties. The survivors of these units were transferred to other grenadier battalions within the division.<cr>On June 22, 1944, the Russians launched their massive summer offensive with 2.5 million men, and their opening attack struck the 299th Infantry; it collapsed within a few hours. Only remnants escaped, but these (along with men returning from leave or convalescent facilities) were used to form a new 299th Infantry Division. This formation, a mere skelton of the original 299th, was the former Corps Detachment G and included the former Division Groups 57, 299, and 337 (now the 528th, 529th, and 530th Grenadier Regiments, respectively), the 299th Artillery Regiment, and assorted divisional troops. It took part in the Polish campaign of 1944 and in the retreat behind the Vistula, and it continued to fight on the Eastern Front until February 26, 1945, when it was practically destroyed on the Heiligenbeil landfront in northern East Prussia. The remnants of the 299th Infantry Division were officially disbanded on April 4, 1945. Its survivors were used to help form Infantry Division Schlageter (RAD Division Nr. 1).<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第297步兵师参与了1941年6月对南俄的初始入侵行动，并在此之后几乎持续作战，参加了在日托米尔、基辅以及顿涅茨河和库尔斯克（1941）的战斗。从1942年1月至1943年8月，该师驻守奥廖尔以东利夫尼地区的防区。<cr>1943年秋天，它参加了布良斯克和戈梅利战役，并作为优秀的作战师而著称，尽管其三个步兵营因伤亡惨重不得不解散。这些单位的幸存者被转移到了师内的掷弹兵营中。<cr>1944年6月22日，苏联发起了拥有250万兵力的大规模夏季攻势，其首次攻击就击溃了第299步兵师；该师仅在几个小时内便土崩瓦解。只有残部得以逃脱，但这些（加上从休假或疗养设施返回的人员）被用来重新组建新的第299步兵师。<cr>这一新编成的部队只是原第299步兵师的一个骨架，包括了原来的军直属队G和第57、299、337师部（现分别为第528、529和530掷弹兵团），以及第299炮兵团和其他师属单位。它参加了1944年的波兰战役，并在撤退至维斯瓦河后继续在东线作战，直至1945年2月26日在北部东普鲁士的海利根贝伊尔陆战区几乎被消灭。<cr>第299步兵师的残部于1945年4月4日被正式解散。其幸存者被用来帮助组建施拉格特尔步兵师（RAD步兵师编号1）。<cr> <cr>德国战斗序列 第二卷 291至999步兵师、命名步兵师及特种部队，二战中的德军步兵师，山缪·W. 米奇姆少校

text: The 29th Army was first formed in July 1941 in the Moscow Military District on the basis of 30th Rifle Corps. The 245th, 252nd, 254th and 256th Rifle Divisions, and a number of smaller units made up the Army. It joined the Reserve Front and conducted defensive works at Staraya Russa, Demyansk, Ostashkov, Selizharovo. It was reassigned on July 21, 1941, to the Western Front, took part in the Battle of Smolensk, conducted defensive fights in area to the south of the city of Toropets. On October 17 it joined the Kalinin Front and participated in the defense of Kalinin, and the Kalinin, Rzhev-Vyazma 1942, and Rzhev-Sychyovka offensive operations (the Battles of Rzhev). From the end of August 1942 the army defended occupied boundaries on the left bank of the Volga River. In the beginning of February, 1943 the Army's units were transferred to 5th and 20th Armies, and the headquarters was reorganised as headquarters 1st Tank Army.<cr><cr>
translation: 第29集团军成立于1941年7月，隶属于莫斯科军区，并以第30步兵军为基础组建。该集团军包括第245、252、254和256步兵师以及若干较小单位。它加入预备方面军，在斯塔罗柳萨、德米扬斯克、奥斯塔什科夫和塞利扎罗沃等地进行防御工事建设。1941年7月21日，该集团军被调往西方面军，并参加了斯摩棱斯克战役，在托尔佩茨城南部地区进行了防御战斗。10月17日，它加入加里宁方面军并参与了加里宁的防御以及1942年的加里宁、列日夫-维亚兹马和列日夫-苏奇奥夫卡进攻行动（列日夫战役）。从1942年8月底开始，该集团军在伏尔加河左岸占领区进行防御。1943年2月初，其部队被转移到第5集团军和第20集团军，司令部重组为第1坦克集团军司令部。<cr> <cr>

text: The 29th Mechanized (Motor Rifle) Division was formed at Omsk as the 4th Rifle Division in September 1920. In November of the same year it became the 29th Rifle Division. It became a motorized division in July 1940. At the start of At the start of Operation Barbarossa the division was deployed with the Western Special Military District. The division was destroyed near Minsk in July of 1941 and formally disbanded in September. The division was reformed from the 7th Moscow People's Militia Division in July 1941 and destroyed at Vyazma in October 1941.<cr>On December 5, 1941, the reforming of the 29th Rifle Division began in Akmolinsk, Kazakhstan and its organization was completed on January 16, 1942. The division was reformed on the basis of the short lived 459th Rifle Division. The division was consisted of the 106th, 128th and 299th Rifle Regiments, the 77th Artillery Regiment, the 125th Anti-Tank Battalsion and various other support units. The division was held in reserve until June 1942, when its men were deemed to have received sufficient training. In July 1943 the 29th Rifle Division was ordered to Stalingrad and joined the 64th Army. In August 1942 units of the division first made contact with the Germans. During the Battle of Stalingrad they killed 5,242 and took 13,447 Axis soldiers captive. For its service at Stalingrad the 29th Rifle Division was redesignated the 72nd Guard Rifle Division by Directorate of the General Staff order ?104 on March 1, 1943.<cr>The 29th Rifle Division was recreated in 1943 and saw action at Kirovograd. It gained the honorific 'Polotsk' serving with the 6th Guards Army of the Kurland Group in May 1945. <cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第29机械化（摩托化步兵）师于1920年9月在奥姆斯克作为第4步兵师组建。同年11月，该师改名为第29步兵师。1940年7月，该师成为摩托化师。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师部署在西部特别军区。1941年7月，该师在明斯克附近被消灭，并于同年9月正式解散。1941年7月，第29步兵师从第7莫斯科民兵师重组，并于10月在维亚兹马被消灭。<cr>1941年12月5日，第29步兵师的重建工作开始于哈萨克斯坦阿克莫林斯克，并于1942年1月16日完成组建。该师是在短命的第459步兵师基础上重组而成的。该师由第106、128和299步兵团，第77炮兵团，第125反坦克营以及各种支援单位组成。直到1942年6月，认为士兵们已经接受了足够的训练后，该师才被投入预备队。<cr>1943年7月，第29步兵师奉命前往斯大林格勒，并加入第64集团军。1942年8月，该师首次与德军接触。在斯大林格勒战役中，他们杀死了5,242名轴心国士兵并俘虏了13,447人。<cr>由于在斯大林格勒的出色表现，第29步兵师于1943年3月1日被总参谋部命令重新指定为第72近卫步兵师。<cr>1943年，第29步兵师再次重建，并在基洛夫格勒作战。<cr>该师在1945年5月与第6近卫集团军的库尔兰集团服役时获得了“波洛茨克”荣誉称号。

text: The 'Falcon Division', as it was nicknamed, performed in an outstanding manner in all of its battles. Crossing into Russia in 1941, it fought in the Bialystok and Minsk encirclements, in the Dniepr crossings, at Smolensk, Bryansk, Tula (in the Moscow sector), and against the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42. In 1942, it fought in the 2nd Battle of Kharkov, in the Don crossings, in the drive on the Volga and at Stalingrad, where it was itself surrounded in November 1942, and was destroyed in the southern Stalingrad pocket on January 31, 1943. Even as late as January 12, 1943, when it was in its death throes, the 29th, together with the 3rd Motorized Infantry Division, repulsed ten to twelve Soviet divisions and knocked out 100 tanks, all in a single day.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 绰号为“猎鹰师”的该部队在所有战斗中表现出色。1941年进入俄罗斯后，参加了比亚韦斯托克和明斯克的包围战、第聂伯河的渡河作战、斯摩棱斯克战役、布良斯克战役以及图拉（莫斯科地区）的防御，并对抗了苏联于1941-42年的冬季攻势。1942年，该师参加了第二次哈尔科夫战役、顿河的渡河作战、向伏尔加河推进的战斗和斯大林格勒战役，在1942年11月自身被包围后，于1943年1月31日在南部斯大林格勒包围圈中被消灭。甚至在1943年1月12日，该师处于垂死挣扎时，与第3摩托化步兵师一起，在一天内击退了十到十二个苏联师，并摧毁了100辆坦克。<cr>德国战斗序列 第三卷 - 二战中的德军装甲、装甲掷弹兵和武装党卫军师<cr>萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: The corps was originally designated the 29th Lithuanian Territorial Rifle Corps and consisted of troops of the former Lithuanian National Army. At the outbreak of hostilities in June 1941, it was part of 11th Army and consisted of 179th and 184th Rifle Divisions. It fought around Velikiye Luki in July-August 1941 and launched a successful counterattack against 19th Panzer Division on July 21st that temporarily recaptured the city. The corps was disbanded in September 1941. It was reformed in July 1943 in Kursk as part of 13th Army and participated in the Battle of the Dnieper of 1943, and the Belorussian Offensive of June-August 1944. <cr><cr> <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军最初被指定为第29立陶宛领土步兵军，并由前立陶宛国民军的部队组成。在1941年6月战争爆发时，它是第11集团军的一部分，包括第179和第184步兵师。它于1941年7月至8月在维捷布斯克附近作战，并于7月21日对第19装甲师发起了成功的反击，暂时收复了该城市。该军于1941年9月被解散。它于1943年7月在库尔斯克重建为第13集团军的一部分，并参加了1943年的第聂伯河战役和1944年6月至8月的白俄罗斯进攻。<cr> <cr> <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert, 红军战斗序列在伟大的卫国战争中，Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text:
The 29th Rifle Division was officially redesignated as a motorised division on 4 July 1940. With 6th Mechanized Corps, 10th Army, Western Front on 22 June 1941. Poirer and Connor appear to say it was wiped out near Minsk in July 1941. It was formally disbanded on 19 September 1941.<cr><cr>It was then recreated from the 7th Moscow People's Militia Division in July 1941, and again wiped out at Vyazma in October 1941.<cr><cr>On December 5, 1941, recreation of the 29th Rifle Division began in Akmolinsk, Kazakhstan, and its organization was completed on January 16, 1942. It was reformed on the basis of the very short lived 459th Rifle Division. The division was made up of 106th, 128th, 299th Rifle and 77th Artillery Regiments. Other units included the 125th Anti-Tank, 78th Sapper, 124th Signal, and 29th Medical Battalions, and the 104th Reconnaissance Company. The division was held in reserve until June 1942, when its men were deemed to have received sufficient training.

In July 1942 29th Rifle Division was ordered to move to Stalingrad and join the 64th Army. In August 1942 units of the division first met with the Germans. During Battle of Stalingrad they killed 5,242 and took 13,447 captive.

On February 2, 1943, the Battle of Stalingrad was finally over. Due to the heroism of the soldiers, the 29th Rifle Division (2nd formation) was redesignated the 72nd Guards Rifle Division by Directorate of the General Staff order No.104 on March 1, 1943.<cr><cr>The 29th Rifle Division was recreated in 1943 and saw action at Kirovograd. It gained the honorific 'Polotsk' and the Order of Suvorov, 2nd class. With 6th Guards Army of the Kurland Group (Leningrad Front) May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第29步兵师于1940年7月4日正式改编为摩托化师。1941年6月22日，该师隶属于西方方面军的第6机械化军和第10集团军。<cr>指挥官报告显示该师在1941年7月明斯克附近被消灭。<cr>它于1941年9月19日正式解散。<cr>然后，该师于1941年7月从第7莫斯科民兵师重建，并于1941年10月在维亚兹马再次被消灭。<cr>1941年12月5日，第29步兵师开始在哈萨克斯坦的阿克莫林斯克重建，其编制于1942年1月16日完成。<cr>该师基于短命的第459步兵师重组。该师由第106、第128和第299步兵团以及第77炮兵团组成。<cr>其他单位包括第125反坦克营、第78工兵营、第124通信营和第29医疗营，以及第104侦察连。该师一直作为预备队直到1942年6月，当时认为其士兵已经接受了足够的训练。<cr>指挥官报告显示，1942年7月，第29步兵师被命令前往斯大林格勒并加入第64集团军。1942年8月，该师的部队首次与德军交战。<cr>在斯大林格勒战役期间，他们杀死了5,242人，并俘虏了13,447人。<cr>指挥官报告显示，1943年2月2日，斯大林格勒战役终于结束。由于士兵们的英勇表现，第29步兵师（第二次组建）于1943年3月1日被总参谋部命令第104号重新指定为第72近卫步兵师。<cr>该师于1943年重建，并在基洛夫格勒作战。它获得了“波洛茨克”的荣誉称号和苏沃罗夫勋章二级奖章。1945年5月，隶属于列宁格勒方面军的第6近卫集团军（库尔兰集团）。<cr>

text:
The 29th Tank Corps was formed February 1943 in Moscow Military District as part of STAVKA Reserves.The 29th Tank Corps was immediately (15 March 1943) assigned to 5th Guards Tank Army, which was being reformed after the winter battles. The corps remained under 5th Guards Tank Army until May 1945. By 1 July 1943 the tank army was in Steppe Front behind the Kursk salient.<cr>On the morning of 12 July, in the 'biggest tank battle of the war' at Prokhorovka, 29th Tank Corps was right in the middle of 5th Guards Tank Army's attacking line. The corps lost 60% of its tanks on that day and the next, and spent the last two weeks of July repairing and average of 20 tanks a day to
rebuild the tank brigades. 29th Tank Corps fought in the Battle of Kharkov and the advance to the Dnepr River throughout August-December 1943. In September 1943 1549th Heavy SU Regiment (SU-152s) was added to the corps, and in October 1943 the corps finally received its rocket unit: 11th Guards Mortar Battalion (8 BM-13 launchers) . 38th Armored Car Battalion was removed after the Kursk Battle, and the 1446th SU Regiment re-equipped with SU-85s sometime in late 1943. Also during the continuous reinforcement of the corps to try to cover the casualties, all the tank brigades were completely re-equipped with T-34 tanks in 3 tank battalions of 65 tanks by the end of 1943.<cr>29th Tank Corps also received recognition for its performance in combat. On 10 December 1943 the corps received the honorific title 'Znamenskikh' for liberating Znamensk, and on 8 January 1944 the corps received the Order of the Red Banner for its performance in the Kirovograd Operation. In February, for its exploits during the Korsun-Shevchenkovskii ('Korsun Pocket') Operation, the 1549th Heavy SU Regiment became the 339th Guards Heavy SU Regiment, and then was removed from the corps so it could be sent into reserve and re-equipped. In May 1944 29th Tank Corps and 5th Guards Tank Army finally went into reserve after 9 months of almost continuous combat.<cr>The 29th Tank Corps was committed in the drive into the southern Baltic states in July 1944, and fought in that region for the rest of 1944. In addition to its assigned units, the corps frequently controlled or was directly supported by units from 5th Guards Tank Army and other units.In October 1944, 165th was redesignated as a Light Artillery Regiment (still with 24 76mm guns) and assigned to 29th Tank Corps permanently. When the Soviet offensives started in January 1945, 29th Tank Corps had been built up.<cr>On 14 January 1945, when the corps went over to the offensive, it had 149 tanks and 111 SUs on hand - which meant that the tank brigades were slightly under strength (averaging 50 tanks each out of 65 authorized) but the 4 SU regiments in the corps were almost 1/3 over strength! 29th Tank Corps ended the war in May 1945 in East Prussia, still part of 5th Guards Tank Army.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第29坦克军于1943年2月在莫斯科军区组建，作为最高统帅部大本营的预备部队。该坦克军于1943年3月15日立即被分配给正在重组的第5近卫坦克集团军，后者是在冬季战斗后进行重建。直到1945年5月，该军一直隶属于第5近卫坦克集团军。<cr>截至1943年7月1日，坦克集团军位于斯捷普方面军，在库尔斯克突出部的后面。<cr>在7月12日上午进行的“战争中最大的坦克战斗”——普罗霍罗夫卡战役中，第29坦克军处于第5近卫坦克集团军攻击线的中心位置。<cr>该军在这两天内损失了60%的坦克，并且在接下来的两周里每天平均修复20辆坦克以重建坦克旅。<cr>1943年8月至12月，第29坦克军参加了哈尔科夫战役和向第聂伯河推进的战斗。<cr>1943年9月，重型SU-152自行火炮团（1549团）加入该军。同年10月，该军终于收到了火箭部队：第11近卫迫击炮营（8门BM-13发射器）。<cr>库尔斯克战役后，装甲车团第38团被移除。<cr>1446团自行火炮也于1943年底某个时候重新装备了SU-85。在持续增援该军以弥补伤亡的过程中，所有坦克旅都完全换装为T-34坦克，在三个坦克营中每营有65辆坦克，到1943年底为止。<cr>第29坦克军也在战斗中获得了认可。1943年12月10日，该军因解放扎缅斯克而获得“扎缅斯克”荣誉称谓；1944年1月8日，该军又因为在基洛夫格勒行动中的表现被授予红旗勋章。2月份，在科尔孙-舍甫琴科夫斯基（“科尔孙包围圈”）行动中，第1549重型SU团成为第339近卫重型SU团，并随后从军中调出进入预备队并重新装备。1944年5月，第29坦克军和第5近卫坦克集团军在连续作战9个月后终于转入预备队。<cr>1944年7月，该军被投入到向波罗的海南部诸州的进攻中，并于同年余下的时间里一直在该地区作战。除了其编配单位外，该军还经常控制或直接得到第5近卫坦克集团军和其他部队的支持。<cr>1944年10月，第165团被改编为轻型炮兵团（仍配备24门76毫米火炮），并永久分配给第29坦克军。当苏联攻势于1945年1月开始时，第29坦克军已经得到了加强。<cr>1945年1月14日，该军转入进攻时拥有149辆坦克和111辆SU——这意味着坦克旅的编制略低于满编（平均每个旅有50辆坦克，而授权编制为65辆），但军中的4个SU团则几乎超编三分之一！第29坦克军在1945年5月结束战争时仍属于第5近卫坦克集团军。

text: The 2nd Air Army was formed on May 12, 1942, by an order of the NKO of May 5, 1942, within the Bryansk Front.<cr> It participated in defensive battles in the Voronezh sector, and then supported the troops of the Southwestern Front during the Battle of Stalingrad. In collaboration with the 8th, 16th and 17th Air Armies it fought for air superiority over the battlefield. The army participated in the Battle of Kursk , the Battle of the Dnieper, Zhitomir-Berdichev Offensive, the Korsun-Shevchenkovsky Offensive, Rivne-Lutsk, Proskurov-Chernivtsi, Lvov-Sandomierz, Sandomir-Silesian, Lower Silesian Offensive, Upper Silesian Offensive, Battle of Berlin and the Prague Offensive.<cr><cr>
translation: 第2空军集团军成立于1942年5月12日，根据1942年5月5日的苏联人民国防委员会命令，在 Bryansk 方面军内组建。它参与了沃罗涅日地区的防御战斗，并随后支持西南方面军在斯大林格勒战役中的作战行动。<cr>与第8、第16和第17空军集团军合作，争夺战场上的制空权。该部队参加了库尔斯克会战、第聂伯河会战、热季奥尔-别列齐夫攻势、科尔松-舍甫琴科夫斯基攻势、利沃夫-桑多梅日攻势、桑多米尔-西里西亚攻势、下西里西亚攻势、上西里西亚攻势、柏林战役和布拉格攻势。

text: The corps was formed in April 1941 and consisted of the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Airborne Brigades. In 1941, it fought as a part of the40th Army in Southwestern Front to defend Kiev. It escaped the collapse of the Kiev pocket in August with heavy losses and fought in the vicinity of Sumy in September. The corps was transferred to the Taman peninsula as part of 47th Army in May 1942 and converted to the 32nd Guards Rifle Division. in August. Hero of the Soviet Union Mikhail Tikhonov commanded the corps from July, 1941 until its conversion, and then commanded the division thereafter. The corps was reformed in December 1942 and converted, probably into a Guards Airborne Division in spring 1943.<cr><cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军成立于1941年4月，由第2、第3和第4空降旅组成。1941年，它作为西南方面军第40集团军的一部分，在基辅助防御战中作战。8月，该军在基辅包围圈崩溃时遭受重大损失后逃脱，并于9月在苏米附近继续战斗。1942年5月，该军被转移到塔曼半岛，成为第47集团军的一部分，并于同年8月改编为第32近卫步兵师。<cr>苏联英雄米哈伊尔·季霍诺夫从1941年7月至改编时一直指挥该军，之后继续指挥该师。该军在1942年12月重组并可能在1943年春季改编为空降师。<cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军战斗序列：伟大卫国战争, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 2nd Army was activated on October 20, 1939 with General Maximilian von Weichs in command. First seeing service in France, the army was involved in the invasion of the Balkans, before offensive operations in the Ukraine as part of Operation Barbarossa.<cr>In 1942 the 2nd Army covered the northern wing of operation Fall Blau operating in the surroundings of Voronezh and suffered a major defeat during the soviet winter offensive that followed the battle of Stalingrad.<cr>In 1945 the army was redisgnated Army East Prussia and was pivotal in the defence of East and West Prussia before finally surrendering on 9 May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第2集团军于1939年10月20日成立，由马克斯米利安·冯·维克斯将军指挥。该集团军首次在法国服役，随后参与了入侵巴尔干的行动，在巴巴罗萨行动中又参加了乌克兰地区的进攻。<cr>1942年，第2集团军负责蓝色行动北部翼侧作战，在沃罗涅日周边地区活动，并在斯大林格勒战役后苏联冬季攻势中遭受重大失败。<cr>1945年，该集团军被改编为东普鲁士集团军群，并在保卫东、西普鲁士的战斗中发挥了关键作用，最终于1945年5月9日投降。

text: The 2nd Belorussian Front was created in February 1944 as the Soviets pushed the Germans back towards Byelorussia. General Colonel Pavel Kurochkin became its first commander. In hiatus in April 1944, its headquarters was reformed from the army headquarters of the disbanding 10th Army.<cr>On 26 June 1944 the Front's forces captured Mogilev in the Mogilev Offensive. On 4 July, 2BF was tasked with mopping up the remains of Army Group Center's 4th Army under the command of General Kurt von Tippelskirch and the remains of the 9th Army in a large pocket southeast of Minsk. On 9 July The 2BF attacks northwest from Vitebsk as part of a major Soviet offensive east of Riga towards Rezekne in order to cut off the German Army Group North. On 29 July Soviets reach the coast cutting Army Group North off in Estonia and Eastern Latvia. On 13 September 2BF captured Lom?a, west of Bialystok. In November 1944 Marshal Konstantim Rokossovsky was appointed commander of 2BF just in time for its last two great offensives of World War II. As part of a massive attack by four Fronts on 14 January 1945 2BF attacked East Prussia (East Prussian Offensive) and later Pomerania (East Pomeranian Offensive).<cr>On 9 April 1945 Konigsberg in East Prussia finally fell to the Red Army. This freed up 2BF to move west to the east bank of the Oder river. During the first two weeks of April the Soviets performed their fastest Front redeployment of the war. General Georgy Zhukov concentrated his 1st Belorussian Front (1BF) which had been deployed along the Oder river from Frankfurt in the south to the Baltic, into an area in front of the Seelow Heights. The 2BF moved into the positions being vacated by the 1BF north of the Seelow Heights. While this redeployment was in progress gaps were left in the lines and the remnants of the German 11th Army which had been bottled up in a pocket near Danzig managed to escape across the Oder.<cr>In the early hours on 16 April the final offensive of the war to capture Berlin and link up with Western Allied forces on the Elbe started with attacks by 1BF and To the south General Ivan Konev's 1st Ukrainian Front (1UF). On 20 April the 2BF join in the attack. By 25 April 2BF broke out of its bridge head south of Stettin and had by the end of the war captured all of Germany north of Berlin as far west as the front lines of the British 21 Army Group which had advanced over the river Elbe in some places.<cr><cr>Wikipedia 2nd Belorussian Front
translation: 第2白俄罗斯方面军成立于1944年2月，当时苏联军队将德军推回白俄罗斯。大将帕维尔·库罗奇金成为该方面军的第一任指挥官。1944年4月，其司令部由解散的第10集团军的集团军司令部重组而成。<cr>1944年6月26日，在莫吉廖夫攻势中，方面军部队占领了莫吉廖夫。7月4日，第2白俄罗斯方面军被命令肃清德中央集团军群第4集团军（由库尔特·冯·蒂佩尔斯基希将军指挥）和第9集团军在明斯克东南的大包围圈中的残部。<cr>1944年7月9日，作为苏联对里加以东的列茨克的重大攻势的一部分，第2白俄罗斯方面军从维捷布斯克向西北发起攻击，旨在切断德北方集团军群。7月29日，苏军抵达海岸，在爱沙尼亚和东部拉脱维亚切断了德北方集团军群。<cr>1944年9月13日，第2白俄罗斯方面军占领了比亚韦斯托克以西的洛马。1944年11月，元帅康斯坦丁·罗科索夫斯基被任命为第2白俄罗斯方面军指挥官，及时赶上该方面军在二战中的最后两次重大攻势。<cr>作为四大方面军的大规模攻击的一部分，1945年1月14日，第2白俄罗斯方面军发起了东普鲁士攻势（东普鲁士进攻），随后是波美拉尼亚攻势（东波美拉尼亚进攻）。1945年4月9日，东普鲁士的柯尼斯堡终于落入红军之手。这使得第2白俄罗斯方面军可以向西移动到奥得河东岸。在四月份的第一周半时间里，苏联完成了战争中最快的方面军重新部署。朱可夫将军将他指挥下的第1白俄罗斯方面军（1BF）从法兰克福以南的奥得河沿岸至波罗的海地区集中到了塞洛高地前方的一个区域。第2白俄罗斯方面军则移动到塞洛高地北部由第1白俄罗斯方面军撤离出来的位置。在重新部署的过程中，防线中留下了空隙，被围困在但泽附近的德国第11集团军残部得以穿越奥得河逃出包围圈。<cr>4月16日凌晨，战争中的最后一次进攻行动开始，目标是攻占柏林并与西线盟军在易北河会师。此次攻势由朱可夫将军指挥的第1白俄罗斯方面军和科涅夫将军指挥的第1乌克兰方面军发起。4月20日，第2白俄罗斯方面军加入攻击。到4月25日，第2白俄罗斯方面军突破了什切青以南的桥头堡，并在战争结束时占领了柏林以北的所有德国领土，最西边到达英军第21集团军群的前线。<cr>维基百科 第2白俄罗斯方面军

text: The corps consisted of 9th, 5th, and 72nd cavalry divisions and 15th Motor Rifle Division. It was part of the 9th Army in the Odessa area in June 1941. It fought in Ukraine in the summer of 1941 and then was withdrawn to STAVKA reserve in the fall. It was reorganized as 1st Guards Cavalry Corps in November 1941. It was reformed in December 1941 from 62nd, 64th and 70th Cavalry Divisions as part of Southern Front. It was destroyed in the Second Battle of Kharkov where it fought as part of 6th Army. The corps was officially disbanded 15 July 1942. <cr><cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军由第9、第5和第72骑兵师以及第15摩托化步兵师组成。它于1941年6月隶属于敖德萨地区的第9集团军。在1941年夏季，它在乌克兰作战，然后在秋季被撤回最高统帅部预备队。该军于1941年11月重组为第1近卫骑兵军，并于12月从第62、第64和第70骑兵师重新组建，成为南方方面军的一部分。它在第二次哈尔科夫战役中被消灭，在此役中隶属于第6集团军作战。该军正式解散日期为1942年7月15日。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军二战战斗序列, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text:
The 2nd Guards Airborne Division was formed from 7th Airborne Corps on 8 December 1942 in Zvenigorod. The division was fully equipped by January 1943 and concentrated in the area of Ostashkov. As a part of the 1st Shock Army, the division attacked the Demyansk Pocket on 26 February 1943. The division only advance 3 kilometers against the German forces and was replaced with the 250th Rifle Division after several days of heavy fighting. The division was transferred to the area of Slugin village. The division was now to take Lyahnovo village, which controlled a road out of the Demyansk Pocket. The 5th Guards Airborne Regiment crossed the Porus River and cut the road on 7 March. However, German counterattacks pushed the division out of Lyahnovo. The division was transferred to the rear afterwards.

The division then transferred to the 18th Guards Rifle Corps in the area of Kursk. They took positions in the second defensive line of the 13th Army, part of the Central Front. From 5 July to 23 August, the 2nd Guards Airborne fought in the Battle of Kursk. Between 26 August and 30 September, the division, now part of the 60th Army participated in the capture of Pryluky during the Chernigov-Pripyat Operation. On 2 October, the 7th Guards Airborne Regiment crossed the Dnieper, capturing a bridgehead near the village of Medwin in the Chernobyl Raion. On 18 November, it went to the village of Rakovic. It captured Radomyshl on 20 November as part of the 15th Rifle Corps. In January 1944, it fought in the Battle of the Korsun-Cherkassy Pocket. It captured Khmelnytskyi on 25 March during the Proskurov-Chernivtsi Offensive, for which it was given the title 'Proskurov'. On 29 March, it captured the villages of Berezhanka and Andreevka in the Chernivtsi Raion, in conjunction with the 62nd Guards Tank Brigade and the 64th Guards Tank Brigade. Between 13 July and 29 August, it fought in the Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive in Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast. As part of the 17th Guards Rifle Corps, it captured the villages of Akreshory and Prokurava on 12 September. With the aid of a Katyusha rocket launcher battery, the division captured the Haarde (mountain) in the Carpathian Mountains on 13 September. On 22 September, the division captured Vorokhta and Yablonitsky Pass. It entered the village of Tatarov on the next day. In October 1944, it fought in the Battle of the Dukla Pass. It captured Mukacheve on 26 October 1944. It captured Uzhhorod on the next day.

The division advanced into Czechoslovakia, capturing Michalovce on 26 November. In conjunction with the 5th Guards Tank Brigade, it captured Kralovsky Chlmec on 27 November. Between December 1944 and January 1945, it crossed the Hornad River and fought south of Kosice. On 25 March 1945, it fought in the Moravska Ostrava Operation and seized a bridgehead on the Oder on 19 April. After advancing across Czechoslovakia, the division was disbanded in late June 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
第2近卫空降师于1942年12月8日在兹韦尼哥罗德从第7空降军组建而成。该师在1943年1月全部装备完毕，并集中在奥斯塔什科夫地区。作为第1突击集团军的一部分，该师于1943年2月26日进攻德梅伊亚斯克包围圈。面对德国军队，该师仅推进了3公里，在几天激烈的战斗后被第250步兵师替换。随后该师被转移到斯卢金村地区。此时该师的任务是夺取利亚诺沃村，控制从德梅伊亚斯克包围圈出去的道路。1943年3月7日，第5近卫空降团渡过普鲁斯河并切断了道路。然而，德国的反攻将该师逐出了利亚诺沃村。之后该师被转移到后方。

该师随后转隶库尔斯克地区的第18近卫步兵军。他们占据了第13集团军第二道防线上的位置，隶属于中央方面军。从7月5日至8月23日，第2近卫空降师参加了库尔斯克战役。8月26日至9月30日期间，该师作为第60集团军的一部分参与了切尔尼戈夫-普里皮亚季行动中普里卢基的攻占。10月2日，第7近卫空降团渡过第聂伯河，在切诺比勒区梅德温村附近夺取了一个桥头堡。11月18日，该师前往拉科维奇村。11月20日，作为第15步兵军的一部分，它攻占了罗曼什尔。1944年1月，它参加了科尔松-切尔卡瑟包围圈战役。3月25日在普罗斯库罗夫-切尔尼夫策攻势中攻占赫梅利尼茨基后，该师被授予“普罗斯库罗夫”荣誉称号。3月29日，在第62近卫坦克旅和第64近卫坦克旅的配合下，它占领了切尔尼夫策区贝雷尚卡村和安德烈夫卡村。7月13日至8月29日期间，该师作为第17近卫步兵军的一部分，在伊万诺-弗兰科夫斯克州参加了利沃夫-桑多梅日攻势，并于9月12日攻占了阿克雷什奥里村和普库拉瓦村。借助喀秋莎火箭炮连的帮助，该师在9月13日占领了喀尔巴阡山脉的哈德山（山地）。9月22日，该师占领了沃罗赫塔和雅布隆茨基隘口。次日进入塔塔罗夫村。1944年10月，它参加了杜克拉山口战役。1944年10月26日，它攻占了穆卡切沃。次日攻占了乌日霍罗德。

该师进入捷克斯洛伐克，于11月26日占领米哈尔诺夫采。与第5近卫坦克旅协同作战，于11月27日占领克拉罗韦茨赫梅茨。从1944年12月至1945年1月期间，该师渡过霍拉德河并在科希策以南地区战斗。1945年3月25日，该师参加了摩拉维亚奥斯特拉发行动，并于4月19日在奥得河上夺取了一个桥头堡。在穿越捷克斯洛伐克后，该师于1945年6月底解散。<cr> <cr>

text: The 2nd Guards Army was formed according to the order of the Staff of the Supreme High Command (Stavka) from October 23, 1942, on the basis of the 1st Reserve Army. Formation and training took place in Tambov, Michurinsk and Morshansk areas. On 1 November 1942 the Combat composition of the Soviet Army lists 1st Reserve Army with the 1st Guards Rifle Corps - 24th Guards, 33rd Guards and 98th rifle divisions [under Guards General-Major I. I. Missan], and the 13th Guards Rifle Corps with the 49th Guards, 3rd Guards and 387th divisions.<cr>By the time of the Battle of Stalingrad, the 2nd Guards Army had become one of the most powerful units in the Red Army. The 2nd Guards Army appeared on the scene after the Soviet Operation Uranus had successfully encircled the German Sixth Army at Stalingrad in November 1942. In December 1942, as preparations started for Operation Saturn, the 2nd Guards Army was ordered by Joseph Stalin to prepare for an attack on Rostov. The assault and capture of Rostov was the ultimate goal of the Red Army for Operation Saturn.<cr>In December 1942, plans for Operation Saturn had to be altered. The German Operation Wintergewitter, led by Field Marshal Erich von Manstein's Army Group Don, made an attack on the Stalingrad Front in an effort to relieve the Sixth Army in Stalingrad. Thus, Operation Saturn was changed to Operation Little Saturn, which was to be a counter-attack that would be launched as soon as Operation Wintergewitter ended. The German forces, spearheaded by Army Group Hoth, made rapid initial advances but was stalled at the Myshkova River. Colonel-General Hermann Hoth's panzer divisions were at a standstill and were suffering heavy casualties, even before the bulk of the 2nd Guards Army had arrived. By this time, Manstein realized that the operation was a failure. The 2nd Guards Army, under General Rodion Malinovsky, had been transferred to the Stalingrad Front to halt the offensive. Stalin had agreed to this decision.<cr>In February 1944, the Army relocated to the area of the Perekop Isthmus. The Crimean Offensive was launched across the Perekop Isthmus on 8 April 1944 by elements of the 2nd Guards Army and 51st Army, under the 4th Ukrainian Front. In cooperation with other troops of the 4th Ukrainian Front and the Black Sea Fleet, Sevastopol was liberated on May 9, 1944. In May and June the 2nd Guards Army was relocated to the area of the cities Dorogobuzh Elnya. On May 20, was moved to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command and on July 8 the unit was a part of the 1st Baltic Front. By that time, it consisted of the 11th and the 13th and 54th Guards Rifle Corps. In this structure, on 520 July 1944 took part in the Vilnius Offensive/operation at the end of July, and in the Siauliai offensive reflect enemy counterattacks west and north-west of Siauliai. In October, the 2nd Guards Army participated in the Memel offensive. On December 20 it was reassigned to the 3rd Belorussian Front.<cr>During the East Prussian Offensive in January-April 1945, the army broke through long-term German strategic defenses, eliminated in conjunction with other troops surrounded the front of its group (south-west of Knigsberg and Samland group).<cr><cr>
translation: 根据最高统帅部大本营（Stavka）于1942年10月23日的命令，第2近卫集团军在第1预备集团军的基础上组建。编成和训练工作在坦波夫、米丘林斯克和莫尔尚斯克地区进行。1942年11月1日，苏军战斗编制中列出了第1预备集团军，包括第1近卫步兵军（含第24近卫师、第33近卫师和第98步兵师）[under Guards General-Major I. I. Missan]以及第13近卫步兵军（含第49近卫师、第3近卫师和第387师）。<cr>到斯大林格勒战役时，第2近卫集团军已成为红军中最强的部队之一。在苏联“天王星行动”于1942年11月成功包围德军第六集团军后，第2近卫集团军出现在战场上。1942年12月，在为“土星行动”做准备期间，约瑟夫·斯大林命令第2近卫集团军准备对罗斯托夫发起攻击。“土星行动”的最终目标是突袭并占领罗斯托夫。<cr>1942年12月，土星行动的计划不得不进行调整。由元帅埃里希·冯·曼施坦因指挥的顿河集团军群发起的冬季风暴行动，对斯大林格勒方面军发动了攻击，试图解救被困在斯大林格勒的第六集团军。因此，土星行动被改为小土星行动，这将是一次反攻，在冬季风暴行动结束后立即展开。德军部队由霍特集团军群领衔，初期进展迅速，但在米什科沃河受阻。霍特上将指挥的装甲师陷入停滞，并遭受了严重损失，甚至在第二近卫集团军主力到达之前就已经如此。此时，曼施坦因意识到行动失败了。第二近卫集团军，在马林诺夫斯基将军的指挥下，被转移到斯大林格勒方面军以阻止进攻。斯大林同意了这一决定。<cr>1944年2月，该集团军迁至佩雷科普地峡地区。1944年4月8日，在第四乌克兰方面军的指挥下，由第二近卫集团军和第51集团军的部分部队发起了穿越佩雷科普地峡的克里米亚攻势。在第四乌克兰方面军其他部队及黑海舰队的配合下，塞瓦斯托波尔于1944年5月9日获得解放。5月至6月间，第二近卫集团军迁至多罗戈布日和埃尔尼亚两城附近地区。5月20日被调往最高统帅部预备队，在7月8日成为第一巴尔干方面军的一部分。此时该集团军编有第11、第13及第54近卫步兵军。在此编制下，于1944年7月5日至月底期间参加了维尔纽斯攻势/行动，并在希奥利艾攻势中反击了敌人从希奥利艾西面和西北面的反攻。10月，第二近卫集团军参与了梅梅尔攻势。12月20日被调至第三白俄罗斯方面军。<cr><cr>在1945年1月至4月进行的东普鲁士攻势中，该集团军突破了长期的德国战略防御阵地，并与其它部队配合消灭了包围其集团正面（柯尼斯堡西南及萨姆兰岛）的敌人。<cr><cr><cr>

text: Formed 11/26/1941 from 9th Cavalry Division as part of I Guards Cavalry Corps, it was part of Southwestern Front reserve. It was awarded the honorific titles 'Krimskaya' and 'In the name of the Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic'. Fought in the Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive and the Dniepr-Carpathian Offensive in 1944 and in the Battle of Berlin in 1945 as part of 1st Ukrainian Front. <cr><cr>Pettibone, Charles D., The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II: volume V - Book B Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Trafford, 2009<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 1941年11月26日由第9骑兵师改编，成为第一近卫骑兵军的组成部分，并隶属于西南方面军预备队。它获得了“克里米亚”和“为了乌克兰苏维埃社会主义共和国”的荣誉称号。参加了1944年的利沃夫-桑多梅日进攻战役和第聂伯河-喀尔巴阡山脉进攻战役，以及1945年第一乌克兰方面军的柏林战役。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>战斗序列<cr>Pettibone, Charles D., 《二战中各国军队的编制与战斗序列：卷V-B 苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟》，Trafford，2009年<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: Formed in the Tambov area on 15 October 1942 from elements of the 22nd Guards Rifle Division, the 2nd Guards Mechanized Corps was under the command of Major General Karp Sviridov and subordinated to the Southern Front and the 2nd Guards Army until late 1943, at which time the corps became a front-level asset and fought with the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th Ukrainian Fronts for the rest of the war. By the end of the war, the 2nd Guards Mechanized Corps commanded the 4th, 5th, and 6th Guards Mechanized Brigades, as well as the 37th Guards Tank Brigade. The corps fought at Stalingrad in 1942-43, at Melitopol in 1943, Odessa and Budapest in 1944, and Vienna in 1945. The 2nd Guards Mechanized Corps finished the war as part of the 6th Guards Tank Army in the area of Benesov, Czechoslovakia, on 9 May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
1942年10月15日，第2近卫机械化军在坦波夫地区组建，由第22近卫步兵师的部分部队组成。该军由卡普·斯维里多夫少将指挥，并隶属于南方方面军和第2近卫集团军，直到1943年底，之后该军成为方面军级别的资产，并与第2、第3和第4乌克兰方面军一起作战直至战争结束。

到战争结束时，第2近卫机械化军指挥着第4、第5和第6近卫机械化旅以及第37近卫坦克旅。该军参加了1942-43年的斯大林格勒战役、1943年的梅利托波尔战役、1944年的敖德萨和布达佩斯战役，以及1945年的维也纳战役。

1945年5月9日，第2近卫机械化军作为第6近卫坦克集团军的一部分，在捷克斯洛伐克的贝内绍夫地区结束战争。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text:
For distinguished combat service, the 127th Rifle Division was renamed to 2nd Guards Rifle Division 18 September 1941. At the end of September 1941, it fought in Hlukhiv area, retreating toward Kleven river as part of the General A.N. Ermakov's operational group of the Bryansk Front. 3 October 1941 the division was transferred to Kursk area and fought a defensive battle around Tim town.

22 December 1941, the division has started to advance as a hart of Winter Campaign of 1941-42. Acting together with the 1st Guards Rifle Division and 87th Rifle Division, it advanced through Cheremisinovo and Sovetsky districts of the Kursk Oblast. By 28 January 1942, the division was located in Stary Oskol.

After participating in the Novorossiysk-Taman Offensive in September-October 1943, the division was renamed to 2nd Guards (Tamanskaya) Motor Rifle Division after the city of Taman, Russia. Starting from 3 November 1943, the division acted in the spearhead of Kerch-Eltigen Operaton in northern Yenikale (Ganikale) beachhead, under the command of the 56th Army.

During the Crimean Offensive the division has liberated Alushta city 15 April 1944, acting under command of Separate Coastal Army. 19 May 1944 it was relieved from the front line duty, reassigned to the Soviet Stratgic Reserve, 2nd Guards Army and transferred to Dorogobuzh for replenishment. It restarted combat operations 8 July 1944 after the 2nd Guards Army was given to the 1st Baltic Front. The division participated in Siauliai Offensive and later in October 1944 - in Battle of Memel. In December 1944, the entire army including the 2nd Guards Motor Rifle Division was transferred to 3rd Belorussian Front and participated in the East Prussian Offensive, ending the war in middle April 1945 on the Baltic Sea coast north of Primorsk.<cr><cr>
translation:
为了表彰其出色的战斗服务，第127步兵师于1941年9月18日改名为第2近卫步兵师。1941年9月底，该师在霍卢希夫地区作战，并作为布良斯克方面军安·尼·叶梅利亚科夫将军行动小组的一部分撤退至克莱文河附近。1941年10月3日，该师被调往库尔斯克地区，在蒂姆镇周围进行防御战斗。

1941年12月22日，该师开始作为1941-42冬季战役的一部分推进。与近卫步兵师和第87步兵师协同作战，它通过库尔斯克州的切雷米希诺夫区和索维茨基区前进。到1942年1月28日，该师位于斯塔里奥斯科尔。

该师参加了1943年9月至10月的诺沃罗西斯克-塔曼进攻后，于1943年11月3日改名为第2近卫（塔曼）摩步师。此后，该师在56集团军指挥下，在杰尔宾特北部的亚尼凯勒海滩头担任尖刀部队，参与刻赤-埃尔蒂琴行动。

在克里米亚攻势期间，该师于1944年4月15日解放了阿卢什塔市，并受命于独立海岸集团军指挥。1944年5月19日，它从一线撤出，被重新分配到苏联战略预备队和第2近卫集团军，并转移到多罗戈布日进行补充。1944年7月8日，在第2近卫集团军被调至波罗的海第1方面军后，该师恢复了作战行动。参加了希奥利艾攻势，并于1944年10月参与了梅梅尔战役。1944年12月，整个集团军包括第2近卫摩托化步兵师被调至白俄罗斯第3方面军，并参加了东普鲁士攻势，在1945年中旬的波罗的海沿岸普里莫尔斯克以北结束了战争。<cr><cr>，<cr>。

text: The 2nd Guards Tank Army was created in January 1943. In spring and summer of 1943 2nd GTA was engaged in the fierce battles at Sevsk and Kursk . The Army played a critical role in containing a strike by the 3rd Panzer Korps in February 1944 to rescue the German units in Cherkassy Pocket. In March-April 1944 2nd GTA carried out a deep raid to Uman and was amongst the first Russian units to cross the Romanian border. In May-June 1944 Army was engaged in combat at Trgu Frumos and Jassy. The rapid and deep 2nd GTA tank raid from Kovel to Warsaw forced German command to engage five German panzer divisions against it. These included the 3rd SS Panzer Division Totenkopf, 5th SS Panzer Division Wiking ,4th Panzer Division, 19th Panzer Division and the Hermann Goering Division. This tank battle fought in July-August 1944 near Warsaw was the biggest tank engagement on the Eastern Front in 1944. German panzer divisions managed to push back units of the 2nd GTA but were not able to destroy it. In January 1945 2nd GTA just in a few weeks swiftly advanced from the Vistula to the Oder river, defeated strong German troops in Pomerania and ended the war by capturing Berlin.<cr><cr>
translation: 第2近卫坦克集团军成立于1943年1月。在1943年的春季和夏季，第2近卫坦克集团军参与了塞夫斯克和库尔斯克的激烈战斗。该集团军在1944年2月对切尔卡瑟包围圈中的德军部队进行救援行动时发挥了关键作用，成功遏制了第3装甲军的攻势。1944年3月至4月期间，第2近卫坦克集团军深入乌曼地区，并成为第一批越过罗马尼亚边境的苏联单位之一。在1944年5月至6月期间，该集团军参与了特古夫鲁莫斯和雅西地区的战斗。从科韦尔到华沙的快速而深远的第2近卫坦克集团军突袭迫使德军调动五个装甲师来应对：包括第3党卫军装甲师骷髅、第5党卫军装甲师威金、第4装甲师、第19装甲师和赫尔曼·戈林装甲师。这场于1944年7月至8月在华沙附近进行的坦克战是当年东线最大的一次坦克战斗。德军装甲师虽然成功击退了第2近卫坦克集团军的部分单位，但未能将其彻底摧毁。1945年1月，在短短几周内，第2近卫坦克集团军从维斯瓦河迅速推进至奥得河，并在波美拉尼亚地区击败了强大的德军部队，最终通过占领柏林结束了战争。<cr><cr><cr><cr>
