text: The 24th Tank Corps was renamed the 2nd Guards Tank Corps for it's actions during the raid on Tatsinskaya.<cr>2nd Guards Tank Corps was initially based on the same units as 24th Tank Corps. The individual combat units were also renamed and renumbered as Guards units. With changing organization and equipment during the war, additional units were added. Depending on the specific tasks allotted to the Corps, units from the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (Stavka Reserve (RVGK)) could be added to help it achieve its mission.<cr>During 1943 it fought in the Third Battle of Kharkov, the Battle of Kursk, the Battle of Prokhorovka, Operation Polokovodets-Rumyantsev and the Battle of Smolensk.<cr>1944 saw it engaged in Operation Bagration, the Minsk Offensive and the Baltic Offensive.<cr> In 1945 it participated in the Vistula-Oder Offensive, the East Prussian Offensive, and the assault on Berlin.<cr><cr>
translation: 第24坦克军因塔季斯卡亚突袭期间的表现而改名为第2近卫坦克军。<cr>第2近卫坦克军最初基于与第24坦克军相同的单位，各个战斗单位也被重新命名为近卫部队并重新编号。随着战争中编制和装备的变化，又增加了其他单位。根据赋予该军的具体任务，可以从最高统帅部预备队（大本营预备队）调派单位以帮助其完成使命。<cr>1943年，它参加了第三次哈尔科夫战役、库尔斯克会战、普罗霍罗夫卡之战、波洛可沃德-鲁缅采夫行动和斯摩棱斯克战役。<cr>1944年，它参与了巴格拉季昂行动、明斯克攻势和波罗的海攻势。<cr> 1945年，它参加了维斯瓦河—奥得河攻势、东普鲁士攻势以及对柏林的突击。<cr><cr>

text: At the end of June, 1941, Germany summoned Hungary to join in the attack on the Soviet Union. Hungary continued to resist joining in the war. The matter was settled on June 26, 1941, when the Soviet air force bombed Kosice(Kassa).<cr>The Kingdom of Hungary declared war on the Soviet Union the next day, June 27, 1941. At first, only Hungary's 'Karpa Group' with its integral 'Rapid Corps' (Gyorshadtest) was sent to the Eastern Front, in support of the German 17th Army. Towards the end of 1941, only the exhausted and battle weary 'Rapid Corps' was left. But, before Hungarian Regent Admiral Mikls Horthy would gain Adolf Hitler's consent to withdraw the 'Rapid Corps', he had to agree to deploy an even larger Hungarian force.<cr>Of the 3 Hungarian field armies, high command decided to send the 2nd Army. (The 1st one was considered to be the 'best' and the 3rd Army was still being organized). However the Armed Forces in general were so poorly equipped that practically all 'modern' equipment (which was still dated by contemporary standards) was provided to the 2nd Army. Even after these desperate measures the 2nd Army still lacked adequate motorized transport and especially anti-armor weapons. Germany has promised to provide the necessary equipment, but failed to deliver any meaningful quantities. Practically all the armoured units Hungary had were re-organized into the 1st Hungarian Armored Division and attached to the 2nd Army. Similarly, almost all combat-worthy aircraft and supporting units were organized into the 1st Flight Group, also attached to the 2nd Army. For both the armored and air units, shortages in supplies and equipment lead to significant delays and they were shipped to Russia significantly later than infantry units.<cr>By April 11, 1942, the 209,000-man-strong Second Army was assigned to the German Army Group South in southern Russia. In June, 1942, the Second Army became part of Army Group B in Operation Blue (Fall Blau). Transportation of the army to the frontline began on 17th April 1942, and the last units arrived by 27th June.<cr>In June and July 1942, prior to the Battle of Stalingrad, the Hungarian Second Army was involved in the Battle of Voronezh as part of Army Group B. Fighting in and around the city of Voronezh on the Don River, the Hungarian troops supported the German 4th Panzer Army against the defending Soviet Voronezh Front. Though technically an Axis success, this pyrrhic victory fatally delayed the arrival of the 4th Panzer Army in the Caucasus. During these operations, the Hungarian Second Army has suffered severe casualties in manpower as without adequate air and armor support all assaults were carried out by infantry units only, against the skillful and determined defense conducted by the Soviet troops.<cr>The Hungarian Second Army is probably the best known Hungarian wartime army because of the part it played in the Battle of Stalingrad. Before being sent to Russia, the rank-and-file of the Second Army had received but eight weeks of training. The only tactical experience for many of these soldiers were the maneuvers held just prior to the departure for the front. This lack of preparation badly affected the soldiers' fighting abilities and morale when confronted with heavy tank assaults. Also, a significant part of the army was made up by reservists (officers and enlisted men alike), who were promised a 'quick victory' and became demoralized as their prospects for getting home soon were worsening.<cr>In 1942, the Hungarian Second Army was given the task of protecting the 8th Italian's Army northern flank between Novaya Pokrovka on the Don River and Rossosh. This allowed the German Sixth Army to continue to attack Soviet General Vasily Chuikov's 62nd Army defending Stalingrad. As winter set in, and with the worsening German situation around Stalingrad, the 2nd Army's transportation collapsed and failed to supply even the basics (food, winter clothing, heating fuel, building materials) for the frontline units. The cold, hungry and demoralized 2nd Army had to defend even longer and longer stretches of the frontline as more and more German units were sent to Stalingrad.<cr>The Hungarian Second Army, as almost all of the armies protecting the flanks of the Sixth Army, was annihilated when the Soviets launched Operaton Uranus, and Operation Little Saturn. As part of these operations, two Soviet pincers drove through the Romanian 3rd Army to the north of Stalingrad and the Romanian 4th Army to the south, cutting off the Sixth Army.<cr>On December 12, 1942, as a counter move, the Germans launched Operation Winter Storm to relieve their Sixth Army by attacking through the pincers of the Soviet armies participating in Operation Uranus. The Soviets counter-attacked on December 16, 1942, and launched Operation Little Saturn, penetrating between the Italian Eighth Army and the Hungarian Second Army near the junction held by the Italian Alpini and threatening the flank of German forces attempting to relieve the Sixth Army by cutting the would-be relievers off at the Donets river. With heavy losses the Soviets conquered some areas west of the Don river, but were temporarily stopped and delayed in their advance.<cr>But on January 13, 1943, Russian forces, overwhelming in numbers and equipment, began the Voronezh-Kharkov Strategic Offensive Operation with the Bryansk, Voronezh, and Southwestern Fronts simultaneously. The Soviet Red Army was totally successful this time: during the Ostrogozhsk-Rossoh Offensive the Russians rapidly destroyed the Hungarian Second Army near Svoboda on the Don River. An attack on the German Second Army further north threatened to bring about an encirclement of that army as well, though it managed to withdraw and was forced to retreat. By February 5, 1943, troops of the Russian Voronezh Front were approaching Kharkov. The losses of the 2nd Army were made especially severe by the attitude of the Army command (Colonel General Gustv Jny), who forbade any sort of withdrawal, in spite of seeing the neighbouring German and Italian Armies pulling back. Most of the Hungarian units were encircled and either annihilated or forced to open terrain where they succumbed to the extreme cold (-30C - -40C). The 1st Armored Division was reduced to a single operational tank within a few days, and most of the personnel of the 1st Air Group died on the ground when their airfields were overran by Soviet tanks.<cr>During its twelve months of activity on the Russian front, the Second Hungarian Army's losses were enormous. Of an initial force of about 200,000 Hungarian soldiers and 50,000 Jewish forced-laborers, about 100,000 were dead, 35,000 wounded, and 60,000 taken prisoners of war. Only about 40,000 men returned to Hungary.<cr>On August 30, 1944, Hungary mobilized a reformed Hungarian Second Army and the Hungarian Third Army. Both armies were primarily composed of weak, undermanned, and underequipped reserve divisions.<cr>General of Artillery Maximilian Fretter-Pico's recently reformed German Sixth Army represented the nucleus of what remained of German Colonel-General (Generaloberst) Johannes Friessner's Army Group South. By October, 1944, seeing that his Hungarian allies were suffering from low morale, Friessner attached the recently reformed Hungarian Second Army under the command of Lieutenant-General Lajos Veress de Dlnok to Fretter-Pico's army. The combination of German and Hungarian armies was designated Army Group Fretter Pico (Armeegruppe Fretter-Pico).<cr>Late in 1944, a reformed Hungarian Second Army enjoyed a modest level of combat success as an integral part of Army Group Fretter-Pico. From September 16 to October 24, 1944, during the Battle of Debrecen, Army Group Fretter-Pico achieved a major success against the Debrecen Offensive Operation. While avoiding encirclement, Army Group Fretter-Pico managed to severely maul three Soviet tank corps of Mobile Group Pliyev under the command of Issa Pliyev. The defeat of the Soviet mobile group by the combined German and Hungarian forces contrasted with Pliyev's earlier victory over the untested Hungarian Third Army. However, the victory ultimately proved too costly to the Hungarians' armor and ammunition reserves. Unable to replace equipment and personnel lost in the Battle of Debrecen, the Hungarian Second Army was smashed in December 1, 1944. Surviving units of the Second Army were transferred to the Third Army.<cr><cr>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Army_(Hungary)

Practically all the armoured units Hungary had were re-organized into the 1st Hungarian Armored Division and attached to the 2nd Army. For both the armored and air units, shortages in supplies and equipment lead to significant delays and they were shipped to Russia significantly later than infantry units.<cr>By April 11, 1942, the 209,000-man-strong Second Army was assigned to the German Army Group South in southern Russia. In June, 1942, the Second Army became part of Army Group B in Operation Blue (Fall Blau). Transportation of the army to the frontline began on 17th April 1942, and the last units arrived by 27th June.<cr>In June and July 1942, prior to the Battle of Stalingrad, the Hungarian Second Army was involved in the Battle of Voronezh as part of Army Group B. Fighting in and around the city of Voronezh on the Don River, the Hungarian troops supported the German 4th Panzer Army against the defending Soviet Voronezh Front. Though technically an Axis success, this pyrrhic victory fatally delayed the arrival of the 4th Panzer Army in the Caucasus. During these operations, the Hungarian Second Army has suffered severe casualties in manpower as without adequate air and armor support all assaults were carried out by infantry units only, against the skillful and determined defense conducted by the Soviet troops.<cr>The Hungarian Second Army is probably the best known Hungarian wartime army because of the part it played in the Battle of Stalingrad. Before being sent to Russia, the rank-and-file of the Second Army had received but eight weeks of training. The only tactical experience for many of these soldiers were the maneuvers held just prior to the departure for the front. This lack of preparation badly affected the soldiers' fighting abilities and morale when confronted with heavy tank assaults. Also, a significant part of the army was made up by reservists (officers and enlisted men alike), who were promised a 'quick victory' and became demoralized as their prospects for getting home soon were worsening.<cr>In 1942, the Hungarian Second Army was given the task of protecting the 8th Italian's Army northern flank between Novaya Pokrovka on the Don River and Rossosh. This allowed the German Sixth Army to continue to attack Soviet General Vasily Chuikov's 62nd Army defending Stalingrad. As winter set in, and with the worsening German situation around Stalingrad, the 2nd Army's transportation collapsed and failed to supply even the basics (food, winter clothing, heating fuel, building materials) for the frontline units. The cold, hungry and demoralized 2nd Army had to defend even longer and longer stretches of the frontline as more and more German units were sent to Stalingrad.<cr>The Hungarian Second Army, as almost all of the armies protecting the flanks of the Sixth Army, was annihilated when the Soviets launched Operaton Uranus, and Operation Little Saturn. As part of these operations, two Soviet pincers drove through the Romanian 3rd Army to the north of Stalingrad and the Romanian 4th Army to the south, cutting off the Sixth Army.<cr>On December 12, 1942, as a counter move, the Germans launched Operation Winter Storm to relieve their Sixth Army by attacking through the pincers of the Soviet armies participating in Operation Uranus. The Soviets counter-attacked on December 16, 1942, and launched Operation Little Saturn, penetrating between the Italian Eighth Army and the Hungarian Second Army near the junction held by the Italian Alpini and threatening the flank of German forces attempting to relieve the Sixth Army by cutting the would-be relievers off at the Donets river. With heavy losses the Soviets conquered some areas west of the Don river, but were temporarily stopped and delayed in their advance.<cr>But on January 13, 1943, Russian forces, overwhelming in numbers and equipment, began the Voronezh-Kharkov Strategic Offensive Operation with the Bryansk, Voronezh, and Southwestern Fronts simultaneously. The Soviet Red Army was totally successful this time: during the Ostrogozhsk-Rossoh Offensive the Russians rapidly destroyed the Hungarian Second Army near Svoboda on the Don River. An attack on the German Second Army further north threatened to bring about an encirclement of that army as well, though it managed to withdraw and was forced to retreat. By February 5, 1943, troops of the Russian Voronezh Front were approaching Kharkov. The losses of the 2nd Army were made especially severe by the attitude of the Army command (Colonel General Gustv Jny), who forbade any sort of withdrawal, in spite of seeing the neighbouring German and Italian Armies pulling back. Most of the Hungarian units were encircled and either annihilated or forced to open terrain where they succumbed to the extreme cold (-30C - -40C). The 1st Armored Division was reduced to a single operational tank within a few days, and most of the personnel of the 1st Air Group died on the ground when their airfields were overran by Soviet tanks.<cr>During its twelve months of activity on the Russian front, the Second Hungarian Army's losses were enormous. Of an initial force of about 200,000 Hungarian soldiers and 50,000 Jewish forced-laborers, about 100,000 were dead, 35,000 wounded, and 60,000 taken prisoners of war. Only about 40,000 men returned to Hungary.<cr>On August 30, 1944, Hungary mobilized a reformed Hungarian Second Army and the Hungarian Third Army. Both armies were primarily composed of weak, undermanned, and underequipped reserve divisions.<cr>General of Artillery Maximilian Fretter-Pico's recently reformed German Sixth Army represented the nucleus of what remained of German Colonel-General (Generaloberst) Johannes Friessner's Army Group South. By October, 1944, seeing that his Hungarian allies were suffering from low morale, Friessner attached the recently reformed Hungarian Second Army under the command of Lieutenant-General Lajos Veress de Dlnok to Fretter-Pico's army. The combination of German and Hungarian armies was designated Army Group Fretter Pico (Armeegruppe Fretter-Pico).<cr>Late in 1944, a reformed Hungarian Second Army enjoyed a modest level of combat success as an integral part of Army Group Fretter-Pico. From September 16 to October 24, 1944, during the Battle of Debrecen, Army Group Fretter-Pico achieved a major success against the Debrecen Offensive Operation. While avoiding encirclement, Army Group Fretter-Pico managed to severely maul three Soviet tank corps of Mobile Group Pliyev under the command of Issa Pliyev. The defeat of the Soviet mobile group by the combined German and Hungarian forces contrasted with Pliyev's earlier victory over the untested Hungarian Third Army. However, the victory ultimately proved too costly to the Hungarians' armor and ammunition reserves. Unable to replace equipment and personnel lost in the Battle of Debrecen, the Hungarian Second Army was smashed in December 1, 1944. Surviving units of the Second Army were transferred to the Third Army.<cr><cr>https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Army_(Hungary)

text: The 2nd Hungarian Cavalry Brigade was formed in 1938. The brigade participated in the German invasion of Yugoslavia in April of 1941 but It remained in Hungary at the start of Operation Barbarossa. In October of 1941 it was merged with the 1st Hungarian Cavalry Brigade to form the 1st Hungarian Cavalry Division. In September 1944 the division was renamed the 1st Hussar Division.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr>Charles D. text: The 2nd Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In the fall of 1941 the brigade was one of five brigades reduced in size and stripped of their artillery that was assigned to the Hungarian Occupation Group for security duties on the Eastern Front. At this time it was redesignated the 102nd Infantry Brigade but in February 1942 was redesignated the 102nd Light Division and assigned to defend Kharkov. In May 1943 the unit became the 2nd Light Division. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 2nd Light Division was merged with other units and disbanded.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第2匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括由少将指挥的9500人，下辖2个步兵团（每个团有3个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1941年秋季，该旅是被缩减规模并剥离了炮兵的五个旅之一，被分配给匈牙利占领集团，在东线方面军担任治安任务。此时它被重新命名为第102步兵旅，但在1942年2月又被改名为第102轻师，并被指派防御哈尔科夫。1943年5月该单位成为第2轻师。作为斯大林格勒战役后匈牙利陆军总体重组的一部分，第2轻师与其他部队合并并解散。<cr>参考文献：Thomas博士和Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利陆军》<cr><cr>Chris Munson提供

text: The 2nd Hungarian Motorized Brigade was formed in 1938. The brigade participated in the German Invasion of Yugoslavia in early 1941. At the start of Operation Barbarossa it was assigned to the Hungarian Mobile Corps or Gyorshadtest which in turn was part of the Carpathian Group. The Carpathian Group invaded Ukrainian Galicia on June 29th, 1941. Shortly thereafter the Carpathian Group was disbanded and its Hungarian VIII Corps was assigned occupation duties while the 2nd Motorized Brigade, still part of the the Hungarian Mobile Corps, continued the drive deep into the Soviet Union. The brigade along with the rest of the Corps were recalled to Hungary in October of 1941. By this time the brigade had lost most of its armor. In early 1942 the brigade was reorganized and became the 2nd Armored Division.<cr>In January of 1944 the Hungarian First Army to which the division was then subordinate, mobilized to defend Hungary's northern Carpathian frontier against the advancing Red Army. In August 1944 the division was part of a reactivated Hungarian Second Army defending Northern Transylvania from the invading Red Army.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第2摩托化旅成立于1938年。该旅参加了德国于1941年初入侵南斯拉夫的行动。在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，它被分配给匈牙利快速部队或Gyorshadtest，后者又属于喀尔巴阡集团军的一部分。喀尔巴阡集团军于1941年6月29日入侵乌克兰加利西亚。不久之后，喀尔巴阡集团军解散，其下属的匈牙利第8军被分配了占领任务，而第2摩托化旅仍然属于快速部队，继续深入苏联境内推进。该旅及其所属的军于1941年10月被召回匈牙利。此时，该旅已经失去了大部分装甲车辆。1942年初，该旅重组为第2装甲师。<cr>1944年1月，下辖该师的匈牙利第一集团军动员起来，以防御北部喀尔巴阡地区的边界，对抗推进中的红军。<cr>1944年8月，该师成为重新激活的匈牙利第二集团军的一部分，保卫北特兰西瓦尼亚地区，抵御入侵的红军。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, 《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利陆军》<cr>条目由Chris Munson提供

text: The 2nd Mechanised Corps was initially formed in June 1940 and was attached to the Odessa Military District, and attached to the 9th Army in the Odessa Fortified Region. It was under the command of Lieutenant General Iu. V. Novoselsky and initially comprised the 11th and 16th Tank Divisions, and the 15th Mechanized Division.<cr>After the invasion began the Odessa Military District was renamed Southern Front, Commanded by Colonel General I. V. Tiulenev. The front fielded the 9th and 18th Armies. The 2nd Mechanized Corps was heavily involved in the first battles of Operation Barbarossa, taking part with Colonel General A. K. Cherevichenko's 9th Army in Operation Mnchen to defend Soviet occupied Bessarabia. Against Generaloberst Schobert's 11th Army, which had penetrated Soviet defenses, captured Iassy and reached the Prut River on the first day of action.<cr>However, after initially withdrawing to behind the Dniester River on Tiulenev's orders Stavka ordered 6th Army and 2nd Mechanized Corps to recapture the Prut River line. By 18 July Schobert's 11th Army, had crossed the Dniester River and Stavka finally realised that the 6th, 12th and 18th Armies faced encirclement and ordered the 2nd Mechanized Corps to the Uman region to halt the German advance into Southern Front's rear.<cr>The line was already in German hands & this decision was far too late. Mikhail Kirponos commander of Southwestern Front now ordered 26th Army to wheel about and cover their withdrawal and for 6th and 12th Armies to attack eastwards to meet up. By 20 July, 2nd Mechanized Corps was holding open a narrow corridor upon to the east between LVIII Panzer Corps and 17th Army.<cr>Two days later the trap was shut, and although the 2nd Mechanized Corps tried to free the surrounded armies on 8 August the fighting was over: 107,000 officers and men, including Generals Pondelin and Muzychenko, four corps commanders and 11 division commanders, 286 tanks and 953 guns were captured. Another two corps commanders and six division commanders perished in the fighting. 2nd Mechanized Corps was largely destroyed.<cr><cr>
translation: 第2机械化军最初于1940年6月组建，并隶属于敖德萨军区，随后被编入敖德萨要塞地区的第9集团军。该部队由少将Iu. V. Novoselsky指挥，最初包括第11和第16坦克师以及第15机械化师。<cr>入侵开始后，敖德萨军区更名为南方方面军，由中将I. V. Tiulenev指挥。该方面军部署了第9集团军和第18集团军。第2机械化军在巴巴罗萨行动的初期战斗中发挥了重要作用，在中将A. K. Cherevichenko指挥下的第9集团军参与了“慕尼黑”行动，以防御苏联占领的比萨拉比亚地区。<cr>面对突破苏军防线、攻占雅西并抵达普鲁特河的德军第11集团军（由大将Schobert指挥），在Tiulenev的命令下最初撤退到德涅斯特河西岸后，最高统帅部下令第6集团军和第2机械化军重新夺回普鲁特河防线。<cr>7月18日，Schobert的第11集团军已经渡过德涅斯特河，最高统帅部终于意识到第6、第12和第18集团军面临被包围的危险，并命令第2机械化军前往乌曼地区阻止德国军队深入南方方面军后方。<cr>防线已落入德军手中，这一决定为时已晚。西南方向指挥官米哈伊尔·基普诺斯现在下令第26集团军转向并掩护其撤退，并令第6和第12集团军向东进攻以会合。<cr>7月20日，第2机械化军在LVIII装甲军和第17集团军之间维持着一条狭窄的东向走廊。两天后陷阱关闭，尽管第2机械化军在8月8日试图解救被包围的部队，战斗已经结束：共俘获了107,000名官兵（包括普德林和穆岑琴科将军、4位军长和11位师长），以及286辆坦克和953门火炮。另外还有两位军长和六位师长在战斗中阵亡，第2机械化军大部分被消灭。<cr><cr>

text: The 2nd Panzer Division crossed into Russia in October 1941, and fought at Vyasma and other points on the road to the Soviet capital. Elements of the unit managed to reach as far as Khimki, small river port five miles from Moscow, and elements of the 5th Panzer Reconnaissance Battalion even reported being able to see the Kremlin itself, before they were thrown back by the start of the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42. Remaining on the central sector, the battered division took part in the defensive fighting in the Rzhev Salient (1942-43), in the Rzhev withdrawal (1943), at the battles of Kursk and Orel, and at Yelnja, Kiev, and Gomel, and the middle Dnieper battles of the winter of 1943-44, where it suffered heavy casualties. It was then withdrawn to France for rest and refit.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text: This unit, which never reached full strength, was created as the sister unit of the (1st) Parachute Panzer Division 'Hermann Gring'. In both cases the term 'parachute' was honorary. The 'H.G.' Panzer Grenadier Division was formed in the Radom zone of Poland on September 24, 1944. Its 3rd Panzer Grenadier Regiment was the former 16th Parachute Regiment, and the 4th Panzer Grenadier Regiment was the former Hermann Goering Guard Regiment. The new division assigned to the new Parachute Panzer Corps 'Hermann Gring', held a sector on the Vistula (October 1944January 1945) and was smashed in heavy fighting East Prussia (February and March 1945). It surrendered to the Soviets at the end of the war.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text: The 2nd Rifle Division was formed in 1919. Its honorific title was 2nd Belorussian Red Banner Rifle Division. At the start of Operation Barbarossa the division was assigned to the Russian 10th Army in the Bialystok 'bulge' on the Polish border and consisted of the 13th, 200th and 261st Rifle Regiments, 164th Light Artillery Regiment, 243rd Howitzer Regiment and various support units. The Germans rapidly surrounded the Russian units in the Bialystok bulge in June of 1941. The division escaped the pocket only to be annihilated in a pocket west of Minsk in early July 1941. The division was removed from the Soviet order of battle in late July 1941 and formally disbanded in Sepember 1941.<cr>In September 1941 a new 2nd Rifle Division was formed from the 2nd Moscow Militia Division and assigned to the 32nd Army. It consisted of the 1282nd, 1284th and 1286th Rifle Regiments, 970th Artillery Regiment and various support units. German pressure forced the division into combat before it was brought up to full strength and it was surrounded and destroyed in the Vyazma Pocket in October 1941. The division was officially removed from the Soviet order of battle in November 1941.<cr>A new 2nd Rifle Division was formed at Sevastopol in November 1941 from the dismounted 2nd Cavalry Division, reservists and NKVD border troops. The division was renamed the 109th Rifle Division in January 1942.<cr>A new 2nd Rifle Division began forming at Arkhangelsk at the end of 1941 with the originally numbered rifle regiments and the 164th Artillery Regiment. By the end of March 1942 the division was deemed ready for combat and transferred to the Volkhov Front. The division was part of the attempted rescue of the 2nd Shock Army in the summer of 1942. In 1943 it participated in Operation Iskra. During 1944 the division particpated in the Leningrad-Novgorod Offensive and then the clearing of the Baltic States ending 1944 in Estonia. The division was near Knigsberg at wars end.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第2步兵师成立于1919年，其荣誉称号为第2白俄罗斯红旗步兵师。巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师被分配给在波兰边境比亚韦斯托克突出部的苏联第10集团军，并由第13、200和261步兵团、第164轻炮兵团、第243榴弹炮团以及各种支援单位组成。德国人迅速包围了该地区内的苏军部队，于1941年6月在比亚韦斯托克突出部形成包围圈。该师仅逃出包围圈便又在明斯克以西的另一个包围圈中被消灭，时间是1941年7月初。第2步兵师于1941年7月底从苏军战斗序列中移除，并于同年9月正式解散。<cr><cr>1941年9月，一个新的第2步兵师由第2莫斯科民兵师改编而成，并被分配给第32集团军。该师包括第1282、1284和1286步兵团、第970炮兵团以及各种支援单位。德军的压力迫使该师在未完全编成的情况下投入战斗，于1941年10月在维亚兹马包围圈中被包围并消灭。该师于1941年11月正式从苏军战斗序列中移除。<cr><cr>一个新的第2步兵师于1941年11月在塞瓦斯托波尔由改编自第2骑兵师的步兵、预备役人员和内务人民委员部边防部队组建而成。该师于1942年1月改名为第109步兵师。<cr>一个新的第2步兵师于1941年底在阿尔汉格尔斯克开始组建，包括原编号的步兵团和第164炮兵团。到1942年3月底，该师被认为已准备好作战，并被转移到沃尔霍夫方面军。该师参与了1942年夏季营救第二突击集团军的行动。1943年，它参加了“火花”行动。在1944年，该师参加了列宁格勒-诺夫哥罗德进攻战役以及波罗的海国家的清理工作，并于1944年底驻扎在爱沙尼亚。战至最后，该师靠近柯尼斯堡。<cr>词条由Chris Munson提供

There it remained through the final defensive battles with the Soviets in Romania proper.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text: The 2nd Sforzesca Italian Mountain Division was mobilized in 1940 in preperation for the Italian invasion of France. Italian Mountain divisions should not be confused with the elite Alpini formations. Mountain divisions had pack horse artillery rather than towed artillery. The division consisted of the 53rd and 54th Infantry Regiments, the 17th Artillery Regiment and various support troops.<cr>In June 1940 during the invasion of southern France the division made limited advances against heavy French fortifications. In 1941 the division participated in the Greco-Italian War. The division remained in occupied Greece until July of 1941 when it was transferred back to Italy. The division was one of seven dispatched as reinforcements to the Eastern Front with the Italian 8th Army in the summer of 1942. The division found itself, along with the rest of the 8th Army, stretched along a 160 mile section of the Don River between the Hungarian Second Army and Romanian 3rd Army on the German left flank at the start of Operation Little Saturn. The division came under heavy attack at the end of November 1942. As part of a general retreat by the 8th Army in December 1942 it was overran by large Soviet armored forces and a great part of the division was destroyed. By January 1943 the remainder of the division was surrounded but managed to break free. The survivors were withdrawn to Italy in March 1943.<cr>The division was disbanded in April 1943 but was reformed in June 1943. The reformed division was posted on the border between Yugoslavia and Italy where it performed anti-partisan duties. It was disbanded by the Germans after Italy's surrender in September 1943. <cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第二索福斯卡意大利山地师于1940年动员，为意大利入侵法国做准备。意大利山地师不应与精英阿尔宾尼部队混淆。山地师配备了驮马炮兵而非牵引式火炮。该师由第53步兵团、第54步兵团和第17炮兵团以及各种支援部队组成。<cr>1940年6月，在入侵法国南部期间，该师面对坚固的法国防御工事仅取得有限进展。1941年，该师参加了希腊-意大利战争，并一直驻扎在被占领的希腊直到1941年7月才返回意大利。<cr>1942年夏季，作为增援部队之一，该师随意大利第8集团军部署到东线。在“小土星行动”开始时，该师与第8集团军其余部分一起，在匈牙利第二集团军和罗马尼亚第三集团军之间沿着顿河160英里长的战线上拉伸，位于德国左翼。<cr>1942年11月底，该师遭到猛烈攻击。作为1942年12月第8集团军全面撤退的一部分，它被强大的苏联装甲部队突破，大部分兵力被消灭。到1943年1月，剩余的部队被包围但设法突围。<cr>幸存者于1943年3月撤回意大利。<cr>该师于1943年4月解散，但在同年6月重组，并部署在南斯拉夫和意大利之间的边境执行反游击任务。随着意大利投降，德国人在1943年9月解散了该师。<cr><cr>Chris Munson 提供

text: The 2nd Shock Army was formed from the Volkhov Front's 26th Army in December 1941 and initially consisted of the 327th Rifle Division and eight separate rifle brigades. <cr>In January 1942 the Volkhov Front commander, Meretskov, had to request the Armys commander, General Lieutenant Sokolov, a former NKVD commissar, be relieved, as he was absolutely incompetent. Command was handed over to the former commander of 52nd Army, General Lieutenant Klykov. Later that same month it was launched against Lyuban, but its offensive saw the Army isolated, under a new commander, General Lieutenant A. A. Vlasov.<cr>On January 7, 1942, Vlasov's army had spearheaded the Lyuban Offensive Operation to break the Leningrad encirclement. Planned as a combined operation between the Volkhov and Leningrad Fronts on a 30 km frontage, other armies of the Leningrad Front (including the 54th) were supposed to participate at scheduled intervals in this operation. Crossing the Volkhov River, Vlasov's army was successful in breaking through the German 18th Army's lines and penetrated 70-74 km deep inside German rear area. The other armies (Volkhov Front's 4th, 52nd, and 59th Armies, 13th Cavalry Corps, and 4th and 6th Guards Rifle Corps), however, failed to provide the required support, and Vlasov's army became stranded. Permission to retreat was refused. With the counter-offensive in May 1942, the Second Shock Army was finally allowed to retreat, but by now, too weakened, it was virtually annihilated during the final breakout at Myasnoi Bor. Vlasov was taken prisoner by the Wehrmacht troops on July 6, 1942.<cr>2nd Shock Army again suffered severe losses during the Siniavino operation from 19 August - 20 October 1942. Again, the army was returned to the Front reserves for rebuilding.<cr>In January 1943 it took part in the offensive which aimed to raise the Siege of Leningrad, Operation Iskra. The Stavka then intervened in Leningrad Front offensive planning during September 1943, changing the plan so that 2nd Shock Army would attack from the Oranienbaum bridgehead. The offensive, under a newly appointed commander, General I.I. Fedyuninskii, begun on 14 January, took part in breaking the almost 900-day Siege of Leningrad, and pushed west to the outskirts of Narva, resulting in the Battle of Narva.<cr>The 2nd Shock Army struggled to take Narva and German positions further west of the city until September 1944, when deep exploitation by Soviet forces in the Baltic States forced a German retreat through Estonia. As a result of the strategic Soviet victory in this region, the 2nd Shock Army was moved south and assigned to the 2nd Belorussian Front. As part of the 2nd Belorussian Front, the 2nd Shock Army fought across Poland and northeastern Germany, with its route of march taking it north of Warsaw and Stettin. In late March, the army helped capture Danzig. On May 1, 1945, the 2nd Shock Army took Stralsund on the Baltic Coast, ending the war there and on the island of Rgen.<cr><cr>
translation: 第2突击集团军于1941年12月由沃尔霍夫方面军的第26集团军组建，最初包括第327步兵师和8个独立步兵旅。在1942年1月，沃尔霍夫方面军指挥官梅列茨科夫不得不请求集团军群司令索科尔斯基将军（前内务人民委员部专员）离职，因为他完全无能。<cr>指挥权交给了第52集团军的前任指挥官克利科夫将军。同月晚些时候，该部队被派往卢班进攻，但其攻势导致了孤立，并在新任指挥官瓦图京将军的领导下继续作战。<cr>1942年1月7日，瓦图京的军队带头发起卢班进攻行动，以打破列宁格勒包围圈。该行动计划由沃尔霍夫和列宁格勒方面军联合进行，在30公里宽的战线上展开。其他列宁格勒方面军部队（包括第54集团军）应在预定时间参与此行动。<cr>瓦图京的军队成功突破了德国第18集团军的防线，并深入德军后方70-74公里。然而，其他部队（沃尔霍夫方面军的第4、第52和第59集团军，第13骑兵军以及第4和第6近卫步兵军）未能提供所需支援，导致瓦图京的军队陷入困境。<cr>撤退请求被拒绝。直到1942年5月反攻时，第二突击集团军才获准撤退，但此时已经过于虚弱，在最终突围过程中几乎全军覆没于米亚斯诺伊博。<cr>1942年7月6日，瓦图京被国防军部队俘虏。<cr>第2突击集团军在1942年8月19日至10月20日期间的辛尼亚文行动中再次遭受严重损失。该部队又被送回方面军预备队重建。<cr>1943年1月，该师参与了旨在解除列宁格勒包围的攻势行动“火花”行动。最高统帅部在1943年9月介入列宁格勒方面军进攻计划，更改方案让第2突击集团军从奥拉宁鲍姆桥头堡发起攻击。<cr>新任指挥官伊·伊·费德尤尼斯基将军于1月14日开始的攻势中参与了几乎长达900天的列宁格勒包围战的突破，并向纳尔瓦郊外推进，导致纳尔瓦战役的发生。第2突击集团军在1944年9月之前一直努力攻占纳尔瓦及其西面德军阵地，直到苏联军队在波罗的海国家深入作战迫使德国人从爱沙尼亚撤退。<cr>由于该地区的战略胜利，第2突击集团军被调往南方，并分配给第2白俄罗斯方面军。作为第2白俄罗斯方面军的一部分，第2突击集团军穿越波兰和东普鲁士北部，在行军路线中绕过了华沙和什切青。3月下旬，该师帮助占领了但泽。<cr>1945年5月1日，第2突击集团军攻占了波罗的海沿岸的斯特拉尔松德，并在那里以及里加岛结束了战争。

text: The 2nd Slovak Infantry Division was part of the Slovakian Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. Shortly thereafter it was reformed as the Slovak Security Division.The Slovak Security Division was in turn disbanded in August of 1943 and a new Slovak 2nd Infantry Division formed from its elements. The division was transferred to Italy where it performed garrison duties until the end of the war.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第2斯洛伐克步兵师在巴巴罗萨行动开始时隶属于斯洛伐克军。不久之后，该师重组为斯洛伐克治安师。而斯洛伐克治安师又于1943年8月解散，并从其编制中组建了新的第2斯洛伐克步兵师。该师被调往意大利，在那里执行守备任务直到战争结束。<cr>词条提供：克里斯·芒森

text: The 2nd SS Panzer Division Das Reich was an elite division of the Nazi Waffen-SS during World War II. It was one of the thirty-eight divisions fielded by the Waffen-SS. It served during the invasion of France and took part in several major battles on the Eastern Front (particularly in the Battle of Prokhorovka against the 5th Guards Tank Army during the Battle of Kursk ). It was then transferred to the West and took part in the fighting in Normandy and the Battle of the Bulge, ending the war with desperate fighting in Hungary and Austria. <cr>Early in 1943, Das Reich was transferd back to the Eastern Front where it helped reclaim the crumbling central front around Kharkov. After helping recapture the city of Kharkov, Das Reich along with many other Divisions was thrown into a massive assault into the Kursk Salient, a huge bulge in the Soviet Front line around the area of Kursk. Das Reich pushed upwards of 40 miles into the southern sector of the bulge, but was pulled out of the battle along with the other SS-Division when the offensive was called off. After a period of brief encounters, Das Reich was refit once again, this time as SS-Panzer-Division 'Das Reich'. In doing so, it left a portion the Division in the East titled Kampfgroup Das Reich, and officially know as Kampfgroup Lammerding. The rest of the Division was transferd to the West to refit, and while doing so also took part in anti-partisan operations in France.<cr><cr><cr><cr>
translation: 党卫军第2装甲师“帝国”是纳粹武装党卫军在二战期间的一支精锐部队。它是武装党卫军所辖的三十八个师之一。“帝国”参加了入侵法国的行动，并且参与了东线战场上的多次重大战役（特别是在库尔斯克会战中与近卫坦克第5集团军交锋）。随后该师被调往西线，参加诺曼底战役和突出部战役，在战争末期又在匈牙利和奥地利进行了绝望的战斗。<cr>1943年初，“帝国”师又被调回东线战场，帮助收复哈尔科夫周边崩溃的中央战线。“帝国”师和其他多个师一起参加了对库尔斯克突出部的大规模突击行动，在该地区苏军防线上的一个巨大凸起地带发动攻势。在南部战区，“帝国”师推进了超过40英里的距离，但当进攻被叫停时，它与其他党卫军师一样也被撤出了战斗。经过一段短暂交锋的时期后，“帝国”师再次整补，并更名为“帝国”装甲师。在此过程中，该师将一部分兵力留在东线，称为“帝国战斗群”，正式名称为拉姆丁战斗群。其余部队则被调往西线进行整补，在此期间还参与了法国境内的反游击队行动。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text:
The 2nd Tank Corps was formed March-April 1942 at Gorkiy in the Moscow Military District and in April began receiving subordinate units at Podmoskov near Gorkiy.<cr>While the two tank brigades should have had a total of 10 KVs, 20 T-34s, and 20 T-60s each, 26th Tank Brigade had no KVs at all. The first Corps commander was Major General A. I. Lizyukov, the commander of the 1st Guards Motorized Division in 1941 and one of the first commanders awarded the title:Hero of the Soviet Union.<cr>When 2nd Tank Corps went to Bryansk Front in late May, the front and high command headquarters tried to build it up with a third tank brigade. For a brief time in June the Corps actually controlled 4 tank brigades.<cr>However, by late June when the 2nd Tank Corps was assigned to the newly formed 5th Tank Army.<cr>Unfortunately, when 5th Tank Army went into action in early July against the German panzers near Voronezh, the attacks were uncoordinated, the units shot up by the Luftwaffe, and the 5th Tank Army commander, 2nd Tank Corps excommander General Lizyukov, was killed in action. By the end of August 2nd Tank Corps had shifted south to Stalingrad under 62nd Army HQ. The corps' tank
brigades were so badly under strength that 99th Tank Brigade was added in August, along with tanks from the Stalingrad Militia Tank Battalions, to bring the corps up to strength.<cr>By 15 September 2nd Tank Corps was stationed on the islands in the Volga River east of Stalingrad as a 'holding headquarters'. At that time the Corps included seven tank brigades.<cr>While impressive on paper, not one of these units had a single tank or armored vehicle! The manpower, all dismounted, was manning positions in the Fortified Sectors in case the Germans broke through to the river and attempted to cross. In October 1942 the 2nd Tank Corps was withdrawn across the Volga into Volga Military District to be rebuilt completely.<cr>The 2nd Tank Corps went to Southwestern Front in late December, and fought with 3rd Guards Army in the ill-fated advance into the Donbass which was smashed by Manstein's counter-attack in February and March 1943. The Corps went back into reserve in March, and there was extensively rebuilt, reequipped, and built up in preparation for the 1943 summer campaign. By 1 June 1943 the 2nd Tank Corps was in Southwestern Front reserves east and south of Belgorod. <cr>On 11 July 2nd Tank Corps was assigned to 5th Guards Tank Army, and on 12 July the Corps went into the attack against II SS Panzer Corps at Prokhorovka. The corps had 62nd Heavy Tank Regiment (KV tanks) temporarily assigned, but primarily, it was T-34s against Tigers and PzKpfw IVs. Once the German advance halted, the corps was removed from 5th Guards Tank Army, and on 23 July went to Voronezh Front reserves, and was nearly back up to strength by 3 August when the Soviet summer offensive started south of Kursk. For the summer offensive, 2nd Tank Corps was reinforced with the 15th Guards Heavy Tank Regiment (21 KV-85 tanks).<cr>As a result of the Corps ' combat achievements at Prokhorovka and in the advance on Belgorod-Kharkov in August and September, on 19 September 1943 it was redesignated as 8th Guards Tank Corps. <cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第2坦克军于1942年3月至4月在莫斯科军区的高尔基组建，并于4月开始在高尔基附近的波多莫斯科接收下属单位。<cr>虽然两个坦克旅应该各有10辆KV、20辆T-34和20辆T-60，但第26坦克旅完全没有KV坦克。首任坦克军指挥官是少将A. I. 利兹尤科夫，他在1941年担任第1近卫机械化师的指挥官，并且是首批获得“苏联英雄”称号的指挥官之一。<cr>当第2坦克军于5月下旬被派往布良斯克方面军时，该方面军和高级指挥部试图通过增加第三个坦克旅来加强它。6月期间，该军实际上控制了4个坦克旅。<cr>然而，到6月底，第2坦克军被分配给新成立的第5坦克集团军。<cr>不幸的是，在7月初与德国装甲部队在沃罗涅日附近的战斗中，进攻缺乏协调性，并且部队遭到德国防空部队的打击，导致第5坦克集团军指挥官、前第2坦克军指挥官利兹尤科夫将军阵亡。到8月底，第2坦克军已转移到斯大林格勒以南地区，在第62集团军司令部下作战。该军的坦克旅兵力严重不足，因此在8月增加了第99坦克旅，并从斯大林格勒民兵坦克营中调来了坦克，以便将部队补充到满员状态。<cr>至9月15日，第2坦克军驻扎在伏尔加河东岸的斯大林格勒附近岛屿上作为“留守司令部”。此时该军包括7个坦克旅。<cr>虽然纸面实力不俗，但这些部队中没有一辆坦克或装甲车辆！所有人员都已下车，在加强防区内的阵地驻守，以防德军突破至伏尔加河并试图渡河。1942年10月，第2坦克军被撤过伏尔加河进入伏尔加军区重建。<cr>第2坦克军于12月底调往西南方面军，在3月和4月期间与第3近卫集团军在不幸的顿巴斯攻势中作战，该攻势遭到曼施坦因反击部队的粉碎。该军于3月进入预备队，并进行了广泛的重建、重新装备和加强，为1943年夏季战役做准备。到1943年6月1日，第2坦克军位于西南方面军预备队中，在别洛戈罗德东面和南面。<cr>7月11日，第2坦克军被分配给第5近卫坦克集团军，并于7月12日对II党卫军装甲军在普罗霍罗夫卡的进攻发起反击。该军临时编入了第62重型坦克团（KV战车），但主要是T-34对抗虎式和PzKpfw IV。一旦德军攻势停止，该军就被从第5近卫坦克集团军中撤出，并于7月23日进入沃罗涅日方面军预备队，在8月3日苏联夏季攻势开始前几乎恢复了满编。<cr>为了夏季攻势，第2坦克军得到了第15近卫重型坦克团（21辆KV-85战车）的加强。<cr>由于该军在普罗霍罗夫卡战斗中的成就以及8月和9月向别洛戈罗德-哈尔科夫推进期间的表现，它于1943年9月19日被重新指定为第8近卫坦克军。<cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普《苏联二战战斗序列 第二卷》

text: The 2nd Tank Division was a division of the Red Army and Soviet Ground Forces. <cr>The 3rd Mechanized Corps was first formed in July 1940, and on 22 June 1941, was stationed at Vilnius in the Baltic Military District under MG A.V. Kurkin. It consisted of 2nd Tank Division (Maj. Gen. Yegor Solyankin) 5th Tank Division, 84th Motorised Division, 15th Motorcycle Regiment, an artillery regiment, and engineer and signals battalions. On 22 June, the 2nd Tank Division was located in the forest in Gajzhuny, in the Ionava area, the 5th Tank Division was positioned to defend the Neman bridge near Alitus, and the 84th Motorised Division - was in forest in the Kajshadoris area. On 22 June 1941, the 3rd Mechanised Corps had 31,975 men & 651 tanks, of which 110 were new T-34 and KV-1 types. <cr>The Corps was heavily engaged in the first battles of Operation Barbarossa, particularly during the Baltic Operation (1941) and at the Battle of Raseiniai. <cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack
translation: 第2坦克师是红军和苏联地面部队的一个师。<cr>第3机械化军成立于1940年7月，至1941年6月22日，该军驻扎在波罗的海军事区的维尔纽斯，由A.V.库尔金中将指挥。该军包括第2坦克师（少将叶戈尔·索连金）、第5坦克师、第84摩托化师、第15摩托车团、一个炮兵团以及工兵和通信营。6月22日时，第2坦克师位于加兹胡尼的森林中，在伊奥纳瓦地区；第5坦克师部署在阿利图斯附近的涅曼桥附近防御位置；而第84摩托化师则驻扎在卡什达罗里斯地区的森林中。1941年6月22日，第3机械化军共有31,975人及651辆坦克，其中包含110辆新式T-34和KV-1型坦克。<cr>该军在巴巴罗萨行动初期战斗中投入了大量兵力，特别是在波罗的海战役（1941）以及拉塞尼艾战役中。<cr><cr><cr><cr> 来源：NotOneStepBack

text:
The Second Tank Division was formed in July 1940 in Western Special Military District as part of 3rd Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr><cr>
3rd Tank Regiment
1st Tank Bn - 15 KV-lA and KV-II tanks
2nd, 3rd Tank Bns - 25 T-34s each
4th Tank Bn - 30 to 33 light tanks
4th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - each 30 to 33 T-26 or BT tanks
2nd Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
2nd Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1 light, 1 medium bn
2nd Reconnaissance Battalion
2nd Motorized Pontoon Battalion
2nd Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>While still forming, the entire 3rd Mechanized Corps moved into the new Baltic Special Military District when it was formed from the newly-occupied Baltic States in August 1940.<cr>The division was formed from a Light Tank Brigade of all T-26 tanks, and was never up to strength in armor. On 1 February 1941, for instance, it only had about 63% of the authorized tanks on hand, and most of those were light BT or T-26 tanks instead of heavier modern tanks. KVs from 2nd Tank Division
were among the first the Germans met in battle, on 24 June near Rassinye, where they made a big impression on 1st and 6th Panzer Divisions. The result of this 'great tank battle in the Baltic', however, was that 2nd Tank Division was caught between the two panzer divisions and shot to pieces. Reduced to fragments, the division was disbanded in July 1941.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第二坦克师于1940年7月在西部特别军区作为机械化军的一部分组建。1941年6月22日编成如下：
第3坦克团
第1坦克营 - 15辆KV-IA和KV-II坦克
第2、3坦克营 - 每个营25辆T-34坦克
第4坦克营 - 30至33辆轻型坦克
第4坦克团
第1、2、3、4坦克营 - 每个营30至33辆T-26或BT坦克
第2摩托化步兵营
第1、2、3营
第2摩托化榴弹炮营
第1轻型、1中型营
第2侦察营
第2摩托化浮桥营
第2防空营

在尚未完全组建的情况下，整个第3机械化军于1940年8月随着新占领的波罗的海国家组成的新的波罗的海军区而转移。

该师由全部装备T-26坦克的轻型坦克旅组成，并且装甲力量从未达到满编。例如，1941年2月1日时，它只有大约63%的授权坦克数量在手，而且其中大多数是较轻的BT或T-26坦克而不是更重的现代坦克。第二坦克师的KV坦克是在6月24日靠近拉辛耶与德军首次交战中被遇到的，给第1和第6装甲师留下了深刻印象。然而，“波罗的海大坦克战”的结果是第二坦克师被困在两个装甲师之间并遭到毁灭性打击。该师被解散为碎片，并于1941年7月被撤销。

查尔斯·C·夏普《苏联战斗序列卷一》

text: The 2nd Tridentina Alpini Italian Mountain Division was formed in 1935 with the 5th and 6th Alpini Regiments and the 2nd Alpine Artillery Regiment. Alpini mountain infantry were considered elite units in the Italian Army. Each division consisted of two Alpini regiments with three battalions each, one Alpine artillery regiment, one mixed engineer battalion and various support troops for a total divisional strength of over 17,000 men. Each Alpini division also possessed nearly 5,000 mules and 500 vehicles of various types. The division was one of three Alpini sent to fight on the Eastern Front with the Italian 8th Army in the summer of 1942. The division was originally to be deployed to the Caucasus Mountains but instead found itself, along with the rest of the 8th Army, stretched along a 160 mile section of the Don River between the Hungarian Second Army and Romanian 3rd Army on the German left flank at the start of Operation Little Saturn. The division, along with most of the 8th Army was surrounded. The division fought its way free although most of the division was lost with barely 4,000 surviors remaining. The survivors returned to Italy and the division was disbanded by the Germans in September 1943 after Italy's surrender.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第2特林提纳阿尔卑斯山地师于1935年组建，包括第5和第6阿尔卑斯团以及第2高山炮兵团。阿尔卑斯步兵被视为意大利陆军中的精锐部队。每个山地师由两个阿尔卑斯团组成，每团有三个营；一个高山炮兵团；一个混合工兵营及各种支援部队，总兵力超过17000人。每个阿尔卑斯师还拥有近5000头骡子和各类车辆共500辆。该师是1942年夏季被派往东线与意大利第8集团军一起作战的三个阿尔卑斯山地师之一。原计划将该师部署到高加索山脉，但最终却与其他部队一道，在“土星行动”开始时，沿着匈牙利第二集团军和罗马尼亚第三集团军之间的160英里长顿河段分散开来，位于德国左翼的最外侧。该师与第8集团军中的大部分都被包围了。尽管该师最终突围成功，但大多数部队已经损失殆尽，仅剩4000名幸存者返回意大利。这些幸存者回到意大利后，该师于1943年9月在意大利投降后被德国解散。<cr>Chris Munson 提供

text:
The 300thth Rifle Division started forming on the 10th July 1941, at Krasnograd, in the Kharkov Military District, and by early August was assigned to the 38th Army, Southwestern Front. When the Axis advanced on Kiev, the Division was fortunate to be pushed to the East and thus avoided being trapped in the Kiev pocket. In October the Division fought in the defense of Kharkov but suffered very heavy casualties. 

In May 1942 the Division fought in the Kharkov offensive, barely avoiding encirclement and by June once again suffered heavy casualties. It was withdrawn for rebuilding in August 1942 and by November was fit enough to take part in the encirclement at Stalingrad. It fought with some success in further operations and in April 1943 was renamed the 87th Guards Rifle Division.

The Division was formed for a second time in August 1943, assigned to the 87th Rifle Corps, 1st Red Banner Army, in the Far East. In 1945 it took part in the Soviet invasion of Manchuria.

The Division was awarded the honorific of 'HARBIN'.



Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第300步兵师于1941年7月10日在哈尔科夫军区的克拉斯诺达尔开始组建，并在8月初被分配给西南方面军第38集团军。当轴心国部队推进至基辅时，该师幸运地被推向东方，从而避免了被困在基辅包围圈的命运。10月份，该师参加了哈尔科夫防御战，但遭受了非常严重的伤亡。

1942年5月，该师参加了哈尔科夫攻势，几乎避免了被包围的危险，并于6月再次遭受严重损失。该师于1942年8月撤出重建，并在11月份恢复到足以参加斯大林格勒包围战的程度。它在进一步行动中取得了一些成功，并于1943年4月改名为第87近卫步兵师。

该师第二次组建是在1943年8月，被分配给远东地区的第87步兵军和第1红旗集团军。1945年，它参加了苏联入侵满洲的行动。

该师获得了“哈尔滨”的荣誉称号。

text: The 301st Rifle Division began service as a standard Red Army rifle division shortly after the German invasion, but was soon largely destroyed in the encirclement of Kiev, although enough of a cadre survived to form the basis of a second formation. This new division began forming in the last days of 1941, and saw some limited service in the Second Battle of Kharkov, but then had to fall back in the face of the German summer offensive, became encircled quite early on, and had to be disbanded in July. Nearly a year later a third 301st was raised, based on the personnel and equipment of two existing rifle brigades. This incarnation of the division compiled a creditable record of service in several major offensives through Ukraine, then into Poland and into the heart of Berlin in April, 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第301步兵师在德国入侵后不久作为标准红军步兵师开始服役，但很快在基辅包围圈中被大量消灭。尽管有一部分骨干幸存下来并成为第二个建制的基础。这个新组建的师于1941年底开始形成，并在哈尔科夫第二次战役中有过一些有限的服务，但在面对德国夏季攻势时不得不撤退，在很早的时候就被包围了，并且不得不在7月解散。近一年后，第三个第301步兵师基于两个现役步兵旅的人员和装备组建起来。这个版本的师在乌克兰几次主要进攻中表现良好，然后进入波兰并向柏林市中心推进，直到1945年4月。<cr>指挥官报告：少校<cr>，第301步兵师司令部，1945年4月。

text: The 302nd Rifle Division began service as a specialized Red Army mountain rifle division, which saw service in the disastrous operations in the Crimea in early 1942. It was later converted to serve for the balance of the war as a standard rifle division. The division played a leading role in the 51st Army's breakthrough south of Stalingrad in the opening stages of Operaton Uranus, and then in the exploitation following this success; however, it was badly battered and routed in the initial stage of the Operation Winter Storm. After recovering from this, the division continued to turn in a creditable record of service in the southern sectors of the Soviet-German front for the duration, and was especially recognized for its role in the liberation of the city of Ternopol, for which it received that city's name as an honorific.<cr><cr>
translation: 第302步兵师最初作为红军专门的山地步枪师服役，在1942年初克里米亚灾难性的行动中参战。后来该师被改编为标准步兵师，一直服役到战争结束。在天王星行动初期阶段，该师在51集团军突破斯大林格勒南部的过程中发挥了重要作用，并在此成功之后继续扩大战果；然而，在“冬季风暴”行动的最初阶段中，该师遭受重创并溃退。恢复后，该师在整个苏联-德国东线南段持续表现出色，并因解放特诺波尔城而受到特别表彰，获得了以该城市命名的荣誉称谓。<cr> <cr>

text: The 303rd 'Doeberitz' Infantry division was formed in early 1945 from an assortment of formations from other units. It consisted of the 300th, 301st and 302nd Grenadier Regiments, 303rd Artillery Regiment and various support units. It was destroyed in the Halbe pocket.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第303步兵师“多伯里茨”成立于1945年初，由其他部队的若干编制组建而成。该师包括第300、301和302掷弹兵团，第303炮兵团以及各种支援单位。它在哈尔贝包围圈中被消灭。<cr>指挥官报告：George F. Nafziger，《二战德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>条目由Chris Munson提供

text: The 303rd Rifle Division began service as a standard Red Army rifle division shortly after the German invasion, and in its first formation fought in the central part of the Soviet-German front for a few months, taking part in the first offensive success of the Red Army at Yelnya, before being encircled and annihilated in the fighting around Vyazma. A second 303rd was raised a few months later and fought on, mainly in the central sector of Ukraine. The men and women of the division first distinguished themselves during the summer offensive of 1943, making an assault crossing of the Dnieper River at Verkhnodniprovsk and gaining a battle honor for it. A second such honor was won in the spring of 1944 for the division's role in the liberation of the city of Beltsy in Moldova. It ended the war at Prague, after advancing through Romania, Hungary and Austria.<cr><cr>
translation: 第303步兵师在德国入侵苏联后不久开始服役，最初作为标准的红军步兵师，在苏德战场中部地区战斗了几个月，并参与了红军在叶连纳的第一个攻势胜利。随后该师被包围并在维亚兹马附近作战中被消灭。几个月后重建的第303步兵师继续战斗，主要是在乌克兰中部地区。该师成员首次脱颖而出是在1943年夏季攻势期间，在维尔霍涅德尼普罗夫斯克渡过了第聂伯河，并因此获得了荣誉。第二次获得荣誉是在1944年春季，因在摩尔多瓦解放别列茨市中的作用而得。战争结束时该师推进至罗马尼亚、匈牙利和奥地利境内，在布拉格结束了战斗。<cr><cr><cr>

text: The 304th Rifle Division had its roots in the 109th Mechanized Division, which served before the Great Patriotic War as a mixed armor and infantry formation. Soon after the German invasion it was reorganized as a standard rifle division and renumbered as the 304th. It served in the southwestern part of the Soviet-German front for more than a year and a half, fighting under difficult conditions, including the German summer offensive of 1942. The division did not distinguish itself until Operation Uranus in late 1942 and the subsequent Operation Ring, in which it helped defeat the encircled German Sixth Army. In recognition of these successes, even before the German surrender at Stalingrad, it was raised to Guards status as the 67th Guards Rifle Division. A second 304th was raised six months later, based on a pair of rifle brigades, facing the German 17th Army in the Kuban. After helping to liberate this region the division continued in combat through Ukraine and Poland, winning its own distinctions at Zhitomir and an Order of the Red Banner, before ending the war near Prague.<cr><cr>
translation: 第304步兵师的前身是第109机械化师，该师在卫国战争爆发前是一支混合装甲和步兵部队。德国入侵后不久，它被重组为标准步兵师，并重新编号为第304师。该师在苏德战场西南部服役了一年半以上，在艰难条件下作战，包括1942年的德国夏季攻势。直到天王星行动（1942年末）和随后的“环”行动中，它才表现出色，帮助击败了被包围的德军第6集团军。为了表彰这些成就，甚至在斯大林格勒战役结束前，该师就被提升为近卫步兵师，并改名为第67近卫步兵师。六个月后，又组建了一个新的第304师，基于两个步兵旅，在库班地区对抗德军第17集团军。帮助解放了这一区域之后，该师继续在乌克兰和波兰作战，分别在日托米尔战役中表现出色，并获得了一枚红旗勋章，最终在布拉格附近结束战争。<cr><cr>指挥官报告<cr><cr>

text: The 304th Static Division was formed as a garrison division in November 1940 as part of the 13th Wave. It consisted of the 573rd, 574th and 575th Infantry Regiments, the 304th Artillery Regiment and various support units. In October 1942 the division was converted to a field division and sent to Russia. In April 1943 after fighting in the Don River basin the division was rebuilt. The 574th Grenadier Regiment was disbanded in October 1943. The division was heavily engaged in the summer of 1944 and suffered serious losses. In January 1945 the division was destroyed at the mouth of the Vistula River but was reformed in Prague in late February 1945. The division was taken prisoner by the Soviets near Deutsch-Brod at the end of the war.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第304步兵师于1940年11月作为守备师组建，属于第13波。该师包括第573、574和575步兵团，第304炮兵团以及各种支援单位。1942年10月，该师被改编为野战师并派往俄罗斯。1943年4月，在顿河盆地作战后，该师进行了重建。第574掷弹兵团于1943年10月解散。该师在1944年夏季遭受重创，并在1945年1月在维斯瓦河口被消灭。但同年2月底在布拉格重组。战败前夕，该师在德意志-布罗德附近被苏联俘虏。<cr>参考文献：George F. Nafziger, 《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>条目由Chris Munson提供

text: The 305th Rifle Division was formed for the first time as a standard Red Army rifle division shortly after the German invasion. It was soon sent north to the Volkhov Front near Novgorod. In the winter of 1942 it participated in an offensive to try to break the Siege of Leningrad which ended with it and most of the rest of the attacking force being cut off and gradually annihilated during the spring. A second 305th was raised a few months later in the southern part of the front, where it distinguished itself in the final liberation of Belgorod. It continued in combat through Ukraine and Poland before ending the war near Prague.<cr><cr>
translation: 第305步兵师首次组建于德国入侵后不久，作为标准的红军步兵师。它很快被派往北方，在诺夫哥罗德附近的沃尔霍夫方面军作战。1942年冬季，该师参与了一次旨在解除列宁格勒包围的进攻行动，但最终与大部分进攻部队一起被切断，并在春季逐渐被消灭殆尽。几个月后，第305步兵师在前线南部重新组建，在解放别尔哥罗德的最后阶段表现出色。它继续在乌克兰和波兰作战，直到战争结束时接近布拉格。<cr><cr><cr>

text: The 306th Rifle Division began its combat path under unusual circumstances. It was partly formed for the first time as a standard Red Army rifle division a few months after the German invasion, but the formation process appears to have been abandoned and the unit was never assigned to the front. A second formation began in April 1942 and was completed on June 16, after which it was sent to the Kalinin Front. Assigned to 43rd Army, it remained in that Army until November 1944, and in that Front (renamed 1st Baltic Front) until March 1945. It ended the war in Leningrad Front, helping to contain the German forces trapped in the Courland Pocket.<cr><cr>
translation: 第306步兵师在不同寻常的情况下开始了它的战斗历程。德国入侵几个月后，该师部分作为标准红军步兵师首次组建，但组建过程似乎被放弃，部队从未被分配到方面军。第二次组建始于1942年4月，并于6月16日完成，之后被派往加里宁方面军。隶属于第43集团军，直到1944年11月都留在该集团军内，在该方面军（改名为波罗的海第一方面军）内待到1945年3月。战争结束时在列宁格勒方面军，帮助围困了被封锁在库尔兰包围圈内的德军。<cr>指挥官报告：<cr><cr><cr>第306步兵师的战斗历程始于不同寻常的情况。德国入侵几个月后，该师部分作为标准红军步兵师首次组建，但组建过程似乎被放弃，部队从未被分配到方面军。第二次组建始于1942年4月，并于6月16日完成，之后被派往加里宁方面军。隶属于第43集团军，直到1944年11月都留在该集团军内，在该方面军（改名为波罗的海第一方面军）内待到1945年3月。战争结束时在列宁格勒方面军，帮助围困了被封锁在库尔兰包围圈内的德军。<cr><cr>

text: The 306th Static Division was formed in November 1940 as part of the 13th Wave. It consisted of the 579th, 580th and 581st Infantry Regiments, the 306th Artillery Regiment (with only two battalions) and various support units. The division was sent to Belgium in May 1941. In October 1942 the division was converted to a field division and in November sent to Russia. It fought in the Stalingrad relief campaign on the Don River and opposed the Soviet drive on Rostov. In November 1943 the division was filled out using forces of the disbanded 328th Infantry Division and its Grenadier regiments were reduced to two battalions each but the 306th Artillery Regiment now contained the standard three light and one heavy artillery battalions. In August and September 1944 the division was destroyed in Romania and was formally disbanded in October 1944.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, German Order of Battle Volume II: 291st-999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions, and Special Divisions in WWII<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第306步兵师成立于1940年11月，属于第13波组建的部队。该师包括第579团、第580团和第581团三个步兵团，以及拥有两个炮兵团的第306炮兵团和其他支援单位。1941年5月，该师被派往比利时。1942年10月，该师转为野战师，并于同年11月被派往俄罗斯。它参加了顿河斯大林格勒解围战役，并对抗苏联对罗斯托夫的攻势。1943年11月，该师使用解散的第328步兵师的部分兵力进行了补充，其掷弹兵团减少为每个团两个营，但第306炮兵团现在包含三个轻型和一个重型炮兵营。1944年8月至9月间，该师在罗马尼亚被消灭，并于同年10月正式解散。<cr>资料来源：George F. Nafziger, 《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, 《二战中的德国战斗序列 第二卷：第291至第999师、命名步兵师及其他特殊部队》<cr>词条提供：Chris Munson

text: The 307th Rifle Division was raised in 1941 as a standard Red Army rifle division, and served for the duration of WWII in that role. The division distinguished itself in the intense defensive fighting around the village of Ponyri during the Battle of Kursk. It was credited with the liberation of the town of Novozybkov on September 25, 1943. After battling its way through eastern Belarus during the autumn and winter of 1943-44, and then helping complete its liberation during Operation Bagration, it was moved to East Prussia, where it took part in the Battle of Knigsberg in the spring of 1945, ending the war on the Baltic coast near the Zemland Peninsula.<cr><cr>
translation: 第307步兵师于1941年作为标准的红军步兵师组建，并在第二次世界大战期间一直担任这一角色。该师在库尔斯克战役中围绕波尼里村进行的激烈防御战斗中表现出色。它因解放诺沃兹比科夫镇（时间为1943年9月25日）而受到表彰。在1943年至1944年的秋季和冬季，该师通过白俄罗斯东部地区时进行了艰苦作战，并在巴格拉季昂行动中帮助完成了该地区的解放后，被调往东普鲁士，在那里参加了1945年春季的柯尼斯堡战役，最终在波罗的海沿岸靠近泽姆兰半岛的地方结束了战争。<cr><cr>

text:
The 308th Rifle Division first started forming on 25 December 1941 at Ivanovo in the Moscow Military District. On 7 January 1942, while still forming the division was redesignated the 117th Rifle Division.<cr><cr>The 308th Rifle Division (2nd formation) was formed in accordance with Order Number 0044 of the Siberian Military District dated 21 March 1942.[2] It was formed at Omsk in the Siberian Military District, using 20% Red Army men (active duty), 25% returning wounded veterans, 25% reservists from industry, and 30% new recruits from the classes of 1922-23. Most of the recruits and reservists came from the Omsk and Krasnoyarsk oblasts. When the division left for the west it had 12,133 officers and men assigned.<cr><cr>The division remained in the Siberian Military District until May 1942 until it was moved to the west. In late May, the division was assigned to the 8th Reserve Army in the Reserve of the Supreme High Command. On 1 June 1942, the division, still with the 8th Reserve Army, was at Saratov.<cr><cr>By the end of September 1942 the division was assigned to the 62nd Army inside Stalingrad. For its actions at Stalingrad September to December 1942 it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner by an order dated 19 June 1943.<cr><cr>Reassigned to the Volga Military District to be rebuilt, the division spent the next several months reconstituting its strength. By 1 March 1943, the division was shipped back to the front and assigned to the Kalinin Front reserves and then to the 11th Army in the STAVKA reserves.<cr><cr>The division went back to the front in the 3rd Army of the Bryansk Front in Operation Kutuzov. Distinguishing itself in combat, the division was awarded Guards status and redesignated the 120th Guards Rifle Division. During the remainder of 1943 the division participated in the Orel, Bryansk, and Gomel - Rechitsa operations. The 308th became the 120th Guards Rifle Division in September 1943 in accordance with NKO Order Number 285.<cr><cr>This division was organized as a Red Army national unit from 5 June to 7 July 1944 from the 1st Latvian Riflemen Reserve Regiment at Gorkiy in the Moscow Military District. The division was the last national, 'ethnic' division formed during the war. The division was formed as a Latvian Division under the 130th Latvian Rifle Corps. The 130th Rifle Corps was assigned to the 2nd Baltic Front's 22nd Army from July to October 1944. They were then reassigned to the Leningrad Front's 67th Army. They fought at Aiviekste River, Jekabpils, Olaine, Dzukste and Blidene. By the end of the month the Corps was back with the 22nd Army and from March 1945 to the end of the war in Latvia, assigned to the Kurland Group on the Baltic Coast.

Gorokhovets district to 1st Latvian Riflemen Reserve Regiment. It contained 319th, 323rd, and 355th Riflemen and 677th Artillery Regiment, 301st Sapper Battalion, 899th Communications Battalion and Reconnaissance Company. Divisions beginning strength was about 7,300 men. On July 12, 1944, the Division headed to the front as part of the 130th Latvian Rifle Corps. First combat happened on August 5. They fought at Aiviekste River, Jekabpils, Olaine, Dzukste and Blidene.<cr><cr>

text: The 309th 'Berlin' Infantry Division was formed in February 1945 with two regiments from the 166th Reserve Division in Denmark, the Grossdeutschland Wachregiment and other forces. The division was destroyed in the Halbe Pocket.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第309“柏林”步兵师于1945年2月在丹麦从第166预备师的两个团、大日耳曼卫戍团和其他部队组建。该师在哈尔贝包围圈中被消灭。<cr>参考文献：乔治·F·纳夫齐格，《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>词条由克里斯·芒森提供

text: The 309th Rifle Division was formed for the first time as a standard Red Army rifle division shortly after the German invasion. It fought its first battles at the Yelnya salient, participating in that early Soviet success before being swept up in Operation Typhoon, encircled and destroyed. At the very end of 1941 the division was reformed. It served on mostly inactive sectors during 1942, but in 1943 it played an important role in containing the offensive of 4th Panzer Army at Kursk. It followed this in September with one of the first successful assault crossings of the Dnieper River, for which many men of the 309th were named as Heroes of the Soviet Union. The division continued in combat through Ukraine, Poland and Silesia before ending the war near Breslau.<cr><cr>
translation: 第309步兵师首次作为标准的红军步兵师组建于德国入侵后不久。它参加了叶尔尼亚突出部的第一次战斗，在早期苏联取得的成功中发挥了作用，随后被卷入台风行动，遭到包围并被消灭。1941年底该师重新组建。在1942年大部分时间里，它驻守在相对平静的战线上，但在1943年，它在库尔斯克战役中对第4装甲集团军的进攻起到了重要的遏制作用。同年9月，该师成功地进行了第聂伯河首次成功的突击渡河行动，许多第309步兵师的官兵因此被授予苏联英雄称号。该师继续在乌克兰、波兰和西里西亚作战，并最终在布雷斯劳附近结束战争。<cr><cr>

text: Tthe 30th Army was formed on 13 July 1941 based on the 52nd Rifle Corps from the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (Stavka). Initially, the 5th Army consisted of the 119th Rifle Division, 242nd Rifle Division, 243rd Rifle Division, 251st Rifle Division, 51st Tank Division, artillery and other units. The army was built around a solid core of NKVD border guard servicemen. The army's first commander, Major General Vasily Khomenko, was the former commander of the Ukrainian District of NKVD Border Guards.<cr>On 15 July 1941 the army was transferred to the Front of the Reserve Armies and assisted to construct defensive works on the defensive line running through Selizharovo, Olenino, and Vasilievo.<cr>The army fought in the Battle of Smolensk from the end of July to August 1941 and later formed part of the Western Front from 21 July. During the battle, 30th Army troops attacked Dukhovshchina from the region south-west of Bely. The army's attacks on the flanks of the German Ninth Army stopped and sapped the strength of the German forces. Between September and October the army fought in defensive operations around the region.<cr>On 17 October 1941 army was incorporated to the Kalinin Front and took part in Kalinin Defensive Operation (5 December 1941 - 7 January 1942).<cr>On 18 November army was again switched to the Western Front. The army fought in the Klin-Solnecznogorsk Defensive Operation (15 November-5 December) and from 6 December on, in the Klin-Solnecznogorsk Offensive Operation (6-25 December). During the operation 30th Army together with 1st Shock Army liberated Klin (15 December)and destroyed a number of German units. As part of the Kalinin Front (from 17 December 1941) during January-April 1942, the army participated in Rzhev-Vyazma Strategic Operation (8 January-20 April). At the end of the operation, army troops nearly reached Rzhev and then took up defensive positions.<cr>On 1 March 1942 the army consisted of the 174th, 178th, 243rd, 348th, 359th, 363rd, 371st, 375th, and 379th Rifle Divisions, and the 75th, 76th, 139th, 145th, 146th, 148th, 149th, 150th, 151st, 152nd, 153rd, and 222nd Separate Ski Brigades.<cr>Later (from 31 August as part of the Western Front) until the end of 1942 army defended and strengthened its position and occasionally went on the offensive.<cr>On March 1943 troops of the army participated in the Rzhev-Vyazma Operation (2-31 March), subsequently liberating Rzhev and on 1 April reached the line Nefedovschina-Pantiukchy where it stopped to dig into defensive positions.<cr>On 16 April the army was reformed into 10th Guards Army.<cr><cr>
translation: 第30集团军于1941年7月13日成立，基于最高统帅部大本营预备队的第52步兵军。最初，该集团军包括第119步兵师、第242步兵师、第243步兵师、第251步兵师、第51坦克师以及炮兵和其他部队。该集团军的核心是由内务人民委员部边防警卫人员组成。首任指挥官瓦西里·霍梅尼科少将曾是乌克兰内务人民委员部边防警卫区的指挥官。<cr>1941年7月15日，该集团军被调往预备方面军，并协助在塞利扎罗沃、奥列宁诺和瓦西里耶夫一线构筑防御工事。<cr>第30集团军于1941年7月底至8月期间参加了斯摩棱斯克战役，并从7月21日起成为西方方面军的一部分。在这场战斗中，第30集团军的部队从别利西南部地区进攻杜霍夫什钦纳。该集团军对德国第九集团军侧翼的攻击削弱了德军的力量。<cr>9月至10月期间，该集团军在加里宁地区参加了防御作战。<cr>1941年10月17日，该集团军被编入加里宁方面军，并参与了加里宁防御战役（1941年12月5日至1942年1月7日）。11月18日，集团军再次被转移到西方面军。该集团军参加了克林-索列茨科戈尔斯克防御战役（11月15日至12月5日）和克林-索列茨科戈尔斯克进攻战役（12月6日至25日）。在此次行动中，第30集团军与第1突击集团军合作解放了克林，并消灭了一定数量的德国部队。作为加里宁方面军的一部分（从1941年12月17日起），该集团军于1942年1月至4月期间参加了日兹德拉-维亚兹马战略行动（1月8日至4月20日）。在此次行动结束时，集团军部队几乎到达了日兹德拉，并随后转入防御态势。<cr>1942年3月1日，该集团军包括第174、178、243、348、359、363、371、375和379步兵师以及第75、76、139、145、146、148、149、150、151、152、153和222独立滑雪旅。<cr>之后（从1942年8月31日起作为西方面军的一部分），直到1942年底，该集团军一直在保卫并加强其阵地，并偶尔发起进攻。<cr>1943年3月，该集团军部队参加了日兹德拉-维亚兹马行动（3月2日至31日），随后解放了日兹德拉，并于4月1日到达涅费多夫斯科耶-潘图克奇线，在此转入防御态势。<cr>4月16日，该集团军重组为第10近卫集团军。<cr><cr>

text: The 30th Guards Rifle Division was reformed as an elite infantry division of the Red Army in May, 1942, based on the 1st formation of the 238th Rifle Division, and served in that role until after the end of WWII. It would soon after help provide the headquarters cadre for the 7th Guards Rifle Corps along with its 'sister' 29th Guards Rifle Division. However, it was not assigned as a unit to the Corps until August when it joined 33rd Army of Western Front and saw extensive fighting, while also suffering extensive casualties, in the summer campaign against the German 3rd Panzer Army in the southern sector of the Rzhev salient. After leaving 7th Guards Corps the division was reassigned to several other armies in the Front until April, 1943 when it joined the 15th Guards Rifle Corps in 30th Army, which became 10th Guards Army the next month; it would remain under these commands for the duration of the war. The division took part in Operation Suvorov, Western Front's summer offensive towards Smolensk, and after the liberation of that city was involved in several unsuccessful drives on the Belarussian city of Orsha. By December the 30th Guards had been redeployed to 2nd Baltic Front and during the summer and fall of 1944 it took part in the offensives through the Baltic states, winning a battle honor for its part in the liberation of Riga. For the rest of the war the division remained in Latvia helping to contain the German forces trapped in the Courland Peninsula, eventually coming under command of Leningrad Front.<cr><cr>
translation: 第30近卫步兵师于1942年5月作为红军精锐步兵师重建，基于第238步兵师的第一个编制。该师在第二次世界大战结束之后继续服役。不久后，它与“姊妹”部队第29近卫步兵师一起为第7近卫步兵军司令部提供人员，并于同年8月被分配到西方面军的第33集团军，在夏季攻势中对抗德国第3装甲集团军时遭受了重大损失。离开第7近卫步兵军后，该师在前线所属的不同集团军之间多次调动，直到1943年4月加入第15近卫步兵军（隶属于第30集团军），后者于次月成为第10近卫集团军；在整个战争期间，该师一直在这两个指挥下服役。该师参加了苏沃洛夫行动，即西方面军向斯摩棱斯克的夏季攻势，并在解放这座城市后参与了几次对白俄罗斯城市奥尔沙的未遂进攻。到12月，第30近卫步兵师被重新部署至第二波罗的海方面军，在1944年夏秋之际参加了通过波罗的海国家的攻势行动，并因解放里加而获得了一项荣誉勋章。在战争剩余时间里，该师一直驻扎在拉脱维亚，帮助封锁困于库尔兰半岛上的德军部队，最终被列宁格勒方面军指挥。

text: The 30th Infantry Division was with Army Group North from 1941 until the end of the war. It fought in the Battle of Dvinsk (1941) and was encircled at Demyansk with II Corps in January 1942. It was not relieved for more than a year. During that time, three of its grenadier battalions were disbanded due to high casualties. After it was freed in February 1943, the Briesen Division fought at Staraja Russa, in the Leningrad withdrawal, in the retreat through the Baltic States, and in the six battles of the Courland Pocket. It finally surrendered in the Courland Pocket on May 8, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第30步兵师从1941年到战争结束都隶属于北方集团军群。它参加了德维纳河战役（1941年），并在1942年1月与第二军在德米扬斯克被包围。超过一年时间里，该师都没有得到解围。在此期间，由于伤亡惨重，其三个掷弹兵营都被解散了。1943年2月获释后，布里森师参加了斯塔罗亚罗斯卡、列宁格勒撤退、波罗的海诸国撤退以及库尔兰包围圈内的六次战斗。最终于1945年5月8日在库尔兰包围圈内投降。<cr>德国二战步兵师战斗序列 第1至290师, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text: The 30th Mountain Division was formed in October 1918 by the merger of the 3rd and 4th infantry divisions of the Ural as the 4th Ural Infantry Division. In November 1918 the division was renamed the 30th Rifle Division. In 1939, based on 30th Rifle Division units, the 132nd and 176th Rifle Divisions were created. Subsequently, the division was reformed as the 30th Mountain Rifle Division and began World War II under this name. At the start of Operation Barbarossa the division was stationed on the Soviet-Romanian border on the Prut River at Sculeni. The division was part of the 35th Rifle Corps of the 9th Army. By June 24th the division was engaged and forced to retreat on June 30, 1941. During the disorganized retreat the division lost much equipment and personnel. On July 5th the division held positions from Popovka to Lipovanka. By July 7, 1941 the division was in reserve and numbered no more than one regiment. The division was again renamed the 30th Rifle Division in August 1941.<cr>On August 6, 1941 the division was transferred to the Separate Coastal Army which was entrusted with the defense of Odessa. Before managing to link up with the Separate Coastal Army however, the division was cut off and was forced to withdraw to the Southern Bug River. The division was then involved in defensive and offensive battles around Rostov, holding the line on the Mius River. In January 1942 the division crossed the Mius and in March 1942 participated in the attack on Taganrog. From the second half of July 1942 the division conducted a fighting retreat in the Caucasus. On July 25th after covering the crossing of the Don River in the Azov area for three days, the division defended positions in the area of Krasnodar. On August 12th the division was forced to retreat from Krasnodar. In August, the division defending near Goryachy Klyuch and then was part of the Tuapse Defensive Operation. By August 20, 1942 the division covered the road through the Pyatigorsk and Khrebtovy passes. After a lull in the fighting which lasted until September 23, 1942 the division was again involved in heavy fighting. By the end of October the 30th Rifle Division held the line in the Kaverze River valley, covering the Khrebtovy Pass. On 12 December 1942 the division became the 55th Guards Rifle Division as a reward for its actions.<cr>The division was reformed at Rossosh in April 1943. It fought at Rostov, Kiev, Zhitomir and in the Carpathian Mountains. It was with 38th Army of the 4th Ukrainian Front in May 1945. The division was disbanded with the Northern Group of Forces in the summer of 1945.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第30山地师成立于1918年10月，由乌拉尔地区的第3步兵师和第4步兵师合并而成的第4乌拉尔步兵师。1918年11月，该师更名为第30步兵师。1939年，基于第30步兵师的部分单位组建了第132步兵师和第176步兵师。随后，该师重组为第30山地步兵师，并以这个名字开始第二次世界大战。巴巴罗萨行动初期，该师驻扎在苏联与罗马尼亚边境的普鲁特河畔斯库列尼地区，隶属于第9集团军下的第35步兵军。到1941年6月24日，该师已投入战斗，并被迫于同年6月30日撤退。在混乱的撤退过程中，该师损失了大量装备和人员。至7月5日，该师从波波夫卡到利波万卡地区坚守阵地。到1941年7月7日，该师已进入预备状态，并仅剩一个团的兵力。该师于1941年8月再次更名为第30步兵师。<cr>1941年8月6日，该师被转移到负责敖德萨防御的独立海岸集团军。然而，在与独立海岸集团军会合之前，该师被切断并被迫撤退到南方布格河。随后，该师在罗斯托夫周围进行了防御和进攻战斗，并在米乌斯河一线坚守阵地。1942年1月，该师渡过米乌斯河；3月份参加了对塔甘罗格的攻击。从1942年7月中旬开始，该师在高加索地区进行艰苦撤退。7月25日，在阿佐夫地区掩护顿河渡口三天后，该师在克拉斯诺达尔附近坚守阵地。8月12日，该师被迫从克拉斯诺达尔撤出。8月份，该师在戈利亚奇克利切附近进行防御，并参与了图阿普谢防御行动。到1942年8月20日，该师掩护了皮亚季戈尔斯克和赫雷布托夫隘口的道路。战斗间歇期持续至1942年9月23日之后，该师再次卷入激烈战斗。到10月底，第30步兵师在卡弗尔泽河谷一线坚守阵地，并掩护了赫雷布托夫隘口。1942年12月12日，该师因行动表现优异而改编为第55近卫步兵师。<cr>该师于1943年4月在罗斯奥什重组。它参加了罗斯托夫、基辅、日托米尔和喀尔巴阡山脉的战斗。1945年5月，它隶属于第4乌克兰方面军的第38集团军。该师随着北方集团军群于1945年夏季解散。<cr><cr>克里斯·芒森提供

text: The 30th Guards Rifle Corps was formed in April 1943 on the basis of three guards rifle divisions, which had distinguished themselves in battle to break through the Siege of Leningrad - the 45th, 63rd and 64th (the last came from the Volkhov Front). So the corps was a Guards unit from the first day of its formation. Nikolai P. Simoniak, who had received for Operation Spark the title of Hero of the Soviet Union, was appointed as commander.<cr>Until the second week of February 1944, the two armies of the Leningrad Front had deployed only vanguard elements while attempting to force entry into Estonia. Army General Leonid A. Govorov of Leningrad Front ordered the 2nd Shock Army to break through the German defence line north and south of Narva town, move the front fifty kilometres westwards and continue towards the town of Rakvere. The artillery of the 2nd Shock army opened fire on all German positions on 11 February, continuing the Battle for Narva Bridgehead. The 30th Guards Rifle Corps joined the Soviet units attempting to seize the Auvere station. The guards riflemen widened the bridgehead to ten kilometres along the front. The remains of the German 227th and 170th Infantry Divisions retreated. General Major Romantsov ordered an assault at Auvere settlement by the Air Force and artillery on 13 February, with the 64th Guard Rifle Division seizing the village in a surprise attack. Half a kilometre westward from Auvere station, the 191st Guard Rifle Regiment cut through the railway two kilometres from the Tallinn highway, which was the last way out for Army Group Narwa, but was repelled by the 170th Infantry Division and the 502nd Heavy Panzer Battalion.<cr><cr>
translation:
第30近卫步兵军成立于1943年4月，由三个在列宁格勒解围战役中表现突出的近卫步兵师组建而成——分别是第45、63和64步兵师（最后一个来自沃尔霍夫方面军）。因此该军从成立之初就是一支近卫部队。尼古拉·P·西蒙尼亚克因火花行动获得苏联英雄称号，被任命为指挥官。

直到1944年2月第二周之前，列宁格勒方面军的两个集团军在试图进入爱沙尼亚时只部署了先头部队。列宁格勒方面军司令亚历山大·L·戈沃罗夫将军命令第2突击集团军突破纳尔瓦镇北南两侧的德国防线，将战线向西推进五十公里，并继续朝拉克韦雷镇方向进攻。1944年2月11日，第2突击集团军炮兵对所有德国阵地开火，继续进行纳尔瓦桥头堡战役。第30近卫步兵军加入苏联部队试图夺取奥乌弗车站的行动中。近卫步枪手将桥头堡沿战线扩大到十公里宽。德军第227和170步兵师残部撤退。少校罗曼采夫于2月13日命令空军和炮兵对奥乌弗定居点发动突击，第64近卫步兵师在一次突袭中占领了村庄。

从奥乌弗车站西边半公里处，第191近卫步兵团切断了距离塔林公路两公里的铁路线，这是北方集团军群最后一条撤退路线，但被第170步兵师和第502重型装甲营击退。

text:
The 30th Mountain Division was renamed the 30th Rifle Division on 25 August 1941.<cr><cr>The division was part of the 'operational army' from 22 June 1941 to 18 December 1942.

On 22 June 1941, the division was stationed at the Soviet-Romanian border on the river Prut at Sculeni (Calarasi, Frontier District Number 5). The division was part of the 35th Rifle Corps of the 9th Army. On 24 June 1941 the division had entered the battle and was forced to retreat on 30 June 1941. The division held the line of Vnishora, German, and Petreshtipri. During the disorganized retreat the division lost much equipment and personnel. On 5 July the division held positions at the front from Popovka to Lipovanka. On 7 July 1941 the division was in reserve. Up to 11 July, the division numbered no more than one regiment.

On 6 August 1941, the division was transferred to the Separate Coastal Army, which was entrusted with the defense of Odessa, but before managing to link up with the Separate Coastal Army, the division was cut off, without linking up with the main forces of the army, and was forced to withdraw to the Southern Bug River. Then the division was involved in defensive and offensive battles on the Rostov axis, holding the line on the river Mius. In January 1942 the division crossed the Mius and in March 1942 participated in the attack on Taganrog. From the second half of July 1942 the division conducted a fighting retreat in the Caucasus. On 25 July, after covering the crossing of the Don in the Azov area for three days, the division defended positions in the area of Krasnodar. On 12 August the division was forced to retreat from Krasnodar. In August, the division defended near Goryachy Klyuch.

The division fought in the Tuapse Defensive Operation. By 20 August 1942 the division covered the road through the Pyatigorsk and Khrebtovy passes, After a lull in the fighting, which lasted until 23 September 1942, the division was again involved in heavy fighting. By the end of October the 30th Rifle Division held the line in the Kaverze River valley, covering the Khrebtovy Pass. On 12 December 1942 the division was transformed into the 55th Guards Rifle Division as a reward for its actions.

The Second Formation of the 30th Rifle Division was recreated at Rossosh in April 1943. It fought at Rostov, Kiev, Zhitomir, and in the Carpathian Mountains. It was with 38th Army of the 4th Ukrainian Front in May 1945.<cr><cr>
