text: The 339th Static Division was formed in December 1940 as part of the 14th Wave using three battalions from the 52nd Infantry Division, two from a fortress regiment and one from the 229th Infantry Division. It consisted of the 691st, 692nd and 693rd Infantry Regiments, 339th Artillery Battalion and various support units. The artillery battalion was formed into a three battalion regiment in June 1943. In November 1943 the division was reduced to the 339th Divisional Group and merged with other divisions to form the 'C' Army Detachment. Remnants of the division were sent to Poland where they were used to rebuild the 363rd Infantry Division.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第339步兵师成立于1940年12月，作为第14波组建的一部分，该师从第52步兵师抽调了三个营，从一个要塞团抽调了两个营，并从第229步兵师抽调了一个营。它包括第691、692和693步兵团，第339炮兵营以及各种支援单位。该炮兵营于1943年6月扩编为三个营的团级编制。1943年11月，该师被缩减为第339师群，并与其他师合并组建了“C”集团军群附队。该师残部被派往波兰，用于重建第363步兵师。<cr>参考文献：George F. Nafziger, 《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr><cr>-<cr>克里斯·芒森提供

text: The 33rd Army was initially formed in the Moscow Military District in July 1941, consisting of the 1st, 5th, 9th, 17th, and 21st Moscow People's Militia divisions, plus artillery and other support units.<cr>With the arrival of the German 2nd Panzer Army to Kashira and its 4th Panzer Group to the Moskva-Volga Canal, the Gemans were poised to assault Moscow. On December 1, the Germans hit the centre of the Soviet front. Two German divisions with 70 tanks broke through in the 33rd Army's sector in the 222nd Rifle Division's area to the north of Naro-Fominsk. On December 2, in the 110th Rifle Division's sector the Wehrmacht went over to the offensive and attacked in the direction of Mogutovo. The 113th Rifle Division together with a regiment from 43rd Army led a counteroffensive on Klotovo and Kamenskoe with the task of hitting the rear of the Germans to relieve the pressure on the 110th Rifle Division. As a result of this counterstroke, the enemy was routed. The Soviets captured 47 tanks and about 50 guns. From the west at Naro Fominsk Germans drovr on to Kubinka along a highway, and then to Golitcin and Aprelevka, threatening rears of 33rd and 5th Soviet Armies. At Akulovo village German forces have met with 32nd Rifle Division and artillery fire. It was the last German attempt to break through to Moscow.<cr>At the Battle of Smolensk (1943), after a day of probing, the goal of which was to determine whether German troops had chosen to withdraw from the first set of trenches. The offensive started on 7 August 1943 at 0630 (with a preliminary bombardment starting at 0440) with a breakthrough towards Roslavl. Three armies (under the control of Soviet Western Front) were committed to this offensive: the 5th Army, the 10th Guards Army and the 33rd Army.<cr>However, the attack quickly encountered heavy opposition and stalled. German troops attempted numerous counterattacks from their well-prepared defense positions, supported by tanks, assault guns, and the fire of heavy guns and mortars. On the first day, the Soviet troops advanced only 4 kilometers, with all available troops (including artillery, communications men and engineers) committed to battle.<cr>From April 1944 the 33rd Army, participated in Operation Bagration to retake Belarus as part of the 2nd Belorussian Front. During the Mogilyov Offensive it successfully crossed the Dniepr and Pronya rivers, and liberated Shklov on June 27, 1944. During the Minsk Offensive the army, in conjunction with the 50th and 49th Armies, participated in the rout of the surrounded Wehrmacht forces to the east of Minsk. At the end of July-August the Army participated in the Kaunas Offensive during which it cleared the approaches to East Prussia. On September 10, it was released from VGK reserve, and joined the 1st Belorussian Front on October 19 in preparation for the Warsaw-Poznan Offensive.<cr>On 1 May 1945 during the Battle of Berlin, the Army consisted of the 16th Rifle Corps (323, 339, 383 RDs), 62nd Rifle Corps (95, 222, 362 RDs), 49th Rifle Division, 115th, 119th Fortified Region, and other support formations and units. After the initial Berlin breakthrough, 33rd Army, alongside other armies of the 1st Belorussian and 1st Ukrainian Fronts helped to rout the surrounded German forces to the east of Berlin. Military operation for 33rd Army concluded on 6 May. <cr><cr>
translation: 第33集团军于1941年7月在莫斯科军区成立，最初由第1、第5、第9、第17和第21莫斯科人民民兵师组成，加上炮兵和其他支援单位。<cr>随着德国第2装甲集团军抵达卡希拉以及其第4装甲集群到达莫斯科-伏尔加运河，德军准备突击莫斯科。12月1日，德军击中了苏军防线的中心。两个拥有70辆坦克的德军师在第33集团军辖区内的第222步兵师北部地区突破至纳罗-福米诺斯克以北。<cr>12月2日，在第110步兵师辖区内，国防军转入进攻并朝莫古托沃方向发动攻击。第113步兵师与来自第43集团军的一个团联合发起反攻，目标是打击德军后方以减轻对第110步兵师的压力。由于这次反击，敌人溃退了。苏军俘获了47辆坦克和大约50门火炮。<cr>从西面的纳罗-福米诺斯克，德国人沿着公路推进至库宾卡，然后到达戈利琴和阿普列沃卡，威胁到第33集团军和第5苏联集团军的后方。在阿库洛沃村，德军部队遭遇了第32步兵师和炮火攻击。<cr>这是德国人最后一次试图突破至莫斯科。<cr><cr>在斯摩棱斯克战役（1943年）中，在一天的试探性进攻之后，目标是确定德军是否选择从第一道战壕撤退。这次攻势于1943年8月7日06:30开始（初步炮击始于04:40），突破方向为罗斯拉夫尔。<cr>苏联西方面军投入了三个集团军：第5集团军、第10近卫集团军和第33集团军。然而，攻击很快遇到了强烈的抵抗并停滞不前。德国军队从其准备充分的防御阵地多次发起反攻，得到坦克、突击炮以及重型火炮和迫击炮火力的支持。第一天里，苏联部队仅推进了4公里，所有可用部队（包括炮兵、通信人员和工兵）都投入战斗。<cr>自1944年4月起，第33集团军参加了巴格拉季昂行动，作为第二白俄罗斯方面军的一部分收复白俄罗斯。在莫吉廖夫攻势期间，该部队成功渡过了第聂伯河和普罗尼亚河，并于1944年6月27日解放了什克洛夫。在明斯克攻势中，该集团军与第50集团军和第49集团军协同作战，在明斯克以东包围并击败了国防军部队。<cr>7月底至8月初，该集团军参加了考纳斯攻势，清理了进入东普鲁士的路线。1944年9月10日，它从苏军总参谋部预备队中释放出来，并于10月19日加入第一白俄罗斯方面军，为华沙-波兹南攻势做准备。<cr>1945年5月1日在柏林战役期间，第33集团军由第16步兵军（第323、339和383步兵师）、第62步兵军（第95、222和362步兵师）、第49步兵师、第115和119要塞区以及其他支援部队组成。在突破柏林后，第33集团军与其他第一白俄罗斯方面军和第一乌克兰方面军的军队一起，在柏林以东包围并击败了德国军队。<cr>军事行动于5月6日结束。

text: The 33rd Guards Rifle Division was formed as an elite infantry division of the Red Army in May, 1942, based on the 2nd formation of the 3rd Airborne Corps, and served in that role until after the end of the WWII. It was the second of a series of ten Guards rifle divisions formed from airborne corps during the spring and summer of 1942. It was briefly assigned to the 47th Army in the North Caucasus Front but was soon moved to the Volga Military District and saw its first action as part of 62nd Army in the fighting on the approaches to Stalingrad. It was withdrawn east of the Volga in September, but returned to the front with the 2nd Guards Army in December, and it remained in this Army until early 1945. After helping to defeat Army Group Don's attempt to relieve the trapped 6th Army at Stalingrad the 33rd Guards joined in the pursuit across the southern Caucasus steppe until reaching the Mius River in early 1943. Through the rest of that year it fought through the southern sector of eastern Ukraine as part of Southern Front (later 4th Ukrainian Fronts) and in the spring of 1944 assisted in the liberation of the Crimea, earning a battle honor in the process. The Crimea was a strategic dead-end, so 2nd Guards Army was moved north to take part in the summer offensive through the Baltic states and to the border with Germany as part of 1st Baltic Front. During the offensive into East Prussia the division and its 13th Guards Rifle Corps was reassigned to 39th and the 43rd 43rd Armies before returning to 2nd Guards Army in April. For its part in the capture of the city-fortress of Knigsberg the 33rd Guards would receive the Order of Suvorov.<cr><cr>
translation: 第33近卫步兵师于1942年5月作为红军精锐步兵师组建，基于第二空降军的第二次编成。它在这一角色中一直服役到二战结束之后。它是1942年春夏季从空降军改编而成的十个近卫步兵师中的第二个。该师曾短暂隶属于高加索方面军第47集团军，但很快被调往伏尔加河军区，并作为第62集团军的一部分参加了斯大林格勒外围战斗。它于9月撤至伏尔加河西岸，在12月随第2近卫集团军重返前线，并一直留在该集团军直到1945年初。在帮助击败德军顿河集团军试图解救被困的第6集团军之后，第33近卫步兵师参加了穿越南部高加索草原的追击行动，直至抵达米乌斯河（1943年初）。同年余下时间里，它作为南方方面军（后为第4乌克兰方面军）的一部分，在东乌克兰南部地区作战。1944年春季，该师协助解放了克里米亚，并因此获得了一项荣誉。由于克里米亚是一个战略死胡同，第2近卫集团军被调往北方参加波罗的海诸国夏季攻势，并作为第1波罗的海方面军的一部分推进至德国边境。在进攻东普鲁士期间，该师及其第13近卫步兵军曾先后隶属于第39和第43集团军，在4月返回第2近卫集团军。由于攻克了要塞城市柯尼斯堡，第33近卫步兵师将获得苏沃洛夫勋章。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The corps was assigned to Arkhangelsk Military District in June 1941 and was the basis for forming 43rd Army in July. The corps was reformed as part of 2nd Ukrainian Front in January 1944. At that time, it consisted of 50th and 297th Rifle Divisions. It fought as a part of 27th Army in Moldova in 1944, participating in the Iasi-Kishinev Offensive in August 1944. At that time, it consisted of 93rd Guards Rifle Division and 78th, 202nd, and 206th Rifle Divisions. Transferred to 6th Guards Tank Army, it fought in Hungary for the rest of the war. In October 1944, it consisted of 78th and 337th Rifle Divisions and 1st Rumanian Volunteer Rifle Division. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军于1941年6月被分配到阿尔汉格尔斯克军区，并成为在7月组建第43集团军的基础。该军于1944年1月作为第2乌克兰方面军的一部分重组，当时由第50步兵师和第297步兵师组成。它作为第27集团军的一部分，在摩尔多瓦作战，参与了1944年8月的伊阿西-奇什利纳攻势。此时，该军包括第93近卫步兵师、第78步兵师、第202步兵师和第206步兵师。转隶给第6近卫坦克集团军后，它在匈牙利作战直到战争结束。1944年10月，该军包括第78步兵师、第337步兵师以及第1罗马尼亚志愿步兵师。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军在伟大卫国战争中的战斗序列, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>词条由Stewart King提供

text: The 33rd Rifle Division was formed in 1922 at Samara and moved to Belarus in the next year. It fought in the Soviet invasion of Poland in September 1939 and in the Occupation of Lithuania in June 1940. After Operation Barbarossa, the division fought in the Baltic Operation and Leningrad Strategic Defensive. In January 1942, it fought in the Tropets-Kholm Offensive. The division participated in the Leningrad-Novgorod Offensive, the Pskov-Ostrov Offensive, the Tartu Offensive and the Riga Offensive. In 1945, the division fought in the East Pomeranian Offensives and the Battle of Berlin.<cr><cr>
translation: 第33步兵师成立于1922年在萨马拉，并于次年迁至白俄罗斯。该师参加了苏联入侵波兰（1939年9月）和占领立陶宛（1940年6月）的行动。巴巴罗萨行动后，该师参与了波罗的海战役和列宁格勒战略防御战。1942年1月，该师参加了特罗佩茨-霍尔姆攻势。之后，该师还参与了列宁格勒-诺夫哥罗德攻势、普斯科夫-奥斯特罗夫攻势、塔尔图攻势以及里加攻势。1945年，该师参加了东波美拉尼亚攻势和柏林战役。<cr><cr>

33rd Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>The 33rd Tank Division had only 40 T-26 tanks on hand on 22 June, no antiaircraft guns, and was short almost 90% of the trucks and tractors it was authorized. It was, officially, 'not up to strength' and considered the least ready division in 11th Mechanized Corps. On its first move, on 22 June, it was caught by the Luftwaffe and lost 50% of the equipment it did have. text:
The 340th Rifle Division began forming in August, 1941, at Balashov, in the Volga Military District. In December it was assigned to the 50th Army, Western Front, near Tula. The Division fought with some success in the Soviet Winter Offensive but by May 1942 it was in reserve recovering from its losses. In July, assigned to the Bryansk Front, it attempted to stop the Axis summer offensive with limited success. 

In late 1942 the Division was transferred to the Voronezh Front and in February 1943 took part in the liberation of Belgorod, and later on Sumy and Kiev. The division fought across the Ukraine and Poland and finished the war In Slovakia assigned to the 38th Army, 4th Ukrainian Front.

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov, Order of Kutuzov and the honorifics 'SUMY' and 'KIEV'.




Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第340步兵师于1941年8月在伏尔加河军区的巴拉萨沃开始组建。同年12月，该师被分配到西方方面军的第50集团军，在图拉附近作战。该师参加了苏联冬季攻势，并取得了一定的成功，但到了1942年5月，由于损失严重而转入预备状态恢复实力。

7月，该师被调往布良斯克方面军，试图阻止轴心国夏季攻势，但收效有限。1942年底，该师转隶沃罗涅日方面军，并于1943年2月参加了贝尔哥罗德的解放行动，随后又参与了苏缅和基辅的战斗。

该师在乌克兰、波兰作战，并最终在斯洛伐克结束战争，隶属于第4乌克兰方面军的第38集团军。

该师荣获红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫勋章、库图佐夫勋章以及“苏缅”、“基辅”的荣誉称号。

text:
The 341st Rifle Division first formed on September 1, 1941 in the North Caucasus Military District at Stalingrad. <cr><cr>
Col. Aleksandr Ilich Shchagin was assigned to command of the division on the day it began forming, and he continued in command throughout the existence of this formation. The division's personnel contained a significant number of non-Russian nationality. In October, while still barely formed, the division was assigned to 57th Army, which was also just in the process of forming-up in the Reserve of the Supreme High Command. In December the division and its Army moved to join Southwestern Front, taking part in the winter counter-offensive which led to the creation of the Izium salient south of Kharkov. By the end of January 1942, the 341st had been transferred to 9th Army in Southern Front, on the southern flank of the salient. It was still holding this position on May 17, as Southwestern Front was attacking northwards from the salient towards Kharkov, when the 14th Panzer Division of 1st Panzer Army smashed through the division's flank, driving its remnants north and west into what became the Izium Pocket. While 9th Army continued to carry the 341st in its order of battle until June 1, in fact it had broken up within 48 hours of the German attack; while Colonel Shchagin and many other personnel managed to escape, the division was effectively disbanded on May 19.<cr><cr>About two years later, almost to the day, a new 341st Rifle Division began forming on May 1, 1944, in the Karelian Front, based on the 77th Naval Rifle Brigade in 19th Army.Col. Ivan Vasilievich Obydenkin commanded the reformed division until mid-October. He was briefly succeeded by Col. A. V. Molokov until Col. Ignatii Alekseevich Moskalev took command on October 28, which he would hold for the duration of the war. The division served directly under 19th Army through September, taking part in the limited fighting that pushed Finnish forces back from Kandalaksha towards Alakurtti. In November the 341st moved even farther north, to the 131st Rifle Corps in 14th Army, which by then was simply a garrison force in northern Finland. In January 1945, the division left the active forces completely, assigned to the Belomorsky Military District on coastal defense duties.<cr><cr>
translation:
第341步兵师于1941年9月1日在斯大林格勒的北高加索军区首次组建。<cr><cr><cr>

亚历山大·伊里奇·什加金上校被指派在该师成立当天担任指挥官，并一直负责直到这支部队解散。该师人员中包含大量非俄罗斯族裔。10月，尽管尚未完全组建完成，第341步兵师还是被分配给正在编成中的最高统帅部预备队的第57集团军。<cr>12月，该师及其所属集团军转移到西南方面军，参与了冬季反攻行动，在哈尔科夫以南形成了伊久姆突出部。到1942年1月底，第341步兵师被调往南方战线的第9集团军，位于突出部的南部翼侧。<cr>5月17日，当西南方面军从突出部向北进攻哈尔科夫时，该师仍在坚守这一位置。此时，第1装甲集团军的第14装甲师突破了其侧翼，将其残余部队驱赶至西北方向，形成了伊久姆包围圈。<cr>尽管第9集团军在战斗序列中继续保留第341步兵师直到6月1日，实际上该师在德国进攻后的48小时内就已经瓦解；什加金上校和其他许多人员设法逃脱，但该师事实上已于5月19日解散。<cr><cr><cr>大约两年后，几乎到同一天，一个新的第341步兵师于1944年5月1日在卡累利阿方面军开始组建，该师基于第19集团军中的第77海军步兵旅。伊万·瓦西里耶维奇·奥宾德金科上校指挥重组后的师直到10月中旬。他短暂被亚历山大·瓦西里耶维奇·莫洛可夫上校接替，后者于10月28日被伊格纳季·阿列克谢耶维奇·莫斯卡列夫上校取代，并一直担任该职直至战争结束。从9月份开始，第341步兵师直接隶属于第19集团军，在有限的战斗中将芬兰军队从金吉尔克沙推回到阿拉库尔蒂。到了11月，第341步兵师进一步向北调动至第14集团军中的第131步兵军，该军此时只是在芬兰北部担任守备任务的一个部队。1945年1月，该师完全退出现役，被分配到别洛摩尔斯克军区执行海岸防御任务。<cr>指挥官报告：奥宾德金科、莫洛可夫、莫斯卡列夫<cr>

text: The 342nd Rifle Division began forming in September 1941, as a standard Red Army rifle division, in the Saratov oblast. It arrived at the front southwest of Moscow in December, in time to take part in the winter counteroffensive. During most of 1942 and into 1943 the division served in primarily defensive roles in 61st Army along the northern face of the German-held salient around Oryol. Following the Soviet victory at Kursk the 342nd took part in the operation that eliminated that salient, and then in the further offensives that liberated Bryansk and pushed on towards Smolensk and the Dnieper River. During these tactical-level actions the division distinguished itself sufficiently to be re-designated as the 121st Guards Rifle Division, one of the last Guards divisions to be formed before the postwar period. In November 1944, a new 342nd was formed in the Far East, and saw action against Japanese forces in northern Manchuria, assaulting across the Sungach river during the Soviet invasion of that region.<cr><cr>
translation: 第342步兵师于1941年9月在萨拉托夫州开始组建，作为标准的红军步兵师。该师于同年12月抵达莫斯科西南方向的前线，及时参加了冬季反攻行动。从1942年到1943年初，第342步兵师主要担任防御任务，在第61集团军辖区内德军奥廖尔突出部北侧地区作战。苏联在库尔斯克战役中获胜后，第342步兵师参加了消除该突出部的行动，并随后参与了进一步进攻，解放布良斯克并向斯摩棱斯克和第聂伯河推进。在这期间战术级别的战斗中，该师表现出色，被重新指定为第121近卫步兵师，这是战后时期前最后一个成立的近卫师之一。1944年11月，在远东地区组建了一个新的第342步兵师，并在苏联入侵满洲北部时对抗日军部队，进攻越过松阿察河。<cr>指挥官报告： 该师于1945年8月在日本投降后解散。

text: The 343rd Rifle Division was first formed in late August, 1941, as a standard Red Army rifle division, at Stavropol, in the Caucasus region. Its first major operation was in the liberation of Rostov in December, 1941. Following this, it was nearly caught up in the debacle near Kharkov in May, 1942, but managed to evade the German spearheads during Operation Blue to join the forces defending the Stalingrad region during the summer and fall. Following the German surrender at Stalingrad, on May 4, 1943, it was re-designated as the 97th Guards Rifle Division. Over a year later, a new 343rd Rifle Division was formed, based on the personnel and equipment of a Fortified Region, just after the start of Operation Bagration, the destruction of Army Groups Center. This new division went on to distinguish itself by helping to liberate the Polish city of Bia?ystok, and ended the war in East Prussia, near Knigsberg.<cr><cr>
translation: 第343步兵师于1941年8月底在高加索地区的斯塔夫罗波尔组建。其首次重大行动是在1941年12月解放罗斯托夫的战役中。随后，该师几乎卷入了1942年5月哈尔科夫附近灾难性的战斗，但在“蓝色行动”期间成功避开德军主力部队，并加入保卫斯大林格勒地区的夏季和秋季作战。在斯大林格勒战役结束后，即1943年5月4日，该师被重新指定为第97近卫步兵师。一年多后，在巴格拉季昂行动开始不久，根据一个设防区的人员和装备组建了一个新的第343步兵师。这个新师通过帮助解放波兰城市比亚韦斯托克而脱颖而出，并在战争结束时驻扎在东普鲁士靠近柯尼斯堡的地方。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text:
The 344th Rifle Division was formed in the Baryshsky and Kuzovatovsky Districts of Ulyanovsk Oblast between August and October 1941 in accordance with an 11 August decree of the State Defense Committee. Its basic order of battle was as follows:

1152nd Rifle Regiment
1154th Rifle Regiment
1156th Rifle Regiment
913th Artillery Regiment
In November 1941, in accordance with Direction number 55 of the Stavka and commander of the 26th Army Reserve op/2999 number from 25 November 1941, the division was loaded onto trains at Cheboksary and shipped to Noginsk, and then to Lyubertsy where it was manned and received weapons.

In December the 344th was assigned to the Moscow Defense Zone as part of the last-ditch defenses of the capital. It first went into combat in January 1942, in the 50th Army of Western Front. It remained in this Army until April 1943, when it was moved to the 49th Army in the same Front. It took part in Operation Suvorov under this command, and on 28 August made probing attacks against the German Gruppe Harpe to prevent the transfer of reserves; by three days later the division had suffered 2,000 casualties, about one-third of its strength. On 25 September it was awarded the battle honor Roslavl in recognition of its part in the liberation of that city. On 29 September the division recaptured Mstsislaw. In April 1944 it was again reassigned, this time to the 62nd Rifle Corps of 33rd Army in 2nd Belorussian Front, and fought under these headquarters during Operation Bagration. It was awarded the Order of the Red Banner on 10 July 1944, for its role in the forcing of the Pronya and Dniepr Rivers and the liberation of the cities of Mogilev, Shklov and Bykhov in the first phase of Operation Bagration. In August it went into the reserves of 1st Baltic Front, and from September 1944 until February 1945 it served in the 19th Rifle Corps of 43rd Army in that Front, along the coast of Lithuania. From at least October 1944, it had attached the 18th SU Battalion of SU-76s in addition to its organic battalion of towed anti-tank guns. During the last months of the war the 344th was part of the force containing the German forces trapped in the Courland Pocket, and it ended the war in the 1st Rifle Corps of the 1st Shock Army in the Kurland Group of Leningrad Front. On 5 April 1945, the 1154th Rifle Regiment was separately awarded the Red Banner for its role in the capture of Memel.<cr><cr>
translation:
第344步兵师于1941年8月至10月间根据国家国防委员会1941年8月11日的法令在乌里扬诺夫斯克州巴拉什斯基区和库佐瓦托夫斯基区组建。其基本战斗序列为：

第1152步兵团
第1154步兵团
第1156步兵团
第913炮兵团
1941年11月，根据最高统帅部指令编号55和第26集团军预备队的司令员于1941年11月25日发布的操作命令/编号2999号指示，该师在切博克萨里装车并运往诺吉因斯克，然后运至卢贝茨，在那里补充人员并接收武器。

12月，第344师被调往莫斯科防御区，作为首都最后一道防线的一部分。它于1942年1月首次在西方方面军的第50集团军投入战斗，并一直留在该集团军直到1943年4月，然后被转移到同一方面的第49集团军。在此指挥下参加了苏沃洛夫行动，在8月28日对德国哈佩群发动了试探性攻击，以阻止德军调动预备队；三天后，该师伤亡达2000人，约占其兵力的三分之一。9月25日，因在罗日杰谢解放战中的贡献，该师被授予罗斯拉夫尔战斗荣誉。9月29日，该师重新夺回姆斯季斯拉夫。1944年4月，它再次转隶至第33集团军的第62步兵军，在第二白俄罗斯方面军指挥下参加了巴格拉季昂行动。因在普罗尼亚河和第聂伯河强渡战以及解放莫吉廖夫、什克洛夫和比霍夫等城市的战斗中的贡献，该师于1944年7月10日被授予红旗勋章。8月，它进入波罗的海第一方面军的预备队，并从1944年9月至1945年2月在该方面的第43集团军的第19步兵军服役，在立陶宛海岸沿线作战。自至少10月起，除了自带的一个牵引式反坦克炮营外，它还附带了第18自行火炮营（SU-76）。在战争最后几个月里，第344师是围困库尔兰包围圈内德军部队的兵力之一，并最终作为第一方面军的第一突击集团军中的第一步兵军，在列宁格勒方面军的库尔兰群中结束战斗。1945年4月5日，因在梅梅尔战役中的贡献，第1154步兵团被单独授予红旗勋章。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: The 344th Static Division was formed in September 1942 from elements of the 327th, 333rd and 335th Infantry Divisions. It consisted of the 854th and 855th Fortress Infantry Regiments, 344th Artillery Regiment and various support units. One battalion of the 854th Fortress Regiment was sent to the Eastern Front in October 1943 and in August 1944 was absorbed by the 292nd Infantry Division. In April 1944 the 624th and 625th Cossack Battalions were absorbed by the division. The division was destroyed in Normandy and the remnants retreated to Belgium and were distributed to other units. The division was reformed in in Aachen in November 1944 from the 91st and Castorf Kampfgruppes, various Landwehr Fortress battalions and miscellaneous other units. It's two infantry regiments were now designated the 1057th and 1058th Grenadier Regiments. The division was then transferred east and was captured by the Russians south of Berlin.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第344静态师于1942年9月由第327、333和335步兵师的部分部队组建而成。该师包括第854和855要塞步兵团，第344炮兵团以及各种支援单位。1943年10月，第854要塞团的一个营被派往东线，在1944年8月并入了第292步兵师。1944年4月，第624和625哥萨克营被该师吸收。该师在诺曼底被消灭，残部撤退到比利时，并分配给其他单位。该师于1944年11月在亚琛重组，由第91战斗群、卡斯托夫战斗群以及各种要塞和杂项部队组成。其两个步兵团现更名为第1057和1058掷弹兵团。随后该师被调往东线，并于柏林以南地区被苏联俘获。<cr>资料来源：George F. Nafziger, 《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>@@PH4@@Chris Munson 提供

text: The 346th Rifle Division began forming in late August, 1941, as a standard Red Army rifle division, in the Volga Military District. It was assigned to the 61st Army while both it and its Army continued to form up before moving to the front lines in December to take part in the winter counteroffensive south of Moscow. In September, 1942, it became part of the 5th Tank Army, and joined the offensive that encircled German 6th Army at Stalingrad during Operation Operaton Uranus. During 1943 and early 1944 it continued to serve in the southern part of the front, taking part in the liberation of Crimea, before being transferred to the Baltic States region, serving in Latvia and Lithuania until February, 1945, when it was once again reassigned, this time to be part of the follow-on forces in the conquest of eastern Germany.<cr><cr>
translation: 第346步兵师于1941年8月下旬在伏尔加河军区开始组建，作为标准的红军步兵师。它被分配给第61集团军，在继续编组的同时，该师及其所属集团军于12月移至前线，参加莫斯科以南地区的冬季反攻作战。1942年9月，该师成为第5坦克集团军的一部分，并参加了在天王星行动中包围德国第6集团军的进攻。1943年至1944年初，它继续在南部战线服役，参与克里米亚解放战役。之后被调往波罗的海地区，在拉脱维亚和立陶宛服役，直到1945年2月再次被重新分配，这次是作为征服东德后续部队的一部分。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 347th Rifle Division began forming in mid-September, 1941, as a Red Army rifle division, in the North Caucasus Military District. It was soon assigned to the 58th Army while both it and its Army continued to form up before entering combat in November, as part of the offensive that first liberated Rostov. During the German summer offensive in 1942 the division retreated back into the Caucasus, fighting to defend the routes to the oil fields at Baku, until the German forces began to retreat after their defeat at Stalingrad. During 1943 and early 1944 it continued to serve in the southern part of the front, taking part in the liberation of Crimea, before being transferred to the Baltic States region, serving in Latvia and Lithuania for the duration of the war, compiling a distinguished record of service along the way.<cr><cr>
translation: 第347步兵师于1941年9月中旬在北高加索军区开始组建，作为红军的一个步兵师。很快被分配给第58集团军，在继续编成的过程中进入战斗，参与了首次解放罗斯托夫的攻势。在德国1942年的夏季攻势中，该师撤退到高加索地区，为保卫巴库油田的道路而战，直到德军在斯大林格勒受挫后开始撤退。从1943年到1944年初，它继续在前线南部服役，参与了克里米亚的解放行动，之后被调往波罗的海地区，在拉脱维亚和立陶宛服役直至战争结束，期间建立了卓越的服务记录。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 348th Rifle Division was first formed in August, 1941, as a standard Red Army rifle division, at Kuibyshev. It was assigned to 60th Army shortly after forming and took part in the winter counteroffensive in front of Moscow. Until the end of 1942 it was involved in the dismal and costly battles around the Rzhev Salient, until it was shifted to take part in the equally difficult fighting around the Demyansk Salient. Both of these German positions were evacuated in March, 1943, and, after rebuilding, the division returned to the front to take part in the summer offensive along the Smolensk axis. During Operation Bagration the 348th distinguished itself in the liberation of Bobruysk, and received the name of that city as an honorific. Not long after it was also decorated for its role in the liberation of Bialystok. In 1945 it helped to liberate northern Poland during the Vistula-Oder Offensive, before being reassigned to 3rd Belorussian Front in East Prussia. In the last weeks of the war it formed part of the reserves of 1st Belorussian Front during the Berlin.<cr><cr>
translation: 第348步兵师成立于1941年8月，作为标准的红军步兵师，在库尔斯克成立。该师刚组建不久就被分配给第60集团军，并参加了莫斯科城外的冬季反攻作战。直到1942年底，它一直参与围绕热季突出部进行的惨烈且代价高昂的战斗，之后被转移到德梅耶斯克突出部参加同样艰难的战斗。这两处德国阵地都在1943年3月被撤离，经过重建后，该师返回前线参加了沿斯摩棱斯克方向的夏季攻势。在巴格拉季昂行动期间，第348步兵师因解放鲍里斯波尔而表现出色，并因此获得了该城市的荣誉名称。不久之后，它又因其在解放比亚韦斯托克中的作用而获得嘉奖。1945年，它帮助解放了波兰北部地区，在维斯瓦-奥得河进攻中作战，随后被重新分配到第3白俄罗斯方面军驻东普鲁士。在战争的最后几周里，它是第1白俄罗斯方面军在柏林战役中的预备队之一。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 349th Rifle Division formed in September, 1941, as a standard Red Army rifle division, at Astrakhan. It was assigned to the southern sector of the Soviet-German front, and first saw action in January, 1942, during the winter counteroffensive, but was badly damaged during the German spring offensive that formed the Izium Pocket. The remaining men and equipment of the unit managed to retreat into the Caucasus region in the face of the German summer offensive in such a weakened state that German intelligence wrote the division off as destroyed in October. In fact, the cadre of the division survived, and was transferred to the reserves of Transcaucasus Front in that same month, where it slowly replenished as a low-priority unit. By the end of the year the 349th was assigned to 45th Army along the border with Turkey, and it remained on this quiet front for the duration of the war.<cr><cr>
translation: 第349步兵师于1941年9月在阿斯特拉罕成立，作为标准的红军步兵师。该师被分配到苏联-德国战场的南部战区，并于1942年1月，在冬季反攻中首次参战，但在德军春季攻势形成的伊久姆包围圈中严重受损。剩余人员和装备在面对德军夏季攻势时撤退至高加索地区，当时该师已经虚弱到被德国情报机构认为已于10月被消灭。实际上，该师的骨干幸存下来，并于同月转移到外高加索方面军的预备队，在那里作为低优先级单位缓慢补充人员和装备。到年底时，第349步兵师被分配给第45集团军，驻守在与土耳其接壤的边境地区，并在此平静战线上一直待到战争结束。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 34th Army was formed on 16 July 1941 in the Moscow Military District.<cr>On 18 July the army was assigned to the Moscow line of defense occupying positions west of Maloyaroslavets where it was assigned troops. On 25 July the army became part of the backup for Lieutenant General Bagdanov, which on 30 July was designated as the Reserve Front the army headquarters located in Lbnitsa, Russia (now Estonia). On 6 August the army was reassigned to the Northwestern Front.<cr>The army was tasked to defend the eastern bank of the Lovat River from Kholm to Kulakovo south of the German held city of Staraya Russa. STAVKA Directive 00824 tasked the army to strike the left wing of the German forces defeating and them in the area between Soltsy and Staraya Russa. If successful, the operation could cut off the entire right flank of the Army Group North. According to the order the army was by 15 August to advance more the 25 miles to the line of Snezhka-Chudinovo-Rechnye Kottsy, and by 18 August was to reach the line of Volot-Dolzhino.<cr>By 11 August the army had reached the Polist River along a 24-mile front from Vzglyady to Gojko and launched their offensive. The German X Corps only had small outposts on its flank with the 30th and 129th Infantry Divisions east of Staraya Russa arrayed against the Soviet 11th Army and the 290th Infantry Division on the south side of Staraya Russa guarding the German right flank. After the start of the Soviet Offensive the German forces were moved west of Staraya Russa.<cr>The first echelon, consisting of the 245th, 257th, 262nd Rifle and the 25th Cavalry Divisions, advanced quickly reaching there 18 August goals by 14 August and cutting the railroad between Dno and Staraya Russa.<cr>By the end of September the army's line had stabilized to the north and northeast of Demyansk from Lake Vella to Lychkova and remained in these positions through the end of the year.<cr>At the end of 1942 and in to 1943, the army prepared itself for its role in the Demyansk Offensive.<cr>Prior to the start of the offensive the German successfully withdrew their forces from the Demyansk Pocket and the 34th Army was limited to pursuing rear guard forces. By 28 February the army had arrived at the Lovat River. By the elimination of the pocket the front line had been significantly decreased, and the units of the 34th Army were reassigned to the 11th and 52nd Armies and the headquarters airlifted to the area northeast of Staraya Russa where it took command of some of the forces assigned to the 27th Army.<cr>On 18 March the army, with forces recently reassigned from the 27th attempted to storm Staraya Russa. The army encountered five German divisions along the line of villages Dinner Medvedno, Bryashnaya Gore Sobolev Derevkovo to Porus, the attack was repulsed, restarted on 20 March when it was able to liberate a few small villages moving a little closer to Staraya Russa but unable to liberate the city. The army remained outside Staraya Russa until November 1943 holding the defensive line and attempting to storm the city.<cr>On 20 November 1943 the forces assigned to the army were transferred to 1st Shock Army and the headquarters placed in STAVKA reserve. On 15 January 1944 the headquarters was redesignated 4th Army.<cr><cr>
translation: 第34集团军于1941年7月16日在莫斯科军区成立。<cr>7月18日，该集团军被分配到莫斯科防御线，在马洛亚罗斯拉夫茨以西占领阵地，并接收部队。<cr>7月25日，该集团军成为巴格达诺夫少将副手的一部分，后者于7月30日被指定为预备方面军，其司令部设在俄罗斯的列宾察（现属爱沙尼亚）。8月6日，该集团军被重新分配给西北方面军。<cr>该集团军的任务是防御洛瓦特河东岸从霍尔姆到库拉科沃一线，位于德国占领的城市斯塔罗伊鲁萨以南。最高统帅部指令00824命令该集团军打击德军左翼，在索茨和斯塔罗伊鲁萨之间的地区击败并包围他们。如果成功，此次行动可以切断北方集团军群的整个右翼。<cr>根据命令，到8月15日，该集团军应推进超过25英里到达斯内兹卡-楚丁诺夫-雷恩耶科茨线，并于8月18日前达到沃尔特-多尔金诺一线。<cr>截至8月11日，该集团军已沿长24英里的前线从乌格利亚迪到戈伊科推进至波利斯特河，并发起了进攻。德国第X军只有小规模前哨部队在其侧翼，第30步兵师和第129步兵师位于斯塔罗伊鲁萨以东，面对苏联第11集团军；第290步兵师则在斯塔罗伊鲁萨南侧保护德军右翼。苏军进攻开始后，德国部队被转移到斯塔罗伊鲁萨西侧。<cr>第一梯队由第245、257、262步兵师和第25骑兵师组成，迅速推进，并于8月14日达到预定目标，切断了德尼奥和斯塔罗伊鲁萨之间的铁路。到九月底，该集团军的战线在德米扬斯克以北和东北方向从维拉湖至利奇科娃一带稳定下来，并一直保持这些位置直到年底。<cr>1942年末及1943年初，该集团军为参与德米扬斯克攻势做准备。<cr>在进攻开始前，德国人成功撤出了德米扬斯克包围圈内的部队，第34集团军仅限于追击后卫部队。到2月28日，该集团军已推进至洛瓦特河。通过消除包围圈，前线显著缩短，第34集团军的单位被重新分配给第11和第52集团军，司令部空运至斯大拉亚·鲁萨东北方向区域，并接管了部分原属第27集团军的部队。<cr>3月18日，该集团军（最近从第27集团军调来的部队）试图攻占斯大拉亚·鲁萨。该集团军在迪纳村、梅德韦诺村、布雅什娜亚戈雷村、索博列夫村和德维克沃村至波罗斯一线遭遇了五个德国师的抵抗，进攻被击退，3月20日重新发起攻势时，成功解放了一些小村庄，并稍微靠近斯大拉亚·鲁萨，但未能攻占该城。该集团军一直保持在斯大拉亚·鲁萨外围直到1943年11月，在防御战线上坚守并试图攻占该城。<cr>1943年11月20日，分配给该集团军的部队被转移到第1突击集团军，司令部被置于最高统帅部大本营预备队中。1944年1月15日，司令部重新指定为第4集团军。<cr><cr>

text: The 34th Guards Rifle Division was originally formed on 29 August 1942 from the 7th Airborne Corps in the Moscow Military District. It was assigned to the 28th Army, part of the Southern Front. In April 1943, it was transferred to the 5th Shock Army, which later became part of the 4th Ukrainian Front. After participation in retaking Yenkiyevo, it was awarded the battle honour. In January 1944, it became part of the 31st Guards Rifle Corps of the 46th Army. In November 1944 it was finally transferred to the 4th Guards Army, which it was part of for the rest of the war. During Operation Konrad I, the 34th Guards were pushed back by battlegroups from the 6th Panzer Division and 8th Panzer Division.<cr><cr>
translation: 第34近卫步兵师最初成立于1942年8月29日，由莫斯科军区的第7空降军组建。它被分配到南方方面军下属的第28集团军。1943年4月，该师转隶至第5突击集团军，后者后来成为第4乌克兰方面军的一部分。在夺回叶尼凯沃之后，该师获得了荣誉称号。1944年1月，它成为了第46集团军下属的第31近卫步兵军的一部分。1944年11月，最终被转隶至第4近卫集团军，并一直属于该集团军直到战争结束。在“康拉德行动”第一阶段中，第34近卫步兵师被来自第6装甲师和第8装甲师的战斗群击退。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: In 1941 the 34th Infantry Division joined in the invasion of the Soviet Union as part of Army Group Center and was heavily engaged at Minsk, Smolensk, Gomel, and Vyazma; in the Battle of Moscow; and against the Russian winter offensive of 1941-42. The 34th Infantry fought around Juchnow in the defensive battles on the central sector in 1942, took part in the bitter defensive battles for Kharkov in January 1943, fought at Orel in July and August, and distinguished itself in the third battle for Kharkov in August 1943. The following month, its grenadier regiments each lost a battalion due to heavy casualties. The division performed well in the retreat through the northern Ukraine in the spring of 1944, fighting at Cherkassy and Uman, among others.<cr>After three years of more or less continuous action on the Eastern Front, however, the division was pretty well burned out by summer and was sent back to Germany.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 1941年，第34步兵师作为中央集团军群的一部分参加了入侵苏联的行动，在明斯克、斯摩棱斯克、戈梅利和维亚兹马等地进行了激烈战斗；在莫斯科战役中；以及对抗1941-42年的俄罗斯冬季攻势。第34步兵师于1942年在中央战区的防御作战中围绕尤赫诺夫地区进行战斗，在1943年1月为哈尔科夫展开激烈的防御作战，参加了7月至8月在奥廖尔的战斗，并在1943年8月第三次哈尔科夫战役中表现出色。次月，其掷弹兵团各损失了一个营，因为伤亡惨重。<cr>第34步兵师在1944年春季撤退通过乌克兰北部期间表现良好，在切尔卡瑟和乌曼等地进行了战斗。<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷 1-290步兵师在二战中的行动，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text: The corps was part of 19th Army in STAVKA reserve at the outbreak of hostilities. At that time, it consisted of 129th, 158th and 171st Rifle Divisions. Originally assigned to the defense of Kiev, the corps was transferred to the Smolensk area and assigned to the Western Front. While fighting with the Western Front and it was cut off in the Vyazma Pocket. Survivors of the corps did escape the pocket, but the corps was disbanded in October 1941. The corps was reformed as part of 46th Army in January 1944 and at that time consisted of 195th, 236th and 394th Rifle Divisions. Future Colonel-General and holder of the Order of Lenin Max Reiter was a former commander of this corps, having turned over command just before the outbreak of hostilities. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军在冲突爆发时隶属于最高统帅部预备队中的第19集团军。当时，它由第129、158和171步兵师组成。最初被分配到基辅的防御任务，该军随后被转移到斯摩棱斯克地区，并编入西方面军。在与西方面军作战期间，该军被困于维亚兹马包围圈中。虽然有部分幸存者从包围圈中逃脱出来，但该军还是在1941年10月被解散了。该军于1944年1月作为第46集团军的一部分重建，并由第195、236和394步兵师组成。未来的上将兼列宁勋章获得者马克斯·赖特尔曾是该军的前指挥官，在冲突爆发前不久移交了指挥权。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 《红军伟大卫国战争战斗序列》, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>词条由Stewart King提供

text:
The 34th Tank Division was formed March 1941 in western Kiev Special Military District and assigned to 8th Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
67th Tank Regiment
1st Tank Bn - 51 KV tanks
2nd, 3rd Tank Bns - each 51 mixed T-34, BT tanks
4th Tank Bn - all light tanks
68th Tank Regiment
1st Tank Bn - 50 T-35 tanks
2nd, 3rd Tank Bns - each 51 mixed T-34, BT tanks
4th Tank Bn - all light tanks
34th Motorized Rifle Regiment
34th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
34th Reconnaissance Battalion
34th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
34th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>The 34th Tank Division was formed with cadre from 14th Tank Brigade plus the 5th Heavy Tank Brigade, the prewar 'showpiece' unit which contained all the T-35 heavy tanks built in the 1930s. Consequently, 34th Tank Division was actually overstrength in heavy tanks, with 51 KVs and 50 T-35s on hand, plus 50 T-34s and 280 light tanks, mostly BT types. Unfortunately, the division never trained together as even battalion units, and the non-tank elements of the division were all too short of trucks and tractor to keep up with even the slow heavy tanks.<cr>In the first tank battles on 26 June, the division's tank regiments ran into German antitank defenses and suffered 'serious losses'. On 27 June, parts of the 23rd and 24th Tank Regiments from 12th Tank Division were attached to 34th Tank Division to form a corps tank group - which continued to take heavy losses from German antitank guns and tanks. By Augsut 1941 the division was withdrawn into reserves, where it was disbanded and the surviving personnel used to form new tank brigades.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

第34坦克师于1941年3月在基辅特别军事区西部成立，并被分配给第8机械化军。6月22日，该师包括：
<cr>
第67坦克团
第一坦克营 - 51辆KV坦克
第二、第三坦克营 - 每个营51辆混合T-34和BT坦克
第四坦克营 - 全部轻型坦克
<cr>
第68坦克团
第一坦克营 - 50辆T-35坦克
第二、第三坦克营 - 每个营51辆混合T-34和BT坦克
第四坦克营 - 全部轻型坦克
<cr>
第34摩托化步兵营
第34摩托化榴弹炮营
第34侦察营
第34摩托化浮桥营
第34防空营

该师由第14坦克旅和第5重型坦克旅的骨干部队组建，后者是战前的“示范”单位，拥有所有在20世纪30年代建造的T-35重型坦克。因此，第34坦克师实际上在重型坦克方面超过编制，有51辆KV、50辆T-35和50辆T-34以及280辆轻型坦克（主要是BT型号）。不幸的是，该师从未作为一个整体进行过训练，甚至营级单位也是如此。此外，师中的非坦克部队严重缺乏卡车和拖拉机，无法跟上重型坦克的步伐。

在6月26日的首次坦克战斗中，该师的坦克团遭遇了德国反坦克防御，并遭受“重大损失”。6月27日，第12坦克师的部分单位（包括第23和第24坦克团）被编入第34坦克师以形成一个军级坦克群——继续遭受德国防空炮和坦克的重大损失。到1941年8月，该师撤出战斗并解散，幸存人员用于组建新的坦克旅。

苏联战斗序列第一卷 作者：查尔斯·C·夏普

text: The 350th Rifle Division formed in late August, 1941, as a standard Red Army rifle division, at Atkarsk. It went to the front in November, and served south of Moscow throughout the winter and as late as August, 1942, after which it made a bewildering number of reassignments over the next six months. Badly battered by the German 'backhand blow' near Kharkov in February, 1943, the division was pulled back into reserve for rebuilding for several months, then fought the summer campaign under command of 12th Army. In November the 350th was honored for its role in the liberation of Zhitomir and received that city's name as an honorific. At this time it was in 1st Guards Army of 1st Ukrainian Front, and it would remain in that Front for the duration of the war. On August 18, 1944, the division received an unusual second honorific for helping to liberate the Polish city of Sandomierz. It ended the war in western Berlin with a distinguished record of service.<cr><cr>
translation: 第350步兵师于1941年8月下旬在阿特卡尔斯克组建，作为标准的红军步兵师。该师于11月前往前线，在莫斯科以南度过整个冬季，并一直服役到1942年8月。接下来的6个月里，它经历了大量的重新部署。1943年2月，在哈尔科夫附近的德国“回击”中遭受重创后，该师被撤回到预备队进行重建数月，然后在第12集团军指挥下参加了夏季战役。11月，由于在解放日托米尔中的作用，第350步兵师获得了荣誉，并以该城市的名字作为荣誉称号。此时它隶属于第1近卫集团军（第1乌克兰方面军），并在整个战争期间都留在该方面军内。1944年8月18日，该师因帮助解放波兰城市桑多梅日而获得了一个不同寻常的第二个荣誉称号。该师以卓越的服务记录在柏林西部结束了战争。<cr>指挥官报告：第350步兵师于1944年8月18日在柏林西部结束其服役生涯，拥有卓越的服务记录。<cr>

text:
The 351st Rifle Division began forming in September, 1941, at Stalingrad, in the North Caucasus Military District, and when assigned to the 57th Army, Southwestern Front, took part in the Soviet winter offensive. In May 1942, at the 2nd Battle of Kharkov, the Division was trapped and destroyed in the Izium pocket. 

The Division started forming for a 2nd time in August 1942, at Ordzhonikidze, in the North Caucasus Military District and moved further into the Caucasus to avoid the advancing Germans. The division fought defensive operations and in 1943 pursued the retreating Axis forces out of Caucasus. 

In 1944 the Division fought in the Ukraine with some distinction and ended the war in near Prague, assigned to the 1st Guards Army of the 4th Ukrainian Front.

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov, Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky and the honorific 'SHEPETOVKA'.



Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第351步兵师于1941年9月在斯大林格勒的北高加索军区开始组建，并被分配到西南方面军第57集团军，参加了苏联冬季攻势。1942年5月，在哈尔科夫第二次战役中，该师被困并被消灭在伊久姆包围圈内。

该师于1942年8月在奥尔忠尼启泽重新组建，并进一步进入高加索地区以避开推进的德军。该师进行了防御作战，并在1943年追击撤退的轴心国部队，使其退出高加索地区。

1944年，该师在乌克兰表现出色，并于战争结束时驻扎在接近布拉格的地方，隶属于第4乌克兰方面军的第1近卫集团军。

该师被授予红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫勋章、博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基勋章和“谢佩托夫卡”荣誉称号。

text:
The 352nd Rifle Division began forming in August, 1941, at Bugulma, Tartarstan, Volga Military District, recruiting a significant number from the local population, Tartars. In late November it was rushed by rail to Khimki, Moscow Military District, and assigned to the 20th Army, Western Front, took part in the Moscow Counteroffensive with some success. 

In 1942 it was essentially held in reserve for the exploitation phase of Operation Mars and thus avoided the heavy casualties associated with that operation. In late 1943 and into 1944 it took part in the unsuccessful offensive to liberate the town of Orsha. As part of Operation Bagration, Orsha was finally liberated and the Division was also recognised for its part in the capture of Grodno. 

In late 1944 the Division fought in East Prussia near Knigsberg and ended the war in Czechoslovakia, assigned to the 31st Army of the 3rd Belorussian Front, where it was disbanded.

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov and the honorific 'ORSHA'.



Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第352步兵师于1941年8月在伏尔加河军区塔塔尔斯坦布古尔马开始组建，从当地人口中招募了大量塔塔尔族人。到11月下旬，该师被紧急通过铁路调往莫斯科军区的基姆基，并被分配给西方方面军第20集团军，在莫斯科反攻中取得了一定的成功。

1942年，该师基本上作为预备队参与火星行动的追击阶段，从而避免了与该行动相关的重大伤亡。到1943年底和1944年初，该师参加了解放奥尔沙镇的未成功进攻。在巴格拉季昂行动中，奥尔沙最终被解放，第352步兵师也因其参与格罗德诺的攻占而受到表彰。

1944年末，该师在东普鲁士靠近柯尼斯堡作战，并于战争结束时驻扎在捷克斯洛伐克，隶属于第三白俄罗斯方面军第31集团军，在那里被解散。

该师获得了红旗勋章、苏沃罗夫勋章以及“奥尔沙”荣誉称号。

text:
The 353rd Rifle Division began forming in August, 1941, at Krasnodar, in the North Caucasus Military District. Barely formed it was rushed to the front and in November took part in the operations that drove the Germans out of Rostov for the first time. In July 1942, assigned to the 18th Army, Southern Front, the Division was in a defensive position southeast of Rostov and retreated into the Caucasus where it remained for the remainder of the year. 

With the Axis retreat from the Caucasus the Division was transferred to the Ukraine in 1943, took part in the Donbass Strategic Offensive and fought with distinction in the liberation of Dnepropetrovsk.

In 1944 the Division fought its way across the Ukraine, into Romania and Hungary and ended the war performing garrison duties in the Balkans.

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner and the honorific 'DNEPRODZERZHINSK'.






Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第353步兵师于1941年8月在北高加索军区的克拉斯诺达尔开始组建。刚一组建就被紧急调往前线，在11月参加了第一次将德军驱逐出罗斯托夫的行动。1942年7月，该师被分配给南方方面军第18集团军，并且位于罗斯托夫东南方向的一个防御位置上，随后撤退到高加索地区并一直待在那里直到年底。

随着轴心国从高加索地区的撤退，该师于1943年被转移到乌克兰，参加了顿巴斯战略进攻行动，并在解放第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克的战斗中表现出色。

1944年，该师穿越了整个乌克兰地区，进入罗马尼亚和匈牙利，并最终在巴尔干地区执行守备任务结束战争。

该师被授予红旗勋章，并获得荣誉称号“DNEPRODZERZHINSK”。

text:
The 354th Rifle Division began forming in August, 1941, at Penzensk, Volga Military District, based on a significant number of experienced officers and local party members. In late November it took part in the defence of Moscow, and in the Moscow Counteroffensive with some success. 

In 1942 it was in the Rzhev sector where it suffered heavy casualties in Operation Mars and was withdrawn from the line for rebuilding. In early 1943 the Division was in the Kursk sector, assigned to the 65th Army, Central Front, but was not directly involved in the Battle of Kursk. The Division subsequently fought in Belarus and and Operation Bagration, where it participated in the liberation of Bobruysk, and then chased the Axis forces through Poland and into Germany, most of the time at 75% strength. 

The Division fought in the Berlin, crossed the Oder river and ended the war near the Elbe river , where it was down to only 6000 men. 

A highly recognised Division, it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov, Order of Lenin, the honorific 'KALINKOVICHI' and Stalins thanks for the capture of Stralsund in Germany.



Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第354步兵师于1941年8月在伏尔加河军区的佩钦斯克开始组建，基于大量有经验的军官和当地党员。到11月下旬，该师参与了莫斯科防御战，并在莫斯科反攻中取得了一定的成功。

1942年，第354步兵师驻扎在勒热夫地区，在火星行动中遭受重大伤亡后被撤出前线重建。1943年初，该师部署于库尔斯克地区的中央方面军第65集团军，但并未直接参与库尔斯克战役。

随后，该师参加了白俄罗斯和巴格拉季昂行动，并在解放鲍里斯波尔时发挥了重要作用。之后，它追击轴心国部队穿越波兰进入德国境内，大部分时间保持75% s%的战斗力。

战争结束时，第354步兵师参与了柏林战役，渡过了奥得河，在易北河边结束了战斗，此时该师仅剩6000人。

这是一支备受认可的部队，被授予红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫勋章、列宁勋章，并因其在德国斯瓦松德的占领行动而获得荣誉称号“卡林科维奇”以及斯大林的感谢。

text: The 355th German Infantry Division was formed May 1943 in southern France. It and its sister 356th Infantry Division were one of two code word 'Gisela' divisions formed to protect southern France after the allied victory in North Africa in May 1943. It consisted of the 866th, 867th and 868th Grenadier Regiments, 355th Artillery Regiment and various support troops. The division was disbanded in February 1944 in southern Russia with the division remnants, now reduced to a the 355th Divisional Group, becoming part of the 161st Infantry Division.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第355德国步兵师于1943年5月在法国南部组建。它和它的姊妹部队第356步兵师是两个代号为“吉塞拉”的师之一，目的是保护战后北非盟军胜利后的法国南部地区。该师由第866、867和868掷弹兵团，第355炮兵团以及各种支援部队组成。该师于1944年2月在南俄解散，其残部现被缩减为第355师团，并成为第161步兵师的一部分。<cr>参考文献：乔治·F·纳夫齐格，《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>条目由克里斯·芒森提供

text:
The 355th Rifle Division began forming in August, 1941, in the Urals Military District. In December it was assigned to the 39th Army, Kalinin Front, and first went into combat in January 1942 helping to carve out the Rzhev salient. Switched to the 22nd Army, the Division held a precarious position near Belyi and in July 1942 was surrounded and destroyed in Operation Sedlitz. Although some troops slipped through Axis lines, the Division suffered massive losses and was officially disbanded on the 21st of July. 

It was not until December 1944 that the Division was raised for a second time and assigned to the 2nd Red Banner Army, Far Eastern Front, where it took part in the Soviet invasion of Manchuria. 




Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第355步兵师开始于1941年8月在乌拉尔军区组建。12月，该师被分配到第39集团军、加里宁方面军，并于1942年1月首次参战，在帮助形成热季突出部的过程中发挥了作用。随后，该师转隶至第22集团军，在贝利附近占据了一个岌岌可危的位置，并在1942年7月的塞德尔里茨行动中被包围并消灭。尽管一些部队成功突破了轴心国防线，但该师遭受了重大损失，并于7月21日正式解散。

直到1944年12月，该师才第二次组建，并分配到远东方面军第2红旗集团军，在苏联入侵满洲的行动中发挥了作用。 

约翰·汤姆林森提供

text:
The 356th Rifle Division began forming in August, 1941, at Kuibyshev, in the Volga Military District, and in January 1942 was assigned to the 61st Army, Western Front. It took part in the defence of Moscow, and in the Moscow Counteroffensive where it was found to be best suited to defensive operations along the Oka river. It remained in this area for the next 18 months.

In 1943 the Division took part in the Gomel-Rechitsa Offensive and later on was recognised for its participation in the liberation of Kalinkovichi. The Division was subsequently withdrawn into Reserve for rebuilding, prior to participation in Operation Bagration, where it participated in the liberation of Bobruysk, and later on, Riga. 

The Division was assigned to the reserves of the 61st Army, 1st Belorussian Front for the Battle of Berlin, crossed the Oder river and ended the war near Havelberg on the Elbe river. It was disbanded in Germany later that year. 

The Division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner (Riga), Order of Suvorov (Bobruisk) and the honorific 'KALINKOVICHI'. 



Courtesy of John Tomlinson
translation:
第356步兵师于1941年8月在伏尔加河军区的库尔斯克开始组建，并于1942年1月被分配给西方方面军第61集团军。该师参加了莫斯科防御战，以及莫斯科反攻，在此期间发现其最适合沿奥卡河进行防御作战。接下来的18个月里，该师一直驻扎在此区域。

1943年，该师参与了戈梅利-列奇察进攻战役，并因在解放卡林科维奇中的表现而受到表彰。随后，该师被撤至预备队重建，为参加巴格拉季昂行动做准备，在此期间参加了波布鲁斯克的解放，并最终参与了解放里加。

该师被分配给第61集团军、第一白俄罗斯方面军的预备队，参加了柏林战役，渡过了奥得河，并在易北河边哈弗尔贝格附近结束了战争。同年晚些时候，该师在德国解散。

该师获得了红旗勋章（里加）、苏沃洛夫勋章（波布鲁斯克）和“卡林科维奇”荣誉称号。

text: The 357th Infantry Division was formed in November 1943 as part of the 21st Wave around the remains of the disbanded 327th Division and several other units. It contained the 944th, 945th and 946th Grenadier Regiments, 357th Artillery Regiment and various support units. In August 1944 the division was rebuilt using the Breslau Infantry Division. In February 1945 the division absorbed three Kampfgruppen, the 7/XVIII, 14/XVII and 16/XVII. The division was captured by the Russians.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第357步兵师于1943年11月组建，作为第21波的一部分，由解散的第327步兵师和其他一些单位重组而成。该师包括第944掷弹兵团、第945掷弹兵团、第946掷弹兵团、第357炮兵团以及各种支援部队。1944年8月，该师使用布雷斯劳步兵师进行了重建。1945年2月，该师吸收了三个战斗群：第7/18、第14/17和第16/17。该师被俄罗斯人俘获。<cr>参考文献：George F. Nafziger, 《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>条目由Chris Munson提供

text: The 35th Guards Rifle Corps was formed in accordance with a Stavka directive of 18 April 1943 by the conversion of the 7th Rifle Corps (Second formation) of the 64th Army (which itself soon became the 7th Guards Army) into a Guards unit in recognition of its actions in the Battle of Stalingrad. Corps troops included the 52nd Separate Communications and 8th Separate Sapper Battalions, which became the 138th and 105th Separate Guards, respectively, on 4 May. Its 12th, 13th, and 14th Guards, and 92nd, 96th, and 149th Rifle Brigades were simultaneously combined to form the 92nd, 93rd, and 94th Guards Rifle Divisions, with each division being formed from two brigades. The commander of the 7th Rifle Corps, Lieutenant General Sergey Goryachev, continued in command of the 35th Guards.<cr>The process of forming the new divisions began on 24 April, with the 92nd Guards formed from the 12th Guards and 149th Rifle Brigades, the 93rd Guards from the 13th Guards and 92nd Rifle Brigades, and the 94th Guards from the 14th Guards and 96th Rifle Brigades, and was completed by 30 April. At this time, due to the arrival of replacements, the three divisions of the corps had between roughly 8,400 and 9,300 men each, and were at approximately 77 to 87 percent of their authorized strength.<cr>With the 7th Guards Army, the corps served with the Voronezh Front and then the Steppe Front from July 1943, fighting in the Battle of Kursk and the Belgorod-Kharkov Offensive. Developing the offensive, the corps reached the Dnieper in late September, assault-crossing the river and capturing a bridgehead on the right bank. Subsequently, with the 7th Guards and then the 27th Armies of the 2nd and 3rd Ukrainian Fronts, the corps fought in the Kirovograd, Uman-Botosani, Jassy-Kishinev, Debrecen, Budapest, Vienna, and Prague Offensives, capturing Kirovograd, Tulchyn, Ploiesti, Cluj, Szolnok, Eger, Zalaegerszeg, and Bratislava. For its actions in the Uman-Boto?ani Offensive the corps received the Prut honorific on 24 April 1944.<cr><cr>
translation: 第35近卫步兵军是在1943年4月18日最高统帅部指示下组建的，通过将第64集团军中的第7步兵军（第二次编成）改编为荣誉单位来表彰其在斯大林格勒战役中的表现。该军部队包括独立通信营第52和独立工兵营第8，在1943年5月4日分别改编为第138近卫独立通信营和第105近卫独立工兵营。其第12、13、14近卫步兵旅和第92、96、149步兵旅同时合并，组建了第92、93、94近卫步兵师，每个师由两个旅编成。第7步兵军指挥官谢尔盖·戈利亚切夫中将继续担任第35近卫步兵军的指挥官。<cr><cr>组建新师的过程于4月24日开始，第92近卫师由第12近卫旅和第149步兵旅编成，第93近卫师由第13近卫旅和第92步兵旅编成，第94近卫师由第14近卫旅和第96步兵旅编成。到4月30日完成组建。<cr>此时，由于补充人员的到来，该军的三个师每师人数在8,400至9,300人之间，约为编制员额的77%至87%。在第7近卫集团军的指挥下，该军从1943年7月起隶属于沃罗涅日方面军，随后转隶草原方面军，在库尔斯克会战和别尔哥罗德-哈尔科夫进攻中作战。发展攻势后，该军于9月下旬抵达第聂伯河，并强渡河流，占领了右岸的桥头堡。之后，该军在第2乌克兰方面军（包括第7近卫集团军）和第3乌克兰方面军（包括第27集团军）的指挥下，在基洛夫格勒、乌曼-波托什卡尼、雅西-奇索尔纳、德布勒森、布达佩斯、维也纳和布拉格进攻中作战，占领了基洛夫格勒、图尔钦、普洛耶什蒂、克卢日、索林、埃格尔、扎拉埃哲塞格和布拉迪斯拉发。由于在乌曼-波托什卡尼进攻中的表现，该军于1944年4月24日获得普鲁特荣誉称号。<cr><cr>

text:
On July 30, 1942, in connection with a serious complication of the situation on the Soviet-German front, the 8th Airborne Corps was transformed into the 35th Guards Rifle Division, at the same time on the basis of the 17th Airborne Brigade was formed the 100th Guards Rifle Regiment, 18th and 19th Brigades became the 101st and 102nd Guards regiments respectively. In August, the division was assigned to the Stalingrad Front and fought on the approaches to Stalingrad, and then in the city as part of 62nd Army (later 8th Guards Army). Guards divisions were one of the first defenders of the Stalingrad grain elevator.

On September 27, 1942, the division was withdrawn from the front line and sent to re-form in the Saratov region.

In January - February 1943, the division participated in the attack on the Donbass area. It freed Starobelsk. On February 11, 1943 released the station Lozova, Novomoskovsk, Sinelnikovo. During these battles was awarded the Order of the Red Banner, which was awarded the division on June 23, 1943 by the commander of the 6th Army, Lieutenant General Ivan Shlemin. Order of the Supreme Commander was awarded the honorary name 'Lozovskaya.'

After retrofitting again took part in the fighting. It freed Barvenkovo/Barvinkove. In September 1943, the division crossed the Dnieper and was fighting on the beachhead, involved in the Nikopol operation.

It fought at Stalingrad, in the Don Basin, at Pavlograd, Kharkiv, Kryvyi Rih, Nikopol, Odessa, the Magnuszew Bridgehead, Kustrin, and in the Battle of Berlin. It was with 4th Guards Rifle Corps of the 8th Guards Army of the 1st Belorussian Front May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
1942年7月30日，由于苏德战场形势严重恶化，第8空降军改编为第35近卫步兵师。同时，以第17空降旅为基础组建了第100近卫步兵团；第18和第19旅分别改编为第101和第102近卫团。

8月，该师被调往斯大林格勒方面军，在接近斯大林格勒的地区作战，并随后作为第62集团军（后改称第8近卫集团军）的一部分在城内战斗。近卫步兵师是保卫斯大林格勒粮仓的第一批部队之一。

1942年9月27日，该师从一线撤出并被调往萨拉托夫地区重组。

1943年1月至2月期间，该师参加了对顿巴斯地区的进攻行动。解放了斯塔罗别尔斯克，并于1943年2月11日解放了洛佐瓦、诺沃莫斯科夫斯克和辛涅利尼科沃。在这些战斗中，该师获得了红旗勋章，由第6集团军司令伊万·谢尔明上将授予，日期为1943年6月23日。

之后再次重组后参加了作战行动，解放了巴文科沃/巴文科夫。1943年9月，该师渡过第聂伯河，在桥头堡地区作战，并参与了尼古拉耶夫卡战役。

该师在斯大林格勒、顿河流域、帕夫洛格勒、哈尔科夫、克里维伊·里赫、尼古拉耶夫卡、敖德萨、马格努舍夫桥头堡、库斯特林以及柏林之战中作战。1945年5月，该师隶属于第8近卫集团军的第4近卫步兵军，属于第一白俄罗斯方面军。<cr> <cr>

text: The 35th Infantry Division was sent to East Prussia in May 1941 and invaded the Soviet Union the following month as part of Army Group Center, fighting at Smolensk and Vyazma, among other battles. It was with General Erich Hoepner's 4th Panzer Group during the final drive on Moscow. When the mid-October thaw came, the men of the 35th trudged eastward through knee-deep mud. Their infantry companies were down to a strength of 30 men; nevertheless they crossed the Ruza River (October 20) and took Volokolanisk (October 27) along with 1,800 prisoners. Their supplies and ammunition were exhausted by this time so the division went over to the defensive. Stalled before the Russian capital in December, the 35th suffered heavy casualties once more against the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42, losing more than 2,500 men;1,000 of them due to severe frostbite. Although in reality a burned-out force by then, the division remained in the line in the Gshatsk sector until early 1943.<cr>In the early spring of 1943, it took part in the Rzhev withdrawal and was heavily engaged in the defensive fighting on the central sector that summer and the following winter. In November 1943, it was rebuilt was a Type 1944 division and now consisted of the 34th Fusilier, 109th Grenadier and 111th Grenadier Regiments, all with two battalions; the 35th Fusilier (reconnaissance) Battalion; the 35th Artillery Regiment; and assorted divisional troops. It fought against the massive Soviet summer offensive of 1944 and suffered such heavy casualties in the Battle of Bobruisk in July 1944 that it had to be taken out of the line for the first time in three years. Sent to Poland, it absorbed the 1034th and 1042nd March Battalions and was hurriedly thrown back into the line. It fought at Brest, Modlin, and in the retreat to the Vistula. After the fall of Danzig, the 35th Infantry Division was largely destroyed during the retreat to the Hela peninsula. Here the remnants of the division surrendered to the Russians at the end of the war.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第35步兵师于1941年5月被派往东普鲁士，并在次月作为中央集团军群的一部分入侵苏联，参加了斯摩棱斯克和维亚兹马等战役。该师随同埃里希·霍平将军的第4装甲集群，在最后进攻莫斯科的过程中作战。当10月中旬解冻来临时，第35步兵师的士兵们在齐膝深的泥泞中艰难向东推进。他们的步兵连只剩下30人；尽管如此，他们还是于10月20日渡过了鲁扎河，并在10月27日占领了沃洛科拉姆斯克，俘虏了1,800名苏联士兵。此时该师的补给和弹药已经耗尽，因此转为防御态势。1941年12月，在莫斯科城下受阻时，第35步兵师再次遭受重创，损失超过2,500人；其中1,000人因严重冻伤而死亡。尽管实际上该师已成强弩之末，但直到1943年初，它仍然在格扎茨克地区坚守阵地。<cr><cr>1943年早春，该师参与了日兹赫夫的撤退行动，并在当年夏季和接下来的冬季，在中央战线进行了激烈的防御作战。1943年11月，它重建为一种1944型步兵师，现在由第34掷弹兵团、第109掷弹兵团和第111掷弹兵团组成，每个团都有两个营；第35侦察营（侦察）；第35炮兵团；以及各种师属部队。它参加了苏联在1944年夏季的大规模攻势，并在1944年7月的日博罗西克战役中伤亡惨重，不得不首次撤出前线长达三年之久。该师被派往波兰，吸收了第1034团和第1042团，并迅速重新投入战斗。它参加了布列斯特、莫德林的战斗以及向维斯瓦河的撤退。在但泽沦陷后，第35步兵师在撤退至赫拉半岛的过程中被大量消灭。战败后，该师残部于战争结束时向苏联投降。<cr>德国二战1-290步兵师战斗序列<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham Jr. 著

text: The 35th Romanian Infantry Division was attached to the German LIV Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. It was the only Romanian reserve division to see combat. It was broken up early in the war to provide replacements for other units.<cr><cr>John Ellis, World War II A Statistal Survey<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第35罗马尼亚步兵师在巴巴罗萨行动开始时隶属于德国第48军。它是唯一一个参战的罗马尼亚预备师。战争初期就被拆散，为其他部队提供补充兵力。<cr>资料来源：John Ellis, 《第二次世界大战统计调查》<cr>词条由Chris Munson提供

text: The corps was in 9th Army at the outbreak of hostilities, and consisted of 95th and 176th Rifle Divisions. It was reorganized in June 1943 as part of Voronezh Front. It served as Front reserve at the Battle of Kursk , and then was assigned to 3rd Army. In June 1944, it was one of the principal attack corps during the Belorussian Offensive. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军在战争爆发时隶属于第9集团军，由第95步兵师和第176步兵师组成。它于1943年6月作为沃罗涅日方面军的一部分进行了重组，并在库尔斯克战役中担任方面军预备队，之后被分配给第3集团军。1944年6月，在白俄罗斯进攻期间，它是主要攻击军之一。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert，《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，Presidio Press，1985 年<cr>条目由Stewart King 提供

text:
The 35th Tank Division was formed March-April 1941 at Novograd-Volynsk in Kiev Special Military District, assigned to 9th Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
69th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd Tank Bns - each 30 to 40 T-26 tanks
70th Tank Regiment
1 Tank Bn with 30 to 40 T-26 tanks
35th Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns, no trucks, no 76mm regimental battery
35th Howitzer Regiment
1 light bn with 6 122mm howitzers
1 battery of 4 152mm howitzers
35th Reconnaissance Battalion
no motorcycles, 1 light tank co
35th Antiaircraft Battalion
1 battery of 4 37mm guns only<cr><cr>By 22 June 1941, 35th Tank Division had received most of its required enlisted personnel, but only 60% of the required NCOs and less than 1/3 of the officers. Specifically, the division had only 3 tank battalion, 13 tank company, and 6 tank platoon commanders on hand. Consequently, although it had 141 T-26 and 1 OT-26 tanks on hand in 3 battalions, most of the junior, first hand supervisors were missing. The rifle regiment was completely on foot, and there were only 7 tractors in the entire division - the howitzer regiment was virtually immobile.<cr>Nevertheless, because it was in reserve when the war started, the division managed to survive the initial tank battles west of Kiev. By 25 August the division had only 2200 men, 12 artillery pieces (of all sizes) and 0 tanks, and in early September the division was dissolved and the surviving personnel added to newly-formed tank brigades.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第35坦克师于1941年3月至4月在基辅特别军区的诺夫格罗德-沃伦斯基组建，并隶属于第9机械化军。6月22日包括：

第69坦克团

第1、第2坦克营——每营有30至40辆T-26坦克
第70坦克团
第1坦克营，配备30至40辆T-26坦克
第35步兵团
第1、第2、第3营，无卡车，无76毫米团炮兵连
第35榴弹炮团
轻型营，装备6门122毫米榴弹炮
炮兵连，配备4门152毫米榴弹炮
第35侦察营
无摩托车，1个轻型坦克连
第35防空营
炮兵连，仅配备4门37毫米高射炮

截至1941年6月22日，第35坦克师已收到大部分所需士兵，但只获得约60%的士官和不到三分之一的军官。具体而言，该师只有3个坦克营、13个坦克连和6个坦克排指挥官在岗。因此，尽管有141辆T-26和1辆OT-26坦克分布在3个营中，大部分初级直接监督人员却缺失了。步兵团完全徒步行军，整个师只有7台拖拉机——榴弹炮团几乎无法移动。

然而，由于战争开始时该师处于预备状态，它在基辅以西的初期坦克战斗中幸存下来。到8月25日，该师仅有2200人、12门各种口径火炮和零辆坦克；9月初，该师被解散，剩余人员加入新组建的坦克旅。

苏联战斗序列第一卷 作者：查尔斯·C·夏普

text: The 361st Infantry Division was formed in November 1943 in Denmark as part of the 21st Wave. It contained the 951st, 952nd and 953rd Grenadier Regiments, 361st Divisional Fusilier Battalion, 361st Artillery Regiment and various support units. The division staff and many of its soldiers came from the defunct 86th Infantry Division which had been destroyed on the Eastern Front.<cr>The division was sent to the Eastern Front in March 1944 and in April participated in the Battle of Tarnopol. As part of Army Group Center during the Soviet summer offensive Operation Bagration the division was severely mauled. The division was encircled along with the rest of the XIII Army Corps at Brody in White Russia. Some elements of the division broke out but most of the division along with its commander were captured. After retreating to Poland the remnants were withdrawn to Germany and the division rebuilt which was completed by the Fall of 1944. Newly designated the 361st Volksgrenadier Division it fought at Arnhem before being transferred to the Saar sector. After fighting in eastern France it was sent to the Vosges Mountains. It was absorbed by the 559th Volksgrenadier Division in March 1945.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, German Order of Battle Volume II: 291st-999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions, and Special Divisions in WWII<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第361步兵师于1943年11月在丹麦组建，属于第21波。该师包括第951掷弹兵团、第952掷弹兵团和第953掷弹兵团，第361师属猎兵营，第361炮兵团以及各种支援单位。<cr><cr>该师的指挥部及许多士兵来自在东线被消灭的第86步兵师。<cr>该师于1944年3月被派往东线，在4月参加了塔尔诺波利战役。作为中央集团军群的一部分，该师在苏联夏季攻势巴格拉季昂行动中遭受重创。<cr><cr>该师与第13军的其余部队一起在白俄罗斯布罗迪地区被包围。该师的部分单位突围成功，但大部分单位及其指挥官都被俘虏。<cr><cr>撤退到波兰后，剩余部分被调往德国重建，并于1944年秋季完成重建工作。<cr>新编为第361国民掷弹兵师的该师参加了阿纳姆战役，并随后被转移到萨尔地区。在东部法国作战之后，该师又被派往孚日山脉。<cr><cr>该师于1945年3月并入了第559国民掷弹兵师。<cr><cr><cr><cr>乔治·F·纳夫齐格，《二战德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>萨缪尔·W·米查姆，《二战德国战斗序列第二卷：第291至第999步兵师、命名步兵师及其他特别编成的师》<cr><cr>克里斯·芒森提供条目

text:
The 361st Rifle Division began forming on August 1, 1941 in the Urals Military District at Ufa. Its basic order of battle was as follows:

1200th Rifle Regiment
1202nd Rifle Regiment
1204th Rifle Regiment
925th Artillery Regiment
Col. Denis Vasilevich Mikhailov was assigned to command of the division on the day it began forming, and he continued in command through the existence of this formation. While the division was not known officially as a Bashkiri national division, given that it was formed in the Bashkir ASSR in the southern Urals, it probably had a large percentage of Bashkirs in its ranks, which numbered about 11,500 by the end of September.

In November the division was assigned to the 39th Army, which was forming in the Arkhangelsk Military District. In the dying days of the German offensive on Moscow, the units of this Army were assigned to build defenses along the line of the Sheksna River. They later consolidated in the Torzhok area, and in late December the 39th was assigned to Kalinin Front.[4] Beginning on January 8, 1942, this Army took part in the Sychevka-Vyasma Offensive Operation, which was planned 'to encircle, and then capture or destroy the enemy's entire Mozhaisk - Gzhatsk - Vyasma grouping, that is, what later became known as the Rzhev salient. The 361st was one of the spearheads of this thrust behind the German lines, reaching a point almost 50km due south of Rzhev by January 15; only the Soviet cavalry units made a deeper advance during this period. The division was recognized for its achievements in this counteroffensive on March 17th when it became the 21st Guards Rifle Division.<cr><cr>It was not until November 22, 1944, that a new 361st was formed, this time in the 15th Army of the Far Eastern Front; it was not officially 'on the books' until December. It was under the command of Lt. Col. Arakel Karapetovich Oganezov until September 3, 1945. Its basic order of battle was as follows:

345th Rifle Regiment
355th Rifle Regiment
394th Rifle Regiment<cr><cr>

text: The 363rd Infantry Division was formed in December 1943 in Poland as part of the 32nd Wave. It contained the 957th, 958th and 959th Grenadier Regiments, 363rd Divisional Fusilier Battalion, 363rd Artillery Regiment and various support units. Elements of the division came from the 147th Reserve Division, the defunct 339th Infantry Division and other units. When its training in Poland was complete it was sent to the Jutland peninsula in Denmark in March and April of 1944. In June it was sent to Rouen in northern France. The next month the division was in Normandy opposing the Allied landings. The division was destroyed in the Falaise Pocket in August 1944 with only 2,500 men escaping.<cr>The survivors returned to Germany in September 1944 and merged with the 566th Volksgrenadier Division to form the 363rd Volksgrenadier Division. Before the month was over though the division was back in combat against the Allies during Operation Market Garden at Nijmegen and Arnhem in Holland. In late November 1944 the division was shifted to the Roer River area. The division surrendered in the Ruhr pocket to the Americans in April 1945.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, German Order of Battle Volume II: 291st-999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions, and Special Divisions in WWII<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation:
第363步兵师于1943年12月在波兰组建，属于第三十二波。该师包括第957、958和959掷弹兵团，第363师属火枪营，第363炮兵团以及各种支援单位。部分人员来自第147预备师、解散的第339步兵师和其他部队。<cr><cr>完成在波兰的训练后，该师于1944年3月和4月被派往丹麦日德兰半岛。同年6月，该师被调至法国北部鲁昂。下个月，该师在诺曼底对抗盟军登陆行动。1944年8月，在法莱斯包围圈中被消灭，只有2500人逃脱。<cr>幸存者于1944年9月返回德国，并与第566国民掷弹兵师合并重组为第363国民掷弹兵师。然而在当月结束前，该师又重新投入对抗盟军的战斗，在市场花园行动中参与了尼美根和阿纳姆战役。<cr>1944年11月底，该师被调往鲁尔河地区。1945年4月，该师向美军在鲁尔包围圈投降。

text:
The 363rd Rifle Division began forming in August 1941 in the Urals Military District in the Sverdlovsk Oblast. Its basic order of battle was as follows:

1205th Rifle Regiment
1207th Rifle Regiment
1209th Rifle Regiment
926th Artillery Regiment
Col. Karp Sviridov was not assigned to command of the division until September 25, but he would continue in command through the existence of this formation. It spent about three months in the Urals forming and training.

In December the division was assigned to the 30th Army, in Kalinin Front. Beginning on January 8, 1942, this Army took part in the Sychevka-Vyasma Offensive Operation, which was planned 'to encircle, and then capture or destroy the enemy's entire Mozhaisk - Gzhatsk - Vyasma grouping', that is, what later became known as the Rzhev salient. 30th Army operated mostly north and northwest of Rzhev itself, and the 363rd advanced over 30km in early January, driving the German forces out of several villages and small towns in the area. The division was recognized for its achievements in this counteroffensive on March 17th when it became the 22nd Guards Rifle Division, the same day that the 361st became the 21st Guards.<cr><cr>It was not until November 25, 1944, that a new 363rd was formed, this time in the 35th Army of the Far Eastern Front. It was under the command of Col. Savva Dmitrievich Pechenenko until at least September 3, 1945.<cr><cr> 
The division spent its entire career in 35th Army. It is shown in the order of battle for January 1, is not present on February 1, but reappears as of March 1, remaining there until August. When the Soviet invasion of Manchuria began that month, 35th Army was in the 1st Far Eastern Front, attacking the Hutou Fortified Region. The 363rd played little role in attacking the fortifications, and it mostly served as a mobile pursuit force aided by its battalion of SU-76s.<cr><cr>
translation:
第363步兵师开始于1941年8月在乌拉尔军区的斯维尔德洛夫斯克州组建。其基本战斗序列为：

第1205步兵团
第1207步兵团
第1209步兵团
第926炮兵团
卡普·斯维里多夫上校直到9月25日才被任命为该师的指挥官，但他将继续担任指挥直至该部队解散。这支部队在乌拉尔地区大约花费了三个月的时间组建和训练。

1941年12月，该师被分配到加里宁方面军的第30集团军。从1942年1月8日开始，该集团军参与了斯切夫卡-维亚兹马进攻战役，计划“包围并摧毁敌人整个莫扎伊斯克-热季茨克-维亚兹马集群”，即后来被称为列宁格勒突出部的地区。第30集团军主要在列宁格勒突出部以北和西北方向行动，第363师于1月初推进了超过30公里的距离，将德军从该地区的几个村庄和小镇驱逐出去。由于在这次反攻中的出色表现，该师于1942年3月17日被授予近卫称号，成为第22近卫步兵师，同一天第361师也成为了第21近卫步兵师。<cr>直到1944年11月25日，一个新的第363师才在远东方面军的第35集团军中组建。至少到1945年9月3日为止，该师一直由萨瓦·德米特里耶维奇·佩切内尼科夫上校指挥。<cr>该师整个服役期间都在第35集团军。它出现在1月1日的战斗序列中，2月1日未出现，但于3月1日重新出现，并一直持续到8月。当苏联入侵满洲时，第35集团军属于远东第一方面军，攻击胡头要塞区。第363师在进攻工事方面作用不大，主要作为机动追击部队发挥作用，得益于其配备的SU-76营。<cr>

text: The 365th Rifle Division began forming on September 1, 1941, as a standard Red Army rifle division, in the Sverdlovsk Oblast. After forming, it was assigned to the 30th Army of Western Front, served briefly in the defense of Moscow, and played a role in the liberation of Klin, and later in the near-encirclement of the German 9th Army around Rzhev in the winter counteroffensive of 1941-42. In late January, 1942, it was transferred to the 29th Army of Kalinin Front, which was very soon after encircled by German forces near Sychevka, and on March 18 the division was disbanded due to very heavy losses. In November, 1944, a new 365th Rifle Division was formed in the Far Eastern Front, based on the 29th Rifle Brigade, and saw action in the Soviet invasion of Manchuria in August, 1945, being awarded the Order of the Red Banner for its services.<cr><cr>
translation: 第365步兵师于1941年9月1日在斯维尔德洛夫斯克州开始组建，作为标准的红军步兵师。组建完成后，该师被分配到西方面军第30集团军，在莫斯科防御战中短暂服役，并参与了解放克林和在1941-42年冬季反攻中几乎包围了德国第9集团军于热季夫地区的行动。1942年1月晚些时候，该师被调至加里宁方面军第29集团军，在不久之后的斯切夫卡地区被德军包围，并在1942年3月18日因严重损失而解散。1944年11月，一个新的第365步兵师在远东方面军组建，基于第29步兵旅，并参加了1945年8月苏联入侵满洲的行动，因其贡献被授予红旗勋章。<cr><cr>

text: The 367th Infantry Division was formed in November 1943 in the Balkans as part of the 21st Wave. It contained the 974th, 975th and 976th Grenadier Regiments, 367th Divisional Fusilier Battalion, 367th Artillery Regiment and various support units. Elements of the division came from the disbanded 330th Infantry Division, the 71st and 297th Infantry Divisions and other units. The division was sent to Croatia in December 1943. In the spring of 1944 it was sent to the Eastern Front. In March 1944 as part of the II SS Panzer Corps it helped rescue the 1st Panzer Army which was surrounded in Galicia. The division surrendered to the Russians at Knigsberg in April 1945.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, German Order of Battle Volume II: 291st-999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions, and Special Divisions in WWII<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第367步兵师于1943年11月在巴尔干地区组建，属于第二十一波。该师包括第974团、第975团和第976掷弹兵团，第367师属猎兵营，第367炮兵团以及各种支援单位。部分部队来自解散的第330步兵师、第71步兵师和第297步兵师以及其他单位。该师于1943年12月被派往克罗地亚，在1944年春天又被调至东线战场。1944年3月，作为第二装甲军的一部分，它帮助救援了在加利西亚被包围的第一装甲集团军。<cr>该师于1945年4月向苏联军队投降。<cr>@PH0@<cr>@PH1@乔治·F·纳夫齐格，《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>@PH2@塞缪尔·W·米查姆，《二战中的德国战斗序列第二卷：第291至第999师、命名步兵师及其他特别编组部队》<cr>@PH3@<cr>@PH4@克里斯·芒森提供

text:
The division began forming on August 29, 1941 in the Urals Military District in the Chelyabinsk Oblast.<cr><cr>Col. Ivan Mikhailovich Puzikov was assigned to command of the division on the day it began forming, and he would remain in command until February 24, 1942. In late November it was assigned briefly to the 28th Army in the Reserve of the Supreme High Command, but was then sent to the front in Karelia, where it was assigned to the Maselskaya Operational Group. In December the division was reported as being made up of men mostly 35 to 41 years old. Colonel Puzikov was replaced by Col. Nikolai Ivanovich Afonskii on February 25, who was in turn replaced by Lt. Col. Nikolai Ivanovich Shpilev on April 22. Meanwhile, the 32nd Army was reformed in March, in part from the Maselskaya Group, and the division was assigned to that Army in May. Col. Fedor Ivanovich Korobko took command on June 24, but less than a month later Colonel Puzikov returned to his previous position.<cr><cr>The 367th remained in 32nd Army until February, 1944. During this entire period this Army was stationed in the Segezhsky District of the Karelo-Finnish SSR, facing the Finnish II Army Corps across the static front. Colonel Puzikov was replaced on November 1, 1942 by Col. Nikolai Antonovich Chernukha, who would be promoted to Major General on May 18, 1943, and would remain in command until June 12, 1944.

In February the division was moved north to join 26th Army in the Ukhta region. It was briefly assigned to 31st Rifle Corps before reverting to being a separate division within the Army. In these positions it faced elements of the German XVIII Mountain Corps over the next several months, while to the south Finland was being driven out of the war in the Vyborg - Petrozavodsk Offensive. Maj. Gen. Yan Petrovich Sinkevich took over the divisional command on June 13, but was in turn replaced by Col. Aleksandr Alexeevich Startzev on August 10; this officer would remain in command for the duration of the war.

At the beginning of September the 367th was assigned to 132nd Rifle Corps, still in 26th Army. On September 4/5 a Soviet-Finnish cease-fire went into effect, and on the 6th the German forces in Finland began Operation Birke, with the goal of a withdrawal into Norway, although the Germans were secretly determined to hold the Pechenga District for the sake of the nickel mines there. XVIII Mountain Corps withdrew by stages, and 26th Army followed up as far as the 1940 Soviet-Finnish border.

In October the division was reassigned to 31st Rifle Corps in the newly-expanded 14th Army, far up north in the Murmansk Oblast. The 367th would remain under these commands for the duration of the war. The Wehrmacht High Command (OKW) had reviewed the German position in Finland and, after being assured by Speer that Germany had sufficient stockpiles of nickel on hand, dropped the plan to hold Pechenga and instead evacuate to Norway in Operation Nordlicht. On October 7, 14th Army opened an offensive against the XIX Mountain Corps on the Litsa River; by the 10th the German forces were in a crisis, and by October 14 had completely lost a front they had held for three years. 14th Army then paused to regroup, resuming its offensive towards the Norwegian border on the 18th and continuing until the 28th when the pursuit began to slow. On November 14 the division was recognized for its part in the taking of the town of Nikel and the surrounding area with the award of the Order of the Red Banner. The 367th Rifle, Order of the Red Banner Division settled down as a garrison unit in the high Arctic until after the end of the war in Europe.<cr><cr>
translation:
该师于1941年8月29日在乌拉尔军区车里雅宾斯克州开始组建。<cr>@col Ivan Mikhailovich Puzikov@@在它开始组建的当天被任命为指挥官，并一直担任此职直到1942年2月24日。11月下旬，该师短暂隶属于最高统帅部预备队中的第28集团军，随后被派往卡累利阿战线，在马泽尔斯卡行动小组中服役。12月报告称该师主要由35至41岁的士兵组成。少校Nikolai Ivanovich Afonskii于2月25日接任指挥官职务，而他则在4月22日被少校Nikolai Ivanovich Shpilev取代。与此同时，第32集团军于3月重组，部分由马泽尔斯卡行动小组组成，并于5月将该师分配给它。6月24日，少校Fedor Ivanovich Korobko接任指挥官职务，但不到一个月后，@col Ivan Mikhailovich Puzikov@@重新担任原职。<cr>第367师一直隶属于第32集团军直到1944年2月。在此期间整个时期，该集团军驻扎在卡累利阿-芬兰苏维埃社会主义共和国的谢格日斯基区，面对芬兰第二军的静态战线。少校Ivan Mikhailovich Puzikov于1942年11月1日被少校Nikolai Antonovich Chernukha取代，后者于1943年5月18日晋升为少将，并一直担任指挥官直到1944年6月12日。<cr>

该师于2月被调往北方，加入第26集团军在乌赫塔地区的部署。它曾短暂隶属于第31步兵军，随后又成为集团军内的独立师。在此期间，接下来的几个月里，它面对的是德国第18山地军的部分部队，而南方芬兰则在 Vyborg - Petrozavodsk攻势中被逐出战争。叶连·彼得罗维奇·辛采夫少将于6月13日接任师长职务，但于8月10日又被亚历山大·亚历克谢耶维奇·斯塔尔采夫上校取代；该军官将一直担任指挥直至战争结束。

九月初，第367步兵师被分配给第132步兵军，仍然隶属于第26集团军。9月4/5日，苏芬停火生效，6日德国在芬兰的部队开始执行“桦树”行动，目标是撤退到挪威，尽管德国有秘密意图要为镍矿的缘故守住别捷尼亚地区。第18山地军分阶段撤离，而第26集团军追击至1940年苏芬边境。

十月，该师被重新分配到新扩编的第14集团军中的第31步兵军，在摩尔曼斯克州北部地区。第367步兵师将在整个战争期间继续隶属于这些指挥机构。国防军最高统帅部（OKW）审查了德国在芬兰的地位，并在施佩尔保证德国拥有足够的镍储备后，放弃了占领别列任加并撤退到挪威的“北方光”行动计划。10月7日，第14集团军对利萨河上的第19山地军发起了进攻；至10日，德军陷入危机，到了10月14日，他们完全失去了坚守了三年的一线阵地。第14集团军随后暂停攻势以重组部队，并于18日重新发起向挪威边境的进攻，直至28日追击速度开始放缓。11月14日，该师因参与夺取尼켈镇及其周边地区而被授予红旗勋章。作为守备部队，第367步兵、红旗师在北极圈内驻扎直到欧洲战争结束。<cr><cr>

text: The 369th Rifle Division began forming on August 1, 1941, as a standard Red Army rifle division, in the Chelyabinsk Oblast. After forming, it was assigned to the 39th Army which soon became part of Kalinin Front, and it participated in the near-encirclement of the German 9th Army around Rzhev in the winter counteroffensive of 1941-42. In late January, 1942, it was transferred to the 29th Army of the same Front, which was very soon after encircled by German forces near Sychevka, and while it was written off by German intelligence in February, enough of the division escaped that it was not officially disbanded. By August it returned to battle, now in 30th Army of Western Front, still fighting near Rzhev. After the salient was finally evacuated in the spring of 1943 the division was moved to Bryansk Front, first in 11th Army and then in 50th Army, under which it served for most of the war. In the summer counteroffensive the 369th was awarded the battle honor 'Karachev' for its part in the liberation of that city. At the start of Operation Bagration the division was in 2nd Belorussian Front and its commander, Maj. Gen. I.S. Lazarenko, was killed a few days later; despite this loss it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner for its successful crossing of the Dniepr River and the liberation of Mogilev. The division continued to advance through Belarus and into Poland and eastern Germany over the following months, but despite a fine record of service was disbanded soon after the German surrender.<cr><cr>
translation: 第369步兵师于1941年8月1日开始在车里雅宾斯克州组建，作为标准的红军步兵师。组建完成后，该师被分配给第39集团军，并很快成为加里宁方面军的一部分，在1941-42年的冬季反攻中参与了对德国第9集团军在热季夫附近几乎完全包围的行动。1942年1月底，它被转移到同一方面的第29集团军，在不久之后就被德军在斯切夫卡附近包围。尽管该师在二月被德军情报部门宣布为已解散，但仍有足够多的人逃脱，使其未正式解散。到8月，该师返回战斗，现在属于西方方面军的第30集团军，仍在热季夫附近作战。随着突出部最终于1943年春季撤出后，该师被转移到布良斯克方面军，在第11集团军和随后在第50集团军服役，直到战争结束前大部分时间都在这里服务。在夏季反攻中，由于其参与解放卡恰耶夫市的行动，第369步兵师获得了“卡恰耶夫”荣誉称号。巴格拉季昂行动开始时，该师属于第二白俄罗斯方面军；几天后，师长伊·斯·拉扎连科少将阵亡；尽管遭受了这一损失，但因成功渡过第聂伯河并解放莫吉廖夫而被授予红旗勋章。接下来几个月中，该师继续在白俄罗斯、波兰和东德推进，但由于出色的服务记录，在德国投降后不久就被解散。<cr><cr>

text: The 36th Cavalry Division was formed prior to 1939 and was assigned to the 11th Army's 3rd Cavalry Corps for the Invasion of Poland.<cr><cr>Assigned to the Belorussion Military District at the onset of Operation Barbarossa.<cr><cr>The division was located on the border of German-occupied Poland at the end of the invasion. This placed it in a position to be attacked by the Germans during the opening hours of the next phase. On 22 June the division was ordered to form part of an Operations Group with the 6th Mechanized Corps to counterattack against the German forces. It was attacked on 23 June by the Luftwaffe causing severe casualties among the troops and horses. The division was effectively destroyed within 48 hours of the invasion and was officially disbanded on 6 July 1941.<cr><cr>
translation: 第36骑兵师成立于1939年前，并被分配给第11集团军的第3骑兵军，参加入侵波兰行动。<cr>在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师被分配到白俄罗斯军区。<cr>在入侵结束时，该师位于德国占领的波兰边境地区。这使它处于德军下一阶段进攻的打击范围内。<cr>1941年6月22日，该师接到命令，与第6机械化军组成作战群，反击德军。<cr>6月23日，德国空军对该师发动攻击，造成严重人员和马匹伤亡。<cr>该师在入侵后的48小时内被有效消灭，并于1941年7月6日正式解散。
