text: The 36th Guards Rifle Division was formed during August 1942 in Ivanovo Oblast from the 9th Airborne Corps. Colonel Mikhail Denisenko, commander of the latter, continued in command of the 36th Guards; he was promoted to major general on 27 November. In addition to smaller support units, it included the 104th, 106th, and 108th Guards Rifle Regiments and the 65th Guards Artillery Regiment. Entering combat on 11 August in the Battle of Stalingrad, it served with the 57th and 64th Armies in fierce defensive battles and participated in the encirclement and elimination of the German troops in Stalingrad. For their steadfastness and courage at Stalingrad, 3,000 soldiers of the division received orders and medals, and the 36th Guards' 39th Guards Anti-Tank (Tank Destroyer) Artillery Battalion was awarded the Order of the Red Banner.<cr>From March 1943 as part of the 64th Army (which became the 7th Guards Army on 16 April) of the Voronezh Front the 36th Guards fought in fierce fighting on the Seversky Donets to the southeast of Belgorod and the defensive phrase of the Battle of Kursk. After the army transferred to the Steppe Front, the division fought in the counteroffensive near Kursk and the recapture of Kharkov, returning to the 57th Army in these battles. On the night of 26 September the division crossed the Dnieper and secured a bridgehead on the right bank of the river near Soshinovka northwest of Dnipropetrovsk. For their successful Dnieper crossing, eight soldiers of the division received the title Hero of the Soviet Union. Developing the offensive, the 36th Guards took the railway station of Verkhnodniprovsk, contributing to the capture of the city of the same name on 22 October. As a result, the division received the name of the city as an honorific on the next day.<cr>Denisenko was transferred and replaced by Major General Georgy Lilenkov in February 1944; Lilenkov commanded the division for the remainder of the war. During the March Uman-Botosani Offensive of the 2nd Ukrainian Front, the 36th Guards, advancing as part of the 7th Guards Army, facilitated the capture of Novoukrainka by the 5th Guards Army and captured the rail junction of Pomoshnaya, for which it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner on 29 March. For successful actions in the crossing of the Southern Bug and the capture of Pervomaysk, the division was awarded the Order of Suvorov, 2nd class, on 1 April. The 36th Guards went on to cross the Prut and fought battles on Romanian territory. The division fought in the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive, with the 104th Guards Rifle and 65th Guards Artillery Regiments receiving the Jassy honorific on 15 September for their actions in the capture of the city on 21 August.<cr>Between October and January 1945, the division fought in the Battle of Debrecen and the Budapest Offensive. For capturing the large rail junction of Szolnok the 104th Guards Rifle and 65th Guards Artillery Regiments were awarded the Order of the Red Banner, and the 41st Guards Sapper Battalion received the Order of Alexander Nevsky. For exemplary actions in the breakthrough of strong fortified defenses and the capture of the Aszod city and rail junction the 106th Guards Rifle Regiment received the Order of Suvorov, 3rd class. During the street fighting in the Siege of Budapest the personnel of the division were credited with killing 3,600 and capturing 5,300 Axis personnel. For distinguishing itself in the Siege of Budapest, the division was awarded the Order of Kutuzov, 2nd class on 5 April. In addition, its 108th and 106th Guards Rifle Regiments received the Order of Alexander Nevsky and the Budapest honorific, respectively, on the same day.<cr>From January 1945, the division, transferred to the 26th Army of the 3rd Ukrainian Front, fought in the Balaton Defensive Operation and the Vienna Offensive. The 36th Guards ended the war on the Mur river near Judenburg in Austria. During the war, 13,000 soldiers of the division received orders and medals, eleven were made Heroes of the Soviet Union, and three became full cavaliers of the Order of Glory.<cr><cr>
translation: 第36近卫步兵师于1942年8月在伊万诺沃州从第9空降军组建而成。该军指挥官米哈伊尔·德尼先科上校继续担任第36近卫师的指挥官，他于11月27日晋升为少将。<cr>除了较小的支援单位外，该师包括第104、106和108近卫步兵团以及第65近卫炮兵团。该师于8月11日在斯大林格勒战役中投入战斗，并与第57集团军和第64集团军一起参加了激烈的防御战，参与了对斯大林格勒德军的包围和消灭。<cr>由于在斯大林格勒表现出的坚定和勇气，该师有3000名士兵获得勋章。第36近卫师下属的第39近卫反坦克（坦克歼击）炮兵团被授予红旗勋章。<cr><cr>自1943年3月起作为第64集团军的一部分（该集团军于4月16日成为第7近卫集团军），隶属于沃罗涅日方面军，第36近卫师在贝尔哥罗德东南部的谢夫斯科耶顿涅茨河畔以及库尔斯克战役防御阶段进行了激烈的战斗。<cr>当该集团军转隶到草原方面军后，该师参加了库尔斯克反攻和哈尔科夫收复战，并在此期间返回第57集团军作战。9月26日晚上，该师渡过第聂伯河，在距离第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克西北部索申诺夫卡附近的右岸建立了桥头堡。<cr>由于成功渡过第聂伯河，该师有8名士兵被授予苏联英雄称号。<cr>在继续进攻的过程中，第36近卫师占领了维尔霍涅德尼普罗夫斯克火车站，并为10月22日攻占同名城市做出了贡献。因此，该师于次日获得以该城市命名的荣誉称谓。1944年2月，丹尼森科被调离，并由少将乔治·利连科夫接任师长职务。利连科夫指挥该师直至战争结束。在第2乌克兰方面军的乌曼-波托恰尼攻势期间，作为第7近卫集团军的一部分，第36近卫师协助第5近卫集团军占领了诺沃卡涅茨克，并俘获了波莫什尼亚铁路枢纽，因此于3月29日被授予红旗勋章。由于在南布格河渡河行动和佩尔沃迈斯克的战斗中表现出色，该师于4月1日被授予苏沃洛夫勋章二级。第36近卫师继续穿越普鲁特河，并在罗马尼亚领土上作战。该师参加了雅西-奇什拉战役，其中第104近卫步兵旅和第65近卫炮兵团因8月21日在城市战斗中的表现而于9月15日被授予雅西荣誉称号。1945年10月至次年1月期间，该师参加了德布勒森战役和布达佩斯进攻。因夺取索尔诺克大型铁路枢纽，第104近卫步兵团和第65近卫炮兵团被授予红旗勋章；第41近卫工兵营则获得亚历山大·涅夫斯基勋章。在突破坚固防御并占领阿绍德市及其铁路枢纽的战斗中，第106近卫步兵团荣获苏沃洛夫勋章三级。在布达佩斯围城战中的巷战期间，该师人员共击毙3600名轴心国士兵，并俘虏5300人。因在布达佩斯围城战中的出色表现，该师于4月5日被授予库图佐夫勋章二级；同一天，其第108近卫步兵团和第106近卫步兵团分别获得亚历山大·涅夫斯基勋章和布达佩斯荣誉称号。<cr>从1945年1月起，该师被调至第三乌克兰方面军的第二十六集团军，在巴拉顿防御行动和维也纳进攻中作战。第36近卫步兵师在奥地利朱德堡附近的穆尔河畔结束了战争。在整个战争期间，该师共有13000名士兵获得勋章；其中11人被授予苏联英雄称号，3人成为三级苏沃洛夫勋章的完全骑士。<cr><cr>

text: The 36th Motorized Division fought its way through the Baltic States in 1941, and was especially heavily engaged at Kalinin, where it helped establish a bridgehead on the upper Volga in late October. Later it stormed the last Leningrad fortifications on Duderhof Hill, before being halted by the order of Adolf Hitler, who thought Leningrad would fall without costly street fighting. The division then fought at Kalinin in the Moscow sector and suffered heavy casualties against the Russian winter offensive of 1941-42. It fought in the defensive battles around Rzhev and Baranova in the summer of 1942, and again took heavy losses.<cr>The division was officially declared demotorized on May 1, 1943, and became the 36th Infantry Division once again, although it did retain more motorized vehicles than the average infantry division. In July 1943 it fought in the bitterly contested Battle of Kursk . Reduced to battle group strength, it took part in the retreats of 194344, on the central sector. In May 1944, it was finally reformed into a two-regiment infantry division. In June 1944, it was smashed near Bobruisk by the massive Soviet summer offensive. Many of its men, including divisional commander Major General Conrady, were taken prisoner. The surviving remnants of the 36th were returned to Germany and reformed at the Baumholder Maneuver Area as a three-regiment Volksgrenadier division.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第36摩托化师于1941年在波罗的海诸国作战，并在加里宁地区特别激烈地参与战斗，帮助在上伏尔加河建立了桥头堡。之后它进攻了杜德尔霍夫山上的最后一个列宁格勒工事，但被阿道夫·希特勒下令停止进攻，他认为无需代价高昂的城市巷战就能攻下列宁格勒。该师随后参加了莫斯科地区的加里宁战斗，并在1941-42年的俄罗斯冬季攻势中遭受了重大损失。它还参与了1942年夏天围绕日兹德拉和巴诺瓦的防御战，再次蒙受重大损失。<cr>第36摩托化师于1943年5月1日正式被宣布为非摩托化，并重新成为步兵师，尽管它保留了比普通步兵师更多的机动车辆。在1943年7月的库尔斯克激战中，该师参与了战斗。缩减到战斗群规模后，它参加了1943-44年的撤退行动，在中央战区作战。1944年5月，它最终被重组为一个拥有两个团的步兵师。在1944年6月，它在鲍里斯拉夫附近遭到苏联夏季攻势的重创。许多士兵，包括师长康拉迪少将，都被俘虏。<cr>第36师残部返回德国，并在巴姆霍尔训练区重组为一个拥有三个团的国民掷弹兵师。<cr>参考文献：<cr>《二战中的德军装甲、摩托化步兵和武装党卫军师战斗序列》第三卷，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text: The corps was assigned to Kiev Military District as general reserve at the outbreak of hostilities and fought around Dubno in July 1941, being mostly destroyed. Reformed in July 1943 as part of 31st Army, it fought in the Battle of Kursk . At that time, it consisted of the 215th and 274th Rifle Divisions. Assigned to Western Front reserve in August 1943, it fought again near Minsk in July 1943 during the Belorussian Offensive. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军在冲突爆发时被分配到基辅军区作为预备队，并于1941年7月在杜布诺附近作战，大部分部队被消灭。1943年7月重新组建为第31集团军的一部分，在库尔斯克战役中参战。当时，它由第215步兵师和第274步兵师组成。该部于1943年8月被分配到西方面军预备队，并在白俄罗斯攻势期间再次参与了1943年7月明斯克附近的战斗。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军二战战斗序列, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text:
The 36th Tank Division was formed in March 1941 near Minsk in Western Special Military District as part of 17th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
71st Tank Regiment - 0 tanks
72nd Tank Regiment - 0 tanks
36th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
36th Howitzer Regiment - 1 light bn only
36th Reconnaissance Battalion - 3 foot cos<cr>
The 36th Tank Division was formed without tanks or armored cars, and by 22 June 1941 still had no armor on hand, no antiaircraft weapons, and no heavy artillery.
Along with the rest of 17th Mechanized Corps, 36th Tank Division was caught in the Minsk pocket and destroyed. The division was officially dissolved on 1 August 1941.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: The 370th Infantry Division was formed in February 1942 in the Reims area of France as part of the 19th Wave. It contained the 666th, 667th and 668th Infantry Regiments, 370th Schnelle Battalion, 370th Artillery Regiment and various support units. Troops were provided from the 302nd, 304th and 320th Infantry Divisions of the 15th Army. The division was sent to the Eastern Front as soon as its organization was completed. It fought on the Mius River Front, at Rostov, in the Caucasus and at the Kuban bridgehead. After the retreat through the Ukraine the division was surrounded and destroyed at Kishinev in Bessarabia in August and September 1944. The few survivors not present when the division was encircled were returned to France and used to help rebuild the 76th Infantry Division.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, German Order of Battle Volume II: 291st-999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions, and Special Divisions in WWII<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第370步兵师于1942年2月在法国兰斯地区组建，属于第19波。该师包括第666团、第667团和第668团，第370快速营，第370炮兵团以及各种支援单位。人员来自第15集团军的第302步兵师、第304步兵师和第320步兵师。该师一组建即被派往东线作战，在米乌斯河方面军、罗斯托夫、高加索以及库班桥头堡等地参战。撤退通过乌克兰后，该师在1944年8月和9月的比萨拉比亚基希讷乌地区被包围并被消灭。少数幸存者未参与围困时返回法国，并用于帮助重建第76步兵师。<cr>参考文献：George F. Nafziger,《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham,《二战中的德国战斗序列 第二卷：291至999步兵师、命名步兵师及特殊师团》<cr>Chris Munson 提供

text: The 371st Infantry Division was formed in February 1942 in Belgium as part of the 19th Wave. It contained the 669th, 670th and 671st Infantry Regiments, 371st Reconnaissance Battalion, 371st Artillery Regiment and various support units. The division completed its training in France in May 1942 and joined the Sixth Army on the Eastern Front in time for the commencement of Operation Fall Blau. The division participated in the street fighting at Stalingrad and along with the rest of the Sixth Army was surrounded. The division surrendered to the Russians when the city fell in January 1943.<cr>By an order dated February 17, 1943 the division was ordered reformed. Reforming in Brittany in March 1943 it absorbed the 156th Reserve Division but was still only a Kampfgruppe. In June it again became a full division. It was sent to Italy and Slovenia in November and to Croatia in December. In January 1944 the division transferred to the Eastern Front where it remained until the end of the war. The division was taken prisoner by the Russians in the Deutsch-Brod pocket east of Prague at the end of the war.<cr><cr>George F. text: The 371st Rifle Division was raised in 1941 as a standard Red Army rifle division, and served for the duration of WWII in that role. It began forming in August 1941 in the Urals Military District. It was soon moved to the front lines near Moscow, and took part in the counteroffensive that began on December 5. It spent all of 1942 and the first months of 1943 in the fighting around the Rzhev salient, and after a short break served in the offensive that liberated Smolensk. After a winter of brutal combat on the approaches to Orsha and Vitebsk it was reassigned to 5th Army in 3rd Belorussian Front and took part in Operation Bagration, during which it was recognized for its role in the liberation of the latter city with a battle honor. The division was further distinguished in late July with the Order of the Red Banner for its part in the liberation of Vilnius. In January 1945, it fought its way into East Prussia, and as that campaign was winding down it was moved across Asia, along with the rest of 5th Army, to take part in the campaign against the Japanese Kwantung Army in Manchuria.<cr><cr>

text: The 373rd Rifle Division was raised in 1941 as an infantry division of the Red Army, and served for the duration of WWII in that role. It began forming in August 1941 in the Urals Military District. It was moved to the front northwest of Moscow while still trying to complete its training and went straight into action in mid-December during the winter counteroffensive. Until May 1943, it was involved in the bloody fighting around the Rzhev salient. After a period in reserve for rebuilding, the division's combat path shifted southward when it was assigned to 52nd Army, where it remained for the duration of the war. It won a battle honor in eastern Ukraine, then fought across the Dniepr River late that year, and was awarded the Order of the Red Banner for its successes. Following this it advanced through western Ukraine in the spring of 1944, then into Romania in the summer, where it played a major role in the second encirclement and destruction of the German 6th Army. After again moving to the reserves the division shifted northwards with its Army to join 1st Ukrainian Front, fighting through Poland, eastern Germany and into Czechoslovakia.<cr><cr>
translation: 第373步兵师于1941年作为红军的一个步兵师组建，并在第二次世界大战期间一直担任该角色。它于1941年8月开始在乌拉尔军区组建，随后被调往莫斯科西北方向的前线，在试图完成训练的同时直接投入了冬季反攻中的战斗。直到1943年5月，它都参与了围绕热季突出部的血腥战斗。经过一段时间作为预备队重建后，该师作战路线转向南方，并被分配给第52集团军，一直待到战争结束。它在乌克兰东部赢得了一项荣誉，在当年晚些时候渡过了第聂伯河，并因取得的成功而获得红旗勋章。随后，它于1944年春季穿越了西乌克兰，夏季进入罗马尼亚，在第二次包围并摧毁德国第六集团军的过程中发挥了重要作用。再次作为预备队调动后，该师随其集团军向北移动，加入第一乌克兰方面军，战斗贯穿波兰、东德，并深入捷克斯洛伐克。<cr>指挥官报告：<cr><cr>部队番号：<cr>

text: The 375th Rifle Division was raised in 1941 as an infantry division of the Red Army, and served for the duration of WWII in that role. It began forming in August, 1941 in the Urals Military District. It reached the fighting front in December, coming under command of the 29th Army in the vicinity of the Rzhev salient and it took part in the bloody and tragic battles for this heavily-fortified position until March, 1943, mostly as part of 30th Army. Following the German evacuation of the salient the 375th got a brief spell in reserve before being reassigned to Voronezh Front in the buildup to the Battle of Kursk . When the offensive began it held a crucial sector on the extreme left flank of 6th Guards Army where the II SS Panzer Corps attempted to break through south of the salient. Following the German defeat the division joined in the counteroffensive towards Kharkov in August and won its first battle honor. It continued to advance through Ukraine and into Romania over the next eight months, being brought to a halt east of Ia?i in the spring of 1944. In late August the 2nd and 3rd Ukrainian Fronts crushed the defending German and Romanian forces, and on the last day of the month the 375th played a leading role in the capture of the Romanian capital, Bucharest; it won its second battle honor and two of its rifle regiments were awarded decorations. For the duration of the war the division fought its way through Romania and Hungary, finally advancing into Austria with 7th Guards Army. Its record of admirable service was capped with the award of the Order of the Red Banner soon following the German surrender, but it was nevertheless disbanded shortly thereafter.<cr><cr>
translation:
第375步兵师于1941年作为红军的一个步兵师组建，并在第二次世界大战期间一直担任该角色。它从1941年8月开始在乌拉尔军区组建，到同年12月抵达战斗前线，在热季突出部附近受命于第29集团军指挥下作战。直到1943年3月，该师主要作为第30集团军的一部分参与了这场重兵设防位置的血腥和悲剧性战役。

随着德军撤离突出部后，第375步兵师短暂进入预备状态，并随后被重新分配到沃罗涅日方面军，在库尔斯克会战前集结。当进攻开始时，它在第6近卫集团军极左翼的一个关键区域坚守阵地，而II SS装甲军试图从突出部以南突破防线。

随着德军的失败，该师参与了8月向哈尔科夫反攻，并赢得了它的第一个战斗荣誉。接下来八个月里，它继续推进穿过乌克兰进入罗马尼亚，在1944年春季在雅西以东被阻止前进。

到8月底，第2和第3乌克兰方面军击溃了守卫的德军和罗马尼亚军队；当月最后一天，第375步兵师在占领罗马尼亚首都布加勒斯特中发挥了主导作用，并赢得了它的第二个战斗荣誉，其两个步兵团被授予勋章。

在整个战争期间，该师一路穿过罗马尼亚和匈牙利作战，最终与第7近卫集团军一起推进到奥地利。随着德国投降后不久获得红旗勋章的嘉奖，它仍然在战后不久解散了。

text: The 376th Infantry Division was formed in March 1942 in southwest France as part of the 19th Wave with personnel from the 327th, 335th and 337th Infantry Divisions. It contained the 672nd, 673rd and 767th Infantry Regiments, 376th Reconnaissance Battalion, 376th Artillery Regiment and various support units. As part of the German Sixth Army during Fall Blau in the summer of 1942 it participated in clearing the Don River bend and the drive to the Volga. The division, like the rest of the Sixth Army, was surrounded during the Battle of Stalingrad. The divisional commander surrendered the division without approval in January 1943. Most of the divisions personnel were either killed at Stalingrad or died later in Russian POW camps in Siberia.<cr>The division was ordered rebuilt in March 1943 as a Kampfgruppe in Holland. By June 1943 it had been rebuilt to a full division. In January 1944 the remants of the 167th Infantry Division were incorporated into the division. The division was destroyed in the southern Ukraine in August 1944. Survivors were incorporated into the 15th and 76th Infantry Divisions. The division was formally disbanded in October 1944.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, German Order of Battle Volume II: 291st-999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions, and Special Divisions in WWII<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第376步兵师于1942年3月在法国西南部组建，作为第19波的一部分，人员来自第327、335和337步兵师。该师包括第672、673和767步兵团，第376侦察营，第376炮兵团以及各种支援单位。在1942年夏季的蓝色行动中，作为德国第六集团军的一部分，它参与了清理顿河弯道并推进至伏尔加河的任务。该师与第六集团军其他部队一样，在斯大林格勒战役期间被包围。<cr>指挥官报告：1943年1月，师长未经批准就投降了该师。大多数人员要么在斯大林格勒阵亡，要么后来死于西伯利亚的苏联战俘营中。<cr>第376步兵师于1943年3月下令重建为荷兰的一个战斗群。到1943年6月已重建为一个完整的师。1944年1月，第167步兵师的残部被并入该师。该师在1944年8月南部乌克兰地区被消灭。<cr>幸存者被编入第15和第76步兵师。该师于1944年10月正式解散。

text: The 377th Infantry Division was formed in March 1942 in LeMans, France as part of the 19th Wave with personnel from the 332nd, 333rd, 708th, 709th and 715th Infantry Divisions. It contained the 768th, 769th and 770th Infantry Regiments, 377th Reconnaissance Battalion, 377th Artillery Regiment and various support units. The division was sent to the Eastern Front that summer. The division suffered terrible losses in the Battle of Stalingrad and the subsequent retreat. Five of its nine grenadier battalions were either destroyed or absorbed by other units in the division. The division was rebuilt but again was nearly destroyed retreating across Russian in the Spring of 1944. The survivors were absorbed by the 340th Infantry Division in March 1944.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, German Order of Battle Volume II: 291st-999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions, and Special Divisions in WWII<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text: The 377th Rifle Division was raised in 1941 as an infantry division of the Red Army, and served for the duration of WWII in that role. It began forming in August, 1941 in the Urals Military District. It followed a very similar combat path to that of the 374th and 376th Rifle Divisions. It joined the fighting front in December with the 4th Army, and then briefly came under command of 2nd Shock Army, but soon moved to the 59th Army along the Volkhov River, and continued to serve in this Army's battles near Leningrad until early 1944. The division took very heavy casualties during the Lyuban Offensive in several attempts to relieve the beleaguered 2nd Shock Army. After rebuilding the division held the Army's bridgehead over the Volkhov during 1943, and finally advanced during the Leningrad-Novgorod Offensive in January, 1944, taking part in the assault that liberated Novgorod. During the spring the division saw heavy fighting in the battles for Narva before moving south for the summer offensive into the Baltic states. In September it won a battle honor in the liberation of Valga, and in October also received the Order of the Red Banner for its part in the liberation of Riga. The division ended the war in Latvia, helping to contain and reduce the German forces trapped in the Courland Pocket, and was disbanded later in 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第377步兵师于1941年作为红军的一个步兵师组建，并在第二次世界大战期间一直担任这一角色。该师从1941年8月开始在乌拉尔军区组建。其战斗路径与第374和第376步兵师非常相似。该师于12月加入第四集团军的前线，随后短暂隶属于第二突击集团军指挥，但很快转移到沿沃尔霍夫河的第五十九集团军，并继续参与该集团军在列宁格勒附近的战斗直到1944年初。该师在卢班进攻行动中遭受了非常严重的伤亡，在几次试图解救被围困的第二突击集团军的努力中损失惨重。重建后，该师于1943年守卫沃尔霍夫河上的桥头堡，并最终参与了1944年1月列宁格勒-诺夫哥罗德进攻行动中的突击部队，解放了诺夫哥罗德。在春季期间，该师在纳尔瓦的战斗中遭受重创，然后转移到南方参加夏季攻势进入波罗的海国家。9月，在解放瓦尔加时获得了一项荣誉，并于10月因参与解放里加而获得了红旗勋章。该师最终在拉脱维亚结束战争，帮助围困并削弱了被困在库尔兰包围圈中的德国部队，并于1945年晚些时候解散。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: The 379th Rifle Division was raised in 1941 as an infantry division of the Red Army, and served for the duration of WWII in that role. It began forming in August, 1941 in the Urals Military District. It first served in the winter counteroffensive west of Moscow, and later in the bitter fighting around the Rzhev salient, but was moved north late in 1942. It took up positions along the Volkhov River, mostly under command of the 8th Army, and continued to serve in this Army's battles near Leningrad until September 1943, when it was transferred to the 2nd Baltic Front, where it would stay for the remainder of its service. During this period the division served under many army and corps commands but mostly in the 3rd Shock Army. The division ended the war in Lithuania, helping to contain and reduce the German forces trapped in the Courland Pocket. By this time it was judged as being surplus to the Red Army's needs and in December 1944 its personnel were parceled out to help bring other units of the Front closer to establishment strength. The 379th officially disbanded on the first day of 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第379步兵师于1941年作为红军的一个步兵师组建，并在第二次世界大战期间一直担任这一角色。该师从1941年8月开始在乌拉尔军区组建。它首次参与了莫斯科西部的冬季反攻，随后参加了围绕热夫突出部的激烈战斗，但于1942年底被调往北方。该师沿沃尔霍夫河布防，主要受第8集团军指挥，并继续参加该集团军在列宁格勒附近的战役，直到1943年9月转隶给波罗的海第二方面军。在此期间，该师曾接受过多个集团军和军的指挥，但大部分时间都在突击第三集团军服役。战争结束时，第379步兵师驻扎在立陶宛，帮助围困并削弱了被困于库尔兰包围圈内的德军部队。此时，它被认为对红军来说是多余的，在1944年12月，其人员被分配到其他方面军的单位以接近编制完整度。第379步兵师在1945年第一天正式解散。<cr> <cr>

text: The 37th Army first formed on 10 August 1941 in the Southwestern Front with the command group from the Kiev Fortified Region and other reserves in front reserves.<cr>Upon formation the army took up defensive positions to the west of Kiev and on the left bank of the Dnieper River. During the defense of Kiev the army suffered serious losses against superior German forces. The army was surrounded in the city of Kiev and was ordered to break out on 19 September. Individual units of the army were able to break out and joined forces with the front. Many of the other units of the army were destroyed. The army was disbanded on 25 September 1941.<cr>The army was reformed on 15 November 1941 in the Southern Front for a counterattack in the Rostov area against the German 1st Panzer Army. These actions facilitated the 9th and 56th Armies liberation of Rostov-on-Don. The army took part in the Barvenkovo-Lozovaya Offensive from 18-31 January 1942 with the goal of destroying the German Army in southern Ukraine.<cr>The army conducted defensive operations during the summer and fall of 1942 in reaction to German operations in the Southern Soviet Union. The army was transferred from the Southern Front to the Don Group of the North Caucasian Front in late July and then the Transcaucasian Front in August 1942.<cr>As part of the North Caucasian Strategic Offensive in January 1943 the army liberated the towns of Kislovodsk, Pyatigorsk, Essentuki and Cherkessk. The army was transferred to the North Caucasian Front on 24 January to participate in the Krasnodar Offensive. In July the army forces were reassigned to the 9th and 56th Armies and the 37th Army was placed under STAVKA control.<cr>On 7 September 1943 the army was assigned to the Steppe Front. The army took part in the liberation of the Left-bank Ukraine east of Kremenchug. In late September it crossed the Dnieper River west of Keleberda and northwest of Mishurin Rog. From October to December the army was involved in offensive operations in the Krivoy Rog area.<cr>Assigned to the 3rd Ukrainian Front on 15 January 1944. Participated in the Odessa Offensive in conjunction with the 46th Army. From 8 August, the army participated in the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive and in September the liberation of Bulgaria. By the end of September, its troops reached the area of Kazanlak, Yambol, and Burgas, where the army's combat history ended. The army remained in Bulgaria as a garrison for the rest of the war.<cr><cr>
translation: 第37集团军于1941年8月10日在西南方面军成立，指挥机构来自基辅要塞区和其他预备队。<cr>组建时，该集团军在基辅西面和第聂伯河左岸布设了防御阵地。在保卫基辅期间，面对优势德军的进攻，该集团军遭受严重损失。9月19日，该集团军被命令从基辅城中突围。<cr>个别部队成功突围并与方面军会合，但其他许多单位被消灭。第37集团军于1941年9月25日解散。<cr>该集团军于1941年11月15日在南方方面军重组，准备在罗斯托夫地区对德军第1装甲集团军发动反击。这些行动促进了第9和第56集团军解放顿河畔罗斯托夫。<cr>该集团军参加了从1942年1月18日至31日的巴尔文科沃-洛佐瓦亚攻势，目标是在乌克兰南部消灭德军。<cr>在1942年夏秋之际，作为对德国南方苏联境内行动的反应，该集团军进行了防御作战。7月底，第37集团军从南方方面军转隶至北高加索方向顿河集群，8月则进一步转隶至外高加索方向。<cr>在1943年1月的北高加索战略攻势中，该集团军解放了基斯洛沃茨克、皮亚季戈尔斯克、埃森图基和切尔克斯克等城镇。第37集团军于1月24日转隶至北高加索方向，参加刻赤攻势。<cr>7月，该集团军部队被重新分配给第9和第56集团军，而第37集团军则置于最高统帅部大本营的控制之下。1943年9月7日，该集团军被分配给顿涅茨方面军。该集团军参与了左岸乌克兰的解放行动，位于克雷门奇格以东地区。9月下旬，它在克列伯尔达以西和米舒林罗格西北方向渡过了第聂伯河。从10月到12月，该集团军参与了克里沃伊罗格地区的进攻作战。<cr>1944年1月15日被分配给第3乌克兰方面军。与第46集团军一起参加了敖德萨攻势。8月8日起，该集团军参与了雅西-奇西瑙攻势，并在9月份解放了保加利亚。<cr>到9月底，其部队到达卡赞拉克、亚米布尔和布尔加斯地区，至此结束了战斗历史。该集团军余下的战争时间里留在保加利亚作为守备部队。<cr>

text: The 37th Guards Rifle Division was formed on 2 August 1942 from the 1st Airborne Corps in Lyubertsy, near Moscow. Its most famous action was the defense of the Stalingrad Tractor Factory during the Battle of Stalingrad. The division was highly decorated, receiving two Orders of the Red Banner, the Order of Suvorov 1st class, the Order of Kutuzov 1st class and the Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky.<cr><cr>
translation: 第37近卫步兵师成立于1942年8月2日，由莫斯科附近的卢贝茨的第1空降军改编而成。该师最著名的行动是在斯大林格勒战役期间防御斯大林格勒拖拉机厂。该师获得多项荣誉，包括两次荣获红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫一级勋章、库图佐夫一级勋章和博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基勋章。<cr><cr>

text: The corps was assigned to the Kiev Military District as general reserve at the outbreak of hostilities. It fought in the Battle of Brody in June 1941 as part of the 6th Army. At this time, it consisted of 41st, 97th and 99th Rifle Divisions. it was dissolved in August 1941. Reformed in May 1943 as part of 44th Army, it participated in the battles around the Kuban bridgehead. In January 1944, it consisted of 248th, 416th, and 417th Rifle Divisions. It participated in the Siege of Budapest in the winter of 1944-45. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军在冲突爆发时被分配到基辅军区作为预备队。它于1941年6月参加布罗迪战役，当时隶属于第6集团军。此时，它由第41、第97和第99步兵师组成。该军于1941年8月解散，并于1943年5月在第44集团军内重建，参加了库班桥头堡周围的战斗。1944年1月，它由第248、第416和第417步兵师组成。该军还参与了布达佩斯围城战（1944-45年冬季）。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军战斗序列：伟大卫国战争，Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text:
In June 1941 ithe 37th Rifle Division was part of the 21st Rifle Corps in the Western Special Military District, directly under Western Front control. Colonel Andrey Chekharin commanded the division at the time. Soon after the beginning of Operation Barbarossa the division was effectively destroyed, though by 29 June 1941 a composite regiment (20th Rifle Regiment) formed mostly from division rear units (Tyl) was attached to the 153rd Rifle Division.

On 24 July 1941 the Petrozavodsk Rifle Division was formed from the 52nd and 1061st Rifle Regiments of the Red Army and the 15th Motor Rifle Regiment of the NKVD. Two days later it was redesignated the 37th Rifle Division. Later fought at Molodechno and Riga. With 22nd Army of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (RVGK) May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
1941年6月，第37步兵师隶属于西方特别军区的第21步兵军，直接接受西方面军指挥。当时该师由安德烈·切卡林上校指挥。巴巴罗萨行动开始不久后，该师实际上被消灭了，不过到1941年6月29日，一个由师部属单位（后勤）主要组成的合成团（第20步兵团）已并入第153步兵师。

1941年7月24日，彼得罗扎沃茨克步兵师由红军的第52和第1061步兵团以及内务人民委员部的第15摩托化步兵团组建。两天后改称为第37步兵师。之后参加了莫洛杰奇诺和里加的战斗。1945年5月隶属于最高统帅部预备队（RVGK）的第22集团军。<cr><cr><cr>

text:
The 37th Tank Division was formed March 1941 at Kremenets in western Kiev Special Military District as part of 15th Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
73rd Tank Regiment
74th Tank Regiment
37th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd bns only: very few trucks
37th Howitzer Regiment
37th Reconnaissance Battalion
37th Pontoon Battalion
37th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>The 37th Tank Division had 1 KV-2, 34 T-34s,258 BT-7s, 22 T-26s, and 1 OT-26 tanks on hand on 22 June. The division was overstrength by 10% in manpower, but short 50% of its NCOs and 60% of its officers - leaving a lot of enlisted men with no one to train or organize them.
The division fought across the Ukraine throughout June, July, and August, and in early August was evacuated to the rear, where the personnel of the division were used to form 3rd Tank Brigade.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: The 381st Rifle Division was raised in 1941 as an infantry division of the Red Army, and served for the duration of WWII in that role. It began forming in August, 1941 in the Urals Military District. It first served in the bitter fighting around the Rzhev salient, deep in the German rear in the 39th Army and came close to being completely destroyed in July, 1942. The division's survivors were moved north well away from the front for a major rebuilding. It returned to the front in October, joining the 3rd Shock Army for the battle and siege of Velikiye Luki. The division remained in this general area in western Russia until March, 1944, when it was moved to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command and then to 21st Army north of Leningrad in April. It served in the offensive that drove Finland out of the war from June to September, winning a battle honor and the Order of the Red Banner in the process, before being transferred back to the Soviet-German front in October. As part of the 2nd Shock Army of 2nd Belorussian Front the 381st advanced across Poland and Pomerania during the winter of 1945, then joined its Front's advance across the Oder River into north-central Germany in late April, ending the war on the Baltic coast.<cr><cr>
translation: 第381步兵师于1941年作为红军的一个步兵师组建，并在第二次世界大战期间一直担任这一角色。该师从1941年8月开始在乌拉尔军区组建。它首次参与了围绕热季突出部的激烈战斗，在第39集团军中，深入德国后方作战，并于1942年7月几乎被完全消灭。<cr>幸存下来的部队被调往北方远离前线的地方进行大规模重建。该师于10月重返战场，加入第3突击集团军参加维捷布斯克的战役和围城战。直到1944年3月，该师一直驻扎在西俄罗斯这一地区。<cr>然后它被转移到最高统帅部预备队，并于4月调往列宁格勒北部的第21集团军。从6月至9月，该师参加了驱逐芬兰出战的攻势，在此过程中赢得了一项荣誉和红旗勋章，随后于10月返回苏德战场。<cr>作为第二白俄罗斯方面军第2突击集团军的一部分，第381步兵师在1945年冬季穿越波兰和波美拉尼亚，并加入其方面军跨越奥得河进入德国中部的攻势，在战争结束时驻扎在波罗的海沿岸。<cr> <cr>

text: The 383rd Infantry Division was formed in January 1942 as part of the 18th Wave. The division was one of the 'Rheingold' (Rhine Gold) divisions hastily formed to deal with the crisis on the Eastern Front. It contained the 531st, 532nd and 533rd Infantry Regiments, 383rd Panzerjger Battalion, 383rd Artillery Regiment and various support units. The division was continuously engaged on the Eastern Front throughout its existance. The division fought at the Battle of Voronezh in the early stages of Operation Fall Blau as well as later at Bryansk, Mogilev and Bobruisk. The division along with many others was destroyed in the 1944 Russian summer offensive against Army Group Center. It was formally disbanded on August 3rd, 1944.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham, German Order of Battle Volume II: 291st-999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions, and Special Divisions in WWII<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第383步兵师成立于1942年1月，属于第18波组建的部队之一。该师是为应对东线危机而匆忙组建的“莱茵金”师之一。它包括第531、532和533步兵团，第383装甲猎兵营，第383炮兵团以及各种支援单位。该师在其存在期间一直持续在东线作战。该师参加了蓝色行动早期阶段的沃罗涅日战役，之后还参与了布良斯克、莫吉廖夫和鲍里斯波尔等地的战斗。1944年夏季攻势中，该师与许多其他部队一起被消灭于中央集团军群防区。正式解散日期为1944年8月3日。<cr>参考文献：George F. Nafziger，《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr>Samuel W. Mitcham，《二战中的德国战斗序列 第二卷：第291至第999师、命名步兵师及其他特别部队》<cr>本文由Chris Munson提供

text:
The formation of the division began in August, at mine #6 in Stalino (now Donetsk). The division included six special anti-tank detachments, created by the city committee of Komsomol in Stalino. Specifically for this division, the production of mines, grenades and other anti-tank weapons in the city was drastically increased. Colonel Konstantin Provalov, graduate of the M. V. Frunze Military Academy and Hero of the Soviet Union, was appointed commander of the division.<cr><cr>'The right to command the newly created divisions went to people who knew and the theory and practice of military art - the graduates of the M.V. Frunze Military Academy. The Heroes of the Soviet Union Colonels KI Provalov, ID Zinoviev and AI Petrakovsky were appointed to command the 383rd, 393rd and 395th Rifle Divisions, respectively). So on, the 20th August 1941 they were summoned the offices of the People's Commissariat for Defence.'<cr><cr>The formation and training of the division ended in September 1941, when it was put into battle. On 30 September 1941, the 383rd division was incorporated into the 18th Army of the Southern Front. The division then took up defensive positions on the 'Krasnoarmiisk-Selydove' line. From 15 October until 22 October, the division participated in the defense of Stalino. By that time, they had destroyed 30 tanks, four mortar batteries, two artillery batteries and had killed more than 5,000 German soldiers. By 23 October, the German Army had finally taken Stalino, and the 383rd killed another 1,500 German soldiers during its retreat.

Following this defeat, the division was transferred to the Transcaucasian Front, to stop the Germans from penetrating to the oil fields of Azerbaijan. There, the division successfully held defensive positions, refusing to give up ground. In the beginning of 1943 the division fought near Novorossisk. On 7 November 1943 the division crossed the Kerch strait and landed its troops near Kerch, as part of the Kerch-Eltigen Operation. On 1 January 1944, the Division was part of the Separate Coastal Army's 16th Rifle Corps, along with the 89th, 227th, and 339th Rifle Divisions. In April 1944 the division liberated Feodosiya, and later helped liberate Sevastopol. By the end of May 1944 the Transcaucasian Front had completely freed Crimea from German occupation.

In January 1945, the 383rd Division was assigned to the 33rd Army of the 1st Belorussian Front where it served for the rest of the war, advancing through Poland and into Germany. From 16 April to 2 May, the division participated in the Battle of Berlin.

The division was disbanded in the summer of 1945 in Germany in accordance with a Stavka directive of 29 May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
该师的组建工作始于八月，在斯大林诺（现顿涅茨克）的第六矿开始。该师包括六个由斯大林诺共青团城市委员会创建的特殊反坦克分队。为了这个师，城市的地雷、手榴弹和其他反坦克武器生产大幅增加。米哈伊尔·弗鲁宁军事学院毕业生、苏联英雄康斯坦丁·普罗瓦洛夫被任命为该师指挥官。<cr>“新组建师的指挥权交给了那些了解军事理论和实践的人——米哈伊尔·弗鲁宁军事学院的毕业生。苏联英雄科尔尼洛夫上校、济诺维耶夫上校和彼得拉科夫斯基上校分别被任命为第383步兵师、第393步兵师和第395步兵师的指挥官。”<cr>1941年8月20日，他们被召集到国防人民委员部办公室。<cr>该师的组建和训练工作于1941年九月结束，并投入战斗。1941年9月30日，第383步兵师加入南方方面军第18集团军。随后，该师在“克拉斯诺亚尔斯克-塞利多沃”线上占据防御阵地。从10月15日至22日，该师参与了斯大林诺的防御战。在此期间，他们摧毁了30辆坦克、4个迫击炮连、2个炮兵连，并杀死了超过5,000名德军士兵。到10月23日，德军终于占领了斯大林诺，第383步兵师在撤退过程中又杀死了1,500名德军士兵。

在此次失败后，该师被调往高加索方面军，阻止德国军队深入阿塞拜疆的油田。在那里，该师成功坚守防御阵地，拒绝放弃任何领土。1943年初，该师在诺沃罗西斯克附近作战。1943年11月7日，该师渡过刻赤海峡，在刻赤地区登陆，作为刻赤-埃利季纳行动的一部分。1944年1月1日，该师隶属于独立海岸集团军的第16步兵军，与第89、227和339步兵师共同作战。1944年4月，该师解放了费奥多西亚，并随后帮助解放了塞瓦斯托波尔。到1944年5月底，高加索方面军已完全从德国占领中解放克里米亚。

1945年1月，第383师被分配到第一白俄罗斯方面军的第33集团军，在那里为余下的战争服务，穿越波兰进入德国。从4月16日至5月2日，该师参加了柏林战役。

该师于1945年夏天根据最高统帅部大本营1945年5月29日的指令在德国解散。<cr><cr>

text: The 387th Infantry Division was formed in February 1942 as part of the 18th Wave. The division was one of the 'Rheingold' (Rhine Gold) divisions hastily formed to deal with the crisis on the Eastern Front. It contained the 541st, 542nd and 543rd Infantry Regiments, 387th Panzerjger Battalion, 387th Artillery Regiment and various support units. The division was largely destroyed in the Don Basin during the Soviet Operaton Uranus. An order of February 17, 1943 directed that the survivors of the 385th and 387th divisions be combined into a Kampfverband which had the strength of a reinforced grenadier division. Some excess troops were sent to the 79th and 295th Infantry and 100th Jger Divisions. In March 1943 the division was ordered rebuilt. The division was disbanded in March 1944.<cr><cr>George F. Nafziger, The German Order of Battle Infantry in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第387步兵师于1942年2月作为第18波组建。该师是为应对东线危机而仓促成立的“莱茵金”师之一，下辖第541、542和543步兵团，第387装甲掷弹兵营，第387炮兵团以及各种支援单位。该师在顿河盆地被苏联天王星行动摧毁。1943年2月17日的命令指示将第385和第387师的幸存者合并为一个战斗群，其战斗力相当于加强掷弹兵师。一些多余的部队被派往第79、第295步兵师和第100猎兵师。1943年3月该师被命令重建。该师于1944年3月解散。<cr>参考文献：George F. Nafziger, 《二战中的德国战斗序列：步兵》<cr><cr>-<cr>Chris Munson 提供

text: The 38th Army was formed on 4 August 1941 after a large Soviet force had been surrounded by Axis forces in the area of Uman in the western Ukraine. 38th Army was based on the forces and headquarters of the 8th Mechanised Corps and incorporated other Soviet units then in the Cherkassy area. The army was subordinated to the Soviet Southwestern Front command, and was to defend the line of the Dnepr upriver from Kremenchuk, a task that became more urgent after the Soviet forces at Uman surrendered on 12 August and German forces began to close up to the Dnepr.<cr>On 12 September German armoured forces broke through 38th Army's lines and struck north, first to Lubny and then to Lokhavytsa where, on 16 September, they made contact with German armoured forces moving south from Romny. 38th Army easily avoided encirclement by the slow-moving infantry divisions of Sixth Army. On 5 January the right flank of 38th Army attacked the German Sixth Army's positions northeast of Kharkov in an attempt to advance on Belgorod, but it had failed to disguise it's intentions and the German defences were well prepared. By the second week of January Southwestern Front's offensives north of Kharkov, including that of 38th Army, had ground to a halt.<cr>During the late winter and spring of 1942 the frontline in the Kharkov area was relatively static. During the spring of 1942 Soviet high command had been preparing a renewed offensive to take Kharkov. This offensive opened on 12 May. The attacks north of Kharkov were held by German forces, and in the south the Germans responded by launching an offensive of their own against the shoulders of the Barvenkovo Pocket. On the morning of 28 June the main German strategic offensive of 1942 (Case Blue) opened with an attack from the Kursk area towards the Don at Voronezh. part of 38th Army was surrounded at Millerovo. On July 23rd the army was formally disbanded.<cr>On 3 August 1942 the 4th Reserve Army, part of the Soviet strategic reserve, was designated as the second formation of 38th Army and was assigned to Bryansk Front. The 38th went on the offensive in early January 1943 and by March the lines had stabilized around the Kursk salient. On 5 July 1943 Germany's last strategic offensive on the Eastern Front (Operation Citadel) opened with attacks on the northern and southern shoulders of the Kursk Salient.<cr>On 12 July Soviet forces began to go over to the offensive. Although during July and August the forces of Voronezh Front made considerable advances east of the Psel river, advancing south to within 50 kilometres of Poltava, 38th Army's positions on the other side of the Psel (on Voronezh Front's extreme right flank south of Korenevo) changed little. By late September 38th Army had crossed the Desna and had seized two small bridgeheads across the Dnepr north of Kiev in the Lutezh area.<cr>On 10 March 1945 38th Army was one of three Soviet armies to launch an offensive from southern Poland across the Czech border towards Ostrava. The offensive met well-prepared and determined German resistance, and Ostrava was not taken until 30 April. The final brief offensive of 38th Army began on 6 May when it was one of more than 20 Soviet armies to launch an offensive against the German Army Group Centre in western Czechoslovakia, the key objective of which was Prague. Against collapsing opposition 38th Army advanced more than 100 kilometres west from the Ostrava area before the final surrender of Army Group Centre on 10 May.<cr><cr>
translation: 第38集团军成立于1941年8月4日，此前在乌克兰西部乌曼地区的大批苏联部队被轴心国军队包围。第38集团军以第8机械化军的兵力和司令部为基础，并纳入了当时驻扎在切尔卡瑟地区的其他苏军单位。该集团军隶属于苏联西南方面军指挥，任务是防御从克列缅丘格到第聂伯河上游的防线。8月12日，乌曼地区苏军投降后，德国军队开始向第聂伯河推进，这一任务变得更加紧迫。<cr>9月12日，德军装甲部队突破了第38集团军的防线并向北进攻，首先到达卢布内，然后到达洛哈夫季察，在那里于9月16日与从罗姆尼向南推进的德军装甲部队会合。由于第六集团军行动缓慢的步兵师，第38集团军轻易避免了被包围的命运。<cr>1月5日，第38集团军右翼对哈尔科夫东北方向德国第六集团军阵地发动攻击，试图推进至别尔哥罗德，但未能掩饰其意图，德军防御准备充分。到一月中旬，西南方面军在哈尔科夫以北的攻势，包括第38集团军的攻势，已经陷入停滞。<cr>1942年冬末春初，哈尔科夫地区的前线相对稳定。1942年春季，苏联最高统帅部准备了一次新的攻势以夺取哈尔科夫。这次进攻于5月12日开始。德国军队在哈尔科夫北部的攻击被击退，在南部则对巴尔文科沃包围圈两侧发起了反击。6月28日上午，德军1942年的主要战略攻势（蓝色方案）从库尔斯克地区向顿河上的沃罗涅日发动进攻。第38集团军的部分部队在米勒诺夫被包围。7月23日，该集团军正式解散。<cr>1942年8月3日，作为苏联战略预备队一部分的第4预备集团军被指定为第38集团军第二编制，并分配给布良斯克方面军。第38集团军于1943年初开始进攻，在3月份战线稳定在库尔斯克突出部周围。7月5日，德国最后一次东线战略攻势（堡垒行动）从北部和南部肩头对库尔斯克突出部发动攻击。<cr>7月12日，苏军开始转入反攻。尽管在7月和8月期间，沃罗涅日方面军部队向东推进，在普塞尔河以西50公里处逼近波尔塔瓦，第38集团军位于普塞尔河另一侧（即沃罗涅日方面军最南端的科雷内沃）的位置几乎没有变化。到9月下旬，第38集团军已越过德斯纳河，并在基辅北部卢切茨地区的第聂伯河上夺取了两个小桥头堡。<cr>1945年3月10日，第38集团军作为三支从南波兰向奥斯特拉发进攻的苏联军队之一，在捷克边境发起攻势。该攻势遭遇了德军顽强且准备充分的抵抗，直到4月30日才攻占奥斯特拉发。<cr>5月6日，第38集团军发起了最后一次短暂攻势，作为超过20支向德国中央集团军群在西捷克斯洛伐克发动进攻的苏联军队之一。其关键目标是布拉格。面对土崩瓦解的抵抗力量，第38集团军从奥斯特拉发地区向西推进了100多公里，直到5月10日中央集团军群最终投降。<cr><cr><cr>

text: The 38th Guards Airborne Corps was formed around 9 August 1944 under the command of Alexander Kapitokhin, part of the Separate Airborne Army. The corps included the 11th, 12th, and 16th Guards Airborne Divisions. On 8 December, the corps became a rifle corps and its divisions were soon converted into infantry divisions. At the same time, the Separate Airborne Army became the 9th Guards Army.<cr>n January 1945, the corps transferred to Hungary with the rest of the 9th Guards Army. The corps first fought in combat on 21 February. On 26 March, Kapitokhin was replaced by Alexander Utvenko in command. It fought during the Vienna Offensive, where its 104th Guards Rifle Division captured Sankt Polten. Its 105th Guards Rifle Division blocked the Vienna-Linz road. For its actions in the Vienna Offensive, the corps was awarded the honorary title 'Vienna'. Advancing on the right flank of the 37th Guards Rifle Corps, the corps entered Czechoslovakia and fought in the Prague Offensive, where the 106th Guards Rifle Division captured Znojmo.<cr><cr>
translation: 第38近卫空降军于1944年8月9日左右在亚历山大·卡皮托金的指挥下组建，隶属于独立空降集团军。该军包括第11、第12和第16近卫空降师。12月8日，该军改编为步兵军，其下的师很快被改组为步兵师。与此同时，独立空降集团军改编为第9近卫集团军。<cr>1945年1月，该军随同第9近卫集团军一起转移到匈牙利。该军首次投入战斗是在2月21日。3月26日，卡皮托金被亚历山大·乌特文科接替指挥权。在维也纳攻势中，其下的第104近卫步兵师占领了圣波尔滕；第105近卫步兵师封锁了维也纳-林茨公路。<cr>由于在维也纳攻势中的表现，该军获得了“维也纳”这一荣誉称号。该军在第37近卫步兵军的右翼推进，在捷克斯洛伐克境内作战，并参加了布拉格攻势，其中第106近卫步兵师占领了兹诺伊莫。<cr>

text: In June 1941 the 38th Rifle Division became part of the 19th Army, formed in the North Caucasus Military District under General Lieutenant Ivan Konev. It was wiped out at Vyazma in October 1941. Recreated at Alma Ata in January 1942, fought at Stalingrad and became 73rd Guards Rifle Division in March 1943. Created again at Kutaisi 4.43, fought on the i>Dnieper River and at Targu Frumos. While with 40th Army, took part in the Battle of Debrecen in October 1944. With 2nd Ukrainian Front May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 1941年6月，第38步兵师成为在北高加索军区组建的第19集团军的一部分，由伊万·科涅夫中将指挥。该师于1941年10月在维亚兹马被消灭。1942年1月在阿拉木图重建后，参加了斯大林格勒战役，并于1943年3月成为第73近卫步兵师。1943年4月再次在库塔伊西组建，参与了第聂伯河的战斗以及塔尔古·弗鲁莫斯的战斗。1944年10月，在与第40集团军一起参加德布勒森战役期间，隶属于第二乌克兰方面军，直至1945年5月。<cr>指 指挥官报告<cr>部队番号：第38步兵师 -> 第73近卫步兵师<cr>所属单位：北高加索军区 -> 第19集团军 -> 斯大林格勒战役 -> 第二乌克兰方面军

text:
The 38th Division was formed February - March 1941 at Borisov in Western Special Military District as part of 20th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
75th Tank Regiment - 2 tank cos with 20 tanks
76th Tank Regiment - 2 tank cos with 20 tanks
38th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
38th Howitzer Regiment - 1 light bn only
38th Reconnaissance Battalion
on foot: no armored cars, no motorcycles, no light tanks<cr><cr>The 38th Tank Division had only about 40 T-26 tanks on hand for training, and had barely even organized most of the division support units: there were no antiaircraft guns, no heavy howitzers, no reconnaissance vehicles, and few trucks or tractors of any kind to move what weapons were on hand. Sucked into the battles around Minsk in June, by 1 July the Soviet command officially listed the division as 'without equipment'. The last division strength report on 7 July showed just 3000 men and 3 howitzers left in the 'division'. By mid- July when the Soviet High Command removed it from the order of battle, the division had already been annihilated in the Minsk pocket.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第38师于1941年2月至3月在明斯克以西的特别军事区波里斯拉夫组建，隶属于第20机械化军，包括：
75坦克团 - 两个坦克营，共20辆坦克
76坦克团 - 两个坦克营，共20辆坦克
第38摩托化步兵团
第一、第二和第三营

第38侦察营
徒步：没有装甲车，没有摩托车，没有轻型坦克<cr>

第38坦克师仅有约40辆T-26坦克用于训练，并且几乎没有组织起大部分支援单位：没有防空炮，没有重型榴弹炮，没有侦察车辆，也没有任何类型的卡车或拖拉机来运输现有的武器。该师被卷入了明斯克周围的战斗，在6月时，苏联指挥官在7月1日的官方记录中将该师列为“无装备”。最后一份关于该师实力的报告于7月7日发布，显示只有3000人和三门榴弹炮留在所谓的“师”内。到7月中旬，当苏联最高指挥部将其从战斗序列中移除时，该师已经在明斯克包围圈中被消灭了。<cr>

查尔斯·C·夏普《苏联战斗序列 第一卷》

text: The 393rd Rifle Division was raised in 1941 as an infantry division of the Red Army, and served twice during WWII in that role. In its first formation the division followed a very similar combat path to that of the 411th Rifle Division. It was first formed on October 1 in the Kharkov Military District, probably on the basis of militia units that had been raised there. It fought in the Barvenkovo-Lozovaya Offensive that created the Izium - Barvenkovo salient in January, 1942 and was intended to play a leading role in a spring offensive aimed at the liberation of Kharkov. In the event a German counteroffensive cut off the salient; the division was deeply encircled and destroyed. In the buildup to the Soviet invasion of Manchuria a new 393rd was formed in the Far Eastern Front in late 1944. The new division fought into the northern part of the Korean peninsula, taking many ports and cities with enough distinction that it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner.<cr><cr>
translation: 第393步兵师于1941年作为红军的一个步兵师组建，并在二战期间两次担任此角色。在其首次编组时，该师的战斗路径与第411步兵师非常相似。它最初于1941年10月1日在哈尔科夫军区成立，可能是基于在那里组建的民兵单位。该师参加了1942年1月的巴尔文科沃-洛佐瓦亚攻势，创建了伊久姆-巴尔文科沃突出部，并被指定在春季攻势中发挥主导作用，旨在解放哈尔科夫。然而，德国反攻切断了这个突出部；该师深陷包围并被消灭。在苏联入侵满洲的集结期间，一个新的第393步兵师于1944年底在远东方面军成立。新编组的师进入了朝鲜半岛北部地区，夺取了许多港口和城市，并因此获得了红旗勋章。<cr><cr>

text: The 39th Army was first formed on 15 November 1941 in the Arkhangelsk Military District, in accordance with a directive issued by the Stavka on 2 November 1941. The army was directly subordinate to the Stavka.<cr>On 1 December 1941 the army was tasked to build defense lines along the eastern bank of the river Sheksna. After regrouping in the area of Torzhok it was sent to the Kalinin Front on 22 December, where the 39th Army took part in the Kalinin Offensive Operation. The Kalinin Offensive Operation had begun on 5 December 1941 and was one part of the Moscow Strategic Counter-Offensive. The army was within the joint sector of the 22nd Army and 29th Army. At the end of December the 39th Army broke through the enemy defenses to a significant depth. During the battles of 2-7 January 1942 the troops on the right wing reached the Volga River and those in the center broke through a new line of defense organized by the enemy on the right bank of the Volga, covering Rzhev from the west and southwest. By the end of the operation on 8 January 1942 the 39th Army had reached the north-west of Rzhev.<cr>The Sychevsk-Vyazma Offensive Operation (8 January-20 April 1942) began immediately and the 39th Army broke through the enemy defenses in a narrow sector, expanding its offensive on Sychevka and providing a corridor through the enemy front for the 29th Army and 11th Cavalry Corps. By the end of January 1942 its troops came to the Vyazma-Smolensk railway on the north of Yartsevo where they met stubborn resistance of the enemy troops. In early February the enemy counter-attacks from Rzhev and Olenino stopped the advance of Soviet troops and the Russian troops on the Kalinin Front were forced into a defensive situation. This resulted in the Kholm-Zhirkovsky ledge being connected to the Kalinin Front by a narrow corridor between Nelidovo and Bely, where the 39th Army faced the threatening situation of having their lines of communication cut by the enemy. The 2nd Shock Army at the Volkhov Front was in a similar situation in the same time.<cr>From February to June 1942 the 39th Army was fighting in the north-west of Vyazma-Kholm-Zhirkovsky in a defensive role. Here the 39th Army engaged in the defense of a salient which contained an enormous enemy forces involved in Operation Seydlitz. The German operation began on 2 July, against the troops of 39th Army and 11th Cavalry Corps, which occupied the Kholm-Zhirkovsky ledge. The Germans attacked at the narrowest part of the corridor, approximately 27-28 km, attacking in the direction of Bely and Olenino. By 6 July, the German troops had closed the corridor and the 39th Army and 11th Cavalry Corps were in encirclement and then dissected into two groups.<cr>On 17 July, around 8,000 troops of the 39th Army, crossed the river Obshu to land on the north bank and occupied the area north of the village Shizderevo. On 18 July, by order of the Kalinin Front commander, the military council of 39th Army with a group of staff officers and the wounded were evacuated in nine Po-2 light aircraft in Andreapol, of which three planes crashed. Battles continued for three weeks while the Germans tried to destroy the encircled groups of the 39th Army. In late July 1942 the individual units were released from the front and, with no troops, the 39th Army was disbanded.<cr><cr>
translation: 第39集团军于1941年11月15日在阿尔汉格尔斯克军区成立，根据最高统帅部在1941年11月2日发布的指令组建。该集团军直接隶属于最高统帅部。<cr>1941年12月1日，第39集团军被命令沿谢克斯纳河东岸建立防御线。重组后于12月22日被派往加里宁方面军，在那里参加了加里宁进攻战役。加里宁进攻战役始于1941年12月5日，是莫斯科战略反攻的一部分。该集团军在第22集团军和第29集团军的联合防区内作战。<cr>到12月底，第39集团军突破了敌方防御线，并深入敌后。在1942年1月2日至7日的战斗中，右翼部队到达伏尔加河，中央部队则突破了敌人在伏尔加河西岸新组织起来的防线，从西南方保护了列别茨克。<cr>到1942年1月8日战役结束时，第39集团军已经推进到了列别茨克西北部。斯切夫斯基-维亚兹马进攻战役（1942年1月8日至4月20日）立即开始，第39集团军在狭窄地带突破了敌方防御，并扩大攻势至斯切夫卡，为第29集团军和第11骑兵军开辟了一条通向敌方防线的走廊。到1942年1月底，其部队抵达雅尔采沃以北的维亚兹马-斯摩棱斯克铁路线，在那里遭遇到顽强抵抗。2月初，敌人从热季韦和奥列宁诺发起反攻，阻止了苏联军队的推进，并迫使加里宁方面军的俄国部队转入防御态势。这导致霍姆-日尔科夫斯基突出部通过内利多沃至别利亚之间的狭窄走廊与加里宁方面军相连，第39集团军面临其补给线被敌人切断的威胁。在同一个时期，沃尔霍夫战区的第2突击集团军也处于类似情况。<cr>从1942年2月到6月，第39集团军在维亚兹马-霍姆-日尔科夫斯基西北部地区进行防御作战。在这里，第39集团军负责保卫一个突出部，该区域集结了大量敌方部队参与塞迪利茨行动。德国人的行动于7月2日开始，针对占据霍姆-日尔科夫斯基突出部的第39集团军和第11骑兵军。德军在走廊最狭窄的部分发起攻击，大约为27至28公里宽，在别利亚和奥列宁诺方向推进。到7月6日，德国军队封闭了走廊，并将第39集团军和第11骑兵军包围并分割成两部分。<cr>7月17日，第39集团军约8000名士兵渡过奥布什河，在北岸登陆并占领了希兹德列沃村以北的地区。7月18日，根据加里宁方面军指挥官的命令，第39集团军军事委员会成员、一组参谋军官和伤员乘坐九架波-2轻型飞机从安德烈亚波尔撤离，其中三架飞机坠毁。战斗持续了三个星期，在此期间德国人试图摧毁被包围的第39集团军部队。1942年7月底，各独立单位离开了前线，由于没有士兵可指挥，第39集团军解散。<cr><cr><cr>

text: The 39th Airborne Corps was formed on 9 August 1944 under the command of Mikhail Tikhonov in Kalinin City. It was converted to infantry on 5 January 1945 and became part of the 9th Guards Army. The corps fought in the Vienna Offensive, where it participated in the capture of Vienna. For his leadership, Tikhonov was awarded the title Hero of the Soviet Union. The corps was also given the honorary title 'Vienna'.<cr><cr>
translation: 第39空降军于1944年8月9日在加里宁市由米哈伊尔·季霍诺夫指挥下组建。该军于1945年1月5日改编为步兵，并成为第9近卫集团军的一部分。该军参加了维也纳攻势，参与了维也纳的占领。由于其领导能力，季霍诺夫被授予苏联英雄称号。该军还获得了“维也纳”这一荣誉称谓。<cr><cr>

text: The 39th Guards Rifle Division was formed as part of the 62nd Army and assigned to the defense of Stalingrad, officially arriving in the theater in August 1942. In September the division fought through German forces which were attempting to encircle the city, and was assigned to defend the 'Volga Corridor,' the last supply line remaining for Soviet units in the city.<cr>From September 30, 1942, the division, which could muster only roughly half its original strength, was assigned to defend the Red October steel works. From that date until February 2, 1943, the division was involved in almost constant combat with numerically superior German forces.<cr>Following the victory at Stalingrad the remnants of the 62nd Army, including the 39th Guards, was placed in reserve and became the basis for the newly formed 8th Guards Army, receiving the honorific 'Guards' in honor of their heroic defense of Stalingrad. The army was placed under the command of Lieutenant General Vasily Chuikov. Through 1943 the 8th Guards Army fought across Ukraine, crossing the North Donets River, establishing a bridgehead south of Isyum, and in cooperation with adjacent armies, advanced on the Don Basin and ultimately liberated it. They fought across the Don, through Dnepropetrovsk, continuing to Zaporozhe, and participated in the fighting on the Zaporozhe bridgehead across the Dnepr on October 10-14.<cr>The division turned south and fought for the liberation of Nikolayev in March 1944, and liberated Odessa in April. Turning north into Moldavia the division liberated Kovel before participating in the Lovov-Sandomir Operation, which began on July 13 and lasted until August 29. On July 20, they crossed the Bug River and crossed into Poland. On July 24, the 39th Guards liberated Lublin and continued to advance on Warsaw, establishing a major bridgehead on the Vistula River which was the key for the Soviet advance towards Silesia, central Poland and the German border. They encountered furious counterattacks by German units, with the 8th Army losing 17,000 men in the process.<cr>On January 12, the 39th Guards participated in the Vistula-Oder Offensive, which lasted 23 days and saw the division advance 500 km through Poland. They crushed the German defenders as they liberated the towns of Lodz and Posnan, finally arriving at the Oder River just north of Frankfurt on February 3. They stormed the Kustrin Fortress and established a bridgehead over the Oder, within 60 km of Berlin. They attacked the city from the east, pushing through the area of Karlshorst, across Tempelhof Airport and Landwehr Canal, destroying the 11th SS Volunteer Panzergrenadier Division Nordland and then the 17th Panzer Division just south of the Reichstag.<cr>The 39th Guards Rifle Division pushed north and fought through the Tiergarten, ending their war along Charlottenburger Chaussee at the Brandenburg Gate, meeting units from the 207th and 150th Rifle Divisions just 250 yards from the Reichstag. The final banner of the division, which had served from the center of Stalingrad to the center of Berlin, read: '39th Barvenkovskikh Guards Order of Lenin, Twice Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov Second Class and Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky Second Class Rifle Division.'<cr><cr>
translation: 第39近卫步兵师作为第62集团军的一部分组建，并被分配到斯大林格勒的防御，于1942年8月正式进入战区。9月份，该师与试图包围城市的德军作战，并被分配保卫“伏尔加走廊”，这是苏联部队在城市中剩余的最后一条补给线。<cr>从1942年9月30日起，该师仅能集结其原始实力的大约一半兵力，被分配到保卫红色十月钢铁厂的任务。从那天起直到1943年2月2日，该师几乎一直在与数量上占优势的德军进行战斗。<cr>在斯大林格勒战役胜利后，第62集团军的残部（包括第39近卫步兵师）被置于预备队，并成为新组建的第8近卫集团军的基础。该集团军获得了“近卫”的荣誉称号以表彰其对斯大林格勒英勇的防御。<cr>该集团军由副将瓦西里·丘伊科夫指挥。1943年，第8近卫集团军在乌克兰作战，渡过了北顿涅茨河，在伊斯尤姆以南建立了桥头堡，并与相邻部队合作，向顿河流域推进并最终解放了该地区。他们穿越顿河，经过第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克，继续前往扎波罗热，并参与了10月10日至14日在扎波罗热的第聂伯河桥头堡的战斗。<cr>该师于1944年3月向南进攻，参与尼古拉耶夫的解放战役，并在4月解放了敖德萨。随后进入摩尔多瓦北部，解放科韦利并参加洛沃夫-桑多米尔行动，该行动从7月13日持续至8月29日。7月20日，他们渡过布格河进入波兰境内。7月24日，第39近卫师解放了卢布林，并继续向华沙推进，在维斯瓦河上建立了重要桥头堡，这是苏联向西里西亚、波兰中部和德国边境推进的关键。在此过程中，德军进行了激烈的反攻，其中第8集团军损失17000人。<cr>1945年1月12日，第39近卫师参加了维斯瓦-奥得河攻势，该行动持续了23天，期间该师在波兰境内推进了500公里。他们摧毁了德军的防御，并解放了洛兹和波兹南等城镇，最终于2月3日抵达奥得河畔法兰克福以北地区。他们攻占库斯特林要塞并在奥得河上建立了桥头堡，距离柏林仅60公里处。从东面进攻该城市，穿过卡尔施托夫区、滕珀尔霍夫机场和兰德韦尔运河，并摧毁了第11志愿党卫军装甲掷弹兵师北方和第17装甲师，后者位于国会大厦以南地区。<cr>第39近卫步兵师向北推进，穿越蒂尔加滕公园，在勃兰登堡门附近的夏洛腾堡大街结束了他们的战斗。他们与来自第207和第150步兵师的部队会合，距离国会大厦仅250码。该师的最后一面旗帜上写着：“第39巴文科夫斯基近卫列宁勋章、两次红旗勋章、苏沃洛夫二级勋章和博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基二级勋章步兵师”。<cr><cr>

text:
The 39th Tank Division was formed March- April 1941 near Chernovitz in Kiev Special Military District as part of 16th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
77th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns
78th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns
39th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
39th Howitzer Regiment
1 light, 1 medium bn
39th Reconnaissance Battalion
39th Pontoon Battalion
39th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr>
The 39th Tank Division had only about 280 light tanks on hand on 22 June, and was short overall about 1/3 of its authorized trucks and tractors. Luckily, 16th Mechanized Corps was not in the line of the major German panzer thrusts, and the corps survived as part of South Front. 39th Tank Division fought with Southern Front, retreating back through the Donbas. By August the division was assigned to 18th Army as a mobile reserve after 16th mechanized Corps HQ was disbanded. In mid-August the division was dissolved; parts of it formed separate tank battalions in the 18th Army Tank Group.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: The 3rd Air Army was formed May 16, 1942, in accordance with a People's Commissariat for Defence order of 5 May 1942, within the Kalinin Front.<cr>The formation started combat operations in July 1942 during a defensive operation in the town of Bely, Tver Oblast, then participated in Rzhev-Sychevskaya and in the Luki operation. In February 1943 a number of its formations supported the troops of the Northwestern Front in the liquidation of the Demyansk pocket. It participated in the Smolensk, Nevel, Gorodok, Vitebsk, Belarusian and the Baltic Offensives. In February 1945, it became operational command for the 1st Air Army, 3rd Belorussian Fronts and participated in the East Prussian Offensive. On 5 May 1945 it was transferred to the operational command of the Leningrad Front and with 15th Air Army took part in the blockade of German forces in the Courland Pocket.<cr><cr>
translation: 第3空军集团军于1942年5月16日根据人民国防委员会1942年5月5日的命令在加里宁方面军内组建。<cr>该部队从1942年7月开始参加防御作战，地点是特维尔州白利镇，随后参加了热季夫-斯奇耶夫斯卡亚和卢基战役。1943年2月，其部分部队支援了西北方面军在德梅扬斯克包围圈的清剿行动。该部队还参与了斯摩棱斯克、涅韦尔、戈罗多克、维捷布斯克、白俄罗斯和波罗的海攻势。<cr>1945年2月，它成为第1空军集团军和第3白俄罗斯方面军的作战指挥，并参加了东普鲁士进攻。1945年5月5日，该部队被转移到列宁格勒方面军的作战指挥下，并与第15空军集团军一起参与了库尔兰包围圈内德军的封锁行动。<cr>指挥官报告：第3空军集团军在多次重要战役中发挥了关键作用。

text: The corps was formed in April 1941 and consisted of 5th, 6th and 212th Airborne Brigades. It was assigned to 9th Army in the Odessa region at the outbreak of hostilities. In August, the corps fought in the the Kiev pocket and escaped with heavy losses. It fought in September-November 1941 in the vicinity of Konotop. In November 1941, it was converted into the 87th Rifle Division, which then became the 13th Guards Rifle division of Stalingrad fame. Hero of the Soviet Union Alexander Rodimtsev was commander of 5th Airborne Brigade and became commander of the corps during the Konotop fighting. <cr><cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军成立于1941年4月，由第5、第6和第212空降旅组成。在战争爆发时被分配到敖德萨地区的第9集团军。8月份，该军在基辅包围圈作战，并遭受了重大损失后逃脱。1941年9月至11月期间，在科诺托普附近作战。1941年11月，该军改编为第87步兵师，随后成为著名的斯大林格勒战役中的第13近卫步兵师。苏联英雄亚历山大·罗季姆采夫曾指挥第5空降旅，并在科诺托普战斗期间担任该军的指挥官。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军战斗序列：伟大卫国战争，Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: After the start of Operation Barbarossa, the 3rd Army included three corps, the 4th Rifle Corps (17th, 56th, and 85th Rifle Divisions), the 21st Rifle Corps (17th, 24th, 37th and 50th Rifle Divisions) and 11th Mechanized Corps (29th and 33rd Tank Division and 204th Motorised Division).<cr>The 3rd Army took part in the operations of the Western, Central, Bryansk, First, Second, and Third Belorussian Fronts during the defenses of Grodno, Lida, and Novogrudok.<cr>The 3rd Army also took part in the Battle of Smolensk, where German troops captured the city in a difficult two-month campaign, and the Battle of Moscow, in which the Red Army's winter counter-attack led by Marshal Georgy Zhukov drove back Army Group Center over 70 miles (110 km) away from Moscow. The 3rd Army took part in the Battle of Kursk, where numerically superior Soviet forces, using good anti-tank defenses, defeated the German forces, thus stopping Operation Zitadelle and robbing the German Army of all hopes of victory on the Eastern Front. The 3rd Army took part in the Bryansk, Gomel - Rechitsa, and Rogachev - Zhlobin operations. During the final phases of the war, the 3rd Army took part in the attacks on Belarus, East Prussia, and eastern Germany, where it participated in the Battle of Berlin.<cr><cr>
translation: 巴巴罗萨行动开始后，第3集团军包括三个军：第4步兵军（第17、56和85步兵师）、第21步兵军（第17、24、37和50步兵师）以及第11机械化军（第29和33坦克师及第204摩托化师）。<cr>第3集团军参加了西方、中央、布良斯克、第一、第二和第三白俄罗斯方面军在格罗德诺、利达和诺夫哥罗德防御战中的行动。<cr>第3集团军还参与了斯摩棱斯克战役，在这场艰难的两个月战役中，德国军队占领了这座城市；以及莫斯科战役，在这次冬季反攻中，由朱可夫元帅领导的红军将中央集团军群击退70英里（110公里），使其远离莫斯科。第3集团军参加了库尔斯克会战，在这场战斗中，数量占优的苏军利用良好的反坦克防御击败了德军，从而阻止了“要塞”行动，并剥夺了德国陆军在东线取得胜利的所有希望。第3集团军还参与了布良斯克、戈梅利-列奇察和罗加乔夫-日洛宾等战役。在战争的最后阶段，第3集团军参加了对白俄罗斯、东普鲁士以及东部德国的攻击行动，并且参与了柏林会战。<cr><cr>

text: The 3rd Baltic Front was set up on 21 April 1944 and disbanded on 16 October that year after a series of campaigns in the Baltic states that culminated with the capture of Riga October 13-15, 1944. During 179 days of existence, the 3rd Baltic Front suffered 43,155 killed and missing in action as well as 153,876 wounded, sick, and frostbitten personnel. The sole commander of the 3rd Baltic Front was Ivan Maslennikov.<cr><cr>The headquarters of the 3rd Baltic Front was formed from that of the disbanded 20th Army, and the field armies subordinated to the front were taken from the left (south) wing of the Leningrad Front. Operations that the 3rd Baltic Front took part in include the Pskov-Ostrov Operation and the Tartu Operation. Upon the capture of Riga, the Soviet high command disbanded the 3rd Baltic Front as a headquarters and reassigned its component armies.<cr><cr>Wikipedia 3rd Baltic Front
translation: 第3方面军（波罗的海）于1944年4月21日建立，同年10月16日解散。在此期间，该方面军参与了在波罗的海国家进行的一系列战役，并最终于1944年10月13日至15日占领里加。<cr><cr>第3方面军（波罗的海）存在了179天，在此期间共有43,155人阵亡和失踪，另有153,876人受伤、患病或冻伤。该方面军唯一的指挥官是伊万·马斯连尼科夫。<cr><cr>第3方面军（波罗的海）司令部由解散的第20集团军司令部组建而成，下辖野战集团军则来自列宁格勒方面军左翼（南翼）。该方面军参与了普斯科夫-奥斯特罗夫行动和塔尔图行动。<cr><cr>占领里加后，苏联最高统帅部解散了第3方面军司令部，并重新分配其下辖集团军。

text: The 3rd Belorussian Front was created on April 24, 1944, from forces previously assigned to the Western Front. Over 381 days in combat, the 3rd Belorussian Front suffered 166,838 killed, 9,292 missing, and 667,297 wounded, sick, and frostbitten personnel while advancing from the region some 50 kilometers southeast of Vitebsk in Russia to Knigsberg in East Prussia.<cr>Operations the 3rd Belorussian Front took part in include the Belorussian Offensive, the Baltic Offensive, and the East Prussian Offensive. Although costly, the advance of the 3rd Belorussian Front was in great part victorious, with one of the few defeats occurring during the Gumbinnen Operation in October 1944.<cr>3rd Belorussian Front was formally disbanded on August 15, 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第3白俄罗斯方面军于1944年4月24日从此前隶属于西方方面军的部队中组建。在超过381天的战斗中，该方面军从位于俄罗斯维捷布斯克东南约50公里处的地区推进至东普鲁士柯尼斯堡，阵亡人数达166,838人，失踪9,292人，受伤、患病及冻伤人员共667,297人。<cr>第3白俄罗斯方面军参与了白俄罗斯进攻战役、波罗的海进攻战役和东普鲁士进攻战役。尽管代价高昂，但该方面军的推进在很大程度上取得了胜利，在1944年10月的贡宾嫩行动中遭受的一次少数失败除外。<cr>第3白俄罗斯方面军于1945年8月15日正式解散。<cr><cr>

text:
The 3rd Guards Airborne Division was formed on 8 December 1942 after the disbanding of the 8th Airborne Corps. The division was placed under the 1st Shock Army on 6 February 1943 for the attack on the Demyansk Pocket. When the attack began on 26 February, the attached tanks of the 37th Separate Tank Regiment became bogged down in the snow, and German resistance slowed the advance. The division captured Sosnovka by 5 March and was on the eastern bank of the Porus River on 11 March. 

As part of the 13th Army and 60th Army, the 3rd Guards Airborne fought in the Battle of Kursk and the Chernigov-Pripyat Offensive. On 9 September, the division captured Bakhmach. After capturing Oster, the division crossed the Desna River and fought to expand the bridgehead on the right bank of the Dnieper to Hornostaipil.

The division fought in the Battle of Kiev, capturing Dymer, Radomyshl and Korostyshiv. In November and December 1943, the 3rd Guards Airborne thwarted German counterattacks in the Kiev defensive operation. It then fought in the Zhitomir-Berdichev Offensive. In January and February 1944, the division fought in the Battle of the Korsun-Cherkassy Pocket. On 3 March 1944, the division became part of the 35th Guards Rifle Corps of the 27th Army. Three days later, the division crossed the Hirsky Tikych, which allowed the capture of Khrystynivka and Uman, for which it was given the title Uman.

Fighting in the Uman-Botosani Offensive, the division crossed the Southern Bug, the Dniester and the Prut, capturing Trostianets, Ladyzhyn, Tulchyn and Mohyliv-Podilskyi. On 26 March, the division reached the Prut after capturing Edinet on the Romanian border. For its performance in crossing of the Dniester and the Prut, the division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner and the Order of Suvorov 2nd class. The division crossed the Siret River at Pascani and held the bridgehead against counterattacks. After the end of the offensive, the division rested before the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive. On 20 August, the division attacked in the direction of Bacau, Vaslui and Husi, seeking to destroy Army Group South Ukraine.

In the Battle of Debrecen, the 3rd Guards Airborne captured Cluj-Napoca and entered Hungary. On the night of 7 November, the division crossed the Tisza and took Fzesabony on 11 November. In conjunction with the 110th Guards Rifle Division, the division captured Eger on 30 November. Moving westward, the division entered Czechoslovakia on 1 January 1945. The division stopped counterattacks during the Siege of Budapest. In March 1945, the division repelled Operation Spring Awakening. After assisting the 4th Guards Army in the capture of Szekesfehervar on 22 March. Days later, the division entered Austria at Frstenfeld. The division entered Graz on 9 May at the end of the war and met British troops on the Mur at Bruck an der Mur.<cr><cr>
translation:
第3近卫空降师成立于1942年12月8日，是在解散了第8空降军之后组建的。该师于1943年2月6日被编入第1突击集团军，参加对德梅耶斯克包围圈的攻击行动。当进攻于2月26日开始时，附属于该师的第37独立坦克团的坦克在雪地中陷入困境，德国人的抵抗减缓了推进速度。到3月5日，该师占领了索斯诺夫卡，并于3月11日抵达普鲁斯河东岸。 

作为第13集团军和第60集团军的一部分，第3近卫空降师参加了库尔斯克战役和切尔尼戈夫-普里皮亚季进攻。9月9日，该师占领了巴赫马奇。在占领奥斯特之后，该师渡过了德斯纳河，并为扩大第聂伯河右岸霍诺斯塔皮尔的桥头堡而战斗。

该师参加了基辅战役，占领了迪梅尔、拉多米什利和科罗斯季希维。1943年11月和12月，在基辅防御作战中，第3近卫空降师挫败了德军的反攻。随后，该师参加了日托米尔-别列斯切夫进攻战役。1944年1月和2月，该师参加了科尔松-切尔卡瑟包围圈战役。<cr><cr>1944年3月3日，该师成为第35近卫步兵军（隶属于第27集团军）的一部分。三天后，该师渡过了希尔斯基季奇河，占领了赫里斯蒂尼夫卡和乌曼，并因此获得了“乌曼”荣誉称号。

在乌曼-波托萨尼攻势中，该师穿越了南布格河、德涅斯特河和普鲁特河，占领了特罗斯蒂亚内茨、拉季日恩、图尔钦和莫吉列夫-波迪利斯基。3月26日，该师在夺取罗马尼亚边境上的埃德内特后抵达普鲁特河。由于成功穿越德涅斯特河和普鲁特河的表现，该师被授予红旗勋章和苏沃洛夫二级勋章。该师在帕斯卡尼渡过了西雷特河，并坚守桥头堡以抵御反攻。攻势结束后，该师休整后参加了雅西-奇什利纳攻势。8月20日，该师向巴恰乌、瓦斯柳和胡希方向发起进攻，旨在消灭南方乌克兰集团军群。

在德布勒森战役中，第3近卫空降师占领了克卢日-纳波卡并进入匈牙利。11月7日晚上，该师渡过蒂萨河，并于11月11日攻占费泽什鲍尼。与第110近卫步兵师协同作战，该师在11月30日占领了埃格尔。向西推进后，该师于1945年1月1日进入捷克斯洛伐克。在布达佩斯围城战期间，该师阻止了反攻。1945年3月，该师击退了“春季觉醒”行动。协助第4近卫集团军占领了塞凯什费赫尔瓦尔后，几天内该师进入奥地利的弗赖堡。在战争结束时，该师于5月9日进入格拉茨，并在穆尔河畔布鲁克与英军会合。<cr><cr>至<cr>

text: The 3rd Guards Army was formed on December 5, 1942 by the redesignation of the 1st Guards Army (Second formation), in accordance with a Stavka order dated the same day, as part of the Southwestern Front. Lieutenant General Dmitry Lelyushenko was appointed to command the formation, and held the reins until March 1943 (and subsequently from August 1943 to February 1944). Up to the middle of December the army comprised the 14th Rifle Corps, 50th Guards, 197th, 203rd and 278th Rifle Divisions, 90th and 94th Separate Rifle Brigades, the 1st Guards Mechanized Corps, the 22nd Motor Rifle Brigade and three separate tank regiments. It began combat operations during Operation Little Saturn in mid-December, defeating German troops on the Middle Don and frustrating Operation Winter Storm, a German attempt to relieve the 6th Army trapped in the Stalingrad Pocket created by the Soviet counteroffensive in the Battle of Stalingrad, Operation Uranus. During January and February 1943, it fought in the Operation Gallop, then defended the line of the Donets. Major General Georgy Khetagurov held command from March to August.<cr>In the summer and fall, the 3rd Guards Army fought in the Donbass Strategic Offensive, then in the Zaporizhia Offensive in October. During the latter, the army broke through heavily fortified German defenses and captured Zaporizhia alongside the 8th Guards Army on October 14, eliminating a German bridgehead on the left bank of the Dnieper. Towards the end of the year, the army joined the 4th Ukrainian Front, participating in fierce fighting to eliminate the Nikopol bridgehead. During the NikopolKrivoi Rog Offensive in January and February 1944, the army crossed the Dnieper and captured Nikopol alongside the 3rd Ukrainian Front's 6th Army on February 8.<cr>3rd Guards Army was assigned in succession to the Soviet Southwestern Front, 3rd, 4th and since March 1944 the First Ukrainian Front led by Marshal Ivan Konev. After a brief stint under the command of Lieutenant General Dmitry Ryabyshev in February and March 1944, from April 1944 to the end of the war in Europe Colonel General Vasily Gordov was in command. The Army participated in the Middle Don and Voroshilovgrad offensive operations, the defensive battles on the northern Donets River, in the Donbass and Zaporozhye offensive operations, in the liquidation of the Germans' Nikopol bridgehead, in the Nikopol - Krivoi Rog and Proskurov-Chernovits operations, the Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive, the Sandomierz-Silesian Offensive, and the Battle of Berlin.<cr><cr>
translation: 第三近卫集团军成立于1942年12月5日，根据最高统帅部大本营当天的命令，由第一近卫集团军（第二次组建）改编而成，隶属于西南方面军。副司令员德米特里·列柳申科被任命为该集团军指挥官，并一直担任此职直到1943年3月（随后从8月至次年2月再次任职）。截至12月中旬，该集团军包括第14步兵军、第50近卫师、第197师、第203师和第278师、第90独立步兵旅和第94独立步兵旅、第一近卫机械化军、第二十二摩托化步兵旅以及三个独立坦克团。该集团军在“土星行动”中期开始作战，击败了中顿河地区的德军，并挫败了德军试图通过“冬季风暴行动”解救被围困于斯大林格勒包围圈内的第六集团军的企图。“冬季风暴行动”是德军对苏军反攻（天王星行动）所造成的后果。1943年1月至2月，该集团军参加了“疾驰行动”，随后在顿涅茨河沿线进行了防御作战。从3月至8月，乔治·赫塔古罗夫少将担任指挥官。<cr>夏季和秋季，第三近卫集团军参与了顿巴斯战略进攻，并于10月参加了扎波罗热攻势，在此次行动中突破了德军坚固的防线并占领了扎波罗热，与第八近卫集团军一起消灭了左岸第聂伯河上的德军桥头堡。年末时，该集团军加入了第四乌克兰方面军，参与激烈战斗以消除尼科波尔桥头堡。1944年1月至2月，在“尼科波尔—克里沃罗格攻势”中，该集团军渡过第聂伯河并与第三乌克兰方面军的第六集团军一起占领了尼科波尔，时间为2月8日。<cr>第三近卫集团军先后被分配到苏联西南方面军、第3方面军、第4方面军，以及自1944年3月起由元帅伊万·科涅夫领导的第一乌克兰方面军。在1944年2月至3月期间短暂隶属于少将德米特里·利亚比谢夫指挥后，从1944年4月至欧洲战争结束，集团军一直由上将瓦西里·戈尔多夫指挥。该集团军参与了中顿河和沃罗希洛夫格勒进攻行动、北部顿涅茨河防御战、顿巴斯和扎波罗热进攻行动、消灭德国尼科波尔桥头堡的作战，以及尼科波尔-克里沃罗格和普罗斯库罗夫-切尔诺维策战役、利沃夫-桑多梅日攻势、桑多梅日-西里西亚攻势和柏林之战。<cr><cr>

text: Formed 11/26/1941 from 50th Cavalry Division as part of II Guards Cavalry Corps. As part of Western Front Reserve, the division participated in the Battle of Moscow in December 1941. Remained in 1st Belorussian Front until the end of the war. <cr><cr>Pettibone, Charles D., The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II: volume V - Book B Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Trafford, 2009<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 1941年11月26日，该师由第50骑兵师改编而成，并隶属于第二近卫骑兵军。作为西方方面军预备队的一部分，该师参加了1941年12月的莫斯科战役。直至战争结束，该师一直隶属于第一白俄罗斯方面军。<cr>资料来源：Pettibone, Charles D., 《第二次世界大战中军事组织与战斗序列：卷V - 书B 苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟》，Trafford, 2009<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: On September 18, 1941, by the Order #308 of the People's Commissar of Defense, the 153rd Rifle Division was renamed the 3rd Guards Rifle Division.<cr>From September 20 to November 9, 1941, the division led military operations as a part of the 54th Army of the Leningrad Front in the area of Mga and Sinyavino. From November 10 to 14, 1941, the division relocated to the left flank of the army, south of the city of Volkhov. From November 15 to December 28, 1941, the division conducted combat operations near Volkhov and then pursued the enemy to the station of Pogostye.<cr>In summer 1942, the division added staff, and then was made a part of the Stavka reserve.<cr>At the end of August - September 1942, the division took part in the Sinyavino Offensive of the Volkhov Front.<cr>In early December 1942, the division was withdrawn from the Stavka reserve and transferred under the 2nd Guards Army of the Stalingrad Front. During winter 1942, the division completed a difficult forced march, passing 200 to 280 km from the discharge point to the assembly areas. From December 15 to 31, 1942, the division engaged in active combat operations near Stalingrad.<cr>During the Stalingrad strategic offensive, on the threshold of the Myshkova River, the division, as a part of the 2nd Guards Army, played a decisive role in repelling the enemy's Kotelnikovo group attack, and on December 24 it started the offensive itself and forced the enemy to withdraw to the south. Continuing the offensive toward Rostov, the troops of the 2nd Guards Army liberated Novocherkassk on February 13, 1943, and three days later reached the Mius River, where the enemy's resistance forced them to take defensive positions.<cr>In AugustSeptember 1943, the 3rd Guards Division took part in the Donbass strategic offensive operation. The division liberated the inhabited localities of Bolshoy Tokmak (on September 20, 1943) and Volnovakha (on September 10, 1943). By the order of VGK, the 3rd Guards Rifle Division (as well as 11th Guards Cavalry Division, 5th Motor Rifle Division, and 12th Motor Rifle Division, 5th and 12th Guards Motorized Brigades, 5th and 6th Guards Motorized Brigades, and 65th Tank Brigade) was named 'Volnovakha'.<cr>In late September, during the Melitopol Offensive, the divisional forces reached the lower course of the Dnieper and liberated Kakhovka on the coast of the Black Sea (on 2 November 1943). In December, as a part of the 4th Ukrainian Front, the divisional forces eliminated the enemy's foothold on the left bank of the Dnieper (in the area of Kherson) after a stubborn battle. In February 1944, the army was transferred to the area of Perekop isthmus, and in April-May it took part in the Crimean strategic operation, resulting in the liberation of Yevpatoriya on April 13, 1944, and, together with other forces of the 4th Ukrainian Front and the Black Sea Fleet, Sevastopol on May 9. In May-June, the 2nd Guards Army was relocated to the area of cities of Dorogobuzh and Yelnya. From May 20, it was in the Stavka reserve, and on July 8 it was included in the 1st Baltic Front. In July, during the Siauliai Offensive, the division countered the enemy's strikes to the west and northwest of Siauliai. In October, it participated in the Memel Offensive. On December 20, it was reassigned to the 3rd Belorussian Front. In January-April 1945, during the East Prussian Offensive, it broke the long-term defenses and eliminated, in conjunction with other troops, encircled German forces southwest of Koenigsberg and the Sambia group.<cr><cr>
translation: 1941年9月18日，根据国防人民委员部第308号命令，第153步兵师被改名为第3师近卫步兵师。从1941年9月20日至11月9日，该师作为列宁格勒方面军第54集团军的一部分，在梅加和辛亚维诺地区进行军事行动。<cr>从1941年11月10日至14日，该师转移到了集团军左翼的沃洛赫夫城南部。从1941年11月15日至12月28日，该师在沃洛赫夫附近进行战斗行动，并追击敌人至波戈斯季车站。<cr>1942年夏季，该师增加了人员编制，并被纳入最高统帅部预备队。<cr>1942年8月底至9月初，该师参加了沃尔霍夫方面军的辛亚维诺攻势。<cr>1942年12月初，该师从最高统帅部预备队中撤出并转隶斯大林格勒方面军第2近卫集团军。在1942年的冬季，该师完成了艰难的强行军，行进距离为200至280公里。<cr>从1942年12月15日至31日，该师在斯大林格勒附近进行积极战斗行动。<cr>在斯大林格勒战略进攻中，在米什科沃河的入口处，作为第2近卫集团军的一部分，该师在抵御敌人的科捷利尼科沃集团攻击时发挥了决定性作用，并于1942年12月24日开始了自己的攻势，迫使敌人向南撤退。继续进攻至罗斯托夫期间，第2近卫集团军的部队解放了诺沃切尔卡斯克并于1943年2月13日到达米乌斯河，在敌人的抵抗下被迫采取防御态势。<cr>1943年8月至9月，第3近卫步兵师参加了顿巴斯战略进攻作战。该师解放了博尔什科伊托克马克（1943年9月20日）和沃洛诺瓦赫（1943年9月10日）等居民点。根据苏联国防委员会的命令，第3近卫步兵师（以及第11近卫骑兵师、第5机械化师、第12机械化师、第5和第12近卫机械化旅、第5和第6机械化旅，以及第65坦克旅）被命名为“沃洛诺瓦赫”<cr>。九月下旬，在梅利托波尔进攻中，师级部队抵达第聂伯河下游地区，并于1943年11月2日解放了黑海沿岸的卡霍夫卡。十二月，作为第四乌克兰方面军的一部分，师级部队在赫尔松附近与敌人的顽强战斗后清除了左岸第聂伯河上的敌人立足点。1944年二月，集团军被转移到佩雷科普地峡地区，在四月至五月期间参加了克里米亚战略行动，解放了叶夫帕托里亚（1944年4月13日），并与第四乌克兰方面军和其他部队以及黑海舰队一起解放了塞瓦斯托波尔（5月9日）。五月至六月间，第二近卫集团军被转移到多罗戈布日和耶尔尼亚市地区。自五月二十日起，该集团军处于最高统帅部预备队中，并于七月八日加入波罗的海第一方面军。七月份，在希奥利艾进攻期间，师在希奥利艾西面和西北面对抗敌人的打击。十月间，参加了梅梅尔进攻。十二月二十日，被重新分配到第三白俄罗斯方面军。1945年一月至四月期间，在东普鲁士进攻中突破了长期防御，并与其它部队协同作战，消灭了科尼斯堡西南部和萨姆比亚地区的包围德军。

text: The Third Tank Army was reformed as the 3rd Guards Tank Army in May 1943, including the 9th Mechanized Corps & 12th & 15th Tank Corps. In 1943, the army took part in the Orel offensive and, assigned to the Voronezh and 1st Ukrainian Fronts, played a leading role in the liberation of Left Bank Ukraine. During the Orel offensive the 12th and 15th Tank Corps became the 6th and 7th Guards Tank Corps, respectively. The army was among the first Soviet troops to reach the Dnieper River in October 1943. In 1944, it fought in the Proskurov-Chernovits and Lvov-Sandomierzoffensive operations. The army subsequently fought in southern Poland, Silesia, and in the Battle of Berlin. It overran the OKH command post at Zossen, headquarters for German Eastern Front operations, on April 21, 1945. Finally, the army drove on Prague, entering that city on May 9.<cr><cr>
translation: 第三坦克集团军于1943年5月重组为近卫第三坦克集团军，包括第9机械化军、第12坦克军和第15坦克军。1943年，该集团军参加了奥廖尔攻势，并被分配给沃罗涅日方面军和第一乌克兰方面军，在解放左岸乌克兰的行动中发挥了主导作用。在奥廖尔攻势期间，第12坦克军和第15坦克军分别改编为近卫第六坦克军和近卫第七坦克军。该集团军是第一批于1943年10月到达第聂伯河的苏联部队之一。1944年，它参加了普罗斯库罗夫-切尔诺维茨攻势和利沃夫-桑多梅日攻势。随后，该集团军在波兰南部、西里西亚作战，并参与了柏林战役。1945年4月21日，该集团军攻占了位于佐森的德国陆军总司令部（Oberkommando des Heeres）指挥所，这是东线德军行动的总部。<cr>最后，该集团军向布拉格推进，在1945年5月9日进入该城。<cr> <cr>
