text: On 5 April 1941, the Hungarian Third Army was mobilized for the invasion of Yugoslavia. The invasion began with the bombing of Belgrade and the crossing of the border by the Germans on 6 April.<cr>The Third Army faced the Yugosalvian First Army. By the time the Hungarians crossed the border and finally attacked, the Germans had been attacking Yugoslavia for over a week. As a result, the Yugoslavs put up little resistance to the Hungarians. Units of the Hungarian Third Army advanced into a triangular shaped area known as the Baranya-triangle between the Danube River and the Drava River. The Hungarians suffered few casualties in this invasion. As a result of participating in the invasion of Yugoslavia, Hungary regained Bcska and Baranya.<cr>On 30 August, the Hungarian Third Army was mobilized to defend Hungary against the relentless advances of the Soviet 2nd and 4th Ukrainian Fronts. The Chief of Staff of the Hungarian Armed Forces, Colonel-General Jnos Vrs, ordered this army of nine weak, undermanned, and underequipped reserve divisions to attack west of the Hungarian Second Army (which was mobilized at the same time). The Third Army was to then cross Arad and the Maros Valley and occupy the mountain passes of Transylvania. This attack failed.<cr>On 6 October, in the opening stages of the Battle of Debrecen, the Hungarian Third Army was badly mauled near Arad. Very quickly, the army was scattered near the town of Kecskemt. Rodion Malinovsky's 2nd Ukrainian Front attempted a pincer maneuver to encircle Army Group Fretter-Pico. The 2nd Ukrainian Front's southern pincer sliced easily through the Hungarian Third Army. This southern pincer was spearheaded by Soviet General Issa Pliyev's Mobile Group Pliyev. Later, in the same battle, Mobile Group Pliyev was encircled and badly mauled by Army Group Fretter-Pico (Armeegruppe Fretter-Pico). The northern pincer was stalled and turned back by veteran German panzer forces. The Hungarian Second Army was an integral part of the victorious German-Hungarian Armeegruppe Fretter-Pico.<cr>From 29 December 1944, the Hungarian capital city, Budapest was under siege. In the Battle of Budapest every available Hungarian unit was employed in the defense of the capital. After great loss, the city was unconditionally surrendered on 13 February 1945.<cr>Between 16 March and 25 March 1945, most of what was left of the Hungarian Third Army was surrounded and destroyed about forty kilometers to the west of Budapest. The army was destroyed by the Soviet 46th Army as it advanced towards Vienna. But, even after this, the Hungarian Third Army did not totally cease to exist. Some remnants remained and they fought on. Fighting as they went, they moved progressively westward to southern Austria. The army was not officially disbanded until 8 May 1945, the end of the war. That is when the last commander of the Hungarian Third Army, Lieutenant General Jzsef Heszlnyi, surrendered.<cr><cr>
translation: 1941年4月5日，匈牙利第三集团军动员参加入侵南斯拉夫的行动。入侵始于贝尔格莱德被轰炸以及德国军队于4月6日越过边境。<cr>第三集团军面对的是南斯拉夫第一集团军。当匈牙利部队越境并最终发起攻击时，德国人已经对南斯拉夫进行了超过一周的进攻。因此，南斯拉夫人对匈牙利人的抵抗微乎其微。匈牙利第三集团军的部分单位推进到一个三角形区域——位于多瑙河和德拉瓦河之间的巴拉尼亚三角区。<cr>在这次入侵中，匈牙利遭受了很少的伤亡。由于参与了入侵南斯拉夫，匈牙利重新获得了巴奇-开瑟和巴拉尼亚。<cr>8月30日，匈牙利第三集团军动员起来，以防御苏联第二乌克兰方面军和第四乌克兰方面军无情推进下的匈牙利。匈牙利武装部队总参谋长上将扬诺斯·沃尔什命令这支由九个虚弱、兵力不足且装备不足的预备师组成的军队向匈牙利第二集团军（同时动员）西侧发起攻击。第三集团军随后要越过阿拉德和马罗什河谷，并占领特兰西瓦尼亚山区的隘口。<cr>这次进攻失败了。<cr>1944年10月6日，在德布勒森战役初期阶段，匈牙利第三集团军在阿拉德附近遭受重创。很快，该集团军就在凯奇克梅特镇附近被击溃。罗季翁·马林诺夫斯基的第2乌克兰方面军试图进行钳形攻势包围弗雷特-皮科集团军群。第2乌克兰方面军南部钳形部队轻松突破了匈牙利第三集团军。这一南线钳形攻势由苏联将军伊萨·普里耶夫指挥的普里耶夫机动集群领导。稍后，在同一场战役中，普里耶夫机动集群被弗雷特-皮科集团军群包围并遭受重创。北线钳形攻势则被经验丰富的德军装甲部队阻止并击退。匈牙利第二集团军是胜利的德国-匈牙利弗雷特-皮科集团军群的重要组成部分。<cr>从1944年12月29日起，匈牙利首都布达佩斯陷入围城。在布达佩斯战役中，所有可用的匈牙利部队都被投入保卫首都。经过巨大损失后，该城市于1945年2月13日无条件投降。<cr>从1945年3月16日至25日，在布达佩斯西边约四十公里处，大部分剩余的匈牙利第三集团军被包围并摧毁。该集团军被苏联第46集团军在向维也纳推进时消灭。但是，即使在此之后，匈牙利第三集团军也没有完全停止存在。一些残部仍然战斗下去，并逐渐向南奥地利移动。直到1945年5月8日战争结束，该集团军才正式解散。这是当时匈牙利第三集团军最后一位指挥官，少将约瑟夫·赫斯林尼的投降日期。<cr>

text: The 3rd Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. The brigade was disbanded in August of 1941.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text: The 3rd Julia Alpini Italian Mountain Division was formed in 1935 with the 8th and 9th Alpini Regiments and the 3rd Alpine Artillery Regiment. Alpini mountain infantry were considered elite units in the Italian Army. Each division consisted of two Alpini regiments with three battalions each, one Alpine artillery regiment, one mixed engineer battalion and various support troops for a total divisional strength of over 17,000 men. Each Alpini division also possessed nearly 5,000 mules and 500 vehicles of various types. The division was one of three Alpini sent to fight on the Eastern Front with the Italian 8th Army in the summer of 1942. The division was originally to be deployed to the Caucasus Mountains but instead found itself, along with the rest of the 8th Army, stretched along a 160 mile section of the Don River between the Hungarian Second Army and Romanian 3rd Army on the German left flank at the start of Operation Little Saturn. The division, along with most of the 8th Army was surrounded. The division fought its way free although most of the division was lost with barely 1,200 surviors remaining. The survivors returned to Italy and the division was disbanded by the Germans in September 1943 after Italy's surrender.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第3朱莉娅阿尔卑斯山地师于1935年组建，包括第8和第9阿尔卑斯团以及第3高山炮兵团。阿尔卑斯步兵被视为意大利军队中的精锐部队。每个山地师由两个阿尔卑斯团组成，每个团有三个营；一个高山炮兵团；一个混合工兵营和其他支援部队，总兵力超过17000人。每个山地师还拥有近5000头骡子和各种类型的500辆车辆。该师是1942年夏季被派往东线与意大利第8集团军一起作战的三个阿尔卑斯师之一。原计划将该师部署到高加索山脉，但最终却与其他第8集团军部队一道，在“小土星行动”开始时，沿着匈牙利第二集团军和罗马尼亚第三集团军之间的顿河160英里地段展开，位于德国左翼。该师与大部分第8集团军一起被包围了。尽管该师成功突围，但大多数兵力损失殆尽，仅剩不到1200名幸存者返回意大利。这些幸存者在意大利投降后于1943年9月被德军解散。<cr> <cr> <cr> <cr> <cr> 入库感谢克里斯·芒森

text: The 3rd Mechanised Corps was first formed in July 1940, and on 22 June 1941, was stationed at Vilnius in the Baltic Military District under MG A.V. Kurkin. It consisted of 2nd Tank Division, 5th Tank Division, 84th Motorised Division, 15th Motorcycle Regiment, an artillery regiment, and engineer and signals battalions. On 22 June, the 2nd Tank Division was located in the forest in Gajzhuny, in the Ionava area, the 5th Tank Division was positioned to defend the Neman bridge near Alitus, and the 84th Motorised Division - was in forest in the Kajshadoris area. On 22 June 1941, the 3rd Mechanised Corps had 31,975 men & 651 tanks, of which 110 were new T-34 and KV-1 types.<cr>The Corps was heavily engaged in the first battles of Operation Barbarossa, particularly during the Baltic Operation (1941) and at the Battle of Raseiniai.<cr>However, by early July the Corps had virtually ceased to exist as a formation, though remnants rejoined Soviet lines later. For example, the 5th Tank Division was at Yelnya by 4 July 1941, and consisted of 2,552 men and a total of 2 BT-7 tanks and four armoured cars. The 2nd Tank Division was encircled and destroyed at Raseiniai and the 5th Tank Division was encircled and destroyed at the Battle of Bia?ystok-Minsk and was disbanded shortly after.<cr>On 11 July 1941 Col P Poluboiarov, Northwestern Front armoured directorate reported that the 3rd Mechanised Corps had 'completely perished' having only 400 men remaining who escaped encirclement with 2nd Tank Division & only 1 BT-7 tank.<cr>The Corps was formed for the second time on 18 September 1942 at Kalinin in the Moscow Military District. General Lieutenant M.E. Katukov took command. It was initially assigned to the 22nd Army of the Kalinin Front. It took part in Operation Mars alongside the 22nd Army. At the beginning of Operation Mars 3rd Mechanised Corps consisted of 232 tanks. Hamazasp Babadzhanian, who commanded the 3rd Mechanised Brigade of the corps, mentioned this operation briefly in his memoirs, quoting a conversation with 22nd Army commander, V. A. Iushkevich, who said, 'We will conduct a rather serious offensive together with Western Front forces-we must liquidate the enemy Rzhev grouping.'<cr>The Corps then fought in the Battle of Kursk, then fought across the Ukraine with the Central, Belorussian, and 1st Belorussian Fronts. On 23 October 1943, it was awarded Guards status and re-designated the 8th Guards Mechanised Corps.<cr><cr>
translation: 第3机械化军成立于1940年7月，1941年6月22日驻扎在波罗的海军事区维尔纽斯，由A.V.库尔金中将指挥。该军包括第2坦克师、第5坦克师、第84摩托化师、第15摩托车团、炮兵团以及工兵和通信营。6月22日时，第2坦克师位于加兹胡尼的森林里，在伊奥纳瓦地区；第5坦克师则在阿利图斯附近的涅曼河桥附近布防；而第84摩托化师则驻扎在卡什达罗里斯地区的森林中。1941年6月22日，第3机械化军共有31,975人和651辆坦克，其中包含110辆新式的T-34和KV-1重型坦克。<cr>该军在巴巴罗萨行动初期战斗中被大量投入，特别是在波罗的海战役（1941）和拉塞尼艾战役中。<cr>然而，到7月初时，该军几乎已不复存在作为一个作战单位，尽管残部后来重新加入了苏军防线。例如，第5坦克师在1941年7月4日到达叶尔尼亚，共有2,552人和总共两辆BT-7快速坦克及四辆装甲车。<cr>第2坦克师在拉塞尼艾被包围并摧毁；而第5坦克师则在比亚韦斯托克—明斯克战役中被包围并摧毁，并随后解散。<cr>1941年7月11日，西北方面军装甲总监P.波卢鲍亚罗夫上校报告称，第3机械化军已“完全毁灭”，仅有400人逃脱了包围圈，与第2坦克师一起仅剩一辆BT-7快速坦克。该军于1942年9月18日在加里宁的莫斯科军区第二次组建。少将M.E.卡图科夫担任指挥官。最初被分配给加里宁方面军下的第22集团军。它参加了与第22集团军一起进行的火星行动。在火星行动开始时，第3机械化军拥有232辆坦克。该军第3机械化旅指挥官哈马扎斯普·巴巴詹尼安在他的回忆录中简要提到了这次行动，并引用了与第22集团军司令V.A.尤什凯维奇的对话：“我们将与西方方面军部队一起进行较为严重的进攻——我们必须消灭敌人的勒热夫集团。”<cr>该军随后参加了库尔斯克战役，然后在乌克兰与中央、白俄罗斯和第1白俄罗斯方面军并肩作战。1943年10月23日，它被授予近卫称号，并改名为第8近卫机械化军。<cr><cr>

text: It crossed into Russia in 1941 as part of Army Group North, took part in the initial drive on Leningrad, and fought at Demyansk. Shifted south late in the year, it was involved in the final thrusts on Moscow and opposed the Russian winter offensive of 194142. In March 1942, it was reorganized again. The 53rd Motorcycle and Reconnaissance Battalions were combined, and the 312th Army Anti-Aircraft Battalion was added to its table of organization. That next summer it was sent to Army Group South, took part in the Battle of Vyazma, the advancee across the Don, the push to the Volga., and the Stalingrad fighting. It was encircled in the Stalingrad Pocket in November. It surrendered to the Russians in the southern part of the Stalingrad Pocket on January 31, 1943.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 它于1941年作为北方集团军群的一部分进入俄罗斯，参加了对列宁格勒的初步攻势，并在德米扬斯克作战。同年晚些时候被转移到南方，参与了对莫斯科的最后一轮攻势，并对抗了苏联1941至1942年的冬季反攻。1942年3月，它再次重组。第53摩托化侦察营和第312军防空营合并。次夏，该部队被派往南方集团军群，参加了维亚兹马战役、顿河攻势、伏尔加河推进以及斯大林格勒的战斗。11月，它在斯大林格勒包围圈中被合围。<cr>1943年1月31日，该部队向南部分解围区内的苏联投降。<cr><cr>德国二战装甲、摩托化步兵和武装党卫军师战斗序列（第三卷）：山姆·米奇安 Jr.

text: The 3rd Panzer invaded Russia on June 22, 1941, and seized the Koden Bridge on the frontier by a coup de main. It took part in the Battle of the Bialystok-Minsk Pocket and the Dnieper River crossings, before being sent to the southern sector, where it helped trap several Russian armies, comprising 667,000 men, in the Kiev area. It then turned north again and fought in the Battle of Moscow. During the Soviet Russian winter offensive of 194142, it acted as a 'fire brigade' and, in March 1942, held Kharkov against massive Soviet attacks. With the 4th Panzer Army, the division took part in the Caucasus campaign and suffered heavy losses in the battles around Mozdok. It escaped from the Kuban by crossing the Sea of Azov over the ice after Rostov was threatened in January 1943. It fought in the Battles of Kursk and Belgorod in July and August, and suffered heavy losses in the Kharkov battles of autumn 1943. Remaining in the line despite its casualties, the 3rd Panzer fought in the Dnieper campaign (where it again distinguished itself), at Kiev, and in the retreat through the Ukraine. It fought its way out of encirclement in Rumania, took part in the Hungarian campaign, and was on the southern sector of the Eastern Front when Hitler committed suicide on April 30, 1945. Prior to the actual German capitulation on May 8, the 3rd Panzer Division managed to break contact with the Russians and headed west to Steyr, where it surrendered to the U.S. Army, and thus avoided Soviet prisons.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第3装甲师于1941年6月22日入侵俄罗斯，占领了边境上的科登桥。它参加了比亚韦斯托克-明斯克包围圈战役和第聂伯河渡口作战，随后被调往南部战区，在那里帮助将几支苏联集团军（共计667,000人）围困在基辅地区。之后，该师再次北上并参与了莫斯科保卫战。在1941-42年的苏军冬季攻势中，它充当“救火队”，并于1942年3月，在哈尔科夫抵挡住了苏联的大规模进攻。与第4装甲集团军一起，该师参加了高加索战役，并在莫兹多克周边的战斗中遭受了重大损失。当罗斯托夫于1943年1月受到威胁时，它通过冰封的亚速海成功撤出库班地区。它参与了1943年7月至8月间的库尔斯克和别洛格勒德战役，并在秋季哈尔科夫战役中遭受重大损失。尽管伤亡惨重，该师仍留在前线并参加了第聂伯河战役（再次表现出色）、基辅保卫战以及乌克兰的撤退行动。它从罗马尼亚的包围圈中突围而出，参与了匈牙利战役，并于1945年4月30日希特勒自杀时仍在东线南部作战。在实际德国投降前的几天里，第3装甲师成功脱离与苏联军队的接触并向西撤退至施泰尔，在那里向美军投降，从而避免被送入苏军战俘营。<cr>参考资料：德国战斗序列卷三 - 装甲、摩托化步兵和武装党卫军师在二战中的表现，萨缪尔·W·米切尔少校

It was a constituent part of Army Group Center and participated in Operation Barbarossa and fought in the Battle of Moscow in late 1941 and early 1942. text: The 3rd Principe Amedeo Italian Celere Division was formed as a cavalry division in 1934. In August 1940 the division consisted of the 3rd Savoia Cavalleria and 5th Novara Lancer Regiments, a light armored battalion, a mobile infantry regiment (equiped primarily with bicycles), an artillery regiment and other support troops. It participated in the invasion of Yugoslavia in early 1941 and was sent to the Eastern Front as part of the Italian Expeditionary Corps in July and August of 1941. The Expeditionary Corps was initially attached to the German 11th Army. Between October 20th and November 2nd 1941 it participated in the assualt on Stalino.<cr>In March 1942 it was reorganized as a light mechanized division with the addition of the 6th Bersaglieri Regiment from the 2nd Emanuele Filiberto Testa di Ferro Cavalry Divsion, the 120th Motorized Artillery Regiment (with a captured Russian T-34 as a command tank), and various other motorcycle, armor and support units. The two cavalry regiments and the horse artillery regiment were removed from the division and returned to Italy. In July 1942 the Italians forces in Russia were substantially increased with the arrival of the Italian Eighth Army to which the division was now subordinated. The 8th Army, stretched along a 160 mile section of the Don River between the Hungarian Second Army and Romanian Third Army on the German left flank was largely destroyed in March 1943 during Operation Little Saturn .<cr>Reduced to half strength the division returned by train to Italy in March 1943. The division was disbanded after a brief resistance to German forces in September 1943 after Italy's surrender.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 意大利阿梅迪奥亲王第三快速师成立于1934年，是一支骑兵师。1940年8月，该师由第3萨沃亚骑兵团、第5诺瓦拉掷弹兵团、一个轻装甲营、一个摩托化步兵团（主要装备自行车）和炮兵团组成，并有其他支援部队。它参加了1941年初入侵南斯拉夫的行动，并于7月和8月作为意大利远征军被派往东线，最初隶属于德国第11集团军。1941年10月20日至11月2日，该师参与了对斯塔里诺的进攻。<cr>1942年3月，该师重组为轻机械化师，并加入了来自意大利第二埃马努埃尔菲利贝托铁拳骑兵师的第6掷弹兵团、装备有从苏联俘获的一辆T-34坦克作为指挥车的第120摩托化炮兵团以及各种摩托车、装甲和支援部队。两个骑兵团和一个马炮团被撤出该师并返回意大利。<cr>1942年7月，随着意大利第八集团军的到来，意大利在俄罗斯的力量大幅增加，该师现在隶属于第八集团军。沿顿河下游约160英里、位于匈牙利第二集团军和罗马尼亚第三集团军之间的区域，第八集团军在1943年3月的“小土星行动”中被摧毁。<cr>实力减半后，该师于1943年3月乘火车返回意大利。在意军投降后的9月份，该师短暂抵抗德军后解散。<cr>感谢克里斯·芒森提供资料

text: The 3rd Ravenna Italian Mountain Division was mobilized in 1939. Italian Mountain divisions should not be confused with the elite Alpini formations. Mountain divisions had pack horse artillery rather than towed artillery. The division consisted of the 37th and 38th Infantry Regiments, the 121st Artillery Regiment and various support troops.<cr>The division participated in the invasion of southern France in June 1940 as part of the Italian III Corps. The division took part in the Invasion of Yugoslavia as part of the Italian XI Corps. After brief occupation duties in Yugoslavia it was transferred back to Italy. The division was one of seven dispatched as reinforcements to the Eastern Front with the Italian 8th Army in the summer of 1942. The division found itself, along with the rest of the 8th Army, stretched along a 160 mile section of the Don River between the Hungarian Second Army and Romanian 3rd Army on the German left flank at the start of Operation Little Saturn. Several elements of the division were either surrounded and forced to surrender of annihilated by the Soviets as part of the operation. The suvivors were withdrawn to Italy in April 1943.<cr>The division was still in the process of being reformed when it was disbanded by the Germans after Italy's surrender in September 1943.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第3拉韦纳意大利山地师于1939年动员。意大利山地师不应与精英阿尔宾步兵部队混淆。山地师装备驮马炮而非牵引炮。该师由第37和第38步兵团、第121炮兵团以及各种支援部队组成。<cr>该师参与了1940年6月意大利第三军对法国南部的入侵行动。该师参加了作为意大利第十一军一部分入侵南斯拉夫的行动。在短暂占领南斯拉夫后，该师被调回意大利。1942年夏季，该师作为增援部队之一随同意大利第八集团军部署到东线。<cr>土星行动开始时，该师与第八集团军其余部分一起，在匈牙利第二集团军和罗马尼亚第三集团军之间、德军左翼的顿河160英里地段上拉长。该师多个单位在此次行动中被包围并被迫投降或遭苏联军队歼灭。<cr>幸存者于1943年4月撤回意大利。<cr>该师仍在重组过程中，因意大利投降而于1943年9月被德军解散。

text: On 22 June 1941, the 3rd Army comprised the 4th Army Corps (6th and 7th Infantry Divisions), the Cavalry Corps (5th and 8th Cavalry Brigades), the Mountain Corps (1st, 2nd, and 4th Mountain Brigades), two separate artillery battalion, a target acquisition battery, and the Air Force's 3rd Army Cooperation Command.<cr>For Operation Mnchen, in the north, the 3rd Army was reduced only to the Mountain Corps (the 1st, 2nd and 4th Mountain Brigades, 8th Cavalry Brigade and 7th Infantry Division), because the Cavalry Corps (5th and 6th Cavalry Brigades) had been subordinated directly to the German 11th Army. In fact the 3rd Army command did not have any operative attributes until 2 July 1941, when the ground offensive started also in the Romanian sector.<cr>In 1942 in the Caucasus, the 3rd Army initially consisted of the Cavalry Corps (Romania) (5th, 6th and 9th Cavalry Divisions) and the 1st Army Corps (Romania) (2nd Mountain Division and German 298th Infantry Division). 3rd Army was subordinated to the German 17th Army. It also had 3 observation squadrons assigned to it. However, after reorganization, on 7 August, only the Cavalry Corps remained with it.<cr>Along with the Romanian 4th Army, the Third Army bore the brunt of the Soviet Operaton Uranus, which saw the German Sixth Army encircled and destroyed during the Battle of Stalingrad.<cr>The Romanian Third Army, commanded by General Petre Dumistrescu, was transferred from the Caucasus and replaced five Italian and two German divisions between Blij Perekopa and Bokovkaya, with the task of defending a front 138 km long, far beyond its capabilities. To make things worse, the Soviets had two bridgeheads over the Don River, at Serafimovich and Kletskaya, which the German High Command ignored, despite repeated requests by General Dumitrescu for permission to eliminate them. At the start of the Soviet offensive in November 1942, the Third Army had a nominal strength of 152,492 Romanian troops and 11,211 German troops, being made up from 1st, 2nd, 4th and 5th Corps in a single echelon (1st Cavalry, 5th, 6th, 7th, 9th, 11th, 13th and 14th Infantry Divisions) from West to East, with 7th Cavalry and 15th Infantry Divisions in reserve. The Long Range Recon (Do-17M) and the 112th Liaison Squadrons (Fleet 10G) were also at its disposal. In November came the German XLVIII Panzer Corps, composed of the 22nd Panzer Division and the 1st Romanian Armored Division, which also was put in reserve. It also had the 2nd, 4th, 5th and 8th Motorized Heavy Artillery Regiments and the 41st Independent Motorized Heavy Artillery Battalion. Opposite the 3rd Army was the Southwestern Front, comprising the 1st Guards Army, 5th Tank Army and the Soviet 21st Army, with a force of 5,888 artillery pieces, 728 tanks and 790 planes.<cr>On 19 November at 0530, in the sector of the Third Romanian Army, a violent artillery barrage battered the entire front line. The weather conditions were harsh: blizzards, snow, -20 degrees Celsius, which made close air support impossible. The Soviets assaulted the positions of the 14th Infantry Division with the 5th Tank Army and the junction between the 13th Infantry Division and the 1st Cavalry Division with the 21st Army, with a total of 338,631 men against three weak divisions. The 37mm and 47mm AT guns were useless against Soviet T-34 tanks, so the Romanian troops had to use grenades, anti-tank mines and Molotov cocktails. In the first hours, they managed to delay the advance and destroy some tanks, but later they had to retreat or face encirclement. The Soviets also attacked west of Sarisa Valley and at Raspopinskaya, but were repulsed. In response to the situation that developed south of Kletskaya, the German 48th Panzer Corps was ordered to move towards the Soviet main thrust and shortly afterwards, the 22nd Panzer Division was redirected to the northwest towards Bolsoy and, reaching Petshany, it engaged Soviet armor. By evening, the 1st Romanian Armored Division reached Sirkovsky, making preparations to attack Bolsoy the next day.<cr>In the first day of the offensive, the Soviet forces succeeded in making two large breaches in the defences of the Third Romanian Army: one in the center, 1618 km wide and 15 km deep and one in the right wing, between the Third Romanian Army and the German Sixth Army, 1012 km wide and 3540 km deep.<cr>On 20 November, the Soviet armored and motorized forces advanced towards Kalach, with the intention of encircling the 6th Army embroiled in ferocious fighting at Stalingrad. The 22nd Panzer Division, overwhelmed at Petshany by the large number of Soviet tanks, withdrew north to Bol. Donschynka. The Romanian 1st Armored Division, without any available radio contact, tried to advance to Petshany in order to make the junction with the 22nd Panzer Division, but was forced to stop a few kilometers west of Korotovsky by stiff Soviet resistance and numerous counterattacks by Soviet tanks, flowing between the German 22nd and the Romanian 1st, occupying the Varlamovsky and Peralasovsky villages and making the junction with forces coming from Gromsky, thus encircling the 5th Corps. In the 4th Corps' sector, 40 Soviet tanks attacked the 15th Infantry Division but were repulsed by evening with heavy loses. Meanwhile, the 7th Cavalry Division unsuccessfully tried to block the enemy's advance; the right wing of the division, which had fully received the blow, retreated south while the left wing was reassigned to the 9th Infantry Division. Also, the 1st Cavalry Division had to retreat towards Stalingrad and was subordinated to the 6th Army. At the end of the day, the defence position of the Third Romanian Army had a 70 km wide gap in the centre. In this pocket were encircled the 1st Armored Division, three infantry divisions (5th, 6th and 15th) and remains of other two infantry divisions (13th and 14th). The former commander of the 6th Infantry Division, Major General Mihail Lascar, took command of the troops from the infantry divisions and formed the 'General Lascar' Group (40,000 men). At this point, the command point of the Third Army began moving to Morozovskaya.<cr>On 21 November, the 22nd Panzer Division tried to advance towards Perelasovsky in order to make the junction with the 1st Armored Division and to relieve the 'General Lascar' Group, but failed and was stopped the next day between Bol. Donschynka and Perelasovky. The 1st Romanian Armored Division advanced towards Bol. Donschynka, where it was hoping to find the German division, but the village was under Soviet control and then headed south and, after grim fighting, crossed the Chir River on the 25 November.<cr>On 22 November, the encircled 'General Lascar' Group, which had been ordered to resist at any cost, was attacked and transmitted its last message. They had run out of food and each gun had only 40 rounds left and after refusing the Soviet proposal to surrender they were entirely destroyed. Only the 1st Battalion of the 15 Infantry Regiment (6th infantry Division), commanded by Major Gheorghe Rasconescu, succeeded in getting to the Chir River with all its soldiers and equipment. His battalion had managed to prevent the Soviet 8th Cavalry Division from capturing the vital German airfield at Oblivkaya from 26 November to 3 December.<cr>On 23 November, the Soviet troops of the South-Western Front and of the Stalingrad Front met at Kalach-na-Donu, completing the encirclement of the German 6th Army, parts of the Romanian 4th Army and six other Romanian infantry divisions as well as one cavalry division.<cr><cr>
translation:
1941年6月22日，第3集团军包括第4军（第6步兵师和第7步兵师）、骑兵军（第5骑兵旅和第8骑兵旅）、山地军（第1、第2和第4山地旅）以及两个独立炮兵团和一个目标搜索炮兵连。<cr>在北方的“慕尼黑”行动中，第3集团军仅保留了山地军（第1、第2和第4山地旅，第8骑兵旅和第7步兵师），因为骑兵军（第5和第6骑兵旅）直接隶属于德国第11集团军。实际上直到1941年7月2日地面进攻开始时，第3集团军指挥部才具备实际作战能力。<cr>在1942年的高加索地区，第3集团军最初包括罗马尼亚骑兵军（第5、第6和第9骑兵师）以及罗马尼亚第1军（第2山地师和德国第298步兵师）。第3集团军隶属于德国第17集团军。它还拥有3个侦察中队。然而，重组后，在8月7日，只有骑兵军留在其编制内。<cr>与罗马尼亚第4集团军一起，第3集团军在苏联的“天王星行动”中遭受重创，该行动导致德国第6集团军在斯大林格勒战役中被包围并消灭。<cr>罗马尼亚第三集团军，由彼得鲁·杜米特雷斯库将军指挥，从高加索地区调来，取代了布利佩雷科帕至博科夫卡亚之间五个意大利师和两个德国师的防区。该集团军的任务是防守长达138公里的防线，远远超出了其能力范围。更糟糕的是，苏联在顿河上拥有塞拉芬维奇和克列茨卡亚两处桥头堡，而德军最高指挥部无视了杜米特雷斯库将军多次请求批准清除这些据点的要求。

1942年11月苏军攻势开始时，第三集团军名义上有152,492名罗马尼亚士兵和11,211名德国士兵。该集团军由第一、第二、第四和第五军组成，在一个梯队中（从西到东依次为：第一骑兵师、第五步兵师、第六步兵师、第七步兵师、第九步兵师、第十一步兵师、第十三步兵师、第十四步兵师），第七骑兵师和第十五步兵师处于预备状态。该集团军还拥有远程侦察（Do-17M）中队和联络机（Fleet 10G）中队。

11月，德国XLVIII装甲军加入，由第二十二装甲师和第一罗马尼亚装甲师组成，并被置于预备状态。此外还有第二、第四、第五和第八摩托化重型炮兵团以及独立的第四十一摩托化重型炮兵团。

面对第三集团军的是西南方面军，包括近卫第一集团军、坦克第五集团军和苏联第21集团军，拥有5,888门火炮、728辆坦克和790架飞机。<cr>11月19日凌晨5点30分，在第三罗马尼亚集团军的防区内，猛烈的炮火轰击了整个前线。天气恶劣：暴风雪、积雪和零下20摄氏度的低温使得近距离空中支援变得不可能。苏联军队用第5坦克集团军攻击了第14步兵师的位置，并用第21集团军攻击了第13步兵师与第1骑兵师之间的结合部，总兵力达338,631人，面对三个薄弱的罗马尼亚师。37毫米和47毫米反坦克炮对苏联T-34坦克无能为力，因此罗马尼亚部队不得不使用手榴弹、反坦克地雷和莫洛托夫鸡尾酒进行反击。在最初的几个小时里，他们设法延缓了进攻并摧毁了一些坦克，但后来要么被迫撤退，要么面临被包围的危险。苏联军队还在萨里斯河谷以西和拉斯波平斯卡亚地区发动攻击，但均遭到了击退。为了应对克列茨卡亚南部局势的发展，德军第48装甲军接到命令向苏军主要突击方向移动，并很快将第22装甲师重新部署到西北方向的博洛伊，到达佩什尼后与苏联坦克部队交战。傍晚时分，第1罗马尼亚装甲师抵达西尔科夫斯基，准备第二天进攻博洛伊。

在第一天的攻势中，苏军成功地在第三罗马尼亚集团军防线上制造了两个大的突破口：一个位于中央，宽达16.18公里、纵深15公里；另一个位于右翼，在第三罗马尼亚集团军与德军第6集团军之间，宽达10.12公里、纵深35.4公里。11月20日，苏联装甲和机械化部队向卡拉萨前进，意图包围陷入斯大林格勒激烈战斗中的第6集团军。在佩什阿尼被大量苏军坦克压倒的第22装甲师撤退到博尔·多恩申卡以北。没有无线电联系的罗马尼亚第1装甲师试图推进到佩什阿尼，与第22装甲师会合，但因遭到苏联部队顽强抵抗和来自苏军坦克的多次反攻而被迫在科罗托夫斯基西面几公里处停止前进。苏军坦克流窜于德军第22装甲师和罗马尼亚第1装甲师之间，占领了瓦尔拉莫夫斯克村和佩拉拉斯克村，并与从格罗姆斯基来的部队会合，从而包围了第5军。在第4军的防区，40辆苏军坦克攻击了第15步兵师，但傍晚时分被击退，损失惨重。与此同时，第7骑兵师未能阻止敌人的推进；该师右翼完全遭到打击后撤向南面，左翼则转隶给第9步兵师。此外，第1骑兵师也必须撤往斯大林格勒，并隶属于第6集团军。到当天结束时，第三罗马尼亚集团军的防御阵地在中央形成了70公里宽的缺口，在这个包围圈内被围困的是第1装甲师、三个步兵师（第5、第6和第15）以及另外两个步兵师（第13和第14）的部分残部。原第6步兵师指挥官米哈伊尔·拉扎尔少将接管了来自各步兵师的部队，并组建了“拉扎尔将军”集团（约4万人）。此时，第三集团军指挥部开始向莫罗佐夫斯卡亚转移。<cr>11月21日，第22装甲师试图向佩雷拉索夫斯基推进，以与第1装甲师会合并解救“拉斯卡将军”集团，但未能成功，并于次日在博尔·多恩什因卡和佩雷拉索夫斯基之间被阻止。第1罗马尼亚装甲师则朝博尔·多恩什因卡前进，希望在那里找到德军，但村庄已被苏联控制，随后向南推进，在惨烈的战斗后于11月25日渡过奇尔河。<cr>11月22日，“拉斯卡将军”集团被包围并遭到攻击。该集团奉命不惜一切代价抵抗，并发送了最后一条信息。他们已经断粮，每门炮只剩下40发弹药，在拒绝苏联提出的投降建议后，整个集团被彻底消灭。只有第6步兵师的第15步兵团（第6步兵师）的第一营在乔治·拉松内斯库少校指挥下成功带领所有士兵和装备到达奇尔河。<cr>从11月26日至12月3日，该团阻止了苏联第8骑兵师占领关键的德国机场奥布利夫卡。<cr>11月23日，西南方面军和斯大林格勒方面的苏军在卡拉奇会合，完成了对德军第6集团军、罗马尼亚第4集团军的部分以及另外六个罗马尼亚步兵师和一个骑兵师的包围圈。

text: The 3rd Romanian Infantry Division was not deployed to the front until July of 1941. It participated in the 73 day Siege of Odessa as part of the Romanian 4th Army. At the end of 1941 it was transferred from the front to Romania where it remained and later participated in the defensive battles in Romania proper in 1944. After Romania's capitulation to the Soviet Union in late 1944 it served in Hungary and Czechoslovakia under Soviet control.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第3罗马尼亚步兵师直到1941年7月才部署到方面军。它参加了罗马尼亚第4集团军在敖德萨进行的为期73天的围攻战。1941年底，该师从前线调回罗马尼亚，并留在国内，在1944年的防御战斗中发挥作用。随着罗马尼亚在1944年末向苏联投降，该师后来在苏维埃控制下驻扎于匈牙利和捷克斯洛伐克。<cr>资料来源： 克里斯·芒森<cr>

text: The 3rd Romanian Security Division was formed in February of 1942 to perform security operations in occupied Russia near the Romanian border. In May of 1943 it was merged with the 9th Romanian Infantry Division .<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson

text: The Army was created from the headquarters of 60th Army (1st formation), which had been formed in the Moscow Military District in November 1941.<cr>It was initially a part of the Moscow Defense Zone in the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (RVGK). However, 3rd Shock was soon allocated to join North-Western Front from 27 December 1941 as part of the Moscow counteroffensive. Matters were not improved by the lack of supplies, aggravated by horrible communications; the assault troops did not get a full meal before the offensive due to food shortages.<cr>However, after a few days the offensive - the Toropets-Kholm operation - began to roll forward, with 3rd Shock approaching Kholm, but it was getting dangerously separated from its neighbour, 4th Shock Army. By mid January, 3rd Shock had surrounded Kholm and its forward units had cut the road between Kholm and Toropets. Kholm itself was surrounded on 22 January (but never taken and relieved on 5 May). With some success in view, Stalin widened the operation's goals, and with a Stavka directive of 19 January directed 3rd Shock, as part of the wider operation, to head for Velikie Luki, and thence to Vitebsk, Orsha, and Smolensk. Two days later, 3rd Shock was shifted from North-Western Front to the Kalinin Front. However, the forces available were becoming dangerously thin for the enormous tasks that Stalin was setting them. But the Army got no further than Velikie Luki (though not taking the town) in the face of stiffening German resistance and shortages of food, fuel, and ammunition. Velikie Luki was finally taken by the Kalinin Front on 17 January 1943.<cr>The Army's next major effort was as part of the Nevel'-Gorodok offensive operation in October- November 1943. Nevel was taken at the start of the offensive on 6 October 1943. Kalinin Front had been renamed Baltic Front on 13 October 1943, and under Yeremenko, used two armies on the left flank, 43rd and 49th, to distract the Germans attention from his main blow, from 3rd and 4th Shock Armies against Third Panzer Army focused on the Nevel area. This would see the Soviets astride the routes leading to the rear of Army Group North and cut vital rail links.<cr>Following the Starorussa-Novorzhev offensive operation (February 1944), the Army's next attack was as part of 2nd Baltic Front's July 1944 offensive the Rezhitsa-Dvina offensive operation. Kicking off on 10 July, 3rd Shock Army had reached the Velikaya River by 12 July, captured the bridges despite the demolition charges laid on them, and gone on to outflank Idritsa. Idritsa was liberated that same day.<cr>As the Army moved quickly across Poland in March 1945, during the Eastern-Pomeranian strategic offensive operation, it liberated a number of cities: Vangerin (now Vengozhino, Poland) and Labes (now Lobez, Poland)(together with the troops of the 1st Guards Tank Army) on 3 March, and Frayenvalde (now Khotsivel, Poland) and Regenvalde (now Resko, Poland) on 4 March 1945. The same day, in conjunction with the Polish 1st Army and the 1st Guards Tank Army, 3rd Shock entered Dramburg (now Dravsko-Pomorske, Poland). A day later, 3rd Shock entered Gyultsov (now Golchevo, Poland), and on 6 March: Kammin (now Kamen'-Pomorski, Poland). On 7 March, 3rd Shock entered Shtepenitts (now Stepnitsa, Poland), and liberated Gollnov (now Golenyuv, Poland) together with troops of the 2nd Guards Tank Army.<cr>The Army took Pankow, a suburb of Berlin, on 23 April 1945. A week later, two regiments of the 150th Rifle Division, 79th Rifle Corps were responsible for erecting flags over the Reichstag on 30 April 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 该集团军由第60集团军（第一组建）司令部于1941年11月在莫斯科军区成立。<cr>最初是最高统帅部预备队（RVGK）莫斯科防御区内的一部分，但很快从27日起被分配给西北方面军，作为莫斯科反攻的一部分。由于补给不足和糟糕的通信状况，突击部队在进攻前因食物短缺而无法吃饱。<cr>然而，在几天后，攻势——托罗佩茨-霍尔姆行动——开始推进，第3突击集团军接近霍尔姆，但与邻近的第4突击集团军越来越远地分离。到1月中旬，第3突击集团军包围了霍尔姆，并切断了霍尔姆和托罗佩茨之间的道路。霍尔姆本身于1月22日被包围（但从未被占领，在5月5日解围）。随着取得一些成功，斯大林扩大了行动的目标，并在1月19日的最高统帅部指令中指示第3突击集团军作为更大规模行动的一部分向维捷布斯克前进。两天后，第3突击集团军从西北方面军转移到加里宁方面军。然而，为斯大林设定的巨大任务提供的人力已经变得过于薄弱。但在德国抵抗加强和食物、燃料及弹药短缺的情况下，该集团军未能推进到维捷布斯克（尽管没有占领这座城市）。最终，加里宁方面军于1943年1月17日攻占了维捷布斯克。<cr>该集团军接下来的重大努力是在1943年10月至11月的涅夫尔-戈罗德克进攻行动中。在此次攻势开始时，即1943年10月6日，加里宁方面军更名为波罗的海方面军。叶廖缅科指挥下，在左翼部署了第43集团军和第49集团军以分散德国人的注意力，而主要攻击则由第3突击集团军和第4突击集团军发起，目标是第三装甲集团军在涅夫尔地区的部队。这将使苏联军队控制通往北方集团军群后方的道路，并切断重要的铁路线。<cr><cr>随着斯塔罗鲁萨-诺沃日耶夫进攻行动（1944年2月）之后，该集团军的下一次攻击是在波罗的海第二方面军1944年7月攻势中的列季奇亚-第维纳攻势。此次攻势于7月10日开始，到7月12日，第3突击集团军已到达韦利卡亚河，并在德军布设了炸药的情况下夺取了桥梁，随后包围了伊德里察。同一天解放了伊德里察。<cr><cr>随着该集团军于1945年3月迅速穿越波兰，在东波美拉尼亚战略进攻行动中，它解放了一系列城市：瓦格宁（现为波兰的韦戈日诺）和拉贝斯（现为波兰的洛贝兹），与第一近卫坦克集团军共同作战，于3月3日解放；弗雷恩瓦尔德（现为波兰的霍奇维夫）和雷根瓦尔德（现为波兰的雷斯科），于1945年3月4日解放。同一天，在波兰第一集团军和第一近卫坦克集团军的配合下，第3突击集团军进入德拉姆堡（现为波兰的达夫斯克-波美拉尼亚）。次日，第3突击集团军进入古尔佐夫（现为波兰的戈尔切沃），并于1945年3月6日：卡明（现为波兰的卡缅-波美拉尼亚）。3月7日，第3突击集团军进入什特佩尼茨（现为波兰的斯捷平察），并与第二近卫坦克集团军共同作战解放了戈尔诺夫（现为波兰的戈伦尤夫）。<cr><cr>集团军于1945年4月23日占领了柏林的郊区潘科夫。一周后，第79步兵军下的两个团负责在1945年4月30日将旗帜插上国会大厦。<cr><cr>

text: The 3rd Tank Army was formed as part of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (RVGK, Stavka reserve) on the basis of the 58th Army in the Moscow Military District in May 1942. It was placed under the command of Lieutenant General Prokofy Romanenko. Its initial composition was 12th and 15th Tank Corps, one motor rifle division, and two rifle divisions. As part of the Soviet Western Front, the 3rd Tank Army successfully counter-attacked the 2nd Panzer Army in August 1942. Soon afterwards, in September 1942, Romanenko handed over to Colonel General Pavel Rybalko, who held command of the Army for the remainder of the war.<cr>Committed to the fighting for Kharkov in March 1943 as part of the Voronezh Front, the 3rd Tank Army was subsequently encircled and virtually destroyed by German forces. The Army's remnants were reorganised as the 57th Army.<cr><cr>
translation: 第3坦克集团军于1942年5月在莫斯科军区的基础上从最高统帅部预备队（RVGK，大本营预备队）中组建。该部队由少将普罗科菲·罗马尼琴指挥。其初始编制包括第12和第15坦克军、一个机械化步兵师以及两个步兵师。作为苏联西部方面军的一部分，第3坦克集团军于1942年8月成功反击了第2装甲集团军。不久之后，在1942年9月，罗马尼琴将指挥权移交给上将帕维尔·里巴尔科，后者在战争剩余时间中一直担任该部队的指挥官。<cr>第3坦克集团军于1943年3月作为沃罗涅日方面军的一部分投入哈尔科夫战斗。随后被德军包围并几乎全军覆没。该集团军残部重组为第57集团军。

text:
The 3rd Tank Corps was formed in March-April at Tula in Moscow Military District.<cr>In late April 1942 3rd Tank Corps was assigned to Bryansk Front south of Moscow. At that time the three tank brigades had a total of 24 to 28 KVs, 90 to 95 medium T-34s or British Lend Lease Matilda Us (in 103rd Tank Brigade), and 60 T-60 light tanks. The Corps remained near the Moscow area throughout the summer and fall of 1942, missing the disasters in the south that engulfed so many of the tank corps in 1942.<cr>In September 1942 the 3rd Motorized Rifle Brigade was removed from the corps to form a Mechanized Brigade. The corps became a tank training unit in STAVKA Reserves for several months in late 1942. In December 57th Motorized Rifle Brigade was assigned to the corps and it was sent to Southwestern Front. 3rd Tank Corps was part of Popov Mobile Group in Southwestern Front in February 1943, when Manstein's counterattack cut off that group. Virtually tankless after heavy losses, the corps went into STAVKA Reserves to be rebuilt in March 1943.<cr>From March to June 1943 3rd Tank Corps was completely re-equipped , first as a separate unit in the reserves, and then as part of the 2nd Tank Army. By 1 July 1943 the corps was in 2nd Tank Army in Central Front reserves.<cr>On 5 July 3rd Tank Corps was directly in front of the 9th German Army's advance against Kursk at Ponyri. From July 1943 until the end of the war 3rd Tank Corps served with 2nd Tank (later 2nd Guards Tank) Army.<cr>In the summer and fall of 1943 the corps gradually replaced all of its light tanks with T-34s and added a third tank battalion of T-34s to each of the tank brigades. In October 1943 the 3rd Tank Corps also received the 1540th
Heavy SU Regiment (12 SU-152s).<cr>In January-March 1944 the Corps converted 881st Antitank Regiment into 881st SU Regiment (21 SU-76) , and the 1818th SU Regiment (21 SU-85) was added temporarily.<cr>In August 1944 3rd Tank Corps received another support unit, the 6th Guards Heavy Tank Regiment (21 IS-II tanks), and in September, while in STAVKA Reserves with the rest of 2nd Tank Army , 341st Guards Heavy SU Regiment (21 ISU-122s) was assigned to the corps.<cr>Finally, in October 1944, the 3rd Tank Corps received 1643rd Light Artillery Regiment (24 76mm guns), the last major supporting unit assigned to it.<cr>On 20 November 1944, the 3rd Tank Corps became the 9th Guards Tank Corps when the entire 2nd Tank Army became 2nd Guards Tank Army.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第3坦克军于1942年3月至4月在图拉的莫斯科军区组建。<cr>1942年4月底，第3坦克军被分配到位于莫斯科南部的布良斯克方面军。<cr>当时三个坦克旅共有24至28辆KV重型坦克、90至95辆中型T-34或英国租借法案提供的马蒂尔达步兵坦克（在第103坦克旅），以及60辆T-60轻型坦克。该军在整个1942年夏季和秋季都驻扎在莫斯科附近，错过了南部地区发生的许多坦克军的灾难。<cr>1942年9月，第3摩托化步兵旅从该军中分离出来组建机械化旅。该军成为最高统帅部预备队中的坦克训练单位，并于1942年底几个月内留在那里。<cr>12月，第57摩托化步兵旅被分配给该军，并被派往西南方面军。1943年2月，第3坦克军是波波夫机动部队的一部分，在西南方面军中遭到曼施坦因反攻的切断。在遭受重大损失后几乎无坦克可用，该军于1943年3月进入最高统帅部预备队重建。<cr>从1943年3月至6月，第3坦克军完全重新装备，最初作为独立单位留在预备队中，然后成为第2坦克集团军的一部分。<cr>到1943年7月1日，该军已成为中央方面军预备队中的第2坦克集团军的一部分。<cr>1943年7月5日，第3坦克军直接位于进攻库尔斯克的德军第9集团军前方的波尼亚里地区。<cr>从1943年7月至战争结束，第3坦克军一直在第2坦克（后来为第2近卫坦克）集团军服役。<cr>1943年夏季和秋季，该军逐渐用T-34替换所有轻型坦克，并在每个坦克旅中增加一个由T-34组成的第三坦克营。10月，第3坦克军还收到了第1540重型SU团（12辆SU-152）。<cr>1944年1月至3月，第881反坦克团被改编为第881自行火炮团（装备21辆SU-76），同时临时增加了第1818自行火炮团（装备21辆SU-85）。<cr><cr>1944年8月，第3坦克军接收了另一支援单位——第6近卫重型坦克团（装备21辆IS-II坦克），而在同年9月，在最高统帅部大本营预备队的第2坦克集团军中，第341近卫重型自行火炮团（装备21辆ISU-122）被分配给该军。<cr><cr>最后，1944年10月，第3坦克军接收了第1643轻型炮兵团（装备24门76毫米火炮），这是最后一个主要支援单位加入该军。<cr><cr>1944年11月20日，随着整个第2坦克集团军改编为第2近卫坦克集团军，第3坦克军也改名为第9近卫坦克军。<cr><cr><cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普著《二战苏联战斗序列 第二卷》

text:
The Third Tank Division was formed in July 1940 in Leningrad Military District as part of 1st Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
5th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - each 40 to 45 BT tanks
6th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - each 40 to 45 BT tanks
3rd Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
3rd Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1 light, 1 medium bn
3rd Reconnaissance Battalion
3rd Motorized Pontoon Battalion
3rd Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>The division was formed with all BT tanks, and was virtually fullstrength by October 1940. Unfortunately, it never received any modern vehicles, and was sent into battle against 4th Panzer Group in early July with 350 BT-2, 5 and 7 tanks. After 1st Mechanized Corps HQ was shut down in August, 3rd Tank Division came under the Novgorod Operational Group, fighting in the swampy forests just north of Lake Urnen. This was the worst possible terrain for armor, but the division had no armor left by then. In November 1941 what was left of the unit was redesignated as 225th Rifle Division.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

第三坦克师于1940年7月在列宁格勒军区组建，隶属于第一机械化军。1941年6月22日包括：

该师组建时全部装备了BT坦克，并在1940年10月几乎满编。不幸的是，它从未获得任何现代化车辆，在7月初被派往对抗第四装甲集群的战斗中，拥有350辆BT-2、5和7型坦克。8月第一机械化军司令部关闭后，第三坦克师转隶诺夫哥罗德作战群，在乌伦湖以北的沼泽森林地区作战。这是对装甲最不利的地貌，但该师到那时已经没有装甲车辆了。1941年11月，剩余部队被重新指定为第225步兵师。

text: The 3rd Ukrainian Front was founded on 20 October 1943, on the basis of a Stavka order of October 16, 1943, by renaming the Southwestern Front. It included 1st Guards Army, 8th Guards Army, 6th, 12th, and 46th Armies and 17th Air Army. Later it included 5th Shock, 4th and 9th Guards Army, 26th, 27th, 28th, 37th, 57th Army, 6th Guards Tank Army, and the Bulgarian First, Second and Fourth Armies. The Danube Flotilla was assigned to the Front's operational control. This included the 83rd Naval Infantry Brigade.<cr><cr>

text: The 40th Army formed in August 1941 at the boundary of the Bryansk Front and the Soviet Southwestern Front. As part of the Southwestern Front, it then took part in the Battle of Kiev. By the time of the main German offensive against Moscow at the end of September, 40th Army was on the extreme right flank of Southwestern Front defending the Kursk axis. The German offensive was directed primarily at Soviet forces to the north of 40th Army, also hit its right flank positions. 40th Army began a slow and steady retreat to the east. By 3 November 40th Army had been driven from Kursk, but by the end of the month it had brought the German advance to a halt near the town of Tim some 50 kilometres further east.<cr>As part of a general winter offensive, on 1 January 1942 40th Army attacked German positions east of Tim. The advance of 40th Army was less rapid than flanking Soviet units. By 3 January 40th Army, in conjunction with 21st Army further south, was involved in heavy fighting on the line of the Seym river. 40th Army retook Tim and advanced to within 30 kilometres of Kursk before being stopped by determined German resistance in mid-January. Thereafter the frontline stabilised west of Tim through the rest of the winter and through the spring. By 16 May the offensive by Southwestern Front north of Kharkov had stalled and Bryansk Front was ordered to divert the bulk of its combat aircraft to 40th Army in the south and to launch an immediate offensive to support Southwestern Front's right wing. However, this hurriedly prepared offensive in the second half of May made little progress.<cr>n June 1942, Operation Blau saw Hoth's Fourth Panzer Army thrust in full force against 40th Army, which had its headquarters overrun by 24th Panzer Division on 29-30 June. The 40th Army fell back from the Kastornoye area back to Voronezh. During July, 40th Army, subordinated to Voronezh Front, was assigned to defend the river Don along the Liski - Pavlovsk sector.<cr>On 12 January 1943 40th Army began offensive operations against the left flank of the Hungarian Second Army north of Liski. By 18 January most of the Hungarian army and an Italian corps had been surrounded east of Alekseyevka. The 40th Army struck north on 24 January to surround much of Second Army. On 2 February 40th Army was launched into an offensive to the southwest. It took Novy Oskol on 5 February and reached Belgorod four days later. Continuing to the southwest, 40th Army had reached Akhtyrka northwest of Kharkov by 23 February, but by then a German counter-offensive was launched and 40th Army was pushed back to defensive positions east of Sumy.<cr>On 5 July 1943 Operation Citadel commenced. At that time 40th Army, occupying what was expected to be a relatively quiet sector of the frontline facing the left flank of the Fourth Panzer Army. During the Battle of Kursk, it transferred a number of reinforcements to 6th Guards Army. 40th Army also transferred a tank brigade to 38th Army at the same time. After the battle, it was involved in the crossing of the Dnepr in September 1943. The Army fought in the Battle of Kiev (1943) and in 1944, actions around the Korsun-Cherkassy Pocket, Kamenets-Podolsky pocket, and the Uman-Botoshany, Iassy-Kishinev, Bratislava-Brno, and Prague Offensives. It also fought in the Battle of Debrecen, at which, due to its low priority, it only had five divisions assigned. 40th Army was disbanded in July 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第40集团军于1941年8月在布良斯克方面军和苏联西南方面军的交界处组建。作为西南方面军的一部分，它参与了基辅战役。到德国主力部队在9月底对莫斯科发动进攻时，第40集团军位于西南方面军最右翼，在库尔斯克方向进行防御。德军的主要攻击目标是第40集团军以北的苏军部队，同时也打击了其右翼阵地。第40集团军开始缓慢而稳定的撤退向东移动。到11月3日，第40集团军已被迫撤离库尔斯克，但到了月底，它在距离蒂姆镇东50公里处成功阻止了德军的推进。<cr>作为冬季攻势的一部分，第40集团军于1942年1月1日对蒂姆以东的德军阵地发起了攻击。与侧翼苏军部队相比，第40集团军的推进速度较慢。到1月3日，第40集团军与更南边的第21集团军一起，在赛姆河沿线展开了激烈战斗。第40集团军重新占领了蒂姆，并推进至距离库尔斯克约30公里处，但于1月中旬被坚决抵抗的德军阻止。此后前线在冬季和春季稳定下来，位于蒂姆以西。<cr>到5月16日，西南方面军在哈尔科夫北部发起的攻势停滞不前，布良斯克方面军接到命令将大部分战斗飞机调往第40集团军所在的南部，并立即发动进攻支援西南方面军的右翼。然而，在5月下旬匆忙准备的这次攻势进展甚微。<cr>1942年6月，蓝色行动中霍特的第四装甲集团军全力进攻第40集团军。在6月29日至30日，第24装甲师攻占了第40集团军司令部所在的卡斯托诺耶地区。第40集团军从该地区撤退至沃罗涅日。7月份，隶属于沃罗涅日方面军的第40集团军被指派在利斯基-帕夫洛夫斯克地段防御顿河。<cr><cr>1943年1月12日，第40集团军开始对匈牙利第二集团军左翼发起进攻，该集团军位于利斯基以北。到1月18日，大部分的匈牙利军队和一个意大利军被包围在阿列克谢耶夫卡以东地区。1月24日，第40集团军向北发动攻势，将第二集团军大部围住。<cr><cr>2月2日，第40集团军发起西南方向的进攻。2月5日攻占诺维奥斯基，并在四天后抵达别尔哥罗德。继续向西南推进，到2月23日，第40集团军已到达哈尔科夫西北部的阿赫图尔卡地区。但此时德国发动了反攻，将第40集团军推回苏缅以东的防御阵地。<cr><cr>1943年7月5日，堡垒行动（库尔斯克会战）开始。当时第40集团军驻守在前线左翼第四装甲集团军相对平静的区域。在库尔斯克战役期间，它向第6近卫集团军调派了部分增援部队，并同时将一个坦克旅调往第38集团军。战斗结束后，该集团军参与了1943年9月渡过第聂伯河的行动。此外，第40集团军还参加了1943年的基辅助攻战、1944年科斯努-切尔卡瑟包围圈、卡缅涅茨-波多利斯基包围圈以及乌曼-博托沙尼战役、伊萨克-奇什尼亚克进攻、布拉迪斯拉发-布罗恩攻势和布拉格攻势。在德布勒森战役中，由于优先级较低，该集团军仅被分配了5个师。第40集团军于1945年7月解散。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 40th Guards Rifle Division was one of a series of ten Guards rifle divisions (32nd - 41st) of the Red Army formed from airborne troops in the spring and summer of 1942 in preparation for, or in response to, the German summer offensive. It fought in the Stalingrad area during that battle, eventually in the operations that encircled German 6th Army, and then continued to serve in the several campaigns in the south sector of the front, helping to liberate Ukraine and the Balkans, and ending the war at Vienna.<cr><cr>
translation: 第40近卫步兵师是红军在1942年春季和夏季从空降部队中组建的十支近卫步兵师（第32至第41近卫步兵师）之一，目的是为应对德国的夏季攻势。该师参加了斯大林格勒战役，并最终参与了包围德军第6集团军的行动。之后，它继续在前线南部战区的多次战役中服役，帮助解放乌克兰和巴尔干地区，并在维也纳结束战争。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 40th Rifle Division was an infantry division of the Red Army during World War II. It gained the honorific 'named for Sergo Ordzhonikidze' on 14 April 1937. It fought in the engagements at Lake Khasan. On 22 June 1941, it was part of the 39th Rifle Corps, 25th Army, in the Far East Military District. The division fought in the Soviet invasion of Manchuria in 1945.<cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack
translation: 第40步兵师是红军在第二次世界大战期间的一个步兵师。该师于1937年4月14日获得“塞格罗·奥尔忠尼启泽命名”荣誉称号。它参加了哈桑湖战斗。1941年6月22日，该师隶属于远东军区的第25集团军下的第39步兵军。该师还参与了1945年的苏联入侵满洲作战。<cr>条目由NotOneStepBack提供

text:
The 40th Tank Division was formed March-April 1941 from separate tank battalions in Kiev Special Military District as part of 19th Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
79th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - each 1 to 3 companies
80th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - each 1 to 3 companies
40th Motorized Rifle Regiment
40th Howitzer Regiment
40th Reconnaissance Battalion - no motorcycles
40th Pontoon Battalion
40th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr>
The 40th Tank Division had 100% of its authorized enlisted, but only 53% of its authorized officers and NCOs. Formed from separate tank battalions removed from the rifle divisions, the bulk of the divisions tanks, 139 of them, were tiny amphibious T-37 tankettes, good only for reconnaissance. The rest of the divisional armor consisted of 19 T-26s and a handful of T-28 medium tanks 'scrounged' in the first days of the war out of repair depots. In addition, the 5th Army command split off elements of the division for direct support of the rifle divisions in the first days of the war, so what strength the division did have was 'nibbled away' in company and battalion-sized detachments of tanks.<cr>By 22 July the division was down to a combat strength of just 700 men, but it survived complete destruction to be evacuated out of the front in late August. In North Caucasus Military District in September the division was disbanded to provide cadres for several forming tank brigades.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第40坦克师成立于1941年3月至4月，由基辅特别军区的独立坦克营组建而成，隶属于第19机械化军。6月22日包括：<cr>
第79坦克团
第1、2、3、4坦克营——每个营有1到3个连
第80坦克团
第1、2、3、4坦克营——每个营有1到3个连
第40摩托化步兵营
第40榴弹炮营
第40侦察营——无摩托车
第40浮桥营
第40防空营<cr>
第40坦克师拥有其编制内全部士兵，但仅拥有53%的编制军官和士官。该师由从步兵师中抽调出的独立坦克营组建而成，其中大部分坦克（共139辆）是小型两栖T-37轻型坦克，仅适合侦察任务。其余装甲车辆包括19辆T-26和少量在战争初期从修理站“搜刮”来的T-28中型坦克。此外，在战争最初几天里，第5集团军指挥部将该师的部分兵力抽调出来直接支援步兵师，因此该师的剩余力量被分散到各个连级和营级坦克分队中。<cr>
至7月22日，该师战斗人员仅剩700人，但其幸免于全军覆没，并在8月下旬撤出前线。9月，在北高加索军区，该师被解散以提供多个正在组建的坦克旅的核心力量。<cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普著《苏联战斗序列 第一卷》

text: The 41st Army was created in May 1942, on the base of Nikolai Berzarin and German Tarasov's operational groups. It also included the 134th, 135th, 179th and 234th Rifle Divisions, the 17th Guards Rifle Division, the 21st Tank Brigade, two separate Guards mortar battalions, and several other separate elements.<cr>From May to November 1942, the army was focused on defending the southwestern approach to the city of Bely. In late November, the army joined the Rzhev offensive operation (Operation Mars). During that time, the army was engaged with the XLI Panzer Corps. The army's offensive failed, and they were surrounded by the German XXX Army Corps . By December 8, the surrounded forces were destroyed.<cr>In March 1943, the newly reformed 41st Army took part in the Rzhev-Vyazma operation. The offensive was a success and German forces in the Rzhev-Vyazma area were annihilated. Following the operation, the forces of the army were transferred to the 39th and the 43rd Armies, while the 41st Army itself was sent to the STAVKA Reserve. On April 9, 1943, the army was disbanded and its remaining forces would form part of the Reserve Front.<cr><cr>
translation: 第41集团军成立于1942年5月，由尼古拉·别尔扎林和德国塔拉索夫的作战群组建而成。该集团军包括第134、135、179和234步兵师，第17近卫步兵师，第21坦克旅，两个独立的近卫迫击炮营以及若干其他独立单位。<cr>从1942年5月到11月，该集团军主要负责保卫白利西南方向的城市。在11月底，该集团军参加了勒热夫进攻行动（火星行动）。在此期间，第41集团军与XL I装甲军交战。其攻势失败，并被德国XXX军包围。至12月8日，被围部队被消灭。<cr>1943年3月，重组后的第41集团军参加了勒热夫-维亚兹马行动。此次进攻取得成功，德军在该地区被彻底摧毁。行动结束后，该集团军的兵力转移到了第39和第43集团军中，而第41集团军则被调往最高统帅部预备队。<cr>1943年4月9日，该集团军解散，其剩余部队成为预备方面军的一部分。

text:
The 41st Cavalry Division was a cavalry formation of the Red Army during the Great Patriotic War.

It was formed on 20 July 1941 in the Northwestern Front using any elements the headquarters could find. In August 1941 the division was moved back to the Moscow Military District to complete its organization. Assigned to the STAVKA Reserves in September when the German offensive started against Moscow. By late October the division was assigned to the 50th Army on the Southern flank of the Western Front. The division covered the gap between the 50th Army and the Southwestern Fronts 3rd Army.

When the Soviet Offensive started in December the division was assigned to the Mishulin's Cavalry Group along with the 57th and 75th Cavalry Divisions. Assigned to the group from 19 December 1941 the division having been burned out the fighting in November was officially disbanded on 5 January 1942.<cr><cr>
translation:
第41骑兵师是苏联红军在卫国战争期间的一个骑兵部队。

该师于1941年7月20日在西北方面军成立，使用司令部能够找到的所有元素。1941年8月，该师被调回莫斯科军区以完成其编制。当德国开始对莫斯科的进攻时，该师于9月被分配给最高统帅部预备队。<cr>到10月下旬，该师被分配给西方方面军南翼的第50集团军。该师填补了第50集团军和西南方面军第3集团军之间的空隙。

当苏联进攻开始时，该师于1941年12月19日被分配到米舒林骑兵集群，与第57骑兵师和第75骑兵师一起行动。由于在11月的战斗中损失惨重，该师于1942年1月5日正式解散。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The corps fought a total 916 days in the war, and at different times it was in service on the Kalinin, the Leningrad and the 2nd Baltic Front. For 344 days, parts of the corps were engaged with German forces, but no significant gains were made. For the next 123 days, the formation was engaging in the Battle of Battle of Velikiye Luki where 13,000 of the 27,000 men were killed or wounded. Then, 37 days were spent in the Battle of Narva, and the final 88 days were devoted to the Battle ot the Courland Pocket. During the Battle of Narva in 1944, the artillery of the rifle corps fired on the 20th Waffen Grenadier Division of the SS(1st Estonian), consisting of Estonians fighting in the Waffen SS. The infantry of the corps was engaged in direct battle with the Estonians on the German side in the battles of Porkuni and Avinurme on 20 and 21 September 1944, where a detachment of the rifle corps murdered a number of wounded prisoners of war. On 22 September elements of the 7th Rifle Division, along with the 45th Estonian Tank Regiment and the 952nd SU Regiment (SU-76s), formed the forward detachment of the corps and entered Tallinn, for which all three units received the name of that city as a battle honor.<cr>Appears to have spent the last of its World War II service in the 42nd Army.<cr>In total, 4100 settlements were captured by the 8th Estonian Rifle Corps. Of the whole rifle corps, one division, six regiments, and one battalion were decorated with an order. The 8th Estonian Rifle Corps was also given the honorific 'Tallinn', and on June 28, 1945, the corps was renamed the 41st Guards Estonian Tallinn Rifle Corps.<cr><cr>
translation:
该军在战争中共作战916天，先后在加里宁、列宁格勒和第2波罗的海方面军服役。其中344天与德国部队交战，但未取得重大进展。接下来的123天内，该部参与了维捷布斯克战役，在这场战斗中，有1.3万名士兵伤亡（总兵力为2.7万人）。随后37天用于纳尔瓦战役，最后88天则致力于库尔兰包围圈的作战。

在1944年的纳尔瓦战役期间，该步兵军的炮兵对德意志第20武装掷弹兵师（爱沙立亚第一）进行了火力打击。该部的步兵部队于1944年9月20日至21日在波克尼和阿文鲁梅战斗中直接与德国一方的爱沙尼亚人交战，期间一个分队杀害了多名受伤的德军俘虏。

9月22日，第7步兵师的部分兵力、第45爱沙立亚坦克团以及第952自行火炮团（SU-76）组成先遣部队进入塔林，并因此获得“塔林”荣誉。<cr>似乎在二战期间的最后服役是在第42集团军中。<cr>总计，该部俘获了4100个定居点。整个步兵军的一个师、六个团和一个营被授予勋章。该8th Estonian Rifle Corps 被赋予“塔林”的荣誉称号，并于1945年6月28日改名为第41近卫爱沙立亚塔林步兵师。<cr><cr>

text: The 41st Guards Rifle Division was formed as an elite infantry division of the Red Army in August, 1942, based on the 1st formation of the 10th Airborne Corps, and served in that role until after the end of WWII. It was the last of a series of ten Guards rifle divisions formed from airborne corps during the spring and summer of 1942. It was briefly assigned to the 1st Guards Army in Stalingrad Front, then to the 24th Army in Don Front, and suffered heavy casualties north of Stalingrad before being withdrawn to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command for a substantial rebuilding. Returning to 1st Guards Army in Southwestern Front in November it took part in Operation Little Saturn as part of 4th Guards Rifle Corps and then advanced into the Donbass where it was caught up in the German counteroffensive in the spring of 1943. During the summer and fall the division fought its way through eastern Ukraine as part of the 6th, and later the 57th Army under several corps commands. It would remain in the southern part of the front for the duration of the war. By February, 1944 it was in the 7th Guards Army and took part in the battle for the Korsun Pocket, winning its first battle honor in the process. Shortly after it was transferred to the 4th Guards Army, where it would remain for the duration, still moving through several corps headquarters. The 41st Guards saw limited service in the first Jassy-Kinishev Offensive in the spring, but considerably more in August's second offensive and several of its subunits received battle honors or decorations. The division itself won a second honorific during the offensive into Hungary in January, 1945 and was later decorated for its role in the capture of Budapest. After the fall of Vienna in April it did garrison duty in the city for a short time before being directed west into lower Austria where it linked up with U.S. forces in the last days of the war.<cr><cr>
translation:
第41近卫步兵师于1942年8月作为红军精锐步兵师组建，基于第十空降军的第一编成。它在该角色上一直服役到二战结束之后。它是1942年春夏季从空降军中组建的十个近卫步兵师中的最后一个。

该师曾短暂隶属于斯大林格勒方面军第一近卫集团军司令部，随后被调往顿河方面军第24集团军，并在斯大林格勒以北遭受了严重损失后撤至最高统帅部预备队进行大规模重建。1943年11月返回西南方向第一近卫集团军，在第四近卫步兵军的指挥下参加了土星行动，随后进入顿巴斯地区，在春季德国反攻中被围困。

夏季和秋季期间，该师作为第六集团军（后为第五十七集团军）的一部分在多个军司令部的指挥下穿越乌克兰东部。在整个战争期间它一直驻守在前线南部区域。

到1944年2月，第41近卫步兵师隶属于第七近卫集团军，并参加了科尔松包围圈战役，在此过程中赢得了第一个战斗荣誉。不久之后被调往第四近卫集团军，并在此停留直至战后，期间多次更换军司令部。

该师在春季第一次雅西-基什尼奥夫攻势中仅有限参战，但在8月的第二次攻势中发挥了重要作用，其多个下属单位获得了战斗荣誉或勋章。第41近卫步兵师还在1945年1月进入匈牙利时赢得了第二个荣誉，并因参与布达佩斯战役而获得嘉奖。维也纳陷落后的四月，该部队在该市短暂执行守备任务，随后被调往西面的下奥地利州，在战争最后几天与美军会合。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: A part of 27th Army in the Baltic Special Military District at the outbreak of hostilities, the corps participated in the battles on the Luga line in July 1941. At that time, it consisted of the 111th, 118th, and 125th Rifle Divisions. Transferred to 13th Army, it fought in the vicinity of Mogliev in July and August 1941, helping delay the advance of the Germans for almost three weeks. Dissolved in August 1941, it was reformed in July 1943 as part of 3rd Army, and fought in the Battle of Kursk. At that time, it consisted of 110th, 356th, and 415th Rifle Divisions. It fought in the Belorussian Offensive in 1944. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 作为波罗的海特别军区第27集团军的一部分，该军在1941年7月参加了卢加防线上的战斗。当时，它由第111、118和125步兵师组成。转隶至第13集团军后，该军于1941年7月至8月在莫吉廖夫附近作战，帮助推迟了德军推进近三周的时间。该军于1941年8月解散，并于1943年7月作为第3集团军的一部分重建，在库尔斯克战役中参战。当时，它由第110、356和415步兵师组成。该军参加了1944年的白俄罗斯进攻行动。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert，《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，Presidio Press，1985年<cr>词条由Stewart King提供

text: Kharkov MD, KOBO; established at Kryvyi Rih in 1940. With 6th Rifle Corps, 6th Army of the Soviet Southwestern Front from 22 June 1941. Wiped out at Kiev Sept 41. Recreated at Chapayevsk Mar 42, wiped out at Izyum May 42. Recreated again in Oct 42 at Verchovye from 118th Rifle Brigade, fought at the Battle of Kursk and in Poland. With 69th Army of the 1st Belorussian Front, May 45. Disbanded in the Group of Soviet Forces in Germany during the summer of 1945. Reformed 1955 from 264th Rifle Division, became 41st Motor Rifle Division in 1957.<cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack
translation: 哈尔科夫军区，KOBO；1940年在克里维伊罗格建立。从1941年6月22日起隶属于苏联西南方面军第6步兵军和第6集团军。1941年9月在基辅被消灭。1942年3月在恰佩利夫斯克重建，1942年5月在伊久姆再次被消灭。1942年10月在维尔霍韦从第118步兵旅重建，参加了库尔斯克战役和波兰的战斗。1945年5月隶属于第一白俄罗斯方面军第69集团军。1945年夏季解散于驻德苏军群。1955年重组自第264步兵师，1957年成为第41摩托化步兵师。<cr> <cr> <cr> <cr> 来源：NotOneStepBack

text:
The 41st Tank Division was formed March 1941 at Vladimir-Volynsk in Kiev Special Military District as part of 22nd Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
81st Tank Regiment
82nd Tank Regiment
41st Motorized Rifle Regiment
41st Howitzer Regiment
41st Reconnaissance Battalion
41st Motorized Pontoon Battalion
41st Antiaircraft Battalion<cr>
The 41st Tank Division, on paper, was well-equipped with armor by 22 June 1941: it had 100% of the authorized number of tanks. The reality was much worse: 342 of the tanks were T-26s, and almost 15% of those were unservicable on 15 June. The 31 KV-II heavy tanks had only arrived in the division a week before the Germans attacked: the crews were untrained on them, and there was not one round of ammunition available for their 152mm guns. While the rifle regiment was almost full strength in personnel, and had all its heavy weapons and machine guns, it was missing most of the trucks to move itself, and the howitzer regiment did not have a single tractor to move its guns. The reconnaissance battalion, antiaircraft battalion, and pontoon battalion were essentially company-sized units, missing 2/3 of their equipment.<cr> To make things, worse, from the first day of the war 41st Tank Division was attached to 15th Rifle Corps HQ, which constantly detached tank companies to support the rifle units. Most of these companies, opposing German panzer units without support and outnumbered at the point of contact, were destroyed before they could rejoin the division. On 26 June no less than 4 out of 8 tank battalions were detached to infantry support. By 6 July, the division had lost most of the T-26s, and had only 9 of the KV-IIs left. By 25 August, the division was down to 2000 men and a handful of tanks and armored cars. In September it was destroyed in the Kiev pocket.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第41坦克师于1941年3月在基辅特别军区的弗拉基米尔-沃林成立，隶属于第22机械化军。截至1941年6月22日包括：
第81坦克团
第82坦克团
第41摩托化步兵团
第41榴弹炮团
第41侦察营
第41摩托化舟桥连
第41防空营

按编制，第41坦克师在1941年6月22日装备了充足的装甲车辆：拥有授权数量的100%坦克。实际情况要糟糕得多：342辆坦克中有326辆是T-26型，其中近15%在6月15日无法使用。31辆KV-II重型坦克仅于德军进攻前一周抵达该师：车组人员尚未接受训练，并且没有一发炮弹可用于其152毫米主炮。虽然步兵团的人员几乎满编，并拥有所有重武器和机枪，但缺少大部分运输卡车以自行移动，而榴弹炮团则没有任何牵引车辆来移动火炮。侦察营、防空营和舟桥连实际上只是连级单位，缺少三分之二的装备。<cr> 为了使情况更糟，从战争第一天起，第41坦克师就被附属于第15步兵军司令部，该司令部不断派遣坦克连支援步兵单位。这些坦克连在接触点上面对没有支援的德国装甲部队且处于劣势，大多数在未能重新加入师之前就被消灭了。6月26日，多达8个坦克营中有4个被派去支援步兵。到7月6日，该师已经失去了大部分T-26坦克，并只剩下9辆KV-II。到8月25日，该师仅剩下2000人和少量坦克及装甲车。9月份，在基辅包围圈中被消灭。
<cr><cr>苏联战斗序列第一卷 查尔斯·C·夏普

text: The 42nd Army reated on 5 August 1941. Formed on the basis of the 50th Rifle Corps under the command of Major General Vladimir Ivanovich Shcherbakov. The army initially consisted of the 291st Rifle Division and the 2nd and 3rd Guards Leningrad Peoples' Militia Divisions. The 51st Corps, 690th Anti-Tank and 740th Artillery Regiments, and the Krasnogvardeisk Fortified Region soon joined the Army.<cr>During August 1941 the army formed a defensive line to the west, northwest and southwest of Krasnogvardeisk. By 19 August 1941, the leading German troops (1st and 8th Panzer Divisions) were fighting the troops of the Krasnogvardeisk Fortified Region. The army's final line of defence was formed on August 21, 1941, when German troops were forced to suspend the offensive in the south-western approaches to Krasnogvardeisk and go on the defensive. The 2nd Guards People's Militia Division especially distinguished itself during the fighting.<cr>During the period September 1941 to January 1944, the army was focused on improving the defense lines. An important mission for the army was counter-battery fire against enemy long-range artillery firing on Leningrad. In January 1943 the army allocated half of it forces to participate in Operation Spark, an attempt to break the blockade of Leningrad.<cr>In the late hours of January 13, 1944, long-range bombers from the Baltic Fleet attacked the main German command points on the defensive line, presaging the Krasnoye Selo-Ropsha Offensive. On January 14, troops from both the Oranienbaum foothold and Volkhov Front attacked, followed the next day by troops of the 42nd Army under the command of Ivan Maslennikov from the Pulkovo Heights. An artillery barrage was launched all along the front, laying down 220,000 shells onto the German lines. Fog inhibited major progress for the first few days, although the 2nd Shock Army and 42nd Army advanced two miles on a seven-mile front while in combat with the 9th and 10th Luftwaffe Field Divisions.<cr>The 42nd Army was tasked with breaking through the heavily fortified bands of enemy defenses established over the past two years. The 42nd Army first was to strike west to connect with the 2nd Shock Army advancing from the Oranienbaum bridgehead. Before the operation, 42nd Army was significantly reinforced; the main striking force of the army was the 30th Guards Rifle Corps. Soviet troops confronted L Army Corps (126th, 170th, 215th Infantry Divisions). The German artillery group consisted of 43 artillery battalions, 12 divisional artillery battalions ( summarized in the 125th, 240th, 215th and 11th Artillery Regiments) and 31 from OKH reserve. The front line of defense was from the coast of the Gulf of Finland to the river Izhorka Popova in the east. In the main line of defense, there were 13 German centers of resistance: Uritsk, Old Panov, Novo-Panov, Finnish Koyrovo, Kokkolevo rarely Kuzmino - Alexandrovka Big Kuzmino station Children's Village, New, State Farm 'Pushkin', settlement Volodarskogo Pushkin and Slutsk. In total, there were 34 centers of resistance strongpoints. The total depth of the enemy defense reached 13-15 kilometers. It took the army two full days to break through the left flank of the German lines. On the right flank was not as successful, with the army taking almost a week to break through the front lines and into the German rear areas.<cr>During 1945 it conducted a number of attacks against the German Army Group Courland positions. The attacks were conducted on 20-28 February, again on 17 March, but were unsuccessful. The army was still on the front lines for the surrender of the Army Group Courland.<cr><cr>
translation: 第42集团军成立于1941年8月5日。基于第50步兵军组建，由少将弗拉基米尔·伊万诺维奇·谢尔巴科夫指挥。该集团军最初包括第291步兵师和第二、第三近卫列宁格勒人民民兵师。不久之后，第51军、第690反坦克团和第740炮兵团以及克拉斯诺瓦尔代斯要塞区加入该集团军。<cr>1941年8月，该集团军在克拉斯诺瓦尔代斯西、西北和西南方向建立了防御线。到1941年8月19日，德军先头部队（第1装甲师和第8装甲师）与克拉斯诺瓦尔代斯要塞区的部队交战。该集团军最终防线于1941年8月21日形成，当时德军被迫在克拉斯诺瓦尔代斯西南方向停止进攻并转入防御状态。<cr>第二近卫人民民兵师尤其在这场战斗中表现出色。<cr>从1941年9月至1944年1月期间，该集团军专注于改善防线。一项重要任务是针对敌方远程炮兵对列宁格勒的射击进行反炮火作战。1943年1月，该集团军分配了一半兵力参与“火花”行动，试图打破列宁格勒的封锁。<cr>1944年1月13日晚，波罗的海舰队的远程轰炸机袭击了德军防御线上的主要指挥点，预示着克拉斯诺耶塞洛-罗普沙攻势即将开始。1月14日，奥拉宁baum桥头堡和沃尔霍夫方面军的部队发起了攻击，次日，在伊万·马斯连尼科夫少将指挥下的第42集团军从普尔科沃高地发起进攻。<cr>全线都进行了炮击，共发射了220,000枚炮弹到德军阵地上。由于大雾的影响，前几日进展不大，尽管第2突击集团军和第42集团军在与第9和第10德国空军野战师的战斗中推进了约3.2公里。<cr><cr>第42集团军的任务是突破过去两年内建立的坚固敌方防御带。首先，第42集团军要向西进攻以与从奥拉宁鲍姆桥头堡推进的第2突击集团军会合。在行动前，第42集团军得到了显著加强；主要突击力量为第30近卫步兵军。苏军面对的是L军（126师、170师和215师）。德军炮兵部队由43个炮兵团组成，其中包括12个师属炮兵团（分别隶属于第125、240、215和11炮兵团）以及来自陆军总司令部预备队的31个炮兵团。防御前线从芬兰湾海岸延伸到东部的伊佐尔卡波夫河。在主要防线上，有13个德军抵抗中心：乌里茨克、老帕诺夫、新帕诺夫、芬尼克奥约罗沃、科科尔列沃（有时为库兹明-亚历山大罗夫卡大库兹明站儿童村）、新村、普希金国营农场、普希金居民点和斯卢茨克。总计有34个抵抗中心强点。敌方防御纵深达13至15公里。集团军花了整整两天时间才突破德军左翼防线。而在右翼，进展并不顺利，集团军几乎花了一周时间才突破前线并进入德军后方区域。<cr>在1945年，该集团军对德国库尔兰集团军群阵地进行了多次攻击。这些攻击分别于2月20日至28日和3月17日进行，但均未成功。直到德国库尔兰集团军群投降时，第42集团军仍然在前线。<cr>

text: The 42nd Rifle Division was a unit of the Red Army during the World War II. The division, first formed in 1940, was nearly destroyed in the opening days of Operation Barbarossa defending the Brest Fortress. Disbanded in late December 1941 and immediately reformed in the Volga Military District. The division then served on the front until disbanded at the end of the war.<cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack
translation: 第42步兵师是红军在第二次世界大战期间的一个单位。该师成立于1940年，在巴巴罗萨行动初期保卫布列斯特要塞时几乎被消灭。该师于1941年底解散，并立即在伏尔加军区重建。之后，该师继续服役直至战争结束再次解散。<cr>词条由NotOneStepBack提供<cr>

text:
The 42nd Tank Division was formed March 1941 from 24th Light Tank Brigade at Gorkiy in Moscow Military District as part of 21st Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
83rd Tank Regiment
1 bn with 2 companies of 10 BT-7 tanks each, plus 1 HQ BT-7 tank
84th Tank Regiment
1 bn with 2 companies of 10 BT-7 tanks each, plus 1 HQ BT-7 tank
42nd Motorized Rifle Regiment
2 bns, one attached to each tank regiment
42nd Howitzer Regiment
1 light bn, 1 medium bn - short tractors
42nd Reconnaissance Battalion
42nd Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>Although formed from an existing tank brigade, 42nd Tank Division had no tanks assigned as late as 1 June 1941, and 70% of its personnel had arrived in the division in the last 2 months before the war started. General Lelyushenko, the corps commander, obtained 98 BT-7 tanks from the Armored Academy in Moscow, and reorganized his tank divisions as Tank Brigades: each tank regiment was organized as shown above, and enough trucks were found to motorize 1 rifle battalion for each tank regiment and some antitank guns which supported the tanks in place of the immobile howitzer regiment. With this organization the 42nd Tank Division went into action against 4th Panzer Group at Daugavpils in late June 1941.
42nd Tank fought back across the Baltic states under 21st Mechanized Corps until August 1941, when it was sent into Leningrad Front reserves and officially reorganized as 42nd Tank Brigade.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

第42坦克师于1941年3月在莫斯科军区的高尔基市从第24轻型坦克旅组建，隶属于第21机械化军。截至6月22日1941年包括：
第83坦克团
1个营，每个营有2个各配备10辆BT-7快速坦克的连队，另加1辆司令部用BT-7坦克
第84坦克团
1个营，每个营有2个各配备10辆BT-7快速坦克的连队，另加1辆司令部用BT-7坦克
第42摩托化步兵团
2个营，分别配属给两个坦克团
第42榴弹炮团
1个轻型营，1个中型营——短轮距牵引车
第42侦察营

尽管该师由一个现成的坦克旅组建而成，但直到1941年6月1日，第42坦克师仍未分配到任何坦克。其人员中有70%是在战争开始前两个月内加入的。军长列柳申科从莫斯科装甲学院获得了98辆BT-7快速坦克，并重组了他的坦克师为坦克旅：每个坦克团都按照上述结构组织，并找到了足够的卡车来摩托化1个步兵营配属给每个坦克团，以及一些反坦克炮以替代无法移动的榴弹炮团。凭借这种编制，第42坦克师于1941年6月下旬在道加瓦皮尔斯对抗第4装甲集团军时投入战斗。

从8月起，在列宁格勒方面军预备队中，该师被正式重组为第42坦克旅。
Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: The 43rd Army was created on 31 July 1941. From its formation the army defended the Desna River south of Yelnya on the line of Kholmets and Bogdanovo, fighting in the Battle of Smolensk. On 6 August, the 43rd with the 24th Army launched unsucessful attacks on German troops around Roslavl. On 2 October, the 4th Panzer Group and the 4th Army attacked the 43rd Army at its boundary with the Bryansk Front. The attack broke through the defenses of the 43rd Army, creating a 4-6 kilometer wedge in its positions. A counter-attack was stopped by the Luftwaffe. On 3 October, the army became part of the Western Front. It was ordered to defend the Snopot River. The army was beaten to the river by German troops and became disorganized. The army retreated in heavy fighting back to the Mozhaisk Defence Line. The army was pushed further back to the Nara River northwest of Serpukhov, where it stopped the German advance.<cr>During December 1941 and January 1942, the army fought in the counteroffensive at Moscow. Until April 1942 it fought in the Rzhev-Vyazma Offensive. On 20 April the army was defending the line of the Vorya River and the Ugra River west of Medyn. The army held the line until the end of August. On 1 September, it reconcentrated in the area northeast of Demidov. On 1 October, the army was assigned to the Kalinin Front. On 12 October its troops occupied the defenses northeast of Demidov.<cr>From January to August 1943 the army was positioned on the shores of Lakes Lososno, Rydov, Sapsho, and the village of Muzhitskaya. From 7 August to 2 October, the army was involved in the Battle of Smolensk. On 20 October the army became part of the 1st Baltic Front. Between November and December the army fought offensives towards Vitebsk.<cr>In February 1944 the army moved to the Haradok area. During the summer of 1944, the army fought in Operation Bagration. Between 23 and 29 June, the army fought in the Vitebsk-Orsha Offensive. The army's troops, operating in conjunction with the 6th Guards Army, broke through German defenses. Parts of the army along with the 39th Army surrounded five German divisions around Vitebsk and on 26 June captured the city. Subsequently the army destroyed the German pocket and captured Lepiel on 28 June. The 43rd Army then fought in the Polotsk Offensive between 29 June and 4 July. By 4 July it was in the Kazyany area. Developing the offensive towards Panevezys, the army captured Svencioneliai on 8 July. The army then repulsed several strong counterattacks and cut the Daugavpils-Vilnius Railway and Daugavpils-Kaunas Railway. By 14 July the army reached a line north of Salakas and Ovanty. During the advance towards Riga, the army fought in fierce battles for Birzai, which was finally captured on 6 August. From 13 August, the army defended the line of the Lielupe south and west of Bauska.<cr>In September the 43rd Army fought in the Riga Offensive and in October, the Battle of Memel. From mid-October to mid-January 1945 the army was involved in the blockade of the Courland Pocket. On 20 January the army was transferred to the 3rd Belorussian Front. Between 13 and 27 January it fought in the Interberg-Koenigsberg Offensive. The army fought in the Battle of Knigsberg from 6 to 9 April and the Samland Offensive from 13 April. It was moved to the area of Danzig, Gdynia, and Neustadt and on 1 May it became part of the 2nd Belorussian Front.<cr><cr>
translation: 第43集团军成立于1941年7月31日。从成立之初，该集团军就在叶连纳以南的德斯纳河一线（科姆列茨和博格达诺沃）防御德国军队。8月6日，第43集团军与第24集团军对罗贾尔斯附近的德军发动了未成功的攻击。10月2日，第4装甲集群和第4集团军在布良斯克方面军边界上向第43集团军发起了进攻。这次攻击突破了第43集团军的防御阵地，在其阵地上形成了一个宽4至6公里的楔形缺口。反攻被德国空军阻止。10月3日，该集团军成为西方面军的一部分，并奉命保卫斯诺波特河一线。德军先于该集团军抵达河流防线并使其陷入混乱。在激烈的战斗中，第43集团军撤退到莫扎伊斯克防御线。随后，它被进一步推回到塞普库霍夫西北部的纳拉河一线，在那里阻止了德国军队的推进。<cr>1941年12月至1942年1月期间，该集团军参加了莫斯科反攻作战。直到1942年4月，它都参与了日兹德拉-维亚兹马攻势行动。4月20日，该集团军在梅季扬以西的沃利亚河和乌格拉河一线进行防御，并一直坚守到8月底。9月1日，该集团军重新集中于德米多夫东北部地区。10月1日，它被分配给加里宁方面军。10月12日，其部队占领了德米多夫东北部的防线。<cr>从1943年1月至8月，该集团军驻扎在洛索诺湖、里多夫湖、萨普什奥湖岸边以及穆日奇斯卡亚村附近。从8月7日至10月2日，它参与了斯摩棱斯克战役。10月20日，该集团军成为波罗的海第1方面军的一部分。在11月至12月期间，它参加了向维捷布斯克方向的攻势行动。<cr>1944年2月，集团军转移到哈拉多克地区。在1944年的夏季，集团军参加了巴格拉季昂行动。6月23日至29日之间，集团军参与了维捷布斯克-奥尔沙进攻战役。集团军与第6近卫集团军协同作战，突破了德国的防御工事。集团军的一部分与第39集团军在维捷布斯克地区包围了5个德军师，并于6月26日占领了该城。随后，集团军消灭了德军的包围圈，并于6月28日占领了列皮埃尔。从6月29日至7月4日，第43集团军参加了波洛茨克进攻战役。到7月4日时，集团军已经推进到了卡扎尼亚地区。在向帕内韦哲斯发展攻势的过程中，集团军于7月8日占领了苏维亚尼艾利。之后，集团军击退了几次强大的反攻，并切断了道加瓦皮尔斯-维尔纽斯铁路和道加瓦皮尔斯-考纳斯铁路。到7月14日时，集团军推进到了萨拉卡斯和奥万蒂以北的战线。在向里加推进的过程中，集团军参加了激烈争夺比尔扎伊的战斗，并最终于8月6日占领了该城。从8月13日起，第43集团军参与了里加进攻战役，并在10月份参加了梅梅尔会战。从1945年10月中旬到次年1月中旬，集团军参与了库尔兰包围圈的封锁行动。1月20日，集团军被调往第三白俄罗斯方面军。1月13日至27日期间，集团军参加了因特贝格-柯尼斯堡进攻战役。从4月6日至9日，集团军参加了柯尼斯堡会战，并于4月13日起参与了萨姆兰进攻战役。集团军被调往但泽、格丁尼亚和纽斯塔特地区，并于5月1日成为第二白俄罗斯方面军的一部分。<cr><cr>9月份，第43集团军参加了里加进攻战役；10月份，则参加了梅梅尔会战。<cr>指挥官报告：从1945年10月中旬到次年1月上旬，集团军参与了库尔兰包围圈的封锁行动。1月20日，集团军被调往第三白俄罗斯方面军。1月13日至27日期间，集团军参加了因特贝格-柯尼斯堡进攻战役。<cr><cr>从4月6日至9日，集团军参加了柯尼斯堡会战，并于4月13日起参与了萨姆兰进攻战役。集团军被调往但泽、格丁尼亚和纽斯塔特地区，并于5月1日成为第二白俄罗斯方面军的一部分。<cr><cr>

text:
The 43rd Cavalry Division was one of the first cavalry divisions formed after the start of the war. The unit was formed in the North Caucasus Military District using the cadre and troops of the district's cavalry training grounds.<cr><cr>Declared ready for combat less than a week after formation the division was in the 21st Army by 19 July 1941. The next day the division was assigned to the Batskelevich Cavalry Group under the command of the 32nd Cavalry Division's commander. In July and August 1941 the group and the division raided into the rear areas and flanks of the German 2nd Army and 2nd Panzer Group south of Smolensk. In September 1941 the division was assigned as the mobile reserve group for the 21st Army and remained there until the end of the year.

The division took part in the Soviet Winter couteroffensive but the division like all the other units in the Southwestern Front was severely worn down prior to the start of the offensive. The remnants of the division were disbanded on 9 February 1942 to provide replacements for other cavalry units assigned to the front.<cr><cr>
translation:
第43骑兵师是在战争开始后不久组建的第一批骑兵师之一。该部队在北高加索军区使用军区内的骑兵训练场的骨干和人员组成。<cr>声明成立不到一周即做好战斗准备，到1941年7月19日，该师隶属于第21集团军。<cr>次日，该师被分配给巴特凯列维奇骑兵群，由第32骑兵师的指挥官指挥。在1941年7月至8月期间，该群和该师对德国第2集团军和第2装甲集群（位于斯摩棱斯克以南）后方及侧翼发动突袭。<cr>1941年9月，该师被分配为第21集团军的机动预备队，并一直担任此角色直到年底。

该师参加了苏联冬季反攻行动，但与西南方面军中的其他所有部队一样，在进攻开始前严重损耗。该师残部于1942年2月9日解散，以补充前线骑兵单位的人手。<cr>

text: The 43rd Guards Rifle Division was formed as an elite infantry division of the Red Army in October, 1942, based on the 1st formation of the 201st Rifle Division, and served in that role until after the end of WWII. The 201st was the only division made up of Latvian nationals in the Red Army until 1944, and the 43rd was immediately nicknamed the 'Latvian Guards' division, which stuck through its existence. Formed in Northwestern Front, its initial service was in the dismal fighting around the Demyansk salient until that was evacuated by German Army Group North in February, 1943. Through the rest of the year it fought in that Front, mostly facing the several German strongpoints in the area of Velikiye Luki. Beginning in January, 1944 the division took part in the offensive that finally drove the German forces away from Leningrad and before the summer offensive, now in 22nd Army of 2nd Baltic Front it provided a cadre to form the 130th Latvian Rifle Corps, and it served in that Corps for the duration of the war. Through 1943 and into 1944 the division was able to remain closer to full strength than many other Soviet units because it drew on a relatively large pool of Latvian refugee Communist Party members and Komsomols who had escaped ahead of the Germans in 1941. It crossed the border back into Latvia in July and entered Riga on October 16, winning a battle honor in the process. For the duration of the war the 43rd Guards served mostly in Leningrad Front, containing and reducing the German forces trapped in the Courland Pocket, and also engaging in restoration work in its war-battered homeland.<cr><cr>
translation:
第43近卫步兵师于1942年10月作为红军精锐步兵师组建，基于第201步兵师的第一次编成。该师一直服役到第二次世界大战结束之后。第201步兵师是红军中唯一一个由拉脱维亚国民组成的师，直到1944年。第43近卫步兵师一成立就被昵称为“拉脱维亚近卫”师，并且这个称呼一直沿用至今。

该师在西北方面军组建，在德军北方集团军群撤离德梅伊安斯克突出部之前，它参与了1943年2月的惨烈战斗。之后的一整年里，它继续在该方面军作战，主要面对维尔基耶卢基地区几个德国强点。

从1944年1月开始，该师参加了最终将德军赶离列宁格勒的进攻行动，并且在夏季攻势之前，在第二波罗的海方面军第22集团军中提供人员来组建第130拉脱维亚步兵军。它在整个战争期间都在这个军服役。

从1943年到1944年初，该师能够保持接近满编状态，因为它可以从相对较大的拉脱维亚难民共产党成员和共青团员的群体中招募士兵，这些人在1941年德军入侵前逃到了苏联境内。它于7月重新进入拉脱维亚，并在10月16日进入里加，期间赢得了一项战斗荣誉。

在整个战争期间，第43近卫步兵师主要在列宁格勒方面军服役，围困并削弱了被封锁在库尔兰包围圈中的德军，并且还参与恢复其饱受战火摧残的家园。

text: The 43rd Rifle Division was a formation of the Red Army, which took part in the Second World War, known to the Soviets as the 'Great Patriotic War'. The 43rd Rifle Division was formed in 1924-1925 in the Velikiye Luki region as part of the Leningrad Military District under the name of the 43rd Territorial Division. Stationed in the Western Special Military District. In autumn 1937 it was relocated directly in Leningrad. The division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner for participation in the Winter War. On June 24, 1941, when the Northern Front was formed, it became part of the 50th Rifle Corps, 23rd Army. In 1941 it fought in the defence of the Karelian isthmus during the Continuation War, from 1941 to 1944 in the Siege of Leningrad, in 1944 in the Leningrad-Novgorod Offensive, the Offensive Krasnoselsky-Ropshinskaya, Offensive Kingiseppsky-Gdovskii, the Baltic Offensive, Offensive Tartu, the Riga Offensive, and the Memel Offensive. In 1945 it fought in the Courland Pocket. With Leningrad Front May 1945. In the summer of 1945, the division moved to Kuybyshev, in the Ural Military District.<cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack
translation: 第43步兵师是红军的一个部队，参加了第二次世界大战，在苏联被称为“伟大卫国战争”。该师成立于1924-1925年，位于维捷布斯克地区的列宁格勒军区，当时称为第43领土师。驻扎在西部特别军事区。1937年秋季直接迁至列宁格勒。该师因参加冬季战争而获得红旗勋章。1941年6月24日北方方面军成立时，成为第50步兵军、第23集团军的一部分。1941年至1944年间，在继续战争期间保卫卡累利阿地峡，在列宁格勒围城战中作战，1944年参加列宁格勒-诺夫哥罗德进攻战役、克拉斯诺斯尔斯科耶-罗普申斯科耶进攻战役、金吉塞普斯科耶-热季沃斯科耶进攻战役、波罗的海进攻战役、塔尔图进攻战役、里加进攻战役和梅梅尔进攻战役。1945年在库尔兰包围圈作战。1945年5月隶属于列宁格勒方面军。1945年夏季，该师迁至库尔斯克，在乌拉尔军区。<cr>条目由NotOneStepBack提供

text:
The 43rd Tank Division wa formed March 1941 from 35th Light Tank Brigade at Berdichev in Kiev Special Military District as part of 19th Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
85th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd Tank Bns - each 51 T-26 tanks, 2 KV-I at Regt HQ
86th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd Tank Bns - each 51 T-26s
2 KVs, 2 T-34S at Regt HQ
43rd Motorized Rifle Regiment
43rd Howitzer Regiment
43rd Reconnaissance Battalion
43rd Sapper Battalion - no trucks<cr>
The 43rd Tank Division had only about 80% of its personnel by June 1941, and while it had 5 KVs, 2 T-34s, and 230 T-26 tanks, only the 7 modern tanks and 80 T-26s were servicable on 22 June - 36.7% of the total. The howitzer regiment, as usual, was missing most of the tractors for its howitzers (there were only 15 tractors in the entire division) and the antiaircraft battalion was never organized: the only light antiaircraft received was added to the recon bn as a separate company (see above).
The division did have the advantage that 35th Tank Brigade, from which it was formed, had been in the Winter War with Finland, so the division included a large percentage of combat veterans. When it moved out for the front on 22 June, the division commander organized his force into two groups.<cr>In constant fighting from the frontier to near Kiev, the division was whittled down until it mustered a combat strength of only 400 men by the end of July. In August the division was pulled back to Kharkov, and in September the surviving cadre of the division was used to form 10th and 12th Tank Brigades.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第43坦克师于1941年3月在基辅特别军区的伯迪切夫市，由第35轻型坦克旅组建，并隶属于第19机械化军。截至1941年6月22日包括：
85坦克团
第一、第二坦克营——每个营有51辆T-26坦克和2辆KV-I在团司令部
86坦克团
第一、第二坦克营——每个营有51辆T-26坦克
2辆KV，2辆T-34在团司令部
第43摩托化步兵团
第43榴弹炮团
第43侦察营
第43工兵营——无卡车<cr>

截至1941年6月，第43坦克师仅有约80%的人员到位。尽管拥有5辆KV、2辆T-34和230辆T-26坦克，但只有7辆现代坦克和80辆T-26坦克在6月22日可以使用——占总数的36.7%。榴弹炮团通常缺少牵引车（整个师仅有15辆牵引车），防空营从未组建：唯一收到的轻型高射炮被加到侦察营中作为独立连队（见上文）。
该师的优势在于，它是由参加过冬季战争的第35坦克旅组建而成，因此包含大量战斗经验丰富的老兵。当于6月22日向前线出发时，师长将部队分为两组。<cr>在从边境到基辅附近持续作战中，该师被削弱至7月底仅剩400名战斗人员。8月份，该师撤退至哈尔科夫，并在9月份，幸存的骨干力量用于组建第10和第12坦克旅。<cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普《苏联战斗序列第一卷》
