text: The 44th Infantry Division formed part of the 1st Panzer Group (later Army) in the initial advance into southern Russia. In 1941 and 1942, the 44th fought in the Ukraine, at Zhitomir, Kiev, and Kharkov, in the Donets, and in the initial advance toward the Caucasus, until being attached to the 6th Army for the drive on the Volga. In mid-November 1942, the remnants of the virtually destroyed 534th, 535th, and 536th Infantry Regiments of the recently dissolved 384th Infantry Division were attached to the 44th Division, which was cut off in Stalingrad with Friedrich Paulus's army soon after. The original 44th ceased to exist on January 31, 1943, three days before the last remnants of the 6th Army surrendered.<cr>A second 44th Infantry Division was recruited in Austria, in 1943, to replace the division destroyed at Stalingrad. By all accounts an excellent fighting unit, the 44th was sent to the Hungarian sector of the Eastern Front in February 1945, where it was soon reduced to Kampfgruppe (regimental) strength in heavy fighting and was largely destroyed at Jenoe on March 23. The remnants of the division nevertheless remained on the southern sector of the Eastern Front until the end of the war. They then managed to disengage from the Red Army and surrendered to the Americans north of Linz on May 8, 1945.<cr><cr><cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第44步兵师是最初进入南俄的第1装甲集团（后来成为集团军）的一部分。在1941年和1942年，第44师在乌克兰作战，在日托米尔、基辅、哈尔科夫以及顿涅茨地区战斗，并参与了向高加索地区的初步推进，直到被编入第6集团军进攻伏尔加河的行动中。1942年11月中旬，几乎被消灭的第384步兵师下辖的第534、535和536步兵团残部被编入了被困在斯大林格勒的第44师，该师不久后随弗里德里希·保卢斯指挥的集团军一起被围困。原第44师于1943年1月31日停止存在，三天前第6集团军的最后一支部队投降了。<cr>第二支第44步兵师在1943年奥地利招募成立，以取代在斯大林格勒被消灭的原第44师。据所有记录显示，该师是一支优秀的战斗部队，在1945年2月被派往东线匈牙利战区，在激烈的战斗中很快就被削弱到团级规模，并于3月23日在杰诺伊几乎全军覆没。然而，该师残部仍然坚守在东线南部战区直到战争结束。他们最终成功脱离红军的包围并向北林茨方向的美军投降，时间是1945年5月8日。<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷 1-290步兵师二战史 Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.

text: The corps was part of 13th Army near Minsk at the outbreak of hostilities. It participated in the Battle of Minsk and Battle of Smolensk and was the basis for the activation of 54th Army in August 1941. Reactivated as part of Kalinin Front in August 1943, it was it was a main attack corps in the initial assault in the Belorussian Offensive in June 1944 and was part of 4th Shock Army starting in July 1944. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation:
该军在1941年苏德战争爆发初期隶属于第13集团军，驻扎在明斯克附近。它参加了明斯克战役和斯摩棱斯克战役，并成为1941年8月激活第54集团军的基础。1943年8月重新组建后，作为加里宁方面军的一部分，在1944年6月白俄罗斯攻势初期突击中是主要攻击军之一，并从1944年7月起隶属于第4突击集团军。

Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert，《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，Presidio Press，1985

text: The 44th Kievskaya of the Red Banner Rifle Division of Nikolay Shchors, or 44th Kievskaya for short, was an elite military formation of the Soviet Union. Although it was an elite formation, the division was destroyed during the Winter War, after being ordered to help the 163rd Infantry Division break a Finnish siege on the Raate road. On 30 November 1939, it was part of the Special Rifle Corps, Ninth Army, together with the 54th Rifle Division. The division was recreated after its destruction and part of 13th Rifle Corps, 12th Soviet Army, Kiev Special Military District in June 1941. By 21 July 1941 the division was already short of shtat (establishment or Table of Organization and Equipment) by over 4,000 soldiers, 199 cargo trucks, and over 3,000 rifles and carbines. Divisional morale fell despite some small victories. Ultimately the division was wiped out in combat near the village of Podvyskoe in the Kirovograd and Uman region. The division was recreated at Leningrad in October 1941. It fought in northern Russia and Kurland with the 54th Army of Volkhov Front in January 1944 and the 67th Army of the Leningrad Front in May 1945.<cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack
translation: 尼古拉·什楚尔斯的第44基辅红旗步兵师，简称第44基辅师，是苏联的一支精英部队。尽管是一支精英部队，该师在冬季战争中被消灭，在接到支援第163步兵师突破芬兰对拉特公路包围的任务后覆灭。1939年11月30日，它隶属于特别步兵军、第九集团军，与第54步兵师同属一个单位。该师在被摧毁后重建，并于1941年6月成为第13步兵军、第12苏联集团军、基辅特别军区的一部分。到1941年7月21日，该师的编制表（TOE）已缺少超过4000名士兵、199辆货卡车和超过3000支步枪和卡宾枪。尽管取得了一些小胜利，但士气仍然下降。最终该师在基洛夫格勒和乌曼地区的波德维斯科耶村附近被消灭。该师于1941年10月在列宁格勒重建，并于1944年1月与沃尔霍夫方面军的第54集团军一起在俄罗斯北部和库尔兰作战，又于1945年5月与列宁格勒方面的第67集团军一同作战。<cr>指挥官报告：《决不后退一步》<cr>尼古拉·什楚尔斯<cr>第44基辅师<cr>

text:
The 44th Tank Division was formed in February - March 1941 from 23rd Light Tank Brigade in Odessa Military District as part of 18th Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
87th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd Tank Bns - each 30 T-26 tanks
88th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd Tank Bns - each 30 T-26 tanks
44th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
44th Motorized Howitzer Regiment - 1 light bn only
44th Reconnaissance Battalion
44th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr>
The 44th Tank Division was still forming when the war started, and its tanks were very old and worn out. Because no extra equipment had arrived, the Howitzer Regiment had no heavy howitzers, and the rifle regiment and artillery both had very few trucks or tractors. Only the fact that 18th Mechanized Corps was deployed in Southern Front against the Rumanians and out of the way of the Panzer Groups kept 44th Tank Division from being annihilated in the first weeks of the war. Nevertheless, by early July the division was down to one amalgamated tank regiment, and in August it was sent back to Kharkov, where in September the division was dissolved to provide cadres for new tank brigades.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第44坦克师成立于1941年2月至3月，由敖德萨军区的第23轻型坦克旅组建，并隶属于第18机械化军。6月22日包括:<cr>
第87坦克团
第1、第2坦克营——每个营配备30辆T-26坦克
第88坦克团
第1、第2坦克营——每个营配备30辆T-26坦克
第44摩托化步兵团
第1、第2、第3营
第44摩托化榴弹炮团——仅有一个轻型营
第44侦察营
第44防空营<cr>
当战争爆发时，该师仍在组建中，其坦克非常老旧且磨损严重。由于没有额外装备到达，榴弹炮团没有任何重型火炮，步兵团和炮兵都没有多少卡车或拖拉机。只有因为第18机械化军被部署在南方方面军对抗罗马尼亚军队，并远离德军装甲集群的进攻路线，第44坦克师才得以避免在战争初期就被消灭的命运。然而，到7月初，该师只剩下了一个合并后的坦克团，在8月又被调回哈尔科夫，在9月解散以提供新坦克旅的核心人员。<cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普《苏联战斗序列第一卷》

text: The 45th Infantry Division was part of the initial attack on the Soviet Union. The Austrian division suffered heavy casualties in the reduction of the fortress of Brest-Litovsk in June and July 1941. Later it fought at Pinsk, Gomel and at Tula (behind and south of Moscow) as part of the 2nd Panzer Army. It put up fierce resistance against the Soviet counteroffensive of December 1941, but was eventually forced to retreat. On December 12 Army Chief of the General Staff Franz Halder reported the division unfit for combat for lack of supplies. The next day its main withdrawal route was cut by the Russians, and part of the division was encircled and dispersed; much of its artillery had to be abandoned because its horses starved or froze to death. The 45th nevertheless remained in the line, fought on the southern sector of the Eastern Front in 1942 (at Orel and Voronezh), and was on the central sector throughout 1943. It suffered serious casualties in the Battle of Kursk in July 1943, when Hitlers last major offensive in the East was turned back. That autumn the division fought in the defense of Sozh, Bryansk, and Gomel, and in the subsequent retreats in the centra sector. The 45th Infantry was largely destroyed near Bobruisk in the Russian summer offensive of 1944, along with most of the rest of Army Group Center.<cr>The very few survivors of the 45th were used as the cadre of the 45th Grenadier Division, which was formed in the Dollersheim Maneuver Area. The new 45th merged with the 546th Grenadier Division (a Sperrdivision, or blocking division) and, as of July 18, 1944, included the 130th, 133rd, and 135th Grenadier Regiments (each with only two battalions), as well as the 98th Artillery Regiment and assorted divisional troops. The 45th Grenadier Division, however, was still understrength, so it was allowed to absorb the 1132nd Grenadier Regiment on September 22. Sent back to Poland, the division was renamed the 45th Volksgrenadier Division on October 21. It was in action on the Eastern Front by autumn, fought in the battles of Warsaw and Radom in early 1945, was pushed into Silesia, and finally capitulated at Kniggrtz, Czechoslovakia, in May 1945. By this time, only one of its grenadier regiments (the 130th) was still extant and, on April 20, 1945, it was redesignated Division Group 45 and was placed under the operational control of the Fhrer Grenadier Division.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第45步兵师是入侵苏联初期攻击部队的一部分。该奥地利师在1941年6月至7月期间，在布列斯特要塞的攻城战中遭受了严重伤亡。之后，它作为第二装甲集团军的一员参加了宾斯克、戈梅利和图拉（莫斯科后方及南部）的战斗。在1941年12月苏联反攻期间，该师进行了顽强抵抗，但最终被迫撤退。12月12日，总参谋长弗兰茨·哈尔德将军报告称由于补给不足，该师已无法作战。次日，其主要撤离路线被俄国人切断，部分部队被包围并分散；许多火炮因马匹饿死或冻僵而不得不放弃。尽管如此，第45步兵师仍留在前线，在1942年东线南部战区（奥廖尔和沃罗涅日）作战，并在1943年整个中央战区作战。该师在1943年7月库尔斯克战役中遭受了严重伤亡，当时希特勒最后一次重大攻势被击退。同年秋天，它参加了索日河、布良斯克和戈梅利的防御战斗以及随后中央战区的撤退行动。第45步兵师在1944年俄罗斯夏季攻势期间，在鲍里斯波尔附近几乎被消灭，与中央集团军群的大部分部队一同覆灭。<cr><cr>从第45师的少数幸存者中组建了第45掷弹兵师，该师在多勒斯海姆演习区成立。新编的第45师与第546掷弹兵师（一个阻击师）合并，并于1944年7月18日包括了第130、133和135掷弹兵团（每个团只有两个营），以及第98炮兵团和其他师属部队。然而，第45掷弹兵师仍然缺额，因此在1944年9月22日吸收了第1132掷弹兵团。该师被派回波兰，并于10月21日改名为第45国民掷弹兵师。它在东线方面军秋季投入战斗，在1945年初参加了华沙和罗兹的战役，随后被推入西里西亚地区，并最终于1945年5月在捷克斯洛伐克的库尼格雷茨投降。此时，只有它的掷弹兵团之一（第130团）仍然存在，并且该师于1945年4月20日重新命名为第45战斗群，并被置于元首掷弹兵师的作战指挥下。<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷 二战中的第1至290步兵师<cr>萨缪尔·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text: The corps was in the vicinity of Rogachev, near Gomel in July 1941. At that time, it consisted of 138th, 148th and 187th Rifle Divisions. It unsuccessfully opposed 2nd Panzer Group's attack across the Dnepr. The corps was reformed in May 1943 as part of 31st Army. At that time, it consisted of 88th, 220th, and 331st Rifle Divisions. It participated in the Battle of Smolensk in August and September 1943, and suffered heavy losses in the liberation of the city. Reinforced and reassigned to 5th Army, it participated in the Belorussian Offensive in June 1944 and crossed the Neman River in July 1944. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军于1941年7月驻扎在罗加乔夫附近，靠近戈梅利。当时它由第138步兵师、第148步兵师和第187步兵师组成。它未能阻止第2装甲集团的进攻，后者穿越了第聂伯河。该军于1943年5月作为第31集团军的一部分重组，当时包括第88步兵师、第220步兵师和第331步兵师。它参加了1943年8月至9月的斯摩棱斯克战役，并在解放该城市时遭受了重大损失。增援后并重新分配给第5集团军，它参与了1944年6月的白俄罗斯攻势，并于1944年7月渡过了尼曼河。<cr>指挥官报告: Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军战斗序列在伟大卫国战争中的变化, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 45th Rifle Division was a Red Army infantry division formed originally during the Russian Civil War that fought in World War II and then served through the Cold War in the Leningrad Military District. The division was originally formed 16 June 1919 in the Odessa raion from the 5th Ukrainian Rifle Division. It was attached to the Kiev Special Military District/Soviet Southwestern Front at the outbreak of World War II, as part of the 15th Rifle Corps, 5th Army. Under Colonel V.P. Solokov, it was earmarked to defend the mid-Volga River islands behind the hard-pressed 62nd Army on 7 October 1942. However it was deployed in Stalingrad proper on 26 October 1942, being ferried over from the east to the west bank of the Volga River to take up positions between the Red October and the Barrikady factories. On 1 January 1943 the division was re-designated the 74th Guards Rifle Division.<cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack
translation: 第45步兵师是红军的一个步兵师，最初成立于俄国国内战争期间，并参加了第二次世界大战，在冷战时期继续服役于列宁格勒军区。该师最初于1919年6月16日在敖德萨地区从第5乌克兰步兵师中组建而成。在第二次世界大战爆发时，它隶属于基辅特别军区/苏联西南方面军的第15步兵军、第5集团军。在V.P.索洛科夫上校指挥下，该师原计划于1942年10月7日在伏尔加河中游岛屿防御62集团军的背后压力。然而，它实际上是在1942年10月26日被部署到斯大林格勒市区的，在东岸通过运输工具运送到西岸的伏尔加河西岸，并在红十月和巴甫洛夫工厂之间布防。1943年1月1日，该师重新命名为第74近卫步兵师。<cr>感谢NotOneStepBack提供条目

The 45th Tank Division was formed February-March 1941 in western Kiev Special Military District as part of 24th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
89th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - only 1 company each
90th Tank Regiment

The division was destroyed in August in the Uman pocket south of Kiev.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: The 46th Guards Rifle Division was formed as an elite infantry division of the Red Army in October, 1942, based on the 2nd formation of the 174th Rifle Division, and served in that role until after the end of WWII. It was in the 6th Army of Voronezh Front when it won its Guards title, but was immediately moved to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command for rebuilding, where it was soon assigned to the 5th Guards Rifle Corps. In mid-November it moved with its Corps to join the 3rd Shock Army in Kalinin Front and played a leading role in the Battle of Velikiye Luki, both in the encirclement of the German garrison of that city and then in fighting off several relief attempts. It remained in the area through the spring and summer of 1943 before taking part in the breakthrough battle at Nevel and the subsequent operations to expand the salient and pinch off the German positions that 3rd Shock had partly surrounded. In June of 1944 the 46th Guards was reassigned to the 6th Guards Army of 1st Baltic Front in preparation for Operation Bagration and made a spectacular advance into Luthuania through the 'Baltic Gap' between Army Groups Center and North. The division would continue to serve in the Baltic states in 6th Guards for the duration of the war, winning the Order of the Red Banner in the process and ending on the Baltic coast in 22nd Guards Rifle Corps helping to contain the German forces trapped in the Courland Pocket.<cr><cr>
translation: 第46近卫步兵师于1942年10月作为红军精锐步兵师组建，基于第174步兵师的第二次改编。该师一直服役到二战结束之后。它在沃罗涅日方面军的第6集团军中赢得了近卫称号，但随即被调往最高统帅部预备队重建，并很快被分配给第5近卫步兵军。1942年11月中旬，该师随其所属军加入加里宁方面军第3突击集团军，在维捷布斯克战役中发挥了重要作用，既参与了对该城德军守备部队的包围行动，又在击退几次救援尝试时起到了关键作用。它一直驻扎在当地直到1943年春季和夏季，并参加了涅夫尔突破战以及随后扩大突出部并压缩第3突击集团军部分围困的德军阵地的作战行动。1944年6月，第46近卫步兵师被调往波罗的海方面军第1集团军群下的第6近卫集团军，为巴格拉季昂行动做准备，并通过“波罗的海缺口”（位于中央和北方集团军群之间）进行了壮观的推进进入立陶宛。该师将继续在波罗的海国家服役于第6近卫集团军直到战争结束，在此期间赢得了红旗勋章，并最终驻扎在库尔兰半岛包围圈中，帮助封锁了被围困的德军部队。

text: The 46th Infantry Division fought in Yugoslavia in April and took part in the Russian campaign, attacking through the Ukraine in July 1941 and penetrating the Perekop Isthmus in the northern Crimea in September. While the bulk of the 11th Army lay siege to the naval fortress of Sevastopol on the southwestern side of the Crimean peninsula, the 46th Infantry Division, now under Lieutenant General Kurt Himer, defended the eastern approaches to the Crimea on the Kerch peninsula. In the Russian winter offensive of 1941-42 it was attacked by two full Soviet armies. Ordered to hold at all costs, General Himer and his corps commander, General Hans Graf von Sponeck, decided to retreat against orders rather than to allow the division to be slaughtered. This action so infuriated Field Marshal Walther von Reichenau that he stripped the division of its banners and its honors. Hitler ordered both von Sponeck and Himer relieved of their commands. Within two weeks Field Marshal Reichenau was dead, and his successor, Field Marshal Fedor von Bock, ordered the banners returned and restored Himer to his command.<cr>Officially restored to honor, the division took part in the Siege of Sevastopol and in the Caucasus campaign of 1942-43, where it formed the rearguard of the XXXIX Mountain Corps in the subsequent retreat. Later it fought in the Kuban, the Donets, at Belgorod and Isjum, in the Battle of Dnepropetrovsk (where it was seriously damaged), and in the retreat through the southern Ukraine, where it again took heavy casualties. It was reduced from nine to six grenadier battalions in September 1943. Despite its reduced numbers, the 46th Infantry distinguished itself in the withdrawal through Transylvania and the Carpathians. In late 1944 the division--now at regimental strength--was in action on the Slovak-Hungarian frontier. It was reorganized and redesignated a Volksgrenadier division in March 1945. The remnants of the 46th surrendered to the Russians in the Deutsch-Brod sector of Czechoslovakia on May 8, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第46步兵师于1941年4月在南斯拉夫作战，并参加了对苏联的进攻，7月穿越乌克兰，在9月突破了克里米亚北部的佩雷科普地峡。当第11集团军主力在克里米亚半岛西南部围攻塞瓦斯托波尔海防要塞时，由库尔特·希默中将指挥的第46步兵师则驻守在克赤半岛东部地区，防御进入克里米亚的道路。在苏联于1941-42年冬季发动的大反攻中，该师遭到两个完整苏军集团军的攻击。接到死守命令后，希默将军和他的军长汉斯·格拉夫·冯·施波内克将军决定违令撤退，以免部队被全歼。这一行动激怒了瓦尔特·冯·里宾特洛甫元帅，他下令剥夺该师的荣誉和旗帜。希特勒命令解除冯·施波内克和希默两人的职务。<cr>不到两周时间，里宾特洛甫元帅去世，他的继任者费多尔·冯·博克元帅则下令归还旗帜，并恢复了希默的指挥权。<cr>正式恢复荣誉后，该师参加了塞瓦斯托波尔围城战和1942-43年的高加索战役，在随后的撤退中，它成为第39山地军后卫部队的一部分。之后，它在库班、顿涅茨克、别尔哥罗德和伊斯丘姆作战，并参加了第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克之战（在那里遭受了严重损失），以及通过南部乌克兰的撤退，在此过程中再次蒙受重大伤亡。1943年9月，该师从九个掷弹兵营减少到六个。尽管人数减少，第46步兵师在穿越特兰西瓦尼亚和喀尔巴阡山脉时表现出色。1944年底，该师（此时已降至团级规模）在斯洛伐克-匈牙利边境作战。1945年3月，它被重组并重新指定为国民掷弹兵师。第46师的残部于1945年5月8日在捷克斯洛伐克德意志-布罗德地区向苏联人投降。<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷 1至290步兵师在二战中的表现<cr>萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: The 46th Rifle Division was a rifle division of the Soviet Red Army, initially formed in 1921 in Ukraine during the Russian Civil War. The Division's 2nd formation formed in 1923 as a 'territorial' within the 136th, 137, 138th Rifle Regiment in Kiev in the 14th Rifle Corps in the Ukrainian Military District. On April 22, 1941, the division was part of the 32nd Rifle Corps, 16th Army, Transbaikal Military District, and still stationed in Irkutsk. The division commander was Maj. Gen. Alexander Filatov. The division was wiped out at Yelnaya in July 1941. Recreated at Ufa post-Jul 1941. Wiped out at Volkhov Pocket Jun 1942. Recreated from the 1st Rifle Division NKVD at Vaskelevo. Fought at Lutsk and Danzig. With 2nd Shock Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front, May 1945. When the Group of Soviet Occupation Forces in Germany was formed in August 1945, the division was with the 109th Rifle Corps, 2nd Shock Army.<cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack
translation: 第46步兵师是苏联红军的一个步兵师，最初于1921年在乌克兰的俄国内战期间组建。该师第二次组建是在1923年，在基辅作为“地方部队”加入第136、137和138步兵团，隶属于乌克兰军区的第14步兵军。1941年4月22日，该师属于远东军区的第16集团军下的第32步兵军，在伊尔库茨克驻扎。师长为亚历山大·菲拉托夫少将。该师于1941年7月在叶连纳被消灭。同年7月后在乌法重建。1942年6月在沃尔霍夫包围圈再次被消灭。从内务人民委员部第1步兵师重组，驻扎在瓦斯凯列沃。参加过卢茨克和但泽的战斗。1945年5月隶属于第二白俄罗斯方面军的第二突击集团军。当苏联占领德国部队于1945年8月成立时，该师属于第109步兵军、第二突击集团军。<cr>感谢NotOneStepBack提供资料

text:
The 46th Tank Division was formed in February-March 1941 in Moscow Military District as part of 21st Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
91st Tank Regiment
1 bn with 2 companies of 10 BT-7 tanks each, plus 1 HQ BT-7 tank
92nd Tank Regiment
1 bn with 2 companies of 10 BT-7 tanks each, plus 1 HQ BT-7 tank
46th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd bns, one attached to each tank regiment
46th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1 light, 1 medium bn - no trucks or tractors<cr>46th Reconnaissance Battalion
46th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
46th Antiaircraft Battalion
2 batteries only - 8 37mm guns<cr>
The 46th Tank Division, like 42nd Tank Division in the same corps, had no tanks when the war started, but 'picked up' some from the Red Army Armor Academy in Moscow before moving to the front. Organized effectively as a tank brigade, the division went over to the attack at Daugavpils against LVI Panzer Corps, and in one day lost its division commander, deputy commander, and most of its regimental commanders!
The division avoided complete destruction, and in August was sent into Leningrad Front reserves, where on 21 August it officially formed into 46th Tank Brigade.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第46坦克师成立于1941年2月至3月，在莫斯科军区作为第21机械化军的一部分组建。1941年6月22日编制如下：
<cr>
第91坦克团
1个营，每个营有2个各装备10辆BT-7快速坦克的连队，另加1辆司令部用BT-7快速坦克
第92坦克团
1个营，每个营有2个各装备10辆BT-7快速坦克的连队，另加1辆司令部用BT-7快速坦克
第46摩托化步兵团
第1、第2营，分别配属给两个坦克团中的一个
第46摩托化榴弹炮团
1个轻型营和1个中型营——无卡车或拖拉机<cr>
第46侦察营
第46机械化舟桥营
第46防空营
仅有2个连队——8门37毫米高射炮<cr>
与同属该军的第42坦克师一样，第46坦克师在战争开始时没有坦克，但在开赴前线前从莫斯科红军装甲学院“接收”了一些。作为有效的坦克旅编制，该师对达乌加皮尔斯的LVI装甲军发起了攻击，并在一天内失去了师长、副师长和大部分团级指挥官！
该师避免了彻底毁灭，在8月被调往列宁格勒方面军预备队，在8月21日正式改编为第46坦克旅。<cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普《苏联战斗序列 第一卷》

text:
The 47th Cavalry Division was one of the first cavalry divisions formed after the start of the war. The unit was formed at Novocherkassk in the North Caucasus Military District from reservists and the cavalry depots in the district's cavalry training grounds.<cr><cr>The division was rushed to the front less than two weeks after being formed. It arrived in the 21st Army by the middle of July and was assigned to the Batskelevich Cavalry Group under the command of the 32nd Cavalry Division's commander. In July and August 1941 the group and the division raided into the rear areas and flanks of the German 2nd Army and 2nd Panzer Group south of Smolensk. The division was on the southern edge of the German offensive against the Western Front.

Assigned to the Southwestern Front reserves in October and November. The continuous fighting in October and November wore down all the units in the front and replacements had to be found for them. As a result, the division was disbanded on 10 November 1941 and the troops used to reinforce the 32nd Cavalry Division.<cr><cr>
translation:
第47骑兵师是在战争开始后不久组建的第一批骑兵师之一。该部队在北高加索军区的诺沃切尔卡斯克从预备役人员和军区内的骑兵补给站中组建而成。<cr>该师成立不到两周就被紧急调往前线，并于7月中旬抵达第21集团军，并被分配至巴特谢列维奇骑兵群，由第32骑兵师指挥官指挥。在1941年7月和8月期间，该群及该师对德国第2集团军和第2装甲集群（位于斯摩棱斯克以南）的后方区域和侧翼进行了突袭行动。<cr>该师处于德军进攻西方方面军南部边缘的位置。

在10月和11月被分配给西南方面军预备队。由于10月和11月连续不断的战斗，前线的所有部队都受到了削弱，并且必须找到替换人员。因此，该师于1941年11月10日解散，其兵力用于增援第32骑兵师。<cr>

text: The corps was stationed near Brobruysk at the outbreak of hostilities. At that time it consisted of 55th, 121st, and 143rd Rifle divisions. It was destroyed July 1-2 in fighting around Borisov, near Minsk. Reformed in July 1943 as part of 40th Army, it participated in the Battle of Kursk, and in the subsequent Belgorod-Kharkov Offensive. It was an independent corps and was assigned to support 6th Guards Tank Army in January 1944. It participated in the suppression of the Korsun-Cherkassy Pocket. At that time, it consisted of 38th, 136th, 167th, 180th and 359th Rifle Divisions. In March 1944, it operated in support of 1st Guards Army during the Proskurov-Chernovits Offensive in March 1944. In May 1944, it participated in the Second Battle of Trgu Frumos. It was the reserve corps for 1st Ukrainian Front during the Lvov-Sandomierz Operation in June-July 1944. In 1945, as a part of Second Belorussian Front, it participated in theBerlin Strategic Offensive. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation:
该军在敌对行动爆发时驻扎在布罗迪斯克附近。当时它由第55、121和143步兵师组成。7月1日至2日在鲍里斯夫附近明斯克地区作战中被消灭。1943年7月重建，作为第40集团军的一部分参加了库尔斯克战役，并随后参加了别尔哥罗德-哈尔科夫进攻行动。它是一个独立的军，在1944年1月被分配支援第6近卫坦克集团军，参与了科尔松切卡斯基包围圈的肃清行动。当时它由第38、136、167、180和359步兵师组成。1944年3月，在普罗斯库罗夫-切尔诺维策进攻中支援第1近卫集团军作战。1944年5月，参加了特鲁日弗鲁莫斯第二次战役。在1944年6月至7月的利沃夫桑多尔采夫行动期间，它是第一乌克兰方面军预备军。1945年作为第二白俄罗斯方面军的一部分，参加了柏林战略进攻。

Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert，《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，Presidio Press, 1985

text: The 47th Rifle Division was an infantry division of the Red Army. It was first formed in 1922 as the Georgian Rifle Division. In 1924, it became the 1st Georgian Mountain Division. The division became the 47th Georgian Mountain Rifle Division in 1936 and dropped the designation 'Georgian' in 1940. It was disbanded in June 1942 after being wiped out at Izyum. In July 1942, the 47th Rifle Division was formed from the 21st Rifle Brigade. It fought in the Nevel Offensive, for which it was awarded the title "Nevel"". The division was disbanded in the Baltic Military District in 1946.<cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack"
translation: 第47步兵师是红军的一个步兵师。它最初于1922年作为格鲁吉亚步兵师组建。1924年，该师成为第一格鲁吉亚山地师。1936年，该师更名为第47格鲁吉亚山地步兵师，并在1940年取消了“格鲁吉亚”的标识。它于1942年6月因伊久姆战役被消灭而解散。1942年7月，第47步兵师从第21步兵旅重组而成。该师参加了内夫尔攻势，并因此获得了“内夫尔”称号。该师在1946年波罗的海军区再次解散。<cr>条目由NotOneStepBack提供

text:
The 47th Tank Division was formed February 1941 from 49th Light Tank Brigade in Odessa Military District as part of 18th Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
93rd Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd Tank Bns - each 30 T-26S tanks
94th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd Tank Bns - each 30 T-26S tanks
47th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
47th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1 light, 1 medium bn
47th Reconnaissance Battalion
47th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
47th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr>
The 47th Tank Division had the newest tanks in 18th Mechanized Corps, but the 49th Tank Brigade it was formed from had only been formed itself in late 1940 - the division had less than 150 tanks overall, and very few experienced tank crew, NCOs, or officers. By August 47th Tank Division was operating independantly as a mobile reserve for 18th Army, and then 38th Army in Southwestern Front. In October 1941 the remnants of the division were sent back to the North Caucasus Military District and converted into 47th Tank Brigade.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp
translation:
第47坦克师成立于1941年2月，由敖德萨军区的第49轻型坦克旅组建，并隶属于第18机械化军。6月22日编成如下：
第93坦克团
第1、第2坦克营——每营30辆T-26S坦克
第94坦克团
第1、第2坦克营——每营30辆T-26S坦克
第47机械化步兵团

轻型和中型各一个营

第47坦克师拥有第18机械化军中最新型的坦克，但其组建基础的第49坦克旅本身仅于1940年底成立——该师总共只有不到150辆坦克，并且几乎没有经验丰富的坦克乘员、士官或军官。到8月，第47坦克师作为机动预备队独立运作，隶属于第18集团军，随后是西南方面军的第38集团军。1941年10月，该师残部被调回北高加索军区，并改编为第47坦克旅。

text: The army was first formed in August 1941. The army was assigned to Northwestern Front and was responsible for the front's left flank north of Lake Ilmen. It also had under command the Ilmen Detachment of Ships. On 12 August the army, along with the 11th, 27th and 34th Armies, began a series of assaults against the German X Army Corps near Staraya Russa. These attacks failed to regain much territory but delayed the German advance on Leningrad by a further week.<cr>Following this, the 48th took up positions forward of Luga and Novgorod as part of the Luga defense line. That line was penetrated in the renewed German advance, and Luga fell on 20 August, with heavy Soviet casualties; the army was a wreck with only 6,235 men, 5,043 rifles and 31 guns remaining. It was transferred to the Northern Front and ordered to defend the Gruzino-Liuban sector southeast of Leningrad. On 23 August Northern Front was subdivided, and 48th Army became part of the new Leningrad Front.<cr>On 1 September the 48th comprised the 128th and 311th Rifle Divisions, the mountain brigade, the 541st Gun Artillery Regiment of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command and the 21st Tank Division. At this time, it was commanded by Lieutenant General Maxim Antoniuk. Heavy attacks by the German XXXIX Motorized Corps forced the army to abandon Mga, a key railway link. Akimov was ordered to retake the town, which he did with the help of a fresh division of NKVD border guards, but the town was lost again the next day. During the first week of September the 20th Motorized Division, reinforced with elements of 12th Panzer Division, ground its way northwards against the resistance of the mountain brigade and the NKVD men before capturing Shlisselburg on Lake Ladoga on 8 September, isolating Leningrad, with the bulk of the army outside, to the east. On 12 September, the remnants of 48th Army were disbanded, being reassigned to the new 54th Army.<cr>Reformed in April 1942 on the Bryansk Front, the army fought in the Maloarkhangelsk Offensive in the winter of 1943. It was sent to the Central Front in March and defended the northern face of the Kursk Bulge. During the summer, it fought in Operation Kutuzov and the Chernigov-Pripyat Offensive. From November, the army fought in the Gomel-Rechitsa Offensive. The army fought in Operation Bagration from June 1944. During the offensive, the army captured Zhlobin and Bobruisk and was on the Narew by early September. During early 1945, the army fought in the East Prussian Offensive and ended the war in East Prussia during May. <cr><cr>
translation: 该集团军成立于1941年8月。它被分配到西北方面军，并负责伊尔门湖以北前线的左翼。此外，还指挥着伊尔门船只分遣队。8月12日，该集团军与第11、第27和第34集团军一起，在斯塔罗耶鲁萨附近对德国第十军发起了多次进攻。这些攻击未能收复多少领土，但推迟了德军向列宁格勒推进的进程一周。<cr><cr>随后，第48集团军在卢加和诺夫哥罗德前方占据了卢加强势防御线的位置。该防线在新一轮德军攻势中被突破，卢加于8月20日失陷，苏军伤亡惨重；此时该集团军只剩下6,235人、5,043支步枪和31门火炮。它随后被转移到北方方面军，并被命令保卫列宁格勒东南方向的古里诺-柳班地区。<cr>8月23日，北方方面军被拆分，第48集团军成为新成立的列宁格勒方面军的一部分。1941年9月1日，第48集团军包括第128步兵师、第311步兵师、山地旅、最高统帅部预备队的第541门炮团和第21装甲师。此时由上将马克斯·安东尤克指挥。德国XXXIX摩托化军的猛烈攻击迫使该集团军放弃关键铁路枢纽麦加镇。阿基莫夫被命令夺回该城镇，他得到了新组建的一支内务人民委员部边防部队的支持，但次日又失去了该城镇。9月初，第20摩托化师在第12装甲师的增援下向北推进，在山地旅和内务人民委员部边防部队的抵抗下攻占了拉多加湖畔的施利谢尔堡，将列宁格勒与外部隔绝开来。该集团军主力位于东面。9月12日，第48集团军残部被解散，并重新编入新成立的第54集团军。<cr>重建于1942年4月在布良斯克方面军，该集团军参加了1943年冬季的小阿尔汉格尔斯克攻势。3月份，它被调往中央方面军，并防守库尔斯克突出部的北面。夏季期间，它参加了库图佐夫行动和切尔尼戈夫-普里皮亚季攻势。从11月起，该集团军参加了戈梅利-雷奇察攻势。自1944年6月至巴格拉季昂行动以来，该集团军一直参战，并在早期9月攻占了日洛宾和鲍里斯波尔，并推进至纳雷夫河附近。1945年初，该集团军参加了东普鲁士攻势，并于5月在东普鲁士结束战争。<cr>指挥官报告

text: The 48th Guards Rifle Division was formed as an elite infantry division of the Red Army in October, 1942, based on the 2nd formation of the 264th Rifle Division, and served in that role until after the end of WWII. It was in the 3rd Tank Army when it formed but this force was badly mauled in Army Group South's counteroffensive south of Kharkov in March, 1943 and the division had to be withdrawn for a substantial rebuilding in 57th Army of Southwestern Front during the spring. It remained in the south of Ukraine into early 1944, mostly in either that or the 37th Army, and won a battle honor in the process. It was then removed to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command for another rebuilding before returning to the front in May, 1944 and joining the 28th Army, where it remained for the duration of the war. Taking part in the summer offensive in Belarus the 48th Guards was awarded the Order of the Red Banner and several of its subunits also received decorations or distinctions. In January, 1945 the division fought into East Prussia and assisted in the fighting southwest of the city of Knigsberg before 28th Army was redeployed westward to take part in the Berlin operation. By now it was part of 1st Ukrainian Front and spent the last days of the war advancing on Prague. <cr><cr>
translation: 第48近卫步兵师于1942年10月作为红军的精锐步兵师组建，基于第264步兵师的第二次改编。该师一直服役到二战结束之后。它最初隶属于第三坦克集团军，在1943年3月南方集团军群在哈尔科夫以南发动反攻时遭受重创，不得不撤出进行重建，当时是在西南方面军的第57集团军中。直到1944年初该师仍然驻扎在乌克兰南部，主要隶属于第57集团军或第37集团军，并在此过程中获得了一项荣誉。随后它被调到最高统帅部预备队进行另一次重建，在1944年5月重返前线并加入第28集团军，直到战争结束都一直驻扎在那里。在白俄罗斯夏季攻势中，第48近卫步兵师获得了红旗勋章，并有多支下属部队也获得了一些荣誉或表彰。1945年1月该师进入东普鲁士作战，在柯尼斯堡西南部协助战斗后，第28集团军被重新部署到柏林战役中。此时它已成为第一乌克兰方面军的一部分，并在战争最后几天向布拉格推进。<cr><cr>@@<cr>

text: This corps was an independent unit in STAVKA reserve at the outbreak of hostilities. It consisted of 30th Mountain Rifle and 74th Rifle Divisions, and was commanded by future Hero of the Soviet Union and Marshal Rodion Malinovsky. It was assigned to the border region in the vicinity of Odessa in support of 9th Army. It fought around Beltsy in early July 1941 during Operation Mnchen. It formed part of a Shock Group with 2nd Cavalry Corps and 2nd Mechanized Corps near Mogliev-Podolsk in late July and then defended the Yuzhny Bug line near Nikolaev in August. It was withdrawn from the line in late August and was the basis for the second formation of 6th Army. Reformed in July 1943, it participated in the Battle of Kursk. It appears to have still been an independent corps under Steppe, later 2nd Ukrainian Front, assigned to support a variety of armies. In January 1944, it consisted of 14th Guards Rifle and 252nd and 299th Rifle Divisions. It participated in the Belgorod-Kharkov Offensive and the crossing of the Vorskla River in 1943, the liberation of Kirovgrad in January 1944, and the Berlin Strategic Offensive in 1945. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军在冲突爆发时是最高统帅部大本营预备队中的独立单位。它由第30山地步兵师和第74步兵师组成，由未来的苏联英雄及元帅罗季翁·马林诺夫斯基指挥。它被分配到敖德萨附近的边境地区支援第9集团军。1941年7月初，在“慕尼黑”行动期间，该军在别列茨附近作战。7月底，它与第2骑兵军和第2机械化军组成突击群，在莫吉廖夫-波多利斯基附近活动，并于8月在尼古拉耶夫附近的尤日内布河沿线进行防御。8月下旬从战线撤出后，成为第6集团军第二次组建的基础。1943年7月重建后，该军参加了库尔斯克战役。它似乎仍然是独立的军，在草原方面军（后来为第2乌克兰方面军）指挥下，被分配支援多个集团军。1944年1月，该军由第14近卫步兵师、第252和第299步兵师组成。它参加了别尔哥罗德-哈尔科夫进攻战役以及1943年的沃斯克拉河渡河行动，解放了基洛夫格勒，并在1945年参与了柏林战略攻势。<cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text:
The 48th Tank Division was formed February-March 1941 in Orel Military District as part of 23rd Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
95th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd Tank Bns - each 30 to 40 light tanks
96th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd Tank Bns - each 30 to 40 light tanks
48th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
48th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1 light bn
48th Reconnaissance Battalion
48th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
48th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr>
This unit was formed outside the frontier Military Districts, and so had no priority for equipment or personnel. Almost 40% of the 150 tanks in the division required major or depot repair work on 1 June, and the non-tank elements of the division were almost completley lacking trucks and tractors.
Nevertheless, 48th Tank Division went into action with 19th Army in early July against 3rd Panzer Group. By 10 July The last of the division's tanks were being split off in a separate tank battalion (no number designation) to support rifle units in 22nd Army. In September the division was disbanded to provide cadres for new tank brigades.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

该部队是在非边境军区组建的，因此在装备和人员方面没有优先权。截至6月1日，该师约有150辆坦克中近40%需要进行重大维修或补给站修理工作，而师内非坦克部分几乎完全缺乏卡车和拖拉机。

尽管如此，第48装甲师于7月初在第19集团军的指挥下与第3装甲集群作战。到7月10日，该师最后一批坦克被拆分成立一个独立的坦克营（无编号），以支援第22集团军中的步兵单位。9月份，该师解散重组为新组建的坦克旅提供骨干力量。

text: On 6 August 1941, a Stavka directive ordered the formation of the 49th Army. One day later the army was formed as part of the Reserve Front, based on the 35th Rifle Corps, commanded by Lieutenant General Ivan Zakharkin.<cr>On 12 October 1941, the 49th Army was placed on the Mozhaisk defense line in the Kaluga area, after giving up its sector to the 32nd Army. The Mozhaisk line was credited for slowing down the German approach toward Moscow. During the Soviet counteroffensive at Moscow, the army fought in the Tula Offensive between 6 and 16 December, and the Kaluga Offensive between 17 December and 5 January 1942.<cr>On 8 January, the 49th Army began fighting in the Rzhev-Vyazma Strategic Offensive, which aimed to eliminate the heavily fortified Rzhev salient, which threatened Moscow. On 5 March, troops of the army recaptured Yukhnov, and by 20 April reached the Ugra and the Ressa Rivers, both west of Yukhnov. The 49th Army held the same positions until March 1943.<cr>From 7 August to 2 October, the 49th Army participated in the Smolensk Operation, advancing towards Spas-Demensk, Stodolishche, and Khislavichi in its first phase, the Spas-Demensk Offensive. Resuming the attack in the Yelnia-Dorogobuzh Offensive on 28 August, the army advanced through the forests south of Yelnya and crossed the Desna River and the Sozh River. On 28 September the army recaptured Mstsislaw, and in early October reached the Pronya River in the Drybin Raion, 35 kilometers north of Chavusy, where it went on the defensive.<cr>From 24 April 1944 to the end of the war, the 49th Army was subordinated to the 2nd Belorussian Front. From late June, the army fought in Operation Bagration, the Soviet strategic offensive in Belorussia and eastern Poland. <cr>From 13 January to 25 April 1945, the 49th Army fought in the East Prussian Offensive. Between 10 February and 4 April, it participated in the East Pomeranian Offensive. The army captured Czersk on 21 February and Berent on 8 March. The army continued its advance towards Danzig, which was taken on 30 March. The army's last operation was the Berlin Offensive, from 16 April to 8 May, during which it advanced in the main shock group of the front. At the end of the war, the 49th Army reached the Elbe in the Ludwigslust area, where it met troops of the British Second Army. <cr><cr>
translation: 1941年8月6日，最高统帅部大本营下达指令组建第49集团军。次日，该集团军在预备方面军内成立，由步兵军改编而成，由伊万·扎哈尔金中将指挥。<cr>1941年10月12日，第49集团军被部署到莫扎伊斯克防线的加里宁格勒地区，在将其防区移交给第32集团军后。莫扎伊斯克防线被认为减缓了德军向莫斯科推进的速度。<cr>在苏联对莫斯科的反攻中，该集团军于1941年12月6日至16日参加了图拉攻势，并于12月17日至1942年1月5日参与了加里宁格勒攻势。<cr>1942年1月8日，第49集团军开始参加列日-维亚兹马战略进攻行动，旨在消灭威胁莫斯科的列日突出部。3月5日，该集团军部队重新占领尤赫诺夫，并于4月20日前推进至尤赫诺夫以西的乌格拉河和雷萨河。<cr>第49集团军一直坚守相同位置直到1943年3月。<cr>从1941年8月7日至10月2日，第49集团军参加了斯摩棱斯克行动，在第一阶段的列日-德梅尼茨攻势中向斯帕斯-德梅尼茨、斯托多利什切和基斯拉维奇推进。在8月28日恢复对叶连纳-多罗戈布扎攻势后，该集团军穿越了叶连纳以南森林中的德嫩河和索热河。<cr>9月28日，该集团军重新占领姆茨斯拉夫，并于10月初推进至查乌西西北35公里的普罗尼亚河，在那里转入防御状态。<cr>从1944年4月24日至战争结束，第49集团军隶属于第二白俄罗斯方面军。自6月下旬起，该集团军参加了巴格拉季昂行动，这是苏联在白俄罗斯和东波兰的战略进攻行动。<cr>从1945年1月13日至4月25日，第49集团军参加了东普鲁士进攻。从2月10日至4月4日，它参与了波美拉尼亚东部进攻。该集团军于2月21日占领切尔斯克，3月8日占领贝伦特。该集团军继续向但泽推进，后者于3月30日被攻占。该集团军的最后一项行动是柏林进攻，从4月16日至5月8日，在此期间它作为方面军主要突击群向前推进。在战争结束时，第49集团军到达了卢茨恩斯多夫地区的易北河，并与英国第二集团军的部队会合。<cr><cr><cr>

text:
The 49th Guards Rifle Division was formed in the Western Front reserves near Moscow on 13 October 1942 from the remains of the 2nd Guards Motor Rifle Division. The unit was immediately assigned to the newly formed 13th Guards Rifle Corps in the 2nd Guards Army. They were sent south to the Stalingrad area in December 1942 and went into action south of Stalingrad. When formed, its order of battle was as follows:

144th Guards Rifle Regiment
147th Guards Rifle Regiment
149th Guards Rifle Regiment
100th Guards Artillery Regiment
56th Guards Separate Anti-tank Battalion
64th Guards Anti-Aircraft Battery (up to 25 April 1943)
1st Guards Machine Gun Battalion (up to 1 June 1943)
51st Guards Reconnaissance Company
57th Guards Separate Sapper Battalion
77th Guards Separate Signals Battalion
561st (53rd) Medical and Sanitation Battalion
52nd Guards Separate Chemical Defense Company
609th (53rd) Auto-Transport Company
638th (48th) Field Bakery
641st (50th) Divisional Veterinary Hospital
572nd Field Postal Station
44th Field Office of State Bank

Troops of the division on the march during the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive, late August 1944. Later the division helped liberate Kherson (the name 'Khersonskaya' was conferred on the division). It took part in the liberation of Romania and Hungary. The division ended the war in Austria. By this time the division had the following honorifics: Khersonskaya, Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov 2nd Class.<cr><cr>

text: The corps was part of Kiev Military District at the outbreak of hostilities and was destroyed in the Kiev Pocket in August 1941. Reformed in July 1943, it appears to have been a reserve corps that operated in support of 53rd Army, 7th Guards Army, 57th Army, and 5th Guards Tank Army at different times during 1943-45. It participated in the Battle of the Dnieper in September 1943, and the reduction of the Korsun-Cherkassy Pocket in January 1944. It was later deployed to Manchuria. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King

text: The 49th Rifle Division was a Soviet Army infantry division, formed three times. First formed as a territorial division in 1931, the 49th Rifle Division's first formation became a regular division by 1939 and fought in the Winter War. For its actions during the war, it was awarded the Order of the Red Banner. However, the 49th Rifle Division was wiped out during the first ten days of Operation Barbarossa. Its second formation occurred in December 1941 and fought at Stalingrad, Battle of Kursk , the Vistula-Oder Offensive and the Battle of Berlin. The second formation was disbanded in 1946. The division was reformed in 1955 by renaming the 295th Rifle Division and became the 49th Motor Rifle Division in 1957.<cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack
translation:
第49步兵师是苏军的一个步兵师，曾三次组建。第一次是在1931年作为地方部队成立，在1939年前后转为常备师，并参加了冬季战争。由于在战争中的表现，该师获得了红旗勋章。然而，在巴巴罗萨行动的前10天里，第49步兵师被彻底消灭了。第二次组建是在1941年12月，参加了斯大林格勒战役、库尔斯克会战、维斯瓦河-奥得河攻势以及柏林战役。第二次组建在1946年解散。该师于1955年重组，通过将第295步兵师改名为第49摩托化步兵师实现。

text:
The 49th Tank Division was formed March 1941 in western Kiev Special Military District as part of 24th Mechanized Corps with:<cr>
97th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - 1 company each
98th Tank Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns - 1 company each
49th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
49th Howitzer Regiment
1 light bn
49th Reconnaissance Battalion
49th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
49th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr>
The 49th Tank Division had less than 100 tanks, all old BT, T-26, or T-27/38 tankettes. In addition, as a reserve unit the 24th Mechanized Corps had received almost no trucks or tractors, and all but a handful of the tanks had arrived in the two months just prior to the outbreak of the war. As a result, 49th Tank Division fought mostly as a brigade-sized unit of partially motorized infantry with tank support until August, when it was destroyed in the Uman pocket.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text: Upon its establishment in May 1942, The 4th Air Army had 208 aircraft and 437 crews.<cr>In June 1942 one more regiment was added, the 588th Light Night Bomber Regiment (commander Ye.D. Bershanskaya), that became the first women's unit in the Soviet Air Force. In February 1943 it was reorganized into 46th Guards Night Bomber Aviation Regiment and in October 1943 it became the 46th Taman Guards Night Bomber Aviation Regiment. In 1943, the Army supported the Kerch-Eltigen Operation and assisted in the battle for air superiority over the Kuban. Two regiments that formed part of the Army, the 57th GIAP and 821st IAP, flew lend-lease Supermarine Spitfires in 1943 for a period. Alexander Pokryshkin was one of its members, and one of the most successful aces of WW2, as well as having the distinction of being awarded the Hero of the Soviet Union three times.<cr>In summer 1944 the Army covered the Separate Coastal Army during the Battle of Crimea (1944). It was then reassigned to the 2nd Belorussian Front and participated in Operation Bagration, the East Prussian Offensive, the East Pomeranian Offensive, and the Battle of Berlin. Overall during the war it flew about 300,000 sorties.<cr><cr>
translation: 1942年5月成立时，第4空军集团军拥有208架飞机和437个机组。<cr>1942年6月又增加了一个团，即第588轻型夜间轰炸机团（团长叶·德·别尔尚斯卡娅），这是苏联空军第一个女性单位。1943年2月该团重组为第46近卫夜间轰炸航空团，并于1943年10月改名为第46塔曼近卫夜间轰炸航空团。1943年，该集团军支持刻赤-埃尔蒂根行动，并协助在库班地区争夺制空权。两个属于该集团军的团，即第57战斗机航空兵团和第821歼击机航空兵团，在1943年曾短暂使用租借来的超级马林喷火式战斗机作战。亚历山大·波克里什金是其成员之一，并且是二战期间最成功的王牌飞行员之一，同时他也是三次获得苏联英雄称号的人。<cr>1944年夏季，该集团军在克里米亚战役（1944）中掩护了独立海岸集团军。随后被重新分配到第2白俄罗斯方面军，并参加了巴格拉季昂行动、东普鲁士进攻、波美拉尼亚进攻以及柏林之战。在整个战争期间，它共执行了约30万次任务。<cr><cr>

text: The corps was formed in April 1941 in the Western Special Military District and consisted of 214th, 8th, and 9th Airborne Brigades in June 1941. It fought as a part of Western Front in the Berezina operation in Belarus in July 1941. The corps made several airborne attacks on German communications during the Rzhev-Vyazma offensive from December 1941 to February 1942. All three brigades were dropped in the vicinity of Dorogobuzh as part of the Vyazma airborne operation. The drops were poorly coordinated and the corps was unable to achieve its objective of cutting off Axis supply lines, but did harass German 4th Army. The corps continued to operate to the south of Vyazma under the command of 1st Guards Cavalry Corps until withdrawn 28 June 1942. This was the longest independent airborne operation of the war. In August 1942, the corps was reorganized as 38th Guards Rifle Division. The corps was reformed in the fall of 1942 and then reorganized as 1st Guards Airborne Division. <cr><cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军于1941年4月在西方特别军事区组建，至1941年6月由第214、第8和第9空降旅组成。它作为西方面军的一部分参加了白俄罗斯别列津纳河战役，在1941年7月作战。该军于1941年12月至1942年2月期间在日兹德拉-维亚兹马攻势中对德军通信发动了多次空降攻击。作为维亚兹马空降行动的一部分，所有三个旅都在多罗戈布日附近降落。这些空降行动协调不佳，该军未能切断轴心国的补给线，但确实骚扰了德国第4集团军。该军继续在维亚兹马以南地区作战，直到1942年6月28日在第1近卫骑兵军指挥下撤出。这是战争中最长的一次独立空降行动。1942年秋季，该军重组，并于1942年再次改编为第1近卫空降师。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 4th Army was activated on 1 August 1939 with General Gnther von Kluge in command. It first went into action during the Invasion of Poland of September 1939 as part of Army Group North, which was under Field Marshal Fedor von Bock. The 4th Army contained the II Corps and III Corps, each with two infantry divisions, the XIX Corps with two motorized and one panzer divisions, the I Frontier Guard Corps with one infantry division, and two infantry divisions in reserve. It was tasked with capturing the Polish Corridor and thus re-linking mainland Germany with East Prussia. Under Kluge, the Fourth Army completed its task without much difficulty. Part of the Fourth Army attacked south into Pomorze and joined other German forces at Warsaw.<cr>During the attack on the Low Countries and France, the 4th Army, as part of Field Marshal Gerd von Rundstedt's Army Group A, went into Belgium from the Rhineland. Along with other German armies, the 4th Army penetrated the K-W Line and completed the trapping of the Allied forces in France. The then Major-General Erwin Rommel, who was under Kluge, contributed immensely to his victories. Kluge, who had been General of the Artillery, was promoted to Field Marshal along with many others on 19 July 1940.<cr>The 4th Army took part in Operation Barbarossa in 1941 as part of von Bock's Army Group Center. Its initial aim was to trap as many Soviet troops as possible around Minsk. The 4th Army performed well and took part in the capture of Smolensk. However, the poor road network contributed to the stalling of the army group and the 4th Army. On 19 December 1941, Kluge resigned along with von Bock and Field Marshal Walther von Brauchitsch. Kluge was replaced by General Ludwig Kbler.<cr>After the launching of Operation Blue, the 4th Army and the entire Army Group Center did not see much action, as troops were concentrated to the south. However, from 1943 on, as Army Group Center was in full retreat, the Fourth Army also had to move its troops backwards. The Red Army's campaign of autumn 1943, Operaton Suvorov (also known as the 'battle of the highways') saw the 4th Army pushed back towards Orsha and Vitebsk.<cr>1944 saw the 4th Army still holding defensive positions east of Orsha and Mogilev in the Belorussian SSR. The first Soviet summer offensive of that year, Operation Bagration, proved disastrous for the German Armed Forces (Wehrmacht), and especially so for the Fourth Army. Commencing on 22 June, an overwhelming Soviet assault saw nearly the entire army trapped in a pocket east of Minsk and destroyed during the first week of July. Very few units were able to escape westwards; those that did so were involved in desperate attempts to stabilise the German lines for the remainder of the summer, after which the Fourth Army required complete rebuilding.<cr>During late 194445 the 4th Army, now under the command of Friedrich Hossbach, was tasked with holding the borders of East Prussia. The Soviet East Prussian Offensive, commencing on 13 January, saw the 4th Army driven steadily backwards towards the Baltic coast over a period of two weeks and threatened with encirclement. Hossbach and Army Group Centre's commander, Georg-Hans Reinhardt, attempted to break out of East Prussia (defying their orders, for which they were relieved of command) by attacking towards Elbing; but the attack was driven back, and the 4th Army was again encircled in what became known as the Heiligenbeil Pocket.<cr>The army held its positions along the coast of the Vistula lagoon until overwhelmed by Soviet attacks in late March. The few remaining forces in the area were incorporated in the East Prussian Army Group commanded by Dietrich von Saucken, which surrendered to the Soviets at the end of the war in May.<cr><cr>

text: On the eve of the German attack on the Soviet Union, the 4th Army suffered, as did many Soviet formations, from German communication sabotage. Units lost telephone connections, electrical power, and the Brest Fortress lost its water supply. From about 5 am on 22 June fierce fighting began around the Brest fortress, but the seven battalions around the fortress, from 28th Rifle Corps, were undermanned, disorganized, and slow off the mark to man the defences. Despite these deficiencies the final German reduction of the fortress took some time in the face of determined Soviet resistance. By 1600 hours on 22 June, 4th Army HQ was back at Zapruda, whereupon Front HQ ordered that 14th Mechanised Corps be launched in an attack to clear Brest and reach the frontier line. However the Army staff felt the plan had no chance of success, and so it proved; when the attack was launched the next day, only insignificant progress was made. Three days later Western Front ordered a general withdrawal to try to keep the frontier armies out of threatened German encirclement; 4th Army was directed to fall back on a line from Bytin to Pinsk. Further instructions came through from Pavlov after a chance meeting later the same day; to cover the concentration of reserve armies on the Dnieper, 4th Army was to hold the Shchara, the Slutsk fortified district, and the Sluch river line. However the Slutsk fortified district, as the district commander reminded Khorobkov, had long ago been instructed to dispatch all its weapons to the Brest fortress (which was continuing to hold). The planned defence was thus practically non-existent, and Slutsk fell on 27 June. The Army took part in the defenses of the area around Babruysk.<cr>At the end of July 1941, the Fourth Army began to dissolve. The Fourth Army's staff members were absorbed into the general staff of the Central Front, and the troops were absorbed into other armies.<cr>At the end of September 1941, the Fourth Army was formed for the second time, retaining its Independent status until December while remaining in the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (RVGK, the Stavka Reserve). The field staffs of the 52nd and 54th Armies were used to fill the command contingent of the Army. The new formation was made up of the 285th, 292nd, and 311th Rifle Divisions along with the 27th Cavalry Division, a Tank brigade, the 2nd Reserve aviation group, and other artillery and support units.<cr>The Fourth Army participated in the defense and attack of Tikhvin from October to December 1941. On December 17, 1941, the Fourth Army was allocated to the Volkhov Front. From January 1942 to November 1943, the Fourth Army fought on the front in Volkhov and Leningrad while also doing many rear-area duties. Unlike in other parts of the Eastern Front, the Red Army was not making significant gains in the north by 1943.<cr>The 4th Army was disbanded in November 1943 and set up again in January 1944 as part of the Transcaucasus Front. The staff of the 4th Army was formed from the staff of the 34th Army. The 4th Army was stationed in Iran until August 1945 in accordance with the Soviet-Iranian treaty of 1921.<cr><cr>
translation: 在德国进攻苏联前夕，第4集团军和许多苏军部队一样遭受了德军的通信破坏。各部失去了电话联系、电力供应，布列斯特要塞还丧失了水源供给。6月22日凌晨5点左右，在布列斯特要塞周围开始了激烈的战斗，但围绕该要塞的七个营（来自第28步兵军）兵力不足、组织混乱，并且在占领防御工事方面行动迟缓。尽管存在这些缺陷，但由于苏联部队的顽强抵抗，最终德国攻陷要塞还是花费了一段时间。6月22日下午4点，第4集团军司令部撤回扎普鲁达，随后方面军司令部命令第14机械化军发动攻击以清除布列斯特并到达国界线。然而，集团军指挥部认为该计划没有成功的可能；当第二天发起进攻时，只取得了微不足道的进展。三天后，西方方面军下令全面撤退，试图将边境部队保持在不受德军包围威胁的位置；第4集团军被指示从布廷到宾斯克一线撤退。当天晚些时候，在一次偶然会面之后，帕夫洛夫下达了进一步指令：为了掩护在第聂伯河集结的预备队集团军，第4集团军应守住什查拉河、斯卢茨克要塞区和斯鲁奇河防线。然而，正如斯卢茨克要塞区指挥官提醒霍罗布科夫的那样，该地区早已被指示将所有武器调往仍在坚守的布列斯特要塞。因此，计划中的防御实际上并不存在，斯卢茨克于6月27日失陷。集团军参与了巴布鲁伊斯克周边地区的防御作战。<cr>1941年7月底，第四集团军开始解散。其成员被吸收进中央方面军的总参谋部，部队则并入其他集团军。<cr>1941年9月底，第四集团军第二次重建，保留独立地位直到同年12月，并且留在最高统帅部预备队（RVGK）。该集团军的指挥人员由第52和第54集团军的野战参谋部成员组成。新编成包括第285、292和311步兵师，以及第27骑兵师、一个坦克旅、第二预备航空大队和其他炮兵及支援单位。<cr>第四集团军从1941年10月至同年12月参与了季霍维纳的防御与进攻。1941年12月17日，第四集团军被分配到沃尔霍夫方面军。从1942年1月至1943年11月，第四集团军在沃尔霍夫和列宁格勒战线上作战，并承担许多后方任务。<cr>与东线其他地区不同，在北部的红军到1943年并没有取得显著进展。<cr>1943年11月，第四集团军解散，并于1944年1月作为高加索方面军的一部分重建。第四集团军参谋部由第34集团军的成员组成。根据1921年的苏伊条约，该集团军驻扎在伊朗直到1945年8月。<cr>

translation: 由第210机械化步兵师于1941年7月10日改编而成，于1942年4月20日解散，其司令部用于组建第七骑兵军。继承了20世纪20至30年代第四骑兵师的荣誉称号“顿河哥萨克”。<cr>第二次世界大战中各国军队编制与战斗序列：第五卷-B册 苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟, 特拉法尔加出版社, 2009年<cr>Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert,伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列, 预科学校出版社, 1985年<cr>贡献者：Stewart King

text: The 4th Cuneense Alpini Italian Mountain Division was formed in 1935 with the 1st and 2nd Alpini Regiments and the 4th Alpine Artillery Regiment. Alpini mountain infantry were considered elite units in the Italian Army. Each division consisted of two Alpini regiments with three battalions each, one Alpine artillery regiment, one mixed engineer battalion and various support troops for a total divisional strength of over 17,000 men. Each Alpini division also possessed nearly 5,000 mules and 500 vehicles of various types. The division participated in every Italian Campaign in World War II with the exception of the North African Campaign. The division was one of three Alpini sent to fight on the Eastern Front with the Italian 8th Army in the summer of 1942. The division was originally to be deployed to the Caucasus Mountains but instead found itself, along with the rest of the 8th Army, stretched along a 160 mile section of the Don River between the Hungarian Second Army and Romanian 3rd Army on the German left flank at the start of Operation Little Saturn. The division, along with most of the 8th Army was surrounded. Unlike its two sister Alpini divisions it was unable to escape the pocket. By January 28, 1943 the division had walked 200 km, fought 20 battles and lost 80% of its personnel in termperatures that reached minus 30 to 40 degrees Celcius at night. That day the divisions remnants were attacked by Cossacks and it ceased to exist. Only about 1,600 stragglers reached German lines.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第4库内塞阿尔宾意大利山地师成立于1935年，由第1和第2阿尔宾团以及第4高山炮兵团组成。阿尔宾山地步兵被认为是意大利陆军中的精锐部队。每个师包括两个各有三个营的阿尔宾团、一个高山炮兵团、一个混合工兵营及各种支援部队，总兵力超过17,000人。每个阿尔宾师还拥有近5,000头骡子和500辆各型车辆。该师参加了第二次世界大战中除北非战役外的所有意大利战役。在1942年夏季，该师是被派往东线作战的三个阿尔宾师之一，隶属于意大利第8集团军。原计划将其部署到高加索山脉，但最终却与第8集团军其余部队一起，在“小土星行动”开始时，沿着匈牙利第二集团军和罗马尼亚第三集团军之间的顿河160英里长的战线上展开，位于德国左翼。该师及其大部分第8集团军被包围了。与其他两个阿尔宾师不同的是，它无法逃脱包围圈。到1943年1月28日，该师已经行走了200公里，打了20场战斗，并且在夜间气温降至零下30至40摄氏度的情况下损失了80%的人员。当天，哥萨克部队攻击了该师残部，它从此不复存在。只有大约1,600名散兵游勇到达德军战线。<cr><cr>指挥官报告<@PH1@@百科条目<@PH2@@由Chris Munson提供

text:
The 4th Guards Airborne Division was an airborne division of the Red Army that fought as infantry during World War II.

Formed in December 1942 from three airborne brigades, the division spent the next few months training for airborne operations. However, it first saw combat as an infantry unit in the Demyansk Offensive in late February 1943, then helped defend Ponyri during the Battle of Kursk . The division fought in Operation Kutuzov and advanced west in the Battle of the Dnieper, during which it captured Pryluky and crossed the Dnieper. It received the Ovruch honorific for the capture of the key rail junction during the Battle of Kiev. The division then fought in the Zhitomir-Berdichev Offensive and the Korsun-Shevchenkovsky Offensive in late 1943 and early 1944.

The 4th Guards received the Order of the Red Banner and the Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky for actions during the Uman-Botosani Offensive, then fought in the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive and received the Order of Suvorov. The division advanced westward into Hungary, fighting in the Battle of Debrecen and the Budapest Offensive in late 1944. In the last months of the war it fought in the Bratisalva-Brno Offensive and ended the war fighting in the Prague Offensive.<cr><cr>
translation:
第4近卫空降师是苏联红军在第二次世界大战期间作为步兵作战的一支空降师。

该师于1942年12月由三个空降旅组建而成，接下来几个月内训练准备空降任务。然而，它首次参战是在1943年2月底的德梅伊安斯克攻势中担任步兵单位，并在库尔斯克战役期间协助防御波尼里镇。该师参加了库图佐夫行动，在第聂伯河战役中向西推进，期间占领了普里卢基并渡过了第聂伯河。它因为在基辅战役中俘获关键铁路枢纽而获得了奥弗鲁奇荣誉称号。

随后，该师在1943年底和1944年初参加了日托米尔-别尔季切夫攻势和科尔松-舍甫琴科夫斯基攻势，并因乌曼-波图萨尼攻势中的行动获得红旗勋章和博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基勋章。之后，该师在雅西-奇索里亚攻势中参战并获得了苏沃洛夫勋章。

1944年底，第4近卫师向西推进至匈牙利境内，在德布勒森战役和布达佩斯攻势中作战。战争最后几个月，它参加了布拉迪斯拉发-布尔诺攻势，并在布拉格攻势中结束了战斗。

text: On April 16, 1943, the STAVKA ordered the 4th Guards Army to be established. On May 5, 1943, the army was formed on the basis of the 24th Army in the Steppe Military District. It included the 20th and 21st Guards Rifle and 3rd Guards Tank Corps. On July 3 the Army was placed in Stavka reserve, on July 18 included in the Steppe Front, and on July 23 once again put in Stavka reserve.<cr>The Army fought in decisive actions such as the Battle of Kursk , the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive, Operation Spring Awakening, and the Vienna Offensive. At the end of the war, the Fourth Guards Army was part of the 3rd Ukrainian Front.<cr><cr>
translation: 1943年4月16日，最高统帅部大本营下令组建第4近卫集团军。5月5日，该集团军在顿河军区的基础上由第24集团军改编而成，包括第20和第21近卫步兵师以及第3近卫坦克军。7月3日，该集团军被最高统帅部列为预备队；7月18日加入顿河方面军；7月23日再次成为最高统帅部的预备队。<cr>该集团军参加了库尔斯克战役、雅西-奇西瑙攻势、春季觉醒行动和维也纳攻势等决定性战斗。<cr>战争结束时，第4近卫集团军是第3乌克兰方面军的一部分。

text: Formed 11/26/1941 from 53rd Cavalry Division as part of II Guards Cavalry Corps. As part of Western Front Reserve, the division participated in the Battle of Moscow in December 1941. Inherited the honorific name 'Kuban Cossack' from 53rd Cavalry Division. Remained in 1st Belorussian Front until the end of the war. <cr><cr>Pettibone, Charles D., The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II: volume V - Book B Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Trafford, 2009<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 1941年11月26日，该师由第53骑兵师改编而成，隶属于第二近卫骑兵军。作为西方方面军预备队的一部分，该师参加了1941年12月的莫斯科战役。继承了第53骑兵师的荣誉名称“库班哥萨克”。直到战争结束都留在第一白俄罗斯方面军。<cr>参考文献：Pettibone, Charles D., 《第二次世界大战中各国军队的编制和战斗序列：卷V - B书 苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟》，Trafford，2009年<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 4th Guards Rifle Division was reformed as an elite infantry division on September 18, 1941, from the 1st formation of the 161st Rifle Divison as one of the original Guards formations of the Red Army, in recognition of that division's participation in the successful counter-offensive that drove German forces out of their positions at Yelnya. The division then moved northwards to serve in the defense of Leningrad, as well as the early attempts to break that city's siege, but later was redeployed to the southern sector of the front as the crisis around Stalingrad developed. The 4th Guards took part in Operaton Uranus which surrounded the German 6th Army in and around that city and then in the pursuit operations that drove the remaining German forces from the Caucasus steppes and the city of Rostov. The division remained in this sector for the duration of the war, fighting through the south of Ukraine through the summer of 1943 and winning the Order of the Red Banner in the process; it was further distinguished with the award of a battle honor in February, 1944. During April and May its advance was halted during the battles along the Dniestr River, but resumed in the August offensive that carried it and its 31st Guards Rifle Corps into the Balkans. It served extensively in the fighting through Hungary and in the outer encirclement during the siege of Budapest in the winter of 1944/45 and in mid-April was awarded a second battle honor for its part in the capture of Vienna.<cr><cr>
translation: 第4近卫步兵师于1941年9月18日从红军最初的近卫部队之一、第161步兵师的第一个编成单位中重建为精锐步兵师。该师因参与在叶连亚地区成功反攻，迫使德军撤离原有阵地而获得此荣誉。随后，该师北上参加列宁格勒的防御，并尝试打破对这座城市的包围，但随着斯大林格勒局势恶化，它被重新部署到前线南部战区。第4近卫步兵师参加了天王星行动，将德军第6集团军及其周边地区包围起来，并在随后的追击作战中迫使剩余德军从高加索草原和罗斯托夫市撤出。该师在整个战争期间都驻扎在这个区域，在1943年夏季穿越乌克兰南部的过程中赢得了红旗勋章；它还在1944年2月获得了一项战斗荣誉。4月和5月，其推进在德涅斯特河沿岸的战斗中被阻止，但在8月攻势中重新开始，并与第31近卫步兵军一起进入巴尔干地区。该师广泛参与了匈牙利地区的作战，在布达佩斯冬季围城战中的外围包围行动中也发挥了重要作用，并在1945年4月中旬因在维也纳战役中的表现而获得第二次战斗荣誉。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>第4近卫步兵师<cr>，在东线的漫长岁月里，它经历了无数战斗和考验。从列宁格勒到高加索，再到巴尔干半岛，该师始终坚守岗位，为最终胜利做出了巨大贡献。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>第4近卫步兵师<cr>

text: On 15 July 1943, after an abortive attempt to form the 4th Tank Army for a second time had been called off in February, it was reformed as 4th Guards Tank Army drawing on the headquarters of the previous 19th Cavalry Corps. Initially the new army consisted of 11th and 30th Ural Volunteer Tank Corps and 6th Guards Mechanized Tank Corps.<cr> Its first operation as 4th Tank Army, under Lt. General Tank Tr. Vasily Badanov, (July 1943- March 1944) was at Orel, the counterattack (Operation Kutuzov) on the northern side of the Kursk bulge after the German defeat at the Battle of Kursk proper. John Erickson writes that '..at 1100 on 26 July, two of Badanov's corps (11th Tank and 6th Guards Mechanised) put in a ragged attack towards Bolkhov. For the next few hours, under the very gaze of Bagramyan [commander of 11th Guards Army, whose sector 4th Tank was attacking through] and Badanov, both corps were heavily battered by the concealed German tanks and assault guns. It took part in the winter battles in the Ukraine in 1944 (Proskurov-Chernovits), then the Lvov-Sandomierz Operation in the summer. Its commander was Lt. Gen. (later Col. Gen.) D.D. Lelushenko.( March 1944- May 1945). It then participated in the Lower Silesia, Upper Silesia, Berlin, and Prague operations. <cr><cr>
translation: 1943年7月15日，第二次组建第4坦克集团军的尝试在2月份被取消后，它重新以第4近卫坦克集团军的形式成立，并利用了之前的第19骑兵军司令部。最初，新集团军由第11乌拉尔志愿坦克军、第30乌拉尔志愿坦克军和第6近卫机械化坦克军组成。<cr>作为第4坦克集团军的首次行动（1943年7月至1944年3月），在少将瓦西里·巴达诺夫指挥下，在奥廖尔对库尔斯克突出部北侧发起反击（库图佐夫行动）。约翰·埃里克森写道：“……7月26日上午11点，巴达诺夫的两个军（第11坦克军和第6近卫机械化军）向博戈罗夫发起了零散攻击。接下来几个小时，在巴格拉米扬[commander of 11th Guards Army, whose sector 4th Tank was attacking through]和巴达诺夫的注视下，这两个军遭到隐蔽德军坦克和突击炮的猛烈打击。<cr>它参加了1944年乌克兰冬季战役（普罗斯库罗夫-切尔诺维策），然后是夏季的利沃夫-桑多梅日行动。其指挥官为少将（后晋升上将）D.D.列卢什琴科<cr>。（1944年3月至1945年5月）。它还参加了下西里西亚、上西里西亚、柏林和布拉格战役。<cr>

text: For distinction in combat during the Operation Little Saturn between 17 December to 30 December 1942, the 17th Tank Corps was renumbered as the 4th Guards Tank Corps in January 1943. The Corps received the honorific Kantemirovsky after the village of Kantemirovka in Kantemirovsky District, Voronezh Oblast, when it had been liberated from German troops by tank units as their baptism of fire.<cr>In the August 1943, the 4th Guards Tank Corps endured continuous combat on the Belgorod-Kharkiv area of the Kursk bulge. For the courage and heroism shown during the liberation of cities on the right-bank Ukraine, including Zbarazh, Ternopil, and Shepetovka in April 1944, the Corps was awarded the Order of the Red Banner. Seventeen regiments and separate battalions were awarded honorifics of Shepetovsky, Zhitomirsky, Yampolsky, and Tarnopolsky, in honor of the cities they had taken.<cr>The Corps for participating in the battle for Krakow, was awarded the Order of Lenin.<cr>The 4th Guards Tank Corps was among the first Red Army formations to reach the river Elbe, and participated in the capture of Dresden in Germany. The Corps made a sudden redeployment to Czechoslovakia, where they saw their final fighting of the war in the suburbs of Prague, during the Prague Offensive. For the courage shown by soldiers and officers of the Corps during wartime, military units were awarded 23 awards, the staff of the Corps was thanked officially by the Supreme commander in chief 18 times, 32 of its members were awarded the Hero of Soviet Union (5 of which are forever enlisted in the unit rolls), more than 20,000 soldiers received awards and medals, five becoming full chevaliers of the Order of Glory.<cr><cr>
translation: 为了在1942年12月17日至30日的土星行动中作战中的卓越表现，第17坦克军于1943年1月被重新编号为第4近卫坦克军。该军因在卡内米罗夫斯基区卡内米罗夫卡村解放后获得荣誉称号“卡内米罗夫斯基”，该村是在坦克部队的首次战斗中从德国军队手中解放出来的。<cr>1943年8月，第4近卫坦克军在库尔斯克突出部别尔哥罗德-哈尔科夫地区经历了连续不断的战斗。因该军在1944年4月解放右岸乌克兰城市（包括兹巴热赫、特伦波利和谢佩托夫卡）时表现出的勇气和英雄主义，该军被授予红旗勋章。<cr>十七个团和独立营获得了谢佩托夫斯基、日托米尔斯基、雅姆波尔斯基和特伦波利斯基等荣誉称号，以表彰他们攻占的城市。<cr>参与了克拉科夫战役后，该军被授予列宁勋章。<cr>第4近卫坦克军是第一批到达易北河的红军部队之一，并参加了德国德累斯顿的占领行动。该军突然部署到捷克斯洛伐克，在布拉格郊区见证了战争中的最后一次战斗。由于士兵和军官在战时表现出的勇气，军事单位获得了23项奖励，军团指挥官18次受到最高统帅部的正式感谢，其中32名成员被授予苏联英雄称号（5人永久记录在部队名单中），超过两万名士兵获得奖章，五人成为全权骑士团成员。

text: The 4th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 4th Light Division. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 4th Light Division was merged with other units and disbanded.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第4匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人在少将指挥下，拥有2个步兵团（每个团有3个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团配有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国人要求匈牙利提供更多东线兵力，大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而，其编制表基本没有变化。该旅更名为第4轻型师。在斯大林格勒战役后对匈牙利陆军进行的一般重组中，第4轻型师与其他部队合并并解散。<cr>资料来源：Dr. Nigel Thomas 和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利军队》<cr>条目由 Chris Munson 提供

text: The 4th Mechanized Corps was initially formed in January 1941, it was serving with the 6th Army, Kiev Special Military District under the command of General Major Andrey Vlasov when the German Operation Barbarossa began in June 1941. On 22 June 1941 4th Mechanised Corps consisted of 28,098 Soldiers and 979 tanks. It initially comprised the 8th and 32nd Tank Divisions, the 81st Mechanised Division, the 3rd Motorcycle Regiment, and other smaller units. It fought in the Battle of Brody, and was destroyed in the Uman Pocket in August 1941 with 6th Army and was disbanded shortly after.<cr>The Corps was reformed for the second time in September 1942. It was commanded by General Vasily Volsky during the Battle of Stalingrad in 1942. The corps entered the sector south of Stalingrad as part of Operation Uranus. The plan was to attack through the 51st Army's sector to obtain an encirclement by cutting through the Romanian Fourth Army led by Constantin Constantinescu.<cr>On 20 November 1942, the Corps started feeding its initial units into the attack, between Lake Tsatsa and Barmatsak when the 126th and 302nd Rifle Divisions of 51st Army began to advance on a three-mile front supported by the 55th and 158th Independent Tank Regiments from 4th Mech Corps. The advance was made against the Romanian 6th Corps, whose units, began to surrender as the tanks got in amongst their positions.<cr>The Corps's main attack opened late, further down the line, with three mechanised brigades hugging one road instead of the planned three, and the left-flank brigades, 36th and 59th, running into minefields. However the attack went on, until a pause at Zety on the evening on 21 November for fuel and ammunition. On the morning of 23 November, 4 Mechanised Corps linked up with 4th and 26th Tank Corps in the Sovietskii-Marinovka area and the northern and southern pincers had met. The German Sixth Army was surrounded in Stalingrad.<cr>In December 1942 the Corps gained a Guards title and became the 3rd Guards Mechanised Corps.<cr><cr>
translation:
第4机械化军最初于1941年1月组建，当时它隶属于基辅特别军事区的第6集团军，在安德烈·瓦利索夫少将指挥下参与德国巴巴罗萨行动。1941年6月22日，第4机械化军拥有28098名士兵和979辆坦克。最初由第8装甲师、第32装甲师、第81机械化师、第3摩托化团和其他较小单位组成。该部参加了布罗迪战役，并于1941年8月在乌曼包围圈中被消灭，与第6集团军一同解散。

该军第二次重组是在1942年9月。瓦西里·沃尔斯基将军指挥该军参加1942年的斯大林格勒战役。作为天王星行动的一部分，该部进入斯大林格勒南部战区。计划是通过第51集团军的战区发起攻击，以切断罗马尼亚第四集团军（由康斯坦丁·康斯坦丁内斯库指挥）来实现包围。

1942年11月20日，该部开始将初始部队投入进攻，在察察湖和巴尔马茨卡之间推进。第51集团军的第126步兵师和第302步兵师在三英里宽的战线上向前推进，并得到来自第4机械化军的第55独立坦克团和第158独立坦克团的支持。进攻面对的是罗马尼亚第六集团军，其部队开始向坦克投降。该军的主要攻击行动启动较晚，从更靠后的地段发起，三个机械化旅沿着一条公路推进，而不是原计划的三条。左翼的第36和第59旅遭遇了地雷场。尽管如此，攻势持续进行，在11月21日晚上于泽蒂暂停以补充燃料和弹药。11月23日清晨，第4机械化军与第4坦克军和第26坦克军在苏维埃-马里诺夫卡地区会合，南北两个钳形攻势成功汇合。德国第六集团军被包围在斯大林格勒。<cr>1942年12月，该军获得近卫称号，并更名为第3近卫机械化军。<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 4th Mountain Division invaded Russia as part of Army Group South and suffered heavy casualties in the initial advances toward the Volga, fighting at Vinniza, Uman, the Dnieper crossings and the drive to the Mius. It suffered 1,778 casualties in the Battle of the Uman Pocket alone.<cr><cr>The 4th Mountain spent much of the winter of 1941-42 fighting the Soviets on the Kerch peninsula of the Crimea, east of Sevastopol. That summer, the division took part in the capture of Rostov and in the Caucasus campaign. Following the retreat from the Caucasus, it was engaged in heavy fighting at Novorossiysk, where the Germans contained the Russian amphibious landings on the Kuban. By early 1944, the 4th Mountain had been shifted northward and fought in the battles of the Dniepr Bend, where Field Marshal von Manstein commended it for its part in smashing a Soviet tank army. The 4th Mountain Division continued to fight on the Russian Front as the German forces retreated across southern Russia, Romania, Hungary, Slovakia and Upper Silesia. The division ended the war at battle group strength on the central sector of the Eastern Front and surrendered to the Russians at Deutsch-Brod in May 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第4山地师作为南方集团军群的一部分入侵苏联，在初期向伏尔加河推进的过程中遭受了重大伤亡，曾在 Vinnytsia、Uman、第聂伯河渡口以及米乌斯河的攻势中作战。仅在 Uman 包围圈一役中就损失了1,778人。<cr><cr>1941-42年冬天，该师主要在克里米亚半岛的刻赤半岛建立防线，塞瓦斯托波尔以东地区与苏联军队作战。次夏，第4山地师参与了罗斯托夫的占领以及高加索战役。<cr><cr>从高加索撤退后，该师在新罗西斯克进行了激烈战斗，在那里德军遏制了俄罗斯人在库班地区的两栖登陆行动。到1944年初，第4山地师被调往北方，并参加了第聂伯河弯道战役，当时曼施坦因元帅称赞其在粉碎苏联坦克集团军中的表现。<cr><cr>随着德国军队从南俄、罗马尼亚、匈牙利、斯洛伐克和上西里西亚撤退，第4山地师继续在东线作战。该师最终以战斗群的规模结束战争，并于1945年5月在德意志-布罗德向苏联投降。<cr><cr>德国战斗序列 第二卷 291至999步兵师、命名步兵师及特殊部队，二战中的德国陆军，萨缪尔·W.米奇姆少校

text: As part of Army Group Center, the 4th Panzer crossed into Russia in June and fought at Minsk, Gomel, Kiev, Bryansk, Vyazma, and other bitterly contested points on the road to Moscow. By November, it had only fifty operational tanks left. In December 1941, it attempted to encircle the strategic city of Tula, southeast of Moscow, but failed, suffering heavy losses in the attempt. Remaining on the central sector of the Russian Front until 1944, it fought at Orel (194243), in the Kursk and Dnieper campaigns, and tried unsuccessfully to check the Soviet summer offensive of 1944. In November 1944, it was isolated in the Courland Pocket but was evacuated by sea to northern Germany in early 1945. Now in remnants, the 4th Panzer was isolated on the Frischen Nehrung in West Prussia in April 1945. Most of the 35th Panzer Regiment was shipped out aboard the Goya on April 16. Unfortunately, it was struck by two Soviet torpedoes just before midnight and sunk in four minutes, taking almost the entire regiment with it. The rest of the division surrendered to the Red Army at the end of the war in May 1945. An outstanding division even by German standards, it was the most heavily decorated of all the panzer divisions.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 作为中央集团军群的一部分，第4装甲师于6月进入俄罗斯，并在明斯克、戈梅利、基辅、布良斯克、弗拉基米尔等地与苏军激战。到11月，它只剩下50辆可操作的坦克了。1941年12月，该师试图包围莫斯科东南方向的战略城市图拉，但未能成功，并在尝试中遭受重大损失。直到1944年，第4装甲师一直在俄罗斯中央战区作战，在奥廖尔（1942-43）、库尔斯克和第聂伯河战役中战斗，并试图阻止苏联1944年的夏季攻势，但未果。1944年11月，该师被孤立在库尔兰半岛的包围圈内，但在1945年初通过海上撤离到了德国北部。到1945年4月，第4装甲师仅存残部，在西普鲁士弗里施海角被孤立。大部分第35装甲团成员于4月16日乘坐戈亚号船撤离。不幸的是，该船在午夜前不久遭到两枚苏联鱼雷的攻击，并在四分钟内沉没，几乎带走了整个团。其余部队在1945年5月战争结束时向红军投降。即使按照德国标准来看，第4装甲师也是一支杰出的部队，它是所有装甲师中获得荣誉最多的。<cr> 德国战斗序列 第三卷 - 装甲、装甲掷弹兵和武装党卫军师在二战中的表现，塞缪尔·W·米查姆少校<cr>

text: On commencement of Operation Barbarossa, the 4th Panzer Group was a part of Army Group North, and consisted of the XLI Panzer and LVI Panzer Corps (mot) which comprised three panzer and two motorized infantry divisions respectively, altogether equipped with 631 tanks.<cr>Acting as the armored spearhead for Army Group North in the opening phase of Operation Barbarossa, it crossed the Neman River, where the XLI Panzer Corps was counter-attacked by 300 Soviet tanks near Raseiniai. In a four day battle, the Germans encircled and destroyed the Soviet armor. The LVI Panzer Corps seized the Dvina bridges and began its advance towards Leningrad.<cr>The Soviets fought a bitter defense around Leningrad and Hitler reinforced 4th Panzer Group with the 3rd Panzer Group and it crept up to within 11 kilometres of the city. However, Hitler withdrew both panzer armies and transferred them to Army Group Center for an all-out offensive against Moscow.<cr>The operation called for the 3rd and 4th Panzer Groups to attack Moscow from the north. The 4th Panzer Army would attack through the center and 2nd Panzer Group from the south. But due to the cold weather, deteriorating supply situation and strong Soviet resistance, only the 4th Panzer Army made any headway against the Soviets and closed to 24 kilometres of Moscow. Exhausted, it was halted and then pushed back 320 kilometres with heavy casualties by the Soviet counter offensive launched in December 1941.<cr>On 1 January 1942, the 4th Panzer Group was redesignated 4th Panzer Army.<cr><cr>
translation: 巴巴罗萨行动开始时，第4装甲群是北方集团军群的一部分，由XL I装甲军和LVI装甲军（摩托化步兵）组成。前者包括三个装甲师和两个摩托化步兵师，后者则拥有631辆坦克。<cr><cr>作为北方集团军群在巴巴罗萨行动初期的装甲尖刀，它渡过了涅曼河，在拉塞尼艾附近遭到300辆苏联坦克的反攻。经过四天激战，德军包围并消灭了苏军装甲部队。LVI装甲军夺取了迪纳河上的桥梁，并开始向列宁格勒推进。<cr><cr>苏联军队在列宁格勒周围进行了顽强防御，希特勒增派第3装甲群支援第4装甲群，使其逼近该城11公里处。然而，希特勒撤回两支装甲集团军并将其调往中央集团军群，准备对莫斯科发动全面进攻。<cr><cr>此次行动要求第3和第4装甲群从北面攻击莫斯科，第4装甲集团军从中路发起攻势，而第2装甲群则从南面出击。但由于严寒天气、补给状况恶化以及苏联的顽强抵抗，只有第4装甲集团军对苏军取得了一些进展，并推进至距离莫斯科24公里处。由于精疲力竭，它被停止前进并被迫后撤320公里，在1941年12月发起的苏联反攻中遭受了重大伤亡。<cr><cr>1942年1月1日，第4装甲群改称为第4装甲集团军。

text: Part of the 3rd Army in the Western Front, it consisted of the 27th, 56th and 85th Rifle Divisions. It was encircled in the Minsk Pocket and was destroyed in June or July 1941. The corps was reformed in April 1942 as part of the 7th Army in the Karelian Front and fought against the Finns until their surrender in 1944. The corps was then assigned to the far north for the remainder of the war . <cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 隶属于西方方面军第3集团军，由第27、56和85步兵师组成。在明斯克包围圈中被合围，并于1941年6月或7月被消灭。该军于1942年4月重组为卡累利阿方面军第7集团军的一部分，与芬兰作战直至1944年芬兰投降。之后该军被部署到北极地区直到战争结束。<cr><cr><cr><cr>条目由斯图尔特·金提供

text: On 22 June 1941, the 4th Army consisted of the 3rd Army Corps (Guards, 15th, and 35th Reserve Divisions), the 5th Army Corps (Border Division and 21st Division), the 11th Army Corps (two fortress brigades), and the 4th Army Cooperation Command. It was under the command of Lieutenant General Nicolae Ciuperca. In 1942, it fought on the Axis side as part of the German Army Group B. In July 1941 it took part in Operation Mnchen, the recapturing of Bessarabia and the Northern Bukovina, which was annexed by the Soviet Union the year before.<cr>By August 1941 during the Siege of Odessa, 4th Army had under command the 1st, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, and 11th Army Corps under its control, with a total of 17 infantry divisions, the 1st Armoured Division (Romania), three cavalry divisions, and a total of 38 artillery regiments. On 9 November 1941, Constantin Constantinescu-Claps was appointed the commander of the Fourth Army, and became a Corps General on 24 January 1942. On 10 February 1943, he was relieved of his assignment and replaced by Constantin Sanatescu.<cr>From late 1942 to early 1943, the Fourth Army was almost entirely destroyed during the Battle of Stalingrad. The Romanian Third Army suffered a similar fate. During AprilMay 1944 the Romanian forces led by General Mihail Racovita, together with elements of the German Eighth Army were responsible for defending Northern Romania during the Soviet First Jassy-Kishinev Offensive, and took part in the Battles of Trgu Frumos.<cr>In August 1944, the Red Army entered Romania after driving back Army Group South from the region. On 23 August, Marshal Ion Antonescu was dismissed by King Michael I, and Romania declared war on Germany and Hungary some days later. The Soviets took control of the oilfields in the Ploie?ti area, and the Romanian Army was used to fight German forces on the Eastern Front.<cr>The Fourth Army became one of the Romanian armies fighting for the Red Army on the Eastern Front. In its campaign from August 1944 to May 1945, the Romanian Army lost some 64,000 men killed. The Fourth Army took part in Soviet offensives, notably at Prague in May 1945, which happened to be the last offensive it took part in World War II.<cr><cr>
translation: 1941年6月22日，第4集团军由第3军（近卫师、第15预备师和第35预备师）、第5军（边防师和第21师）、第11军（两个要塞旅）以及第4集团军协同指挥部组成。其指挥官为尼古拉·丘佩尔卡少将。1942年，它作为轴心国部队在德军北方集团军群中作战。<cr>到1941年8月，在敖德萨围城战期间，第4集团军下辖第1、3、4、5、6和11军，共有17个步兵师，罗马尼亚第1装甲师，三个骑兵师以及总计38个炮兵团。1941年11月9日，康斯坦丁·克朗特内斯库-克拉普被任命为第四集团军指挥官，并于1942年1月24日晋升为军长。1943年2月10日，他被解除职务并由康斯坦丁·桑塔特斯库接替。<cr>从1942年末到1943年初，第4集团军几乎在斯大林格勒战役中被完全消灭。罗马尼亚第三集团军也遭遇了类似的命运。1944年4月至5月期间，在苏联第一次雅西-奇尔卡斯基攻势中，由米哈伊·拉科维塔将军领导的罗马尼亚部队以及德军第8集团军的部分兵力负责保卫北罗地区，并参与特鲁弗鲁莫斯战役。<cr>1944年8月，红军在击退南方集团军群后进入罗马尼亚。8月23日，国王米哈伊一世解除了安东内斯库元帅的职务，几天后罗马尼亚对德国和匈牙利宣战。苏联控制了普洛耶什蒂地区的油田，并利用罗马尼亚军队在东线对抗德军。<cr>第四集团军成为在东线上为红军作战的罗马尼亚部队之一。从1944年8月到1945年5月，罗马尼亚军队有约6.4万人阵亡。第四集团军参加了苏军的攻势行动，特别是在1945年5月的布拉格战役中，这也是它在第二次世界大战中的最后一次进攻。<cr>

text: The 4th Romanian Infantry Division did not participate in the opening phase of Operation Barbarossa and remained in Romania. In late 1941 it was transferred east and assigned to the Romanian V Corps. In 1942 it particpated in the German summer campaign Fall Blau. The division was heavily engaged during the Battle of Stalingrad and was down to 250 men and 10 guns by the end of 1942. In March of 1943 it was sent back to Romania. It participated in the defensive battles in Romania in 1944 against the Red Army suffering heavy casualties and was disbanded in November of 1944.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第4罗马尼亚步兵师没有参加巴巴罗萨行动的初期阶段，留在了罗马尼亚。1941年底被调往东线，并隶属于罗马尼亚第5军。1942年参加了德国夏季攻势“蓝色行动”。该师在斯大林格勒战役中遭受重创，在1942年底仅剩250人和10门火炮。<cr>1943年3月，该师被调回罗马尼亚。1944年参加了罗马尼亚境内对抗红军的防御战，并遭受了重大伤亡，于1944年11月解散。<cr>条目由Chris Munson提供

text: The 4th Shock Army was formed from the 27th Army on 25 December 1941 (1st formation) within the Northwestern Front. On 1 October 1942 it included the 249th, 332nd, 334th, 358th and 360th Rifle Divisions, 21st Rifle Brigade, a number of separate tank battalions, the 66th, 67th, 68th, and 69th separate ski battalions, artillery and other subunits.<cr>The army defended the frontier along the eastern shore of lakes Velye, Seliger. In early 1942 the 4th participated in the Toropets-Kholm Offensive as a member of the Kalinin Front.<cr>During 1943 it was invovled in the Nevel, Gorodok and Polotsk Offensives. It was transferred to the 1st Baltic Front.<cr> On the 4th of July it was reassigned to the 2nd Baltic Front and back to the 1st Baltic Front on the 8th of August. During that year it participated in the Rezhitsk-Dvina, Riga and Memel Offensives. The 4th culminated its combat operations during the Courland blockade. <cr><cr>
translation: 第4突击集团军于1941年12月25日（第一次组建）在西北方面军中由第27集团军改编而成。1942年10月1日，该集团军包括第249、332、334、358和360步兵师，第21步兵旅，若干独立坦克营，第66、67、68和69独立滑雪营，炮兵和其他分队。<cr>该集团军保卫了加里宁湖以东的边界。 1942年初，作为加里宁方面军的一员，参加了托罗佩茨-霍尔姆进攻战役。<cr>在1943年，它参与了涅夫勒、戈罗德克和波洛茨克进攻战役，并被转移到第1巴尔干方面军。<cr>7月4日，该集团军被重新分配到第2巴尔干方面军，并于8月8日返回第1巴尔干方面军。在这一年中，它参加了里加、梅梅尔和列季茨克-迪维纳进攻战役。第4突击集团军在其作战行动的最后阶段参与了库尔兰封锁。<cr>
