text:
By Order of the People's Commissariat of Defence of the USSR ? 034 from January 21, 1943, the 293rd Rifle Division was reorganized into the 66th Guards Rifle Division. Major General Akim Yakshin became Division's new commander after Pavel Lagutin was promoted to Executive officer of the 21st Army. On February 7, 1943, most of the Divisions units were renamed.

On March 17, 1943, the 66th was assigned to 6th Guards Rifle Corps, 1st Guards Army, Southwestern Front, from May 5, 1943, the 66th was assigned to 5th Guards Army Steppe Military District. From May 9, 1943, the 66th was with 32nd Guards Rifle Corps 5th Guards Army. During Battle of Kursk and Lower Dnepr strategic offensive operation the 66th was with 33rd Guards Rifle Corps 5th Guards Army, later it was again assigned to 32nd Guards Corps. On September 23, 1943, the 66th was awarded with the honorable name 'Poltava' by Supreme Commander. By the end of October the 66th was with 53rd Army, 2nd Ukrainian Front. On November 28, 1943 Major General Sergey Frolov became new Divisions commander, he would remain there until the end of the war. On November 30, 1943, the 66th was with 20th Guards Rifle Corps 4th Guards Army. On January 3, 1944 66th was assigned to 48th Rifle Corps 53rd Army. While taking part in Korsun-Shevchenkovsky Offensive Operation, 66th was with 75th Rifle Corps, later it was assigned to 26th Guards Rifle Corps.

On March 1, 1943 66th was with 69th Army (STAVKA Reserve) near Shpola Cherkasy Oblast. On April 11, 1944 the division was relocated by rail to Zaporizhia with 1st Ukrainian Front. During Lvov-Sandomierz Offensive 66th was with 95th Rifle Corps 18th Army 1st Ukrainian Front. During the East Carpathian Strategic Offensive Operation (the Dnieper-Carpathian Offensive) the division was assigned to 18th Guards Rifle Corps 18th Army 4th Ukrainian Front. From September 16, 1944, Division also took part in Carpathian-Uzhgorod Offensive.

On November 14, 1944 66th with 18th Guards Rifle Corps was assigned to 2nd Ukrainian Front where it took part in Battle of Budapest. On January 23, 1943 66th was with 104th Rifle Corps 4th Guards Army 3rd Ukrainian Front and took part in Balaton Defensive Operation. On April 5, 1945, the Division was awarded Order of the Red Banner by Supreme Soviet of the USSR. From April 15, 1945 66th was with 21st Guards Rifle Corps 4th Guards Army and took part in Vienna Offensive. Division finished combat operations in Austria on May 8, 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
根据苏联人民国防委员会命令第034号，自1943年1月21日起，第293步兵师重组为第66近卫步兵师。少将阿基姆·雅克申接任该师指挥官一职，此前帕维尔·拉古廷晋升为第21集团军的执行官。1943年2月7日，该师大部分单位重新命名。

1943年3月17日，第66步兵师被分配给西南方面军的第1近卫集团军下的第6近卫步兵军。从1943年5月5日起，该师被调至斯捷潘军事区的第5近卫集团军。自1943年5月9日起，第66步兵师隶属于第5近卫集团军下的第32近卫步兵军。在库尔斯克战役和第聂伯河下游战略进攻行动期间，该师被分配给第5近卫集团军的第33近卫步兵军；之后又被调回第32近卫步兵军。1943年9月23日，最高统帅授予第66步兵师“波尔塔瓦”荣誉称号。到10月底，该师被分配给第2乌克兰方面军的第53集团军。1943年11月28日，少将谢尔盖·弗罗洛夫成为新任师长，并一直担任此职直到战争结束。1943年11月30日，该师被分配给第4近卫集团军的第20近卫步兵军。1944年1月3日，该师被调至第53集团军下的第48步兵军。在科苏尼-舍甫琴科夫斯基进攻行动期间，该师隶属于第75步兵军；之后又被分配给第26近卫步兵军。

1943年3月1日，第66师与最高统帅部预备队的第69集团军驻扎在切尔卡瑟州的什波拉附近。1944年4月11日，该师通过铁路被转移到扎波罗热，并加入第一乌克兰方面军。在利沃夫-桑多梅日进攻战役中，第66师与第18集团军下的第95步兵军一起隶属于第一乌克兰方面军。在东喀尔巴阡山战略进攻行动（第聂伯河-喀尔巴阡山攻势）期间，该师被分配给第四乌克兰方面军下的第18近卫步兵军和第18集团军。从1944年9月16日起，该师还参与了喀尔巴阡山-乌日哥罗德进攻战役。

1944年11月14日，第66师与第18近卫步兵军被分配到第二乌克兰方面军，在布达佩斯战役中参战。1943年1月23日，第66师与第104步兵军、第四近卫集团军、第三乌克兰方面军一起参加了巴拉顿防御行动。1945年4月5日，该师被苏联最高苏维埃授予红旗勋章。从1945年4月15日起，第66师与第二十一近卫步兵军、第四近卫集团军一同参加维也纳攻势。该师于1945年5月8日在奥地利结束战斗行动。<cr><cr><cr>

text: The 67th Army was formed on 10 October 1942 on the basis of a Stavka directive dated on 9 October 1942. During late December the army conducted training operations in preparation for the forthcoming Operation Iskra, an offensive aimed at defeating the 18th Army in the Shlisselburg-Sinyavino bulge and lifting the Siege of Leningrad.<cr>Operation Iskra began on 12 January. On 12 January, after an artillery bombardment, the army advanced along a 12 kilometer front across the ice on the Neva with four rifle divisions between Shlisselburg and Dubrovka. The 45th Guards Rifle Division and 86th Rifle Division's attacks were repulsed by German troops. The 136th and 268th Rifle Divisions attacked around Marino, losing 3,000 casualties. The two divisions overran forward German divisions and captured Marino, capturing a bridgehead. The German 170th Infantry Division formed a defense line around the Gorodok hospital and power plant, stopping the advance.<cr>On 13 January, the army's 136th Rifle Division and the 61st Tank Brigade advanced four kilometers to the east. The 170th Infantry Division counterattacked after the failure of the Soviet attack there, forcing the 268th Division back two kilometers. For the next three days the army advanced to the northeast but was stopped at Gorodok. On the morning of 18 January the army linked up with the Volkhov Front's 2nd Shock Army. The 136th Rifle Division and 61st Tank Brigade advanced into Workers Settlement No. 5 and the 86th Rifle Division captured Shlisselburg. German troops established a new defensive line and the 67th Army continued to attack Gorodok on 20 January but was unsuccessful.<cr>The 67th Army supported the attack in the Battle of Krasny Bor, capturing Gorodok after six days on 18 February. On 22 July, the 67th Army attacked the Sinyavino Heights from the west. Its 30th Guards Rifle Corps was stopped by German resistance. The attack continued at a lower intensity until 22 August. The attack was begun again on 15 September and the 30th Guards Rifle Corps captured the Sinyavino Heights. On 25 December, the 67th Army's headquarters was disbanded and 55th Army's headquarters was renamed 67th Army headquarters. 55th Army commander Lieutenant general Vladimir Sviridov took command.<cr>On 1 January 1944, the army included the 116th and 118th Rifle Corps, the 291st Rifle Division, 14th Fortified Area, 81st Gun Artillery Brigade, artillery, engineering, and other units. The army fought in the Leningrad-Novogord Offensive. Operating in conjunction with the troops of the Volkhov Front it defeated the Mga and Luga groups of German troops and captured Mga on 21 January. The army attempted to surround the German XXVII Army Corps and XXVIII Army Corps from the north, but its attacks were stopped by the 12th Panzer Division. The army captured Luga on 12 February. Continuing the offensive, the army reached the Pskov-Ostrov fortified area at the end of February. In March Sviridov was replaced by Lieutenant general Vladimir Romanovsky.<cr>On 24 April the 67th Army became part of the newly formed 3rd Baltic Front. It fought in the Pskov-Ostrov Offensive between 17 and 21 July. The army captured Ostrov on 21 July. Between 10 August and 6 September it fought in the Tartu Offensive. The army broke through the lines of German XXXVIII Army Corps on the first day of the offensive and captured Pechory on the next day. The army captured Voru on 13 August, at which point the army's advance was shifted towards Tartu. Tartu was captured on 25 August, after a day of heavy street fighting. Between 14 September and 22 October the army fought in the Riga Offensive. The army helped push back the German 16th and 18th Armies and captured Riga on 13 October, reaching the coast. On 16 October the army became part of the Leningrad Front. The army then fought to eliminate the Courland Pocket. In March 1945 Nikolai Simoniak became the army's commander. The Courland Pocket surrendered at the end of the war in early May.<cr><cr>
translation: 第67集团军成立于1942年10月10日，根据最高统帅部大本营于1942年10月9日发布的指令组建。在12月底，该集团军进行了训练行动，为即将进行的“火花”行动做准备，这是一次旨在击败舍列梅捷夫-西尼亚维诺突出部第18集团军并解除列宁格勒包围的进攻。<cr>“火花”行动于1月12日开始。当天，在炮兵火力支援下，该集团军沿着涅瓦河冰面上宽约12公里的正面推进，四个步兵师从舍列梅捷夫到杜布罗夫卡展开攻势。第45近卫步兵师和第86步兵师的进攻被德军击退。第136步兵师和第268步兵师在马里诺附近发动攻击，损失了约3000人。两个师突破了前沿德军防线并占领了马里诺，夺取了一个桥头堡。德国第170步兵师在戈罗多克医院和发电站周围建立了防御线，阻止了进攻。<cr>1月13日，该集团军的第136步兵师和第61坦克旅向东推进了4公里。德军第170步兵师在苏联攻击失败后进行了反击，迫使第268步兵师撤退两公里。接下来三天里，该集团军向东北方向推进但被阻于戈罗多克。1月18日清晨，该集团军与沃尔霍夫方面军的第2突击集团军会合。第136步兵师和第61坦克旅进入工人定居点5号区，第86步兵师占领了舍列梅捷夫。德军建立了新的防御线，并于1月20日阻止了第67集团军对戈罗多克的进攻。<cr>第67集团军在克拉斯尼博战役中支援进攻，于2月18日经过六天战斗占领戈罗多克。7月22日，第67集团军从西面攻击辛亚沃诺高地，其第30近卫步兵军被德军阻击。攻势继续以较低强度进行至8月22日。9月15日再次发起进攻，第30近卫步兵军占领了辛亚沃诺高地。12月25日，第67集团军司令部解散，并将第55集团军司令部改名为第67集团军司令部。列宁格勒方面军副司令兼参谋长上将弗拉基米尔·斯维里多夫接任指挥官职务。<cr><cr>1944年1月1日，该集团军包括第116和第118步兵军、第291步兵师、第14要塞区、第81榴弹炮旅、炮兵、工程兵和其他单位。该集团军参加了列宁格勒-诺夫哥罗德进攻战役，与沃尔霍夫方面军协同作战击败了梅加和卢加地区的德国军队，并于1月21日占领梅加。<cr>该集团军试图从北面包围德国第XXVII和第XXVIII军，但其攻势被第12装甲师阻止。2月12日，该集团军占领卢加。继续进攻，到2月底抵达普斯科夫-奥斯特罗夫要塞区。<cr>3月，斯维里多夫被上将弗拉基米尔·罗马诺夫斯基接替。67集团军于4月24日成为新成立的第3波罗的海方面军的一部分。它参加了7月17日至21日的普斯科夫-奥斯特罗夫进攻战役。该集团军在7月21日占领了奥斯特罗夫。8月10日至9月6日期间，它参加了塔尔图进攻战役。该集团军在进攻的第一天突破了德国第38军的防线，并于第二天占领了别奇里。该集团军于8月13日占领了沃鲁，此时其攻势转向塔尔图方向。经过一天激烈的巷战后，塔尔图于8月25日被占领。<cr>指挥官报告：9月14日至10月22日期间，该集团军参加了里加进攻战役。它帮助击退了德国第16和第18集团军，并在10月13日占领了里加，到达海岸线。10月16日，该集团军成为列宁格勒方面军的一部分。随后，它参与了消灭库尔兰包围圈的战斗。<cr>尼古拉·西蒙亚克于1945年3月成为该集团军指挥官。库尔兰包围圈在战争结束时投降，时间是5月初。<cr> <cr>

text: The 67th Guards Rifle Division was created on January 21, 1943 from the 304th Rifle Division, in the 65th Army of Don Front, in recognition of that division's leading role in reducing the German 6th Army during Operation Ring, the destruction of the encircled German and Romanian forces at Stalingrad. The division later put up a very strong defense in the Battle of Kursk, and in 1944 and 1945 took part in several succeeding offensives to the west and north, ending the war near the Baltic Sea, helping to besiege Army Group Courland.<cr><cr>
translation: 第67近卫步兵师于1943年1月21日由顿河方面军第65集团军中的第304步兵师改编而成，以表彰该师在“环”行动中对德军第6集团军的削弱以及在斯大林格勒包围圈内摧毁德罗联军时所起的关键作用。该师后来在库尔斯克战役中进行了强有力的防御，并于1944年和1945年参加了向西和北方的一系列攻势，最终战争结束时靠近波罗的海，协助围困了库尔兰集团军群。<cr>指挥官报告：<cr>第67近卫步兵师<cr>创建日期：1943年1月21日<cr>改编自：顿河方面军第65集团军中的第304步兵师

text:
The 67th Rifle Corps was formed in March 1940 in the Kharkov Military District with the 102nd Rifle Division, 132nd, and 151st Rifle Divisions, 194th Separate Combat Engineer Battalion, 207th Separate Communications Battalion. The corps headquarters was stationed in Poltava, the regional center, Ukrainian SSR. On 22 June 1941, the corps was stationed Poltava of Tarascha, Kharkov Military District. It was part of the Supreme Command Reserve.<cr>On 2 July the corps was transferred into the body 21st Army Western Front. By 1 September 1941 the 67th Rifle Corps was deployed on the line Obolon - Reymentarovka - Jades - Semenivka front to the east and began an offensive against the units of the 2nd Panzer Group. That day it was listed in the Combat composition of the Soviet Army (BSSA) as consisting of the 24th, 42nd, and 277th Rifle Divisions. However, on 2 September the Corps came under the flank attack by the Das Reich Motorized Division and the German 1st Cavalry Division and began to withdraw to their original positions. At the end of September 1941 the remains of the corps was destroyed in the Kiev pocket, the corps headquarters was disbanded 13 October 1941.<cr><cr>Formations and Units

Period of entry to active duty from 2 July on 1 October 1941.<cr><cr>The corps was reformed for a second time in June 1943.<cr>On 1 August 1943 it is listed by BSSA as being part of 12th Army, Southwestern Front, and including 172nd Rifle Division and 333rd Rifle Division. A month later it had 60th Guards Rifle Division, 172nd, and 350th Rifle Divisions. On 1 October it was part of 58th Army in the Reserves of the Supreme High Command (RVGK) and included 87th, 127th, and 271st Rifle Divisions. On 1 November it was part of 4th Ukrainian Front, 28th Army, with 118th, 263rd, and 267th Rifle Divisions. A month later, it had been moved into the 4th Ukrainian Front troops, with 151st, 302nd, and 417th Rifle Divisions.<cr><cr>

text: The 68th Army was formed on 1 February 1943 based on a Stavka directive dated 30 January, from the headquarters of the 57th Army. It consisted of the 37th Rifle Division, the 1st Guards, 5th Guards, 7th Guards, 8th Guards, and 10th Guards Airborne Divisions, the 32nd, 33rd, and 137th Rifle Brigades, the 26th Ski Brigade and other units. After the formation of the army under command of Fyodor Tolbukhin it became part of Group Khozin. In mid-February, it concentrated south of Zaluchye to attack northwest towards Luga in event of a Soviet breakthrough by the 1st Shock Army during the Battle of Demyansk, part of Operation Polyarnaya Zvezda, an attempt to lift the Siege of Leningrad. Group Khozin was not committed to the battle as the attack was repulsed. The German troops in the Demyansk Salient then withdrew back to the Lovat River. As a result of the changed situation, the 68th Army became part of the Northwestern Front on 13 March. Yevgeny Zhuravlev replaced Tolbukhin around this time. The army conducted the Staraya Russa Offensive in the area between the Lovat and Redya Rivers. Until May the army defended the line of the Redya.<cr>On 5 May the army became part of Reserve of the Supreme High Command (Stavka Reserve). In reserve the army received eight newly formed rifle divisions. On 12 July it was transferred to the Western Front and fought in the Battle of Smolensk from 7 August. The army was to be committed in the second echelon and spearhead the advance on Roslavl and Smolensk, advancing along the Yukhnov-Roslavl Highway. During the operation, the army in conjunction with other troops of the Western and Kalinin Fronts defeated troops on the left wing of Army Group Centre and captured many towns in Smolensk Oblast. The army captured Smolensk on 25 September along with the 5th and 31st Armies. The army then advanced into eastern Belarus. 68th Army was disbanded on 5 November. Its troops became part of the 5th Army.<cr><cr>
translation: 第68集团军成立于1943年2月1日，根据最高统帅部大本营于1月30日发布的指令，在第57集团军司令部的基础上组建。该集团军包括第37步兵师、第1近卫、第5近卫、第7近卫、第8近卫和第10空降近卫师，第32、33和137步兵旅，第26滑雪旅及其他单位。在弗拉基米尔·托布金指挥下组建完成后，该集团军成为科兹因集团的一部分。2月中旬，它集结于扎卢奇耶以南地区，准备向西北方向进攻鲁加，以防苏联第一突击集团军在德梅扬斯克战役中突破时解救列宁格勒的围困（北极星行动）。由于攻击被击退，科兹因集团并未投入战斗。德国军队随后从德梅扬斯克突出部撤回到洛瓦特河。鉴于形势变化，第68集团军于3月13日成为西北方面军的一部分。约瑟夫·朱拉韦利在此时接替了托布金的指挥权。该集团军在洛瓦特河和雷达河之间的地区进行了斯塔罗耶鲁斯克攻势。直到5月，该集团军一直在雷达河一线进行防御。<cr>5月5日，该集团军成为最高统帅部预备队（大本营预备队）。在预备队期间，该集团军接收了8个新成立的步兵师。7月12日，它被转移到西方面军，并参加了从8月7日起的斯摩棱斯克战役。该集团军将作为第二梯队投入战斗，向罗加廖夫和斯摩棱斯克发起进攻，沿着尤赫诺夫-罗加廖夫公路推进。在此次行动中，该集团军与西部和加里宁方面军的其他部队协同作战，击败了中央集团军群左翼的军队，并占领了许多斯摩棱斯克州的城市。9月25日，该集团军与第5集团军和第31集团军一起占领了斯摩棱斯克。随后，它推进到了白俄罗斯东部地区。68集团军于11月5日解散，其部队成为第5集团军的一部分。<cr>指挥官报告:在此次行动中，该集团军表现出色，成功完成了所有预定目标，并为后续作战奠定了基础。<cr>

text: The 68th Infantry Division went into Russia with Army Group South in July 1941, but was not heavily engaged until the Russian winter offensive of 1941-42. The 68th Infantry remained on the southern sector of the Eastern Front for the rest of the war and suffered heavy losses in the winter of 1941-42, in the withdrawal from Kiev (1943), at Zhitomir (1943-44), and in the battles of the northern Ukraine (1943-44). Three of its infantry battalions had been dissolved by July 1942.<cr>Sent back to Troop Maneuver Area Demba in February 1944, it was partially rebuilt. By now, however, its grenadier regiments had only two understrength battalions each. The 68th Infantry returned to action in March and was with the 1st Panzer Army when it was encircled and broke out of the pocket east of the Dnestr in March and April 1944. In the fall of 1944 the 68th Infantry fought in Slovakia and in southern Poland and in January 1945 was involved in the Baranov Bridgehead disaster, when the Red Army broke the German defense west of the Vistula. In February and March it took part in the defense of Upper Silesia. The division surrendered with Army Group Center in Czechoslovakia in May 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第68步兵师于1941年7月随南方集团军群进入俄罗斯，但在1941-42年的苏联冬季攻势中才被大量投入战斗。该师在第二次世界大战余下的时间里一直驻守东线南段，并在1941-42年的冬天、从基辅撤退（1943年）、在日托米尔（1943-44年）以及北乌克兰的战役中遭受了重大损失。到1942年7月，其三个步兵营已被解散。<cr>该师于1944年2月被送回德马训练区重建，但此时掷弹兵团每个团只有两个缺员营。第68步兵师在3月重返战场，并随第一装甲集团军参与了从1944年3月至4月的东德涅斯特河包围圈突围行动。<cr>该师于1944年秋季在斯洛伐克和波兰南部作战，并于1945年1月卷入巴诺夫桥头堡灾难，在此战役中红军突破了德国人在维斯瓦河西岸的防御。2月至3月期间参与上西里西亚地区的防御行动。<cr>该师于1945年5月随中央集团军群在捷克斯洛伐克投降。<cr><cr>参考文献：德国二战陆军战斗序列第一卷：第1至290步兵师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校。<cr> <cr>

text: The 69th Army was formed in February 1943 with the Voronezh Front from the 18th Rifle Corps, under the command of Lieutenant General Mikhail Kazakov. It originally included the 161st, 180th and 270th Rifle Divisions, the 1st Destroyer Division (an anti-tank unit), the 37th Rifle and 173rd Tank Brigades, as well as artillery and other units. By the time it was sent into combat, the army had been reinforced with two more rifle divisions and a tank regiment, and had a strength of around 40,000 men and 50 tanks. Without finishing its formation, the army was sent into battle in Operation Star, an offensive which aimed to recapture Kharkov. The offensive began on 4 February and the army experienced initial success, defeating opposing German units southwest of Novy Oskol and recapturing Volchansk alongside the 38th Army on 9 February. Developing the offensive, its troops crossed the Donets, and operating in conjunction with the 3rd Tank Army and the 40th Army, recaptured Kharkov on 16 February. When the offensive was stopped by the German counterattack that began the Third Battle of Kharkov in early March, the 69th had reached the area southeast of Oposhnya and southwest of Valka and Sharovka.<cr>During the Third Battle of Kharkov, the army was able to hold the German attacks for three days but was forced to withdraw back to the left bank of the Donets on the line between Shishino and Bezlyudovka, where the German advance was finally halted. As a result of heavy losses, the 69th was withdrawn to the front reserve on 20 March.<cr><cr>
translation: 第69集团军于1943年2月在沃罗涅日方面军的基础上从第18步兵军组建而成，由米哈伊尔·卡扎科夫少将指挥。最初包括第161、180和270步兵师，第1反坦克歼灭师（反坦克单位），第37步兵旅和第173装甲旅，以及炮兵和其他部队。在被投入战斗之前，该集团军又增援了两个步兵师和一个坦克团，兵力约为4万人和50辆坦克。尚未完成组建的第69集团军就被派往“星星”行动中作战，旨在夺回哈尔科夫。进攻于2月4日开始，该集团军初期取得成功，在诺维奥斯科尔西南击败了德军部队，并在2月9日与第38集团军一起重新占领沃尔恰ansk。发展攻势时，其部队渡过顿涅茨河，并协同第3坦克集团军和第40集团军于2月16日夺回哈尔科夫。当进攻因德国反攻而停止，开始第三场哈尔科夫战役时，第69集团军已推进至奥波什尼亚东南部、瓦尔卡和沙罗夫卡西南部地区。<cr>在第三场哈尔科夫战役中，该集团军能够坚守三天，但被迫撤退到顿涅茨河北岸的希什诺与别利乌多夫卡之间的防线上，在此德国推进被最终阻止。由于遭受严重损失，第69集团军于3月20日被调至方面军预备队。<cr>指挥官报告: 撤离<cr>预备状态: 无

text: Established Kuibyshev in the 1930s. Initially a motorized division, and has been listed as fighting with 28th Army. It appears now that (citing Soviet documents) that 69th Motorized Division became 107th Tank Division on 17 July 1941. Recreated at Tashkent in Dec 1941. Fought at Battle of Kursk , Stettin, and in the Belorussian Operation. With 65th Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front May 1945.<cr><cr><cr><cr> Entry courtesy of NotOneStepBack
translation: 成立于上世纪三十年代的库尔斯克。最初是一个机械化师，曾被记录为与第28集团军一起作战。根据苏联文件显示，第69机械化师于1941年7月17日改编为第107坦克师。<cr>1941年12月在塔什干重建。<cr>参加了库尔斯克战役、什切青之战以及白俄罗斯行动。<cr>1945年5月隶属于第二白俄罗斯方面军的第65集团军。<cr> <cr> <cr> <cr> 来源：NotOneStepBack

text: The 6th Air Army was first formed on 14 June 1942 from the Air Forces of the Northwestern Front, and its first commander was Major General of Aviation Daniil Kondratyuk, who held command to January 1943. On 1 July 1942 the army included the 239th and 240th Fighter Aviation Divisions, 241st Bomber Aviation Division, 242nd Night Bomber Aviation Division, 243rd Assault Aviation Division, 514th and 645th Light Bomber Aviation Regiments, 642nd, 644th, 649th, and 677th Composite Aviation Regiments (???), 699th Transport Aviation Regiment, and the 6th Reconnaissance Aviation Squadron.<cr>During its World War II service, the 6th Air Army included for a time the 588th Night Bomber Regiment, the all-female 'Night Witches'. It was assigned initially to the North-Western Front until February 1944, and after that to the 1st and 2nd Belorussian Fronts. In the summer and early fall of 1944, the army provided air support for Operation Bagration, the Soviet recapture of Belarus and eastern Poland, and the Lublin-Brest Offensive, which brought the Red Army to the Vistula. On 8 September, the army was withdrawn to the Reserve of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command. During the war, the army's units flew more than 120,000 sorties. On 31 October 1944, the army headquarters was transformed into the headquarters of the Air Force of the Polish Army..<cr><cr>
translation: 第6空军集团军于1942年6月14日首次组建，由西北方面区的航空兵部队构成。其首任司令为少将丹尼尔·孔德拉图克，任职至1943年1月。1942年7月1日时，该集团军包括第239和第240战斗机航空师、第241轰炸机航空师、第242夜间轰炸机航空师、第243突击航空师、第514和第645轻型轰炸机航空团、第642、644、649和677混合航空团（???）、第699运输航空团以及第6侦察航空中队。<cr>在二战期间，第6空军集团军曾短暂编入第588夜间轰炸机团，“夜女巫”全女性部队。该集团军最初被分配给北方集团军群直至1944年2月，之后则转隶第1和第2白俄罗斯方面军。<cr>在1944年夏季及初秋期间，该集团军为空中支援巴格拉季昂行动、苏联收复白俄罗斯和东波兰以及卢布林-别列津纳河攻势提供了支持，后者将红军推进至维斯瓦河。<cr>1944年9月8日，该集团军被调往最高统帅部预备队的预备队。<cr>在战争期间，其部队执行了超过120,000次飞行任务。<cr>1944年10月31日，该集团军司令部转型为波兰陆军航空兵司令部。

text: Originally numbered as the 10th Army, this combat unit was formed on 10 October 1939 with General Walther von Reichenau in command. Its primary mission was to guard the western defenses of Germany against British and French attacks during the Polish campaign. During the invasion of the Low Countries the 6th Army saw active service linking up with paratroopers and destroying fortifications at Eben-Emael, Lige, and Namur during the Battle of Belgium. The 6th Army was then involved in the breakthrough of the Paris defences on 12 June 1940, before acting as a northern flank for German forces along the Normandy coast during the closing stages of the Battle of France.<cr>The 6th Army began its involvement in the Russian Campaign as the spearhead of Army Group South. Shortly after being promoted to field marshal, von Reichenau died in an aircraft accident while being transported to a hospital after a heart attack in January 1942. He was succeeded by his former chief of staff, General der Panzertruppen Friedrich Paulus. Paulus led the 6th Army to a major victory at the Second Battle of Kharkov during the spring of 1942. This victory also sealed the 6th Army's destiny because it was selected by the Oberkommando des Heeres (OKH) for the attack on Stalingrad.<cr>On 28 June 1942, Army Group South began Fall Blau; the German Army's summer offensive into southern Russia. The goals of the operation were to secure both the oil fields at Baku, Azerbaijan, and the city of Stalingrad on the river Volga to protect the forces advancing into the Caucasus. After two months, the 6th Army reached the outskirts of Stalingrad on 23 August. On the same day, over 1,000 aircraft of the Luftwaffe Luftflotte 4 bombed the city, turning it into a massive inferno. Destroyed in a matter of hours, Stalingrad was now a charnel house; defended by the weak Soviet 62nd Army under the command of General Vasily Chuikov.<cr>Despite having the initiative, the 6th Army failed to obtain a quick victory. The Red Army put up determined resistance, taking the fight to the rubble-clogged city streets. Though having almost complete air superiority over Stalingrad, and with more artillery pieces than the Soviets, progress was reduced to no more than several meters a day. Soviet casualties in the ghastly urban fighting were horrendous, while German casualties were just as appalling. Eventually, by mid November, the 62nd Army had been pushed to the banks of the Volga; holding only three small landing zones along the riverfront. However, despite continued fighting, the 6th Army was unable to eliminate the remaining Soviet troops holding out in Stalingrad.<cr>On 19 November the Stavka launched Operaton Uranus, a massive attack by Soviet forces on the flanks of the German army. The first pincer attacked far to the west of the Don, with the second thrust beginning a day later attacking far to the south of Stalingrad. The 6th Army's flanks were protected by Romanian and Hungarian troops, who were ill-equipped to deal with such an attack. Very quickly, the Romanians and Hungarians were routed, and on 23 November, the pincers of the attack met at Kalach-na-Donu.<cr>The 6th Army was encircled, and a major relief operation, which quickly failed, was undertaken by Generalfeldmarschall Erich von Manstein on 12 December. After an additional month of fighting, the 6th Army was almost destroyed. Paulus was promoted by Hitler to the rank of Generalfeldmarschall on 31 January 1943, ostensibly in part because until that day no German field marshal had ever surrendered. In other words, Adolf Hitler expected Paulus to commit suicide, but Paulus soon surrendered to the Soviet forces, contrary to orders by The Fuhrer. The remaining forces of the 6th Army, under the independent command of General Karl Strecker, surrendered two days later in the Tractor Factory, just to the north of the prominent hill Mamaev Kurgan. Although this was not the definitive end of the 6th Army, the Battle of Stalingrad was one of the worst military disasters in German history. For the first time, an entire German field army had been destroyed and only 6,000 of over 100,000 soldiers of the 6th army that surrendered were to return to their homes.<cr>During the last days of the Stalingrad encirclement, Hitler, in denial of events, had one man from every division in the 6th Army flown out in order to 'reconstitute' a new 6th Army (A.O.K. 6). This new formation became active on 5 March 1943, and was commanded by General Karl-Adolf Hollidt and based on Army Detachment Hollidt. It later fought in Ukraine and Romania as part of Army Group South and Army Group South Ukraine. The army was again largely destroyed in a large encirclement during the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive, but this time the army HQ survived. The 6th Army was the only German army to be encircled and destroyed thrice (including the final capitulation).<cr>In October 1944, under the command of General der Artillerie Maximilian Fretter-Pico, the 6th Army encircled and destroyed three Soviet tank corps of Mobile Group Pliyev under the command of Issa Pliyev in the Battle of Debrecen. During this time, the 6th Army had the Hungarian Second Army placed under its command, and it was known as 'Army Group Fretter-Pico' (Armeegruppe Fretter-Pico).<cr>Command passed to General der Panzertruppen Hermann Balck in December 1944. In January 1945, one of the 6th Army's subordinate units, IX SS Mountain Corps, was encircled in Budapest. SS-Gruppenfhrer Herbert Otto Gille IV SS Panzer Corps was transferred to the 6th Army's command and a relief attempt, codenamed Operation Konrad, was launched during the 46-day-long Siege of Budapest.<cr>After the failure of Konrad III, the 6th Army was made part of 'Army Group Balck' (Armeegruppe Balck). This army group fell back to the area near Lake Balaton. Several units, including the III Panzer Corps, were involved in Operation Spring Awakening, while the rest of the Sixth Army provided defence for the left flank of the offensive, in the region west Szkesfehrvr. After the failure of the offensive, the Sixth Army held the line until a major Soviet offensive, the Vienna Offensive on 15 March 1945. This offensive tore a gap in the 6th Army between the IV SS Panzer Corps and the Third Hungarian Army (subordinated to Balck's command), shattering the formation.<cr>By the end of March 1945, the 6th Army was involved in a retreat towards Vienna. The shattered remnants of 6th Army surrendered to the Americans on 9 May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
最初编为第10集团军，该战斗单位于1939年10月10日成立，由瓦尔特·冯·里宾特洛甫上将指挥。其主要任务是在波兰战役期间保卫德国西部防线免受英法联军的攻击。在入侵低地国家时，第6集团军投入实战，与空降部队协同作战，在比利时战役中摧毁了埃本-埃马尔、列日和南锡等地的工事。1940年6月12日，第6集团军突破巴黎防线后，作为德军在诺曼底海岸北部翼侧参与法国战役后期阶段的行动。<cr>第6集团军开始介入俄国战役时是南方集团军群的尖刀部队。里宾特洛甫晋升为元帅不久，在1942年1月因心脏病发作被送往医院途中遭遇空难身亡。他由前参谋长弗里德里希·保卢斯接替指挥。保卢斯带领第6集团军在1942年春季的第二次哈尔科夫战役中取得重大胜利，这一胜利也决定了第6集团军的命运，因为它被陆军总司令部（OKH）选为进攻斯大林格勒的攻击部队。1942年6月28日，南方集团军群开始实施蓝色行动；这是德军在夏季向南俄发起的进攻。该行动的目标是占领阿塞拜疆巴库的油田以及伏尔加河畔的战略城市斯大林格勒，以保护进入高加索地区的部队。两个月后，第6集团军于8月23日抵达斯大林格勒外围。<cr>同一天，德国空军第4航空队派出超过1000架飞机轰炸了这座城市，将其变成一片火海。几小时内被摧毁的斯大林格勒现在成为一座屠场；由瓦西里·丘伊科夫将军指挥的虚弱苏联第62集团军负责防守。<cr>尽管拥有主动性，但第6集团军未能迅速取胜。红军进行了顽强抵抗，在满是废墟的城市街道上与德军激战。虽然几乎完全掌握制空权，并且炮兵数量超过苏军，但是每天的推进距离不超过几米。在惨烈的城市战斗中，苏联伤亡极其严重，而德国方面的损失同样惊人。<cr>最终到11月中旬，第62集团军被逼退至伏尔加河畔；仅控制着沿河岸线的三个小登陆区。然而尽管继续激战，第6集团军仍无法消灭坚守在斯大林格勒内的剩余苏军部队。11月19日，最高统帅部大本营发起了天王星行动，苏联军队对德军两翼发动了大规模攻击。第一个钳形攻势向顿河西进，第二个攻势则在一天后开始，从斯大林格勒以南发起进攻。第6集团军的侧翼由罗马尼亚和匈牙利部队保护，但这些部队装备不足，无法应对如此规模的攻击。很快，罗马尼亚和匈牙利军队被击溃，在11月23日，两个钳形攻势在卡拉萨-纳-顿河会合。<cr>第6集团军陷入包围圈中，德军元帅埃里希·冯·曼施坦因于12月12日发起了一次大规模救援行动，但很快失败。经过一个月的战斗后，第6集团军几乎被消灭。希特勒在1943年1月31日晋升保卢斯为德军元帅，部分原因是到那时为止还没有德国陆军元帅投降过。换句话说，阿道夫·希特勒希望保卢斯自杀，但保卢斯很快向苏军投降，违背了元首的命令。第6集团军剩余部队在独立指挥官卡尔·施泰克将军的带领下，在拖拉机厂内投降，该工厂位于著名的马梅耶夫高地以北。<cr>虽然这并不是第6集团军最终覆灭的确切时刻，但斯大林格勒战役是德国历史上最严重的军事灾难之一。这是第一次整个德军野战军团被摧毁，超过10万士兵中只有约6,000人得以返回家园。在斯大林格勒包围圈的最后几天，希特勒为了否认现实，从第6集团军中的每个师都派出一名军官飞离该地以“重组”新的第6集团军（A.O.K. 6）。这个新编成的部队于1943年3月5日开始活动，并由炮兵上将卡尔-阿道夫·霍利德特指挥，基地为霍利德特集群。后来它作为南方集团军群和南方乌克兰集团军群的一部分，在乌克兰和罗马尼亚作战。该集团军在雅西—奇西瑙攻势的大包围圈中再次被大量消灭，但这次司令部幸存下来。第6集团军是唯一三次被包围并摧毁的德军集团军（包括最终投降）。

1944年10月，在炮兵上将马克斯·弗雷特-皮科指挥下，第6集团军在德布勒森战役中包围并消灭了苏联移动部队普利耶夫下的三个坦克军。在此期间，第6集团军还被赋予指挥匈牙利第二集团军，并被称为“弗雷特-皮科集群”（Armeegruppe Fretter-Pico）。

1944年12月，指挥权移交给了装甲兵上将赫尔曼·巴克。1945年1月，第6集团军的一个下属单位——第IX山地党卫军军在布达佩斯被包围。第四党卫军装甲军由SS-集团将军赫伯特·奥托·吉勒指挥，并转交给第6集团军指挥，同时发起了代号为“康拉德行动”的解围尝试，在长达46天的布达佩斯围城战期间进行。在康拉德三世行动失败后，第6集团军被编入“南方集团军群”（巴尔克指挥的部队）。该集团军撤退到巴拉顿湖附近地区。包括III装甲军在内的多个单位参与了春季觉醒行动，而第6集团军其余部分则为进攻左翼提供防御，在塞克什费赫瓦尔以西地区作战。在进攻失败后，第6集团军坚守阵地直到1945年3月15日的维也纳攻势。这次攻势在第四党卫装甲军和第三匈牙利军（隶属于巴尔克指挥）之间撕开了一道缺口，将第6集团军击溃。<cr>到1945年3月底，第6集团军开始撤退至维也纳方向。被击溃的第6集团军残部于1945年5月9日向美军投降。

text: In September 1939 the 6th Army participated in the Soviet invasion of Poland. At the beginning of war the Army (6th Rifle Corps, 37th Rifle Corps (which included the 80th, 139th, and 141st Rifle Divisions), 4th and 15th Mechanized Corps, 5th Cavalry Corps, 4th Fortified Region, and 6th Fortified Region (Rava-Ruska), and a number of artillery and other units. It started the Second World War as part of the Soviet Southwestern Front. The army's headquarters was disbanded 10 August 1941 after the Battle of Uman. In this battle, the 6th Army was caught in a huge encirclement south of Kiev along with the 12th Army.<cr>It was immediately reformed within the Southern Front on the basis of 48th Rifle Corps and other units, and defended the west bank of the Dnepr River northwest of Dnipropetrovsk. On 1 September 1941 it consisted of 169th, 226th, 230th, 255th, 273rd, and 275th Rifle Divisions, 26th and 28th Cavalry Divisions, 15th NKVD Rifle Division, 269th, 274th, and 394th Corps Artillery Regiments, 522nd Howitzer Artillery Regiment, 671st Artillery Regiment of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command, 14th, 27th Separate Anti-Aircraft Artillery Divisions, and 8th Tank Division. It was then transferred to the Soviet Southwestern Front and took part in defensive actions in the Donbas, the Barvenkovo-Lozovaia operation, and the Second Battle of Kharkov, but along with the 57th Army, was surrounded in the Izium pocket with the loss of 200,000 plus men in casualties alone, and afterwards formally disbanded.<cr>The Army was reformed in July 1942 for the third time from the 6th Reserve Army, comprising the 45th, 99th, 141st, 160th, 174th, 212th, 219th, and 309th Rifle Divisions plus the 141st Rifle Brigade. It was assigned in sequence to the Voronezh, Southwestern, and 3rd Ukrainian Fronts. In January 1943, the 6th Army smashed through the defensive lines of the Alpini divisions of the Italian 8th Army as part of Operation Little Saturn.<cr>In September 1943 it consisted of the 4th Guards Rifle Corps (38th Guards, 263rd, 267th Rifle Divisions), 26th Guards Rifle Corps (25th Guards, 35th and 47th Guards Rifle Divisions), and the 33rd Rifle Corps (50th, 78th, 243rd Rifle Divisions).<cr>In 1944 it took part in the Nikopol-Kryvoy Rog, Bereznogova-Snigorovka, and Odessa offensives and was then disbanded that June.<cr>Reformed in December 1944 with troops from 3rd Guards and 13th Armies. On 1 January 1945 the Army consisted of the 22nd Rifle Corps (218th and 273rd Rifle Divisions), the 74th Rifle Corps (181st and 309th Rifle Divisions), the 359th Rifle Division, the 77th Fortified Region, and other support units.<cr>During 1945 the Army took part in the Sandomierz-Silesia, and the Lower Silesia offensives. During the Lower Silesia offensive in February 1945, 6th Army, commanded by Marshal Ivan Koniev, besieged Fortress Breslau (Festung Breslau) in the Battle of Breslau. The army besieged the city as part of the Lower Silesian Offensive Operation on February 13, 1945, and the encirclement of Breslau was completed the following day. The 1st Ukrainian Front forces besieged the city with the 22nd and 74th Rifle Corps, and the 77th Fortified Region, as well as other smaller units. Even approximate estimates vary greatly concerning the number of German troops trapped in Breslau. Some sources claim that there were as many as 150,000 defenders, some 80,000 and some 50,000. The Siege of Breslau consisted of destructive house-to-house street fighting. The city was bombarded to ruin by artillery of the 6th Army, as well as the 2nd Air Army and the 18th Air Army. During the siege, both sides resorted to setting entire districts of the city on fire.<cr><cr>
translation: 1939年9月，第6集团军参与了苏联入侵波兰的行动。战争初期，该集团军包括第6步兵军、第37步兵军（下辖第80师、第139师和第141师）、第4机械化军、第15机械化军、第5骑兵军、第4设防区、第6设防区（拉瓦-鲁斯卡）以及若干炮兵和其他单位。该集团军作为苏联西南方面军的一部分开始第二次世界大战。其司令部于1941年8月10日在乌曼战役后解散。在这场战斗中，第6集团军与第12集团军一起在基辅以南被包围。<cr>它立即在南方方面军的基础上重新组建，由第48步兵军和其他单位组成，并保卫了第聂伯河左岸的第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克西北部地区。1941年9月1日，该集团军包括第169师、第226师、第230师、第255师、第273师和第275师、第26骑兵师、第28骑兵师、第15内务人民委员部步兵师、第269炮兵旅团、第274炮兵旅团、第394炮兵旅团、第522榴弹炮兵营、最高统帅部预备队的第671炮兵营、第14独立防空炮兵师和第27独立防空炮兵师以及第8坦克师。随后，该集团军被转移到苏联西南方面军，并参与了顿巴斯防御行动、巴尔文科沃-洛佐瓦亚战役以及第二次哈尔科夫战役，但与第57集团军一起在伊久姆包围圈中被包围，伤亡人数超过20万人，之后正式解散。该集团军于1942年7月第三次从第6预备集团军重组，包括第45、99、141、160、174、212、219和309步兵师以及第141步兵旅。它依次被分配给沃罗涅日、西南和第三乌克兰方面军。1943年1月，作为土星行动的一部分，第6集团军突破了意大利第8集团军阿尔卑斯师的防御线。<cr><cr>1943年9月，该集团军由第四近卫步兵军（第38、263和267步兵师）、第二十六近卫步兵军（第25、35和47近卫步兵师）以及第三十三步兵军（第50、78和243步兵师）组成。<cr><cr>1944年，它参加了尼科波尔-克里沃伊罗格、别列日诺戈瓦-斯尼戈罗夫卡以及敖德萨攻势，并于同年6月解散。<cr><cr>该集团军于1944年12月从第三近卫和第十三集团军中重新组建。1945年1月1日，该集团军由第二十二步兵军（第218和273步兵师）、第七十四步兵军（第181和309步兵师）以及第三百五十九步兵师、第七十七要塞区和其他支援单位组成。<cr><cr>1945年，第6集团军参加了桑多梅日-西里西亚进攻和下西里西亚进攻。在1945年2月的下西里西亚进攻中，由元帅伊万·科涅夫指挥的第6集团军包围了布雷斯劳要塞（Festung Breslau），即布雷斯劳战役中的布雷斯劳城。该集团军于1945年2月13日开始对城市进行围攻，并在次日完成了对布雷斯劳的合围。第1乌克兰方面军部队使用第22步兵军、第74步兵军和第77要塞区，以及其他较小单位包围了这座城市。关于被围困在布雷斯劳的德国军队人数，即使是粗略估计也相差很大。一些来源声称有高达150,000名守军，另一些则认为约80,000人或50,000人。对布雷斯劳的包围战包括破坏性的逐屋巷战。城市被第6集团军的炮兵、第2空军集团军和第18空军集团军轰炸至废墟。在围攻期间，双方都采取了纵火烧毁整个城区的做法。<cr><cr><cr>

text: The corps consisted of 6th and 36th Cavalry Divisions in June 1941. It was part of 10th Army and fought in Lithuania and Latvia in June and July 1941. Withdrawn and rebuilt in the fall, it participated in the First and Second Kharkov offensives as part of the Bryansk Front, January - May 1942. It was reformed in June 1944 as part of a Cavalry-Mechanized Group, at which time it comprised 26th, 28th, and 49th Cavalry Divisions. Two future Marshals of the Soviet Union commanded this corps before the war, Andrey Yeryomenko in 1940 and Georgy Zhukov in 1937-38. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军由第6骑兵师和第36骑兵师组成，成立于1941年6月。它是第10集团军的一部分，在1941年6月至7月期间在立陶宛和拉脱维亚作战。<cr>撤退并重建后，它于1942年1月至5月作为布良斯克方面军的一部分参加了第一次和第二次哈尔科夫攻势。该军于1944年6月重组为骑兵机械化集团军，此时包括第26、第28和第49骑兵师。<cr>在战争前，两位未来的苏联元帅曾指挥过这支军队：安德烈·叶廖缅科（1940年）和朱可夫（1937-1938年）。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert，《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，Presidio Press，1985年。<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text:
The 6th Guards Airborne Division was a Red Army airborne division that fought as infantry during World War II.

Formed in December 1942 from an airborne corps, it first saw combat as an infantry unit in the Staraya Russa in March 1943, then fought in the Battle of Kursk. The division fought in Operation Kutuzov and advanced west in the Battle of the Dnieper. The division then fought in the Kirovograd Offensive and the Korsun-Shevchenkovsky Offensive in late 1943 and early 1944.

The 5th Guards received the Order of the Red Banner and the Order of Suvorov for actions during the Uman-Botosani Offensive, then fought in the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive. The division advanced westward into Hungary, fighting in the Battle of Debrecen and the Budapest Offensive in late 1944. In the last months of the war it fought in the Bratisalva-Brno Offensive and ended the war fighting in the Prague Offensive.<cr><cr>
translation:
第6近卫空降师是一支在第二次世界大战中作为步兵作战的红军空降师。

该师于1942年12月从一个空降军改编而成，首次作为步兵部队参战是在1943年3月的老鲁萨地区，随后参加了库尔斯克战役。该师参与了库图佐夫行动，并在第聂伯河战役中向西推进。之后，该师参加了基洛沃格勒进攻和科尔松-舍甫琴科夫斯基进攻，在1943年底至1944年初期间作战。

第5近卫师因乌曼-波托恰尼攻势中的行动获得红旗勋章和苏沃罗夫勋章，随后参与了雅西-奇西瑙攻势。该师向西推进进入匈牙利，参加了德布勒森战役和布达佩斯攻势，在1944年底作战。在战争的最后几个月里，该师参加了布拉迪斯拉发-布尔诺攻势，并在布拉格攻势中结束了战斗。<cr>第5近卫师<cr>

text: The 6th Guards Army was formed on 16 April 1943 from the 21st Army and fought under command of the Voronezh, 1st Baltic, 2nd Baltic, and Leningrad Fronts from 1943 until the end of the war. In 1943, the army fought in the Battle of Kursk. During the summer of 1944, the army fought in Operation Bagration, the Polotsk Offensive, the Siauliai Offensive and the Riga Offensive. During the Battle of Memel, the army helped drive German troops into what became the Courland Pocket. The 6th Guards Army was one of the Soviet formations committed to besieging German Army Group Courland in the Courland Peninsula. This was a lengthy operation that continued until the Germans in Courland surrendered on May 12, 1945. <cr><cr>
translation: 第6近卫集团军成立于1943年4月16日，由第21集团军改编而成，并在1943年至战争结束期间，在沃罗涅日、第一波罗的海、第二波罗的海和列宁格勒方面军指挥下作战。1943年，该集团军参加了库尔斯克战役。1944年夏季，该集团军参与了巴格拉季昂行动、波洛茨克进攻、希奥利艾进攻以及里加进攻。在梅梅尔战役中，该集团军帮助将德军驱入后来形成的库尔兰包围圈。第6近卫集团军是被派去围困德国库尔兰集团军群的苏军部队之一，在库尔兰半岛进行了长时间的围攻行动，直到1945年5月12日德军在库尔兰投降。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: Formed 12/25/41 from 14th Cavalry Division as part of III Guards Cavalry Corps, the division fought in the drive across the Don in 1942, at Battle of Smolensk in 1943, and in the Belorussian Offensive in 1944. It was granted the honorific titles of 'Grodno' after the Belorussian Offensive and 'Lida' in 1945. It was also known as the 'General Parkhemenko Guards Cavalry Division' after an honorific title the predecessor 14th Cavalry earned during the Civil War.<cr><cr>Pettibone, Charles D., The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II: volume V - Book B Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Trafford, 2009<cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 成立于1941年12月25日，由第14骑兵师改编而成，隶属于第三近卫骑兵军。该师参加了1942年的顿河攻势、1943年的斯摩棱斯克战役以及1944年的白俄罗斯进攻行动。在白俄罗斯进攻之后获得“格罗德诺”荣誉称号，并于1945年获得“利达”荣誉称号。此前的第14骑兵师曾在内战期间获得荣誉称号，因此该师也被称为“帕尔钦科夫将军近卫骑兵师”。<cr><cr>Pettibone, Charles D., The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II: volume V - Book B Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Trafford, 2009<cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 6th Guards Rifle Corps headquarters was formed on March 16, 1942, at Malaya Vishera on the basis for a continued advance in the Lyuban Offensive Operation. The corps initially included one infantry division and one airborne brigade, and the 42nd Guards Corps Artillery Regiment, which supported the corps for almost the entire war.<cr>The corps was part of the 'operational army' from March 28, 1942 - October 13, 1942, and November 5, 1942 - May 9, 1945.<cr>During the fighting with Volkhov Front, the corps did not see combat. In the summer, in anticipation of the .Sinyavino Offensive, a number of new roads were built and the Volkhov Front relocated slightly to the north. The Corps were put into action as part of the effort to relieve Leningrad on August 27, 1942. In the early days of the offensive, the corps successfully, broke through the first line of defense at the junction 227th and 223rd infantry divisions. On August 29th on the approaches to Sinyavino the 3rd Guards Rifle Division launched an attack on Work Settlement No. 5, 24th Guards Rifle Division began moving towards lake Sinyavinskaya, and the 19th Guards Rifle Division attacked Sinyavino. By September 27th, the corps had suffered heavy losses and unable to advance and parts of it were surrounded by a German counter-attack. In October 1942, the Corps headquarters was transferred to Reserve of the Supreme High Command (Stavka Reserve (RVGK)).<cr><cr>
translation: 第六近卫步兵军司令部于1942年3月16日在马利亚维谢拉成立，为继续推进柳班进攻行动做准备。该军最初包括一个步兵师和一个空降旅，并且有第42近卫军炮兵团为其提供支援，几乎贯穿整个战争时期。<cr>第六近卫步兵军于1942年3月28日至10月13日以及1942年11月5日至1945年5月9日期间属于“作战集团军”。<cr>在与沃尔霍夫方面军的战斗中，该军没有参战。夏季时，在准备辛亚维诺进攻前，修建了一些新道路，并且沃尔霍夫方面军向北稍作转移。1942年8月27日，该军作为解救列宁格勒行动的一部分被投入战场。<cr>在攻势初期，该军成功突破了第227步兵师和第223步兵师交界处的第一道防线。8月29日在接近辛亚维诺时，第三近卫步兵师对第五工作区发起攻击，第二十四近卫步兵师向辛亚维斯卡湖推进，而第十九近卫步兵师则进攻辛亚维诺。<cr>到9月27日，该军遭受了严重损失，并且无法继续前进。部分部队被德军反攻包围。10月1942年，第六近卫步兵军司令部转移到最高统帅部大本营预备队（RVGK）。

text: Initially commanding the 5th Mechanized Corps and the 5th Guards Tank Corps, the 6th Tank Army's first major operation was the suppression of the Korsun-Cherkassy Pocket in January-February 1944. It then fought in the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive during August 1944 before gaining a Guards title in September 1944. Under its new title, it was soon engaged in the Battle of Debrecen on the 2nd Ukrainian Front, before fighting against the Germans during Operation Spring Awakening in January 1945. Pushing west, the tank army moved south of Vienna, Austria and pivoted to the north in a wide encircling maneuver that cut Vienna off from the rest of the German Reich. At the end of the war, one of its subordinate formations, the 2nd Guards Mechanized Corps, ended operations in the area of Beneov, Czechoslovakia, on 9 May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 最初指挥第5机械化军和第5近卫坦克军，第6坦克集团军的第一个主要行动是镇压科苏尼-切尔卡瑟包围圈（1944年1月至2月）。随后在8月参加了雅西-奇西瑙攻势作战，并于同年9月获得近卫称号。在其新称号下，该部队很快参与了第2乌克兰方面军的德布勒森战役，之后又在“春季觉醒行动”中（1945年1月）与德国人交战。向西推进后，坦克集团军南下奥地利维也纳，并转向北侧进行大规模包围机动，切断了维也纳与德国本土之间的联系。战争结束时，其下属部队之一的第2近卫机械化军在捷克斯洛伐克贝诺夫地区结束了作战行动，时间为1945年5月9日。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text: The 6th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 6th Light Division. The Hungarian Government reluctantly agreed to support the Germans 1942 summer offensive Fall Blau and allocated the division as part of the Hungarian Second Army to the task. Each light division in the Second Army was reinforced with three battalions from sister divisions in Hungary but nonetheless each division was only slightly larger than half the size of its German counterparts. Second Army's role in the offensive was to guard the German northern flank on the Don River. During the Stalingrad Campaign the Second Army suffered over 60% casualties but was generally able to retreat in good order. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 6th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 6th Infantry Division.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第6匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖2个步兵团（每个团有3个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多兵力以参加东线作战，并且大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而其编制表基本没有变化。该旅更名为第6轻型师。匈牙利政府勉强同意支持德军在1942年夏季的攻势——蓝色行动，并将该师编入匈牙利第二集团军，参与进攻任务。第二集团军中的每个轻型师都从匈牙利国内的兄弟部队中得到3个营的增援，但即便如此，每个师仍然只有其德军同行的一半左右规模。第二集团军在攻势中的角色是保护德国北部战线，在顿河地区防御。在斯大林格勒战役期间，第二集团军遭受了超过60%的伤亡率，但仍能有组织地撤退。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas 和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利陆军》<cr>条目由 Chris Munson 提供% c<cr>

text: In June 1941 the 6th Infantry Division took part in the invasion of Russia as part of the 9th Army, Army Group Center. The division took part in heavy fighting on the drive to Moscow but managed to cross the Volga River at Kalinin, north of the Russian capital, in late November. It was in an exposed position when the Soviet winter offensive began, holding sixteen miles of frontage when the average division supposedly could hold only six miles successfully against a determined assault. The 6th nevertheless repulsed several Soviet attacks and gave ground only gradually, while both inflicting and sustaining heavy casualties.<cr>The 6th Infantry remained with Army Group Center for the next two and a half years. In 1942 it fought in the defensive battles of the Rzhev salient and in March of the following year took part in the 9th Army's brilliant retreat from the Rzhev bulge, a maneuver that freed a dozen divisions from a very exposed position. In July 1943, after a brief rest period at Smolensk, it saw action at Kursk and Orel and in the defensive battles on the middle Dniepr. It was smashed near Mogilev during the Soviet summer offensive of 1944, which also shattered Army Group Center. Most of the division was surrounded with the XXXV Corps and forced to surrender.<cr>Enough of the 6th escaped, however, for the High Command to recommission a skeleton division in the autumn of 1944. It was organized in Troop Maneuver Area (Truppenbungsplatz) Sennelager (near Paderborn) from Rhinelanders and Westphalians. The new division included 1,100 survivors of the old 6th Infantry Division (mostly returning wounded) plus the entire 552nd Grenadier Division, with which it was merged to form the 6th Volksgrenadier Division. It included the 18th, 37th and 58th Grenadier Regiments, the 6th Artillery Regiment, and the 6th Engineer Battalion. Its grenadier regiments, however, only had two understrength battalions each. Initially designated the 6th Grenadier Division on July 25, 1944, it became the 6th Volksgrenadier Division on October 9. Meanwhile, it added the 6th Fusilier Battalion, the 6th Flak (light anti-aircraft) Company, the 6th Tank Destroyer Battalion and the 1006th Assault Gun Battalion to its table of organization. The rebuilt 6thwhich was never more than a battle groupwas sent back to the Eastern Front and took part in the retreat through Poland. It fought at Warsaw and Radom and was in action on the Vistula in December 1944. In the last campaign the remnants of the 6th Volksgrenadier fought in Silesia and Bohemia, and was part of Field Marshal Ferdinand Schrner's army group, which was surrounded by the Russians at Deutsch-Brod, east of Prague, Czechoslovakia, in late April and May 1945. It surrendered to the Red Army on May 8, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 1941年6月，第6步兵师作为中央集团军群下的第9集团军的一部分参加了入侵苏联的行动。该师参与了向莫斯科推进时的激烈战斗，并于11月下旬在加里宁（位于俄罗斯首都以北）成功渡过了伏尔加河。<cr>然而，在苏联动员发起冬季攻势时，第6步兵师处于一个暴露的位置，当时它防守着长达16英里的战线，而据称一般师只能成功防御6英里长的战线。尽管遭受了重大伤亡，该师还是击退了几波苏联进攻，并逐渐撤退。<cr><cr>第6步兵师在接下来的两年半时间里一直隶属于中央集团军群。1942年，它参加了热季突出部的防御战斗；次年3月，它参与了第9集团军从热季突出部撤退的行动，这一机动使12个师脱离了一个非常暴露的位置。<cr><cr>1943年7月，在斯摩棱斯克短暂休整后，该师参加了库尔斯克和奥廖尔地区的战斗以及中段第聂伯河防御战。在1944年的苏联夏季攻势期间，它被击溃于莫吉廖夫附近，这次攻势也使中央集团军群遭到重创。<cr><cr>该师大部分部队与第35军一起被包围，并被迫投降。然而，第6步兵师在1944年秋季重组时，仍有足够的人员逃脱。该师在森内拉格（靠近帕德博恩）的部队训练区从莱茵兰人和威斯特伐利亚人中重新组建。新编的第6国民掷弹兵师包括大约1100名老第6步兵师幸存者（主要是伤愈归队人员），以及整个第552掷弹兵师，两者合并后形成了新的第6国民掷弹兵师。该师包括第18、37和58掷弹兵团，第6炮兵团，以及第6工兵营。不过，其每个掷弹兵团只有两个缺员的营。最初在1944年7月25日被指定为第6掷弹兵师，在10月9日改名为第6国民掷弹兵师。与此同时，该师增加了第6燧发枪手营、第6防空（轻型）连、第6坦克歼击营和第1006突击炮营到其编制中。重建后的第6师始终只是一个战斗群，并被派回东线参与波兰的撤退行动。它参加了华沙和拉多姆的战斗，在1944年12月还在维斯杜拉河一线作战。在最后一次战役中，第6国民掷弹兵师残部在西里西亚和波希米亚作战，并成为费迪南德·舍纳尔元帅指挥的集团军群的一部分，该集团军群于1945年4月底至5月初在捷克斯洛伐克布拉格以东的德意志-布罗德被苏联红军包围。它于1945年5月8日向红军投降。<cr>参考文献：<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷 二战中的第1至290步兵师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: The 6th Mechanised Corps was formed on 15 July 1940 at Bialystok in the Western Special Military District. It was attached to the 10th Army in the Bialystok area and was under the command of Major General M.G. Khatskilevich when Operation Barbarossa began in June 1941.<cr> The 6th Mechanized Corps was heavily involved in the first battles with Germans. The tank divisions of 6th Mechanized Corps were inferior against the advancing German units often without infantry support and were relentlessly pounded by the German aircraft of the Luftflotte 2. Without adequate ammunition and with many tanks in a state of disrepair and sent to several different locations without fuel reserves, they were quickly immobilized.<cr>The only battle that 6th Mechanized Corps saw was an attack of 24 June, when it lost 2% of tanks. The corps dissipated soon without any other combat, with negligible losses to aircraft, and with distance traveled that hardly necessitated any fuel tanking or repairs. The corps dispersed on 27 June near Krynki, with the personnel retreating east in small groups, and the equipment being abandoned or destroyed en masse.<cr>The idea of mechanized corps were revived in the spring of 1942. The second formation of 6th Mechanized Corps was assembled in November 1942. On the basis of Headquarters' 14th Tank Corps, the 6th Mechanized Corps was reformed on Nov. 26, 1942 at the station Kostereva in accordance with NKO directive number 11905907ss and GABTU number 1105723 dated November 26, 1942. Major General of Armored Forces Semyon Ilyich Bogdanov was appointed the commander of the 6th Mechanized Corps.<cr>On December 18, 1942, 6th Mechanized Corps was assigned to the 2nd Guards Army of the Southern Front, where it was involved in stopping the onset of Operation Winter Storm. The Manstein's attempted breakthrough to the Sixth Army stationed in Stalingrad. On January 8, 1943, the Corps - participating in the counterattack - captured the Zimovniki station (Rostov Oblast), a vital point of the Luftwaffe's munitions supply chain. For this reason the Corps was given the honorific Zimovnikovsky. Soon it was raised to the elite 'Guards' status; thus it became the 5th Zimovnikovsky Guards Mechanised Corps.<cr><cr>
translation: 第六机械化军于1940年7月15日在比亚韦斯托克的西部特别军事区成立。它隶属于比亚韦斯托克地区的第十集团军，并在巴巴罗萨行动开始时由少将M.G.哈茨基列维奇指挥。<cr> 第六机械化军在与德军的第一批战斗中发挥了重要作用。第六机械化军的坦克师在面对没有步兵支援的推进中的德国部队时处于劣势，经常遭到空战第二航空队的无情轰炸。由于弹药不足且许多坦克因维修不当而分散到不同地点并且缺乏燃料储备，它们很快就被迫停止行动。<cr> 第六机械化军仅参与了6月24日的一次攻击，并损失了2%的坦克。该军在没有其他战斗的情况下迅速解散，飞机造成的损失微乎其微，行进距离也不需要大量加油或维修。该军于6月27日在克林基附近解散，人员向东分散撤退，装备被遗弃或大规模销毁。<cr> 机械化军的概念在1942年春天重新兴起。第六机械化军的第二次组建是在1942年11月进行的。根据司令部第十四坦克军的编制，第六机械化军于1942年11月26日在科斯特列瓦车站重组，并遵循了NKO指令编号11905907ss和GABTU编号1105723（日期均为1942年11月26日）。装甲部队少将谢苗·伊里奇·波格达诺夫被任命为第六机械化军的指挥官。<cr>1942年12月18日，第6机械化军被分配到南方方面军的第2近卫集团军，在那里参与阻止“冬季风暴”行动的攻势。曼施坦因试图突破驻扎在斯大林格勒的第6集团军防线。1943年1月8日，该军——参加反攻——占领了罗斯托夫州的齐莫夫尼基车站（德国空军弹药补给链上的关键点）。为此，该军获得了“齐莫夫尼基”的荣誉称号；不久后被提升为精英近卫部队；因此成为第5齐莫夫尼基近卫机械化军。<cr><cr>

text: Sent to Russia in 1941, it broke through the Stalin Line and was involved on the drive to and early stages of the Siege of Leningrad. Transferred to Army Group Center, it suffered heavy losses in the Soviet winter offensive of 194142. Temperatures fell to minus 22 degrees Fahrenheit and all of the Czech tankswhich featured pneumatic clutches, brakes and steering columnsfailed. On December 10, 1941, the division lost its only remaining tank, which the men had dubbed 'Anthony the Last.' The 11th Panzer Regiment now reorganized as a battalion and fought as marching infantry. By the end of the year, the division had lost almost every one of its motorized vehicles and the soldiers referred to it as 'the 6th Panzer of Foot.' They had, however, incorporated more than 1,000 Russian panje wagons (two-wheeled peasant carts) into their ranks. By the end of January 1942, the division had fewer than 1,000 combat effectives left and only three operational guns. Its nevertheless played a prominent role in keeping the lifeline of the 9th Army in the Rzhev salient open.<cr><cr>In April 1942, after the spring thaw, the 6th Panzer Division was sent back to France to rest and refit. After Stalingrad was surrounded, the 6th Panzer was rushed back to the Soviet Union, where it tried to relieve the 6th Army, but was halted at Bolwassiljewka, thirty miles south of the city, in very heavy fighting. The division lost half of its tanks in the Stalingrad relief attempt. After the retreat from the Volga, the 6th Panzer Division fought in the retreat to the Don, in the Donetz, and in the Manstein offensive that led to the encirclement of Kharkov in March 1943. Later, it fought at Kursk , Belgorod, at Kharkov again, in the Dnieper battles, and in the northern Ukraine, where it was encircled, but broke out. By early 1944, the 6th Panzer Division had destroyed more than 1,500 Soviet tanks. Withdrawn from the line to refit, the 6th was hastily sent to the central sector of the Eastern Front shortly after the Russians surrounded the bulk of the 4th and 9th armies. It helped stabilize the German front in the east before being sent to Hungary, where it fought in the battles around Budapest and knocked out its 2,400th Soviet tank. It fought in the Battle of Vienna and ended the war on the southern sector of the Eastern Front.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 1941年被派往俄罗斯，突破了斯大林防线，并参与了向列宁格勒围城战的推进。后调至中央集团军群，在苏联1941-42年的冬季攻势中遭受重大损失。气温降至零下22华氏度，所有配备气动离合器、刹车和转向柱的捷克坦克均失效。1941年12月10日，该师失去了最后一辆坦克，士兵们将其称为“安东尼最后”。第11装甲团重组为营，并作为行军步兵作战。到年底时，该师几乎损失了所有机动车辆，士兵们称其为“步行的第6装甲师”。不过，他们已将超过1000辆俄罗斯平板车（两轮农用马车）纳入编制。到1942年1月底，该师只剩下不到1000名战斗人员和3门可操作火炮。然而，它在保持第9集团军在热季突出部的生命线畅通方面发挥了重要作用。<cr><cr>1942年4月，春融之后，第6装甲师返回法国休整和整补。在斯大林格勒被包围后，第6装甲师又被紧急调回苏联境内，试图解救被困的第6集团军，但最终在距离城市南面30英里的博尔瓦西柳耶卡（Bolwassiljewka）遭到重创而被迫停止进攻。该师在斯大林格勒救援行动中损失了半数坦克。从伏尔加河撤退后，第6装甲师参加了向顿河的撤退、顿涅茨战役以及曼斯坦因攻势，后者导致哈尔科夫被包围（1943年3月）。之后，该师又参与了库尔斯克、别洛戈罗德和哈尔科夫的战斗，在第聂伯河战役中作战，并在乌克兰北部地区作战。在那里它曾一度陷入包围圈但成功突围。到1944年初，第6装甲师已经摧毁超过1500辆苏联坦克。该师被撤出前线进行整补后，又被紧急调往东线中央战区，以帮助稳定德国的防线，之后又前往匈牙利作战，在布达佩斯周边战斗中击毁了它的第2400辆苏军坦克。它参加了维也纳战役，并在东线南部战区结束了战争。<cr> 德国战斗序列 第三卷 - 二战中的装甲师、装甲掷弹兵师和武装党卫军师，塞缪尔·W·米查姆少校<cr>

text: Part of the 6th Army in the Kiev Military District at the outbreak of the war, it consisted of the 97th, 159th and 41st Rifle Divisions. It was stationed on the border in the Lvov oblast. It launched several counterattacks against German forces in the first week of the war and was destroyed in early July. The corps was reformed in 1942 and was redesignated 19th Guards Rifle Corps in April 1943. It was reformed again in May 1943 as part of the 59th Army and in January 1944 consisted of the 65th, 239th and 310th Rifle Divisions. It fought in the Vyborg-Ptrozavodsk Offensive that brought the war with Finland to an end. It was then transferred to Germany and fought in the final campaigns there, ending the war in the Czech Republic. <cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 作为基辅军区第6集团军的一部分，在战争爆发时，该部队由第97步兵师、第159步兵师和第41步兵师组成。它驻扎在利沃夫州的边境地区。在战争的第一周内，它对德军发动了几次反击，并于7月初被消灭。该军在1942年重组，并于1943年4月改称为第19近卫步兵军，在1943年5月作为第59集团军的一部分再次重组，到1944年1月由第65步兵师、第239步兵师和第310步兵师组成。它参加了结束与芬兰战争的维堡-彼得罗扎沃茨克进攻战役。随后被转移到德国，并在那里的最后几场战役中作战，最终在捷克斯洛伐克结束战争。<cr>贡献者：斯图尔特·金

text: The 6th Rifle Division was formed in May 1918 as the Gatchina Division however by the end of 1918 was renamed the 6th Rifle Division. In 1939 the division became a training unit and split into separate cadres. The division was activated later the same year and took part in the Soviet invasion of Poland. It consisted of the 84th, 125th and 333rd Rifle Regiments, 131st Artillery Regiment, 204th Howitzer Regiment and various support troops.<cr>At the start of Operation Barbarossa the division was deployed with the Western Special Military District in the Brest-Litovsk Fortress. The division experienced heavy casualties the first day of the German invasion and its elements either dispersed or destroyed. The division fought in many defensive battles after the German invasion and by October 1941 was part of the 13th Army in the Bryansk Front. In June 1942 during the German summer offensive Fall Blau the division was assigned to defend the approaches to Voronezh. Subsequently the division participated in the liberation of the Ukraine, Romania, Hungary and Czechoslovakia. In August 1945 the division participated in the Soviet invasion of Manchuria.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第6步兵师成立于1918年5月，最初名为加特奇纳师。然而到1918年底，该师被更名为第6步兵师。1939年，该师成为训练单位，并分裂为不同的骨干部队。同年晚些时候，该师重新激活并参加了苏联入侵波兰的行动。它由第84、第125和第333步兵团、第131炮兵团、第204加农炮团以及各种支援部队组成。<cr>在巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师部署于西方特别军区的别列兹诺耶-利托夫斯克要塞。德国入侵的第一天，该师遭受了重大伤亡，其部分兵力或溃散或被消灭。德国入侵后，该师参加了许多防御战役，并在1941年10月成为布良斯克方面军第13集团军的一部分。<cr>1942年6月，在德军夏季攻势“蓝色行动”期间，该师被分配保卫沃罗涅日的外围地区。随后，该师参与了乌克兰、罗马尼亚、匈牙利和捷克斯洛伐克的解放行动。1945年8月，该师参加了苏联入侵满洲的行动。<cr>Chris Munson 提供

text: The 6th Romanian Cavalry Brigade was attached to the German XXX Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. In March of 1942 it was reorganized as the 6th Romanian Cavalry Division. The division participated in many battles in the Kuban and in the Caucasus. By the end of 1943 it was on the defensive in the Crimea where it remained until forced to evacuate by sea from Sevastopol in April of 1944. The division was disbanded in November of 1944.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第6罗马尼亚骑兵旅在巴巴罗萨行动开始时隶属于德国第30军。1942年3月，该部队重组为第6罗马尼亚骑兵师。该师参与了库班和高加索地区的多次战役。到1943年底，它已在克里米亚转入防御态势，并一直驻守至1944年4月被迫从塞瓦斯托波尔撤退为止。该师于1944年11月被解散。<cr><cr><cr>第6罗马尼亚骑兵旅<cr>@PH1@<cr>@PH2@<cr>@PH3@<cr>@PH4@<cr>条目由克里斯·芒森提供

text: The 5th Romanian Infantry Division was attached to the German XI Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. It subsequently participated in the 73 day Siege of Odessa. The division was one of six Romanian infantry divisions encircled during the Battle of Stalingrad that became known as the General Lascar Group. On the 22nd of November 1942, refusing calls to surrender, out of food and down to 40 rounds per gun, the Group transmitted its last message and was destroyed. The division was reestablished by merging its remanants with the 1st Romanian Security Division and spent 1943 in anti-partisan duties in the Transnistria region near Moldavia. It participated in the defense of Romania in 1944 and was absorbed into the Romanian 9th Infantry Division in November of 1944.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第5罗马尼亚步兵师在巴巴罗萨行动开始时隶属于德国第11军。该师随后参加了敖德萨73天的围城战。在斯大林格勒战役中，该师是被包围的六个罗马尼亚步兵师之一，并被称为拉斯卡尔集团。1942年11月22日，在拒绝投降要求、弹尽粮绝的情况下，该集团发送了最后一封电报后被消灭。该师于1943年在摩尔达维亚附近的特拉普尼斯特里亚地区与第1罗马尼亚治安师合并重组，并参与反游击队行动。它参加了1944年的罗马尼亚防御战，并于同年11月被并入罗马尼亚第9步兵师。<cr>词条由Chris Munson提供

text: The 6th Romanian Infantry Division was attached to the German XI Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. As with most Romanian infantry divisions it was withdrawn to Romania after the Siege of Odessa. The division was one of six Romanian infantry divisions encircled during the Battle of Stalingrad that became known as the General Lascar Group. On the 22nd of November 1942, refusing calls to surrender, out of food and down to 40 rounds per gun, the Group transmitted its last message and was destroyed. The 1st Battalion of the divisions 15th Infantry Regiment was the only unit in the Group to escape the encirclement intact.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第6罗马尼亚步兵师在巴巴罗萨行动开始时隶属于德国第11军。与其他大多数罗马尼亚步兵师一样，该师在敖德萨围城战后被撤回罗马尼亚境内。该师是六个在斯大林格勒战役中被包围的罗马尼亚步兵师之一，这些部队被称为拉斯卡尔将军集团。1942年11月22日，在拒绝投降要求、弹尽粮绝的情况下，该集团发送了最后一条信息后被消灭。第1营（隶属于该师第15步兵团）是唯一一个完整逃离包围圈的单位。<cr>资料来源：克里斯·芒森

text:
The 6th Tank Corps was formed in April 1942 at Moscow.<cr>Basically, the Corps HQ acted as a Training Command for tank units for about a month, and then in May 1942 formed up as a regular Tank Corps in Western Front reserves.<cr>The 6th Tank Corps remained in Western Front for the rest of 1942, sporadically taking part in Western Front's attempts to break the German 9th Army's hold on Rzhev. The first time 6th tank Corps was committed to one of these armored breaking and entering attempts in August 1942, it had 24 KVs, 46 T-34s, 30 T-70s, and 69 T-60s, for a total of 169 tanks. It lost most of them in just three days, in which the entire Soviet force involved (2 tank corps and a cavalry corps) lost 236 tanks to no effect on the German defense.<cr>By December 1942 6th Tank Corps had only one tank brigade left with KV tanks (7 in the Corps) , and had 64 T-34s, but only 29 T-70s and T-60s left - the light tanks were death traps against an intact defense.<cr>In February 1943, still in Western Front, 6th Tank Corps began reorganizand
building up to the 1943 corps standard. When 1st Tank Army was formed in March 1943, 6th Tank Corps was assigned to it.<cr>In March 1943, 100th Tank Brigade left the corps to help form 31st Tank Corps.<cr>When 1st Tank Army went into action against 4th Panzer Army in the southern portion of the Kursk battle in July, 6th Tank Corps also controlled the 1461st SU Regiment (17 SU-76, 8 SU-122).<cr>This time, the corps was completely equipped with medium tanks but 200th, and possibly 22nd Tank Brigade, included Lend Lease M3 Grant medium tanks along with T-34/76 s. The corps suffered terrible losses at Kursk: because of its gasoline engine, high profile and riveted construction the
Grant had been nicknamed 'a coffin for seven brothers' by its Russian crews.<cr>After a quick rehabilitation and repair in late July, 6th Tank Corps took part in the Soviet August offensive that liberated Belgorod and Kharkov, and started the German Army on the road back to the Dnepr. In recognition of the corps' efforts in these attacks, and in stopping 48th Panzer Corps on the road to Kursk, 6th Tank Corps became llth Guards Tank Corps on 23 October 1943.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp
translation: 第6坦克军于1942年4月在莫斯科成立。司令部基本上充当了大约一个月的训练指挥部，然后在1942年5月作为常规坦克军加入西方方面军预备队。<cr>第6坦克军在1942年的剩余时间里一直留在西方方面军，偶尔参与西方方面军试图打破德国第9集团军对日兹赫姆控制的尝试。第一次投入此类装甲突破行动是在1942年8月，当时拥有24辆KV坦克、46辆T-34坦克、30辆T-70坦克和69辆T-60坦克，总计169辆坦克。它们在短短三天内损失殆尽，在此期间整个苏联部队（包括两个坦克军和一个骑兵军）共损失了236辆坦克，但对德国防御毫无影响。<cr>到1942年12月，第6坦克军只剩下一支装备KV坦克的坦克旅（7辆），拥有64辆T-34坦克，但仅剩下29辆T-70和T-60轻型坦克——这些轻型坦克在面对完整防御时几乎成了死亡陷阱。<cr>1943年2月，仍在西方方面军内，第6坦克军开始重组并重建至1943年的标准编制。当第1坦克集团军于1943年3月成立时，第6坦克军被分配给它。<cr>第6坦克军在1943年3月将第100坦克旅调出以帮助组建第31坦克军。<cr>当第1坦克集团军于7月在库尔斯克战役南部地区对德国第4装甲集团军发起进攻时，第6坦克军还控制了第1461自行火炮团（包括17辆SU-76和8辆SU-122）。这次，该军完全装备了中型坦克，但第200和可能还有第22坦克旅包括租借的M3“格兰特”中型坦克以及T-34/76坦克。该军在库尔斯克遭受了惨重损失：“格兰特”由于其汽油发动机、高轮廓和铆接结构，被苏联车组人员戏称为“七兄弟的棺材”。<cr>经过7月底迅速休整和维修后，第6坦克军参加了1943年8月的苏军进攻行动，解放了别尔哥罗德和哈尔科夫，并开始将德军驱逐回第聂伯河。鉴于该军在这次攻势中的努力以及阻止第48装甲军前往库尔斯克的努力，第6坦克军于1943年10月23日改编为第11近卫坦克军。<cr>Charles C. Sharp的《二战苏联战斗序列 第二卷》

text: The 707th Infantry Division was sent to the Eastern Front and was performing line-of-communications duties for Army Group Center in August. In the winter of 1942-43 and summer of 1943, it was fighting on the front line near Bryansk and Orel. In June 1944, it was one of only two divisions in 9th Army's reserve when the massive Soviet summer offensive hit Army Group Center. Quickly committed, the 707th was soon smashed. Major General Gihr, the divisional commander, was taken prisoner near Bobruisk, along with most of his men. The remnants of the little division were officially disbanded soon after.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第707步兵师被派往东线，在1942年8月为中央集团军群执行后勤任务。在1942-1943年的冬季和1943年的夏季，该师在布良斯克和奥廖尔附近的一线作战。1944年6月，当苏联发动大规模夏季攻势时，第707步兵师是中央集团军群中仅有的两个驻扎在第9集团军预备队中的师之一。<cr>德国战斗序列 第二卷 291至999步兵师、命名步兵师和特殊师（Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.）

text: The 70th Army began forming in October 1942 near Sverdlovsk in Siberia as a separate NKVD Army of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command (Stavka Reserve). It was recruited primarily from NKVD border guards, with other redundant manpower from lines of communications troops and GULAG personnel.<cr>70th Army was assigned to the re-deploying Don Front (soon re-designated Central Front) under command of Gen. K.K. Rokossovsky. It was some time before Rokossovsky could knock it into shape as a front-line formation, forcing him to remove many senior, ex-NKVD officers. From 28 February the 70th Army took part in both offensive and defensive operations to the northwest of Kursk. Central Front exploited a gap between the weak Second German Army and the Second Panzer Army, but was brought to a halt by the spring rasputitsa, German reserves released by their evacuation of the Rzhev Salient, and the German counter-offensive to the south. The Front's armies created defenses in depth during the lull in operations during the spring.<cr>During the Battle of Kursk the 70th Army fought on the left flank of the 2nd Tank Army and played a role in stopping the German 9th Army that was trying to break through to Kursk from the north. During the subsequent Red Army counterattack, the 70th Army took part in Operation Kutuzov and attacked Trosna to the south of the town of Kromy. On 5 Aug., its units reached the region southwest of Kromy, and on 17 Aug., they reached the German 'Hagen' defense line near Domakha.<cr>After the end of this operation, the field headquarters of the 70th Army was transferred to the Reserve of the Central Front and on 1 Feb. to STAVKA Reserve, where it received new units.<cr>During the second half of February 1944, the 70th Army was transferred to the front at the Turya River north of Kovel. On 25 Feb., it was subordinated to the Belorussian Front and on 16 Apr. it joined that formation, which had been re-designated 1st Belorussian Front. In June, prior to the outbreak of the Soviet summer offensive, the Army was still in the vicinity of Kovel.<cr>During the Lublin-Brest Offensive (18 July - 2 August), its units, along with units of the 61st Army and the 26th Army, surrounded Brest from the south-east and destroyed up to four German divisions to the west of Brest.<cr>After a short period assigned to the front reserves, on 10 Aug. the 70th Army attacked a region to the north of Warsaw. By the end of August, it reached the Narew River near the town of Serock. As of 26 Aug. was reduced to just the 72nd Rifle Corps. On 29 Oct., the 70th Army was back again as reserves of the 1st Belorussian Front and on 19 Nov. as reserves of the 2nd Belorussian Front.<cr>During the East Prussian Offensive (13 January to 25 April), 70th Army attacked from the Serock bridgehead towards Modlin, P?ock, and Toru? (Thorn).<cr>70th Army, together with other armies of the front and forces of Baltic Fleet, took part in the East Pomeranian Offensive (10 February - 4 April 1945).<cr>During the Battle of Berlin (16 April - 8 May), 70th Army was attached to the spearheads of 2nd Belorussian Front, attacking on the Neubrandenburg - Wismar axis. (Szczecin).<cr><cr>
translation: 第70集团军于1942年10月在西伯利亚的斯维尔德洛夫斯克附近开始组建，作为最高统帅部预备队（大本营预备队）的一个独立内务人民委员部陆军。该部队主要由内务人民委员部边防警卫人员组成，并辅以通信兵和古拉格劳改犯中的多余人员。<cr>第70集团军被分配给重新部署的顿河方面军（很快更名为中央方面军），受命于科·康斯坦丁诺维奇·罗科索夫斯基将军。罗科索夫斯基花了很长时间才将它打造成一线部队，迫使他撤换了许多高级内务人民委员部军官。<cr>2月28日之后，第70集团军参与了库尔斯克西北方向的进攻和防御行动。中央方面军利用了第二德国集团军与第二装甲集团军之间的缺口，但因春季泥泞期的到来、德军从热季夫突出部撤出释放的预备队以及南部德军反攻而被迫停止。<cr>在作战间歇期间，该方面的部队创建了纵深防御体系。<cr>库尔斯克战役中，第70集团军与第二坦克集团军左翼并肩战斗，并参与阻止了试图从北部突破至库尔斯克的德军第9集团军。在随后红军反攻中，第70集团军参加了“库图佐夫”行动，并向克罗姆镇南部的特罗斯纳发动进攻。<cr>8月5日，其部队到达了克罗姆西南地区，8月17日，他们抵达了德国‘哈根’防御线附近多马卡。<cr>此行动结束后，第70集团军的野战司令部被转移到中央方面军预备队，并于2月1日转至最高统帅部大本营预备队，在那里接收了新部队。1944年2月下旬，第70集团军被调往科韦利以北图尔亚河的方面军。2月25日，该集团军隶属于白俄罗斯方面军；4月16日，它加入改称第一白俄罗斯方面军的部队。在苏联夏季攻势爆发前的六月里，第70集团军仍驻扎在科韦利附近。<cr>在卢布林-别列斯进攻战役（7月18日至8月2日）中，该集团军与第61集团军和第26集团军的部分部队一起从东南方向包围了别列斯，并消灭了位于别列斯以西的多达4个德国师。<cr>短暂被划归方面军预备队后，8月10日，第70集团军向华沙北部地区发起进攻。到八月底，它已推进至塞罗茨克附近的纳雷夫河。截至8月26日，该集团军仅剩第72步兵军。<cr>10月29日，第70集团军再次成为第一白俄罗斯方面军的预备队；11月19日则成为第二白俄罗斯方面军的预备队。<cr>在东普鲁士进攻战役（1月13日至4月25日）中，第70集团军从塞罗茨克桥头堡向莫德林、波兹南和托伦方向发起攻击。<cr>在波美拉尼亚进攻战役（2月10日至4月4日）中，第70集团军与白俄罗斯方面军的其他部队以及波罗的海舰队的兵力共同参与了作战行动。<cr>在柏林战役（4月16日至5月8日）中，第70集团军隶属于第二白俄罗斯方面军的突击集群，在纽布兰登堡-维斯马轴线方向发起进攻。

text: The 70th Guards was one of several Guards rifle divisions created in the aftermath of the fighting for Stalingrad, on Feb. 6, 1943. It was formed from the remnants of the 138th Rifle Division, in recognition of that division's stalwart defense against the German Sixth Army in the Battle of Stalingrad, in particular the Barrikady Ordnance Factory.<cr> The division spent February and March rebuilding, before being sent north in April to 17th Guards Rifle Corps in Central Front reserves north of Kursk.<cr>The 70th Guards was soon moved into 13th Army which held most of the north shoulder of the Kursk salient. The division defended part of the Olkhovatka sector. When the Germans launched Operation Citadel on July 5, the division faced elements of two panzer corps of German Ninth Army. Reinforced with over 50 tanks and self-propelled guns (SU-122s of the 1441st SU Regiment), 72 antitank guns, and 80 heavy guns, mortars and rocket launchers, the division stopped the German attacks literally in their tracks, with German losses of up to 50 tanks a day. On 6 July the division stopped the advance of the XXXXVII Panzer Corps. On 8 July the 4th Panzer Division broke through at the junction of the 70th Guards with the 75th Guards Rifle Division, but was repulsed after heavy fighting. On July 21 the division was awarded the Order of Lenin. Five gunners or battery commanders of the 137th Guards Artillery Regiment, who fought off German tanks over open sights at point-blank range, became Heroes of the Soviet Union, and the regiment as a whole was awarded the Order of the Red Banner.<cr>Following the German defeat, the 70th Guards joined in the advance out of the Kursk salient. On August 30 the division, backed by the 23rd and 95th Tank Brigades and the 1454th Self-propelled Artillery Regiment, was credited with the liberation of the Ukrainian town of Glukhov (Hlukhiv, in Ukrainian) and got the town's name as an honorific. On September 9 the division was awarded its first Order of the Red Banner. In October the division was reassigned to the 38th Army for the rest of the war, first in the 1st Ukrainian and later the 4th Ukrainian Front.<cr>During the Lvov-Sandomierz operation in July, 1944, the 70th Guards was temporarily motorized with the 26th Truck Brigade to exploit the breakthrough of the German lines. It was one of the first rifle divisions to have its towed antitank battalion replaced with a battalion of 12 SU-76 assault guns, becoming the 74th Guards SU Battalion, in late 1944. 38th Army was moved to 4th Ukrainian Front, and in 101st Rifle Corps the 70th Guards fought through the Carpathian Mountains into Czechoslovakia in early 1945. The division ended the war near Prague. Its full title at this time was 70th Guards Rifle Glukhov, Order of Lenin, twice Order of the Red Banner, Order of Suvorov, Order of Kutuzov, Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky Division.<cr><cr>
translation:
第70近卫步兵师是在1943年2月6日斯大林格勒保卫战之后成立的数个近卫步兵师之一。该师由第138步兵师残部组建，以表彰其在斯大林格勒战役中对德国第六集团军的顽强防御，特别是巴里卡达兵工厂的战斗。<cr><cr>该师于2月和3月重建后，在4月份被派往中央方面军预备队中的第17近卫步兵军，位于库尔斯克以北。<cr><cr>不久之后，第70近卫步兵师被调至第13集团军，后者负责库尔斯克突出部的大部分北部肩头。该师防守奥尔霍瓦茨卡地区的部分区域。<cr><cr>当德国人于7月5日发动堡垒行动时，该师面对的是德第九集团军中的两个装甲军的部分部队。得到超过50辆坦克和自行火炮（第1441自行火炮团的SU-122）、72门反坦克炮、80门重炮、迫击炮和火箭发射器增援后，该师在战场上直接阻止了德军攻势，导致德国人每天损失多达50辆坦克。<cr><cr>7月6日，该师阻止了第XXXXVII装甲军的推进。7月8日，第4装甲师突破了第70近卫步兵师与第75近卫步兵师之间的结合部，但在激烈战斗后被击退。7月21日，该师获得列宁勋章。<cr><cr>第137近卫炮兵团的五名炮手或连长，在开阔地带近距离对抗德军坦克时表现出色，成为苏联英雄；整个团获得了红旗勋章。在德国战败之后，第70近卫师参加了从库尔斯克突出部的进攻。8月30日，该师得到了第23和第95坦克旅以及第1454自行火炮团的支持，解放了乌克兰城镇格卢霍夫（Hlukhiv，在乌克兰语中），并以该镇的名字作为荣誉称谓。9月9日，该师获得了第一个红旗勋章。10月，该师被重新分配到第38集团军，并在余下的战争期间隶属于第一和第四乌克兰方面军。

1944年7月的利沃夫-桑多梅日行动中，第70近卫师暂时得到了第26卡车旅的支持，以利用突破德国防线的机会。该师是最早将拖曳反坦克营替换为装备有12门SU-76突击炮的新营之一，并成为第74近卫自行火炮营。38集团军被调至第四乌克兰方面军，在第101步兵军中，第70近卫师在1945年初穿越喀尔巴阡山脉进入捷克斯洛伐克。该师最终停战时位于布拉格附近。

其当时的全称是第70近卫红旗格卢霍夫、列宁勋章、两次获得红旗勋章、苏沃罗夫勋章、库图佐夫勋章和博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基勋章步兵师。

text: The 71st Infantry Division was sent to Russia in June 1941, the division fought in the drive on Kiev and suffered heavy losses. Rotated back to Belgium and France to rest and refit in November 1941, it returned to Stalino in southern Russia in the spring of 1942. Assigned to the 6th Army, the 71st Infantry Division fought at Kharkov and in the Battle of the Izyum Pocket in May, in the Battle of Voronezh in June and July, and in the Battle of the Kalach Pocket in August. It was trapped in the Stalingrad Pocket in November and was largely destroyed in the subsequent street fighting. The division commander, General Alexander von Hartmann was among those killed; in the last week of the battle he reportedly deliberately exposed himself to enemy fire, preferring death to a Siberian prison camp. Very few of his men survived Soviet captivity.<cr><cr>A second 71st Infantry Division was formed in Denmark on February 17, 1943. The division fought in Italy, until it was transferred to the southern sector of the Eastern Front in late 1944 and fought in the Hungarian and Austrian campaigns. It was still in the East when the war ended but managed to disengage and escape to the west. It surrendered to the British at St. Veith in May 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation:
第71步兵师于1941年6月被派往俄罗斯，该师参加了进攻基辅的战斗，并遭受了重大损失。在1941年11月返回比利时和法国休整后，它于1942年春天重返南部俄罗斯的斯塔里诺。第71步兵师被分配给第六集团军，在5月份参与了哈尔科夫战役以及伊久姆包围圈之战，在6月至7月期间参加了沃罗涅日战役，并在8月份参加了卡拉萨包围圈之战。该师于11月被困在斯大林格勒包围圈中，随后的巷战使其大部分被消灭。师长亚历山大·冯·哈特曼将军是阵亡者之一；据说他在战斗的最后一周故意暴露自己以吸引敌方火力，宁愿选择死亡也不愿被送往西伯利亚监狱。他的部下很少有人幸存下来并逃脱了苏联的俘虏。

第二支第71步兵师于1943年2月17日在丹麦组建。该师参加了意大利战役，并在1944年末转移到东线南部战区，参与了匈牙利和奥地利战役。战争结束时它仍在东部作战，但成功脱离战场并向西逃去，在1945年5月向英国人投降于圣维特。

<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷：二战中的第1至290步兵师，山姆·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text:
The 29th Rifle Division (2nd formation) was redesignated the 72nd Guards Rifle Division by Directorate of the General Staff order No.104 on 1 March 1943.<cr><cr>On March 3, 1943, 72nd Guards Rifle Division was involved in battles for liberation of Belgorod. Soon they were near Kharkiv and Krasnohrad. On 19 September, the division was awarded the title Krasnohrad. On 8 January 1944, the division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner.

The division fought in the Budapest Offensive from late October 1944. On 15 December, units of the division reinforced Cavalry Mechanized Group Pliev during the attack on Szecseny. On 9 January, the division was attached to the 24th Guards Rifle Corps. The division captured the area around Bart. The division's attack was stopped by the 1st Battalion of 317th Grenadier Regiment a kilometer north of the village.<cr><cr>

text: The 72nd Infantry Division crossed into Russia as a part of Army Group South. It fought in the Crimea and in the subsequent siege of Sevastopol before being transferred to Army Group Center in September 1942. On the central sector it took part in the winter fighting of 194243, in the Rzhev withdrawal, and in the Battle of Kursk .<cr>Transferred back to the southern sector, it fought at Orel and Bryansk, in the Dnieper bend battles, at Kiev, and in the southern Ukraine. It was finally encircled at Cherkassy with the IX Infantry Corps. During the battle and eventual break-out attempt, General Wilhelm Stemmermann, the corps commander, personally assumed command of the division. When he was killed by an anti-tank shell, all order disappeared in the 72nd. Perhaps half of the division escaped. Reformed in the spring of 1944, its grenadier regiments were each reduced from three to two battalions each. The 72nd was in Poland in the summer and was officially cited for its performance in the Vistula defensive battles in August. It suffered very heavy casualties in southern Poland and was smashed in the Battle of the Baranov Bridgehead on January 12, 1945, as the Russians drove on Breslau and Silesia. It rallied quickly and was soon back in combat on the Oder, although it was now a Kampfgruppe. Most of the division finally surrendered to the Russians in Czechoslovakia on May 8, 1945, although small elements did escape through the mountains to the west.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第72步兵师作为南方集团军群的一部分进入俄罗斯。它在克里米亚作战，并参加了随后对塞瓦斯托波尔的围攻，之后于1942年9月被转移到中央集团军群。<cr>在中部战区，该师参与了1942-43年的冬季战斗、热季河后撤以及库尔斯克战役。<cr>转回南部战区后，它参加了奥廖尔和布良斯克的战斗，在第聂伯河弯道战役中作战，并且在基辅和乌克兰南部进行了战斗。<cr>最终该师被包围在切尔卡瑟，与第九步兵军一起被困。<cr>在这场战斗及其突围尝试期间，军长威廉·施特默曼将军亲自接管了该师的指挥。当他被一枚反坦克炮弹击中身亡后，第72师的所有秩序都消失了。或许有一半的人成功逃脱。<cr>该师在1944年春天重组时，每个掷弹兵团从三个营减少到两个营。<cr>该师于夏季进入波兰，并因在8月的维斯瓦河防御战中的表现而受到官方表彰。<cr>它在南波兰遭受了非常严重的伤亡，在1945年1月12日的巴兰诺夫桥头堡战役中被彻底击溃，当时苏联军队正向布雷斯劳和西里西亚推进。<cr>该师迅速重整旗鼓，并很快重新投入奥得河战区的战斗，尽管此时它已变成一个战斗群。<cr>该师大部分人员最终于1945年5月8日在捷克斯洛伐克向苏联军队投降，尽管有小部分人通过山脉逃到了西方。

text: The 73rd Infantry Division invaded Russia in July 1941. It fought in the Crimea, the subsequent Siege of Sevastopol, on the Mius River, in the advance across the Don, and in the Caucasus campaign. The division retreated into the Kuban bridgehead after the tide of the war in Russia turned against Germany and in January 1943 was heavily engaged against the Soviet amphibious landings at Novorossiysk (Novorossisk), in which it was primarily responsible for checking the surprise Russian attack.<cr>Shortly afterward the 73rd Infantry-now at battle group strength-was pulled out of the bridgehead and sent north, where it fought at Melitopol and on the lower Battle of Kursk . Returned to the Crimea in early 1944, it was smashed in April and May during the retreat to Sevastopol. Part of the division escaped by sea when the fortress fell, but much of it was trapped in the city; General Boehme, the division commander, was captured when his tactical headquarters was overrun by the Russians. The 73rd was reformed in eastern Hungary the summer of 1944 and was reduced to six understrength grenadier battalions.<cr>It reappeared in combat in September, when it helped crush the Polish Home Army in the Warsaw uprising. Later the division was sent toArmy Group Center , where it held a bridgehead on the eastern bank of the Vistula until it was struck by the entire Soviet 47th Army. Under this massive attack the veteran division finally collapsed and was largely destroyed at Thorn on January 30, 1945; nevertheless, the remnants of the 73rd Infantry were still in action in February 1945, opposing the Russian winter offensive in eastern Germany. It fought in West Prussia and was finally effectively destroyed in the Battle of Danzig in early April 1945. The division commander was transferred elsewhere, the few surviving combat units were absorbed by other units, and the staff was withdrawn into OKH reserve. It boarded the Goya for the trip back to the Reich and most of it went down with the ship when it was sunk by the Soviets on April 17.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第73步兵师于1941年7月入侵苏联。该师在克里米亚作战，随后参加了塞瓦斯托波尔的围城战，在缪斯河畔、顿河战役中以及高加索战役中均有参战。随着战争形势逆转，德国军队从库班桥头堡撤退，第73步兵师于1943年1月在诺沃罗西斯克（新罗西斯克）的苏联两栖登陆作战中遭受重创，并主要负责遏制突然发起攻击的苏军。不久之后，第73步兵师被从桥头堡撤出并北上，在梅利托波尔和库尔斯克南部战场作战。1944年初返回克里米亚后，该师在撤退至塞瓦斯托波尔的过程中于四五月间遭到重创。<cr>部分部队通过海路逃脱，但大部分部队被困在城市中；师长博赫梅将军在其战术司令部被苏联军队攻占时被俘。1944年夏季，第73步兵师在东部匈牙利重组，并缩减为六个战斗力不足的掷弹兵营。该师于9月再次参战，帮助镇压了华沙起义中的波兰民族军。之后该师被派往中央集团军群，在维斯瓦河东岸的桥头堡坚守至苏联第47集团军发动全面进攻为止。在此次大规模攻势下，这支部队老练的师终于崩溃，并于1945年1月30日在托伦几乎全军覆没；然而，该师残部仍在2月份参与了对抗苏军冬季攻势的战斗，在东德地区作战直至1945年4月初格但斯克战役中被彻底消灭。师长调往他处，少数幸存的战斗单位并入其他部队，指挥部则撤至陆军总司令部预备队。该师登上戈亚号返回帝国，大部分人员在苏联击沉该船时丧生。<cr><cr>德国二战步兵师作战序列 第一卷 1-290师，萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.
