text:
The 74th Guards Rifle Divison was formed from the 45th Rifle Division on 1 March 1943. The division's entire World War II service was with the 62nd Army.<cr><cr>In July 1943, participated in the battles on the outskirts of Izium, Izyum-Barvenkovo Offensive, in August 1943 in the Barvenkovo-Pavlograd Offensive, as part of the Donbass Strategic Offensive Operation . In the Lower Dniper Offensive Operation crossed the Dnieper south of Dnipropetrovsk. During Nizhnedneprovskiy offensive forced the Dnieper to the south of Dnipropetrovsk. Then took part in the Nikopol-Krivoi Rog Offensive.

During the Winter Spring campaign of 1944 the division participated in the Bereznegovatoye-Snigirevka Offensive and the follow on Odessa Offensive. In July 1944 the division participated in the Lublin-Brest Offensive as part of the Operation Bagration and the beginning of the liberation of Poland.

In January 1945 the division was part of the Vistula-Oder Offensive and the liberation of Poland. In April 1945 it broke through enemy defenses at the Battle of the Battle of Seelow Heights, taking part in the Berlin Strategic Offensive..<cr><cr>
translation: 第74近卫步兵师于1943年3月1日由第45步兵师改编而成。该师在整个第二次世界大战期间都隶属于第62集团军。<cr>指挥官报告：1943年7月，参加了伊久姆外围战斗和伊久姆-巴文科沃进攻战役；同年8月，在顿巴斯战略进攻作战中参与了巴文科沃-帕夫洛格勒进攻战役。在第聂伯河下游攻势中，该师从第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克以南渡过第聂伯河，并在此后的尼科波尔-克拉马托尔斯克进攻战役中继续参战。<cr>指挥官报告：1944年冬春战役期间，参加了别列日涅戈瓦托耶-斯尼格里夫卡攻势和敖德萨攻势。1944年7月，在“巴格拉季昂行动”框架内参与了卢布林-布列斯特进攻战役，并开始解放波兰。<cr>指挥官报告：1945年1月，参加了维斯瓦河-奥得河攻势和波兰的解放。同年4月，在谢诺高地战斗中突破敌军防御阵地，并在柏林战略进攻作战中继续参战。

text: The 75th Guards Rifle Division was redesignated at the beginning of March 1943 from the second formation of the 95th Rifle Division in recognition of the latter's courage and heroism during the Battle of Stalingrad. It fought in the Battle of Kursk, defending positions around Ponyri on the northern face of the Kursk Bulge, and was awarded the Order of the Red Banner for its actions. The division fought in Operation Kutuzov and the Battle of the Dnieper in the summer and early fall. It was awarded the honorific 'Bakhmach' for helping to capture that city. The division then fought in the Battle of Kiev and advanced into eastern Belarus towards the end of the year. In January 1944 it fought in the Kalinkovichi-Mozyr Offensive and received the Order of Suvorov, 2nd class for its actions. From late June the 75th Guards fought in Operation Bagration, advancing westwards into Belarus. For its actions the division was awarded its second Order of the Red Banner. In September the division was transferred to the Baltic and fought in the Riga Offensive. It was relocated to eastern Poland in December and fought in the Vistula-Oder Offensive, East Pomeranian Offensives, and Battle of Berlin in the final months of the war.<cr><cr>
translation: 第75近卫步兵师于1943年3月初从第二组建的第95步兵师改编而来，以表彰后者在斯大林格勒战役中的勇气和英雄主义。该师参加了库尔斯克会战，在北部突出部波尼里的防御战斗中表现出色，并因行动获得红旗勋章。该师还参与了库图佐夫行动和第聂伯河战役的夏季及初秋阶段，因其帮助攻占巴赫马奇城而获“巴赫马奇”荣誉称号。同年末，该师参加了基辅会战并向白俄罗斯东部推进。1944年1月，该师参加了卡林科维奇-莫吉廖夫攻势，并因行动获得苏沃洛夫勋章二级。从6月下旬开始，第75近卫步兵师参与了巴格拉季昂行动，在向西推进进入白俄罗斯的战斗中表现出色，并因此获得了其第二个红旗勋章。9月，该师被调往波罗的海地区并参加了里加攻势。12月，该师被转移到波兰东部并参加了维斯瓦-奥得河攻势、东波美拉尼亚攻势和柏林会战，在战争最后几个月中继续作战。<cr><cr>

text: The 75th Infantry Division was assigned to Army Group South, it fought at Kholm, Kiev (1941), Belgorod (1941-42), and Voronezh (1942-43), and was not particularly distinguished in the early phases of the war in the East. Later it performed quite well in the Kiev withdrawal, in the retreat across the northern Ukraine, and in the battles on and around the Dnestr. It suffered heavy losses in the Battle of Kiev in the fall of 1943, at Cherkassy (February-March 1944) and in the Brody sector (April-June 1944). Meanwhile, on October 2, 1943, it was reorganized as a Type 44 division. By the end of the year, it only had five grenadier battalions. Attached to 1st Panzer Army, it fought in the Carpathians, in the Beskiden district (in the Polish Carpathians) and in Upper Silesia. It was crushed at Bohemian Ostrau in early 1945 and ended the war in the pocket east of Prague in May 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation:
第75步兵师被分配到南方集团军群，它参加了霍姆、基辅（1941年）、别尔哥罗德（1941-1942年）和沃罗涅日（1942-1943年）的战斗，在东线战争初期表现并不突出。后来在基辅撤退中表现出色，还在乌克兰北部的撤退以及德涅斯特河及其周边地区的战斗中表现出色。它在1943年秋季的基辅助战、切尔卡瑟（1944年2-3月）和布罗迪地区（1944年4-6月）遭受了重大损失。同年10月2日，该师重组为Type 44师。到年底时，它只剩下五个掷弹兵营。作为第1装甲集团军的一部分，它参加了喀尔巴阡山脉、贝斯基迪地区（波兰喀尔巴阡山脉）和上西里西亚的战斗。在1945年初被彻底击败于波希米亚奥斯特劳，并在1945年5月结束战争时被困在布拉格以东的一个包围圈内。
<cr><cr>德国二战步兵师战斗序列 第1-290师，萨缪尔·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text: The 75th Mountain Rifle Division was established Lubny May 1939. On 15 May 1939 the 75th Rifle Division was transferred from the 14th Rifle Corps (Kharkov Military District) and arrived in the Leningrad Military District. Fought in Winter War with Finland. With 4th Army, Western Front, from June 1941. Wiped out vicinity Kiev Aug 1941. Recreated by January 1942 from 473rd Rifle Division, which became 75 RD (II Formation). translation: 第75山地步兵师于1939年5月在卢布尼建立。1939年5月15日，该师从第14步兵军（哈尔科夫军区）转隶至列宁格勒军区。参加冬季战争对抗芬兰。自1941年6月起隶属于西方方面军的第4集团军。于1941年8月在基辅附近被消灭。到1942年1月，该师由第473步兵师重建为第75步兵师（第二组建）。1945年5月隶属于高加索方面军的第4集团军。<cr>注：II Formation 表示第二次组建。

text:
On 1 March 1943 the 157th Rifle Division became the 76th Guards Rifle Division for its actions in the Battle of Stalingrad. Major General Alexander Kirsanov commanded the division. The division fought in the Battle of Kursk, fighting in the northern part of the Kursk Bulge. Until 3 July the division was part of the Bryansk Front in the area of Belyov. On 12 July the division began the crossing of the Oka. By the end of the day the division had captured bridgeheads. The division received thanks from the Supreme Commander (Stalin) for this action. On 8 September, the division began to advance from the Oryol area to Chernigov. After three days the division had advanced 70 kilometers and reached the village of Tolstoles on 20 September, three kilometers northeast of Chernigov. The division then helped capture the city and advanced to the west. By an order of the Supreme Commander on 21 September the division was thanked and awarded the honorific 'Chernigov'.<cr>
The division then advanced into Belarus. It became part of the 1st Belorussian Front. On 17 July 1944 it began an attack northwest of Kovel. On 21 July the vanguard of the division moved north towards Brest in heavy fighting. On 26 July, troops advancing from the north and south linked up 20 to 25 kilometers west of Brest. German troops in the area were surrounded. For its actions in the capture of Brest, the division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner. On 25 January 1945, the division, as part of the 2nd Belorussian Fronts, blocked the route out of Torun, surrounding German forces. In late February, the division attempted to cut the road out of Konitz. German troops were able to escape in the fighting. On 23 March the division captured Sopot and advanced to the Baltic Sea. By 25 March it had captured Oliwa and was advancing towards Danzig. The division helped captured Danzig on 30 March. The division was moved from Danzig to Germany and on 24 April was concentrated near Kortenhaten, 20 kilometers south of Stettin. On 26 April the division crossed the Rondov canal and broke through the German line. By the end of the day it had captured Pretslavu.<cr>
On 2 May, the division captured Gstrow. On 3 May, after advancing 40 kilometers, it captured Karow and Butzow. The forward detachments of the 76th Guards Rifle Division reached the Baltic and on the outskirts of Wismar met with Allied airborne units of the 6th Airborne Division. The division was part of the 114th Rifle Corps of the 70th Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front in May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
1943年3月1日，由于在斯大林格勒战役中的表现，第157步兵师改编为第76近卫步兵师。该师由少将亚历山大·基尔萨诺夫指挥，在库尔斯克战役中参加了库尔斯克突出部北部的战斗。直到7月3日，该师隶属于布良斯克方面军，并驻扎在别利沃地区。7月12日，该师开始渡过奥卡河。到当天结束时，该师已占领了桥头堡。最高统帅（斯大林）对该行动表示感谢。9月8日，该师从奥廖尔地区向切爾尼戈夫推进。三天后，该师推进了70公里，并于9月20日到达距离切爾尼戈夫东北三公里的托尔斯勒村。随后，该师协助占领了该城市并向西推进。<cr>根据最高统帅部9月21日的命令，该师受到表彰并获得“切爾尼戈夫”荣誉称号<cr>
该师随后进入白俄罗斯。它成为第1白俄罗斯方面军的一部分。1944年7月17日，该师开始在科韦尔西北方向发动攻击。7月21日，在激烈的战斗中，该师的先头部队向布列斯特北部推进。7月26日，来自北面和南面的部队在距离布列斯特西边约20至25公里处会合，包围了当地的德军。由于在占领布列斯特中的表现，该师被授予红旗勋章。1945年1月25日，作为第2白俄罗斯方面军的一部分，该师封锁了通向托伦的路线，并包围了德国部队。2月底，该师试图切断科尼茨的出口道路。德军在战斗中得以逃脱。3月23日，该师占领索波特并向波罗的海推进。到3月25日，它已占领奥利瓦并继续向但泽推进。该师帮助于3月30日占领了但泽。随后该师从但泽转移到德国，并在4月24日集中在科滕哈特恩附近，距离什切青南边约20公里处。<cr>4月26日，该师越过罗多夫运河并突破德军防线。到当天结束时，它已占领普雷斯特拉乌。<cr><cr>5月1日，该师占领格施特劳。5月3日，在推进了40公里后，它占领卡罗和布茨沃。第76近卫步兵师的前哨部队抵达波罗的海，并在维斯马郊区与盟军空降部队第6空降师会合。<cr>该师是1945年5月第2白俄罗斯方面军第70集团军第114步兵军的一部分。<cr><cr>

text: The 76th Infantry Division invaded Russia in 1941 and served on the southern sector from the beginning. It took part in the sweep across the Ukraine, the winter battles of 1941-42 in which Army Group South had to retreat from Rostov, the Izyum counteroffensive of May 1942, and the German victories at Voronezh and Kalack, which almost won the war on the southern sector for Germany. The 76th took part in the street fighting in Stalingrad and was encircled there in November 1942. It fought on the heavily attacked western perimeter from then until January 31, 1943, when it was destroyed. Lieutenant General Karl Rosenburg, the divisional commander, was among those taken prisoner when the city fell.<cr>A second 76th Infantry Division was built in the spring of 1943, to replace the division destroyed at Stalingrad. Its unit numbers remained the same as the original 76th, except that its 230th Regiment was given the honorary title 230th Fusilier Grenadier Regiment, and its l76th Reconnaissance Battalion was replaced by the 76th Fusilier Battalion. The new division was initially based in Brittany, France, before crossing into Italy in August 1943. That winter it was transferred to the southern sector of the Eastern Front, where it fought at Krivoi Rog, in the Nikolajev Bridgehead, and on the Dniepr bend, and suffered heavy losses in the Dnieper withdrawal in March 1944. It absorbed the remnants of the 5th Luftwaffe Field Division that same month. Even so, it had to cut its number of infantry battalions from nine to six. Continuing in action on the Eastern Front, the 76th retreated across the Ukraine and Romania, and fought in the Hungarian campaign, where it was virtually destroyed in the Battle of Oradea (October 8-12, 1944) when it and the 23rd Panzer Division defended the city for five days against the Soviet 6th Guards Tank Army. The remnants of the division were sent to Slovakia and then Moravia, where they were reorganized. The division-now a Kampfgruppe-was surrounded with the 1st Panzer Army at Deutsch-Brod (east of Prague) at the end of April 1945. They surrendered to the Russians after Hitler committed suicide on April 30, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第76步兵师于1941年入侵俄罗斯，并从一开始就驻守在南部战区。它参与了横扫乌克兰的行动，以及1941-42年的冬季战役，在这场战役中南方集团军群不得不从罗斯托夫撤退。该师还参加了1942年5月伊久姆反攻、德国在沃罗涅日和卡累茨取得的胜利，这些胜利几乎让德国赢得了南部战区的战争。第76步兵师参与了斯大林格勒巷战，并于1942年11月在那里被包围。从那时起直到1943年1月31日被消灭，它一直在遭受猛烈攻击的西部外围作战。<cr>师长卡尔·罗森堡中将和其他人一起在城市陷落时成为俘虏。<cr>1943年春天组建了第二个第76步兵师，以替代在斯大林格勒被消灭的原师。新师的单位编号与原来的第76师相同，除了其第230团获得荣誉掷弹兵称号，成为第230掷弹兵团，以及侦察营176号被第76号步枪兵营取代。该新师最初驻扎在法国布列塔尼地区，随后于1943年8月进入意大利。那年的冬天，它被转移到东线南部战区，在克里沃伊罗格、尼古拉耶夫桥头堡和第聂伯河弯道作战，并在1944年3月的第聂伯河撤退中遭受了重大损失。同月，该师吸收了第5空军野战师的残部。即便如此，它还是不得不将其步兵营数量从九个削减到六个。继续在东线作战，第76师撤过乌克兰和罗马尼亚，并参加了匈牙利战役，在奥拉迪亚战役（1944年10月8日至12日）中几乎被消灭，当时该师与第23装甲师一起坚守城市五天，对抗苏联第6近卫坦克集团军。该师的残部被送往斯洛伐克和摩拉维亚，在那里重新组织起来。到1945年4月30日，希特勒自杀后，他们向俄国人投降了。<cr> 德国战斗序列 第1-290步兵师在二战中的经历，山姆·W·米奇姆少校著<cr>

text: The 78th Infantry Division served with Army Group Center in the initial campaign. The division fought at Bialystok and Smolensk and distinguished itself in the battles of Bialowieza and the Yelnya bend. It also fought in the Battle of Moscow and against the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42. During that period it dropped the 238th Infantry Regiment from its table of organization and received the 14th Infantry (later Sturm) Regiment from the 5th Infantry Division. The 78th fought in the Rzhev salient and remained on the central sector of the Russian Front. It acquired such an excellent combat record that it was given the honorary title 'Sturm' (Storm or Assault) division on January 1, 1943. In 1943 it took part in the Battle of Kursk and in the successful defense of Smolensk and Orscha, before being crushed near Minsk in the massive Soviet summer offensive of 1944. The divisions commander, Lieutenant General Hans Traut, and most of his men were captured.<cr>The 78th was reformed at the Muensingen Troop Maneuver Area in late July 1944 by absorbing the 543rd Grenadier Division (a Sperr, or blocking, unit). It was redesignated the 78th Volksgrenadier Division on October 9, 1944, returned to action in Galacia (southern Poland) in autumn, and again suffered heavy casualties. The division was again largely destroyed in January 1945, when it attempted to block the Russian drive into Upper Silesia. The remnants of this veteran division remained in action despite its losses and finally surrendered at Deutsch-Brod, Czechoslovakia, with the rest of Army Group Center, in May 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation:
第78步兵师在初期战役中隶属于中央集团军群。该师参加了比亚韦斯托克、斯摩棱斯克的战斗，并在比亚韦斯托克森林和叶尔尼亚弯道的战斗中表现出色。它还参与了莫斯科会战以及1941-1942年冬季苏军反攻作战。在此期间，第78师将其编制中的第238步兵团裁撤，并从第5步兵师接收了第14步兵团（后来改名为突击团）。该师参加了热季突出部的战斗，并一直驻守在东线中央战区。它取得了如此出色的战绩，以至于于1943年1月1日被授予“突击”称号。1943年，该师参与了库尔斯克会战，并成功防御了斯摩棱斯克和奥尔沙，但在1944年苏军夏季攻势中，在明斯克附近遭到重创。师长汉斯·特劳特少将及其大部分官兵被俘。

第78步兵师于1944年7月下旬在穆恩施廷演习区重建，并吸收了第543掷弹兵师（一个阻击单位）。该师于1944年10月9日改名为第78国民掷弹兵师，返回加利西亚（波兰南部）作战，在秋季再次遭受重大损失。1945年1月，该师在试图阻止苏军进入上西里西亚时几乎被完全消灭。尽管遭受了巨大损失，这支部队的老兵们仍然继续战斗，并最终于1945年5月随中央集团军群在德意志-布罗德（捷克斯洛伐克）投降。

参考文献：《二战中的德国步兵师第1至290师》第一卷，萨缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text: The 79th Guards Rifle Division was formed from the remnants of the 284th Rifle Division, in recognition of that division's stalwart defense against the German 6th Army in the Battle of Stalingrad, in particular the Mamayev Kurgan hill and parts of the city's center. The 79th Guards continued a record of distinguished service through the rest of WWII.<cr><cr>
translation: 第79近卫步兵师由第284步兵师的残部组建而成，以表彰该师在斯大林格勒战役中对德国第6集团军的顽强防御，特别是马梅耶夫高地和市区的部分地区。第79近卫步兵师继续在二战余下的时间里保持卓越的服务记录。<cr><cr>

text: The 79th Infantry Division joined Army Group South in Russia in July 1941 and fought its way through the Ukraine and across the Dnieper. It took part in the Battle of Kiev, where several Soviet armies were encircled and destroyed, and later opposed the Russian winter offensive of 1941-42. In 1942 the 79th Infantry fought in the Battle of Kharkov, in the encirclement of 200,000 Russians at Izyum, in the Battle of Voronezh, and in the encirclement at Kalack, where another Russian army was destroyed. The division was itself surrounded with 6th Army in the Stalingrad Pocket in November 1942 and destroyed in late January 1943. Shortly before the fall, however, the Luftwaffe flew part of the division staff and elements of the 179th Infantry Regiment out of the pocket. They would make the nucleus of a new division.<cr>A second 79th Infantry Division was created at Stalino in the spring of 1943 and was quickly sent to the southern sector of the Russian Front, which had undergone crisis after crisis since November 1942. The division was initially engaged in the Kuban bridgehead in the summer of 1943 before being evacuated via the Crimea to the lower Dnieper, where it was involved in heavy fighting in the Nikopol Bridgehead (November 1943-January 1944). At first the combat ability of the 79th was considered low, but its rating improved with experience. It took part in the retreats through the Ukraine and into Romania in 1943 and 1944. The division absorbed the 1001st March Battalion in early 1944, but still had to disband three of its infantry battalions in June. In late August 1944, Romania defected from the Axis, leaving the rebuilt 6th Army and much of Army Group South Ukraine-including the 79th Infantry-cut off. The division tried to cut its way through Russian lines with General Mieth's IV Corps but was destroyed by the Red Army near the village of Chitcani on the Berlad River. General Mieth died in this battle. Only one soldier from the division made good his escape, reaching German lines in Hungary 12 days after the division was destroyed.<cr>A third 79th Infantry Division was formed as a Volksgrenadier unit in the Thorn area of Wehrkries XX (Poland) on October 27, 1944. Most of its new recruits were transferred from the partially formed 586th Volksgrenadier Division. Transferred to the Western Front in December 1944, it was about half its authorized strength in the Battle of the Bulge, where it formed part of the LXXXV Corps of the 7th Army. In this campaign the 79th had very little artillery, but its infantrymen proved to be formidable opponents and were highly praised by U. S. Army Intelligence. By February 1945 the division was with the LIII Corps (7th Army) in western Germany and fought in the battles of the Vianden Bulge and Bitburg. The remnants of the 276th Volksgrenadier Division were attached to the 79th near the end of the war, while the 79th VG retreated across the Mosel and Rhine. Its survivors surrendered to the Americans around Heidelburg and Darmstadt at the end of the war.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第79步兵师于1941年7月加入南方集团军群，进入俄罗斯境内，并穿越乌克兰和第聂伯河。该师参加了基辅战役，在此役中数个苏联集团军被包围并消灭。之后，它又对抗了1941-1942年的俄冬季攻势。在1942年，第79步兵师参与了哈尔科夫战役、伊久姆地区对20万俄军的包围战、沃罗涅日战役以及卡拉萨地区的包围圈，在此役中又一个苏联集团军被消灭。该师于1942年11月在斯大林格勒包围圈内与第6集团军一同被包围，并于1943年1月底被消灭。然而，就在覆灭前夕，德国空军将部分师部人员和第179步兵团的部分兵力从包围圈中空运出来。他们将成为新组建的一个师的核心力量。<cr><cr>1943年春天在斯塔林诺组建了第二个第79步兵师，并迅速被派往俄罗斯方面军南部战区，自1942年11月以来该地区危机四伏。该师最初于1943年夏天在库班桥头堡作战，随后经克里米亚撤退到第聂伯河下游，在尼科波尔桥头堡（1943年11月至1944年1月）参与了激烈战斗。起初认为第79师的战斗力较低，但其评级随着经验积累而提高。该师参加了1943年至1944年间从乌克兰撤退进入罗马尼亚的行动。1944年初，第79师吸收了第1001营，但仍不得不在6月解散三个步兵营。1944年8月底，罗马尼亚倒向盟军阵营，导致重建的第6集团军和大部分南方乌克兰集团军群——包括第79步兵师——被切断联系。该师试图与米特将军指挥的第4军一起突破苏联防线，在贝拉德河附近的奇塔尼村附近遭到红军毁灭性打击。米特将军在这场战斗中阵亡。只有该师一名士兵成功逃脱，12天后抵达匈牙利境内的德国战线。<cr>第三个第79步兵师于1944年10月27日在波兰卫戍区XX（托伦地区）作为国民掷弹兵部队组建。其大部分新兵是从尚未完全编成的第586国民掷弹兵师调来的。该师于1944年12月被转移到西线，在突出部战役中隶属于第7集团军的LXXXV军，此时它的兵力约为编制的一半。尽管炮兵力量薄弱，但其步兵证明是强大的对手，并得到了美国陆军情报部门的高度赞扬。到1945年2月，该师已加入第7集团军的LIII军，在德国西部参与了维安登突出部和比特堡战役。在战争末期，第276国民掷弹兵师残部被并入第79师，而第79国民掷弹兵师则撤退至摩泽尔河和莱茵河。其幸存者于战后在海德堡和达姆施塔特附近向美军投降。<cr><cr>德国二战步兵师战斗序列卷一（第1-290步兵师），萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: The 79th Rifle Corps was formed in July 1943 as a headquarters with no troops assigned, and subordinated to the Ural Military District. The headquarters was subsequently transferred to the 21st Army of the Western Front in August, and the 20th Army of the Reserve of the Supreme High Command in September. The 79th joined the 3rd Shock Army of the 2nd Baltic Front in October, with which it remained for the rest of the war, and was assigned the 146th and 326th Rifle Divisions under the command of Major General Fyodor Zuyev from 15 October. The 146th and 326th were replaced by the 28th, 171st, and 219th Rifle Divisions in November.<cr>On May 1, 1945, the 79th Rifle Corps was the superior headquarters for the 150th, 171st, and 207th Rifle Divisions. The 150th Rifle Division was among those units that stormed the Reichstag.<cr>In recognition of its actions, the corps received the Berlin honorific shortly after the end of the war.<cr><cr>
translation: 第79步兵军于1943年7月成立，当时只是一个没有部队的司令部，并隶属于乌拉尔军区。该司令部随后在8月转隶给西方方面军第21集团军，在9月又转隶给最高统帅部预备队第20集团军。第79步兵军于10月加入波罗的海第二方面军第3突击集团军，并一直留在那里，从10月15日起由费多尔·祖耶夫少将指挥第146和第326步兵师。第146和第326步兵师在11月被第28、第171和第219步兵师取代。<cr>1945年5月1日，第79步兵军是第150、第171和第207步兵师的上级司令部。其中第150步兵师参与了攻占国会大厦的战斗。<cr>作为对其行动的认可，该军在战争结束不久后获得了柏林荣誉称谓。<cr><cr>

text: Formed in September 1941 and consisting of the 14th, 15th and 16th Airborne Brigades, the corps never reached full strength and was never committed to combat. It was reorganized in August 1942 into the 34th Guards Rifle Division. A second formation of the corps in the fall of 1942 was converted into the2nd Guards Airborne Division .<cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 成立于1941年9月，由第14、15和16空降旅组成。该军从未达到满编状态，也未投入战斗。它于1942年8月重组为第34近卫步兵师。1942年秋季再次组建的该军被改编为第2近卫空降师。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert，《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，Presidio Press，1985<cr>词条由Stewart King提供

text: The 7th Guards Army was re-designated from the 64th Army on April 16, 1943. 64th Army had originally been formed from 1st Reserve Army in July 1942, and alongside the 62nd Army, fought the German offensive during the Battle of Stalingrad to a standstill, for which it was raised to Guards status. General Lieutenant M.S. Shumilov, who had commanded the 64th Army, continued to command 7th Guards Army through the rest of the war, though he was promoted to General Colonel in October 1943.<cr>It included the 15th, 36th, 72nd, 73rd, 78th and 81st Guards Rifle Divisions, which were incorporated in the 24th and 25th Guards Rifle Corps. As part of the Voronezh Front and the Steppe Front since July 18, 1943, the Army participated in the Battle of Kursk and the Battle for the Dnieper River from July through August, 1943. Subsequently, as part of the 2nd Ukrainian Front, it participated in the Kirovograd Offensive, and those of Uman and Botosani, Jassy-Kishinev, Debrecen, Budapest, Bratislava and Brno, and Prague.<cr><cr>
translation: 第七近卫集团军是在1943年4月16日由第64集团军改编而成。第64集团军最初于1942年7月从第一预备集团军组建，并与第62集团军一起，在斯大林格勒战役中对抗德国的进攻，成功将其遏制，因此被授予近卫称号。指挥第64集团军的大将M.S.舒米罗夫继续担任第七近卫集团军的指挥官直至战争结束，尽管他在1943年10月晋升为上将。<cr>该集团军包括第15、第36、第72、第73、第78和第81步兵师，并被编入第二十四和二十五近卫步兵军。作为沃罗涅日方面军和草原方面军的一部分，自1943年7月18日起，该集团军参与了库尔斯克战役以及从7月至8月的第聂伯河战役。<cr>随后，作为第二乌克兰方面军的一部分，它参加了基洛夫格勒攻势、乌曼攻势、博托沙尼攻势、雅西-奇尔诺夫行动、德布勒森战役、布达佩斯战役、布拉迪斯拉发和布尔诺攻势以及布拉格攻势。

text:
Order No. 78 of the Commissariat of the Defense of the USSR dated 14 February 1943 the 8th Cavalry Corps was redesignated the 7th Guards Cavalry Corps.<cr>After receiving its Guards designations the corps withdrew from behind German lines through snowstorms. After a week of dodging German patrols the Corps slipped back through Soviet lines, having disrupted the rear areas and movement of most of a Panzer Corps. After returning to Soviet lines and due to the heavy losses from Stalingrad offensive and the cavalry raid the Corps was sent into the reserves to rebuild.<cr>Between March and May 1943 the corps was reinforced and rebuilt in the Southwestern Front. The corps sent north to join the Steppe Front in the STAVKA Reserves in June.<cr>The Corps was not committed in the first part of the summer offensive after Kursk, remaining in STAVKA reserves until September. Assigned to the 61st Army on 19 September 1943 the corps had added the 1897th SU Regiment (SU-76s) and the 7th Guards Mortar Regiment (120mm mortars).<cr>From late September 1943 to March 1944 the corps operated in the 61ast or 65th Armies of the Belorussian Front, trying to enlarge the penetration south of Gomel. In January 1944 the 1897th SU Regiment was replaced by the 1816th SU Regiment (Su-76s), which remained in the Corps until the end of the war. On 5 March 1944 the Corps was sent to the 2nd Belorussian Front reserves, and in April helped clear the Germans out of the Mozyr and River Turya areas, clearing the south edges of the Pripyet marshes for operations later in the summer. On 17 May 1944 the Corps went to the 1st Belorussian Front in the area of Brest and Kobrin. On 14 July 1944 Operation Bagration began with the Corps advancing with the 2nd Tank Army,. By the end of the week the corps had advanced 200 km, south of Lublin to Radom. The front line stabilized and the corps was on the defensive from 8 August 1944 to 7 January 1945.<cr>When the Vistula-Oder offensive started in January 1945 the 1st Belorussian Front formed the Konstantinov Cavalry-Mechanized Group under the 7th Guards Cavalry Commander, Lieutenant General M. P. Konstantinov. The group consisted of:<cr><cr>7th Guards Cavalry Corps:-<cr>
14th Guards Cavalry Division
15th Guards Cavalry Division
16th Guards Cavalry Division
1816th SU Regiment
145th Guards Antitank Regiment (76mm)
1773rd Antiaircraft Regiment
7th Guards Antitank Battalion
57th Guards Mortar Battalion (rockets)
7th Guards Mortar Regiment<cr><cr>
9th Tank Corps:-<cr>
23rd Tank Brigade (T-34/85)
95th Tank Brigade (T-34/85)
108th Tank Brigade (T-34/85)
8th Motorized Rifle Brigade
36th Guards Heavy Tanks Regiment (IS-IIs)
1445th SU Regiment
1508th SU Regiment
868th Light Artillery Regiment
216th Antiaircraft Regiment
218th Mortar Regiment (120mm)
286th Guards Mortar Battalion (rockets)
90th Motorcycle Battalion<cr><cr>This group advanced over 400 km from the center of the 1st Belorussian front to the Oder River in just 17 days. The group then turned north into Pomerania, where it spent two months clearing the flanks of the Soviet penetration of German lines. In April and May 1945 the Group advanced as part of the Berlin Strategic Operation operating independently weeping north of the city to seize Brandenburg and then continuing on to meet advancing units of the US 9th Army.<cr><cr>
translation:
苏共中央国防委员会第78号命令，1943年2月14日：将第8骑兵军改名为第7近卫骑兵军。<cr>获得近卫称号后，该军从德军防线后方通过暴风雪撤回苏联境内。一周内躲避德军巡逻队的追捕后，该军成功潜入苏军防线之后，扰乱了德军装甲军的后勤区域和行动。返回苏军战线并因斯大林格勒攻势及骑兵突袭造成的重大损失，该军被送入预备队重建。<cr>从1943年3月至5月期间，该军在西南方面军得到补充和重建。6月时，该军北上加入草原方面军的最高统帅部预备队。<cr>库尔斯克战役后初夏攻势的第一阶段中，该军未被投入战斗，一直留在最高统帅部预备队直到9月。1943年9月19日，该军被分配给第61集团军，并增加了装备SU-76自行火炮的第1897团和装备120毫米迫击炮的第7近卫迫击炮团。<cr>从1943年晚秋到1944年3月，该军在白俄罗斯方面军第61或第65集团军中行动，试图扩大戈梅利以南的突破。1944年1月，第1897自行火炮团被第1816自行火炮团（Su-76）取代，并一直留在该军直到战争结束。1944年3月5日，该军被调往第二白俄罗斯方面军预备队，在4月份帮助清除了莫吉廖夫和图尔亚河地区的德军，清理了普里皮亚季沼泽的南部边缘，为夏季后期行动做准备。1944年5月17日，该军前往第一白俄罗斯方面军布列斯特和科宾地区。1944年7月14日，巴格拉季昂行动开始，该军与第二坦克集团军一起推进。到周末结束时，该军已向南推进了200公里，从卢布林到达姆。战线稳定下来，从1944年8月8日至1945年1月7日，该军处于防御状态。<cr>当维斯瓦河-奥得河攻势于1945年1月开始时，第一白俄罗斯方面军在第7近卫骑兵军指挥官、中将M. P. 康斯坦丁诺夫的领导下组建了康斯坦丁诺夫骑兵机械化集团。该集团包括：<cr>第7近卫骑兵军：-<cr>第14近卫骑兵师<cr>第15近卫骑兵师<cr>第16近卫骑兵师<cr>第1816自行火炮团<cr>第145近卫反坦克团（76毫米）<cr>第1773防空团<cr>第7近卫反坦克营<cr>第57近卫迫击炮营（火箭弹）<cr>第7近卫迫击炮团<cr>第9坦克军：-
第23坦克旅（T-34/85）
第95坦克旅（T-34/85）
第108坦克旅（T-34/85）
第8摩托化步兵旅
第36近卫重型坦克团（IS-II）
第1445自行火炮团
第1508自行火炮团
第868轻型炮兵团
第216防空团
第218迫击炮团（120毫米）
第286近卫火箭炮营
第90摩托车营<cr><cr>这个部队从第一白俄罗斯方面军中心向奥得河推进了400多公里，仅用了17天。随后该部队转向波美拉尼亚北部，在那里花了两个月清理苏联突破德国防线的侧翼。1945年4月和5月，作为柏林战略行动的一部分，这个集团独立北上，占领勃兰登堡，并继续前进与美国第9集团军会合。<cr><cr>

text: Formed 1/5/42 from 31st Cavalry Division as part of I Guards Cavalry Corps. It fought in the Don Basin and in the Kharkov and in the Dnieper crossing in 1943, was part of the Zhitomir-Berdichev Operation in winter 1943-44, in the Carpathian Offensive in the fall, and in the Berlin Strategic Operation in 1945. It was also known as the Suvorov and Bogdan Khmelnitskiy Cavalry Division and received the honorific title 'Zhitomir for its role in the Berdichev Offensive. <cr><cr>Pettibone, Charles D., The Organization and Order of Battle of Militaries in World War II: volume V - Book B Union of Soviet Socialist Republics, Trafford, 2009<cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 成立于1942年5月1日，由第31骑兵师改编而成，隶属于第一近卫骑兵军。该部队参加了顿河盆地、哈尔科夫和1943年的第聂伯河渡口战役，在1943-44年冬季的扎波罗热-别尔季切夫行动中作战，并在秋季卡帕奇亚攻势以及1945年的柏林战略行动中参战。该部队还被称为苏沃洛夫和博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基骑兵师，因其在别尔季切夫攻势中的表现而获得“扎波罗热”荣誉称号。<cr>参考文献：Pettibone, Charles D., 《第二次世界大战中军事组织与战斗序列：第五卷B - 苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟》，Trafford, 2009<cr>Poirier, Robert 和 Conner, Albert, 《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，Presidio Press, 1985<cr>词条贡献者：Stewart King

text: The 7th Guards Rifle Division was reformed as an elite infantry division of the Red Army in September, 1941, based on the 1st formation of the 64th Rifle Division and served in that role until after the end of the Great Patriotic War. It was first assigned to Bryansk Front, then moved to Western Front where it took part in the early stages of the winter counteroffensive northwest of Moscow as part of 16th Army. On December 31 the 1st Guards Rifle Corps was formed for the second time and the 7th Guards was assigned to it as its core formation. It was then sent north to join Northwestern Front and became locked into the dismal fighting around Demyansk until that salient was finally evacuated by the German II Army Corps in February, 1943. Through the rest of that year it participated in battles in the Staraya Russa region, mostly under command of 1st Shock Army, until in January, 1944 it was transferred to the 7th Guards Rifle Corps of 10th Guards Army in the Nevel region. During operations in the Baltic states that summer and autumn the 7th Guards was awarded both a battle honor and the Order of the Red Banner. In March, 1945 it joined the Courland Group of Forces of Leningrad Front on the Baltic coast containing the German forces encircled in northwest Latvia. Following the German surrender it was moved to Estonia where it was disbanded in 1946.
translation: 第7近卫步兵师于1941年9月作为红军的精锐步兵师重建，基于第64步兵师的第一个编制，并一直担任此角色直到伟大卫国战争结束。该师最初被分配给布良斯克方面军，随后调至西方方面军，在莫斯科西北部冬季反攻初期阶段中隶属于第16集团军作战。1941年12月31日，第1近卫步兵军第二次组建，并将第7近卫步兵师作为其核心编制。之后该师被派往北方方向加入西北方面军，在德意志第二集团军于1943年2月撤离之前一直参与德梅耶斯克地区的惨烈战斗。在接下来的一年里，它主要在第1突击集团军的指挥下参加了斯塔罗伊鲁萨地区的一些战役，直到1944年1月被调至列宁格勒方面军第10近卫集团军下的第7近卫步兵军，在涅韦尔地区作战。该师于当年夏季和秋季在波罗的海国家进行行动期间获得了一项战斗荣誉以及红旗勋章。1945年3月，它加入列宁格勒方面军在波罗的海沿岸包围德国军队的库尔兰集团军群。随着德军投降，第7近卫步兵师被调往爱沙尼亚，并于1946年解散。

text: On 26 July 1943, the 7th Guards Tank Corps, part of the 3rd Guards Tank Army on the Bryansk Front, was formed from the 15th Tank Corps in recognition of the 'courage and bravery' of its actions in Operation Kutuzov, the Soviet counterattack after the Battle of Kursk, under the command of Major General Filipp Rudkin. The 88th Tank Brigade became the 54th Guards Tank Brigade, the 113th became the 55th Guards, the 195th became the 56th Guards, and the 17th Motor Rifle Brigade became the 23rd Guards. On the same day as it became a Guards unit, the corps and the rest of the army attempted to advance towards Stanovoy Kolodez, but were stopped by heavy fire after Soviet aerial reconnaissance detected a concentration of German tanks in the area of Mikhailovka and Pilatovka.<cr>On 6 September, the army was ordered to begin moving to the Sumy area on 8 September and to complete the relocation by 15 September, when it was to join the Voronezh Front to fight in the Chernigov-Poltava Strategic Offensive, part of the Battle of the Dnieper. As planned, the army's troops relocated by road to the Sumy area, completing the 150 kilometer (93 mi) march by 13 September, but the equipment, moved by rail, was delayed due to the German airstrikes and destruction of railway ties during their retreat. While the army moved to the front, the Voronezh Front was advancing westward, and the deployment of the army to Sumy was no longer necessary. As a result, the army's place of concentration was switched to Romny, which was reached by 19 September after a march of 150-200 kilometers (93-124 mi). The army was tasked with pursuing the retreating German forces westwards towards Pryluky, Turovka, Yahotyn, Pereiaslav, and seizing a bridgehead south of Pereiaslav on the Dnieper, with the 6th and 7th Guards in the first echelon.<cr>At the end of October and the beginning of November, the 7th Guards were secretly transferred from Bukrin to the Lyutezh bridgehead. The corps fought in the capture of Kiev during the Battle of Kiev. It then fought in fierce fighting against a large German counterattack southwest of Fastov. The 7th Guards fought in the Zhitomir-Berdichev Offensive and the Proskurov-Chernovitsy Offensive in early 1944.<cr>In the Sandomierz-Silesian Offensive and Lower Silesian Offensive in early 1945, the 7th Guards advanced over 150 kilometers and captured fortified city of Cz?stochowa on the Warta alongside the 5th Guards Army's 31st Tank Corps on 17 January. In the Berlin Offensive, which began in mid-April, the corps advanced over 400 kilometers. The 7th Guards' last combat operation was the Prague Offensive, during which it advanced south into Czechoslovakia and participated in the liberation of Prague.<cr><cr>
translation: 1943年7月26日，第7近卫坦克军在布良斯克方面军的第3近卫坦克集团军内组建。该部队由第15坦克军改编而成，以表彰其在库图佐夫行动中的“勇气和英勇”，这是库尔斯克战役后苏联的反击行动，在菲利普·鲁德金少将的指挥下进行。第88坦克旅改名为第54近卫坦克旅，第113坦克旅改名为第55近卫坦克旅，第195坦克旅改名为第56近卫坦克旅，第17摩托化步兵旅则改名为第23近卫旅。在成为近卫部队的同一天，该军及其所属集团军试图向斯坦诺沃伊科洛德内兹推进，但苏联航空侦察发现米哈伊洛夫卡和皮拉托夫卡地区集结了大量德国坦克后，他们遭到了猛烈炮火的阻击。<cr>9月6日，该集团军接到命令于9月8日开始向苏米地区转移，并在9月15日前完成搬迁。届时它将加入沃罗涅日方面军参加切尔尼戈夫-波尔塔瓦战略进攻行动，这是第聂伯河战役的一部分。按计划，集团军的部队通过公路迁移到苏米地区，在9月13日前完成了约150公里（93英里）的行军，但装备则因德国空军在撤退期间对铁路设施的轰炸而延迟了铁路运输。当该集团军向前线移动时，沃罗涅日方面军正在西进，因此将该集团军集中地改为罗马尼，于9月19日前通过约150-200公里（93-124英里）的行军到达。该集团军的任务是追击撤退中的德军至普里卢基、图罗夫卡、雅霍廷和佩雷亚斯拉夫，并在第聂伯河佩雷亚斯拉夫以南夺取桥头堡，其中近卫第6师和近卫第7师为第一梯队。<cr>10月底到11月初，近卫第7师秘密从布克林转移到柳特切赫桥头堡。该军在基辅战役中参与了夺取基辅的战斗，并随后与德军在法斯托夫西南部的大规模反攻进行了激烈交战。近卫第7师还参加了1944年初的扎波罗热-别尔季切夫进攻和普罗斯库罗夫-切尔诺维策进攻。<cr>在1945年初的桑多梅日-西里西亚进攻和下西里西亚进攻中，第7近卫军推进了超过150公里，并于1月17日在维斯瓦河畔与第5近卫集团军的第31坦克军一起攻克了设防城市什切青。在4月中旬开始的柏林进攻中，该军推进了超过400公里。第7近卫军的最后一场战斗行动是布拉格攻势，在此期间它向南进入捷克斯洛伐克并参与解放布拉格。<cr>指挥官报告：<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 7th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In January 1942 the Germans demanded more Hungarian forces for the Eastern Front and most Hungarian infantry brigades were reclassified as 'light divisions'. Their TOE however remained largely unchanged. The brigade was renamed the 7th Light Division. The Hungarian Government reluctantly agreed to support the Germans 1942 summer offensive Fall Blau and allocated the Hungarian Second Army to the task. Each light division in the Second Army was reinforced with three battalions from sister divisions in Hungary but nonetheless each division was only slightly larger than half the size of its German counterparts. Second Army's role in the offensive was to guard the German northern flank on the Don River. During the Stalingrad Campaign the Second Army suffered over 60% casualties but was generally able to retreat in good order. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 7th Light Division was merged with other units and renamed the 7th Infantry Division. The division was disbanded in August of 1944.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第7匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由一名少将指挥，下辖2个步兵团（每个团有3个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团拥有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1942年1月，德国要求匈牙利提供更多兵力参加东线作战，并且大多数匈牙利步兵旅被重新分类为“轻型师”。然而其编制表基本没有变化。该旅更名为第7轻型师。匈牙利政府勉强同意支持德军在1942年夏季的蓝色行动，将匈牙利第二集团军投入任务中。第二集团军中的每个轻型师都从匈牙利国内的兄弟部队得到3个营的增援，但即便如此，每个师仍然只有其德国同行的一半左右规模。第二集团军在进攻中的角色是保卫德军北线顿河沿岸的安全。在斯大林格勒战役期间，第二集团军伤亡超过60%% c，但仍能有组织地撤退。作为战后对匈牙利军队进行重组的一部分，第7轻型师与其他部队合并，并更名为第7步兵师。该师于1944年8月解散。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson<cr><cr>

text: In June the 7th Infantry Division took part in the invasion of Russia with Army Group Center and fought in the siege of Mogilev on the upper Dnieper, as well as in the battles of Bialystok, Minsk, Smolensk, and Vyazma (Vjasma). Later it was involved in the final thrust toward Moscow and in the ensuing Russian counteroffensive that saved Stalin's capital. The division spent 1942 on the relatively quiet central sector at Gshatsk and Spas-Demyansk and took part in the Battle of Kursk offensive as part of the 9th Army. It managed to escape the near-annihilation of Army Group Center in the summer of 1944 and conducted a fighting retreat across the Bug and Narev (Narew) and through Poland that fall. It finally was cut off by the last Soviet offensive and ended the war isolated behind Russian lines on the Hela peninsula, at the mouth of the Vistula, where it surrendered on May 8, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 6月，第7步兵师参加了中央集团军群入侵俄罗斯的行动，并参与了上第聂伯河畔莫吉廖夫的围攻战，以及比亚韦斯托克、明斯克、斯摩棱斯克和维亚兹马（Vyasma）的战斗。后来它还参与了向莫斯科的最后一击，以及随后拯救斯大林首都的苏联反攻行动。该师在1942年驻守相对平静的中央战区格扎茨克和斯帕斯-德米扬斯克，并作为第9集团军参加了库尔斯克战役进攻。它成功避开了1944年夏季中央集团军群几乎被消灭的命运，进行了从布格河和纳雷夫（Narew）到波兰的战斗撤退行动。最终在苏联最后一次攻势中被切断，于1945年5月8日在维斯瓦河口赫拉半岛向苏军投降，结束了孤立于苏军战线后的战争。<cr>参考文献：德国二战步兵师作战序列（第1-290师），萨缪尔·W·米奇姆 Jr.

text: The corps began forming on 8 July 1940 in the Moscow Military District from the 39th and 55th Light Tank Brigades, and the 1st Motorized Division.<cr>On 22 June, the German invasion of the Soviet Union, Operation Barbarossa, began. At the time, the corps had a strength of 959 tanks. The corps was put on alert for movement to the front and on 24 June was ordered to join the Reserve of the Supreme High Command in the Gzhatsk District. While passing through Gzhatsk, the corps received new orders to concentrate at Vyazma. While moving to Vyazma, the corps received new order, directing it to move to Yartsevo and then Smolensk. The final destination of the corps was to be Orsha.<cr>By the time it went into battle, the strength of the corps had been reduced to 428 tanks due to breakdowns. The corps attacked without air support, and with a shortage of fuel, ammunition, and anti-aircraft guns. The corps advanced 48 to 58 kilometers on 6 July and advanced to the area north and south of Senno, where it ran into the lines of the 7th Panzer Division. The corps withdrew east across the Dnieper to the Orsha region, where it received replacement tanks and new attack orders for 11 July.<cr>The corps was subordinated to the 19th Army. The attack in support of 19th Army south of Vitebsk resulted in the loss of a combined 100 tanks from both the 5th and 7th Mechanized Corps. By 14 July, the 14th Tank Division had been encircled and destroyed around Liozno. The corps was encircled in the pocket between Smolensk and Orsha by 15 July.<cr>The corps was reformed between 1 August and 30 September 1943. On 4 October, the corps was loaded onto trains and ten days later arrived at Kharkov. The corps crossed the Dnieper and on 16 October began an attack in the Piatykhatky area. From 24 December, the corps fought in the DnieperCarpathian Offensive and the Kirovograd Offensive.<cr>During March and April 1944, the corps fought in the Uman-Botosani Offensive. In August, the corps fought in the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive. The corps supported the main attack of the 3rd Ukrainian Front on the west bank of the Dniester. During the offensive it crossed the Prut. In early September, the corps fought in the capture of Romania and Bulgaria.<cr>From 29 October, the corps fought in the Budapest Offensive. At the time the corps had a strength of 107 tanks and assault guns. In January, the corps received T-34/85 tanks from the 1st Guards Mechanized Corps. The German relief attempt at Budapest in late January, Operation Konrad III, surprised the corps. Its counterattack was defeated by tanks of the 5th SS Panzer Division Wiking. In the last weeks of the war in Europe, the corps fought in the Prague Offensive.<cr><cr>
translation: 该军于1940年7月8日在莫斯科军区开始组建，由第39和第55轻型坦克旅以及第1摩托化师组成。<cr>6月22日，德国入侵苏联的巴巴罗萨行动开始。当时，该军拥有959辆坦克的实力。该军被命令准备前往前线，并于6月24日接到前往最高统帅部预备队在格扎茨克区集结的命令。经过格扎茨克时，该军收到新指令，要求其集中到维亚兹玛。在前往维亚兹玛的过程中，该军又收到了新的指令，指示其先移动至雅尔采沃，然后是斯摩棱斯克。最终目的地为奥尔沙。<cr>当它投入战斗时，由于机械故障，该军的实力已减少到428辆坦克。该军在没有空中支援的情况下发动攻击，并且燃料、弹药和防空炮短缺。7月6日，该军推进了48至58公里，到达森诺北部和南部地区，在那里遇到了第7装甲师的防线。该军向东撤退越过第聂伯河到奥尔沙地区，在那里获得了替换坦克并收到了新的攻击指令，时间为7月11日。<cr>该军隶属于第19集团军。在支持第19集团军对维捷布斯克南部发动进攻时，来自第5和第7机械化军的合计约100辆坦克被摧毁。到7月14日，第14坦克师已在利亚兹诺地区被包围并消灭。该军于7月15日在斯摩棱斯克与奥尔沙之间的包围圈中被包围。<cr>该军于1943年8月1日至9月30日重建。10月4日，该军登上火车并于十天后抵达哈尔科夫。该军渡过第聂伯河，并于10月16日在皮亚季赫特基地区发起攻击。从12月24日起，该军参加了第聂伯-喀尔巴阡进攻和克里沃罗格进攻。<cr>1944年3月至4月期间，该军参加了乌曼-博托沙尼进攻。8月份，该军参加了雅西-奇西瑙进攻。该军支持了第3乌克兰方面军在德涅斯特河西岸的主要攻击行动，在此次攻势中渡过了普鲁特河。9月初，该军参与了罗马尼亚和保加利亚的占领作战。<cr>从10月29日起，该军参加了布达佩斯进攻。当时该军拥有107辆坦克和突击炮。1月份，该军从第1近卫机械化军接收了T-34/85坦克。德国在1月底对布达佩斯的救援行动“康拉德三号”令该军感到意外。其反击被第5党卫装甲师威克人击败。在欧洲战争最后几周，该军参加了布拉格进攻。<cr><cr>

text:
The 7th Mechanized Division was formed July 1940 from 7th Rifle Division in Kiev Special Military District with:<cr>
27th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
300th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns
23rd Tank Regiment (from 34th Cavalry Division)
1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th Tank Bns
27th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
97th Reconnaissance Battalion
283rd Antitank Battalion
118th Signal Battalion<cr>
The 7th Mechanized Division was formed as part of the 8th Mechanized Corps in the western Ukraine. By 1 October 1940 it was nearly full strength, with over 250 tanks. However, while the bulk of these were BT-5 or BT-7 types, on 22 June 1941 the division had no modern tanks at all, and was still short a great deal of the authorized trucks and tractors.<cr> The 7th Mechanized went into action in the first days of the war, on 26 June 1941. Under continuous German air attack, with only light tanks and lacking artillery support because the guns could not be moved without the never-issued tractors, the division took heavy losses before the end of June.<cr> By mid-July 7th Mechanized Division was effectively a rifle brigade. In August, to replace the destroyed tank regiment, the 7th Mechanized became 7th Rifle Division by adding the 405th Rifle Regiment to the division in early September 1941.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

第七机械化军于1940年7月在基辅特别军事区从第7步兵师组建而成：<cr>

第七机械化军作为第八机械化军的一部分在乌克兰西部组建。到1940年10月1日，该军已接近满编，拥有超过250辆坦克。然而，尽管大部分是BT-5或BT-7型，但在1941年6月22日，该师没有任何现代坦克，并且缺少许多授权的卡车和拖拉机。<cr>第七机械化军在战争的第一天就投入战斗，在1941年6月26日遭受了持续的德国空军攻击。由于只有轻型坦克并且缺乏炮兵支援（因为没有发放的拖拉机无法移动火炮），该师在六月底之前损失惨重。<cr>到7月中旬，第七机械化军实际上已变成一个步兵旅。8月，为了替换被摧毁的坦克团，第七机械化军于1941年9月初通过增加第四零五步兵团成为第7步兵师。<cr><cr>苏联战斗序列第一卷 查尔斯·C·夏普著

text: The 7th Panzer Division was engaged in occupation duties in the Bordeaux region until being sent east in the spring of 1941. It crossed into Russia in June with 14,400 men and fought in the battles of the Minsk Pocket, the Dniepr crossings, Smolensk, and Moscow. It suffered such heavy losses in the winter fighting that it was sent back to France in May 1942 to rest and refit.<cr><cr>Sent to the southern sector of the Russian Front after the fall of Stalingrad,the 7th Panzer defended against heavy Soviet attacks aimed at Rostov in early 1943, and later fought in the Battle of Kharkov. After being repulsed in the Battle of Kursk offensive, the 7th Panzer fought in the battles around Kiev and Zhitomir, where it was twice cited for distinguished conduct. In November, the division took heavy casualties in the Kiev withdrawal and fought in the Tarnopol area until March 1944, when it was overrun and the 1st Panzer Army encircled. The remnants of the division broke out, but its losses were ruinous. The division was reduced to a strength of 1,872 men, nine guns, eleven anti-tank guns, and nine tanks. The 7th Panzer nevertheless fought on and opposed the Russian summer offensive of 1944 as a part of Army Group Center, fighting at Minsk, Lida and Memel. Escaping disaster yet again, it was again officially cited for distinguished conduct in August 1944, for its action in the Battle of Raseiniai in Lithuania. It was heavily engaged when the Russian winter offensive of 1944-45 hit the Vistula and was trapped in Danzig as part of Army Group North in early 1945. Evacuated by sea, but without any vehicles or tanks, the 7th Panzer took part in the Battle of Berlin in April 1945. Most of its men managed to escape to Allied lines and surrendered to the British at Schwerin, Schleswig-Holstein, on May 3, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第7装甲师在1941年春季之前一直在波尔多地区执行占领任务。该师于6月进入俄罗斯，共有14,400人，并参加了明斯克包围圈、第聂伯河渡口、斯摩棱斯克和莫斯科的战斗。由于冬季作战中损失惨重，它在1942年5月被送回法国休整和整补。<cr>指挥官报告：<cr> <cr>第七装甲师在斯大林格勒陷落后被调往俄罗斯方面军南部战区，在1943年初抵御了苏联对罗斯托夫的猛烈进攻，并参加了哈尔科夫战役。在库尔斯克攻势中遭到击退后，该师又参与了基辅和日托米尔周边的战斗，其中两次因卓越表现而受到表彰。11月，第七装甲师在基辅撤退中遭受重大伤亡，在塔尔诺波尔地区作战至1944年3月，此时被包围，第一装甲集团军也被合围。该师残部突围而出，但损失惨重。其兵力缩减为1872人、九门火炮、十一门反坦克炮和九辆坦克。尽管如此，第七装甲师继续作战，并作为中央集团军群的一部分参加了1944年夏季攻势，在明斯克、利达和梅梅尔地区作战。该师再次因在立陶宛拉塞尼艾战役中的表现而于1944年8月被正式表彰。当苏联冬季攻势于1944-45年袭击维斯杜拉河时，第七装甲师作为北方集团军群的一部分被困在但泽。通过海上撤离，但没有车辆和坦克，该师参加了1945年4月的柏林战役。大多数士兵成功逃至盟军战线，并于1945年5月3日在石勒苏益格-荷尔斯泰因州的施维林向英军投降。<cr> 德国战斗序列 第三卷 - 二战中的装甲师、装甲掷弹兵师和武装党卫军师，塞缪尔·W·米查姆少校

text: Part of the Southern Front at the outbreak of the war, it consisted of the 116th, 196th and 206th Rifle Divisions. It was dissolved in August of 1941. The corps was reformed in September 1942 as part of the 64th Army and consisted of the 93rd, 96th and 97th Separate Rifle Brigades. It fought in the Battle of Stalingrad and was redesignated 35th Guards Rifle Corps for its performance in that battle. The corps was reestablished in June 1943 as part of the 3rd Shock Army and consisted of the 146th, 265th and 364th Rifle Divisions. It fought in the Battle of Berlin.<cr><cr> Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 作为战争初期南方方面军的一部分，它由第116步兵师、第196步兵师和第206步兵师组成。该军于1941年8月解散。1942年9月，作为第64集团军的一部分重新组建，包括第93独立步兵旅、第96独立步兵旅和第97独立步兵旅。它参加了斯大林格勒战役，并因在该战役中的表现被改称为第35近卫步兵军。1943年6月，作为第3突击集团军的一部分重新建立，包括第146步兵师、第265步兵师和第364步兵师。它参加了柏林战役。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军战斗序列在伟大卫国战争中的演变, Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 7th Rifle Division was originally formed in September 1918. The division was reformed in August 1939 at Poltava as part of the Kiev Special Military District. It consisted of the 27th, 257th and 300th Rifle Regiments, 23rd Reconnaissance Battalion, the 405th Separate Tank Battalion and various support units. The division then took part in the Soviet invasion of Poland. In January of 1940 the division was sent to fight in the war with Finland. It returned to the Kiev Special Military District in April 1940. It took part in the Soviet occupaton of Romanian Bessarabia and Nothern Bukovina in June and July 1940.<cr>In August 1940 the division was reformed as the 7th Motorized Division. The division, assigned to the Southwestern Front was decimated at the start of Operation.Barbarossa. It was reformed in December 1941 from remnants of the 22nd Estonian Territorial Rifle Corps and in 1942 officially became an Estonian national formation. At the end of 1942 the division participated in the Battle of Velikiye Luki. In September 1944 the division helped liberate Tallinn.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第7步兵师最初成立于1918年9月。该师于1939年8月在波尔塔瓦重组，成为基辅特别军区的一部分。它由第27、257和300步兵团、第23侦察营、第405独立坦克营以及各种支援单位组成。随后参加了苏联入侵波兰的行动。1940年1月，该师被派往与芬兰作战。1940年4月返回基辅特别军区。<cr>1940年8月，该师重组为第7摩托化师。该师被分配到西南方面军，在巴巴罗萨行动初期遭到重创。1941年12月，该师由残余的第22爱沙尼亚地方步兵军重建，并于1942年正式成为一支爱沙尼亚民族部队。<cr>1942年底，该师参加了维捷布斯克战役。1944年9月，该师帮助解放了塔林。

text: The 7th Romanian Cavalry Brigade was attached to the Romanian III Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. As with most Romanian units it was withdrawn to Romania after the Siege of Odessa. In March of 1942 it was reorganized as the 7th Romanian Cavalry Division. At the start of the Battle of Stalingrad it was in reserve with the Romanian 3rd Army. The division was heavily involved in the fighting and retreated in good order being awarded 28 Iron Crosses by Germany for its actions. In March of 1943 it was merged with the Romanian 1st Cavalry Division.<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第7罗马尼亚骑兵旅在巴巴罗萨行动开始时隶属于罗马尼亚第三军。与其他大多数罗马尼亚部队一样，它在敖德萨围城战后被撤回罗马尼亚。1942年3月，该部重组为第7罗马尼亚骑兵师。在斯大林格勒战役初期，它作为预备队与罗马尼亚第三集团军一同行动。该师在战斗中发挥了重要作用，并有秩序地撤退，德国授予其成员28枚铁十字勋章以表彰其表现。1943年3月，该师与罗马尼亚第一骑兵师合并。<cr>词条由 Chris Munson 提供

text: The 7th Romanian Infantry Division was attached to the Mountain Romanian Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. It subsequently participated in the 73 day Siege of Odessa. The division was withdrawn back to Romania after the capture of Odessa. In October of 1942 it was sent to the Stalino region for Fall Blau. Along with the rest of the I Romanian Corps it was surrounded during the Battle of Stalingrad and largely destroyed. The survivors marched the 1800 km home on foot. It participated in the defense of Romania in 1944 and was absorbed into the Romanian 6th Infantry Division in November of 1944.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第7罗马尼亚步兵师在巴巴罗萨行动初期隶属于山地罗马尼亚军。随后参加了敖德萨长达73天的围城战。占领敖德萨后，该师被撤回罗马尼亚。1942年10月，它被派往斯塔利诺地区参加蓝色行动。与第1罗马尼亚军其他部队一起，在斯大林格勒战役中被包围并大部分被消灭。幸存者徒步跋涉1800公里返回家园。该师参加了1944年的罗马尼亚防御战，并于同年11月被合并到第6罗马尼亚步兵师。<cr>资料提供：克里斯·芒森<cr>

text:
The 7th Tank Corps was formed April-May 1942 from Kalinin Front reserves and with: <cr>3rd Guards Tank Brigade
1st Tank Battalion (21 KVs)
2nd Tank Battalion (T-34s and T-60s)
3rd Guards Motorized Rifle Battalion
Antiaircraft Battalion (12 37mm guns)
62nd Tank Brigade
27th, 164th Tank Battalions
62nd Motorized Rifle Battalion
87th Tank Brigade
167th, 168th Tank Battalions
Each Bn: 5 KVs, 10 T-34S, 8 T-60S
87th Motorized Rifle Battalion
7th Motorized Rifle Brigade
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Battalions
Artillery Battalion (12 76mm guns)
Antiaircraft Battery (4 37mm guns)
Submachine Gun Company (80 men) <cr>The 7th Tank Corps was shifted south to join 5th Tank Army on 5 July 1942, and in its first combat action got chewed up in the uncoordinated Soviet counterattacks around Voronezh. The corps was withdrawn into Bryansk Front reserves by the end of the month, and then sent south with 1st Guards Army. It took part in another series of disastrous Soviet attacks, this time north of Stalingrad in September and early October. The corps went back into Volga Military District in late October and was re-equipped so that on 16 December when it went, back into action with 2nd Guards Army, the corps had 20 KV, 41 T-34, and 31 T-70 tanks. 7th Tank Corps and its commander, Major General Pavel
Rotmistrov, so distinguished themselves in the fighting around Kotelnikovo in December, that Rotmistrov was promoted to Lieutenant General and awarded the Order of Suvorov, while the 7th Tank Corps, on 29 December 1942, became 3rd Guards Tank Corps with the honorific title: 'Kotelnikoskikh.'<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp

冲锋枪连（80人）<cr>第7坦克军于1942年7月5日被调往南方，加入第5坦克集团军，在其首次战斗行动中，在沃罗涅日周边的不协调苏军反击战中损失惨重。该军在月底撤至布良斯克方面军预备队，并随后与第1近卫集团军一同南下。它参与了另一次灾难性的苏军攻势，这次是在9月和10月初斯大林格勒以北地区。该军于10月下旬返回伏尔加河军区并重新装备，因此在12月16日再次投入战斗时（与第2近卫集团军一同），该军拥有20辆KV、41辆T-34和31辆T-70坦克。第7坦克军及其指挥官帕维尔少将罗特米斯特罗夫，在12月科捷利尼科沃周边的战斗中表现出色，以至于罗特米斯特罗夫被晋升为中将军衔并授予苏沃洛夫勋章，而第7坦克军则于1942年12月29日成为第3近卫坦克军，并获得荣誉称号：“科捷利尼科沃”。<cr><cr>查尔斯·C·夏普《二战苏联战斗序列》第二卷

text:
The 7th Tank Division was formed in July 1940 in Western Special Military District as part of 6th Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
13th Tank Regiment
1st Tank Bn - 25 KV tanks
2nd, 3rd Tank Bns - each 50 T-34s
4th Tank Bn - light tanks<cr>14th Tank Regiment
1st Tank Bn - 25 KV tanks
2nd Tank Bn - 50 T-34s
3rd Tank Bn - 52 BT tanks
4th Tank Bn - light tanks
7th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
7th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1 light, 1 medium bn
7th Reconnaissance Battalion
7th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
7th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>Like 4th Tank Division in the same corps, this was one of the bestequipped units in the Red Army by June 1941; its fate shows graphically how
little equipment on hand can contribute to combat effectiveness when everything else is missing. By 1 June the division had 51 KVs, 150 T-34s, 125 BT-5 or BT-7, and 42 T-26 tanks, and was at virtually full strength in artillery, armored cars, mortars, antiaircraft weapons, and personnel. On paper, it was a very powerful armored force.<cr>In reality, the division did not have a single round of 76mm armor-piercing ammunition on hand, so the 201 modern tanks were almost useless against German armor. In addition, the division had only enough diesel fuel to fill up its vehicles one time. and once the 10th Army fuel depot in Bialystok was destroyed by bombing, as it was on 22 June, no one in the division knew where any other fuel depots were located! By 28 June the division commander was killed in action, the rifle regiment separated and overrun without support, the artillery and heavy weapons immobilized for lack of working tractors, and most of the tanks abandoned for lack of fuel. The 7th Tank Division disappeared from the Soviet order of battle before 1 July - less than 9 days after the war started.<cr>German officers who interrogated prisoners from 6th Mechanized Corps in July 1941 remarked on the fact that both 4th and 7th Tank Divisions were better equipped in heavy and medium tanks and artillery than any panzer division in 1941. The fact that both divisions were destroyed in a few days, without doing any comparable damage to the enemy, shows how difficult it is for even a relatively well-equipped armored force to go from a peacetime environment to full-scale battle, on no notice, with poorly trained officers and men, and no support.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

第7坦克师于1940年7月在西部特别军区组建，隶属于第6机械化军。1941年6月22日编入：
第13坦克团
第1坦克营 - 25辆KV坦克
第2、第3坦克营 - 每个各50辆T-34坦克
第4坦克营 - 轻型坦克<cr>
第14坦克团
第1坦克营 - 25辆KV坦克
第2坦克营 - 50辆T-34坦克
第3坦克营 - 52辆BT快速坦克
第4坦克营 - 轻型坦克
第7摩托化步兵团
第1、第2、第3营
第7摩托化榴弹炮团
轻型和中型营各一个
第7侦察营
第7摩托化浮桥营
第7防空营<cr>
如同同军区的第4坦克师，这是在1941年6月之前红军装备最好的单位之一；它的命运生动地说明了当其他方面都缺乏时，手头拥有的少量装备如何无法贡献于战斗力。到6月1日，该师拥有51辆KV坦克、150辆T-34坦克、125辆BT-5或BT-7快速坦克和42辆T-26坦克，并且在炮兵、装甲车、迫击炮、高射炮武器以及人员方面几乎满编。纸面上，它是一支非常强大的装甲部队。<cr> <cr> <cr>实际上，该师没有一枚76毫米穿甲弹药，因此这201辆现代坦克几乎无法对抗德国装甲部队。此外，该师仅拥有足够的柴油燃料为其车辆加注一次。一旦第10集团军在比亚韦斯托克的燃料补给站于6月22日被轰炸摧毁，没有人知道其他燃料补给站的位置！到6月28日，师长阵亡，步兵团失去支援后被击溃，炮兵和重武器因缺乏可用拖拉机而无法移动，大多数坦克也因为缺油而被遗弃。第7坦克师在1941年7月1日前就从苏联战斗序列中消失——开战不到9天。

德国军官于1941年7月审讯第六机械化军的战俘时指出，第四和第七坦克师装备重型和中型坦克及炮兵的数量比1941年的任何装甲师都要多。这两个师在几天内就被摧毁，并未对敌人造成相当程度的破坏，这表明即使是相对装备较好的装甲部队，在没有任何预警的情况下从和平时期环境转入全面战斗是多么困难，尤其是在军官和士兵训练不足且缺乏支援的情况下。

苏联战斗序列第一卷 作者：查尔斯·C·夏普

text:
The 80th Guards Rifle Division was formed on 1 March 1943 from the second formation of the 298th Rifle Division in honor of the 'exemplary fulfillment of combat missions' of the latter during the Battle of Stalingrad. The 886th, 888th, and 892nd Rifle Regiments became the 217th Guards, the 230th Guards, and the 232nd Guards, respectively; the 828th Artillery Regiment became the 171st Guards, and the rest of the division's units also became Guards units. The division remained in reserve, receiving reinforcements and reequipping, until early August, when it joined the 4th Guards Army, concentrated in the forests southwest of Stary Oskol. Between 8 and 13 August the 80th Guards moved forward to the front line at Grayvoron. In a period of two and a half months, the division marched around 1,000 kilometers (620 mi) at night. Joining the Voronezh Front, the 4th Guards Army was concentrated 20 kilometers (12 mi) east of Akhtyrka. During the Battle of the Dnieper, the troops of the front broke through the German lines at Akhtyrka and crossed the Vorskla River at Kuzmino. The army's 68th Guards Rifle Division captured Mikhailovka. After being pushed back, the German troops held positions on the line of Bilsk on the Kotelevka River, but began retreating on 22 September. In two days, the 80th Guards advanced 50 kilometers (31 mi) against the German rear guard, reaching positions west of Poltava.

In early October, the division, along with the rest of 21st Guards Rifle Corps, began crossing the Dnieper. The 80th Guards, under the command of Colonel A.E. Yakovlev, were tasked with the main crossing on the night of 5-6 October. The first to cross the river were soldiers of Colonel Pyotr Kamishnikov's 230th Guards Rifle Regiment's 3rd Battalion, under the command of Captain Nikolay Zaryanov. At 20:00 hours on 5 October, a submachine gun company led by Lieutenant Alexey Priglebov launched its boats from Koldovoy Island. The crossing was met by a hail of German fire, but the battalion managed to establish a bridgehead on the opposite bank. The bridgehead was reinforced and expanded despite multiple German counterattacks by the rest of the division; Zaryanov and Priglebov were made Heroes of the Soviet Union for their actions. By the morning of 6 October, the entire 230th Regiment was across the river, and the division continued its westward advance.

The division fought in the Korsun-Shevchenkovsky Offensive, encircling a German pocket, in January and February 1944. In the spring it helped capture Zvenigorodka, and on 5 March attacked at Olkhovets during the Uman-Boto?ani Offensive, advancing through the mud of the spring rasputitsa. The division, alongside the rest of the army, opened a 35-kilometer (22 mi) penetration in the Axis line, and advanced west.<cr><cr>
translation:
第80近卫步兵师于1943年3月1日由第二组建的第298步兵师改编而成，以表彰后者在斯大林格勒战役中“出色完成战斗任务”。第886、888和892步兵团分别改组为第217近卫团、第230近卫团和第232近卫团；第828炮兵团则改编为第171近卫炮兵团，其余部队也均被授予“近卫”称号。该师一直作为预备队接受增援和重新装备，直到8月初加入第四近卫集团军，在斯塔里奥斯科尔西南部的森林中集结。从8月8日至13日，第80近卫步兵师前进至格拉沃龙前线。在两个半月的时间里，该师夜间行军约1,000公里（620英里）。加入沃罗涅日方面军后，第四近卫集团军集结于阿赫捷尔卡以东20公里处。在第聂伯河战役中，前线部队突破了德国人在阿赫捷尔卡的防线，并在库兹明诺渡过了沃尔斯克拉河。该集团军的第68近卫步兵师占领了米哈伊洛夫卡。被击退后，德军部队坚守科特列夫卡河西岸比尔斯克线上的阵地，但于9月22日开始撤退。两天内，第80近卫步兵师推进50公里（31英里），突破德国后卫防线，抵达波尔塔瓦以西的阵地。

10月初，该师与第21近卫步兵军一起开始渡过第聂伯河。80近卫师在亚历山大·伊万诺维奇·雅科夫列夫上校的指挥下负责主渡口，并于10月5日至6日夜间展开行动。率先渡河的是彼得·卡米什尼科夫上校指挥下的230近卫步兵师第3团，该团由尼古拉·扎里亚诺夫中校领导。10月5日晚8时，亚历山大·普利格洛博夫少尉带领的一个轻机枪连从科尔多沃伊岛出发划船过河。尽管遭遇德军猛烈的火力阻击，该团还是在对岸建立了桥头堡。扎里亚诺夫和普利格洛博夫因他们的英勇行为被授予苏联英雄称号。到10月6日清晨，整个230步兵师都渡过了第聂伯河，该师继续向西推进。

该师参加了1944年1月至2月的科韦利-舍甫琴柯夫斯基进攻，包围了德军的一个包围圈。春季时协助占领了兹韦尼哥罗德卡，并于3月5日在乌曼-巴托西纳攻势期间在奥尔霍维采发动攻击，在春季泥泞期中艰难推进。该师与整个集团军一起，在轴心国阵线上开辟了一个35公里（22英里）的突破口，并向西推进。<cr><cr>

506th Antiaircraft Battery (from 20 April 1943)<cr><cr>The 81st Guards continued a record of distinguished service through the rest of the war.<cr><cr>

The 81st Mechanized Division became part of 4th Mechanized Corps in July 1940, and from then on priority for armor went to the tank divisions in that Corps. Although nearly full strength in artillery and personnel, and reasonably well-trained by Soviet peacetime standards, 81st Mechanized Division only had about 65 working BT or T-26 light tanks on 22 June 1941.<cr>
Fighting under 4th Mechanized Corps HQ, 81st Mechanized frequently had one or both of its motorized rifle regiments detached to support the tanks in the corps' tank divisions or other rifle units in Southwestern Front. In August, 81st Mechanized Division was redesignated as 81st Rifle Division.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

text:
The 82nd Guards Rifle Division was formed from a cadre of the 321st Rifle Division, in recognition of that division's steadfast qualities in the encirclement and siege of the German Sixth Army in the Battle of Stalingrad, and in particular its pursuit of the defeated Axis forces from the Caucasus region.

The division formed up in 62nd Army as that army was being reformed as the 8th Guards Army in the spring of 1943. The 82nd was one of the first units assigned to the new 29th Guards Rifle Corps, and, remarkably, remained under these two commands for the duration of the war and into the postwar era. 8th Guards Army was originally assigned to Southwestern Front. 

During the Battle of the Dnieper, 8th Guards Army closed on the city of Zaporozhye, famous before the war for its hydro-electric dams. The Front's first attack on Oct. 10 made few gains, but a following night attack on the 13th, supported by a massive artillery bombardment, forced the Germans to abandon the city the next day. In recognition of its role in this success, the men and women of the 82nd Guards were awarded the city's name as an honorific.

As the Dnieper-Carpathian Offensive continued, in early April 1944, 8th Guards Army was advancing through difficult conditions towards the city of Odessa. On Apr. 10, that city was liberated by a three-pronged attack by 8th Guards, 6th and 5th Shock Armies. Following this, 8th Guards advanced to the estuary of the Dniestr River by the 13th. This was a dead end, and in early May, during the First Jassy-Kishinev Offensive, the army was ordered up the east bank of the river to relieve 5th Guards Army in the bridgehead it held at Tashlyk. This relief occurred over the nights of May 5, 6 and 7. The 82nd Guards did not enter the bridgehead immediately, but remained with its corps holding the east bank between Tashlyk and Grigoriopol. All this activity was not missed by the Germans, and very early on May 10 their XXXX Panzer Corps launched a powerful attack to drive in the bridgehead. Over the next three days this assault drove the bridgehead back until it was about 11km wide but only 1 - 3km deep. On the morning of May 14 the division entered the bridgehead and relieved the 39th Guards Rifle Division, helping to stabilize the situation. Due to this setback, among others, the Soviet offensive was halted, and would not resume until August.

The final offensive on the German capital began on April 20. The units of 8th Guards Army were tasked with seizing the Seelow Heights on the west bank of the Oder. When the fighting ended, the men and women of the 82nd Guards had earned the full title: 82nd Guards Rifle, Zaparozhye, Order of the Red Banner, Order of Bogdan Khmelnitsky, Division.<cr><cr>
translation:
第82近卫步兵师是由第321步兵师的部分骨干组建而成，以表彰该师在斯大林格勒战役中对德国第六集团军的包围和围攻时表现出的坚定品质，特别是在从高加索地区追击失败的轴心国部队方面的贡献。

该师于1943年春天在第62集团军重组为第8近卫集团军的过程中组建。第82师是最早被分配到新成立的第29近卫步兵军的部队之一，并且令人惊讶的是，它在整个战争期间以及战后时期都一直隶属于这两个指挥机构。第8近卫集团军最初被分配给西南方面军。 

在第聂伯河战役期间，第8近卫集团军逼近了泽佩罗日市，在战争爆发前这里以水力发电站而闻名。方面军的首次攻击于10月10日展开，但进展不大，但在13日晚上发动的一次夜袭，并得到了大规模炮兵炮击的支持，迫使德军在第二天放弃了该城市。为了表彰其在这场胜利中的作用，第82近卫师的官兵被授予“泽佩罗日”荣誉称号。

随着第聂伯河-喀尔巴阡山脉攻势的持续，1944年4月初，第8近卫集团军在恶劣条件下向敖德萨市推进。4月10日，该城市由第8近卫、第6和第5突击集团军三路夹击解放。随后，在13日前后，第8近卫集团军推进至德涅斯特河口。然而这是一条死胡同，5月初，在第一次雅西-奇西瑙攻势期间，该集团军被命令沿河东岸向塔什利克桥头堡的第5近卫集团军提供支援。这一行动发生在5月5日至7日夜间。第82近卫师并未立即进入桥头堡，而是留在其所属装甲军内，在塔什利克和格里戈罗波尔之间守卫东岸。

这一切活动没有逃过德军的注意，5月10日凌晨，德国XXXX装甲军发动强大攻势试图摧毁该桥头堡。接下来三天中，这一突击将桥头堡压缩至约宽11公里但纵深仅1-3公里。5月14日清晨，师级部队进入桥头堡并替换第39近卫步兵师，帮助稳定了局势。

由于这次挫折以及其他因素，苏联攻势被迫停止，并直到8月份才重新发起。

4月20日，进攻德国首都的最后攻势开始。第8近卫集团军的任务是占领奥得河西岸的塞洛高地。战斗结束后，第82近卫步兵师获得了完整的荣誉称号：第82近卫红旗扎波罗热博格丹·赫梅利尼茨基勋章步兵师。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The 82nd Rifle Corpsc was formed as part of the 34th Army of the Northwestern Front on 15 July 1943 under the command of Major General Pavel Kuznetsov, who led it for the rest of the war. It initially existed as a headquarters without assigned troops, and transferred to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command in August with the 1st and 10th Guards Airborne Divisions. In September it was transferred to the 37th Army of the Steppe Front (the 2nd Ukrainian Front from 20 October), being reinforced by the 188th Rifle Division. The corps fought in the capture of Left-bank Ukraine east of Kremenchuk, then crossed the Dnieper and captured a bridgehead northwest of Mishurin Rog during the Battle of the Dnieper. Between October and December it attacked towards Krivoi Rog. The 1st Guards Airborne was replaced by the 89th Guards Rifle Division in October, and the latter was replaced by the 28th Guards Rifle Division the following month. The 15th Guards Rifle Division replaced the 10th Guards Airborne in January 1944.<cr>Transferred to the 3rd Ukrainian Front with the army in mid-January, the corps fought in the advance into Right-bank Ukraine during the Dnieper-Carpathian Offensive, participating in the Nikopol-Krivoi Rog Offensive, the Bereznegovatoye-Snigirevka Offensive, and the Odessa Offensive. In these operations it advanced 350 kilometers, crossing the Inhulets, Inhul, Southern Bug, and Dniester while helping to capture the cities of Krivoi Rog, Voznesensk, and Tiraspol. The 10th Guards Airborne briefly returned to the corps in February and the 15th Guards left it in March. The 10th Guards Airborne was replaced by the 92nd Guards Rifle Division in April; the corps would include the 28th and 92nd Guards and the 188th for the rest of the war. The 82nd fought in the Jassy-Kishinev Offensive and the advance into Bulgaria in August. This was its last combat action, as it spent the rest of the war on garrison duty in Bulgaria.<cr><cr>
translation: 第82步兵军于1943年7月15日在西北方面军的第34集团军内组建，由少将帕维尔·库兹涅佐夫指挥，他一直带领该部队到战争结束。最初它只是一个没有分配部队的司令部，并在8月份与第1空降师和第10近卫空降师一起被转移到最高统帅部预备队。9月，该军转隶至顿斯克方面军（从10月20日起为第2乌克兰方面军），得到了第188步兵师的增援。该军参与了左岸乌克兰地区克雷门丘格以东地区的占领行动，并在第聂伯河战役期间渡过第聂伯河，夺取了米舒林罗格西北方向的一个桥头堡。从10月到12月，它向克里沃伊罗格发动进攻。第1近卫空降师于10月份被第89近卫步兵师替换，后者又在次月被第28近卫步兵师替换。第15近卫步兵师于1944年1月取代了第10近卫空降师。<cr>1月上旬调至第3方面军，该军参加了第聂伯河-喀尔巴阡山脉进攻战役中的右岸乌克兰攻势，并参与了尼科波尔-克里沃罗格攻势、别列任戈瓦特耶-斯尼吉雷夫卡攻势和敖德萨攻势。在这些行动中，它推进了350公里，跨越了因胡莱茨河、因胡尔河、南布格河和德涅斯特河，并帮助占领了克里沃罗格、沃兹涅先斯克和提拉斯波尔等城市。第10近卫空降军于2月短暂返回该军，而第15近卫步兵师则在3月离开。第10近卫空降军被第92近卫步兵师取代；该军在战争剩余时间里包括了第28、第92和第188近卫步兵师。第82军参加了雅西-奇西瑙攻势以及8月进入保加利亚的进攻行动。这是它的最后一次作战行动，因为该军余下的战争时间都在保加利亚执行守备任务。<cr><cr>

text: The 82nd Rifle Division was established Perm in 1932. Sent to Far East, returned for Moscow counter-attack in Dec 1941. Was a motorized division until Mar 1942. Became 3rd Guards Motor Rifle Division in Mar 1942 which later became the 6th Guards Mechanized Corps (and finally 90th Guards Tank Division). Recreated Jul 1942. Fought in Poland 1945. With 47th Army of the 1st Belorussian Front May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 第82步兵师成立于1932年的 Perm。后被派往远东，于1941年12月返回参与莫斯科反攻。该师直到1942年3月都是摩托化师。1942年3月改名为第3近卫摩托化步兵师，后来成为第6近卫机械化军（最终改编为第90近卫坦克师）。于1942年7月重建。1945年在波兰作战，在1945年5月隶属于第一白俄罗斯方面军的第47集团军。<cr>指挥官报告：<cr><cr>

text:
The 83rd Rifle Division began forming on 11 February 1944 from the 61st and 85th Naval Rifle Brigades as part of the 31st Rifle Corps of the 26th Army of the Karelian Front, in accordance with an order of the 26th Army from 9 February. The division included the 11th, 26th, and 46th Rifle Regiments, the 588th Artillery Regiment, and smaller support units. The 1st and 3rd Separate Rifle Battalions of the 61st Brigade were used to form the 11th Rifle Regiment, the 2nd and 3rd Separate Rifle Battalions of the 85th Brigade were used to form the 26th Rifle Regiment, and the 2nd Separate Rifle Battalion of the 61st Brigade and 1st Separate Rifle Battalion of the 85th Brigade were used to form the 46th Rifle Regiment. The 588th Artillery Regiment was formed from the two batteries of 76 mm divisional guns included in each brigade. Lieutenant Colonel Aleksey Mikhailovich Alekseyev, the commander of the 61st Brigade, became division commander.

From 14 February, the 26th Rifle Regiment defended the previous positions of the 85th Brigade to the northwest of Lake Bolshoye Severnoye, between Ozero Nizhneye and Ozero Verkhneye Chernoye, opposite the German 6th SS Mountain Division Nord, which held positions to the north of Kestenga. To the south was the 205th Rifle Division on the southern shore of Ozero Verkhneye Chernoye, while to its north there were no Soviet troops for more than a hundred kilometers. The 83rd was the northernmost unit in its corps and army. The 1st Rifle Battalion of the 46th Rifle Regiment moved up on the right flank of the 26th Rifle Regiment on 16 February. There was little action during this period, besides a near-daily mortar barrage by the 26th Rifle Regiment against the opposing German positions, sporadic exchanges of machine gun fire, and the uneventful sending out of reconnaissance patrols.

During the night of 19-20 February, the 11th relieved the 26th and the 1st Battalion of the 46th on the defensive line. On the morning of 25 February three rifle companies of the 11th advanced to a line in direct contact with the opposing German troops, 150 to 200 meters away from the positions of the latter. The advance was conducted under sporadic rifle and machine gun fire, and German artillery and mortar fire at 08:00 wounded two soldiers of the regiment. A squad of 11 riflemen and anti-tank riflemen sent out on reconnaissance in front of the advanced positions at 17:00 were cut off by a German platoon and went missing. At 21:00 on 27 February the 11th lost one killed and two wounded to German artillery fire.

On 14 November the division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner in recognition of its part in the taking of the town of Nikel and the surrounding.<cr><cr>
translation:
第83步兵师开始于1944年2月11日组建，由第61海军步兵旅和第85海军步兵旅的部分部队组成，隶属于卡累利阿方面军的第26集团军下的第31步兵军。根据第26集团军在2月9日下达的命令进行编组。该师包括第11、第26和第46步兵团以及第588炮兵团和其他较小的支持单位。第61旅中的第1和第3独立步兵营被用来组建第11步兵团，第85旅中的第2和第3独立步兵营被用来组建第26步兵团，而第61旅的第2独立步兵营与第85旅的第1独立步兵营则用于组建第46步兵团。第588炮兵团由每个旅中包含的两门76毫米团属火炮编成。第61旅指挥官上校亚历山大·米哈伊洛维奇·阿列克谢耶夫成为该师指挥官。

从2月14日起，第26步兵团在博洛舍特诺耶湖西北方向的前85旅阵地进行防御，在尼日涅湖和切尔诺韦尔赫涅湖之间，面对北方集团军群的第6党卫山地师。南方是位于切尔诺韦尔赫涅湖南岸的第205步兵师，而在其北面超过一百公里内没有苏军部队。第83团是它所在军和集团军最北端的单位。2月16日，第46步兵团第1营从右翼增援了第26步兵团。在此期间几乎没有战斗行动，除了第26步兵团几乎每天对德军阵地进行迫击炮齐射、机枪零星交火以及无事发生的侦察巡逻派出任务。

2月19日至20日夜间，第11步兵师接替了第26步兵师和第46团第一营的防御阵地。2月25日上午，第11步兵师的三个步兵连推进到距离对面德国部队约150至200米的一线。此次推进在零星的步枪和机枪火力下进行，并且德军炮兵和迫击炮于8:00造成两名士兵受伤。17:00时，一支由11名步兵和反坦克步兵组成的侦察队从前沿阵地派出，在被一个德国班切断后失踪。2月27日21:00，第11步兵师因德军炮火损失一名阵亡、两名受伤。

11月14日，该师因参与夺取尼켈镇及其周边地区而被授予红旗勋章。<cr><cr>

The 84th Mechanized Division was formed April - July 1940 from 84th Rifle Division at Tula in Moscow Military District with:<cr>

1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Bns

The 84th Rifle Division was moved from Tula in Moscow Military District to west of Minsk in July 1940 to become part of 3rd Mechanized Corps. When Lithuania became part of the Soviet Union in late 1940, 84th Mechanized Division moved to Vilnius, where it was stationed until the Germans attacked on 22 June 1941. 84th Mechanized Division had almost a full complement of tanks on that date, but most of its 200 armored vehicles were old T-26 tanks, a type that had the worst reliability rate of any in the Soviet prewar arsenal.<cr>
3rd Mechanized Corps was directly in front of 4th Panzer group's strike to the Southern Dvinia River, and was quickly smashed. By early July 84th Mechanized, effectively a weak rifle brigade, was under 27th Army command. By mid-July the division was officially redesignated 84th Rifle Division by redesignating the 41st as a rifle regiment.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

第84步兵师于1940年7月从图拉的莫斯科军区转移到明斯克以西，成为第3机械化军的一部分。当立陶宛在1940年末并入苏联后，第84机械化军移至维尔纽斯，并驻扎到德国于1941年6月22日发动攻击为止。该日期时，第84机械化军几乎拥有完整的坦克编制，但其约200辆装甲车辆中大多数是老旧的T-26坦克，这种类型的坦克在苏联战前装备中最不可靠。<cr>

第3机械化军直接位于第4装甲集团军向南德维纳河进攻路线之前，并迅速被击溃。到7月初，实际上已成为弱步兵旅的第84机械化军由第27集团军指挥。到7月中旬，该师正式重新命名为第84步兵师，通过将第41坦克团改编为步兵团来实现。<cr><cr>苏联战斗序列第一卷 查尔斯·C·夏普

text:
After heavy and bloody battles on the Neman river, the 84th Motorized Division suffered heavy losses and was reorganized into the 84th Rifle Division in mid-July 1940.

In August, the 84th was withdrawn for reorganization in Valday. From September, the division, assigned to the 11th and then the 34th Army of the Northwestern Front, defended Valday, then fought in the Demyansk Offensive. In late August 1942, the division was sent to the Stalingrad Front. As part of the 4th Tank Army and then the 66th Army from October, it fought in continuous defensive battles, preventing Axis forces from breaking through to Stalingrad. From November, as part of the 24th Army of the Don Front, the division fought in the encirclement and destruction of the German troops in Stalingrad in Operation Operation Koltso.

In April 1943, after the end of the latter, the division was relocated to the area of Voronezh for rebuilding. As part of the 53rd and 5th Guards 5th Guards Armies of the Steppe Front (the 2nd Ukrainian Front from October 1943), the division fought in the Battle of Kursk, the Battle of the Dnieper, the Kirovograd Offensive, the Korsun-Shevchenkovsky Offensive, and the Jassy-Kinishev Offensive. The division received the name of Kharkov as an honorific on 23 August 1943 for its actions in the capture of that city and the Order of the Red Banner a month later. In late 1944, the division as part of the 20th Guards Rifle Corps of the 4th Guards Army was withdrawn to the Reserve of the Supreme High Command, and in November joined the 3rd Ukrainian Front to participate in the Budapest Offensive. In the last weeks of the war the division fought in the Vienna Offensive.<cr><cr>
translation:
经过涅曼河畔的激烈战斗，第84摩托化师在1940年7月中旬遭受重大损失并重组为第84步兵师。

8月，该师被撤至瓦尔代进行重组。从9月开始，该师先后隶属于西北方面军的第11集团军和第34集团军，在瓦尔代地区防御作战，随后参加了德梅扬斯克攻势。1942年8月底，该师被调往斯大林格勒方面军。作为第四坦克集团军的一部分，从10月起隶属于第六十六集团军，参与了持续的防御战斗，阻止轴心国部队突破至斯大林格勒。自11月起，作为顿河方面军第二十四集团军的一部分，该师参加了围歼德军在斯大林格勒的“科特索”行动。

1943年4月，在后者结束后，该师被调往沃罗涅日地区重建。作为草原方面军（从1943年10月起为第二乌克兰方面军）第五十三集团军和第五近卫集团军的一部分，该师参加了库尔斯克会战、第聂伯河战役、基洛夫格勒攻势、科尔松-舍甫琴科夫斯基攻势以及雅西-奇西瑙攻势。由于在夺取哈尔科夫城中的表现，该师于1943年8月23日获得“哈尔科夫”荣誉称号，并一个月后被授予红旗勋章。1944年底，作为第四近卫集团军第二十近卫步兵军的一部分，该师被调至最高统帅部预备队，并在11月加入第三乌克兰方面军参与布达佩斯攻势。战争最后几周，该师参加了维也纳攻势。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>第84摩托化师<cr>1940年7月中旬重组为步兵师<cr>1942年8月底调往斯大林格勒方面军<cr>1943年4月调至沃罗涅日地区重建<cr>获得“哈尔科夫”荣誉称号和红旗勋章

text: The 85th Rifle Corps was formed in September 1943, under the command of Major General Nikondor I. Samonov. Part of the 17th Army of the Transbaikal Front, it included the 36th and 57th Motor Rifle Divisions, stationed in the Mongolian People's Republic, as well as the 284th Rifle Division and the 1st and 3rd Motor Rifle Regiments. On 4 April 1944, 57th Motor Rifle Division commander Major General Viktor I. Nikiforov replaced Samonov. The 284th Division and the two motor rifle regiments were directly subordinated to the army headquarters in December, leaving the 85th with only the 36th and 57th Divisions. From July 1945, the corps headquarters was used to provide a headquarters for the Soviet-Mongolian Cavalry-Mechanized Group. In this capacity, it participated in the Soviet invasion of Manchuria. Nikiforov served as chief of staff of the group during this period.<cr><cr>
translation: 第85步兵军成立于1943年9月，由少将尼孔多尔·I·萨莫诺夫指挥。该部队隶属于外贝加尔方面军的第17集团军，包括驻扎在蒙古人民共和国的第36和第57摩托化步兵师、第284步兵师以及第1和第3摩托化步兵团。1944年4月4日，少将维克多·I·尼基福罗夫接替萨莫诺夫指挥第57摩托化步兵师。1943年12月，第284步兵师以及两个摩托化步兵团直接隶属于集团军司令部，仅留下第36和第57步兵师在第85步兵军中。从1945年7月起，该步兵军的司令部被用于提供苏蒙骑兵机械化集群的司令部。在此期间，尼基福罗夫担任该集团军参谋长。<cr><cr><cr><cr>

text:
The 85th Rifle Division was assigned to 4th Rifle Corps, 3rd Army, Soviet Western Front on outbreak of war, under the command of Major General Aleksandr Bondovsky.<cr><cr>After the division's first formation was disbanded or destroyed, the division was reformed. In late 1941 it was reformed during the Leningrad Strategic Defensive from the 2nd Guard People's Militia Division.

In early 1945 the division was operating as part of 122nd Rifle Corps in the 2nd Baltic Front. On 10 March the division marched into the area of Balozi and Kreyli. It attacked between the 43rd and 46th Rifle Divisions on 22 March, capturing Slugi and Meiri, where it ran into strong German counterattacks and went on the defensive until 30 April, when it was relieved by the 43rd and 56th Guards Rifle Divisions. The division transferred to a new defensive line between Mengravil and Yatsy, relieving elements of the 11th Rifle Division.

By the end of the day on 7 May, the German troops began to retreat to the northwest. Units of the division pursued the retreating troops towards Lubenki, Rumbiniska, and Tseri and by 17:00 on 8 May reached the line of Myzi Gayta, Yurdi, and Kausi, where at 18:00 they accepted the German surrender.<cr><cr>
translation:
第85步兵师在战争爆发时被分配到苏联西方面军的第3集团军下的第4步兵军，由少将亚历山大·邦多夫斯基指挥。<cr>该师首次组建后解散或被消灭，随后重建。1941年末，在列宁格勒战略防御期间，它从第2近卫人民民兵师重组而成。

1945年初，该师作为第122步兵军的一部分在第二波罗的海方面军中作战。3月10日，该师进入巴洛齐和克雷利地区。3月22日，它在第43步兵师和第46步兵师之间发起进攻，占领了斯卢吉和梅里，在那里遭遇德军强烈反攻并转入防御状态，直到4月30日才被第43近卫步兵师和第56近卫步兵师解围。该师转移到门格拉维尔至雅茨的新的防线上，替换部分第11步兵师。

到5月7日结束时，德军开始向西北方向撤退。该师部队追击撤退中的德军前往卢宾基、鲁姆比尼斯卡和策里，并于5月8日下午5点到达米兹加伊塔至尤尔迪至考西的战线，在下午6点接受德军投降。<cr>

text: In July 1941 the 86th Infantry Divison was sent to Army Group Center in Russia. It fought at Vyazma and in the Battle of Moscow and suffered heavy casualties. It remained on the central sector of the Eastern Front, where it took part in the defensive battles of the Rzhev salient in 1942-43, in the Rzhev withdrawal (1943), and in the Battle of Kursk , where it distinguished itself. It also suffered so many losses that the High Command decided to disband it, effective November 2, 1943. The Staff and the signal battalion were sent to Denmark to form the 361st Infantry Division. Most of the rest of the division was assigned to Corps Detachment E as Division Group 86. The corps detachment fought in the Pripyet marshes and at Gomel and Warsaw before being absorbed by the 251st Infantry Division in October 1944.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 1941年7月，第86步兵师被派往中央集团军群赴俄参战。该师参加了维亚兹马战役和莫斯科会战，并遭受了重大损失。它一直驻守在东线中部战区，在1942年至1943年的日洛宾突出部防御战、1943年日洛宾撤退以及库尔斯克会战中表现出色。由于伤亡惨重，最高指挥部决定于1943年11月2日正式解散该师。师部和通信营被派往丹麦重组为第361步兵师。其余大部分部队则编入E军直属队作为第86师团，在波伊普特沼泽地、戈梅利和华沙作战，直至1944年10月被并入第251步兵师。<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷 1至290号步兵师在二战中的经历萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

The division was disbanded soon after, but in 1943 partisans found all the divisional standards in a hide, and the units were reinstated on the RKKA rolls.

The 86th Rifle Division (2nd Formation) was established at Lavrovo in September 1941 from the 4th Division of the Leningrad People's Militia Army, as part of the 7th Army. The 4th People's Militia Division was one of the better quality Leningrad provisional divisions, with men mostly having prior military service. The Division fought near Leningrad in extremely difficult weather conditions at the Nevsky Pyatachok at which time it was renamed as the 86th Rifle Division. When formed it included 1st, 3rd and 4th Separate Special Rifle Brigades, 50th, 111th and 112th Separate Rifle Battalions and Special Sailor's Battalion.[5] From January 1942 the division fought in the 8th Army sector of the Leningrad Front. The division later served in the capture of Tartu on 25 August 1944 as part of the 67th Army (3rd Baltic Front), and in East Prussia. With 2nd Shock Army of the 2nd Belorussian Front May 1945.<cr><cr>

text:
The 87th Guards Rifle Division was created on April 16, 1943, from the veterans of the 300th Rifle Division, in recognition of that division's leading role in the penetration of the German/Romanian defenses south of Stalingrad in the opening stages of Operaton Uranus, its subsequent defense against Army Group Don's attempt to relieve the German 6th Army at Stalingrad, and later for its pursuit of the defeated German forces along the Don River to Rostov-na-Donu as far as the Mius River. The 87th Guards continued a record of distinguished service through the rest of the war, first in the southern sector of the front, where it participated in the liberation of the Donbass region and the Crimea, and then, after a major redeployment, in the north-central sector, advancing through the Baltic states and into eastern Germany.<cr><cr>When formed, its order of battle was as follows:
