text: The 87th Infantry Divison crossed into Russia with Army Group Center, where it fought at the Bialystok, Smolensk, Vyazma, the Yelnya bend, and the Battle of Moscow and against the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42, among others. The 87th spent most of June 1942 to February 1943 in the Rzhev salient. Meanwhile, its reconnaissance and tank destroyer battalions were consolidated into a single schnelle (mobile) battalion. On November 16, 1943, the division was encircled near Malashkinki. It escaped on December 16, but only after it lost all of its heavy equipment and weapons and was reduced to a strength of 5,000 men. Withdrawn from the line, it was rebuilt as a Type 44 division, with six grenadier battalions. In the spring of 1944 the 87th Infantry Division was transferred to Army Group North and was involved in the retreat through the Baltic States, the defense of the Narva, and the six battles of the Courland Pocket. While in Courland, the 185th Grenadier Regiment was disbanded. The division surrendered to the Soviets in western Latvia in May 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第87步兵师随中央集团军群进入俄罗斯，参加了比亚韦斯托克、斯摩棱斯克、维亚兹马、叶连纳河弯道以及莫斯科会战等战役，并且对抗了苏联在1941-1942年冬季的攻势。该师于1942年6月至1943年2月期间驻扎在热季夫突出部。与此同时，其侦察营和坦克歼击车营合并为一个快速（机动）营。1943年11月16日，该师在马拉萨金斯基附近被包围。它于12月16日逃脱，但在此之前已经失去了所有重型装备和武器，并且兵力减少到5000人。从战线撤出后，它重建为一种拥有六个掷弹兵营的44型步兵师。1944年春季，第87步兵师被调往北方集团军群，并参与了通过波罗的海国家的撤退、纳尔瓦河的防御以及库尔兰包围圈内的六次战役。在库尔兰期间，第185掷弹兵团解散。该师于1945年5月在西部拉脱维亚向苏联投降。<cr>德国战斗序列 第一卷 1-290步兵师在二战中的表现萨缪尔·W·米查姆 Jr.

text: On 10 July 1945 the 87th Rifle Corps comprised 231st and 300th Rifle Divisions.<cr>On the dawn of 8 August 1945 the artillery preparation of the invasion of Manchuria began when the USSR declared war on Japan.<cr>On 9 August 1945 the corps received an order to commence operations, and to cross the international border in the region of Grodekovo settlement.<cr>In the course of the Manchurian offensive operation the 87th Rifle Corps moved in into the reserve of the 35th Army.<cr>The 342nd Rifle Division was committed to battle once at the approaches to the Mishan (Japanese) Fortified Region. The 357th Rifle Regiment (from 342nd Rifle Division) reached Khobiy city in North Manchuria while constantly engaged in combat.<cr>The 35th Army, from the staging area Guberovo, Ruzhino, Lesozavodsk, delivered the supporting attack of the 1st Far-Eastern Front, in the direction of Lesozavodsk, Khutou, Mishan with the task of destroying the Mishan group of Japanese troops.<cr>After assaulting across the Sungach river, the 342nd RD with 357th Rifle Regiment directed its concentrated efforts toward securing the area of Tsikhulin region, Khubey, and Yangan. As a result of persistent and bloody combat the 357th RR took the railway station and the city of Khubey.<cr>In the middle of August 1945 the 87th Rifle Corps returned to the area of Lesozavodsk - Sibirtsevo, where it entrained and was transported to Vladivostok. During this time (on 11 to 12 August 1945) the 87th Rifle Corps was brought out from the reserve of the 1st Far-Eastern Front, and received new orders to prepare for landing operations on the island of Hokkaido.At the end of August 1945, the 87th RC moved from Harbin in its entirety (264th, 342nd, 355th RD) and began redeployment to Sakhalin for the purpose of concentrating the troops for the planned landing operation on the island of Hokkaido. This landing operation did not take place, but the corps still completed its concentration at Sakhalin. <cr>Although the 342nd was in the process of being transported to Sakhalin on 25 August, on 22 August Stalin had already ordered thehalt of the planned landing preparations on Hokkaido until further notice. However he allowed the transfer of the 87th Rifle Corps to continue to Sakhalin.<cr>By 27 August 1945 the landing operation on was Hokkaido postponed, and then completely abandoned.<cr>At 0000 on 30 August 1945 the 87th RC was transferred to the 2nd Far East Front. The corps became a part of the 16th Army.<cr>Unloading the last regiment of the 264th RD on Sakhalin was completed at 1900 on 1 September 1945.<cr>On 2 September 1945 the transportation of the 87th Rifle Corps to Sakhalin island was completed.<cr><cr>
translation: 1945年7月10日，第87步兵军包括第231和第300步兵师。<cr>1945年8月8日凌晨，苏联对日本宣战后，远东地区开始炮击准备入侵满洲。<cr>1945年8月9日，该军接到作战命令，并被指示穿越国界进入戈德科沃定居点区域。<cr>在满洲攻势中，第87步兵军一度进入第35集团军的预备队。<cr>第342步兵师曾在接近密山（日本）要塞区时投入战斗。第357步兵团（来自第342步兵师）在北满洲不断作战中抵达霍比耶市。<cr>从古别廖沃、鲁日诺和林纸厂集结地出发，第35集团军作为第一远东方面军的支援攻击力量，在林纸厂、胡图和密山方向行动，任务是消灭密山地区的日本军队。<cr>渡过松阿察河后，第342步兵师与第357步兵团集中兵力向茨基鲁林、胡比耶和扬甘地区推进。由于持续而激烈的战斗，第357步兵团占领了胡比耶火车站及城市。<cr>1945年8月中旬，第87步兵军返回列索扎沃茨克-西比尔采沃地区，在那里乘火车前往符拉迪沃斯托克。在此期间（1945年8月11日至12日），第87步兵军从第一远东方面军的预备队中调出，接到新命令准备在北海道岛进行登陆行动。1945年8月底，第87步兵军连同其下属部队（第264、342和355团）整体从哈尔滨转移，并开始向萨哈林岛调动以集中兵力为计划中的北海道岛登陆作战做准备。虽然第342团在1945年8月25日仍在被运往萨哈林，但斯大林已于1945年8月22日下令暂停北海道的登陆准备工作，直到另行通知为止。然而他允许第87步兵军继续向萨哈林岛调动。<cr>1945年8月27日0时，对北海道的登陆行动被推迟并最终放弃。<cr><cr>1945年8月30日0时，第87步兵军转隶第二远东方面军，并成为第16集团军的一部分。<cr><cr>1945年9月1日19时，最后一个团（第264团）在萨哈林岛的卸载工作完成。<cr><cr>1945年9月2日，第87步兵军向萨哈林岛的调动全部完成。

text: In June 1941, the 87th Rifle Division included the 16th, 96th, and 283rd Rifle Regiments, the 197th Artillery Regiment, the 212th Howitzer Artillery Regiment, and smaller units. It was officially disbanded on 19 September 1941.<cr><cr>The division was reformed from the 3rd Airborne Corps on 20 November 1941; the commander of the latter, Colonel Aleksandr Rodimtsev, continued in command of the 87th for the duration of its existence. It included the 16th, 96th, and 283rd Rifle Regiments, the 197th Artillery Regiment, and smaller units. It was converted into the 13th Guards Rifle Division on 19 January 1942.<cr><cr>The division was reformed in 1942. It included the 1378th, 1379th, and 1382nd Rifle Regiments, the 1058th Artillery Regiment, and smaller units. It was part of the active army from 21 July to 14 September 1942, 23 November 1942 to 10 September 1943, 16 October 1943 to 20 May 1944, and 1 July 1944 to the end of the war in Europe. Wartime commanders were Colonel Alexander Ignatyevich Kazartsyev from 8 March to 27 December 1942, Lieutenant Colonel Mikhail Sergeyevich Yekhokhin (promoted to colonel 22 March 1943) from 28 December 1942 to 2 August 1943, Lieutenant Colonel Georgy Stepanovich Ivanov (promoted to colonel 21 September 1943) from 5 August 1943 to 1 May 1944, and Colonel Georgy Petrovich Kulyako from 2 May 1944 to after the end of the war.<cr><cr>
translation: 1941年6月，第87步兵师包括第16、第96和第283步兵团，第197炮兵团，第212榴弹炮团以及较小的单位。该师于1941年9月19日正式解散。<cr>第87步兵师于1941年11月20日从第3空降军改编而成；后者指挥官亚历山大·罗季姆采夫上校继续担任该师的指挥官直至其存在结束。该师包括第16、第96和第283步兵团，第197炮兵团以及较小的单位。于1942年1月19日改编为第13近卫步兵师。<cr>第87步兵师于1942年重组。包括第1378、第1379和第1382步兵团，第1058炮兵团以及较小的单位。该师从1942年7月21日至9月14日，1942年11月23日至1943年9月10日，1943年10月16日至1944年5月20日以及1944年7月1日至欧洲战争结束期间属于现役部队。战时指挥官包括亚历山大·伊格纳季耶维奇·卡查茨耶夫上校（1942年3月8日至12月27日），米哈伊尔·谢苗诺维奇·叶霍赫欣少校（于1943年3月22日晋升为上校，1942年12月28日至1943年8月2日），格奥尔基·斯捷潘诺维奇·伊万诺夫少校（于1943年9月21日晋升为上校，1943年8月5日至1944年5月1日）以及格奥尔基·彼得罗维奇·库利亚科上校（1944年5月2日至战争结束之后）。

text:
The 88th Rifle Division was twice formed as an infantry division of the Red Army, first as part of the prewar buildup of forces. In its first formation in the far north it had an unusual shtat (table of organization and equipment) probably to facilitate its movement in the roadless tundra and forests of that region. During the Winter War against Finland it saw action in the fighting around Salla. Its organization again proved beneficial in the spring of 1942 during the first stages of WWII. It played a large role in holding and then pushing back the Finnish III Army Corps during Operation Silver Fox and for this success was redesignated as the 23rd Guards Rifle Division.

A new 88th began forming in April, 1942 based on the first formation of the 39th Rifle Brigade, mostly in the Moscow Military District and was soon assigned to the 31st Army of Western Front; it would remain in that Army for the duration of the war. It took part in the savage and mostly fruitless fighting around the Rzhev salient into the winter of 1942/43 and then in the summer offensive that liberated Smolensk. During the following fall it became badly depleted as Western Front repeatedly attempted to batter its way through the German defenses to Orsha. After rebuilding in the spring of 1944 it served as part of 3rd Belorussian Front during Operation Bagration, soon being awarded a battle honor as well as the Order of the Red Banner. During this offensive it reached the border of East Prussia and won a second decoration in the unsuccessful Gumbinnen-Goldap Operation. During the East Prussian Offensive in January, 1945 it made steady progress, eventually earning its third Order after the battle for the Heiligenbeil Pocket. After the East Prussian campaign the 31st Army was railed south to Czechoslovakia where the 88th ended the war marching on Prague.<cr><cr>
translation:
第88步兵师作为红军的步兵师两次组建，第一次是在战前兵力扩充期间。在首次于北极地区组建时，它拥有一个不同寻常的编制表（组织与装备），可能是为了便于其在该地区的无路冻原和森林中行动。在冬季战争对抗芬兰期间，该师参与了萨拉周边的战斗。1942年春季，在第二次世界大战初期阶段，它的编制作出了积极贡献。它在“银狐”行动中发挥了重要作用，成功地阻止并反击了芬军第III军（即芬军第3集团军），为此被重新指定为第23近卫步兵师。

一个新的第88步兵师于1942年4月开始组建，主要基于第39步兵旅的第一个编成单位，在莫斯科军区进行。很快该师被分配到西方方面军的第31集团军，并在战争期间一直留在该集团军内。它参与了围绕热季村突出部展开的残酷且大多无果的战斗，直到1942/43年的冬季；然后参加了解放斯摩棱斯克的夏季攻势。在随后的秋季中，由于西方方面军多次试图突破德国防御以攻占奥尔沙，第88步兵师严重减员。经过1944年春季重建后，该师作为第三白俄罗斯方面军的一部分参与了巴格拉季昂行动，并很快获得了一项战斗荣誉以及红旗勋章。在此攻势中，它推进到了东普鲁士边境，在不成功的贡宾嫩-戈尔达普行动中又赢得了一个装饰品。在1945年1月的东普鲁士进攻中，该师稳步前进，最终因海利根贝伊尔包围圈战役而获得第三个红旗勋章。在东普鲁士战役之后，第31集团军被铁路运送到捷克斯洛伐克，在向布拉格进军时结束了战争。<cr>指挥官报告：第88步兵师在巴格拉季昂行动中表现卓越，并在海利根贝伊尔包围圈战斗中获得第三个红旗勋章。

text: The 89th Rifle Division was established at Kursk prior to June 1941. On 22 June 1941 it was part of 33rd Rifle Corps in the interior Orel Military District. Fighting as part of the 19th Army, it was wiped out at Vyazma in October 1941.<cr><cr>The division was re-formed in December 1941 in the capital of the Armenian SSR, Yerevan, following the German invasion of the Soviet Union. It was a redesignation of the 474th Rifle Division, which was formed on 14 December 1941 and renumbered the 89th Rifle Division on 26 December 1941.<cr><cr>In August 1942, the 89th Division was dispatched toward the North Caucasus Front, where it took up defensive positions to block the German drive toward Grozny. From November to December 1942, the unit took part in several fierce battles in the area around the cities of Elekhotvo, Malgobek, and Voznesenskaya and helped bring the German penetration into the Caucasus to a halt. As the Soviet armies shifted to the offensive during the winter of 1942-43, the 89th Division began its gradual advance toward the Crimea. <cr><cr>In September 1943, the division was redeployed and ordered to attack the Axis defensive fortifications on the Taman Peninsula. On September 6, it moved in a northeasterly direction from Novorossiysk and engaged in heavy fighting for several days until the Axis defenses were overwhelmed and the villages of Verkhnebakansk and Taman were liberated on September 18 and October 3, respectively. The 89th distinguished itself in these two battles and was given the honorary title of 'Tamanskaya'.<cr><cr>On November 21, the 89th Division participated in the Kerch-Eltigen Operation, an ambitious Soviet military operation involving the landing of amphibious troops onto the Kerch Peninsula. Beginning in January 1944, it slowly made headway toward Kerch and dislodged the defending Axis troops from one portion of the city.<cr><cr>In May 1944, the Soviet army began its offensive to retake Sevastopol. The 89th Division was given the objective of capturing the Gornaya Height, which would then open the way to Sevastopol. This was accomplished and the unit subsequently took part in Sevastopol's and the promontory of Kherson's recapture. For the liberation of the Sevastopol the division was bestowed with the Order of the Red Banner.<cr><cr>In October-September 1944, the division was transferred first to Brest and then deployed along the defensive line near Lublin. With the commencement of the VistulaOder Offensive on January 12, 1945, the 89th Division took part in the general advance into Poland and aided in the liberation of dozens of Polish settlements and towns. By February, it had crossed the Oder River and had taken control of the approach leading to Frankfurt an der Oder and prevented the Germans from breaking through to endanger the Soviet forces now converging onto Berlin.<cr><cr>The 89th arrived in the German capital on the night of April 29, along with other elements of the 3rd Shock Army, and deployed the 390th, 400th, and 526th Regiments to take part in heavy street-to-street battles in the Wedding and Reinickendorf districts. In several days of fighting the division had overran seven districts. For its role in the capture of Berlin, the 89th was awarded with the Order of Kutuzov 2nd Class.<cr><cr>
translation: 第89步兵师于1941年6月之前在库尔斯克建立。1941年6月22日，它隶属于奥廖尔军区内的第33步兵军。作为第19集团军的一部分作战时，在1941年10月的维亚兹马战役中被消灭。<cr>该师于1941年12月在苏联外高加索加盟共和国首都叶卡捷琳堡重建，重新编号为第89步兵师。原番号为第474步兵师，成立于1941年12月14日，并于同年12月26日改称为第89步兵师。<cr>1942年8月，第89师被派往北高加索方面军，在那里它采取防御态势以阻止德军向格罗兹内的推进。从1942年11月至12月期间，该部队参与了在埃列克霍特沃、马尔戈别克和沃兹涅先斯卡亚周边地区进行的多次激烈战斗，并帮助将德军在高加索地区的渗透行动遏制下来。<cr>随着苏联军队于1942-43年冬季转入进攻，第89师开始逐步向克里米亚推进。<cr>1943年9月，该师被重新部署并命令攻击轴心国在塔曼半岛的防御工事。9月6日，它从新罗西斯克向东北方向移动，并进行了数天的激烈战斗直到突破轴心国防御，分别于9月18日和10月3日解放了维赫涅巴坎斯克村和塔曼村。<cr>第89师在这两场战役中表现出色并被授予“塔曼”荣誉称号。<cr>1943年11月21日，第89师参加了克里米亚半岛刻赤-埃尔蒂琴行动，这是一项雄心勃勃的苏军军事行动，涉及两栖部队在刻赤半岛登陆。从1944年1月开始，该师逐步向刻赤推进，并迫使轴心国守军撤离城市的一部分。<cr>1944年5月，苏军发起了夺回塞瓦斯托波尔的攻势。第89师被赋予了夺取戈罗尼亚高地的任务，这将为攻占塞瓦斯托波尔打开道路。这一目标得以实现，并且该师随后参与了塞瓦斯托波尔和赫尔松角的收复行动。<cr>由于在解放塞瓦斯托波尔中的贡献，第89师被授予红旗勋章。<cr>1944年10月-9月，该师首先被调往布列斯特，然后部署到卢布林附近的防御线上。随着<cr>1945年1月12日开始的维斯瓦河-奥得河攻势，第89师参加了进入波兰的大规模推进，并帮助解放了数十个波兰定居点和城镇。<cr>到了2月，该师已经渡过奥得河并控制了通往法兰克福（奥德）的道路，阻止了德国人突破以威胁正在向柏林集结的苏军。<cr>1945年4月29日夜，第89师与其他3个突击集团军的部分部队一起抵达德国首都。该师部署了第390团、第400团和第526团参与重大的街区战斗，在魏德恩区和赖尼克登福尔特区进行了激烈的巷战。<cr>在几天的战斗中，该师占领了7个城区。<cr>由于在攻占柏林中的贡献，第89师被授予库图佐夫勋章二级奖章。

text: Formed in September 1941, the corps was never committed to combat and was reorganized in July 1942 as 35th Guards Rifle Division. A second formation of the corps took place in August 1942 but it was rapidly reorganized as 3rd Guards Airborne Division. Hero of the Soviet Union Ivan Konev commanded the corps during its second formation and went on to command 3rd Guards Airborne Division for most of the rest of the war. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该军成立于1941年9月，从未投入战斗，并于1942年7月重组为第35近卫步兵师。第二次组建发生在1942年8月，但很快被重组为第3空降师。苏联英雄伊万·科涅夫在该军的第二次组建期间担任指挥官，并继续领导第3近卫空降师直到战争结束。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 红军战斗序列：伟大卫国战争，Presidio Press, 1985<cr>条目由Stewart King提供

text: The 8th Army was activated on August 1, 1939 with General Johannes Blaskowitz in command. First seeing service in Poland participated in heavy fights during Battle of Bzura, the army was later reorganised into the 2nd Army for the Invasion of France, before later being reactivated as being part of the Ostfront in the Soviet Union. The army was involved in the fighting in Hungary, Romania, and Austria before finally surrendering.<cr><cr>
translation: 第8集团军成立于1939年8月1日，由约翰内斯·布拉斯科维茨将军指挥。该部队首次在波兰参战，并参与了布祖拉河战役中的激烈战斗。之后，它被重组为第2集团军参加入侵法国的行动，后来又作为东线部队的一部分重新组建，在苏联境内作战。该部队还参加了匈牙利、罗马尼亚和奥地利境内的战斗，最终投降。<cr><cr><cr>

text: From the morning of 22 June 1941 as part of the Northwestern Front the 8th Army (10th Rifle Corps with 10th, 48th, and 90th Rifle Divisions and 11th Rifle Corps with 11th Rifle Division and 125th Rifle Division, 12th Mechanised Corps, 47th, 51st, and 74th Corps Artillery Regiments, and 9th Anti-Tank Artillery Brigade and a number of other units) joined the heavy fighting against the superior forces of the German Wehrmacht on the Shyaulyay axis.<cr>On 23-25 June its 12th Mechanised Corps with the part of the 3rd Mechanised Corps of the 11th Army southwest of Shyaulyaya executed a counterblow on the 4th Panzer Group , as a result of which their advance was delayed by several days. After 30 June the 22nd Motor Rifle Division NKVD started operating as part of 10th Rifle Corps.<cr>During July-August the troops of the 8th Army conducted persistent defensive actions in Estonia. On 14 July, the army was transferred to the Northern Front, and on 27 August of the Leningrad Front. In the beginning of September 1941 the army's troops fought on the neighboring approaches to Leningrad, retaining contact with the forces of the Red Banner Baltic Fleet on the Oranienbaum bridgehead which played an important role in the Siege of Leningrad. At the beginning of November, the Army headquarters and some formations and units of the 8th Army were relocated into the eastern sector of the defence of the Leningrad Front and to the bridgehead on the Neva River in Moscow Dubrovki. During November- December, they conducted persistent offensive combat to try an achieve a breakthrough of the Leningrad blockade.<cr> On 9 June, the army was subordinated to the Volkhov Front. In August- September, it acted as a part of the Front's assault group for the Sinyavinsk Offensive Operation. During January 1943, the 8th Army participated in the Leningrad blockade breakthrough, covering the southern flank of the Fronts assault group. During July-August it fought in the furious fighting of the Mga Offensive Operation.<cr>During January 1944, the army headquarters and its support units were moved between Novgorod and Lake Peipus.<cr>After accepting new formations, the Army participated in the Novgorod-Luga Offensive Operation. After regrouping as part of the Leningrad Front (from 16 February), the Army made several attempts to encircle the German Army Group Narwa in the battle for Narva Bridgehead. After the failure to do so, the army took up defensive positions in late March to July. The Army participated in the Narva Offensive (July 1944) and the Battle of Tannenberg Line, 25 July to 10 August 1944. During September in cooperation with the 2nd Shock Army and the Baltic Fleet, the army conducted the Tallinn Offensive, as a result of which, mainland Estonia and the capital Tallinn were captured.<cr>In OctoberNovember the army together with the Baltic Fleet conducted the Moonsund Landing Operation to capture the West Estonian archipelago (Moonsund archipelago).<cr>From December 1944, the Army carried out coastal defence tasks in Estonia to the end of the war.<cr><cr>
translation: 从1941年6月22日清晨开始，作为西北方面军的一部分，第8集团军（包括第10步兵军的第10、第48和第90步兵师，第11步兵军的第11和第125步兵师，第12机械化军，第47、第51和第74炮兵团，以及第9反坦克炮兵旅和其他一些单位）加入了在什亚乌利亚轴线上对德国国防军优势兵力的激烈战斗。<cr>6月23日至25日，其第12机械化军与第11集团军西南部什亚乌利亚附近的第3机械化军的一部分执行了反击第4装甲集群的任务，导致对方推进延迟数天。从6月30日起，内务人民委员部的第22摩托化步兵师开始作为第10步兵军的一部分进行作战。<cr>7月至8月期间，第8集团军在爱沙尼亚进行了持久防御行动。7月14日，该集团军被转移到北方方面军，并于8月27日转到列宁格勒方面军。1941年9月初，该集团军的部队在邻近列宁格勒的地区作战，与红旗下波罗的海舰队在奥拉宁鲍姆桥头堡的力量保持联系，在列宁格勒围城战中发挥了重要作用。11月初，第8集团军司令部和一些部队被转移到列宁格勒方面军东部防御区以及涅瓦河上的莫斯科杜布罗夫基桥头堡。从11月至12月期间，他们进行了持久的进攻战斗，试图突破列宁格勒封锁线。<cr> 6月9日，该集团军隶属于沃尔霍夫方面军。8月至9月期间，它作为方面军突击群的一部分参加了辛亚文斯克进攻战役。1943年1月，第8集团军参与了列宁格勒封锁突破行动，掩护了方面军突击群的南翼。<cr>1944年1月，司令部及其支援单位在诺夫哥罗德和佩普斯湖之间调动。<cr>接受新编成后，该集团军参加了诺夫哥罗德-卢加进攻战役。重组为列宁格勒方面军的一部分（从2月16日开始），该集团军多次尝试包围德国北方集团军群在纳尔瓦桥头堡的战斗。<cr>未能成功后，该集团军于3月下旬至7月采取了防御态势。该集团军参加了纳尔瓦进攻战役（1944年7月）和坦能堡防线之战（1944年7月25日至8月10日）。<cr>9月份，在第二突击集团军和波罗的海舰队的合作下，该集团军进行了塔林进攻行动，结果占领了爱沙尼亚本土及首都塔林。<cr>10月至11月，该集团军与波罗的海舰队合作实施了穆斯隆德登陆作战以夺取西爱沙尼亚群岛（穆斯隆德群岛）。<cr>从1944年12月开始，该集团军在爱沙尼亚执行海岸防御任务直至战争结束。

text:
The 8th Guards Airborne Division was formed on 8 December 1942 from the 10th Airborne Corps in the Moscow Military District. The personnel of the airborne division received training in airborne tactics. Major general Alexander Kapitokhin, commander of the 10th Airborne Corps, became the division's first commander. In February 1943, the division was transferred to the Northwestern Front, where it became part of the 68th Army, fighting in the Demyansk Offensive.

On 24 April 1943, the division was withdrawn from the front and moved to Voronezh as part of the Central Front . At the beginning of May, the division became part of the 20th Guards Rifle Corps and from 3 October became part of the 21st Guards Rifle Corps. The division fought in the last part of the Battle of Kursk and the Chernigov-Poltava Offensive. From the area of Kotelva it advanced to the northwestern part of Poltava, establishing contact with the 5th Guards Army. On the night of 5 October, it crossed the Old Dnieper and crossed the Dnieper on the next night, capturing a bridgehead on the right bank near the village of Voronovka.

On 19 October, the division was transferred to the 7th Guards Army on the Steppe Front. It fought in defensive battles on the Inhulets River during early December. The 8th Guards Airborne took part in battles west of Kirovohrad until March 1944. In March 1944, the division was on the left wing of the 2nd Ukrainian Front during the Uman-Botosani Offensive. It advanced towards Kompaniivka. At Semyonovka village, the division reached the left bank of the Southern Bug. On 22 March, the 22nd and 27th Guards Airborne Regiments, in conjunction with the 36th Guards Rifle Division's 108th Guards Rifle Regiment, crossed the Southern Bug near the village of Myhiya, seizing a bridgehead at Grushevka village in Pervomaisk Raion. Fighting the German 106th Infantry Division and 282nd Infantry Division, it reached the outskirts of Pervomaisk.

At this time, the 25th Guards Airborne Regiment crossed the Southern Bug in the area north of Semyonovka together with the 81st Guards Rifle Division capturing the villages of Romanova Balka, Ivanovka and Sokolovka. These units created a threat to the Germans holding Pervomaisk, which caused them to retreat. For its part in taking the city, the division was awarded the honorary title 'Pervomaisk'.<cr><cr>

text: The Soviet 8th Guards Army was formed from the 62nd Army on May 5 1943 and received Guards status in recognition of its actions in the Battle of Stalingrad.<cr>In July 1943, it took part in the Izyum-Barvenkovo Offensive (July 17-27), and in August-September - in the Donbass strategic offensive operation (August 13 - September 22) . Developing the offensive in the direction of the Dnieper, the Army with other troops of the Southwestern Front liberated Zaporozhye (October 14), crossed the Dnieper south of Dnipropetrovsk south and captured a bridgehead on its right bank. By this time 28th, 29th and 4th Guards Rifle Corps were part of the army.<cr>The army was part of the 3rd Ukrainian Front during the Dnieper-Carpathian Offensive. By March 25, 1944, the Prut River had fallen and the 3rd Ukrainian Front was dispatched to secure Odessa. On April 2, Vasily Chuikov Eighth Guards Army and 46th Army attacked through a blizzard and, by April 6, had driven the defenders past the Dniester River and isolated Odessa. Odessa capitulated on April 10, and Soviet troops began entering Romania proper.<cr>In June, 1944 the army was transferred to the 1st Belorussian Front and took part in the Lublin-Brest Offensive, seizing and defending a bridgehead over the Vistula river at Magnuszew.<cr>In 1945 the army was part of Marshal Georgy Zhukov's 1st Belorussian Front. One of the cities which the Army took in its westward drive was Poznan, which the Army seized in January-February 1945.<cr>In a deliberate symbolic move the 8th Guards Army was then sent northwards to the center of the front, coming under command of 1st Belorussian Front; Stalin was determined that the Army that had defended Stalingrad would take part in the capture of Berlin. On 2 May 1945, Chuikov took the surrender of the German General Helmuth Weidling, the commander of the Berlin Defensive Area, and the rest of the Berlin garrison. <cr><cr>
translation: 苏联第8近卫集团军于1943年5月5日由第62集团军改编而成，并因在斯大林格勒战役中的表现而获得近卫称号。<cr>1943年7月，该集团军参加了伊久姆-巴尔文科沃攻势（7月17日至27日），并在8月至9月期间参与了顿巴斯战略进攻行动（8月13日至9月22日）。在向第聂伯河方向推进的过程中，该集团军与其他西南方面军部队解放了扎波罗热（10月14日），渡过了第聂伯河南部的第聂伯罗彼得罗夫斯克，并占领了其右岸桥头堡。此时，第28、第29和第4近卫步兵军是该集团军的一部分。<cr>在第聂伯-喀尔巴阡攻势期间，该集团军隶属于第3乌克兰方面军。到1944年3月25日，普鲁特河已被突破，第3乌克兰方面军被派往确保敖德萨的安全。4月2日，在暴风雪中，瓦西里·丘伊科夫的第八近卫集团军和第46集团军发起攻击，并于4月6日前驱逐了守军至德涅斯特河以东并孤立了敖德萨。敖德萨于4月10日投降，苏军开始进入罗马尼亚境内。<cr>1944年6月，该集团军被调往第1白俄罗斯方面军，并参加了卢布林-布列斯特攻势，在马格努谢夫渡过了维斯瓦河并守卫了桥头堡。<cr>1945年，该集团军隶属于朱可夫元帅的第1白俄罗斯方面军。在向西推进的过程中，该集团军占领的城市之一是波兹南，该城市于1945年1月至2月被该集团军攻占。<cr>为了表达象征意义，第8近卫集团军被派往前线中部，在第1白俄罗斯方面军的指挥下行动；斯大林决心让保卫过斯大林格勒的军队参与攻克柏林。1945年5月2日，丘伊科夫接受了德国将军赫尔穆特·魏德林的投降，后者是柏林防御区的指挥官以及柏林守备部队的其余成员。<cr>

text: Formed 1/19/43 from 11th Cavalry Division, it inherited the honorific title of 'Oldenburg Volunteers' from its parent formation. It was part of VI Guards Cavalry Corps throughout the war. It fought in the Rzhev in winter 1942-43 and was awarded the titles 'Rzhev' and 'Rechitsa', and later fought in the advance into Poland in 1944. <cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 该师于1943年1月19日由第11骑兵师组建，继承了其上级部队的荣誉称号“奥尔登堡志愿兵”。在整个战争期间，它隶属于第六近卫骑兵军。在1942-1943年的冬季，它参加了列日夫战役，并获得了“列日夫”和“雷奇察”的荣誉称号；1944年，该师又参与了进入波兰的进攻作战。<cr>指挥官报告：罗伯特·波尔耶尔、阿尔伯特·康纳，《伟大卫国战争中的红军战斗序列》，普雷斯迪奥出版社，1985年<cr>词条由斯图尔特·金提供

text: The 3rd Mechnanized Corps fought in the Battle of Kursk , then fought across the Ukraine with the Central, Belorussian, and 1st Belorussian Fronts. On 23 October 1943, it was awarded 'Guards' status and re-designated the 8th Guards Mechanised Corps. In 1944, it took part in the Zhitomir-Berdichev, Korsun-Shevchenkovsky, Proskurov-Chernovits, and Lvov-Sandomierz battles, gaining the 'Carpathian' honorific in April 1944. It ended the war in Berlin after participating in the Warsaw-Poznan and East Pomeranian Offensives. <cr><cr>
translation: 第3机械化军参加了库尔斯克战役，随后与中央、白俄罗斯和第1白俄罗斯方面军一起在乌克兰作战。1943年10月23日，该部被授予“近卫”称号，并改组为第8近卫机械化军。1944年，它参与了日托米尔-别尔迪切夫、科尔松-舍甫琴科夫斯基、普罗斯库罗夫-切尔诺维策和利沃夫-桑多梅日战役，在1944年4月获得了“喀尔巴阡”荣誉称号。战争结束时，该部在柏林参战之前参加了华沙-波兹南攻势和东波美拉尼亚攻势。<cr><cr>

text:
On 17 November, Joseph Stalin as People's Commissar of Defense passed a decree to promote the 316th Rifle Division to a Guards formation, in recognition of the role it played in defending the capital; it sustained 9,920 casualties, including 3,620 soldiers killed in action and 6,300 wounded. Marshal Dmitry Yazov, who researched the division's history, wrote that it considerably delayed the enemy's march on Moscow in its sector.<cr>On the 18th, a group of journalists traveled to Major General Ivan Panfilov's headquarters in the village of Guseniovo, and told him of the news. As he briefed them in the open, they came under a mortar attack. The general was killed by a shell splinter. The decree came into effect on that very day, turning the 316th to the 8th Guards Rifle Division; it also received the Order of the Red Banner. It was named in honor of Panfilov on 23 November, thus becoming one of the only two Red Army divisions to be named after their commanders, along with the Chapayevska. As a Guards Division the numbering of its subordinate units was as follows:

19th Guards Rifle Regiment from 1073rd Rifle Regiment
23rd Guards Rifle Regiment from 1075rd Rifle Regiment
30th Guards Rifle Regiment from 1077rd Rifle Regiment
27th Guards Artillery Regiment from 857th Artillery Regiment
2nd Guards Sapper Battalion from 597th Sapper Battalion<cr><cr>
The 8th Guards took part in the December counteroffensive in Moscow, liberating the villages of Kryukovo and Istra.<cr>During late January 1942, the 8th Guards was assigned to the 2nd Guards Rifle Corps of Northwestern Front, and participated in the battles near the Demyansk Pocket; for its performance during the operation, it was collectively awarded the Order of Lenin on 16 March. In June, still in 2nd Guards Corps, it was transferred to 3rd Shock Army in Kalinin Front.[10] In late 1942, the 30th Guards Rifle Regiment fought as a separate unit in the Battle of Velikiye Luki near the Lovat River. In 1944, it took part in the Leningrad-Novgorod Offensive and later, in the battle of Rezekne; for its role in taking the city and the surrounding region, it was awarded the honorary title Rezhitskaya on 27 July 1944. On 3 November, the division received the Order of Suvorov 2nd Class. The 8th Guards ended the war with the 10th Guards Army, as part of the forces besieging Courland.<cr><cr>

text: The 8th Hungarian Infantry Brigade was formed in 1939. Its TOE consisted of 9,500 men under a major-general with 2 infantry regiments (each with 3 battalions and a machine gun company), an artillery regiment with 7 batteries and various support troops. In the fall of 1941 the brigade was one of five brigades reduced in size and stripped of their artillery that was assigned to the Hungarian Occupation Group for security duties on the Eastern Front. At this time it was redesignated the 108th Infantry Brigade but in February of 1942 was redesignated at the 108th Light Division. In May of 1943 the unit became the 8th Light Division. As part of a general reorganization of the Hungarian Army after Stalingrad the 8th Light Division was merged with other units and disbanded.<cr><cr>Dr. Nigel Thomas and Lazlo Pal Szabo, The Royal Hungarian Army in World War II<cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation: 第8匈牙利步兵旅成立于1939年。其编制表包括9500人，由少将指挥，下辖两个步兵团（每个团有三个营和一个机枪连），一个炮兵团配有7个炮兵连以及各种支援部队。1941年秋季，该旅是被缩减规模并剥离炮兵的五个旅之一，被分配给匈牙利占领集团，在东线方面军执行治安任务。此时，它被重新命名为第108步兵旅，但在1942年2月又被改名为第108轻师。1943年5月，该单位成为第8轻师。在斯大林格勒战役后对匈牙利陆军进行的一般重组中，第8轻师与其他部队合并并解散。<cr>参考文献：Dr. Nigel Thomas 和 Lazlo Pal Szabo，《第二次世界大战中的皇家匈牙利军队》<cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr><cr>

text: The Italian Army in Russia (Armata Italiana in Russia, or ARMIR) was an army-sized unit of the Italian Royal Army (Regio Esercito Italiano) which fought on the Eastern Front during World War II. The ARMIR was also known as the 8th Italian Army and initially had 235,000 soldiers.<cr>In July 1942, the ARMIR was created when Italian dictator Benito Mussolini decided to scale up the Italian effort in the Soviet Union. The existing Italian Expeditionary Corps in Russia (Corpo di Spedizione Italiano in Russia, or CSIR) was expanded to become the ARMIR. Unlike the 'mobile' CSIR which it replaced, the ARMIR was primarily an infantry army. A good portion of the ARMIR was made up of mountain troops (Alpini). While in many ways the mountain troops added greatly to the capabilities of the ARMIR, in other ways these elite mountain fighters were ill-suited to the vast, flat expanses of southern Russia.<cr>Like the CSIR, the ARMIR included an Aviation Command (Comando Aereo) with a limited number of fighters, bombers, and transport aircraft. This command was part of the Regia Aeronautica (lit. 'Royal Air Force') and was also known as the Corpo Aereo Spedizione in Russia ('Air Expeditionary Corps in Russia').<cr>The ARMIR was subordinated to German Army Group B (Heeresgruppe B) commanded by General Maximilian von Weichs.<cr>Italian General Italo Gariboldi took command of the newly formed ARMIR from General Giovanni Messe. As commander of the CSIR, Messe had opposed an enlargement of the Italian contingent in Russia until it could be properly equipped. As a result, he was dismissed by Mussolini and the CSIR was expanded without his further input. Just prior to commanding the ARMIR, Gariboldi was the Governor-General of Italian Libya. He was criticized after the war for being too submissive to the Germans in North Africa.<cr>In late summer 1942, after participating in the conquest of eastern Ukraine, the highly-mobile riflemen (Bersaglieri) of the ARMIR eliminated the Soviet bridgehead at Serafimovi? on the Don river. Then, with the support of German tanks, the Gariboldi troops repelled a Soviet attack during the first defensive battle of the Don.<cr>Finally the ARMIR faced Operation Little Saturn in December 1942. The aim of this Soviet operation was the complete annihilation of the Italian 8th Army, as a result of the operations related to the Battle of Stalingrad.<cr>On December 11, 1942 the Soviet 63rd Army, backed by T-34 tanks and fighter-bombers, first attacked the weakest Italian sector. This sector was held on the right by the Ravenna and Cosseria infantry divisions. Indeed, from the Soviet bridgehead at Mamon, 15 divisionssupported by at least 100 tanksattacked the Italian Divisions, and although outnumbered 9 to 1, the Italians resisted until 19 December, when ARMIR headquarters finally ordered the battered divisions to withdraw. Only before Christmas both divisions were driven back and defeated, after heavy and bloody fighting.<cr>Meanwhile, on 17 December 1942, the Soviet 21st Army and the Soviet 5th Tank Army attacked and defeated what remained of the Romanians to the right of the Italians. At about the same time, the Soviet 3rd Tank Army and parts of the Soviet 40th Army hit the Hungarians to the left of the Italians. This resulted in a collapse of the Axis front, north of Stalingrad: the ARMIR was encircled, but for some days the Italian troops were ablewith huge casualtiesto stop the attacking Soviet troops.<cr>The Soviet 1st Guards Army then attacked the Italian center which was held by the 298th German, the Pasubio, the Torino, the Prince Amedeo Duca d'Aosta, and the Sforzesca divisions. After eleven days of bloody fighting against overwhelming Soviet forces, these divisions were surrounded and defeated and Russian air support resulted in the death of General Paolo Tarnassi, commander of the Italian armoured force in Russia.<cr>On 14 January 1943, after a short pause, the 6th Soviet Army attacked the Alpini divisions of the Italian Mountain Corps. These units had been placed on the left flank of the Italian army and, to date, were still relatively unaffected by the battle. However, the Alpinis position had turned critical after the collapse of the Italian center, the collapse of the Italian right flank, and the simultaneous collapse of the Hungarian troops to the left of the Alpini. The Julia Division and Cuneense Division were destroyed. Members of the 1st Alpini Regiment, part of Cuneese Division, burned the regimental flags to keep them from being captured. Part of the Tridentia Division and other withdrawing troops managed to escape the encirclement.<cr>On 26 January 1943, after heavy fighting which resulted in the Battle of Nikolayevka, the Alpini remnants breached the encirclement and reached new defensive positions set up to the west by the German Army (Wehrmacht Heer). But, by this time, the only operational fighting unit was the Tridentina Division and even it was not fully operational. The Tridentina Division had led the final breakout assault at Nikolajewka. Many of the troops who managed to escape were frostbitten, critically ill, and deeply demoralized: for practical purposes, the Italian Army in Russia did not exist anymore by February 1943.<cr>Mussolini disbanded what was left of the Italian 8th Army and the surviving Italian troops were unceremoniously brought home from Russia.<cr><cr>
translation: 意大利皇家陆军在俄罗斯部队（Armata Italiana in Russia，简称ARMIR）是意大利皇家陆军的一个军级单位，在第二次世界大战期间于东线作战。1942年7月，意大利独裁者贝尼托·墨索里尼决定扩大意大利在苏联的行动规模时，ARMIR成立，并将原有的意大利远征军俄罗斯部队（Corpo di Spedizione Italiano in Russia，简称CSIR）扩编为ARMIR。与被取代的“机动”CSIR不同，ARMIR主要是一支步兵部队，其中很大一部分是由山地部队（阿尔卑斯猎兵）组成的。虽然在很多方面，这些精英山地战士大大增强了ARMIR的能力，但在其他方面，他们并不适合俄罗斯南部广阔平坦的土地。<cr><cr>与CSIR一样，ARMIR也包括一个航空指挥部（Comando Aereo），拥有一定数量的战斗机、轰炸机和运输机。该指挥部隶属于意大利皇家空军（Regia Aeronautica），又称为空中远征军俄罗斯部队（Corpo Aereo Spedizione in Russia）。<cr><cr>ARMIR隶属于德军北方集团军群B（Heeresgruppe B），由马克斯米利安·冯·魏克斯将军指挥。<cr><cr><cr><cr>意大利将军伊塔洛·加里波尔迪接任了由乔瓦尼·梅塞将军新组建的ARMIR（意大利驻俄军队）指挥官职务。作为CSIR（意大利驻俄志愿军）的指挥官，梅塞反对在俄罗斯扩大意军规模，直到其能够得到充分装备。因此，墨索里尼解除了他的职务，并在没有他进一步参与的情况下扩充了CSIR。在担任ARMIR指挥官之前，加里波尔迪曾是意大利利比亚总督。战后他因在北非对德国过于顺从而受到批评。<cr>1942年夏末，在参加占领乌克兰东部的行动之后，ARMIR中的高机动步兵（掷弹兵）消灭了顿河畔塞拉芬诺沃的苏联桥头堡。随后，在德军坦克支援下，加里波尔迪部队击退了苏军在第一次顿河防御战中的进攻。<cr>1942年12月，ARMIR面临“小土星行动”。该行动旨在彻底消灭意大利第8集团军，这是与斯大林格勒战役相关的作战的一部分。<cr>1942年12月11日，得到T-34坦克和歼击机支援的苏联第63集团军首先攻击了最薄弱的意军防区。该防区由拉文纳步兵师和科塞里亚步兵师在右翼防守。事实上，从马蒙的苏军桥头堡出发，15个师得到至少100辆坦克支援，对意大利师发起进攻。尽管兵力对比为9:1，意军仍顽强抵抗至12月19日，ARMIR司令部最终下令疲惫不堪的部队撤离。<cr>圣诞节前，两支部队在激烈的战斗后被击溃并撤退。与此同时，1942年12月17日，苏联第21集团军和第5坦克集团军攻击并击败了意大利军队左侧的罗马尼亚残部。大约在同一时间，苏联第3装甲集团军和部分苏联第40集团军向意大利军队右侧的匈牙利部队发起了进攻。这导致轴心国在斯大林格勒以北的战线崩溃：ARMIR被包围，但数日内意军仍能以巨大的伤亡阻止苏军攻势。<cr>随后，苏联第1近卫集团军攻击了由德意志第298师、帕苏比奥师、都灵师、阿梅代奥亲王杜卡·达斯托亚师和索福塞卡师组成的意军中央阵地。经过十一天血腥的战斗，在压倒性的苏军攻势下，这些部队被包围并击败。苏联空军支援导致意大利装甲部队指挥官保罗·塔尔纳西将军阵亡。<cr>1943年1月14日，短暂休整后，第6苏联集团军攻击了意军山地师团的阿尔卑斯师。这些单位被部署在意军左翼，并且到目前为止相对未受战斗影响。然而，在意军中央战线崩溃、右翼战线崩溃以及同时左侧匈牙利部队崩溃之后，阿尔卑斯师的位置变得危急。朱莉娅师和昆内塞师被消灭。昆内塞师第1阿尔卑斯团成员烧毁了团旗以防止其落入敌手。特里迪齐亚师的部分和其他撤退部队设法逃出了包围圈。<cr>1943年1月26日，在尼古拉耶夫卡战役的激烈战斗之后，阿尔卑斯师残部突破了包围圈，并到达了德国陆军（国防军陆军）在西面设置的新防御阵地。然而，此时唯一能作战的部队只剩下特伦蒂纳师，而且它也未能完全投入战斗。特伦蒂纳师领导了尼古拉耶夫卡最后的突围突击。许多成功逃脱的士兵都患上了冻伤、严重疾病，并且士气低落：从实际意义上讲，意大利军队在俄罗斯已经不存在了。<cr>墨索里尼解散了意大利第8集团军剩余的部分，并将幸存的意军草草地撤回了意大利。<cr><cr>

text: The 8th Infantry Division was sent to central Russia in June 1941, and suffered heavy losses in the initial campaign, especially at Bryansk, Vyazma, and the Battle of Moscow. The division was returned to France in late 1941, and was converted into a light division, losing its 28th Infantry Regiment in the process. Returned to Russia in early 1942, the 8th fought in the Demyansk (Demjansk) relief operations in the northern sector until II Corps was freed in February 1943. The division continued to fight on the northern sector (at Demjansk and Lake Ilmen) until after the retreat from Leningrad began. In March 1944, it was sent to the southern sector and fought in the retreats through the Ukraine, the Carpathians and Slovakia. What remained of the 8th Jger was surrounded in Czechoslovakia in April 1945, and surrendered to the Russians in May.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第8步兵师于1941年6月被派往俄罗斯中部，初期战役中遭受了重大损失，尤其是在布良斯克、弗雅兹马和莫斯科保卫战。该师在1941年底返回法国，并改编为轻型师，在此过程中失去了其第28步兵团。<cr><cr>第8师于1942年初再次被派往俄罗斯北部地区，参与德梅扬斯克（德米亚ansk）解围行动，直到1943年2月第二军获释。该师继续在北部战区作战（包括德梅扬斯克和伊利门湖），直至列宁格勒撤退开始。<cr><cr>1944年3月，第8师被派往南部战区，在乌克兰、喀尔巴阡山脉及斯洛伐克的撤退行动中作战。1945年4月，该师残部在捷克斯洛伐克被包围，并于同年5月向苏联人投降。<cr><cr>参考文献：<cr>德国战斗序列 第二卷 291至999步兵师、命名步兵师及特殊部队二战史 Mitcham Jr. Samuel W.

text: The formation of the 8th Mechanized Corps began on June 4, 1940. The commander was General Lieutenant Dmitry Ryabyshev.<cr> On June 22, 1941, the corps comprised the 12th Tank Division, 34th Tank Division, 7th Mechanized Division, 2nd Motorcycle Regiment, an artillery regiment, an engineer battalion, and a signal battalion. It was located at river Styr in the Kiev Military District. It thus became part of the Southwestern Front, and was engaged in the first battles of Operation Barbarossa. The 34th Tank Division itself comprised the 67th and 68th Tank Regiments and the 34th Motor Rifle Regiment.<cr>On 23 June General Kirponos, Commander of the Southwestern Front, ordered the 8th Mechanized Corps, part of 26th Army at the time, to move to Brody out of Kostenko's command. Afterwards, the formation operated assigned to the N. I. Muzychenko's 6th Army. During the 500 kilometres (310 mi) road march from its initial positions in the Drogobychskaja sector in the Ukraine to the Brody area, the corps lost about half its older tanks to mechanical breakdown and enemy air attack. It then became embroiled in the Battle of Brody (1941). On 25 June 1941, 12th and 34th Tank Divisions were clearing the hills south of Brody before the whole corps opened its attack later that day. '...Its 34th Tank Division and elements of the 12th Tank Division advanced northwards, cutting the main road between Dubno and Brody. This forced the 16th Panzer Division to wheel round and attack the 34th Tank Division in the area of Kozin, in order to clear the road.'<cr>On June 26, attack plans that had been under preparation for some time were upstaged by direct orders from representatives of Southwestern Front HQ, who demanded that the corps attack immediately. Thus much of the unengaged remnants of 34th Tank Division were formed into an about 9,000-strong strike group led by Brigade Commissar Popel of corps headquarters, whose attack saw some initial success. Later however the strike group was encircled and destroyed.<cr>In July 1941 the corps command was redesignated Headquarters 38th Army, and thus the corps was disestablished.<cr><cr>
translation: 第8机械化军的组建工作始于1940年6月4日。指挥官是少将德米特里·利亚比舍夫。<cr> 1941年6月22日，该军包括第12坦克师、第34坦克师、第7机械化师、第2摩托化团、一个炮兵团、一个工兵营和一个通信营。它位于基辅军区的斯特里河畔。因此成为西南方面军的一部分，并参与了巴巴罗萨行动的第一场战斗。第34坦克师本身包括第67坦克团、第68坦克团以及第34摩托化步兵团。<cr> 6月23日，西南方面军指挥官基尔波诺斯将军命令当时隶属于第26集团军的第8机械化军离开科岑科的指挥，前往布罗迪。之后该部队被分配给穆奇琴科上将领导的第6集团军。在从乌克兰德罗戈比茨卡亚地区原驻地到布罗迪地区的500公里（310英里）公路行军过程中，该军大约损失了一半的老式坦克，原因是机械故障和敌方空军攻击。随后它卷入了布罗迪战役（1941）。6月25日，第12坦克师和第34坦克师正在清理布罗迪以南的山丘，在当天晚些时候整个军展开了进攻。“……其第34坦克师以及第12坦克师的部分部队向北推进，切断了杜布诺与布罗迪之间的主要道路。这迫使第16装甲师转向并攻击位于科津地区的第34坦克师，以清理道路。”<cr>1941年6月26日，经过一段时间准备的攻击计划被西南方面军司令部直接命令取代。该司令部要求各军立即发起进攻。因此，第34坦克师未参战的残余部队大部分被编成一个约9000人的突击群，由军团总部的政治委员波佩尔领导。突击群最初取得了一些成功，但后来遭到包围并被消灭。<cr>1941年7月，军团指挥部改称为第38集团军司令部，因此该军团解散。<cr>

text: In June 1941, the 8th Panzer Division invaded Russia as part of Erich von Manstein's LVI Panzer Corps and was heavily engaged in sweep through the Baltic States and in the drive on Leningrad, fighting in the battles of Dvinsk, Luga, Lake Ilmen, and Novgorod. By mid-July, the divisions tank strength had been reduced from 175 to 80. It nevertheless helped check Stalin's Winter Offensive of 194142 in the Volkhov sector, south of Leningrad. In 1942, it fought in the defensive battles ofArmy Group Center (including Kholm, Orel and Smolensk) and was transferred to the southern sector in 1943, after the Battle of Kursk attacks failed. That autumn it sustained heavy losses in the withdrawal from Kiev. It was more or less continuously in combat in 1944, fighting in the northern Ukraine, in southern Poland, and in Slovakia, including the battles of Zhitomir, Tarnopol and Brody. The 8th Panzer was sent to Hungary in December and fought near Budapest until January 1945, when it was sent north to Czechoslovakia. It ended the war on the central sector of the Eastern Front and surrendered to the Soviets at Deutsch-Brod on May 9, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol III - Panzer, Panzer Grenadier and Waffen SS Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation:
1941年6月，第8装甲师作为埃里希·冯·曼施坦因的LVII装甲军的一部分入侵俄罗斯，并在波罗的海国家的大规模扫荡行动和向列宁格勒推进中发挥了重要作用。该师参与了迪维纳、卢加、伊利门湖以及诺夫哥罗德等战役。到7月中旬，其坦克数量已从175辆减少至80辆。尽管如此，在1941-42年冬季攻势期间，它仍然帮助稳定了沃尔霍夫地区（列宁格勒以南）的战线。在1942年，该师参加了中央集团军群防御战役中的科尔姆、奥廖尔和斯摩棱斯克等战斗，并于1943年库尔斯克攻势失败后被转移到南部战区。同年秋天，在从基辅撤退时遭受了重大损失。该师在1944年几乎一直在作战，参与了乌克兰北部、波兰南部以及斯洛伐克的战役，包括日托米尔、塔尔诺波尔和布罗迪等战斗。第8装甲师于12月被派往匈牙利，并在布达佩斯附近作战至1945年1月，之后被调往捷克斯洛伐克北部。该师最终在东线中央战区结束战争，并于1945年5月9日在德意志-布鲁德向苏联投降。

<cr>

text: Part of the 5th Army at the outbreak of hostilities, it consisted of the 99th and 173rd Rifle and 72nd Mountain Rifle Divisions. 8th Corps was deployed in the vicinity of Przymysl in June 1941 and was destroyed in the Kiev pocket. It was reformed in November 1942 as part of Kalinin Front and designated the 'Estonian' corps, because some of its troops were veterans of the pre-1940 Estonian armed forces. It consisted of the 7th and 249th Rifle and 19th Guards Rifle divisions. It fought in the Battle of Narva (1944) and was the first Red Army unit to enter Talinn. During the Estonian campaign in 1944, the corps fought against the 20th Grenadier Divsion of the Waffen SS (Estonian). The corps was redesignated the 41st Guards Estonian Talinn Rifle Corps in December 1944.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, The Red Army Order of Battle in the Great Patriotic War, Presidio Press, 1985<cr><cr>Entry contributed by Stewart King
translation: 作为冲突爆发时第5集团军的一部分，它由第99步兵师、第173步兵师和第72山地步兵师组成。第8军于1941年6月部署在普热梅希尔附近，并在基辅包围圈中被消灭。该部队于1942年11月作为加里宁方面军的一部分重建，被称为“爱沙尼亚”军，因为其中一些部队成员是1940年前爱沙尼亚武装力量的老兵。它由第7步兵师、第249步兵师和第19近卫步兵师组成。该军参加了1944年纳尔瓦战役，并成为第一个进入塔林的红军单位。在1944年的爱沙尼亚战役中，该军与武装党卫军（爱沙尼亚）第20掷弹兵师作战。该军于1944年12月重新命名为第41近卫爱沙尼亚塔林步兵军。<cr>参考文献：Poirier, Robert and Conner, Albert, 《红军在伟大卫国战争中的战斗序列》，Presidio Press, 1985<cr>词条由Stewart King提供

text: The 8th Rifle Division was originally formed in 1918. The division took part in the 1939 Polish Campaign as part of the 16th Rifle Corps, 11th Army. On January 22, 1940 it was part of the 13th Rifle Corps of the Northwestern Front during the Winter War, but was shifted to the 23rd Rifle Corps by the end of January 1940. In June 1941 at the start of Operation Barbarossa the division consisted of the 151st, 229th and 310th Rifle Regiments, 62nd Light Artillery Regiment, 117th Howitzer Regiment and various support units. In July 1941 the division was destroyed as part of the German encirclement west of Minsk. The division was officially disbanded in September 1941.<cr>In July 1941 the 8th Krasnopresnenskaya Peoples' Militia Rifle Division was formed under the command of the Moscow Military District. The division contained an unusually large number of writers, musicians and historians; the writers were put together in the 3rd Company of the 1st Battalion of the 24th Rifle Regiment, which became known as the 'Writers' Company'. By July 10, 1941 the division had moved to the forest near Nicholas Urupino and Buzlanova. In late July 1941 the division was engaged in the fortification of defensive lines on the Mozhaysk line of defense. In August 1941 the division took positions on the Rzhev-Vyazma line of defence and subsequently on the eastern shore of the Dnieper River as well. On August 24, 1941 the formation was formally renamed the 8th Rifle Division. It included the 22nd, 23rd, and 24th Rifle Regiments. In October 1941 in connection with the beginning of the German Operation Typhoon it moved to the east of Yelnya. The division entered combat on October 4 1941 and by the next day it had already lost more than half of its personnel. October 6, 1941 the division was cut off and effectively destroyed although some of the division's survivors were able to join partisan units. The divisions was formally disbanded in November 1941.<cr>In early 1942 the 458th Rifle Division in Central Asia was renamed the 8th Rifle Division. Its three rifle regiments were numbered the same as the original 8th Rifle Division (151st, 229th and 310th). The division participated in many battles including the Battle of Kursk and the Crossing of the Dnieper. The division ended the war fighting at Prague.<cr><cr><cr><cr>Entry courtesy Chris Munson
translation:
第8步兵师最初成立于1918年。该师参加了1939年的波波兰战役，隶属于西北方向的第16步兵军、第11集团军。1940年1月22日，在冬季战争期间，它属于西北方向的第13步兵军，但到1940年1月底被转移到了第23步兵军。1941年6月巴巴罗萨行动开始时，该师由第151、229和310步兵团，第62轻型炮兵团，第117榴弹炮团以及各种支援单位组成。1941年7月，该师在明斯克以西的德军包围圈中被消灭。该师于1941年9月正式解散。<cr>1941年7月，第8克拉斯诺普列斯内人民民兵步兵师在莫斯科军区的指挥下组建。该师包含了一个异常多作家、音乐家和历史学家的群体；这些作家被编入了第24步兵团第1营的第3连，被称为“作家连”。到1941年7月10日，该师已经转移到尼古拉乌里波诺和布兹洛诺娃附近的森林中。1941年晚些时候，该师在莫扎伊斯克防御线参与了工事的建设工作。8月份，该师在热季-维亚兹马防御线上占据阵地，并随后占据了第聂伯河东岸的部分地区。1941年8月24日，该部队正式更名为第8步兵师。它包括第22、23和24步兵团。由于德国台风行动的开始，该师于10月份转移到叶连纳以东的位置。该师在10月4日投入战斗，并且到第二天已经损失了超过一半的人力资源。1941年10月6日，该师被切断并实际上被消灭，尽管一些幸存者能够加入游击队。该师于11月份正式解散。

1942年初，中亚的第458步兵师更名为第8步兵师。它的三个步兵团编号与原来的第8步兵师相同（第151、229和310团）。该师参加了许多战斗，包括库尔斯克战役和第聂伯河渡口行动，并在战争结束时参与了布拉格的战斗。

text: The 8th Romanian Cavalry Brigade was attached to the German XI Corps at the start of Operation Barbarossa. In March of 1942 it was reorganized as the 8th Romanian Cavalry Division. In July of 1943 the division was motorized. The division was intended to be converted into the 2nd Romanian Armored Division and was being refitted in the summer of 1944 when the Soviets arrived at the Romanian border. text:
The 8th Tank Corps was formed May 1942 in Moscow Military District with:<cr>
25th Tank Brigade
25th, 362nd Tank Battalions
25th Motorized Rifle Battalion
31st Tank Brigade
194th, 195th Tank Battalions
31st Motorized Rifle Battalion
93rd Tank Brigade
211th, 212th Tank Battalions
93rd Motorized Rifle Battalion
8th Motorized Rifle Brigade
1st, 2nd, 3rd Rifle Battalions<cr>For virtually its entire existence 8th tank Corps was assigned to Western Front, usually under Front HQ directly along with 6th Tank Corps. After several months of training and preparation, on 1 August the corps had 169 tanks, including 24 KVs, 46 T-34s, 30 T-7S and 69 T-60s. Unfortunately, the corps was committed to exploit the 'breakthrough' by 20th and 31st Armies in August. Since the breakthrough was not complete, in a grinding battle with German infantry and panzer forces the corps was thoroughly shot up. In September 1942 8th Tank Corps was pulled back to the Kalinin area, where the tank brigades were re-assigned and the corps HQ was used to form the 3rd Mechanized Corps.<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle World War II Volume II by Charles C. Sharp

Formed 6 July 1940 from 24th Light Tank Brigade at Lvov in Kiev Special Military District as part of 4th Mechanized Corps. On 22 June 1941 included:<cr>
15th Tank Regiment
1st Tank Bn - 25 KV tanks
2nd, 3rd Tank Bns - each 52 mixed T-34 and T-28 medium tanks
4th Tank Bn - 30 to 33 light tanks
16th Tank Regiment
1st Tank Bn - 25 KV tanks
2nd, 3rd Tank Bns - each 52 mixed T-34 and T-28 medium tanks
4th Tank Bn - 30 to 33 light tanks
8th Motorized Rifle Regiment
1st, 2nd, 3rd bns
8th Motorized Howitzer Regiment
1 light, 1 medium bn
8th Reconnaissance Battalion
8th Motorized Pontoon Battalion
8th Antiaircraft Battalion<cr><cr>The 4th Mechanized Corps was the only Mechanized Corps which actually went through corps and division manuevers in fall 1940. In that respect, 8th Tank Division was possibly the best trained tank division in the Red Army in June 1941, and it was one of the best-equipped with modern tanks. On 22 June
1941, the division had 50 KVs, 140 T-34s, 68 T-28s, 31 BT-7s, and 36 T-26 tanks. Almost full strength in other weapons, armored cars, and personnel, the biggest shortages in the division were in trucks and tractors - shortages that were endemic throughout the Red Army in 1941.<cr>The 8th Tank Division took part in the great armored battles across the Ukraine in June - July 1941 with the rest of 4th Mechanized Corps. Drawn into reserve at Dnepropetrovsk in August, the corps missed the Uman encirlcement. 8th Tank Division became an independant division after the corps HQ was disbanded in early August, and fought under 6th Army in in late August-early September 1941.<cr>In mid-September 1941 the division was withdrawn and the cadres of the division and the two tank regiments were used to form 130th and 131st Tank Brigades..<cr><cr>Soviet Order of Battle Volume I by Charles C. Sharp

第4营 - 30至33辆轻型坦克

第4机械化军是唯一一个在1940年秋季进行过军区和师级演习的机械化军。从这方面来看，第8坦克师可能是1941年6月红军中训练最充分的装甲师之一，并且装备了大量现代化坦克。1941年6月22日，该师拥有50辆KV坦克、140辆T-34坦克、68辆T-28坦克、31辆BT-7坦克和36辆T-26坦克。其他武器、装甲车和人员几乎满编，但该师最大的短缺在于卡车和拖拉机 - 这种短缺在1941年的红军中普遍存在。

第8坦克师参加了1941年6月至7月乌克兰的大规模装甲战斗，与第4机械化军的其余部队一起。8月份被调往德涅普罗彼得罗夫斯克作为预备队时，该军错过了乌曼包围战。在第4机械化军司令部于8月初解散后，第8坦克师成为独立师，并在1941年8月下旬至9月上旬隶属于第6集团军作战。

1941年9月中旬，该师被撤出战斗，师的骨干和两个装甲团的人员用于组建第130旅和第131旅。<cr> <cr>苏联战斗序列 第一卷 作者：查尔斯·C·肖普

text:
On 26 June 1941, after the German invasion of the Soviet Union four days earlier, the 91st Rifle Division began loading onto trains. On 29 June it left Achinsk. Between 8 and 10 July the trains arrived in Yelnya and Sychyovka. The division and its corps, which also included the 119th Rifle Division, joined the 24th Army.

The 91st Rifle Division was active with 52nd Rifle Corps (24th Army) in June 1941, and then transferred to 19th Army, Western Front before being destroyed at Vyazma. The Soviet defense, still under construction, was overrun and spearheads of the 2nd and 3rd Panzer Groups met at Vyazma on 10 October 1941. Four Soviet armies (the 19th, 20th, the 24th, and 32nd) were trapped in a huge pocket just west of the city. It was formally disbanded in December 1941.

On 5 December 1941 the 464th Rifle Division was formed in Dagestan in the North Caucasus Military District, near the cities of Makhachkala and Bataysk. On 27 January 1942 the division was redesignated the 91st Rifle Division (Second Formation) in the North Caucasus Military District. On 19 November 1942, the division was fighting in the Battle of Stalingrad, part of the 51st Army of the Stalingrad Front under N.I.Trufanov. On 1 April 1944, the division was part of the 1st Guards Rifle Corps of 51st Army and appears to have become involved in the Battle of the Crimea.<cr><cr>
translation:
1941年6月26日，在德国入侵苏联四天后，第91步兵师开始装载到火车上。6月29日离开阿钦斯克。7月8日至10日期间，火车抵达叶连纳和苏奇沃夫卡。该师及其所属的军（还包括第119步兵师）加入了第24集团军。

第91步兵师于1941年6月在第52步兵军（第24集团军）中活跃，随后转隶至西方方面军第19集团军，并在维亚兹马被消灭。苏联仍在建设中的防御工事被突破，第二和第三装甲集群的尖刀部队于1941年10月10日在维亚兹马会师。四个苏军集团军（第19、20、24和32集团军）被困在城市西边的一个巨大包围圈内。该师正式解散于1941年12月。

1941年12月5日，第464步兵师在北高加索军区的达吉斯坦地区成立，靠近马哈奇卡拉和巴塔伊斯基两座城市。1942年1月27日，该师被重新指定为北高加索军区的第91步兵师（第二组建）。1942年11月19日，该师在斯大林格勒方面军第51集团军下参与了斯大林格勒战役。1944年4月1日，该师成为第51集团军第1近卫步兵军的一部分，并似乎卷入了克里米亚之战。<cr> <cr>

text:
The 92nd Guards Rifle Division was formed in March 1943 in Kupyansk from the soldiers of the 149th and 12th Guards Rifle Brigades, which had fought in the Battle of Stalingrad. The 93rd Rifle Brigade was established in September 1942 in the Urals. It became 12th Guards Rifle Brigade, then in April 1943, 92nd Guards Rifle Division.

During the summer of 1943 the division participated in the Battle of Prokhorovka , then in the capture of the cities of Kharkov, Poltava, Voznesensk, Pervomaysk.

On 1 September 1943 the division was part of the 57th Rifle Corps. The corps comprised the 62nd Guards, 92nd Guards, 110th Guards and 53rd Rifle Divisions. It was part of the 37th Army, STAVKA Reserve (RVGK).

In 1943 the division liberated Kryvyi Rih, for which the division was named Krivorozhskaya. It crossed the River Dnieper near the village of Mishurin Rog. Soon afterwards, the division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner.

The division fought in Moldavia, and in the Jassy-Kinishev Offensive in Romania. It was with 37th Army in Bulgaria in May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation:
第92近卫步兵师于1943年3月在库皮扬斯克成立，由参加斯大林格勒战役的第149步兵旅和第12近卫步兵旅的士兵组成。第93步兵旅于1942年9月在乌拉尔地区建立，并于同年成为第12近卫步兵旅，在1943年4月进一步改编为第92近卫步兵师。

1943年夏季，该师参加了普罗霍罗夫卡战役，随后参与了哈尔科夫、波尔塔瓦、沃兹涅先斯克和佩尔沃迈斯基的攻城战。

1943年9月1日，该师隶属于第57步兵军。该军包括第62近卫、第92近卫、第110近卫和第53步兵师。它属于最高统帅部大本营预备队的第37集团军。

在1943年解放克里沃罗格期间，该师被命名为“克里沃罗格”师，并于靠近米舒林角村的地方渡过了第聂伯河。不久之后，该师获得了红旗勋章。

该师参加了摩尔达维亚的战斗，在罗马尼亚进行了雅西-奇西瑙攻势行动。1945年5月，它随第37集团军驻扎在保加利亚。<cr> <cr>

text: The 93rd Guards Rifle Division was formed at Valuki in April 1943 from 13th Guards and 92nd Rifle Brigades. The Division fought at Kursk, Kharkov, Budapest and Prague, and was serving with the 53rd Army of the 2nd Ukrainian Front in May 1945.<cr><cr>

text: The 95th Infantry Division was in more or less continuous action on the southern sector of the Russian Front from July 1941 until late 1942, fighting at Kiev, the Ukraine, Bryansk and Kursk (1941-42). Most of the guns of its 195th Artillery Regiment were lost when the Soviets cut into the rear of the 2nd German Army in mid-December 1941.<cr>What was left of the division continued to oppose the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42 and was involved in the initial drives on the Volga. Transferred to Army Group Center in late 1942, it took part in the Rzhev withdrawal and later formed part of 4th Armys line at Gomel and west of Smolensk in the summer fighting of 1943. It suffered heavy losses in the Bryansk attack that summer. During the winter of 1943-44, it was reorganized as a Type 44 division and each of its grenadier regiments was reduced to two battalions. In July 1944, the 95th was the only division in the 3rd Panzer Armys reserve when the huge Russian summer offensive began. Thrown into action, it was quickly overwhelmed near Vitebsk. Its divisional commander, Major General Michaelis, was captured and only remnants of his unit escaped. Nevertheless, the 95th was reformed as a Volksgrenadier division (with the same unit numbers) from Corps Detachment H and was sent back into action on the central sector in October. It fought at Memel(where it was smashed), was evacuated by the German Navy to Samland and, at battle group strength, opposed the Soviet invasion of East Prussia. It was trapped near Pillau and destroyed on April 16, 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol I 1st - 290th Infantry Divisions in WWII, Samuel W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 第95步兵师从1941年7月到1942年底一直在俄罗斯方面军南部战区持续作战，参与了基辅、乌克兰、布良斯克和库尔斯克（1941-1942）的战斗。其第195炮兵团的大部火炮在1941年12月中旬苏联切断德军中央集团军群后方时损失殆尽。<cr>剩余部队继续对抗苏军1941-1942年的冬季攻势，并参与了伏尔加河的初期进攻。该师于1942年底被调往中央集团军群，参加了日兹德拉撤退行动，并在1943年夏季战斗中成为第4集团军在戈梅利和斯摩棱斯克以西防线的一部分。同年夏天，在布良斯克攻势中遭受了重大损失。<cr>在1943-1944年的冬季，该师重组为Type 44师，并将其掷弹兵团缩减至两个营。1944年7月，第95步兵师是唯一一个被编入第3装甲集团军预备队的师，在巨大的苏联夏季攻势开始时被迫投入战斗。在维捷布斯克附近迅速被击溃后，其师长迈克尔少将被俘虏，只有该师残部得以逃脱。<cr>尽管如此，第95步兵师还是从H集群分离出的一个国民掷弹兵师（保留相同的单位编号）重新组建，并于10月在中央战区投入战斗。它参加了梅梅尔的战斗（在那里遭到重创），被德军海军撤离到萨姆兰岛，在战斗群规模下对抗苏联入侵东普鲁士，最终被困在皮劳并于1945年4月16日被消灭。

text: The 95th Rifle Division was first formed in November 1923 with the 6th Rifle Corps. It fought in the Winter War and the Soviet occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina. After Operation Barbarossa, the division fought in the retreat from Moldova and fought in the Siege of Odessa and the Siege of Sevastopol. It was destroyed during the Siege of Sevastopol and was disbanded in late July 1942. The division was reformed in August 1942 from the 13th Motor Rifle Division NKVD and fought at the Battle of Stalingrad. For its actions during the battle, the division became the 75th Guards Rifle Division in March 1943. In April 1943, the division was formed a third time at Kaluga from the 121st Rifle Brigade. It fought in Operation Bagration.<cr><cr>
translation: 第95步兵师成立于1923年11月，隶属于第6步兵军。该师参加了冬季战争和苏联占领比萨拉比亚及北布科维纳的行动。巴巴罗萨行动后，该师参与了从摩尔多瓦撤退，并在敖德萨围城战和塞瓦斯托波尔围城战中作战。它在塞瓦斯托波尔围城战中被消灭，并于1942年7月底解散。该师于1942年8月重组，由内务人民委员部第13摩托化步兵师改编而成，并参加了斯大林格勒战役。由于其在战斗中的表现，该师于1943年3月成为近卫第75步兵师。1943年4月，该师第三次重组，在卡卢加由第121步兵旅改编而成，并参与了巴格拉季昂行动。<cr><cr><cr>

text: It was converted to a rifle division in October 1941. Became 14th Guards Rifle Divison January 1942. Recreated July 1942. Fought at Stalingrad. Became 68th Guards Rifle Division in February 1943. It was recreated at Tula in March 1943. In mid July 1943 it was part of the 11th Army. During the Lublin-Brest Offensive, 350th Rifle Regiment company commander Mikhail Linnik distinguished himself and was subsequently awarded the title Hero of the Soviet Union. The division fought in Belorussia, East Prussia, and near Berlin (Battle of Berlin). With 48th Army of the 3rd Belorussian Front May 1945.<cr><cr>
translation: 它于1941年10月改编为步兵师。1942年1月成为第14近卫步兵师。1942年7月重建。参加了斯大林格勒战役。1943年2月改称第68近卫步兵师。1943年3月在图拉重建。1943年7月中旬隶属于第11集团军。<cr>在卢布林—别列津纳进攻战役中，第350步兵师第350团连指挥官米哈伊尔·利尼克表现出色，并随后被授予苏联英雄称号。该师参加了白俄罗斯、东普鲁士和柏林（柏林之战）的战斗。<cr>1945年5月隶属于第三白俄罗斯方面军第48集团军。<cr>指挥官报告<cr>

text:
On May 4, 1943, the 343rd Rifle Division was re-designated as the 97th Guards Rifle Division. Its order of battle was as follows:

289th Guards Rifle Regiment from 1151st Rifle Regiment
292nd Guards Rifle Regiment from 1153rd Rifle Regiment
294th Guards Rifle Regiment from 1155th Rifle Regiment
232nd Guards Artillery Regiment from 903rd Artillery Regiment
104th Guards Antitank Battalion from 567th Antitank Battalion
110th Guards Sapper Battalion from 620th Sapper Battalion
141st Guards Signal Battalion from 791st Signal Battalion
100th Guards Reconnaissance Company from 402nd Reconnaissance Company<cr>
The day before its re-designation the division was assigned to the newly-formed 33rd Guards Rifle Corps. On May 2, the commander of the division, Matvei Usenko, was promoted to the rank of Major General. Just ten days later he was killed after being blown up by a land mine while crossing a road in a vehicle.

The division took part in the Battle of Kursk, along with the rest of 5th Guards Army as part of the Steppe Front. Later, it fought in the liberation of left-bank Ukraine. In September, the division was awarded the 'Poltava' honorific, along with its sister divisions, the 13th and 95th Guards Rifle Divisions. In 1944 and 1945, it took part in the Kirovograd, Uman-Botoshany, Lvov-Sandomir, Sandomir-Silesia, Upper and Lower Silesia, Berlin, and Prague offensives. The division ended the war in 32nd Guards Rifle Corps, still in 5th Guards Army.<cr><cr>
translation:
1943年5月4日，第343步兵师改组为第97近卫步兵师。其战斗序列如下：

来自第1151步兵师的第289近卫步兵团
来自第1153步兵师的第292近卫步兵团
来自第1155步兵师的第294近卫步兵团
来自第903炮兵团的第232近卫炮兵团
来自第567反坦克营的第104近卫反坦克营
来自第620工兵营的第110近卫工兵营
来自第791通信营的第141近卫通信营
来自第402侦察连的第100近卫侦察连<cr>

改组前一天，该师被分配到新成立的第33步兵军。5月2日，师长马特维·乌森科晋升为少将。仅仅十天后，他在乘车穿越公路时因地雷爆炸而牺牲。

该师参加了库尔斯克会战，作为第5近卫集团军的一部分隶属于草原方面军。之后，它参与了左岸乌克兰的解放行动。9月，该师与姊妹部队第13和第95近卫步兵师一起被授予“波尔塔瓦”荣誉称号。在1944年和1945年，它参加了基洛夫格勒、乌曼-博托尚尼、利沃夫-桑多梅日、桑多梅日-西里西亚、上西里西亚和下西里西亚、柏林和布拉格攻势。该师在战争结束时仍隶属于第32步兵军，作为第5近卫集团军的一部分。<cr><cr>

text: It was initially dubbed the 97th Light Division, but was renamed 97th Jger Division on July 6, 1942. It was equipped almost entirely with captured French vehicles. Meanwhile, it crossed in to southern Russia in 1941, and fought in the Ukraine and Donets campaigns of that year, including the battles of Lemberg, Vinnitsa, Uman, and Kiev. It was involved in repulsing the Soviet winter offensive of 1941-42, and took part in the Battle of Isjum, the Caucasus Campaign of 194243, and in the subsequent retreats. It also fought in the Battle of Kursk (July 1943), where it suffered heavy casualties.<cr>Transferred to the lower Dnieper that autumn, it fought very well in the retreats through the Ukraine and in the Nikopol Bridgehead, and was officially cited for bravery. (The men of the division received 10,690 Iron Crosses, 2nd Class, during the war and 1,468 Iron Crosses, 1st Class, as well as 30 German Crosses in Gold, 14 Knights Crosses, and 4 Knights Crosses with Oak Leaves. The numbers of Iron Crosses are particularly impressive. Over the course of the war, the division also lost 13,000 men killed in action.) The 97th Jger - now much reduced by heavy fighting - was routed in March 1944 by the rapidly advancing Russians but continued to resist on the front line for the rest of the war. It was transferred to the Slovakian sector in October 1944, fought in Upper Silesia in early 1945, and ended the war in the huge pocket at Deutsch-Brod (east of Prague) in May 1945, when it surrendered to the Soviets.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 它最初被称为第97轻师，但在1942年7月6日改名为第97猎兵师。该师几乎完全装备了从法国缴获的车辆。与此同时，在1941年进入南俄，并参加了当年在乌克兰和顿涅茨地区的战役，包括伦贝格、文尼察、乌曼和基辅之战。它参与了抵御苏联1941-42年冬季攻势的行动，并参加了伊久姆战役、1942-43年的高加索战役以及随后的撤退行动。该师还参加了库尔斯克会战（1943年7月），在此期间遭受了重大伤亡。<cr>同年秋天，它被转移到第聂伯河下游地区，在乌克兰的撤退中表现非常出色，并在尼科波尔桥头堡作战时正式获得嘉奖。（该师官兵在战争期间共获得了10690枚二级铁十字勋章、1468枚一级铁十字勋章以及30枚金质德意志十字勋章、14枚骑士十字勋章和4枚橡叶骑士十字勋章。其中，铁十字勋章的数量尤其令人印象深刻。在整个战争过程中，该师还损失了13000名阵亡官兵。）第97猎兵师（由于激烈的战斗而大幅减员）在1944年3月被迅速推进的苏联军队击溃，但继续坚守前线直到战争结束。<cr>它于1944年10月被转移到斯洛伐克战区，在1945年初参加了上西里西亚地区的作战，并在1945年5月在德意志布罗德（布拉格以东）的大包围圈中向苏联投降。

text: The 97th Rifle Division was established Zhmerinka before 1940. The 377th OTB of the 97th Rifle Division arrived at the front he Winter War on 28 January 1940 with 31 T-26s (including 11 twin-turreted) and 6 KhT-26 flame-throwing tanks. With 6th Rifle Corps, 6th Army of the Southwestern Front from 22 June 1941. Wiped out at Kiev Sep 1941. Recreated Divisionnaya Jan 1942. Became 83rd Guards Rifle Division Apr 1943. Recreated Belev May 1943. Fought near Vitebsk, Vilnius, and in Hungary. With 5th Army of the RVGK 5.45.<cr><cr>
translation: 第97步兵师成立于1940年之前，驻扎在日梅林卡。该师的第377个坦克营于1940年1月28日在冬季战争期间抵达前线，装备有31辆T-26（包括11辆双炮塔型）和6辆KhT-26火焰喷射坦克。从1941年6月22日起隶属于西南方面军第6步兵军、第6集团军。于1941年9月在基辅被消灭。1942年1月重建为师级单位。1943年4月改编为第83近卫步兵师。1943年5月再次重建，驻扎在别利夫。曾在维捷布斯克、维尔纽斯和匈牙利作战。从1945年5月起隶属于红军建设与训练总局（RVGK）的第5集团军。<cr><cr><cr>

text: The 98th Guards Rifle Division ws formed in December 1943-January 1944 at Demitrov in the Moscow Military District. It incorporated 296th Guards Rifle Regiment (formerly the 18th Independent Guards Airborne Brigade), 299th GRR (fmr 19 IGAB), 302nd GRR (fmr 20 IGAB). It was part of the 37th Guards Airborne Corps, 9th Guards Army on the Karelian Front (May 1944), on the Svir river (June 1944) and near Budapest in February 1945. The division ended the war near Prague.<cr><cr>
translation: 第98近卫步兵师于1943年12月至1944年1月在莫斯科军区的德米特罗夫组建，由第296近卫步兵团（原独立第18空降旅）、第299近卫步兵团（原独立第19空降旅）和第302近卫步兵团（原独立第20空降旅）组成。该师隶属于第37空降军，参加了北方方面军的卡累利阿方向作战（1944年5月），在西维尔河沿岸作战（1944年6月），并在1945年2月布达佩斯附近作战。战争结束时，该师位于布拉格附近。<cr><cr>

text: The 98th Rifle Division was established Ishevsk Feb 1941. Wiped out at Vyazma Oct 1941. Recreated Spassk Oct 1941. Fought in Stalingrad. Became 86th Guards Rifle Division Apr 1943. Recreated at Leningrad from 250th Rifle Brigade. Fought vicinity Leningrad. With 59th Army of the 1st Ukrainian Front 5.45.<cr><cr>
translation: 第98步兵师于1941年2月在伊热夫斯克建立。1941年10月在维亚兹马被消灭。1941年10月在斯帕斯克重建。参加过斯大林格勒战役。1943年4月改编为第86近卫步兵师。从第250步兵旅重建于列宁格勒。参加了列宁格勒附近的战斗。隶属于第1乌克兰方面军的第59集团军，5.45。<cr><cr>

text:
The 99th Guards Rifle Division was formed from the 14th Guards Airborne Division on 19 January 1944.

Prior to June 1944, it was stationed in the Moscow Military District, but was transferred to the line of the Svir to fight in the Svir-Petrozavodsk Operation. On 21 June 1944, the division crossed the Svir and breaking through the Finnish defences, seized its objectives. On 25 June, it captured the strongpoint of Kuytezha. During the river crossing, the division supported the 275th Separate Motorized Battalion of Special Forces and the 92nd Independent Tank Regiment, which utilized the T-37A amphibious tank, in the last such use of tanks in the war. On the same day, the division captured the strongholds of Pirkinichi and Semenovschinu. The division advanced to the north to Svirstroy and prevented the Finnish from blowing up a dam.

On 15 July 1944, the division, supported by the 29th Tank Brigade, attacked. After the Finnish troops were partially routed, 460 soldiers from the division were surrounded after advancing too far and killed or captured. On 9 August, the division was put in reserve near Orsha. On 9 August it became the 99th Guards Airborne Division.

From 29 December 1944 to 5 January 1945, the division was reorganised as the 99th Guards Rifle Division in the Belorussian Military District in accordance with Stavka VGK Prikaz 0047 of 18 December 1944.

In January 1945, the division was transferred to Hungary and was positioned southeast of Budapest . On 13 March 1945, it repulsed the German counterattack during Operation Spring Awakening. During the Vienna Offensive, it broke through the German defences north of Szekesfehervar, into the 6th Panzer Army's rear area, penetrating the German line between Lake Velence and Lake Balaton.

On 29 March it fought in the capture of Szombathely. In early April, in conjunction with the 6th Guards Tank Army, it advanced to the Danube, cutting of German escape routes to the west. On 1 April 1945 it was on the outskirts of Wiener Neustadt, on 2 April in Baden bei Wien. The division fought in the Vienna Offensive until 13 April. On 8 May, it captured Znojmo. The division advanced to the Elbe and in May was in the area of Mlaka in Czechoslovakia.<cr><cr>
translation:
第99近卫步兵师于1944年1月19日由第14空降师改编而成。

1944年6月之前，该师驻扎在莫斯科军区，但随后被调往斯维里河沿线参加斯维里-彼得罗扎沃茨克战役。6月21日，该师渡过斯维里河，突破芬兰防御并占领了目标区域。6月25日，它攻克了库伊特扎强点。在渡河期间，该师支援了特种部队独立机械化第275营和独立坦克团第92团的行动，后者使用了T-37A两栖坦克，在战争中这是最后一次使用此类装备。同一天，该师还占领了皮尔金尼奇和塞梅诺夫斯基两个要地，并向北推进至斯维里斯特罗伊，阻止芬兰人炸毁水坝。

1944年7月15日，该师在第29坦克旅的支援下发动进攻。芬兰部队部分溃退后，该师有460名士兵因推进过远而被包围，并被击毙或俘虏。8月9日，该师被调至奥尔沙附近作为预备队。同一天，该师改编为第99近卫空降师。

从1944年12月29日至1945年1月5日，该师根据最高统帅部大本营1944年12月18日第0047号命令，在白俄罗斯军区重组为第99近卫步兵师。

1945年1月，该师被调往匈牙利，并部署在布达佩斯东南方向。1945年3月13日，它击退了德国的反击行动“春季觉醒”计划。在维也纳攻势期间，它突破了设克什费海瓦尔北部的德国防线，进入第6装甲集团军后方区域，在维伦切湖和巴拉顿湖之间穿过了德军防线。

3月29日，该师参加了索博陶莱的攻占。4月初，在第6近卫坦克集团军配合下，它推进至多瑙河，切断了德军向西逃窜的道路。4月1日，该师位于维也纳新城郊外；4月2日，则在维也纳附近的巴登。该师参加了维也纳攻势，直至4月13日。5月8日，它占领了兹诺伊莫。随后该师推进至易北河，并于5月进入捷克斯洛伐克的姆拉卡地区。<cr><cr>

text: Originally formed as the 99th Jger Division on November 15, 1940, this division initially included the 206th and 218th Jger Regiments. After seeing action at Zhitomir and Kiev on the Russian Front, it was reformed as a mountain division in the Grafenwoehr Troop Maneuver Area on November 15, 1941. In the spring of 1942, it was sent to Finland and remained there until the Finns renounced their military alliance with the Nazis in the fall of 1944. In the subsequent retreat from Lapland the 7th Mountain formed part of the XVIII Mountain Corps, 20th Mountain Army. After arriving in Norway, the High Command ordered the division to return to Europe; however, the war ended before it could embark. The division surrendered to the British at Trondheim in May 1945.<cr><cr>German Order of Battle Vol II 291st - 999th Infantry Divisions, Named Infantry Divisions and Special Divisions in WWII, Samue; W. Mitcham Jr.
translation: 原初成立于1940年11月15日的第99猎兵师，最初包括第206和第218猎兵团。在俄罗斯战场上的热季托米尔和基辅作战后，该师于1941年11月15日在格拉芬沃赫部队演习区重组为山地师。1942年春天，它被派往芬兰，并一直驻扎到1944年秋季芬兰拒绝与纳粹的军事联盟为止。在随后从拉普兰撤退的过程中，第7山地师成为第18山地军和第20山地集团军的一部分。抵达挪威后，最高指挥部命令该师返回欧洲；然而，战争结束前它尚未启程。该师于1945年5月向英国人投降，在特隆赫姆。<cr><cr>德国战斗序列 第二卷 291至999步兵师、命名步兵师及特殊部队在二战中的编成，萨缪尔·W·米奇姆少校

text:
In 1939 the 99th Rifle Division took part in the Soviet invasion of Poland as part of the 13th Rifle Corps, 12th Army, Ukrainian Front. On 29 September 1939 the division entered Przemysl. Recognised as one of the best divisions in the Army under Andrey Vlasov's command in 1940. On 22 June 1941 it was serving with 8th Rifle Corps, 26th Army, Southwestern Front, and participated in a counterstroke at Przemysl.

During the German-Soviet War, on 27 June 1941 the division left Przemysl for Nikolaev, and then Vinnitsa. On 22 July 1941 the division was awarded the Order of the Red Banner for its actions at Przemysl. In the Uman encirclement in July-August 1941, most of the division was lost or was taken prisoner, with only a part of the division artillery and rear services avoiding capture; in total, from the Uman 'kessel' only about two thousand soldiers broke free, though carrying with them the divisional banner, and also the banners of its units.

On 1 May 1942 the division was part of the 57th Army alongside the 14th Guards Rifle Division, 150th, 317th, and 351st Rifle Divisions preparing to fight what became the Second Battle of Kharkov. During the battle the division was practically wiped out at Izyum in mid-May 1942, when it was surrounded at Barvenkovo (place), with only 1067 of the unit's personnel managing to evade capture. From 8 to 15 June 1942 the division was transferred out of the Southern Front, and from the Redkovskiye Peski area the division was sent to Balashov to be reorganised. During this period it was part of the 6th Reserve Army. From 10 July 1942 the division was transferred to the 8th Reserve Army, though it may have stayed at Balashov, reforming, until as late as August 1942. The division then fought at Stalingrad. On 1 September 1942 the division was part of the 66th Army, preparing for its part in Operation Uranus, and 1 December 1942 the division was still with the 66th Army but the Army had been transferred from the Stalingrad Front to the Don Front.

By 10 March 1943, as part of the 62nd Army the division was loaded on a train at station Panshino and sent to the disposition of the Southwestern Front at Dvurechnaya station (literally two-rivers). On 18 April 1943 it became the 88th Guards Rifle Division.<cr><cr>The division was recreated from 99th Rifle Brigade in May 1943. Fought near Zhitomir and in Carpathians. With 46th Army of the 2nd Ukrainian Front 5.45.<cr><cr>
translation:
1939年，第99步兵师参加了苏联入侵波兰的行动，隶属于乌克兰方面军第12集团军下的第13步兵军。9月29日，该师进入普热梅希尔。在安德烈·弗拉索夫指挥下，该师于1940年被公认为是陆军中最好的部队之一。1941年6月22日，它隶属于西南方面军第26集团军下的第8步兵军，并参与了普热梅希尔的反击行动。

在苏德战争期间，该师于1941年6月27日从普热梅希尔出发前往尼古拉耶夫，随后到达 Vinnytsia。1941年7月22日，由于在普热梅希尔的表现，该师被授予红旗勋章。在 1941 年 7-8 月的乌曼包围圈中，该师大部分部队损失或被俘虏，只有部分炮兵和后勤人员得以逃脱；总计从乌曼包围圈中仅有约两千名士兵突围而出，他们带着师旗以及所属单位的旗帜。

1942年5月1日，该师隶属于第57集团军，与第14近卫步兵师、第150步兵师、第317步兵师和第351步兵师一起准备参加第二次哈尔科夫战役。在战斗中，该师于1942年5月中旬几乎被消灭，在伊久姆遭到包围，仅1067名人员成功逃脱俘虏。从1942年6月8日至15日，该师从南方方面军调出，并从雷德科夫斯基佩斯克地区转移到巴拉绍夫重组。在此期间，它隶属于第6预备集团军。自1942年7月10日起，该师转隶第8预备集团军，但可能直到同年8月仍在巴拉绍夫重组。之后，该师参加了斯大林格勒战役。1942年9月1日，该师隶属于准备参加天王星行动的第66集团军；至1942年12月1日，该师仍属于第66集团军，但该集团军已从斯大林格勒方面军转隶顿河方面军。

截至1943年3月10日，该师作为第62集团军的一部分，在潘什诺车站装车，并被送往西南方面军的杜维尔奇纳亚车站（直译为“两河”站）。1943年4月18日，该师改编为第88近卫步兵师。<cr>@PH1@@该师于1943年5月从第99步兵旅重建，并在扎波罗热和喀尔巴阡山脉附近作战。作为第2乌克兰方面军的第46集团军的一部分，参与了1945年5月的战斗。<cr><cr>
